> अधि श्रिये दुहिता सूर्यस्य रथं तस्थौ पुरुभुजा शतोतिम् ।
> प्र मायाभिर्मायिना भूतमत्र नरा नृतू जनिमन्यज्ञियानाम् ॥

> *adhi śriye duhitā sūryasya rathaṃ tasthau purubhujā śatotim |*
> *pra māyābhirmāyinā bhūtamatra narā nṛtū janimanyajñiyānām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6. 63. 5) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "For glory the daughter of the Sun mounted your chariot of a hundred aids, O you of many enjoyments; by your wondrous powers, wonder-working heroes, dancers, you surpassed here the race of those worthy of worship.")

> ओ त्यमह्व आ रथमद्या दंसिष्ठमूतये ।
> यमश्विना सुहवा रुद्रवर्तनी आ सूर्यायै तस्थथुः ॥

> *o tyamahva ā rathamadyā daṃsiṣṭhamūtaye |*
> *yamaśvinā suhavā rudravartanī ā sūryāyai tasthathuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8. 22. 1) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "I have called here today, for help, that most wondrous chariot which you, Aśvins, easy to invoke, of Rudra's path, mounted for Sūryā.")

> को मृळाति कतम आगमिष्ठो देवानामु कतमः शंभविष्ठः ।
> रथं कमाहुर्द्रवदश्वमाशुं यं सूर्यस्य दुहितावृणीत ॥

> *ko mṛḷāti katama āgamiṣṭho devānāmu katamaḥ śaṃbhaviṣṭhaḥ |*
> *rathaṃ kamāhurdravadaśvamāśuṃ yaṃ sūryasya duhitāvṛṇīta ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4. 43. 2) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Who is gracious? Which of the gods comes most readily, which brings most weal? Which swift chariot with running horses do they mean, that the daughter of the Sun chose?")

In such contexts it is well known that Sūryā chose the Aśvin deities for a *svayaṃvara*. In the ṛk 6. 63. 5 quoted above it is said that the Aśvin deities, seated in their three-wheeled chariot, won victory in the contest arranged for the gods. But in the ṛk 10. 85. 15 quoted above from the sūkta-mantras, it is described that when they set out to approach Sūryā one wheel of their chariot became invisible. Explaining what its intent is, the English scholar called Maryla Falk has made known her opinion in this way:

"What were the three wheels of the Aswin's car? The twin gods are most frequently said to come at early dawn, but this is not the only time of their coming. The express statement repeatedly occurs that they are invoked both in the morning and in the evening. (VIII. 22-14; X. 39-1; X. 40-4). Once it is said that they come also at noon (V. 76-3.) It remains undecided what specific natural phenomenon they were supposed to represent, but their connection with the transition between light and darkness is certain. They may thus have been meant to represent the morning and evening star as they are said to have been born separately. (V. 73-4). Their path is red or golden — it is dawn and sunset. Their car runs also by day and by night since it is said to move round the whole of the sky (I. 180-10) to cover the whole expanse of heaven in its course (IV. 43-5) to compass Heaven and Earth in one day' (III. 58-8). But at those times, it is not seen. In its nightly course it separates the extreme points of heaven and at that time' सूर्या (*sūryā*) enfolds the Aswin's brightness. (VII. 69-3 & 4). The other, more obvious, moment of their marriage with सूर्या (*sūryā*) is when they cross the path of the Sun at the zenith: This was when the Sun mounted on their car and when the third, the middle or noontide wheel of that car disappeared, [according to the 15th stanza of the सूर्यासूक्त (*sūryāsūkta*)] or was promptly arrested, [according to the 3rd stanza of the hymn V 73.] One beautiful wheel you *(the quotation continues on the next page; the words given here in Devanagari are printed in Kannada script within the English; the stray marks after "day" and "time" are as printed)*
### Printed p. 29  (PDF 47)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 1".)* *(Maryla Falk's English, continued, as printed.)*

promptly arrested for the sake of the beauty (of सूर्या (*sūryā*)) wherea s round [sic] the other spheres you fly powerfully". The 5th stanza of the same hymn explains that, when सूर्या (*sūryā*) mounted on their ever swift-running car, they were encompassed hy [sic] the flaming rays of the Sun's glow. The! [sic] wheel of the Sun, of the flaming सूर्या (*sūryā*), absorbed the wheel of the Aswins, made it disappear in its rays.

[The Indian Historical Quarterly Vol. XVIII. No. 1. March 1942. p. 28.]

The gist of this opinion is as follows.

> यो वां परिज्मा सुवृदश्विना रथो दोषामुषासो हव्यो हविष्मता ।
> शश्वत्तमासस्तमु वामिदं वयं पितुर्न नाम सुहवं हवामहे ॥

> *yo vāṃ parijmā suvṛdaśvinā ratho doṣāmuṣāso havyo haviṣmatā |*
> *śaśvattamāsastamu vāmidaṃ vayaṃ piturna nāma suhavaṃ havāmahe ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-39-1) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Your chariot, Aśvins, that goes around, well-rolling, to be invoked at evening and at dawn by him who has the oblation — that chariot of yours we, ever and again, call upon, easy to invoke, like the name of a father.")

In such ṛks it is made known that the Aśvin deities are invoked both at the time of dawn and at the time of evening twilight. Not only that,

> उता यातं संगवे प्रातरह्नो मध्यंदिन उदिता सूर्यस्य ।
> दिवा नक्तमवसा शंतमेन नेदानीं पीतिरश्विना ततान ॥

> *utā yātaṃ saṃgave prātarahno madhyaṃdina uditā sūryasya |*
> *divā naktamavasā śaṃtamena nedānīṃ pītiraśvinā tatāna ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5. 76. 3.) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "And come at the cattle-gathering time, in the early part of the day, at midday, at the rising of the Sun, by day and by night, with most beneficent help; the drinking, Aśvins, has not now [ceased to] extend.")

— by such mantras they are invoked to the midday pressing as well. In this way the Niruktakāras have made clear that it is not possible to state definitely what the nature is of the Aśvin deities, who have prominence in all three pressings, and that each states a different opinion (Ni. 12-1). And

> नाना जातावरेपसा समस्मे बन्धुमेयथुः ।

> *nānā jātāvarepasā samasme bandhumeyathuḥ |*

(Ṛ-Saṃ-5-73-4) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Born separately, spotless, you have come to kinship with this one.")

— in such places, as नाना जातौ । पृथगेव समृद्धौ (*nānā jātau | pṛthageva samṛddhau*) ("born separately: grown up each on his own"), their individual origin and growth are shown. In some places it is made known that the two names Nāsatya and Dasra are separate individual forms of the Aśvin pair (Journal of Oriental Research, Madras Vol XV). It is understood that they are deities who shine at dawn and at evening. For that very reason, in हिरण्ययाः वां पवयः (*hiraṇyayāḥ vāṃ pavayaḥ*) (1-180-1) and similar places, the twilight-red colour of their chariot and chariot-wheel is described. The Aśvin deities of such a nature —

> युवोः श्रियं परियोषावृणीत सूरो दुहिता परितक्म्यायाम् ।
> यद्देवयन्तमवथः शचीभिः परि घ्रंसमोमना वां वयो गात् ॥

> *yuvoḥ śriyaṃ pariyoṣāvṛṇīta sūro duhitā paritakmyāyām |*
> *yaddevayantamavathaḥ śacībhiḥ pari ghraṃsamomanā vāṃ vayo gāt ‖*

(Ṛ-Saṃ-7-69-4) — here it is praised thus: "O Aśvin deities, the daughter of Sūrya, ever attached to the service of your beauty, joins you at the times of the pressings and pervades [all] in you." Besides this description, it is also made known in some places that this same daughter of Sūrya, when they [the Aśvins] come to be in the middle of the Sun's path in the antarikṣa, overpowers the Aśvin deities and joins them. At such times, *(continues on the next page)*

> ईर्मान्यद्वपुषे वपुश्चक्रं रथस्य येमथुः ।
> पर्यन्या नाहुषा युगा मह्ना रजांसि दीयथः ॥

> *īrmānyadvapuṣe vapuścakraṃ rathasya yemathuḥ |*
> *paryanyā nāhuṣā yugā mahnā rajāṃsi dīyathaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ-Saṃ-5-73-3) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "One wondrous wheel of your chariot you held fast for beauty; around the other [spheres], the generations of men, you fly by your greatness through the regions.")

By such mantras the third wheel of the chariot of the Aśvin deities, and its light, are described. That Sūryā joins the Aśvin deities who have such a chariot-wheel is praised in such places as

> आ यद्वां सूर्या रथं तिष्ठद्रघुष्यदं सदा ।

> *ā yadvāṃ sūryā rathaṃ tiṣṭhadraghuṣyadaṃ sadā |*

(Ṛ-Saṃ-5-73-5) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "When Sūryā mounted your swift-running chariot, ever …"). And in this same mantra, with the sentence परि वामरुषा वयो घृणावरन्त आतपः (*pari vāmaruṣā vayo ghṛṇāvaranta ātapaḥ*), it is praised that as soon as Sūryā mounted the chariot of the Aśvin deities their chariot was filled with the golden radiance of the Sun. That is, the meaning is that the Sun's radiance made their chariot-wheel hidden.

Among the opinions of the scholar called Maryla Falk quoted above, some are both critical and explanations in keeping with tradition. But some other explanations of that writer are merely imagined. In what way they are contrary to tradition will be made known clearly later, when the Sūryā-sūkta is explained. In the present place, after noticing one or two contradictory points regarding Sūryā's marriage that appear to a gross view, it must next be noticed who the other deities are that are described as identified with Sūryā, and what their nature is. And what kind of harmony there is among these contradictory points that appear to a gross view will be made known later.

> अपागूहन्नमृतां मर्त्येभ्यः कृत्वी सवर्णामददुर्विवस्वते ।
> उताश्विनावभरद्यत्तदासीदजहादु द्वा मिथुना सरण्यूः ॥

> *apāgūhannamṛtāṃ martyebhyaḥ kṛtvī savarṇāmadadurvivasvate |*
> *utāśvināvabharadyattadāsīdajahādu dvā mithunā saraṇyūḥ ‖*

(Ṛ-Saṃ-10-17-2) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "They hid the immortal one from mortals; making one of like appearance they gave her to Vivasvat; and she bore the Aśvins when that happened; Saraṇyū left behind the two pairs.")

— in this ṛk there is the description that the gods gave Saraṇyū to Vivasvān in marriage, and that she, in the form of a mare, bore the Aśvin deities. That is, from this it is understood that the Aśvin deities are sons of Vivasvān. But, quoted above,

> सावित्री चैव सूर्या च स्यैवपत्नी विशेषतः ।

> *sāvitrī caiva sūryā ca syaivapatnī viśeṣataḥ |*

(Bṛ. De. 7-119; here printed स्यैवपत्नी विशेषतः, where p. 27 has स्यैव पत्नी विवस्वतः.) ("Sāvitrī and Sūryā [are] … wife, in particular.") — from this sentence of the Bṛhaddevatā it is understood that Sūryā is the wife of Vivasvān. What then is meant by saying that the Aśvin deities chose her herself? Likewise, *(continues on the next page)*
### Printed p. 31  (PDF 49)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 1".)*

> सोमो वधूयुरभवदश्विनास्तामुभा वरा ।
> सूर्यां यत्पत्ये शंसन्तीं मनसा सविताददात् ॥

> *somo vadhūyurabhavadaśvināstāmubhā varā |*
> *sūryāṃ yatpatye śaṃsantīṃ manasā savitādadāt ‖*

(Ṛ Saṃ 10-85-9) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Soma was the bride-seeker; the Aśvins were both the groomsmen, when Savitṛ gave Sūryā, longing in her mind for a husband.")

— here [it is said that] Savitṛ gave his daughter Sūryā to Soma and performed the marriage; the Aśvin deities were then merely spectators; after the marriage Sūryā went to the house of Soma, her husband, and joined him. In what way the intent here is to be stated, and so on, will be made known clearly in the explanation of the Sūryā-sūkta, and the harmony of these contradictory points will be shown.

In the description of Sūryā and her marriage set out in the Sūryā-sūkta of the Ṛksaṃhitā, a deep spiritual (*ādhyātmika*) truth lies hidden. Some mantras of the Sūryā-sūkta make this aspect known. The truth described in the sentences of the Upaniṣads is made known by these mantras. For example,

> मनो अस्या अन आसीद्द्यौरासीदुत च्छदिः ।
> शुक्रावनड्वाहावास्तां यदयात्सूर्या गृहम् ॥
> ऋक्सामाभ्यामभिहितौ गावौ ते सामनावितः ।
> श्रोत्रं ते चक्रे आस्तां दिवि पन्थाश्चराचरः ॥

> *mano asyā ana āsīddyaurāsīduta cchadiḥ |*
> *śukrāvanaḍvāhāvāstāṃ yadayātsūryā gṛham ‖*
> *ṛksāmābhyāmabhihitau gāvau te sāmanāvitaḥ |*
> *śrotraṃ te cakre āstāṃ divi panthāścarācaraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10. 85. 10, 11) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Her mind was the cart, and heaven was the covering; the two bright ones were the draught-oxen when Sūryā went to her [husband's] home. Yoked by Ṛk and Sāman, your two oxen went in harmony; your ears were the two wheels; in heaven was the path, moving and unmoving.")

In such ṛks there is not merely a description of Sūryā's physical body: there is a description that gives the sense that Sūryā is a power reflecting the principle of the universe. According to this description, mind itself is her chariot; the antarikṣa itself is its covering; the two orbs of radiance shining in the antarikṣa are her draught-animals; those draught-animals, yoked by Ṛk and by Sāman, drew Sūryā; the chariot-wheels themselves are her ears; the path on which she travels lay in the antarikṣa. When the Aśvin deities came to choose Sūryā, adorned with such wedding attire, all the gods approved, it says.

From some further descriptions it is understood that identity is stated between Sūryā and Vāk in the form of Śabdabrahman. Making this very point known, the Bṛhaddevatā [says]:

> यदा तु वाग्भवत्येषा सूर्यामुं लोकमाश्रिता ।
> तथा सूक्तमुषा भूत्वा सूर्या च भजतेऽखिलम् ॥

> *yadā tu vāgbhavatyeṣā sūryāmuṃ lokamāśritā |*
> *tathā sūktamuṣā bhūtvā sūryā ca bhajate 'khilam ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 2. 79; the first numeral is the curled glyph read as 2, as on p. 26.) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "And when this Vāk, resting on yonder world, becomes Sūryā, then, having become Uṣas and Sūryā, she shares in the whole hymn.")

> सूर्यामेव सतीमेतां गौरीं वाचं सरस्वतीम् ।
> पश्यामो वैश्वदेवेषु निपातेनैव केवलाः ॥

> *sūryāmeva satīmetāṃ gaurīṃ vācaṃ sarasvatīm |*
> *paśyāmo vaiśvadeveṣu nipātenaiva kevalāḥ ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 2. 81) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "This same [Vāk], being Sūryā, we see as Gaurī, Vāk, Sarasvatī in the Vaiśvadeva hymns, only by incidental mention.") *(The Special Topics of Ṛk 3 continue on the next page.)*

### Printed p. 32  (PDF 50)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 184".)* …by such verses (it is made known that) Vāk, of the nature of Śabdabrahman, is stationed in the antarikṣa in the form of Sūryā. She is described as Sūryā, as the goddess Uṣas, as Gaurī and as Sarasvatī. The greatness of this Vāk has been explained in detail earlier in the Special Topics of Ṛk 1. 164. 45 [?]. Since identity with Vāk is thus stated, a marital relation between Sūryā and the Gandharva is also implied. How Sūryā fell to the Gandharva who had received Soma is described in the last ṛks of the Sūryā-sūkta, as follows.

> तुभ्यमग्रे पर्यवहन्त्सूर्यां वहतुना सह ।
> पुनः पतिभ्यो जायां दा अग्ने प्रजया सह ॥
> पुनः पत्नीमग्निरदादायुषा सह वर्चसा ।
> दीर्घायुरस्या यः पतिर्जीवाति शरदः शतं ॥
> सोमः प्रथमो विविदे गन्धर्वो विविद उत्तरः ।
> तृतीयो अग्निष्टे पतिस्तुरीयस्ते मनुष्यजाः ॥
> सोमो ददद्गन्धर्वाय गन्धर्वो दददग्नये ।
> रयिं च पुत्रांश्चादादग्निर्मह्यमथो इमां ॥

> *tubhyamagre paryavahantsūryāṃ vahatunā saha |*
> *punaḥ patibhyo jāyāṃ dā agne prajayā saha ‖*
> *punaḥ patnīmagniradādāyuṣā saha varcasā |*
> *dīrghāyurasyā yaḥ patirjīvāti śaradaḥ śataṃ ‖*
> *somaḥ prathamo vivide gandharvo vivida uttaraḥ |*
> *tṛtīyo agniṣṭe patisturīyaste manuṣyajāḥ ‖*
> *somo dadadgandharvāya gandharvo dadadagnaye |*
> *rayiṃ ca putrāṃścādādagnirmahyamatho imāṃ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-38 to 41.) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "For you, Agni, they carried Sūryā round with her bridal train; give the wife back to the husbands, Agni, with offspring. Agni gave the wife back, with life and splendour; may her husband be long-lived and live a hundred autumns. Soma first found her, the Gandharva found her next; Agni was your third husband; the fourth is born of men. Soma gave her to the Gandharva, the Gandharva gave her to Agni; Agni gave me wealth and sons, and this woman as well.")

— in these ṛks it is stated that Sūryā was given first to Agni, then from Agni to Soma, from Soma to the Gandharva, and from the Gandharva again to Agni. The relation between this Gandharva and Soma is made known elsewhere. The story of Soma giving the goddess Vāk to the Gandharva is told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa as follows.

> सोमो वै राजा गन्धर्वेष्वासीत्तं देवाश्च ऋषयश्चाभ्यध्यायन्कथमयमस्मान्सोमो राजागच्छेदिति सा वागब्रवीत्स्त्रीकामा वै गन्धर्वा मय्येव स्त्रिया भूतया पणध्वमिति नेति देवा अब्रुवन्कथं वयं त्वदृते स्यामेति साब्रवीत्क्रीणेत्येव [?] यर्हि वाव वो मयार्थो भविता तर्ह्येव वोऽहं पुनरागन्तास्मीति तथेति तया महानग्न्या भूतया सोमं राजानमक्रीणन् ।

> *somo vai rājā gandharveṣvāsīttaṃ devāśca ṛṣayaścābhyadhyāyankathamayamasmānsomo rājāgacchediti sā vāgabravītstrīkāmā vai gandharvā mayyeva striyā bhūtayā paṇadhvamiti neti devā abruvankathaṃ vayaṃ tvadṛte syāmeti sābravītkrīṇetyeva [?] yarhi vāva vo mayārtho bhavitā tarhyeva vo 'haṃ punarāgantāsmīti tatheti tayā mahānagnyā bhūtayā somaṃ rājānamakrīṇan |*

(Ai. Brā. 3-2 [?].) *(Note: the line is broken after* कथमय- *as printed; the word क्रीणेत्येव is read with doubt, "यर्हि वाव" as printed.)*

Soma the king was among the Gandharvas. The gods and the ṛṣis, too, were considering how they might get him. Then the goddess Vāk, knowing the Gandharvas' passion for women, declared that she herself would become a beautiful woman and could be offered to the Gandharvas and Soma obtained. The gods were unwilling to let her go. Then, when she was desired by them again, she told them she would join them again at their need; and when she gave this assurance, the gods changed her into a naked woman, handed her to the Gandharvas and got Soma — so the story goes.

### Printed p. 33  (PDF 51)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 1".)* Which is this world of the Gandharvas, and what is meant by saying that Sūryā reached this world in the form of Vāk — this too is explained in Sūkta 10-85. The relation of this Sūryā and the Gandharva is described by the scholar Eggeling thus:

> *(English as printed)* The Rigvedic Gandharva was primarily wedded to the hypercosmic Sūryā [printed in Kannada script] — the original immortal abode of Soma — and the wedding of king Soma who was derived from the Gandharva to Sūryā — in other words, the return of the moon to the hypercosmic sphere of the nocturnal Sun — is the happy ending of the Gandharva's drama so tragically started. Soma's dying is not a death, for he is actually re-born through his union with Sūryā.

Thus, as explained above, Sūryā is spoken of now as wife of Soma, now as wife of the Gandharva, and at times as wife of Sūrya. The Aśvin deities are also said to be Sūryā, the moon and so on [?]. In the present ṛk, in "sūryāṃ vahatuṃ" the Aśvin deities are described as seating Sūryā in their three-wheeled chariot.

**अप्सु जातः (*apsu jātāḥ*)** — in the present ṛk, the word *ap* is explained as "sacrificial work". Sāyaṇa, on the authority of the Nirukta sentence "अपः इत्यन्तरिक्षनाम" (Ni. 2-10 [?]), explains *apsu* as "in the antarikṣa" in 1-95-2 [?] and similar places; in 1-104-6 [?] and similar ṛks he explains *abdevatā* the same way. In the ṛk 1-163-4 [?], where *apsu trite* occurs, he says, "because water gives life, the earth too is denoted by the word *ap*", giving the sense "earth". Moreover the word is read among the 26 [?] names of work (karman): *apaḥ*, *apnaḥ* and so on. In the present ṛk, the meaning is "sacrificial work".

**ककुहाः (*kakuhāḥ*)** — the word *kakuha* is read among the names of "great" in the Nirukta (Ni. 3-13 [?]). In the present ṛk the meaning is "worthy-of-worship praises".

**॥ Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā — grammar page, noted briefly (Pā. numerals in small type: `[?]` unless clear).** *śriye* (root *śriñ sevāyām*; *kvip* by "Uṇ. sū. 2-25 [?]", lengthening, dative singular in another form; udātta on the case-ending by *sāvekācas tṛtīyādiḥ*, Pā. 6-1-168 [?]). *iṣukṛtā iva* (root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*, *kvip*; *tuk* by *hrasvasya piti kṛti tuk*, Pā. 6-1-71 [?]; *kṛdutarapadaprakṛtisvara*; dual *ā* by *supāṃ suluk*). *vahatum* (root *vaha prāpaṇe*; *tumun*, with *aḍāgama*; ending-accent).

### Printed p. 34  (PDF 52)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 184".)* *(Grammar page of Ṛk 3, continued.)* **सूर्यायाः (*sūryāyāḥ*)** — *sūryasya iyaṃ sūryā*; by *sūryā-devatāyāṃ cāp vācyaḥ* [as read; Pā. 4-1-48-2 [?]] the *ṭāp* suffix, the sense being that of a deity; genitive in the object sense by *kartṛkarmaṇoḥ kṛti* (Pā. 2-3-65 [?]). **वच्यन्ते (*vacyante*)** — root *brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci*, *laṭ* in the passive; *yak* by *sārvadhātuke yak* (Pā. 3-1-67 [?]); *vacādeśa* for *brū* by *bruvo vaciḥ* (Pā. 2-4-53 [?]); *saṃprasāraṇa* of *va* to *u* by *vacisvapiyajādīnām kiti* (Pā. 6-1-15 [?]); no *pūrvarūpa* by *vā chandasi* (Pā. 6-1-106 [?]); *yaṇ* for *u* by *iko yaṇaci*; no *nighāta* accent as it begins a pāda; the *yak* accent remains. **जूर्णा इव (*jūrṇā iva*)** — root *jyuṣ vayohānau* [as read], used in the sense of praise; *kta*; no *iḍ* by *śryukaḥ kiti* (Pā. 7-2-11 [?]); *bahulaṃ chandasi* gives *utva*; accent on the ending; lengthening by *halica* (Pā. 8-2-77 [?]). **रदाभ्यां निष्ठातः (*radābhyāṃ niṣṭhātaḥ*)** (Pā. 8-2-42 [?]) — *natva* after *ra*; *ṇatva* after *ṣ* by the sūtra; neuter plural *śeḥ chandasi bahulam* (Pā. 6-1-70 [?]) with loss of *śi*.

## Sūkta 184, Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अस्मे सा वां माध्वी रातिरस्तु स्तोमं हिनोतं मान्यस्य कारोः ।
> अनु यद्वां श्रवस्या सुदानू सुवीर्याय चर्षणयो मदन्ति ॥ ४ ॥

> *asme sā vāṃ mādhvī rātirastu stomaṃ hinotaṃ mānyasya kāroḥ |*
> *anu yadvāṃ śravasyā sudānū suvīryāya carṣaṇayo madanti ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अस्मे इति । सा । वाम् । माध्वी इति । रातिः । अस्तु । स्तोमम् । हिनोतम् । मान्यस्य । कारोः ।

> *asme iti | sā | vām | mādhvī iti | rātiḥ | astu | stomam | hinotam | mānyasya | kāroḥ |*

### Printed p. 35  (PDF 53)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 1".)*

> अनु । यत् । वाम् । श्रवस्या । सुदानू इति सुऽदानू । सुऽवीर्याय । चर्षणयः । मदन्ति ॥ ४ ॥

> *anu | yat | vām | śravasyā | sudānū iti su 'dānū | su 'vīryāya | carṣaṇayaḥ | madanti ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed)*

*Gist:* May the well-known gift of you two Aśvins, the honey-vessel bearers, be ours; gratify the praise of the revered poet Agastya; men, for glory and heroic strength, take delight after you.

> हे माध्वी मधुपूर्णपात्रयुक्तावश्विनौ वां युवयोः सम्बन्धिनी सा प्रसिद्धा रातिर्दानमस्मे अस्माकमस्तु भवतु । तदर्थं मान्यस्य मननीयस्य कारोः स्तोतुरगस्त्यस्य स्तोमं स्तुतिं हिनोतम् । प्रीणयतम् । हे सुदानू शोभनफलदानौ वां युवां श्रवस्या कीर्तीरन्नस्य वेच्छयो [?] यस्मात्सुवीर्याय यजमानाय शोभनबलाय वा चर्षणयो मनुष्या ऋत्विग्रूपा अनु मदन्ति । अनुक्रमेण माद्यन्ति युवाभ्यां सह स्वयं वा ॥

**Pratipadārtha.** *sudānū* — O Aśvin deities, who give good fruits; *yat* — for which reason; *carṣaṇayaḥ* — men in the form of ṛtvijs; *suvīryāya* — (for the sacrificer, or) for excellent fruit; *śravasyā* — also by desire for food; *vām* — both of you; *anu madanti* — they gratify in order; *mānyasya* — of the honoured one; *kāroḥ* — of the praiser; *agastya's*; *stomam* — the praise; *hinotam* — hear and be gratified; *mādhvī* — O Aśvin deities accompanied by a vessel full of honey; *vām* — coming from you; *sā* — the famed; *rātiḥ* — gift; *asme* — to us; *astu* — be.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Aśvin deities, who give good fruits: because men in the form of ṛtvijs gratify you both in order, for the sake of excellent fruit and out of desire for food, hear the praise of Agastya — honoured, and a praiser — and be gratified. O Aśvins, accompanied by a vessel full of honey, may that famed gift given by you be ours.

**English Translation (as printed):** Receivers of ihe [sic] oblation, may your liberality be displayed towards us : be pleased with the hymn of the venerable author, so that men may honour the institutor of the ceremony, as (they honour) you, liberal donors, for the sake of renown.

### Printed p. 36  (PDF 54)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 184".)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**सुदानू (*sudānū*)** — *śobhanaphaladānau*: the quality of the Aśvins as givers of auspicious fruits is praised. The word *dānu* is used in many places in the sense of "juice" (*rasa*). *sudānavaḥ* can mean "filled with juice" or "givers of juice"; when this word is used as an epithet of the Maruts, "givers of juice" means those who send down excellent rain-water. For example,

> पिन्वन्त्यपो मरुतः सुदानवः पयो घृतवद्विदथेष्वाभुवः ।

> *pinvantyapo marutaḥ sudānavaḥ payo ghṛtavadvidatheṣvābhuvaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-64-6 [?]) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The bountiful Maruts swell the waters, the milk like ghee, present at the rites.")

— and many similar places it gives the above sense as an epithet of the Maruts. Generous giving may, besides, be a quality not only of gods but of sacrificers.

> इषं पृञ्चन्ता सुकृते सुदानव आ बर्हिः सीदतं नरा ।

> *iṣaṃ pṛñcantā sukṛte sudānava ā barhiḥ sīdataṃ narā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-47-8 [?]) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Mingling nourishment for the pious, O bountiful ones, sit on the barhis, O heroes.")

> सेदग्ने अस्तु सुभगः सुदानुर्यस्त्वा नित्येन हविषा य उक्थैः ।

> *sedagne astu subhagaḥ sudānuryastvā nityena haviṣā ya ukthaiḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-4-7 [?]) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "He, Agni, would be fortunate and bountiful, who [serves] you with regular oblation and with praises.")

— in such ṛks it is an epithet of sacrificers, as excellent givers. In 1-8?-43-2 [?] and similar ṛks the word *dānu* may also mean Soma-juice. Further,

> उत्तरा सूरधरः पुत्र आसीद्दानुः शये सहवत्सा न धेनुः ।

> *uttarā sūradharaḥ putra āsīddānuḥ śaye sahavatsā na dhenuḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-32-9 [?]) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The mother was above, the son below; Dānu lay like a cow with her calf.")

— in such ṛks the word *dānu* means the demoness (Asura-woman), mother of Vṛtra. The special sense of this word, the derivation of *jīradānu* and its special usages have been given earlier.

**चर्षणयः (*carṣaṇayaḥ*)** — in explaining the word *carṣaṇī* in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-109-5 [?], Sāyaṇa has given the sense सर्वस्य द्रष्टारौ इन्द्राग्नी (*sarvasya draṣṭārau indrāgnī*). Skandasvāmin too gave this sense first and then (cited) "मनुष्यनाम वा चर्षणीशब्दः (Ni. 3-2 [?]) मनुष्याकारौ वा [?] द्रष्टारौ [?] वा सर्वार्थानाम्"; since the word *carṣaṇi* is read among the names of men, the sense "those who look upon all, in human form" is given. Again, in 1-109-6 [?], Sāyaṇa has explained the word *carṣaṇi* simply as "men".

### Printed p. 37  (PDF 55)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 1".)* The scholar Monier Williams states that it is derived from the root *kṛṣ*; Griffith, from the root *car*. Their discussion has been given in detail in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā Part 2 and in page 4 [?].

**मान्यस्य (*mānyasya*)** — the special meaning of this word has been explained concisely in the 12th [?] volume of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā (p. 725). There, on the word in ṛk 1-165-15 [?], Sāyaṇa explained "worthy of worship"; and it was used as an epithet of Agastya. In the Bṛhaddevatā, in telling the order of Agastya's origin, it is said:

> मानेन सम्मितो यस्मात् तस्मान्मान्य इहोच्यते ।
> यद्वा कुम्भादृषिर्जातः कुम्भेनापि हि मीयते ॥

> *mānena sammito yasmāt tasmānmānya ihocyate |*
> *yadvā kumbhādṛṣirjātaḥ kumbhenāpi hi mīyate ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 5-153 [?]) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Because he is measured [*sammita*] by the *māna* [measure], therefore he is here called *mānya*; or because the ṛṣi was born from a jar [*kumbha*], and is measured with a jar.")

It is explained that, because he is worthy of worship, or because he was born in the jar (*kumbha*) which shows the type of *māna* (measure), that is, in the *māna* in the form of a jar, the name *mānya* has become famed for Agastya. The epithets *māndāryasya* and *mānyasya* of Agastya occur in many places. The scholar Max Müller, in explaining the ṛk 1-165-15 [?], says:

*(English as printed, continuing on the next page)* — "I translate *mānya*, the son of *māna*, because the poet is so called in I-189-8 [as printed] is in all probability the same as our *māndārya*, *mānya*. But it may also be *mānya*, descendant of *māndāri*." (S. B. E. XXXII. P. 206) *(Kannada-script words in the English are given here in Devanagari; the printed sentence is incomplete as it stands: "…is so called in I-189-8 is in all probability…", sic.)*

The word *māna*, as a proper name, is the name of an ancestor, say the English scholars. For example, Keith has said:

> *(English as printed)* "*Māna* is the name of man occuring [sic] in several passages of the Rig-veda. In one place, express mention is made of his son (*sūnu*) by whom *Agastya* must have been meant. In another passage, apparently the same meaning applies to *Māna* — ie. *Agastya* as *Māna*." [Index to Vedic names and subjects by Madconell & Keith. Vol. II. p. 152.]

That is,

> अवोचाम निवचनान्यस्मिन्मानस्य सूनुः सहसाने अग्नौ ।
> वयं सहस्रमृषिभिः सनेम विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुम् ॥

> *avocāma nivacanānyasminmānasya sūnuḥ sahasāne agnau |*
> *vayaṃ sahasramṛṣibhiḥ sanema vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-189-8.) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "We have spoken our words in this [fire], the son of Māna, in the mighty Agni; may we win a thousand with the ṛṣis, may we find strength, a way, a long-lived giver.") *(The Special Topics of Ṛk 4 continue on the next page.)*

### Printed p. 38  (PDF 56)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 184".)* *(Special Topics of Ṛk 4 continued.)* In the ṛk 1-189-8 [as printed] the words *mānasya sūnuḥ* mean, in the opinion of the English scholars, Agastya, the son of the ṛṣi named Māna. But Sāyaṇa, in explaining this word in that very ṛk, has given the following commentary:

> मानस्य सूनुः; मीयत इति मानः मन्त्रः । तस्य सूनुः अग्निः मन्त्रेणोत्पाद्यमानत्वात् । मानस्य सूनौ अग्नौ ॥

> *mānasya sūnuḥ; mīyata iti mānaḥ mantraḥ | tasya sūnuḥ agniḥ mantreṇotpādyamānatvāt | mānasya sūnau agnau ‖*

(Ṛ. Bhā. 1-189-8) — that is, *māna* means a mantra; its son is Agni; therefore *mānasya sūnuḥ* means "Agni", so he has explained. Similarly in

> सत्रे ह जाताविषिता नमोभिः कुम्भे रेतः सिषिचतुः समानम् ।
> ततो ह मान उदियाय मध्यात्ततो जातमृषिमाहुर्वसिष्ठम् ॥

> *satre ha jātāviṣitā namobhiḥ kumbhe retaḥ siṣicatuḥ samānam |*
> *tato ha māna udiyāya madhyāttato jātamṛṣimāhurvasiṣṭham ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-33-13) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "In the sacrificial session, the two, urged on with homage, poured their seed together into the jar; then *Māna* arose from the middle; from there they say the ṛṣi Vasiṣṭha was born.") — although the sense there too is Agastya together with Vasiṣṭha, Sāyaṇa has not stated that *māna* is a proper name (*aṅkitanāma*). Hence, where the word *mānyasya* occurs, what the English scholars explain and what Sāyaṇa explains are bound to differ. In the present ṛk too, the sense is either Agastya the son of Māna, or Agastya the esteemed and honoured one.

**कारोः (*kāroḥ*)** — Sāyaṇa: स्तोतुः अगस्त्यस्य (*stotuḥ agastyasya*) — "of Agastya, the praiser". The Nirukta-kāras have read the word *kāru* among the names of hymn (stotra) (Ni. 3-19). The author of the Bṛhaddevatā has used this word in the sense of poets, ṛṣis of subtle vision:

> अग्नेः[?] सप्त योनि सूक्तानि पञ्च नामानि कारवः ।
> षड्विंशतिस्तथेन्द्रस्य प्राहुः सूर्यस्य सप्त च ॥

> *agneḥ[?] sapta yoni sūktāni pañca nāmāni kāravaḥ |*
> *ṣaḍviṃśatistathendrasya prāhuḥ sūryasya sapta ca ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 2-22) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "…for Agni seven … hymns; five names; the *kāru*s; and for Indra twenty-six, they say, and for Sūrya seven.")

> पृथक्त्तेन [?] समास्तत्र [?] यज्ञे यज्ञस्यते [?] नृभिः ।
> स्तवन्त्याप्रेषु तेनेमं नराशंसं तु कारवः ॥

> *pṛthakttena [?] samāstatra [?] yajñe yajñasyate [?] nṛbhiḥ |*
> *stavantyāpreṣu tenemaṃ narāśaṃsaṃ tu kāravaḥ ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 2-28) *(Lines 1–2 of this verse are transcribed letter by letter from print and are doubtful; no gloss given.)*

In such sentences "the *kāru*s praise" is used as a word equivalent to "poets" (*kavi*). In the Ṛksaṃhitā too:

> प्रदक्षिणिदभि [sic?] गृणन्ति कारवो वयो वदन्त ऋतुथा शकुन्तयः ।

> *pradakṣiṇidabhi [sic?] gṛṇanti kāravo vayo vadanta ṛtuthā śakuntayaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-43-1) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The poets praise [him] around to the right; birds speak, each in its season.") — in these and other ṛks the use of this word in the sense of "poet" has been explained at length earlier.

### Printed p. 40  (PDF 58)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 184".)*

## Sūkta 184, Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> एष वां स्तोमो अश्विनावकारि मानेभिर्मघवाना सुवृक्ति ।
> यातं वर्तिस्तनयाय त्मने चागस्त्ये नासत्या मदन्ता ॥ ५ ॥

> *eṣa vāṃ stomo aśvināvakāri mānebhirmaghavānā suvṛkti |*
> *yātaṃ vartistanayāya tmane cāgastye nāsatyā madantā ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> एषः । वाम् । स्तोमः । अश्विना । अकारि । मानेभिः । मघवाना । सुवृक्ति । यातम् । वर्तिः । तनयाय । त्मने । च । अगस्त्ये । नासत्या । मदन्ता ॥ ५ ॥

> *eṣaḥ | vām | stomaḥ | aśvinā | akāri | mānebhiḥ | maghavānā | suvṛkti | yātam | vartiḥ | tanayāya | tmane | ca | agastye | nāsatyā | madantā ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed)*

*Gist:* O Aśvins, with oblations, this sin-removing hymn has been made for you; come to Agastya's sacrificial house for offspring and for his own good.

> हे अश्विनौ हे मघवाना हविर्लक्षणान्नवन्तौ वां युवाभ्यामेष स्तोमः स्तोत्रं सुवृक्ति सुष्ठु पापवर्जनं यथा भवति तथा यद्वा सुसमाप्त्यकारि । कृतः । कीदृशोऽयं । मानेभिर्मान्यैर्हविष्प्रदानरूपैः सहितः । हे नासत्यासत्यरहितौ युवामगस्त्य एतन्नाम्नि महर्षौ मयि मदन्तौ माद्यन्तौ सन्तौ वर्तिर्गृहं यज्ञसम्बन्धि यातं । प्राप्नुतं । किमर्थं । तनयाय पुत्रादिलाभाय त्मने आत्मने च हिताय ॥

**Pratipadārtha.** *maghavānā* — endowed with food in the form of oblations; *aśvinau* — O Aśvin deities; *vām* — for you; *mānebhiḥ* — accompanied by the giving of oblations; *suvṛkti* — having the power to remove sin (or: complete); *eṣaḥ stomaḥ* — this hymn; *akāri* — has been made; *nāsatyā* — O Aśvin deities free from untruth (you both); *agastye* — in me, famed by the name Agastya (by my hymn); *madantā* — having obtained satisfaction; *tanayāya* — for the gain of sons and so on; *tmane ca* — and for one's own good; *vartiḥ* — to the sacrificial house; *yātam* — come.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Aśvin deities, endowed with food in the form of oblations: this hymn, accompanied by the giving of oblations, with power to remove sin and complete, has been made for you. O Aśvin deities free from untruth, satisfied by my hymn, famed by the name Agastya, come also to my sacrificial house for the gain of sons and so on and for my own good.

---

### Printed p. 41  (PDF 59)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 1".)*

**English Translation (as printed; the heading is printed "Trnslation" [sic]):** Ashwins, possessors of wealth, this sin-removing hymn has been addressed to you, together with respectful (oblations): Nasatyas, be favourable to Agastya ; come to his dwelling for (conferring on him) progeny, and for his own (good).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**मघवाना (*maghavānā*)** — for this epithet Sāyaṇa has explained हविर्लक्षणान्नयुक्तौ (*havirlakṣaṇānnayuktau*) — "(the Aśvins) endowed with food in the form of oblations". Although the epithet *maghavān* is ordinarily of Indra, this epithet is used here and there in the Ṛksaṃhitā also when describing the qualities of other deities. Or, since the word *magha* is read among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9), here it may be said to be wealth in the form of food. The Nirukta-kāra, having given the derivation of the word *magha* —

> मघमिति धननामधेयं मंहतेर्दानकर्मणः ।

> *maghamiti dhananāmadheyaṃ maṃhaterdānakarmaṇaḥ |*

— explained the sense of the word *maghonī* (Ni. 1-7 [?]). In the same way, the explanation of the epithet *maghavānā* may be given in the present ṛk too. Or:

*maghavānā* — even if one explains it as "the Aśvin deities accompanied by Viṣṇu", it is not wrong. For, in the Śatapatha-brāhmaṇa and others the identity of Viṣṇu and *makha* (sacrifice, मख (*makha*)) has been stated, as was shown earlier (Śa. Brā. 14-11-13 [as read]); and the companionship of the Aśvin deities with Viṣṇu, in the form of *makha*, is well known. This too was shown earlier, in

> तमस्य राजा वरुणस्तमश्विना क्रतुं सचन्ते मारुतस्य वेधसः ।
> धधार [sic?] दक्षमुत्तममहर्विदं व्रजं च विष्णुः सखिवा अपोर्णुते ॥

> *tamasya rājā varuṇastamaśvinā kratuṃ sacante mārutasya vedhasaḥ |*
> *dhadhāra [sic?] dakṣamuttamamaharvidaṃ vrajaṃ ca viṣṇuḥ sakhivā aporṇute ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-15[7?]-4 [?]) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Him [Agni?], King Varuṇa and the Aśvins attend, [his] will, of the wise Maruts; Viṣṇu, the friend, upheld the highest skill, day-knowing, and opens the stall.") — when explaining the special topics of that ṛk (Ṛgveda Saṃhitā Part 11, pp. 656–657, as printed). Besides, the Ṛksaṃhitā too describes the same companionship thus:

> यदिन्द्रेण सरथं याथो अश्विना यद्वा वायुना भवथः समोकसा ।
> यदादित्येभिरृभुभिः सजोषसा यद्वा विष्णोर्विक्रमणेषु तिष्ठथः ॥

> *yadindreṇa sarathaṃ yātho aśvinā yadvā vāyunā bhavathaḥ samokasā |*
> *yadādityebhirṛbhubhiḥ sajoṣasā yadvā viṣṇorvikramaṇeṣu tiṣṭhathaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-9-12) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Whether you, Aśvins, drive in one chariot with Indra, or are of one dwelling with Vāyu, or in unison with the Ādityas and Ṛbhus, or stand in Viṣṇu's strides.")

---

### Printed p. 42  (PDF 60)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 184".)* — in these and other ṛks too the companionship of the Aśvin deities with Viṣṇu is shown. For this reason *maghavānā* may also be explained as "the Aśvins accompanied by Viṣṇu"; but in the present context it appears more fitting to the passage to give the sense stated by Sāyaṇa, "endowed with the wealth of food in the form of oblations".

**सुवृक्ति (*suvṛkti*)** — Sāyaṇa: सुष्ठु पापवर्जनं यथा भवति तथा । यद्वा । सुसमाप्ति (*suṣṭhu pāpavarjanaṃ yathā bhavati tathā | yadvā | susamāpti*) — "completely freed from sin, or having a pure completion". This word is an epithet of the word *stoma*, and the epithet is used here and there in one sense or another. The Nirukta-kāra, citing

> इयं शुष्मेभिर्बिसखा इवारुजत्सानु गिरीणां तविषेभिरूर्मिभिः ।
> पारावतघ्नीमवसे सुवृक्तिभिः सरस्वतीमा [वि?]वासेम धीतिभिः ॥

> *iyaṃ śuṣmebhirbisakhā ivārujatsānu girīṇāṃ taviṣebhirūrmibhiḥ |*
> *pārāvataghnīmavase suvṛktibhiḥ sarasvatīmā [vi?]vāsema dhītibhiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-61-2) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "She, with her powerful waves, broke the ridge of the mountains as one digging lotus-stalks; to Sarasvatī, destroyer of the distant, may we come with attentions, for help, with excellent praises.") explained the word *suvṛktibhiḥ* there as सुप्रवृत्ताभिः शोभनाभिः स्तुतिभिः (*supravṛttābhiḥ śobhanābhiḥ stutibhiḥ*), "excellent praises". The word *vṛkti* is also used elsewhere in the sense of "abandoning" (*varjana*). For example:

> कुविदङ्ग यवमन्तो यवं चिद्यथा दान्त्यनुपूर्वं वियूय ।
> इहेहैषां कृणुहि भोजनानि ये बर्हिषो नमोवृक्तिं न जग्मुः ॥

> *kuvidaṅga yavamanto yavaṃ cidyathā dāntyanupūrvaṃ viyūya |*
> *ihehaiṣāṃ kṛṇuhi bhojanāni ye barhiṣo namovṛktiṃ na jagmuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-131-2) — here *namovṛktim* is explained: "of *namas*, of the food in the form of oblation, or of the hymn in the form of homage, the abandonment, the doing; they did not go" ("*namaso havirlakṣaṇasyānnasya namaskārātmakasya stotrasya vā varjanaṃ karaṇaṃ na jagmuḥ*"). It is prayed to Indra: "they have not abandoned the praise in the form of homage". Here the word *vṛkti* is used in the sense of abandonment; but the use of this word in the sense of praise is by far more frequent. For example:

> अस्मा इदु त्यमुपमं स्वर्षां भराम्याङ्गूषमास्येन ।
> मंहिष्ठमच्छोक्तिभिर्मतीनां सुवृक्तिभिः सूरिं वावृधध्यै ॥

> *asmā idu tyamupamaṃ svarṣāṃ bharāmyāṅgūṣamāsyena |*
> *maṃhiṣṭhamacchoktibhirmatīnāṃ suvṛktibhiḥ sūriṃ vāvṛdhadhyai ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-61-3) — in these and all such places the sense is "excellent praise".

**वर्तिः (*vartiḥ*)** — वर्तनहेतुभूतं गृहम् (*vartanahetubhūtaṃ gṛham*) — "a house, serving as the support for dwelling": Sāyaṇa explains this word so wherever it occurs. But Skandasvāmin has in general explained it everywhere as "the well-known path". For example,

---

### Printed p. 43  (PDF 61)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 1".)*

> त्रिर्वर्तिर्यातं त्रिरनुव्रते जने त्रिः सुप्राव्ये त्रेधेव शिक्षतम् ।
> त्रिर्नान्द्यं वहतमश्विना युवं त्रिः पृक्षो अस्मे अक्षरेव पिन्वतम् ॥

> *trirvartiryātaṃ triranuvrate jane triḥ suprāvye tredheva śikṣatam |*
> *trirnāndyaṃ vahatamaśvinā yuvaṃ triḥ pṛkṣo asme akṣareva pinvatam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-34-4) — in these and all such ṛks Sāyaṇa explains *vartiḥ* as "house", Skandasvāmin as "path". It is one special point that all the sūktas containing ṛks with the word *vartiḥ* as in *trirvartiḥ*, *aśvinā vartiḥ*, such as 1-116-18 [?]; 1-112-2 [?]; 1-119-4, are addressed to the Aśvin deities. But,

> इषं दुहन्त्सुदुघां विश्वधायसं यज्ञप्रियो यजमानाय सुक्रतो ।
> अग्ने घृतस्नुस्त्रिर्ऋतानि [?] दीद्यद्वर्तिर्यज्ञं परियन्सक्रतोयसे [?] ॥

> *iṣaṃ duhantsudughāṃ viśvadhāyasaṃ yajñapriyo yajamānāya sukrato |*
> *agne ghṛtasnustrirṛtāni [?] dīdyadvartiryajñaṃ pariyansakratoyase [?] ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-122-6) — only in this ṛk, which is addressed to Agni, is the word used in a mantra of that kind; here the sense "sacrificial house" has been given. Sāyaṇa too has in some places explained this word as "path". For example,

> यो ह स्य वां रथिरा वस्त उस्रा रथो युजानः परियाति वर्तिः ।
> तेन नः शंयोरुषसो व्युष्टौ न्यश्विना वहतं यज्ञे अस्मिन् ॥

> *yo ha sya vāṃ rathirā vasta usrā ratho yujānaḥ pariyāti vartiḥ |*
> *tena naḥ śaṃyoruṣaso vyuṣṭau nyaśvinā vahataṃ yajñe asmin ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-69-5) — here *vartiḥ* is explained as "path". This is a mantra of prayer addressed to the Aśvin deities themselves. In the present ṛk the sense is "house"; ordinarily it is a synonym of "sacrificial house".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page of Ṛk 5, begun; continues on the next page) — *akāri* (root *ḍukṛñ karaṇe*, *luṅ* passive 3rd singular; *ati-ṅanta* *nighāta* accent); *mānebhiḥ* (root *man jñāne*, *ghañ*; *upadhā*-vṛddhi; initial udātta; by *bahulaṃ chandasi* the *ais* for *bhis* is optional, hence not here); *maghavānā* (*vanip* by *chandasīvanipau*, in the sense of possession; vocative dual, *ā*-substitution by *supāṃ sulug*; *āmantrita* *nighāta*); *suvṛkti* (root *vṛjī varjane*, *ktin* in the sense of the action; *kutva* of the *j* by *coḥ kuḥ*; *car* by *khari ca*; accent on the last member of the compound by the *nañ-subhyām* sūtra).

## Sūkta 184, Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अतारिष्म तमसस्पारमस्य प्रति वां स्तोमो अश्विनावधायि ।
> एह यातं पथिभिर्देवयान्यैर्विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुम् ॥ ६ ॥

> *atāriṣma tamasaspāramasya prati vāṃ stomo aśvināvadhāyi |*
> *eha yātaṃ pathibhirdevayānyairvidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānum ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अतारिष्म । तमसः । पारम् । अस्य । प्रति । वाम् । स्तोमः । अश्विनौ । अधायि ।
> आ । इह । यातम् । पथिऽभिः । देवयान्यैः । विद्याम । इषम् । वृजनम् । जीरऽदानुम् ॥ ६ ॥

> *atāriṣma | tamasaḥ | pāram | asya | prati | vām | stomaḥ | aśvinau | adhāyi |*
> *ā | iha | yātam | pathi 'bhiḥ | devayānyaiḥ | vidyāma | iṣam | vṛjanam | jīra 'dānum ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed)*

*Gist:* The sixth ṛk, *atāriṣma*, "has been explained" (referring back to its earlier occurrence).

> अतारिष्मेति षष्ठी व्याख्याता ॥

**Pratipadārtha.** *aśvinau* — O Aśvin deities; *asya tamasaḥ* — of this misery (which obstructs prosperity); *pāram* — the end; *atāriṣma* — (by your grace) we have crossed; *vāṃ prati* — addressed to you; *stomaḥ* — the praise; *adhāyi* — has been made (indicated) *(the Pratipadārtha continues on the next page)*.

### Printed p. 45  (PDF 63)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 1").*

(Pratipadārtha, concluded:) *devayānyaiḥ pathibhiḥ* — by paths trodden by the gods; *iha* — to this sacrifice; *ā yātam* — come; (*vayam* — we); *iṣam* — food; *vṛjanam* — strength; *jīradānum* — long life; *vidyāma* — may we obtain.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Aśvin deities, by your grace we have crossed the end of this misery that is an obstacle to prosperity. This praise has been addressed to you. Come to this sacrifice by the paths the gods travel. May we obtain food, strength and long life.

**English Translation (as printed):** (Through your aid), Ashwins, we cross over the limit of darkness : to you this (our hymn) has been addressed : come hither by the path traversed by the gods, that we may obtain food, strength, and long life.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**देवयान्यैः पथिभिः (*devayānyaiḥ pathibhiḥ*)** — Sāyaṇa: देवगन्तव्यैर्मार्गैः (*devagantavyairmārgaiḥ*): "by paths on which gods travel" — he has given the material sense. In the Upaniṣads the words *devayāna* and *pitṛyāna* have a technical meaning. But in many places in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā the word *devayāna* means only "the path on which the gods travel". In a few places alone a spiritual import, as described in the Upaniṣads, is also suggested.

In the Upaniṣads the words *devayāna* and *pitṛyāna* are well known as the two paths on which the soul, which is eternal, goes after a man's death, when his body has become ashes. Of the paths by which people go to experience the fruit of good works, one is *devayāna*, the other *pitṛyāna*: one is the path of the gods, the other the path of the fathers. Those who, having learned the *pañcāgni-vidyā*, hold faith in truth itself set out by the path of the gods and reach the Supreme Brahman. After their death the soul enters flame, and through it day, the bright fortnight, the northern course of the sun, the year, the sun, lightning; and through these, with the help of the non-human (*amānava*) person, they reach the Supreme Brahman — this is what the Upaniṣads describe.

As for those who please the world by sacrifice alone and by gifts and the like — that is, those who, not knowing the *pañcāgni-vidyā*, are devoted merely to good works — they travel after death by another path. After the body is burnt the soul joins the smoke, and then reaches night, and through it *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 46  (PDF 64)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 184".)* — Joining the dark fortnight and, through it, the southern course, then the world of the fathers and finally the world of the moon. That is their final station. There they fully enjoy the fruits proper to their good works, being with the fathers; and as soon as the effect of their works is exhausted they return to the earth by the same smoke path. This is the nature of the *devayāna* and *pitṛyāna* described in the Upaniṣads.

What we have to notice in the present context is whether all the ideas described in the Upaniṣads as above are suggested in full by the word *devayāna* used in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, or whether the meaning is merely the material one, "the path on which the gods travel". And likewise, for the word *pitṛyāna* as described in the Upaniṣads, the meaning is to be considered in the present context.

The word *devayāna* is used in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in all thirteen times. [1-72-7 [?]; 1-162-4 [?]; 1-183-6 [?], 1-184-6; 4-37-1 [?]; 5-43-6 [?]; 7-38-8 [?]; 7-76-2 [?]; 10-18-1 [?]; 10-51-2 [?]; 10-51-5 [?]; 10-98-11 [?]; 10-185-3 [?]] (as read; thirteen references are listed). In all these places Sāyaṇa has chiefly given only two meanings. By his explanation, the first is the path on which the sacrificers, human beings, go with their oblations to approach the gods; the second is the path on which the gods come to the earth to accept their oblations.

The word *pitṛyāna* is used in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā only once. In what context is that use?

> यं त्वा द्यावापृथिवी यं त्वापस्त्वष्टा यं त्वा सुजनिमा जजान ।
> पन्थामनु प्रविद्वान् पितृयाणं द्युमदग्ने समिधानो वि भाहि ॥

> *yaṃ tvā dyāvāpṛthivī yaṃ tvāpastvaṣṭā yaṃ tvā sujanimā jajāna |*
> *panthāmanu pravidvān pitṛyāṇaṃ dyumadagne samidhāno vi bhāhi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-2-2 [?]) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Whom heaven and earth, whom the waters, Tvaṣṭṛ, whom the good creator begot — knowing the path, the path of the fathers, shine forth brilliant, O Agni, kindled.") In this ṛk Agni, kindled — one who has been born of heaven-and-earth, the waters and the creator, and who knows fully the nature of the *pitṛyāṇa* — is prayed to shine forth. For this word in the third pāda Sāyaṇa explains "पितृयाणं पितरो येन मार्गेण गच्छन्ति तं" (*pitṛyāṇaṃ pitaro yena mārgeṇa gacchanti taṃ*): "the path by which the fathers travel".

## Sūkta 185 — *katarā pūrvā* (Anuvāka 24, sixth Sūkta; 11 ṛks)

### Printed p. 47  (PDF 65)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 1"; the Kannada half-title reads "ನೂರ ಎಂಭತ್ತೈದನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು", "the hundred-and-eighty-fifth sūkta".)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; Anukramaṇikā wording and viniyoga)*

*Gist:* *katarā pūrvā* is the sixth sūkta, of 11 ṛks, by Agastya, to Dyāvāpṛthivī, in *triṣṭubh*; used for the Dyāvāpṛthivī *nivid-dhāna* in the Vaiśvadeva śastra of the sixth day of the Abhiplava and in the Mahāvrata.

> कतरा पूर्वेत्येकादशर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तमागस्त्यं त्रैष्टुभम् । कतर्यैकादश द्यावापृथिवीयमित्यनुक्रान्तम् ॥ अभिप्लविके षष्ठेऽहनि वैश्वदेवशस्त्रे द्यावापृथिव्यनिविद्धानमिदम् । तृतीयस्येति खण्डे सूत्रितम् । कतरा पूर्वेषासानक्तेति वैश्वदेवम् । आश्व. 2-2 [?] इति ॥ महाव्रतेऽपि वैश्वदेवशस्त्र इदमेव द्यावापृथिव्यनिविद्धानम् । उत्तमादाभिप्लविकात्तृतीयसवनम् । ऐ. आ. 5-3-2 । इत्येतिदेशात् ॥

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta, *katarā pūrvā*, is the sixth sūkta in the twenty-fourth anuvāka. There are eleven ṛks in it. Agastya is the ṛṣi; Dyāvāpṛthivī (Heaven-and-Earth) are the devatā; the metre is *triṣṭubh*. In the Anukramaṇikā it is stated "*katarā*, eleven, to Dyāvāpṛthivī". When the Vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras are recited on the sixth day of the Abhiplava sacrifice, the application of this sūkta is for the *nivid-dhāna* (praise of qualities) mantras of the Dyāvāpṛthivī deities, as explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra in the sūtra "*katarā pūrveṣāsānaktā iti vaiśvadevam*" in the section beginning *tṛtīyasya* (Āś. 2-2 [?]). And in the Mahāvrata, when the Vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras are recited, the application of this sūkta for the Dyāvāpṛthivī *nivid-dhāna* mantras is stated by the sentence *uttamādābhiplavikāttṛtīyasavanam* of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka (5-3-2).

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> कतरा पूर्वा कतरापरायोः कथा जाते कवयः को वि वेद ।
> विश्वं त्मना बिभृतो यद्ध नाम वि वर्तेते अहनी चक्रियेव ॥ १ ॥

> *katarā pūrvā katarāparāyoḥ kathā jāte kavayaḥ ko vi veda |*
> *viśvaṃ tmanā bibhṛto yaddha nāma vi vartete ahanī cakriyeva ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> कतरा । पूर्वा । कतरा । अपरा । आयोः । कथा । जाते इति । कवयः । कः । वि । वेद ।
> विश्वम् । त्मना । बिभृतः । यत् । ह । नाम । वि । वर्तेते इति । अहनी इति । चक्रिया इव ॥ १ ॥

> *katarā | pūrvā | katarā | aparā | āyoḥ | kathā | jāte iti | kavayaḥ | kaḥ | vi | veda |*
> *viśvam | tmanā | bibhṛtaḥ | yat | ha | nāma | vi | vartete iti | ahanī iti | cakriyā iva ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed)*

*Gist:* Which of heaven and earth is prior and which later, and by what cause were they born? Who knows? They themselves, unaided, uphold the whole universe; the two revolve like day and night on wheels.

> आयोरेनयोर्द्यावापृथिव्योर्मध्ये कतरा पूर्वा पूर्वमुत्पन्ना । कतरा वापरा पश्चाद्भाविनी । एवं पौर्वापर्यप्रश्नः । उभयोरविनाभावेन सहैव वर्तमानत्वादिति भावः । तथा कथा केन हेतुना जाते । किमनयोरुत्पादनमित्यर्थः । हे कवयः क्रान्तदर्शिनोऽतीन्द्रियज्ञाः यूयं वदत को वि वेद । पौर्वापर्यं कारणं च विशेषेण विविच्य वा जानाति । न केनापि ज्ञायत इत्यर्थः । अज्ञाने कारणमाह । यद्ध यस्मात्खलु हेतोर्नाम प्रसिद्धं विश्वं कृत्स्नमपि जगदविशेषेण त्मनात्मनैवान्यैरपेक्ष्यैव बिभृतः धारयतः । यद्वा । यद्ध नाम यत्किंचित्पदार्थजातमस्ति विश्वं तत्सर्वमात्मना बिभृतः । अनेन यत्कारणं ब्रूमस्तदप्याभ्यामेव भ्रियत इति कारणाभावः प्रतिपादितः । उत्तरेण पौर्वापर्यभाव उच्यते । अहनी एते द्यावापृथिव्यौ चक्रियेव चक्रयुक्ते इव वि वर्तेते । अत्र कतरा पूर्वा कतरापरैनयोरित्यादि निरुक्तं प्रष्टव्यम् । नि. 3-22 [?] ॥

**Pratipadārtha.** *āyoḥ* — in these two, heaven and earth; *katarā* — which one; *pūrvā* — was born first; *katarā* — which one; *aparā* — was born afterwards; *kathā* — by what material cause; *jāte* — these two were born; *kavayaḥ* — O far-seeing ṛṣis; *kaḥ* — who (himself) (continues on the next page).

### Printed p. 49  (PDF 67)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 2".)* — *vi veda* — has fully understood this truth; *yaddha* — the group of things that can be called their cause, whichever it is; (*tat*) *viśvam* — the whole world including all those things; *tmanā* — (without the aid of anything else, heaven and earth) by themselves; *bibhṛtaḥ* — they uphold; *ahanī* — (belonging to them) both day and night together; *cakriyā iva* — as if furnished with wheels; *vi vartete* — they go round in recurrence.

**Bhāvārtha.** Which of this heaven and earth was born first? Which was born afterwards? By what material cause were these two born? O far-seeing ṛṣis, who himself has fully understood this truth? Heaven and earth uphold by themselves, without the help of anything else, the whole world, including that group of things that can be called their cause; and both day and night, belonging to them, go round in recurrence, as if furnished with wheels.

**English Translation (as printed):** Which of these two, (Heaven and Earth), is prior, which posterior ? how were they engendered ? (declare), sages, who knows this ? Verily, you uphold the Universe of itself, and the days (and nights) revolve as if they had wheels.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

Stating the application of this sūkta (1-185), Sāyaṇa, in "*abhiplavike ṣaṣṭhe 'hani vaiśvadevaśastre dyāvāpṛthivyanividdhānam idam*" and "*mahāvrate 'pi vaiśvadevaśastre idam eva dyāvāpṛthivyanividdhānam*", has cited the Āśvalāyana sūtra (Āś. Śrau. 2-2 [?]) and shown that its recitation is prescribed both in the Vaiśvadeva-śastra of the Abhiplava and in that of the Mahāvrata. If the mantras praising Dyāvāpṛthivī are to be recited at the time of the rite called Abhiplava and at the time of the Mahāvrata, one must know what the nature of those two rites is, and what the importance of reciting these mantras at that time is.

When the prefix *abhi* is joined to the root *plu*, which has the sense of going, the meaning is "to leap across"; and its use in this sense is also common. Likewise, although the word *abhiplava* has a technical use connected with ritual, it gives this same purport, as the Śruti *(continues on the next page)*

---


### Printed p. 50  (PDF 68)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 185".)* — sentences themselves make known. Having learned in what way the derivation (*nirvacana*) of this word is given in the Brāhmaṇas and elsewhere, let us then examine what the form of this rite is.

> ते देवा एतमभिप्लवं समभरन् । तेनाभ्यप्लवन्त । तदभिप्लवस्याभिप्लवत्वं ।

> *te devā etamabhiplavaṃ samabharan | tenābhyaplavanta | tadabhiplavasyābhiplavatvaṃ |*

(Jaiminīya Brāhmaṇa II. 440. 3, as printed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The gods brought together this Abhiplava; by it they leapt across; that is the Abhiplava-ness of the Abhiplava.")

By these sentences the purport of the word *abhiplava* is made known in the Jaiminīya Brāhmaṇa. When the asuras belonging to the band called Paṇi carried off the cows, Indra sent the divine bitch called Saramā to search for those cows. That she found the asuras' place, held a conversation with them and afterwards reported the news to the gods — this matter is told elsewhere. In some places it is described that this same Saramā acted favourably to the gods, and in some other places that she acted out of a selfish view so as to be hostile to the gods: such is the opinion of some. In the present case, in the Jaiminīya Brāhmaṇa sentence cited above, it is said that by Saramā's help the gods crossed over their trouble, and since it was helpful to their crossing (*abhiplava*), they performed the Abhiplava sacrifice. Because it is said that by performing this sacrifice they crossed their calamity, it bears the name Abhiplava: thus its purport and its use are made known.

Likewise,

> त आदित्याः । चतुर्भिस्स्तोमैश्चतुर्भिः पृष्ठैर्लघुभिः सामभिः
> स्वर्गं लोकमभ्यप्लवन्त यदभ्यप्लवन्त तस्मादभिप्लवाः ।

> *ta ādityāḥ | caturbhisstomaiścaturbhiḥ pṛṣṭhairlaghubhiḥ sāmabhiḥ*
> *svargaṃ lokamabhyaplavanta yadabhyaplavanta tasmādabhiplavāḥ |*

(Śa. Brā. 12 2-2-10, as printed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Those Ādityas, by four stomas, four pṛṣṭhas, light sāmans, leapt across to the heaven-world; because they leapt across, therefore [they are] the Abhiplavas.")

On the days of the Abhiplava sacrifice the gods, by reciting four *pṛṣṭha*-sāmans, crossed to the heaven-world; because they crossed thus (*yadabhyaplavanta*), this rite got the name Abhiplava — a purport indicating the context of a story is stated. Showing that, besides this kind of derivation, there is another reason too for this name, another kind of meaning is stated:

> एतद्ध स्म वै तद्विद्वानाह पैङ्ग्यः । प्लवन्ते इव वाऽभिप्लवास्तिष्ठतीव पृष्ठ्यः
> इति प्लवत इव ह्ययमङ्गैस्तिष्ठतीवात्मनेति ।

> *etaddha sma vai tadvidvānāha paiṅgyaḥ | plavante iva vā 'bhiplavāstiṣṭhatīva pṛṣṭhyaḥ*
> *iti plavata iva hyayamaṅgaistiṣṭhatīvātmaneti |*

(Śa. Brā. 12-2-4-8) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Knowing this, Paiṅgya said: 'The Abhiplavas, as it were, float; the Pṛṣṭhya, as it were, stands' — for this [body] floats, as it were, with its limbs, and stands, as it were, with its trunk.")

Paiṅgya, the disciple of Yājñavalkya, knew the nature of the Abhiplava and of the Pṛṣṭhya. Knowing their secret he said: "Because it has a nature consisting of floating (*plavana*) it is Abhiplava, and because it has a stable nature it is Pṛṣṭhya — these are the names of these two rites (Abhiplava and Pṛṣṭhya)": this purport too is explained in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa. In sum, whether gods or men, this *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 51  (PDF 69)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 2".)* — rite: because by performing it they cross over calamity, the derivation has been stated so as to indicate its greatness. In the present sūkta too, in the prayer "द्यावा रक्षतं पृथिवी नो अभ्वात्" (*dyāvā rakṣataṃ pṛthivī no abhvāt*) there is the plea "protect us from great fear"; so if these mantras are recited at the time of the Abhiplava sacrifice one can cross out of calamity. This Abhiplava holds a principal place from the spiritual point of view too. It is a member (*aṅga*) of the sacrifice called "Gavāmayana". The "Gavāmayana" is of the nature of the year (*saṃvatsara*). Man (*puruṣa*) too is of the nature of the year. If the Abhiplava is a member of the Gavāmayana, which is of the nature of the year, it must also be a member of the principle of Puruṣa, which is of the nature of the year. Describing this very thing, the Śatapatha, in "पुरुषो वै संवत्सरः . . . . उरोऽभिप्लवः" (*puruṣo vai saṃvatsaraḥ . . . . uro'bhiplavaḥ*), gives its description thus: if the year itself reflects the principle of Puruṣa, then the Abhiplava is his chest, and so on (Śa. Brā 12-1-4-1). The principal means for crossing the ocean that is of the nature of the year (the ocean in the form of the *sattra*) is the Abhiplava: "प्रस्नेयोऽभिप्लवः" (*prasneyo'bhiplavaḥ*, as printed) (Śa. Brā. 12-2-1-1). Āruṇeya Śvetaketu, knowing this principle of the year, makes known the greatness of the Abhiplava:

> तदाहुः । कस्मादुभयतो ज्योतिषोऽभिप्लवा भवन्त्यन्यतो ज्योतिः पृष्ठ्य
> इतीमे वै लोका अभिप्लवा उभयतो ज्योतिषो वा इमे लोकाः ॥

> *tadāhuḥ | kasmādubhayato jyotiṣo 'bhiplavā bhavantyanyato jyotiḥ pṛṣṭhya*
> *itīme vai lokā abhiplavā ubhayato jyotiṣo vā ime lokāḥ ‖*

(Śa. Brā. 12-2-2-1) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "So they ask: why are the Abhiplavas lighted on both sides, the Pṛṣṭhya lighted on one side? These worlds are the Abhiplavas; and these worlds are lighted on both sides.")

The Abhiplava shines with light of both forms. These worlds themselves (heaven, earth and the mid-region) are the Abhiplavas. This Abhiplava shines both through the portion of the earth, by light in the form of the terrestrial Agni, and through the portion of the heavenly world, by light in the form of Āditya. "त आदित्याः स्वर्गं लोकमभ्यप्लवन्त" (*ta ādityāḥ svargaṃ lokamabhyaplavanta*) — by this very boat in the form of the Abhiplava the Ādityas (together with the Aṅgirases) reached the heavenly world: in this and many other ways the nature of the Abhiplava is described. Since heaven and earth themselves are of the form of the Abhiplava, the description and praise of heaven and earth at the time of this rite is natural. Moreover, stating the identity of the Jyotiṣṭoma and the others, which are members of the Abhiplava, with heaven and earth, the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa describes it thus:

> ज्योतिर्गौरायुरिति स्तोमेभिर्यन्त्ययं वै लोको ज्योतिरन्तरिक्षं
> गौरसौ लोक आयुः स एवैष उत्तरस्त्र्यहः ज्योतिर्गौरायुरिति त्रीण्यहानि
> गौरायुर्ज्योतिरिति त्रीणि । अयं वै लोको ज्योतिरसौ लोको
> ज्योतिस्ते एते ज्योतिषी उभयतः संलोकेते । तेनैतेनोभयतो
> ज्योतिषा षळहेन यन्ति तद्यदेतेनोभयतो ज्योतिषा षळहेन यन्त्य-
> नयोरेव तल्लोकयोरुभयतः प्रतितिष्ठन्तो यन्त्यस्मिंश्च लोकेऽ-
> मुष्मिंश्चोभयोः ॥

> *jyotirgaurāyuriti stomebhiryantyayaṃ vai loko jyotirantarikṣaṃ*
> *gaurasau loka āyuḥ sa evaiṣa uttarastryahaḥ jyotirgaurāyuriti trīṇyahāni*
> *gaurāyurjyotiriti trīṇi | ayaṃ vai loko jyotirasau loko*
> *jyotiste ete jyotiṣī ubhayataḥ saṃlokete | tenaitenobhayato*
> *jyotiṣā ṣaḷahena yanti tadyadetenobhayato jyotiṣā ṣaḷahena yantya-*
> *nayoreva tallokayorubhayataḥ pratitiṣṭhanto yantyasmiṃśca loke '-*
> *muṣmiṃścobhayoḥ ‖*

(Ai. Brā. 18-1) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "They go with the stomas *jyotiḥ, gauḥ, āyuḥ*: this world is *jyotis*, the mid-region *gauḥ*, yonder world *āyuḥ*; that same is the later three-day rite — *jyotiḥ, gauḥ, āyuḥ* three days, *gauḥ, āyuḥ, jyotiḥ* three. This world is light, yonder world is light; these two lights look at each other from both sides. With this six-day rite lighted on both sides they go; in that they go with it, they go standing firm on both sides in these two worlds, in this world and in yonder, in both.")

### Printed p. 52  (PDF 70)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 185".)*

Of the Abhiplava, which consists of six days (*ṣaḍaha*): first, of the three days called **Jyotiṣṭoma, Goṣṭoma and Āyuṣṭoma**, the Jyotiṣṭoma is the earth, the Goṣṭoma the mid-region, and the Āyuṣṭoma the heavenly world. In the second part, the three-day group (*tryaha*), there is again the order **Goṣṭoma, Āyuṣṭoma and Jyotiṣṭoma**. The **Jyoti** (-*ṣṭoma*) that belongs to the first group is of the form of the earth; that same **Jyoti** (belonging to the second part) is of the form of the heavenly world. They perform this sacrifice in the form of the Abhiplava, with its six members, between the two worlds that are of the form of light at both ends. (Jyotiṣṭoma, Goṣṭoma and Āyuṣṭoma — these three belong to the first group; Goṣṭoma, Āyuṣṭoma and Jyotiṣṭoma — these three are the order belonging to the second group. Hence (the name *ṣaḍaha* for the Abhiplava).) Making the light shine at both ends and performing this Abhiplava in the form of a *ṣaḍaha*, they also give help to the maintenance of the two worlds. And,

> परियद्वा एतद्देवचक्रं यदभिप्लवः षळहस्तस्य यावभितोऽग्निष्टोमौ तौ
> प्रधी ये चत्वारो मध्य उक्थ्यास्तन्नभ्यं । गच्छति वै वर्तमानेन यत्र
> कामयते तत्स्वस्ति संवत्सरस्य पारमश्नुते य एवं वेद । यो वै तद्वेद
> यत्प्रथमः षळहः स वै स्वस्ति संवत्सरस्य पारमश्नुते यस्तद्वेद यद्द्वि-
> तीयो यस्तद्वेद यत्तृतीयो यस्तद्वेद यच्चतुर्थो यस्तद्वेद
> यत्पञ्चमः ॥

> *pariyadvā etaddevacakraṃ yadabhiplavaḥ ṣaḷahastasya yāvabhito 'gniṣṭomau tau*
> *pradhī ye catvāro madhya ukthyāstannabhyaṃ | gacchati vai vartamānena yatra*
> *kāmayate tatsvasti saṃvatsarasya pāramaśnute ya evaṃ veda | yo vai tadveda*
> *yatprathamaḥ ṣaḷahaḥ sa vai svasti saṃvatsarasya pāramaśnute yastadveda yaddvi-*
> *tīyo yastadveda yattṛtīyo yastadveda yaccaturtho yastadveda*
> *yatpañcamaḥ ‖*

(Ai. Brā. 18-15) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The six-day Abhiplava is a revolving wheel of the gods; the two Agniṣṭomas on either side are its felloes, the four Ukthyas in the middle its nave. With it, revolving, one goes where one wishes; he reaches safely the far shore of the year who knows thus. He who knows which is the first six-day period reaches safely the far shore of the year; he who knows which is the second, the third, the fourth, the fifth.")

This Abhiplava consisting of six days is, for the gods, a wheel of circular form. The Agniṣṭomas at both ends are the two felloes of the wheel; the four Ukthyas in the middle are the nave. Whoever knows this principle crosses to the far shore of the year by the help of this wheel. In the same way, if one knows the full nature of the Abhiplava and performs it duly, all the desired objects for the completion of the year are accomplished for him: thus the greatness of the Abhiplava is praised. Besides,

> सा यथा स्रुतिरञ्जसायन्येवमभिप्लवः षळहः स्वर्गस्य लोकस्याथ यथा
> महापथः पर्याण एवं पृष्ठ्यः षळहः स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य तद्यदुभाभ्यां
> यन्त्युभाभ्यां वै यन्न रिष्यत्युभयोः कामयोरुपाप्त्यै यश्चाभिप्लवे
> षळहे यश्च पृष्ठ्ये ।

> *sā yathā srutirañjasāyanyevamabhiplavaḥ ṣaḷahaḥ svargasya lokasyātha yathā*
> *mahāpathaḥ paryāṇa evaṃ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḷahaḥ svargasya lokasya tadyadubhābhyāṃ*
> *yantyubhābhyāṃ vai yanna riṣyatyubhayoḥ kāmayorupāptyai yaścābhiplave*
> *ṣaḷahe yaśca pṛṣṭhye |*

(Ai Brā. 18-3) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "As a path is a straight way, so the six-day Abhiplava is to the heavenly world; and as a highway is a roundabout way, so the six-day Pṛṣṭhya is to the heavenly world. In that they go by both — going by both one is not harmed — it is for obtaining both desires, that in the Abhiplava six-day rite and that in the Pṛṣṭhya.")

This Abhiplava-*ṣaḍaha* is the straight road that leads to heaven; the Pṛṣṭhya is the winding road. By both these means, going forward, the sacrificer, his attainment of desired objects *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 53  (PDF 71)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 2".)* — (for his attainment of desired objects) can strive. What the place of the Jyotiṣṭoma, Goṣṭoma and Āyuṣṭoma is in these *ṣaḍaha*s will be made known later, when the occasion comes. Praising the greatness of this same *ṣaḍaha*, the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa makes it known thus: "The year is, for the gods, of the form of an immortal wheel. Within it are contained six kinds of food, namely *sa[?]ādi* (the word is unclear). Standing on the support of this wheel they perform the sacrifice in the form of the Abhiplava. All gods and men who perform this sacrifice, standing on the support of this wheel in the form of the year, obtain the six kinds of food as well. By performing the Jyotiṣṭoma and the others twice each, he obtains these six kinds of food too doubled" — so it says.

The **Mahāvrata** too is a member of the '**Gavām ayana**' *sattra*. Of the *sattra* in the form of the Gavāmayana, which is performed through one full year (360 days), the **Prāyaṇīya Atirātra** is the opening day and the **Udayanīya Atirātra** the final day. The rites before the very last, the **Udayanīya Atirātra**, are named **Mahāvrata** (it is of the nature of an Agniṣṭoma). Just as the **Caturviṃśa** is the opening rite of this great *sattra*, so the **Mahāvrata** is the rite in the form of its completion. The procedure of the **Mahāvrata** is explained in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa thus:

> यद्वै चतुर्विंशं तन्महाव्रतं बृहद्दिवेनात्र होता रेतः सिञ्चति तददो
> महाव्रतीयेनाह्ना प्रजनयति संवत्सरे संवत्सरे वै रेतः सिक्तं जायते
> तस्मात्समानं बृहद्दिवः . . . . . . . . . य एवं विद्वानेतदहरुपैति ।

> *yadvai caturviṃśaṃ tanmahāvrataṃ bṛhaddivenātra hotā retaḥ siñcati tadado*
> *mahāvratīyenāhnā prajanayati saṃvatsare saṃvatsare vai retaḥ siktaṃ jāyate*
> *tasmātsamānaṃ bṛhaddivaḥ . . . . . . . . . ya evaṃ vidvānetadaharupaiti |*

(Ai. Brā. 17-8) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "What the Caturviṃśa is, that is the Mahāvrata. Here with the Bṛhaddiva the Hotṛ pours seed; that he generates yonder with the Mahāvrata day; seed poured is born in a year; therefore the Bṛhaddiva is the same . . . he who, knowing thus, comes to this day.")

The importance the **Caturviṃśa** has at the beginning of the "**Gavām ayana**", the **Mahāvrata** has at the end. With the **Bṛhaddiva** mantras the Hotṛ pours out the *retas* that is of the form of seed, and on the day of the Mahāvrata he becomes a helper in the act of generation. Whatever seed it be, within one year it develops into the form of fruit. One who knows this principle crosses the noose of the year and obtains wealth of food and wealth of offspring. One main point understood from this explanation is this: just as with the **Pravargya** rite, so with the rite in the form of the **Mahāvrata** too, the aim of this rite may be said to be to protect the seed of the sacrifice for a year and then to make it bear fruit. This rite also shows a continuous connection between the year that is passing and the year to come.

At the time of this rite the recitation of the sāman in the form of the **Mahaduktha** is principal. This praises the **Mahāvrata**-*graha*. First the **Mahāvrata** sāman recitation, and then the **Mahaduktha** recitation *(continues on the next page)*

---


### Printed p. 54  (PDF 72)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 185".)* — together make known the greatness of the **Mahāvrata**. In this recitation the secret principle of **Agni and Prajāpati** lies hidden. This Mahaduktha, consisting of five divisions, reflects the five divisions of the bodily principle, which is in the form of the **union of Agni and Prajāpati**. That is as follows:

(1) The **Gāyatra-sāman**, which is also of the form of a bird, being of the nature of the Trivṛt stoma, reflects the head; (2) the **Rathantara-sāman**, being of the nature of the Pañcadaśa stoma, the right wing; (3) the **Bṛhat-sāman**, being of the nature of the Saptadaśa stoma, the left wing; (4) the **Bhadra-sāman**, being of the nature of the Ekaviṃśa stoma, the tail; and (5) the Rājanya-sāman, being of the nature of the Pañcaviṃśa stoma, the body (*ātman*). Explaining the greatness and the spiritual principle of the **Mahāvrata, the Mahāvrata-sāman and the Mahaduktha**, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa praises their glory thus:

> प्रजापतिरिमान्लोकानैप्सत् । स एतं वयोविधमात्मानमपश्यदग्निं तं व्यधत्त
> तेनेमं लोकमाप्नोत्स द्वितीयं वयोविधमात्मानमपश्यन्महाव्रतं
> तद्व्यधत्त तेनाऽन्तरिक्षमाप्नोत्स तृतीयं वयोविधमात्मानमपश्यन्महदुक्थं
> तद्व्यधत्त तेन दिवमाप्नोत् ।

> *prajāpatirimānlokānaipsat | sa etaṃ vayovidhamātmānamapaśyadagniṃ taṃ vyadhatta*
> *tenemaṃ lokamāpnotsa dvitīyaṃ vayovidhamātmānamapaśyanmahāvrataṃ*
> *tadvyadhatta tenā 'ntarikṣamāpnotsa tṛtīyaṃ vayovidhamātmānamapaśyanmahadukthaṃ*
> *tadvyadhatta tena divamāpnot |*

(Gloss, mine and tentative: "Prajāpati wished to obtain these worlds. He saw this bird-shaped self, Agni; he arranged it, and with it obtained this world. He saw a second bird-shaped self, the Mahāvrata; he arranged it, and with it obtained the mid-region. He saw a third bird-shaped self, the Mahaduktha; he arranged it, and with it obtained the sky.")

Prajāpati had the aim of obtaining all these worlds. Then he created Agni in the form of a bird (the Agni-*citi*). Then, constructing it, he obtained this world. Then, having had the vision of the Mahāvrata in the form of a second bird, he constructed it and obtained the mid-region. Finally, having had the vision of the Mahaduktha in the form of a third bird, after constructing it he obtained the heavenly world.

> अयं नाव [?] लोक एषोऽग्निश्चितः । अन्तरिक्षं महाव्रतं द्यौर्महदुक्थं तस्मा-
> देतानि सर्वाणि सहोपेयादग्निं महाव्रतं महदुक्थग्ं सह हीमे
> लोका असृज्यन्त इत्यधिदेवतम् ।

> *ayaṃ nāva [?] loka eṣo 'gniścitaḥ | antarikṣaṃ mahāvrataṃ dyaurmahadukthaṃ tasmā-*
> *detāni sarvāṇi sahopeyādagniṃ mahāvrataṃ mahadukthagṃ saha hīme*
> *lokā asṛjyanta ityadhidevatam |*

(Gloss, mine and tentative: "This world is this built fire-altar; the mid-region the Mahāvrata; the sky the Mahaduktha. Therefore one should undertake all these together — the fire-altar, the Mahāvrata, the Mahaduktha — for these worlds were created together. So with regard to the deities.")

This Agni-*citi* built by Prajāpati is the terrestrial world; the Mahāvrata is the mid-region; the Mahaduktha is the heavenly world. Since all these worlds were created together by Prajāpati, one should know the natures of the Agni-*citi*, the Mahāvrata and the Mahaduktha together. Among them too, since the earth was created first, the Agni-*citi*, the earth-deity, was built first. This was the description explaining the divine form (*devatā-svarūpa*). In the same way, explaining the bodily principle:

> अथाध्यात्मम् । मन एवाग्निः प्राणो महाव्रतं वाङ्महदुक्थं . . . . . .
> आत्मैवाग्निः । प्राणो महाव्रतं वाङ्महदुक्थं . . . . . . . .
> शिर एवाग्निः । प्राणो महाव्रतमात्मा महदुक्थं . . . . . . .

> *athādhyātmam | mana evāgniḥ prāṇo mahāvrataṃ vāṅmahadukthaṃ . . . . . .*
> *ātmaivāgniḥ | prāṇo mahāvrataṃ vāṅmahadukthaṃ . . . . . . . .*
> *śira evāgniḥ | prāṇo mahāvratamātmā mahadukthaṃ . . . . . . .*

(Śa. Brā. 10-1-2-1 to 9) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Now with regard to the self: mind is Agni, breath the Mahāvrata, speech the Mahaduktha . . . the body is Agni, breath the Mahāvrata, speech the Mahaduktha . . . the head is Agni, breath the Mahāvrata, the trunk the Mahaduktha . . .")

### Printed p. 55  (PDF 73)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 2".)*

Explaining the spiritual principle, it describes the mind as the Agni-*citi*, breath as the Mahāvrata and speech as the Mahaduktha; and explaining the bodily principle — the body (*ātman*) as the Agni-*citi*, breath as the Mahāvrata and speech as the Mahaduktha. And, stating the derivation of the **Mahāvrata**,

> " . . . . . . . यजुष्टः प्राण एव महांस्तस्यान्नमेव व्रतं
> तन्महाव्रतग्ं सामतः प्राण उ एवोक् तस्यान्नमेव थं तदुक्थं . . .

> *" . . . . . . . yajuṣṭaḥ prāṇa eva mahāṃstasyānnameva vrataṃ*
> *tanmahāvratagṃ sāmataḥ prāṇa u evok tasyānnameva thaṃ tadukthaṃ . . .*

(Śra. [sic] Brā. 10-4-1-23) (Gloss, mine and tentative: ". . . from the Yajus side, breath is the 'great' (*mahān*), its food the *vrata*: that is the Mahāvrata; from the Sāman side, breath is the *uk*, its food the *tha*: that is the *uktha* . . .")

Agni, the presider over the sacrifice, is *mahān*; his food is the *vrata*; therefore it is known as **Mahāvrata**. **Breath is the *uk*** and its **food the *tha***; therefore it is known also as *uktha*: so the derivation from the spiritual side is given. And the glory of the Mahāvrata (-*graha*) too is praised thus:

> अथातो महाव्रतीयस्यैव । प्रजापतेर्ह वै प्रजाः ससृजानस्य पर्वाणि वि
> सस्रग्ंसुः स विस्रस्तैः पर्वभिर्न शशाक संहातुं ततो देवा अर्चन्तः
> श्राम्यन्तश्चेरुस्त एतं महाव्रतीयं ददृशुस्तमस्मा अगृह्णंस्तेनास्य
> पर्वाणि समदधुः ।

> *athāto mahāvratīyasyaiva | prajāpaterha vai prajāḥ sasṛjānasya parvāṇi vi*
> *sasragṃsuḥ sa visrastaiḥ parvabhirna śaśāka saṃhātuṃ tato devā arcantaḥ*
> *śrāmyantaścerusta etaṃ mahāvratīyaṃ dadṛśustamasmā agṛhṇaṃstenāsya*
> *parvāṇi samadadhuḥ |*

(Gloss, mine and tentative: "Now of the Mahāvratīya [cup] itself. When Prajāpati had created the creatures, his joints became loosened; with loosened joints he could not hold himself together. Then the gods went on praising and toiling; they saw this Mahāvratīya, drew it for him, and with it put his joints together.")

After Prajāpati had created all the creatures, from that toil all the joints of his body became loosened; so it became a toil for him even to rise up. All the gods, by prayer full of faith, obtained the vision of the Mahāvrata-*graha*, took it and offered it with him in view. Then all his joints were set right.

> स सग्ंहितैः पर्वभिः । इदमन्नाद्यमभ्युत्तस्थौ यदिदं प्रजापतेरन्नाद्यं यद्वै
> मनुष्याणामशनं तद्देवानां व्रतं महद्वा इदं व्रतमभूद्येनायग्ं
> समहास्तेति तस्मान्महाव्रतीयो नाम ।

> *sa sagṃhitaiḥ parvabhiḥ | idamannādyamabhyuttasthau yadidaṃ prajāpaterannādyaṃ yadvai*
> *manuṣyāṇāmaśanaṃ taddevānāṃ vrataṃ mahadvā idaṃ vratamabhūdyenāyagṃ*
> *samahāsteti tasmānmahāvratīyo nāma |*

(Śa. Brā. 4-6-4-1 to 2) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "With his joints put together he rose up to this food — this which is Prajāpati's food; what is men's eating is the gods' *vrata*. 'Great indeed has this *vrata* become, by which this one has been restored' — therefore it is called the Mahāvratīya.")

When his joints were set right, Prajāpati accepted this food in the form of the Mahāvratīya-*graha*. What is food for Prajāpati and for the creatures created by him, that same is food in the form of *vrata* for the gods too. Because it has the greatness of setting right Prajāpati's bodily distress too and making him endowed with vitality, it came to be known by the name **Mahāvrata**: this is its praise. What the characteristic of the **Mahāvrata**, of such greatness, is, is made known at great length in the Aitareya Āraṇyaka. In the present context, since it is not possible to give its explanation in full, it is given briefly. The special part will be made known later.
