### Printed p. 56  (PDF 74)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 185". Special Topics of Ṛk 1 continue.)*

> अथ महाव्रतं । इन्द्रो वै वृत्रं हत्वा महानभवद्यन्महानभवत्तन्महाव्रत-
> मभवत्तन्महाव्रतस्य महाव्रतत्वं ।

> *atha mahāvrataṃ | indro vai vṛtraṃ hatvā mahānabhavadyanmahānabhavattanmahāvrata-*
> *mabhavattanmahāvratasya mahāvratatvaṃ |*

(Aitareya Āraṇyakam 1-1) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Now the Mahāvrata. Indra, having slain Vṛtra, became great; because he became great, that became the Mahāvrata: that is the Mahāvrata-ness of the Mahāvrata.")

Indra, having killed Vṛtra, displayed his greatness. Thereafter the Mahāvrata, which celebrates that greatness, was begun. Therefore this same name came to the rite called Mahāvrata. By this very rite, which consists in the slaying of the asura Vṛtra, the name **Mahendra** also became famous for Indra: this story-context is set out in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (12-10) by sentences such as "इन्द्रो वै वृत्रं हत्वा (*indro vai vṛtraṃ hatvā*) . . . . यन्महानिन्द्रोऽभवत्तन्महेन्द्रस्य महेन्द्रत्वं (*yanmahānindro 'bhavattanmahendrasya mahendratvaṃ*)", and in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (6-5-5-3). Although in the Aitareya Āraṇyaka the context celebrating Indra's greatness is stated by the sentence "तन्महाव्रतस्य महाव्रतत्वं (*tanmahāvratasya mahāvratatvaṃ*)", Sāyaṇa, when giving his explanation in this context, has given the very derivation (*nirvacana*) stated in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa. Just as, in the sentences quoted above from the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, the context of the offering of the Mahāvrata for removing Prajāpati's fatigue is described, so the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa too makes known the same matter. The order of that description is as follows, and it is somewhat different from the Śatapatha's description:

> प्रजापतिः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा वृत्तोऽशयत् । तं देवा भूतानाग्ं रसं तेजः
> संभृत्य । तेनैनमभिषज्यन् । महानववर्तीति । तन्महाव्रतस्य महाव्रतत्वं ।
> महद्व्रतमिति । तन्महाव्रतस्य महाव्रतत्वं । महतो व्रतमिति । तन्महाव्रतस्य
> महाव्रतत्वं ॥

> *prajāpatiḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā vṛtto 'śayat | taṃ devā bhūtānāgṃ rasaṃ tejaḥ*
> *saṃbhṛtya | tenainamabhiṣajyan | mahānavavartīti | tanmahāvratasya mahāvratatvaṃ |*
> *mahadvratamiti | tanmahāvratasya mahāvratatvaṃ | mahato vratamiti | tanmahāvratasya*
> *mahāvratatvaṃ ‖*

(Tai. Brā. 1-2-6-1) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Prajāpati, having created the creatures, lay exhausted. The gods, gathering the essence, the brilliance of beings, healed him with it. 'Great, he has turned back' — that is the Mahāvrata-ness of the Mahāvrata. 'A great vow' — that is the Mahāvrata-ness of the Mahāvrata. 'The vow of the great one' — that is the Mahāvrata-ness of the Mahāvrata.")

In this description: when Prajāpati, exhausted by the work of creation, had fallen down weary from toil, the gods procured the brilliance (*tejas*) that is the essence of all creatures and with its help removed his fatigue. Therefore Prajāpati became **mahān** (great). Making known that this same essential brilliance is the oblation to be offered at the time of the Mahāvrata, they explain why this name became famous for the **Mahāvrata**:

*Gist:* Three derivations: "by this rite he became great"; "a great vow", as the rite yields a great fruit; or "the vow (medicine) of the great one, Prajāpati".

> महानवर्तिष्ट अनेन कर्मणा इति व्युत्पत्त्या तस्य कर्मणः महाव्रतमिति नाम
> संपन्नं । यद्वा कर्मणोऽस्य महाफलहेतुत्वेन महत्त्वान् महच्च
> तद्व्रतमिति तद्व्युत्पत्तिः । अथवा महतः प्रजापतेरौषधरूपत्वान्महतो
> व्रतमिति व्युत्पत्तिः ॥

> *mahānavartiṣṭa anena karmaṇā iti vyutpattyā tasya karmaṇaḥ mahāvratamiti nāma*
> *saṃpannaṃ | yadvā karmaṇo 'sya mahāphalahetutvena mahattvān mahacca*
> *tadvratamiti tadvyutpattiḥ | athavā mahataḥ prajāpaterauṣadharūpatvānmahato*
> *vratamiti vyutpattiḥ ‖*

### Printed p. 57  (PDF 75)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 2".)* Sāyaṇa has made known that this rite has the name Mahāvrata either because its purport is that Prajāpati became *mahān* (great) through the rite consisting in the offering of the oblation; or because it is a rite having the power to give a great fruit and the fitness of its own nature; or because it is of the form of medicine for Prajāpati, who is *mahān*. At the time of such a Mahāvrata the recitation of the present sūkta is prescribed. This very thing is made known in the sentences

> कतरा पूर्वा कतरापरायोरिति द्यावापृथिवीयं समानोदर्कं समानो-
> दर्कं वा एतदहरेतस्याह्नो रूपं ॥

> *katarā pūrvā katarāparāyoriti dyāvāpṛthivīyaṃ samānodarkaṃ samāno-*
> *darkaṃ vā etadaharetasyāhno rūpaṃ ‖*

(Ai. Ā. 1-5-3) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "'*katarā pūrvā katarāparāyoḥ*' — the Dyāvāpṛthivī hymn, having a like ending; for this day has a like ending: it is the form of this day.")

The Niruktakāra's derivation (*nirvacana*) for the present ṛk is as follows:

> कतरा पूर्वा कतरापरा । एनयोः कथं जाते कवयः क एने
> विजानाति । सर्वमात्मना बिभृतो यद्धैनयोः कर्म विवर्तेते
> चैनयोरहनी अहोरात्रे चक्रियेव चक्रयुक्ते इवेति द्यावा-
> पृथिव्योर्महिमानमाचष्ट आचष्टे

> *katarā pūrvā katarāparā | enayoḥ kathaṃ jāte kavayaḥ ka ene*
> *vijānāti | sarvamātmanā bibhṛto yaddhainayoḥ karma vivartete*
> *cainayorahanī ahorātre cakriyeva cakrayukte iveti dyāvā-*
> *pṛthivyormahimānamācaṣṭa ācaṣṭe*

(Ni. 3-22) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Which is prior, which later, of these two? How were they born, O sages? Who knows them? They bear everything by themselves, whatever is their work; and their two days, day and night, revolve as if wheeled — so he declared the greatness of Heaven and Earth.")

Which of these two deities is the one born first? What is the order of their origin? O ṛṣis, which of you knows this secret? These two themselves are the support of all the beings of the universe. Like the two wheels of a chariot, both day and night revolve continuously around them — so it is explained. Explaining "कतरा पूर्वा कतरा अपरा (*katarā pūrvā katarā aparā*)", Durgācārya has made known that the question is "किं पौर्वापर्येण, उत युगपत् भवेतां (*kiṃ paurvāparyeṇa, uta yugapat bhavetāṃ*)" — whether one was born after the other, or whether both were born together. In the matter of the origin of these deities, sometimes wonder and sometimes uncertain conjecture are natural:

> किं स्विद्वनं क उ स वृक्ष आस यतो द्यावापृथिवी निष्टतक्षुः ।
> संतस्थाने अजरे इत ऊती अहानि पूर्वीरुषसो जरन्त ॥

> *kiṃ svidvanaṃ ka u sa vṛkṣa āsa yato dyāvāpṛthivī niṣṭatakṣuḥ |*
> *saṃtasthāne ajare ita ūtī ahāni pūrvīruṣaso jaranta ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-31-7) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "What was the wood, what the tree, from which they fashioned Heaven and Earth, which stand firm, unaging, with help from here, while the many days and dawns have grown old?")

While countless days and dawns too roll away, the ṛṣi has expressed his admiring wonder: from which trees of which forest were these Heaven and Earth fashioned, which stand imperishable, unbroken and firm?

The curiosity expressed in the ṛk "किं स्विद्वनं (*kiṃ svidvanaṃ*)" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-31-7; the first letter printed like *kṣi*) is indicated in many other places too. In some places a fitting answer too is given. For example,

---

### Printed p. 58  (PDF 76)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 185".)*

> किंस्विदासीदधिष्ठानमारम्भणं कथमत्स्वित्कथासीत् ।
> यतो भूमिं जनयन्विश्वकर्मा वि द्यामौर्णोन्महिना विश्वचक्षाः ॥

> *kiṃsvidāsīdadhiṣṭhānamārambhaṇaṃ kathamatsvitkathāsīt |*
> *yato bhūmiṃ janayanviśvakarmā vi dyāmaurṇonmahinā viśvacakṣāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-81-2; *kathamat* as read) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "What was the standing-place, what the beginning, how was it, from which Viśvakarman, all-seeing, generating the earth, spread out the sky by his greatness?")

It is asked: what was the support for their construction available to the all-seeing Viśvakarman, who created the earth and made the mid-region spread out widely? As an answer to this,

> किग्ं स्विद्वनं क उ स वृक्ष आसीत् । यतो दाव्यापृथिवी निष्टतक्षुः । मनीषिणो
> मनसा पृच्छतेदु तत् । यदध्यतिष्ठद्भुवनानि धारयन् । ब्रह्म वनं ब्रह्म
> स वृक्ष आसीत् । यतो द्यावापृथिवी निष्टतक्षुः । मनीषिणो मनसा वि ब्र-
> वीमि वः । ब्रह्माध्यतिष्ठद्भुवनानि धारयन् ॥

> *kigṃ svidvanaṃ ka u sa vṛkṣa āsīt | yato dāvyāpṛthivī niṣṭatakṣuḥ | manīṣiṇo*
> *manasā pṛcchatedu tat | yadadhyatiṣṭhadbhuvanāni dhārayan | brahma vanaṃ brahma*
> *sa vṛkṣa āsīt | yato dyāvāpṛthivī niṣṭatakṣuḥ | manīṣiṇo manasā vi bra-*
> *vīmi vaḥ | brahmādhyatiṣṭhadbhuvanāni dhārayan ‖*

*(The first "दाव्यापृथिवी (*dāvyāpṛthivī*)" is so printed [sic].)*

(Tai. Brā. 2-8-9-6-3 [?]) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "What was the wood, what the tree, from which they fashioned Heaven and Earth? O thinkers, ask with your mind that on which he stood supporting the worlds. Brahman was the wood, Brahman the tree, from which they fashioned Heaven and Earth; O thinkers, I tell you with my mind: Brahman stood supporting the worlds.")

For the creation of these Heaven and Earth, Brahman itself (the imperishable reality called Brahman) is the forest, and Brahman itself the tree; from that alone is their construction — so it is made known in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa.

"*Kavayaḥ* — क्रान्तदर्शनः (*krāntadarśanaḥ*) — अतीन्द्रियज्ञाः (*atīndriyajñāḥ*)": so (Sāyaṇa) has stated the meaning of the word *kavi*. The derivation of the word *kavi* was made known earlier, citing the Niruktakāra's sentence "मेधावी कविः क्रान्तदर्शनो भवति कवतेर्वा (*medhāvī kaviḥ krāntadarśano bhavati kavatervā*)" (Ni. 12-13). What the nature of a *kavi* is and what his power is, and that the word *kavi* is used in the Ṛksaṃhitā to make known such a nature and powers, was also made known briefly earlier. In the present ṛk, asking "who knows the secret of Heaven and Earth, which reflect the principle of the universe?", it asks, "कवयः, को विवेद (*kavayaḥ, ko viveda*)" — O ṛṣis who know what is beyond the senses, which one of you has fully known this principle? That is, this secret is not to be known by a merely ordinary and physical view. To break open this secret and understand it, there must be an extraordinary power having the fitness for it. Only one who has such extraordinary power of vision is called a *kavi*.

> समानं नीळं वृषणो वसानाः सं जग्मिरे महिषा अर्वतीभिः ।
> ऋतस्य पदं कवयो नि पान्ति गुहा नामानि दधिरे पराणि ।

> *samānaṃ nīḷaṃ vṛṣaṇo vasānāḥ saṃ jagmire mahiṣā arvatībhiḥ |*
> *ṛtasya padaṃ kavayo ni pānti guhā nāmāni dadhire parāṇi |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-5-2) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Wearing a common nest, the bulls, the buffaloes, have come together with the mares; the poets guard the place of Ṛta; they have placed the highest names in secret.")

In ṛks such as this the true nature of the *kavi* is described. It is described that the *kavis*, having entered the path of **Ṛta**, hold in the most hidden heart the supreme names of the secret, and make them manifest so that the world comes to know them. That is, hidden secretly, the world's *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 59  (PDF 77)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 2".)* — the portions not within the range of sight, and are able to make them known somewhat to the world's view too: in this sense this word is used. In the present ṛk too, addressing the ṛṣis who have obtained such knowledge beyond the senses, it asks: what is the secret principle of Heaven and Earth?

**विश्वं त्मना बिभृतः (*viśvaṃ tmanā bibhṛtaḥ*)** — it praises that the deity presiding over the heavenly world and the Earth-goddess, protectors of the universe, hold all the worlds in themselves and themselves bear them all.

> नमो द्यावापृथिवीभ्यामिति तदाभ्यां द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां निह्नुवते ययोरिदं
> सर्वमधि ।

> *namo dyāvāpṛthivībhyāmiti tadābhyāṃ dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ nihnuvate yayoridaṃ*
> *sarvamadhi |*

(Śa. Brā. 3-4-3-21) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "'Homage to Heaven and Earth' — thereby they make amends to these two, Heaven and Earth, upon whom all this rests.")

In this and many other places is made known the matter stated, that the existence and the support of all the worlds, and the whole work of protection, rest on Heaven and Earth alone. This very idea was explained earlier, when giving the Special Topics of the ṛk

> उरुव्यचसा महिनी असश्चता पिता माता च भुवनानि रक्षतः ।
> सुधृष्टमे वपुष्ये३ न रोदसी पिता यत्सीमभि रूपैरवासयत् ॥

> *uruvyacasā mahinī asaścatā pitā mātā ca bhuvanāni rakṣataḥ |*

## Sūkta 185, Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> भूरिं द्वे अचरन्ती चरन्तं पद्वन्तं गर्भमपदी दधाते ।
> नित्यं न सूनुं पित्रोरुपस्थे द्यावा रक्षतं पृथिवी नो अभ्वात् ॥ २ ॥

> *bhūriṃ dve acarantī carantaṃ padvantaṃ garbhamapadī dadhāte |*
> *nityaṃ na sūnuṃ pitrorupasthe dyāvā rakṣataṃ pṛthivī no abhvāt ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> भूरिम् । द्वे इति । अचरन्ती इति । चरन्तम् । पत्ऽवन्तम् । गर्भम् । अपदी इति । दधाते इति ।
> नित्यम् । न । सूनुम् । पित्रोः । उपऽस्थे । द्यावा । रक्षतम् । पृथिवी इति । नः । अभ्वात् ॥ २ ॥

> *bhūrim | dve iti | acarantī iti | carantam | pat 'vantam | garbham | apadī iti | dadhāte iti |*
> *nityam | na | sūnum | pitroḥ | upa 'sthe | dyāvā | rakṣatam | pṛthivī iti | naḥ | abhvāt ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed)*

*Gist:* The two motionless ones, heaven and earth, footless themselves, bear the great moving, footed brood of all creatures, as parents hold a dear son in their lap; may they guard us from great fear (*abhva* = great).

> अचरन्ती अविचले द्वे एते द्यावापृथिव्यौ भूरिं बहुतरं चरन्तं पद्वन्तं पादयुक्तं गर्भं गर्भवदाश्रितं कृत्स्नं प्राणिजातमपदी स्वयं पादरहिते दधाते धारयतः । अनयोर्मध्ये खलु सर्वं जगत्क्षेमेण वर्तते । धारणे दृष्टान्तः । पित्रोर्मातापित्रोरुपस्थ उत्सङ्गे वर्तमानं नित्यं ध्रुवमात्मजं सूनुं न पुत्रमिव यथा स्नेहेन वर्धयन्तौ धारयन्तौ मातापितरौ तद्वत् । अथ प्रत्यक्षेणाह । हे द्यावा पृथिवी द्यावापृथिव्यौ । इतरेतरापेक्षया द्वित्वमुभयोः । नोऽस्मानभ्वान्महतो भयहेतोः पापाद्रक्षतं पालयतम् । यद्वा । अभ्वादभ्वं महत् । अत्यर्थमित्यर्थः । अभ्वेति महन्नाम ॥ द्वन्द्वे कृतद्यावादेशस्य द्यावापृथिवीशब्दस्य मध्ये रक्षतमिति पदप्रयोगश्छान्दसः । आमन्त्रितस्याविद्यमानत्वेन निघाताभावः ॥

> *acarantī avicale dve ete dyāvāpṛthivyau bhūriṃ bahutaraṃ carantaṃ padvantaṃ pādayuktaṃ garbhaṃ garbhavadāśritaṃ kṛtsnaṃ prāṇijātamapadī svayaṃ pādarahite dadhāte dhārayataḥ | anayormadhye khalu sarvaṃ jagatkṣemeṇa vartate | dhāraṇe dṛṣṭāntaḥ | pitrormātāpitrorupastha utsaṅge vartamānaṃ nityaṃ dhruvamātmajaṃ sūnuṃ na putramiva yathā snehena vardhayantau dhārayantau mātāpitarau tadvat | atha pratyakṣeṇāha | he dyāvā pṛthivī dyāvāpṛthivyau | itaretarāpekṣayā dvitvamubhayoḥ | no 'smānabhvānmahato bhayahetoḥ pāpādrakṣataṃ pālayatam | yadvā | abhvādabhvaṃ mahat | atyarthamityarthaḥ | abhveti mahannāma ‖ dvandve kṛtadyāvādeśasya dyāvāpṛthivīśabdasya madhye rakṣatamiti padaprayogaśchāndasaḥ | āmantritasyāvidyamānatvena nighātābhāvaḥ ‖*

### Printed p. 61  (PDF 79)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 2".)*

**Pratipadārtha.** *pitroḥ* — of the parents; *upasthe* — growing up on the lap; *nityaṃ sūnuṃ na* — as (parents) hold with love and protect their own-born son; *acarantī* — themselves free of motion; *apadī* — and footless; *dve* — the two, heaven and earth, together; *bhūrim* — manifold; *padvantam* — footed; *carantam* — and moving; *garbham* — the brood of living beings that rests on these two, as an embryo rests on the mother; *dadhāte* — they uphold; *dyāvāpṛthivī* — O Heaven and Earth; *naḥ* — us; *abhvāt* — from sin, which is great and a cause of fear; *rakṣatam* — protect.

**Bhāvārtha.** As parents with love hold and protect their own-born son growing up on their lap, so heaven and earth, both together, themselves free of motion and footless, uphold the whole brood of living beings — manifold, footed, moving — which rests on them as an embryo rests on the mother. O Heaven and Earth, protect us from sin, which is great and a cause of fear.

**English Translation (as printed; heading printed "English Trnslation" [sic]):** Footless and motionless, they sustain numerous moving and footed races, as a son is even (nursed) on the lap of his parents : defend us, Heaven and Earth, from great (danger).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

In this ṛk the relation between heaven and earth and the rest of the brood of living beings, and the difference between the two, are made known. By the two epithets **अचरन्ती (*acarantī*) अपदी (*apadī*)** the stability of heaven and earth is made known, and by the epithets **पद्वन्तं (*padvantaṃ*) चरन्तं (*carantaṃ*)** the activity of going etc. of all living beings, or likewise their unsteadiness. Although by the words **पित्रोः (*pitroḥ*) उपस्थे (*upasthe*) नित्यं (*nityaṃ*) सूनुं (*sūnuṃ*)** a common worldly comparison is shown, yet since further on by the word **गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)** all the broods of living beings, in the form of the embryo, are meant, the word **पित्रोः (*pitroḥ*)** may also be taken to mean heaven and earth in the form of mother and father. The sense is: as in the world parents hold their own-born son on their lap and protect him, so heaven and earth, the mother and father of the whole universe, hold and protect the broods of living beings, which are their own embryos.

### Printed p. 62  (PDF 80)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 185". Special Topics of Ṛk 2, continued.)*

If for the word **पित्रोः (*pitroḥ*)** the meaning "Heaven and Earth in the form of mother and father" is made, then the question arises which of them is the father and which the mother.

> पितुः — पितृस्थानीयायाः पृथिव्याः मातुः — माताऽन्तरिक्षं निर्मीयन्तेऽस्मिन् भूतानि

> *pituḥ — pitṛsthānīyāyāḥ pṛthivyāḥ mātuḥ — mātā 'ntarikṣaṃ nirmīyante 'smin bhūtāni*

(Ni. 2-8) — so the Niruktakāra has explained. From his explanation it is understood that the Earth, being derived from the root पा (*pā*), meaning protection, and protecting all beings, has the name *pitṛ* (father), and the Antarikṣa, since all beings are formed in it, has the name *mātṛ* (mother). This explanation is in one way sound from the standpoint of word-derivation, but it does not fit the traditional meaning. Generally the sentences that designate the Antarikṣa as father and the Earth as mother are the well-known ones.

> तन्नो वातो मयोभु वातु भेषजं तन्माता पृथिवी तत् पिता द्यौः ।
> तद्ग्रावाणः सोमसुतो मयोभुवस्तदश्विना शृणुतं धिष्ण्या युवम् ॥

> *tanno vāto mayobhu vātu bheṣajaṃ tanmātā pṛthivī tat pitā dyauḥ |*
> *tadgrāvāṇaḥ somasuto mayobhuvastadaśvinā śṛṇutaṃ dhiṣṇyā yuvam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-89-4) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "May the wind waft to us that healing remedy which is a source of joy; that, mother Earth; that, father Heaven; that, the soma-pressing stones, sources of joy; hear that, O Aśvins, you two worthy of the hearth.")

That in these and many other contexts the Antarikṣa is designated father and the Earth mother was made known clearly earlier. In sentences such as "मधु द्यौरस्तु नः पिता (*madhu dyaurastu naḥ pitā*)" (Ṛ. Saṃ 1-90-7), the epithet *pitṛ* (father) is established for the deity presiding over the heavenly world as well. In the present ṛk we may take the meaning "mother and father" together. The sense is: on the lap (thigh) of such a mother and father the broods of living beings grow.

**उपस्थे (*upasthe*)** — the word *upastha* is used in different senses. In many places Sāyaṇa has given meanings such as उपस्थः यज्ञः, आहवनीयो वा अन्तरिक्षं वा (*upasthaḥ yajñaḥ, āhavanīyo vā antarikṣaṃ vā*). In the present ṛk it comes to mean "on the lap of the parents".

Generally the words **पित्रोः उपस्थे (*pitroḥ upasthe*)** are used to indicate the relation that Agni has with Heaven and Earth. For example,

> त्रिमूर्धानं सप्तरश्मिं गृणीषेऽनूनमग्निं पित्रोरुपस्थे ।
> निषत्तमस्य चरतो ध्रुवस्य विश्वा दिवो रोचनापप्रिवांसम् ॥

> *trimūrdhānaṃ saptaraśmiṃ gṛṇīṣe 'nūnamagniṃ pitrorupasthe |*
> *niṣattamasya carato dhruvasya viśvā divo rocanāpaprivāṃsam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-146-1) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "I praise the three-headed, seven-rayed Agni, complete, in the lap of his parents, seated, who has filled all the luminous spaces of heaven, of the moving and the fixed.")

— there, **पित्रोः उपस्थे निषत्तं अग्निं (*pitroḥ upasthe niṣattaṃ agniṃ*)** means Agni seated on the lap of his parents, Heaven and Earth. But in the present ṛk only the relation that all the broods of beings have with Heaven and Earth is stated.

**नित्यं सूनुं (*nityaṃ sūnuṃ*)** — here the word *nitya* has been given the meaning *dhruva* (fixed). In the present ṛk (the poet) has described the fixedness of Heaven and Earth and the unfixedness of the broods of living beings, and made known the difference between them. Therefore *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 63  (PDF 81)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 2".)* here, rather than the meaning *dhruva* for the word **नित्य (*nitya*)**, the meaning "one's own" is the fitting one. The word *nitya* is used in many places in the sense **सहज (*sahaja*)** (natural, inborn) too. In the present case it may be taken to mean the *aurasa* son (one's own born son).

In the present ṛk, besides stating the relation of Heaven and Earth in the form of mother and father, it is prayed that they protect the world from great fear. The refrain "**द्यावा रक्षतं पृथिवी नो अभ्वात् (*dyāvā rakṣataṃ pṛthivī no abhvāt*)**" is in ṛks 2–8 of the sūkta.

**अभ्वात् (*abhvāt*)** — the word *abhva* is read among the **names of water (*udaka*)** (Ni. Ni. 24) and among the **names of "great" (*mahat*)** (Ni. 3-23). But since this word is used in other senses as well, not only in these two, once it is known that Sāyaṇa too has stated its meaning according to the context, its correct meaning in the present ṛk can then be determined.

> नहि ते क्षत्रं न सहो न मन्युं वयश्चनामी पतयन्त आपुः ।
> नेमा आपो अनिमिषं चरन्तीर्न ये वातस्य प्रमिनन्त्यभ्वम् ॥

> *nahi te kṣatraṃ na saho na manyuṃ vayaścanāmī patayanta āpuḥ |*
> *nemā āpo animiṣaṃ carantīrna ye vātasya praminantyabhvam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-6) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Not your dominion, nor your might, nor your wrath have even these flying birds attained, nor these waters moving unwinking, nor those who check the force of the wind.")

In this ṛk there is the praise of **Varuṇa**. Here, explaining वातस्य ये गतिविशेषाः ते त्वदीयम् अभ्वं वेगं न हिंसन्ति (*vātasya ye gativiśeṣāḥ te tvadīyam abhvaṃ vegaṃ na hiṃsanti*) — "even the speed of the wind's motion cannot check the speed of Varuṇa" — (Sāyaṇa) has given the word *abhva* the meaning "speed". And,

> युष्मेषितो मरुतो मर्त्येषित आ यो नो अभ्व ईषते ।
> वि तं युयोत शवसा व्योजसा वि युष्माकाभिरूतिभिः ॥

> *yuṣmeṣito maruto martyeṣita ā yo no abhva īṣate |*
> *vi taṃ yuyota śavasā vyojasā vi yuṣmākābhirūtibhiḥ ‖*

(Ṛ Saṃ. 1-39-8) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "O Maruts, whatever monster, sent by you or sent by a mortal, comes at us, drive him away by your strength, by your vigour, by your aids.")

— there the Maruts are praised. Here, explaining यः कश्चिदभ्वः शत्रुः नः प्राप्नोति तं शवसा वियुयोत (*yaḥ kaścidabhvaḥ śatruḥ naḥ prāpnoti taṃ śavasā viyuyota*), the word *abhva* has been given the meaning "enemy".

> असूत पृश्निर्महते रणाय त्वेषमयासां मरुतामनीकम् ।
> ते सप्सरासोऽजनयन्ताभ्वमादित्स्वधामिषिरां पर्यपश्यन् ॥

> *asūta pṛśnirmahate raṇāya tveṣamayāsāṃ marutāmanīkam |*
> *te sapsarāso 'janayantābhvamāditsvadhāmiṣirāṃ paryapaśyan ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-168-9) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Pṛśni bore, for great battle, the brilliant host of the restless Maruts; they, of one form, generated the cloud, and then they beheld the vigorous refreshment.")

In this ṛk, by अभ्वं मेघं जनयन्ति (*abhvaṃ meghaṃ janayanti*) the word *abhva* has been given the meaning "cloud", and *(in the second line the word is read "जजुर्वाँ" as printed)*,

> आ यन्मे अभ्वं वनदः पनन्तोशिग्भ्यो नामिमीत वर्णम् ।
> स चित्रेण चिकिते रंसु भासा जजुर्वाँ यो मुहुरा युवा भूत् ॥

> *ā yanme abhvaṃ vanadaḥ panantośigbhyo nāmimīta varṇam |*
> *sa citreṇa cikite raṃsu bhāsā jajurvā~ yo muhurā yuvā bhūt ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-4-5) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "When the admirers of the woods praised my mighty one, he made his colour for the Uśijs; he has become known with bright light amid delights, he who, grown old, again and again became young.") *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 64  (PDF 82)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 185".)* — in that place the word **अभ्व (*abhva*)** praises the greatness of Agni. Here *abhva* comes to mean **"greatness"**. Likewise,

> अर्हन्बिभर्षि सायकानि धन्वार्हन्निष्कं यजतं विश्वरूपम् ।
> अर्हन्निदं दयसे विश्वमभ्वं न वा ओजीयो रुद्र त्वदस्ति ॥

> *arhanbibharṣi sāyakāni dhanvārhanniṣkaṃ yajataṃ viśvarūpam |*
> *arhannidaṃ dayase viśvamabhvaṃ na vā ojīyo rudra tvadasti ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-33-10) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Worthy, you bear arrows and bow; worthy, the adorable many-formed necklace; worthy, you protect this whole vast world; there is nothing mightier than you, O Rudra.")

In this ṛk, विश्वं अभ्वं । महन्नामैतत् । अतिविस्तृतं जगत् । (*viśvaṃ abhvaṃ | mahannāmaitat | ativistṛtaṃ jagat |*) — since it is read among the names of "great", Sāyaṇa has given the meaning "the exceedingly extended world". That is, in 2-4-5, cited above, it indicates the spiritual (*ādhyātmika*) greatness of Agni; here, in ṛk 2-33-10, it indicates the physical extent of the world.

What the root meaning of the word *abhva* is, and how these traditional meanings can be derived on the basis of that root meaning: if one wishes to know this, the root meaning becomes known on attending to the word *abhva* used in a sentence of the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa.

> अथ ब्रह्मैव परार्धमगच्छत् । तत्परार्धं गत्वैक्षत कथं न्विमान्लोकान्प्र-
> त्यवेयामिति तद्द्वाभ्यामेव प्रत्यवैद्रूपेण चैव नाम्ना च स यस्य कस्य
> च नामास्ति तन्नाम यस्योऽपि नाम नास्ति यद्वेद रूपेणेदग्ं रूपमिति
> तद्रूपमेतावद्वा इदं यावद्रूपं चैव नाम च । ते हैते ब्रह्मणो
> महती अभ्वे । स यो हैते ब्रह्मणो महती अभ्वे वेद महद्धैवाभ्वं
> भवति ॥

> *atha brahmaiva parārdhamagacchat | tatparārdhaṃ gatvaikṣata kathaṃ nvimānlokānpra-*
> *tyaveyāmiti taddvābhyāmeva pratyavaidrūpeṇa caiva nāmnā ca sa yasya kasya*
> *ca nāmāsti tannāma yasyo 'pi nāma nāsti yadveda rūpeṇedagṃ rūpamiti*
> *tadrūpametāvadvā idaṃ yāvadrūpaṃ caiva nāma ca | te haite brahmaṇo*
> *mahatī abhve | sa yo haite brahmaṇo mahatī abhve veda mahaddhaivābhvaṃ*
> *bhavati ‖*

(Śa. Brā. 11-2-3-3) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Then Brahman went up to the higher half. Having gone to the higher half, it considered: 'How now could I come down into these worlds?' It came down by two: by form and by name. Whatever has a name, that is name; and what has no name, what one knows by its form — 'this is its form' — that is form. So far indeed is all this, as far as form and name. These are the two great powers (*abhva*) of Brahman; he who knows these two great powers of Brahman becomes himself a great power.")

In these sentences it is said that name and form are the great *abhvas* of Brahman. The *abhva* of Brahman is of two kinds, **mūrta** (Concrete) and **amūrta** (Abstract). Therefore the meaning is that both kinds of power that are Brahman's greatness, the **mūrta power** and the **amūrta power**, pervade the universe. From these root meanings the remaining purports follow. In this way the pervasive meaning "the principle of the universe in the form of the mūrta and the amūrta",

> उदू अयाँ उपवक्तेव बाहू हिरण्यया सविता सुप्रतीका ।
> दिवो रोहांस्यरुहत्पृथिव्या अरीरमत्पतयत्कच्चिदभ्वम् ॥

> *udū ayā~ upavakteva bāhū hiraṇyayā savitā supratīkā |*
> *divo rohāṃsyaruhatpṛthivyā arīramatpatayatkaccidabhvam ‖*

(Ṛ Saṃ. 6-71-5) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Savitṛ has raised up his golden, fair-faced arms like one who speaks forth; he has climbed the heights of heaven and earth; he has brought to rest whatever mighty thing was flying.")

— is contained in the word *abhva* in this ṛk. Explaining the meaning of this word, Sāyaṇa has stated its pervasive purport: "अभ्वं महत् सर्वं वस्तुजातम् (*abhvaṃ mahat sarvaṃ vastujātam*)". In some *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 65  (PDF 83)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 2".)* places a pervasive **good power** (*sacchakti*) is indicated, and in some other places an **evil power** (*duṣṭaśakti*). In the Ṛksaṃhitā this word is used in both these senses.

*(In line 1 the letter of "दुर्ये (*durye*)" is doubtful, da or dha [?].)*

> प्र ये वसुभ्य ईवदा नमो दुर्ये मित्रे वरुणे सूक्तवाचः ।
> अवैत्वभ्वं कृणुता वरीयो दिवस्पृथिव्योरवसा मदेम ॥

> *pra ye vasubhya īvadā namo durye mitre varuṇe sūktavācaḥ |*
> *avaitvabhvaṃ kṛṇutā varīyo divaspṛthivyoravasā madema ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-49-5) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Those who bring homage with well-spoken words to the Vasus, to Mitra and Varuṇa at the house — let the mighty one come; make wide space; may we rejoice in the help of Heaven and Earth.")

— there, by अभ्वं महद्धनं तेजो वा (*abhvaṃ mahaddhanaṃ tejo vā*), it means the **great power of splendour**; and

*(Line 2 ends "पूर्वाणि (*pūrvāṇi*)" as printed.)*

> द्यावो न यस्य पनयन्त्यभ्वं भासांसि वस्ते सूर्यो न शुक्रः ।
> वि य इनोत्यजरः पावकोऽश्नस्य चिच्छिश्नथत्पूर्वाणि ॥

> *dyāvo na yasya panayantyabhvaṃ bhāsāṃsi vaste sūryo na śukraḥ |*
> *vi ya inotyajaraḥ pāvako 'śnasya cicchiśnathatpūrvāṇi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ, 6-4-3) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Whose might the heavens, as it were, praise; he clothes himself in lights, bright like the sun; the unaging purifier who drives away, who has pierced even the ancient strongholds of the devourer.")

— there, by अभ्वं महत्कर्म (*abhvaṃ mahatkarma*), it means the **great power of action**. In these two contexts too this word is used in the sense of a good power.

*(Line 1 as printed: "इन्न्वे ३ इव (*innve 3 iva*)", with the pluta numeral 3.)*

> ता इन्न्वे३ इव समना समानीरमीतवर्णा उषसश्चरन्ति ।
> गूहन्तीरभ्वमसितं रुशद्भिः शुक्रास्तनूभिः शुचयो रुचानाः ॥

> *tā innve3 iva samanā samānīramītavarṇā uṣasaścaranti |*
> *gūhantīrabhvamasitaṃ ruśadbhiḥ śukrāstanūbhiḥ śucayo rucānāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-51-9) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Those same Dawns move in the same way, alike, of unchanging colour, hiding the black monster with their gleaming bodies, bright, pure, shining.")

— in this ṛk, by अतिमहत्कृष्णं रूपम् (*atimahatkṛṣṇaṃ rūpam*), it means the **great darkness**. Just as the word **अभ्व (*abhva*)** is used when indicating an elemental power that is distorted and violent, so in the present ṛk too it is used. Here, नः अस्मान् अभ्वात् महतो भयहेतोः पापात् रक्षतं पालयतम् (*naḥ asmān abhvāt mahato bhayahetoḥ pāpāt rakṣataṃ pālayatam*) — "protect us from sin, which is great and a cause of fear": so it is prayed.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** *acarantī* (root *cara gatibhakṣaṇayoḥ*; *śatṛ* for *laṭ*; *ṅīp* in the feminine by *ugitaś ca* (Pā. Sū. 4-1-7 [?], as read); negative *tatpuruṣa*, so by *tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…* (Pā. Sū. 6-2[?]-2) the original accent of the indeclinable first member). *padvantam* (पात् पादः अस्य अस्ति इति पद्वान् (*pāt pādaḥ asya asti iti padvān*); *matup* by *tadasyāsti…*; *va* for *ma* by *jhayaḥ* (Pā. Sū. 8-2-10); udātta on *matup* by *vyatyaya*; *num* augment in the accusative singular as it is *ugit*). *apadī* (न विद्यते पादः ययोस्ते (*na vidyate pādaḥ yayoste*); final acute of the latter member by *nañsubhyām* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172); *pad* for *pāda*; *ṅīp* by *pādo'nyatarasyām* (Pā. Sū. 4-1-8); before the dual ending, by the sūtra *supāṃ suluk*, *pūrvasavarṇa* lengthening).

## Sūkta 185, Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अनेहो दात्रमदितेरनर्वं हुवे स्वर्वदवधं नमस्वत् ।
> तद्रोदसी जनयतं जरित्रे द्यावा रक्षतं पृथिवी नो अभ्वात् ॥ ३ ॥

> *aneho dātramaditeranarvaṃ huve svarvadavadhaṃ namasvat |*
> *tadrodasī janayataṃ jaritre dyāvā rakṣataṃ pṛthivī no abhvāt ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अनेहः । दात्रम् । अदितेः । अनर्वम् । हुवे । स्वःऽवत् । अवधम् । नमस्वत् ।
> तत् । रोदसी इति । जनयतम् । जरित्रे । द्यावा । रक्षतम् । पृथिवी इति । नः । अभ्वात् ॥ ३ ॥

> *anehaḥ | dātram | aditeḥ | anarvam | huve | svaḥ 'vat | avadham | namasvat |*
> *tat | rodasī iti | janayatam | jaritre | dyāvā | rakṣatam | pṛthivī iti | naḥ | abhvāt ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; continues on the next page)*

*Gist:* I call for the wealth belonging to Aditi (Earth, and by implication the sky) — free of sorrow, unfailing, full of fruit like heaven, unharmed, with food; O Heaven and Earth, produce it for the praiser; the refrain as before.

> अदितेः । एतदन्तरिक्षस्याप्युपलक्षणम् । अखण्डनीयायाः पृथिव्यास्तादृशस्यान्तरिक्षस्य च संबन्धि दात्रं धनं हुवे । आह्वयामि । स्पृहयामीत्यर्थः । कीदृशं तद्धनम् । अनेहोऽपापं दुःखरहितं सुखात्मकम् अनर्वमनरणम् । अक्षीणमित्यर्थः ।

> *aditeḥ | etadantarikṣasyāpyupalakṣaṇam | akhaṇḍanīyāyāḥ pṛthivyāstādṛśasyāntarikṣasya ca saṃbandhi dātraṃ dhanaṃ huve | āhvayāmi | spṛhayāmītyarthaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ taddhanam | aneho 'pāpaṃ duḥkharahitaṃ sukhātmakam anarvamanaraṇam | akṣīṇamityarthaḥ |*


### Printed p. 67  (PDF 85)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 2". Bhāṣya of Ṛk 3, concluded.)*

> स्वर्वत् सर्वतः फलभूतेन स्वर्गेण तद्वत् अवधमहिंसितं नमस्वदन्नवत् । ईदृशं धनं हुवे । तदस्माभिः काङ्क्षितमुक्तलक्षणं धनं हे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ जरित्रे स्तोत्रे यजमानाय जनयतम् । उत्पादयतम् । द्यावेत्यादि व्याख्यातम् ॥

> *svarvat sarvataḥ phalabhūtena svargeṇa tadvat avadhamahiṃsitaṃ namasvadannavat | īdṛśaṃ dhanaṃ huve | tadasmābhiḥ kāṅkṣitamuktalakṣaṇaṃ dhanaṃ he rodasī dyāvāpṛthivyau jaritre stotre yajamānāya janayatam | utpādayatam | dyāvetyādi vyākhyātam ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** *aditeḥ* — belonging to the Antarikṣa and the Earth, which are without division (complete); *anehaḥ* — free of sorrow (and therefore of the nature of happiness); *anarvam* — free of decay; *svarvat* — like heaven, full of fruit; *avadham* — unharmed; *namasvat* — furnished with food — such; *dātram* — wealth; *huve* — I desire; *rodasī* — O Heaven and Earth; *tat* — that wealth desired by us; *jaritre* — for the sacrificer who is the maker of praise; *janayatam* — bring into being; *dyāvāpṛthivī* — O Earth and Antarikṣa; *abhvāt* — from sin, the cause of fear; *naḥ* — us; *rakṣatam* — protect.

**Bhāvārtha.** I desire wealth belonging to the Earth and the Antarikṣa, which are of complete nature — wealth that is of the nature of happiness through the absence of sorrow, free of decay, like heaven full of fruit, unharmed, and furnished with food. O Heaven and Earth, bring into being that wealth desired by us for the sacrificer who is the maker of praise. Protect us from sin, the cause of fear.

**English Translation (as printed):** I solicit of Aditi wealth, without pain or decay, like heaven (in its fullness of enjoyment), exempt from injury, and abounding in food : grant, Heaven and Earth, such wealth to him who praises you : defend us, Heaven and Earth, from great (danger).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

In this ṛk there is the prayer **दात्रं हुवे (*dātraṃ huve*)** — "I desire wealth". And **अदितेः (*aditeḥ*), अनेहः (*anehaḥ*), अनर्वं (*anarvaṃ*), स्वर्वत् (*svarvat*), अवधं (*avadhaṃ*), नमस्वत् (*namasvat*)** — all these are epithets describing the nature of the wealth called **दात्रं (*dātraṃ*)**.

**अदितेः (*aditeḥ*)** — for this word Sāyaṇa has stated the meaning thus: एतदन्तरिक्षस्याप्युपलक्षणम् । अखण्डनीयायाः पृथिव्याः तादृशस्यान्तरिक्षस्य च संबन्धि दात्रम् । (*etadantarikṣasyāpyupalakṣaṇam | akhaṇḍanīyāyāḥ pṛthivyāḥ tādṛśasyāntarikṣasya ca saṃbandhi dātram |*) The word *aditi* may be a synonym of the Antarikṣa, and it may also make known the nature of the Earth as undivided. *(continues on the next page)*

---

### Printed p. 68  (PDF 86)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 185". Special Topics of Ṛk 3, continued.)* In the present ṛk it is an epithet of both the Earth and the Antarikṣa, and it has been given the meaning "wealth belonging to both the Earth and the Antarikṣa, which are of undivided nature".

The Nairuktas (the author of the Nirukta) have given for the word *aditi* the meaning **अदीना (*adīnā*)** (Ni. 4-23, as read) — "not poor (not wretched), being of undivided nature, not decaying". This is an epithet that makes known the infinite principle of Agni, of Aditi the mother of the gods, and so on. About the special character of the purport of this word, the scholar Max-Muller has stated thus:

" Aditi, an ancient God or Goddess is in reality, the earliest name invented to express the infinite. That was called A-diti, the unbound, the un-bounded. It is derived from Diti, bond and the negative particle and meant there-fore, originally what is free from bonds of any kind whether of space or time, free from physical weakness, free from moral guilt."

( S. B. E. Vol. XXXII. p. 241. )

To make known the nature of whatever principle is infinite, not limited by place, time and the like, and immeasurable, this word is used in many places in the Ṛksaṃhitā. The ṛṣis who are the seers of the sūktas have expressed a profound idea by the use of this word. Making known the negative sense of the word *diti*, which has the meaning "being bound, being limited, being restrained", he (Max Müller) has said that this is a word which indicates the infinite principle in which there is neither physical limitation nor moral deficiency.

> अदितिर्द्यौरदितिरन्तरिक्षमदितिर्माता स पिता स पुत्रः ।
> विश्वे देवा अदितिः पञ्च जना अदितिर्जातमदितिर्जनित्वम् ॥

> *aditirdyauraditirantarikṣamaditirmātā sa pitā sa putraḥ |*
> *viśve devā aditiḥ pañca janā aditirjātamaditirjanitvam ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ 1-89-10) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Aditi is heaven, Aditi the mid-space, Aditi the mother, she the father, she the son; Aditi is all the gods, Aditi the five peoples; Aditi is what is born, Aditi what is to be born.")

As described in such ṛks, Aditi is the mother of the universe and of the nature of the universe. It may be said that such a deity, who is the mother of the world, presides over the whole physical world and over moral conduct. But it has to be examined whether the word *aditi* makes known the nature of one separate deity, or whether it is an epithet of Heaven and Earth and the like, whose nature is that of Aditi. There is also an opinion that, apart from the 72nd sūkta of Ṛ. Saṃ. 10 (as read: "10-72"), in all other places the word *aditi* makes known only the nature of the Ādityas and others who are the sons of Aditi. For example,

" Aditi is not a prominent deity in the Veda, she is celebrated rather in her sons, Adityas, than in her own person . . . . . . . . "

( S. B. E. XXXII. p. 243 )

---

### Printed p. 69  (PDF 87)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 2". Special Topics of Ṛk 3, continued.)* — such is the opinion of the scholars Max Muller and others. Since that discussion is not so necessary in the present context, this subject will be discussed later at a suitable place. In the present ṛk too there is the prayer that unlimited wealth belonging to Heaven and Earth, whose nature is infinite and undivided, may be obtained.

**अनेहः (*anehaḥ*)** — for this word Sāyaṇa has given the meaning **अपारं (*apāraṃ*)** [sic; the bhāṣya reads अपापं (*apāpaṃ*)], **दुःखरहितं (*duḥkharahitaṃ*), सुखात्मकं (*sukhātmakaṃ*)**. In some places it also means "free of enemies".

**अनर्वं (*anarvaṃ*)** — the meaning is given as **अनरणं, अक्षीणं (*anaraṇaṃ, akṣīṇaṃ*)** | "free of decay". From " **अनर्वा प्रत्यृतोऽन्यस्मिन् (*anarvā pratyṛto 'nyasmin*)** " (Ni. 6-23) one meaning, "without dependence on or subjection to others", and another meaning, "eternal, without old age, death and the like", become possible. The meaning stated in the ṛk containing " **त्रिनाभि चक्रमजरमनर्वं (*trinābhi cakramajaramanarvaṃ*)** " (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-2) belongs to the word *anarva* in the present mantra too. Its special meanings will be explained in the places where the forms **अनर्वन्, अनर्वाणं (*anarvan, anarvāṇaṃ*)** and so on are used.

**स्वर्वत् (*svarvat*)** — it is an epithet of **दात्रं (*dātraṃ*)**, meaning "like heaven, which is full of fruit". What the root of the word **स्वर् (*svar*)** is, and how this word is derived, has been explained earlier together with the Nairukta's etymology **स्वः आदित्यो भवति ; सु अरणः (*svaḥ ādityo bhavati ; su araṇaḥ*)** etc. (Ni. 2-14), and it has been shown that the word *svaḥ* is used in various senses. Just as there is the word *svarvat*, there are also usages such as **स्वर्दृशः, स्वर्विद् (*svardṛśaḥ, svarvid*)** in many places, and they give special meanings suited to their contexts. Here, citing only a few contexts in which the form *svarvat* is used, its meaning is explained.

> या इन्द्र भुज आभरः स्वर्वाँ असुरेभ्यः ।
> स्तोतारमिन्मघवन्नस्य वर्धय ये च त्वे वृक्तबर्हिषः ॥

> *yā indra bhuja ābharaḥ svarvā~ asurebhyaḥ |*
> *stotāraminmaghavannasya vardhaya ye ca tve vṛktabarhiṣaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ Saṃ 8-97-1) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The enjoyments, O Indra, which you, possessed of heaven, brought from the Asuras — with them, O Maghavan, increase the praiser of this one, and those who have spread the sacred grass for you.")

There, स्वर्वान् — सुखवान् ; स्वर्गवान् वा । अथवा स्वः शब्दः सर्वपर्यायः । सर्वं भूतजातं आत्मन एवोत्पन्नत्वात् तद्वान् ॥ (*svarvān — sukhavān ; svargavān vā | athavā svaḥ śabdaḥ sarvaparyāyaḥ | sarvaṃ bhūtajātaṃ ātmana evotpannatvāt tadvān ‖*) That is, since the word *svaḥ* has the meanings heaven, happiness, or all, **svarvān** means "one possessed of happiness, one possessed of heaven, or one who possesses everything".

*(Line 2 as printed: "भेदत्यजैः (*bhedatyajaiḥ*)" and "सर्वतीरपो (*sarvatīrapo*)", without the *v* of *svar-*.)*

> तं शिशीता स्वध्वरं सत्यं सत्वानमृत्वियं ।
> उतो नु चिद्य ओहते आण्डा शुष्णस्य भेदत्यजैः सर्वतीरपो नभन्तामन्यके समे ॥

> *taṃ śiśītā svadhvaraṃ satyaṃ satvānamṛtviyaṃ |*
> *uto nu cidya ohate āṇḍā śuṣṇasya bhedatyajaiḥ sarvatīrapo nabhantāmanyake same ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-40-11) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Sharpen him, of good sacrifices, true, the warrior, the timely one; he who is now praised breaks the eggs of Śuṣṇa; he has won the waters full of light; let all the others perish.")

---

### Printed p. 70  (PDF 88)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 185". Special Topics of Ṛk 3, continued.)* — in such places, when it is an epithet of water as **स्वर्वतीः अपः (*svarvatīḥ apaḥ*)**, the meaning is **दिव्यानि (*divyāni*)**, that is, "water produced in the heavenly world (in Svarga)". This same epithet also describes the nature of the other deities, Agni and the rest. For example,

> ज्योतिष्मतीमदितिं धारयत्क्षितिं स्वर्वतीमा सचेते दिवेदिवे जागृवांसा
> दिवेदिवे ।
> ज्योतिष्मत्क्षत्रमाशाते आदित्या दानुनस्पती ॥

> *jyotiṣmatīmaditiṃ dhārayatkṣitiṃ svarvatīmā sacete divedive jāgṛvāṃsā*
> *divedive |*
> *jyotiṣmatkṣatramāśāte ādityā dānunaspatī ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-136-3) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "They attend on luminous Aditi, who upholds the dwelling-places, possessed of heaven, day after day, the two wakeful ones, day after day; the two Ādityas, lords of gifts, obtain luminous dominion.")

There the word *svarvatī* is an epithet of Aditi. Here the meaning given is **यज्ञनिष्पत्तिद्वारा स्वर्गवतीं (*yajñaniṣpattidvārā svargavatīṃ*)** — "possessed of heaven through the accomplishment of the sacrifice".

*(Line 2 as printed: "समेत्वर्वाजिन्द्र (*sametvarvājindra*)", with ja.)*

> आ ते शुष्मो वृषभ एतु पश्चादोत्तरादधरादा पुरस्तात् ।
> आ विश्वतो अभि समेत्वर्वाजिन्द्र द्युम्नं स्वर्वद्धेह्यस्मे ॥

> *ā te śuṣmo vṛṣabha etu paścādottarādadharādā purastāt |*
> *ā viśvato abhi sametvarvājindra dyumnaṃ svarvaddhehyasme ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-19-9) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "May your vigour, O bull, come from behind, from above, from below, from in front; may it come together towards us from all sides; O Indra, place in us splendour possessed of heaven.")

In such contexts they have given the meaning **सुखयुक्तं धनं (*sukhayuktaṃ dhanaṃ*)** — "wealth joined with happiness". In the same way, in the present ṛk too, "like heaven" means *dātra* (wealth) that gives happiness like the happiness obtained in heaven.

**रोदसी (*rodasī*)** — the etymology and purport of this word have been shown briefly before. Its special meanings will be set out at greater length later in the Special Topics.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** *anehaḥ* (root *hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; *asi* suffix by *nañi hana eha ca* (Uṇ. Sū. 4-[?]); *eha* substitute for the root; loss of the *n* of *nañ* by *nalopo nañaḥ*; *nuṭ* augment by *tasmān nuḍ aci*; loss of the case-ending in the neuter by *svamor napuṃsakāt* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-23, a stray mark between 7 and 1); final acute by the *kṛd*-latter-member accent). *dātram* (root *ḍudāñ dāne*; *tran* suffix by *dādibhyaś chandasi* (Uṇ. Sū. 4-[?]); final acute by *vyatyaya*). *huve* (root *hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca*; *laṭ*, 1st person singular; no *nighāta* at the start of a pāda; final acute by the suffix accent). *svarvat* (स्वर् स्वर्गः अस्य अस्ति इति स्वर्वत् (*svar svargaḥ asya asti iti svarvat*); *matup*, unaccented as *pit*; *svarita* on *svar* by *nañsvarau svaritau* (Phi. Sū. 74)).

Grammar of Ṛk 3, concluded.)* *avadham* (root *hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*; *vadha* substitute with the suffix *ap*; न विद्यते वधः यस्य तत् (*na vidyate vadhaḥ yasya tat*); final acute of the latter member by *nañsubhyām* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-92); *loṭ*, 2nd person dual of the causative; *nighāta* as it follows a non-verb).

## Sūkta 185, Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

*(As printed: "अन्हां (*anhāṃ*)" for *ahnāṃ*, here and in the Pada.)*

> अतप्यमाने अवसावन्ती अनु ष्याम रोदसी देवपुत्रे ।
> उभे देवानामुभयेभिरन्हां द्यावा रक्षतं पृथिवी नो अभ्वात् ॥ ४ ॥

> *atapyamāne avasāvantī anu ṣyāma rodasī devaputre |*
> *ubhe devānāmubhayebhiranhāṃ dyāvā rakṣataṃ pṛthivī no abhvāt ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अतप्यमाने इति । अवसा । अवन्ती इति । अनु । स्याम । रोदसी इति । देवपुत्रे इति देवऽपुत्रे ।
> उभे इति । देवानाम् । उभयेभिः । अन्हाम् । द्यावा । रक्षतम् । पृथिवी इति । नः । अभ्वात् ॥ ४ ॥

> *atapyamāne iti | avasā | avantī iti | anu | syāma | rodasī iti | devaputre iti deva 'putre |*
> *ubhe iti | devānām | ubhayebhiḥ | anhām | dyāvā | rakṣatam | pṛthivī iti | naḥ | abhvāt ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; continues on the next page)*

> अवसा स्वतोऽधिकेन केनचित्कृतेनावनेन समृद्ध्याऽतप्यमाने अनीश्वरे ॥ तप ऐश्वर्यकर्मणि इदं रूपम् ॥ अतप्यमाने अन्यैरपीड्यमाने । अवसान्नेनावन्ती तर्पयन्त्यौ देवपुत्रे देवा व्यवहर्तारो मनुष्याः पुत्रस्थानीया ययोस्तादृश्यौ । लोकद्वयस्था मनुष्याश्च देवाश्च तदुपजीव्यत्वात्तत्पुत्रा इत्युच्यन्ते ।

> *avasā svato 'dhikena kenacitkṛtenāvanena samṛddhyā 'tapyamāne anīśvare ‖ tapa aiśvaryakarmaṇi idaṃ rūpam ‖ atapyamāne anyairapīḍyamāne | avasānnenāvantī tarpayantyau devaputre devā vyavahartāro manuṣyāḥ putrasthānīyā yayostādṛśyau | lokadvayasthā manuṣyāśca devāśca tadupajīvyatvāttatputrā ityucyante |*

### Printed p. 72  (PDF 90)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 185". Bhāṣya of Ṛk 4, concluded.)*

*Gist:* Heaven and Earth, unoppressed (or sovereign through abundance), sustaining all with food, having gods and men as their sons, marked by the twofold qualities of days and nights — may we serve them; the refrain as before.

*(Line 1 as read: "ईदृशावुभे (*īdṛśāvubhe*)".)*

> ईदृशावुभे रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ देवानामह्नाम् । एतद्रात्रेरप्युपलक्षणम् । द्योतमानानामह्नां रात्रीणां च संबन्धिभिरुभयविधैः शीतोष्णादिरूपैर्विलक्षणैर्धर्मैर्निमित्तभूतैः । तेषां लाभायेत्यर्थः । तदर्थं युवामनु स्याम । अनुभवेम । शिष्टो व्याख्यातः ॥

> *īdṛśāvubhe rodasī dyāvāpṛthivyau devānāmahnām | etadrātrerapyupalakṣaṇam | dyotamānānāmahnāṃ rātrīṇāṃ ca saṃbandhibhirubhayavidhaiḥ śītoṣṇādirūpairvilakṣaṇairdharmairnimittabhūtaiḥ | teṣāṃ lābhāyetyarthaḥ | tadarthaṃ yuvāmanu syāma | anubhavema | śiṣṭo vyākhyātaḥ ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** *avasā* — with abundant lordship (prosperity); *atapyamāne* — having no lords higher than themselves; [or: *atapyamāne* — not harmed by others; *avasā* — with food; *avantī* — satisfying (all);] *devaputre* — having the gods (and men) as sons; *devānām* — shining; *ahnām* — of days and nights; *ubhayebhiḥ* — endowed with both kinds of marks, cold, heat and the like; *ubhe rodasī* — both Heaven and Earth; *anu syāma* — may we serve with devotion; *dyāvāpṛthivī* — O Heaven and Earth; *abhvāt* — from fearful calamity; *naḥ* — us; *rakṣatam* — protect.

**Bhāvārtha.** May we serve with devotion both Heaven and Earth, who are not harmed by others, who satisfy all with food, who have the gods and men as their sons, and who are endowed with both kinds of marks, cold, heat and the like, of the shining days and nights. O Heaven and Earth, protect us from fearful calamity.

**English Translation (as printed):** May we ever be (devoted to) that Heaven and Earth, who are not subject to annoyance, who satisfy (all beings) with food, who have the gods (and men) for sons, and who are both endowed with the double (condition) of the divine days (and nights) : defend us, Heaven and Earth, from great (danger).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**अवसा (*avasā*)** — the word *avas* is read among the names of food (Ni. 3-8, as read). On that basis one may give the meaning "with lordship in the form of food" in the present ṛk. Or else, of the Ṛksaṃhitā (ṛk) which the Nirukta's author has cited in another place (Ni. 10-3),

> हिरण्यस्तूपः सवितर्यथा त्वाङ्गिरसो जुह्वे वाजे अस्मिन् ।
> एवा त्वार्चन्नवसे वन्दमानः सोमस्येवांशुं प्रति जागराहम् ॥

> *hiraṇyastūpaḥ savitaryathā tvāṅgiraso juhve vāje asmin |*
> *evā tvārcannavase vandamānaḥ somasyevāṃśuṃ prati jāgarāham ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-149-5) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "As Hiraṇyastūpa, the Āṅgirasa, called on you, O Savitṛ, in this contest, so, praising you for help, worshipping, I keep watch over you as over the stalk of Soma.")

### Printed p. 73  (PDF 91)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 2". Special Topics of Ṛk 4, continued.)* — just as there, for the word **अवसे (*avase*)**, the meaning **अवनाय (*avanāya*)**, that is **रक्षणाय (*rakṣaṇāya*)**, "for protection", has been given, so in the present ṛk too it may be said "with protection (in the form of food)". Sāyaṇa in this context has given the meaning in two ways. First, for the word **अतप्यमाने (*atapyamāne*)** he has given the meaning *anīśvare* ("having no lord"). Explaining how that is so, he has explained **तपेः ऐश्वर्यकर्मणः इदं रूपम् । (*tapeḥ aiśvaryakarmaṇaḥ idaṃ rūpam |*)** — "this is a form of the root *tap* in the sense of lordship". The meaning is: "not subject to any other lord, but themselves lords of the whole world". Then **अवसा अतप्यमाने (*avasā atapyamāne*)** has the purport "lords of the world through abundance of wealth". Secondly: **अतप्यमाने अन्यैरपीड्यमाने । (*atapyamāne anyairapīḍyamāne |*)** — "not harmed by others"; **अवसा अवन्ती (*avasā avantī*)** | — the meaning is "protecting the world with protections".

**देवपुत्रे (*devaputre*)** — **देवाः, व्यवहर्तारो मनुष्याः पुत्रस्थानीयाः ययोस्तादृश्यौ । लोकद्वयस्थाः मनुष्याश्च देवाश्च तदुपजीव्यत्वात् पुत्रा इत्युच्यन्ते । (*devāḥ, vyavahartāro manuṣyāḥ putrasthānīyāḥ yayostādṛśyau | lokadvayasthāḥ manuṣyāśca devāśca tadupajīvyatvāt putrā ityucyante |*)** Since men, relying on the heaven-world, live by the favour of its rain and the like, and the gods, relying on the earth, live by the offering of sacrificial oblations, and so both are dependent on them, Heaven and Earth are addressed as having all these as their sons.

*(Line 1 as printed: "समपतत्ते (*samapatatte*)".)*

> इमौ वै लोकौ सहास्तां तौ व्यैतां नावर्षन्न समपतत्ते पञ्चजना न सम-
> जानत तौ देवाः समनयंस्तौ संयन्तावेतं देवविवाहं व्यवहेताम् ।

> *imau vai lokau sahāstāṃ tau vyaitāṃ nāvarṣanna samapatatte pañcajanā na sama-*
> *jānata tau devāḥ samanayaṃstau saṃyantāvetaṃ devavivāhaṃ vyavahetām |*

(Ai. Brā. 19-5, as read) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "These two worlds were together; they went apart. It did not rain, the sun did not burn; the five peoples did not agree. The gods brought the two together; coming together, they made this divine marriage.")

The conjugal relation of Heaven and Earth explained in this passage, and the point that they themselves are the support of the conduct of all the worlds, have been shown earlier.

> य इमे द्यावापृथिवी जनित्री रूपैरपिंशद्भुवनानि विश्वा ।
> तमद्य होतरिषितो यजीयान् देवं त्वष्टारमिह यक्षि विद्वान् ॥

> *ya ime dyāvāpṛthivī janitrī rūpairapiṃśadbhuvanāni viśvā |*
> *tamadya hotariṣito yajīyān devaṃ tvaṣṭāramiha yakṣi vidvān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 11-1[?]0-9, as printed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "He who adorned with forms these two parents, Heaven and Earth, and all the worlds — that god Tvaṣṭṛ, O Hotṛ, impelled, best at sacrificing, knowing, worship here today.")

There Heaven and Earth are described as the mother and father of the whole universe. The meaning is that they are the begetters of the whole world of gods, men and the rest. Likewise,

> उपहूते द्यावापृथिवी पूर्वजे ऋतावरी देवी देवपुत्रे इति ।

> *upahūte dyāvāpṛthivī pūrvaje ṛtāvarī devī devaputre iti |*

(Śa. Brā. 1-8-1-29) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Invoked are Heaven and Earth, the first-born, the righteous, the goddesses having gods as sons.")

In such Brāhmaṇa sentences too the epithet **देवपुत्रे (*devaputre*)** applied to Heaven and Earth is established. The present ṛk also shows the same point. And the description of their greatness — "Heaven and Earth are the mother and father who are the support and the protectors of the whole universe" — is *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 74  (PDF 92)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 185". Special Topics of Ṛk 4, concluded; the word broken over the page ends "…ragaḷalli", "in the …s".)* — how it is described in the …s will be made known later in this same part, in the Special Topics of Ṛk 1-185-6.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** *atapyamāne* (root *tapa aiśvarye*, *divādi*; *śānac* for *laṭ*; *śyan* by *divādibhyaḥ śyan*; *muk* augment by *āne muk* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-82); negative *tatpuruṣa*, so by *tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…* the original accent of the indeclinable first member; dual form). *avantī* (root *ava rakṣaṇe*; *śatṛ* for *laṭ*; *ṅīp* in the feminine by *ugitaś ca*; before the dual ending (*au*) *pūrvasavarṇa* lengthening by *supāṃ suluk*). *syāma* (root *asa bhuvi*; *liṅ*, 1st person plural; *tiṅanta nighāta*; *ṣ* for the root's *s* by *upasargaprādurbhyām* (Pā. Sū. 8-3-87)). *devaputre* (देवाः पुत्राः ययोस्ते देवपुत्रे (*devāḥ putrāḥ yayoste devaputre*); accent of the first member by *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1); dual form). *ubhayebhiḥ* (*ayac* suffix to *ubha* by *ubhayo'nyatra*; *ais* for *bhis* does not come, as *bahulaṃ chandasi* makes it optional; *e*-substitution; initial acute of the suffix).

*(Ornamental rule "— :0: —": end of Ṛk 4.)*

## Sūkta 185, Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> संगच्छमाने युवती समन्ते स्वसारा जामी पित्रोरुपस्थे ।
> अभिजिघ्रन्ती भुवनस्य नाभिं द्यावा रक्षतं पृथिवी नो अभ्वात् ॥ ५ ॥

> *saṃgacchamāne yuvatī samante svasārā jāmī pitrorupasthe |*
> *abhijighrantī bhuvanasya nābhiṃ dyāvā rakṣataṃ pṛthivī no abhvāt ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥** *(begins at the foot of p. 74; concluded on p. 75)*

> संगच्छमाने इति सम्ऽगच्छमाने । युवती इति । समन्ते इति सम्ऽअन्ते । स्वसारा । जामी इति । पित्रोः । उपऽस्थे ।

> *saṃgacchamāne iti sam 'gacchamāne | yuvatī iti | samante iti sam 'ante | svasārā | jāmī iti | pitroḥ | upa 'sthe |*

---

### Printed p. 75  (PDF 93)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 2". Pada of Ṛk 5, concluded; "nābhiṃ", "rakṣataṃ" as printed.)*

> अभिजिघ्रन्ती इत्यभिऽजिघ्रन्ती । भुवनस्य । नाभिं । द्यावा । रक्षतं । पृथिवी इति । नः । अभ्वात् ॥ ५ ॥

> *abhijighrantī ityabhi 'jighrantī | bhuvanasya | nābhiṃ | dyāvā | rakṣataṃ | pṛthivī iti | naḥ | abhvāt ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed)*

*Gist:* Heaven and Earth, joined by mutual help (rain and oblation) or united after being parted, ever young, sisters born together of Prajāpati, sitting in the lap of the parents and touching the water, the bond of beings — protect us.

> संगच्छमाने परस्परमुपकारित्वेन सह युज्यमाने । वृष्टिहविषोश्च परस्परमुपकार्योपकारकभावः । यद्वा । पूर्वं संसृष्टे एव सत्यौ पश्चाद्वियुज्य वृष्टिहविषी अकुर्वन्त्यौ पश्चान्मनुष्यैः प्रार्थितैर्देवैर्विवाहिते सत्यौ संगते अभूतामित्यर्थः । अयमर्थो द्यावापृथिवी सहास्ताम् । तै. ब्रा. १-१-३-२ । इत्यादि ब्राह्मणे समाम्नातः । युवती नित्यतरुण्यौ मिश्रयन्त्यौ वा सर्वेषु भावेषु समन्ते समानान्तिके समानपर्यन्ते वा स्वसारा परस्परं स्वसृभूते जामी बन्धुभूते । प्रजापतेः सकाशात्सहोत्पन्नत्वात्परस्परं जामित्वम् । तथा च निगमौ दिवं च पृथिवीं चान्तरिक्षमथो स्वः । ऋ. १०-१९०-३ । यतो द्यावापृथिवी निष्टतक्षुः । ऋ. १०-३१-७ । इति । पित्रोः सर्वस्य पितृस्थानीययोः पालकयोस्तयोरुपस्थ उत्सङ्गे स्थितं भुवनस्य भूतजातस्य नाभिं बन्धकमुदकमभिजिघ्रन्ती अभिघ्राणं कुर्वन्त्यौ स्पृशन्त्यौ । समानमेतदुदकम् । ऋ. १-१६४-५१ । इत्यादिमन्त्रवर्णादुभयोरुदकप्रदत्वं प्रसिद्धम् । ईदृश्यौ नो रक्षतम् ॥

> *saṃgacchamāne parasparamupakāritvena saha yujyamāne | vṛṣṭihaviṣośca parasparamupakāryopakārakabhāvaḥ | yadvā | pūrvaṃ saṃsṛṣṭe eva satyau paścādviyujya vṛṣṭihaviṣī akurvantyau paścānmanuṣyaiḥ prārthitairdevairvivāhite satyau saṃgate abhūtāmityarthaḥ | ayamartho dyāvāpṛthivī sahāstām | tai. brā. 1-1-3-2 | ityādi brāhmaṇe samāmnātaḥ | yuvatī nityataruṇyau miśrayantyau vā sarveṣu bhāveṣu samante samānāntike samānaparyante vā svasārā parasparaṃ svasṛbhūte jāmī bandhubhūte | prajāpateḥ sakāśātsahotpannatvātparasparaṃ jāmitvam | tathā ca nigamau divaṃ ca pṛthivīṃ cāntarikṣamatho svaḥ | ṛ. 10-190-3 | yato dyāvāpṛthivī niṣṭatakṣuḥ | ṛ. 10-31-7 | iti | pitroḥ sarvasya pitṛsthānīyayoḥ pālakayostayorupastha utsaṅge sthitaṃ bhuvanasya bhūtajātasya nābhiṃ bandhakamudakamabhijighrantī abhighrāṇaṃ kurvantyau spṛśantyau | samānametadudakam | ṛ. 1-164-51 | ityādimantravarṇādubhayorudakapradatvaṃ prasiddham | īdṛśyau no rakṣatam ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** *saṃgacchamāne* — (from the wish to help each other) always being together; *yuvatī* — ever young; *samante* — of equal pervasion; *svasārā* — loving each other like elder and younger sisters; *jāmī* — (being children of Prajāpati) having kinship with each other; *pitroḥ* — of the father and mother, or of the protectors; *upasthe* — in the lap (on the thigh), being there; *bhuvanasya* — for all living beings in the world; *nābhim* — the water that is their support; *abhijighrantī* — touching (holding) — being such; *dyāvāpṛthivī* — O Heaven and Earth; *abhvāt* — from great fear; *naḥ* — us; *rakṣatam* — protect.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Heaven and Earth, you two are always together and ever young. Being children of Prajāpati, you are both loving like sisters and kin to each other. You hold the water that is the support of all living beings. You, being such, protect us from great fear.

### Printed p. 76  (PDF 94)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 185". Ṛk 5, continued.)*

**English Translation (as printed):** Going always together, equally young, and of the like termination, sisters, and kindred, and scenting the navel of the world, placed on their lap as its parents : defend us, Heaven and Earth, from great danger.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

The ṛṣi Agastya has shown his skill of composition well in this sūkta. The extraordinary deeds of Heaven and Earth, the deities of this sūkta, and their protection of the world are described with a most excellent and natural group of words. That is, in describing or praising these deities the words **अतप्यमाने, अवन्ती, देवपुत्रे, संगच्छमाने, युवती, समन्ते, स्वसारा, जामी, अभिजिघ्रन्ती, उर्वी, सद्मनी, बृहती, जनित्री, सुप्रतीके, पृथ्वी, बहुले, दूरेअन्ते, सुभगे, सुप्रतूर्ती (*atapyamāne, avantī, devaputre, saṃgacchamāne, yuvatī, samante, svasārā, jāmī, abhijighrantī, urvī, sadmanī, bṛhatī, janitrī, supratīke, pṛthvī, bahule, dūreante, subhage, supratūrtī*)** have been used. Besides being natural, of deep meaning and suited to the context, the use of these words in praising the qualities of the deities gives depth and devotional feeling to the poetry. So there is no need to say separately that the composition of the ṛks of this sūkta is of a very high standard. Besides this, the profound truths set forth in the form of question and answer in the first ṛk of this sūkta, and the similes used here and there, are excellent examples of the ṛṣi's poetic skill of composition.

**संगच्छमाने (*saṃgacchamāne*)** — this word means "going together" or "being together". Sāyaṇa in his bhāṣya has said: **परस्परमुपकारित्वेन सह युज्यमाने । वृष्टिहविषोश्च परस्परमुपकार्योपकारकभावः । यद्वा । पूर्वं संसृष्टे एव सत्यौ पश्चाद्वियुज्य वृष्टिहविषी अकुर्वन्त्यौ पश्चान्मनुष्यैः प्रार्थितैर्देवैर्विवाहिते सत्यौ संगते अभूतामित्याहुः । (*parasparamupakāritvena saha yujyamāne | vṛṣṭihaviṣośca parasparamupakāryopakārakabhāvaḥ | yadvā | pūrvaṃ saṃsṛṣṭe eva satyau paścādviyujya vṛṣṭihaviṣī akurvantyau paścānmanuṣyaiḥ prārthitairdevairvivāhite satyau saṃgate abhūtāmityāhuḥ |*)** That is, "they are together in order to help each other". Here the help means the rain of water and the oblation offered to the deities. Because of rain, crops and the like grow and the grain and other things needed for the oblation are obtained; so it is described here that rain and oblation are obtained through mutual help. As to what relation there is between Heaven and Earth and rain, the ṛṣi has explained that too in this very ṛk by the sentence **अभिजिघ्रन्ती भुवनस्य नाभिं (*abhijighrantī bhuvanasya nābhiṃ*)**. That is, because the clouds in the Antarikṣa (*dyāvā*) gather together and produce rain, crops and the like grow on the earth (*pṛthivī*). So the purport is that Heaven and Earth are of mutual help both for rain and for the growth of crops and the like.

Or else: though Prajāpati created Heaven and Earth together, that is, at one time, they were apart, separated by other causes, and the rain, most necessary for the world, *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 77  (PDF 95)

*(Header as printed: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 3, Varga 2" — the Adhyāya digit is printed 3 here, 5 on the neighbouring odd pages. Special Topics of Ṛk 5, continued.)* — when they did not produce it, the gods, at the prayer of men, accomplished the marriage of Heaven and Earth and made them become one: this other meaning too Sāyaṇa has stated. On the point that Heaven and Earth were together, Sāyaṇa has cited the Taittirīya-Brāhmaṇa sentence

> द्यावापृथिवी सहास्ताम् । ते वियती अब्रूताम् ॥

> *dyāvāpṛthivī sahāstām | te viyatī abrūtām ‖*

(Tai. Brā. 1-1-3 2, as printed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Heaven and Earth were together; going apart, they said …")

On the point that Prajāpati created Heaven and Earth there is the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa sentence

> प्रजापतिरकामयत प्रजायेय भूयान्त्स्यामिति स तपोऽतप्यत स तपस्तप्त्वेमाँल्लोकानसृजत पृथिवीमन्तरिक्षं दिवम् ।

> *prajāpatirakāmayata prajāyeya bhūyāntsyāmiti sa tapo'tapyata sa tapastaptvemā~llokānasṛjata pṛthivīmantarikṣaṃ divam |*

(Ai. Brā. 25-7) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Prajāpati desired, 'May I be propagated, may I become many'; he performed austerity; having performed austerity he created these worlds — the earth, the mid-space, the sky.")

The purport of this mantra is: Prajāpati (Brahmā), desiring to create, performed austerity; then by the greatness of that austerity he created these worlds, that is, the worlds called Earth, Antarikṣa and Svarga. This point is found in the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā itself, namely,

> सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ धाता यथापूर्वमकल्पयत् ।
> दिवं च पृथिवीं चान्तरिक्षमथो स्वः ॥

> *sūryācandramasau dhātā yathāpūrvamakalpayat |*
> *divaṃ ca pṛthivīṃ cāntarikṣamatho svaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-190-3) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The Ordainer fashioned sun and moon as before, and heaven and earth and the mid-space, and the light.")

— in this ṛk it is said that Brahmā, that is, the Creator, when creating, created the sun and moon and the worlds called Svarga, Earth and Antarikṣa. Besides this,

> जनिता दिवो जनिता पृथिव्याः पिबा सोमं मदाय कं शतक्रतो ।

> *janitā divo janitā pṛthivyāḥ pibā somaṃ madāya kaṃ śatakrato |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-36-4) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Begetter of heaven, begetter of earth — drink the Soma for exhilaration, O Śatakratu.")

> यन्मातरं च पितरं च साकमजनयथास्तन्वः स्वायाः ।

> *yanmātaraṃ ca pitaraṃ ca sākamajanayathāstanvaḥ svāyāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-54-3) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "When you begot the mother and the father together from your own body.")

— in such ṛks it is said that Indra himself created Heaven and Earth. But since in many contexts the identity of Indra and Prajāpati is stated, there is no contradiction in this. And —

> सोमापूषणा जनना रयीणां जनना दिवो जनना पृथिव्याः ।
> जातौ विश्वस्य भुवनस्य गोपौ देवा अकृण्वन्नमृतस्य नाभिम् ।

> *somāpūṣaṇā jananā rayīṇāṃ jananā divo jananā pṛthivyāḥ |*
> *jātau viśvasya bhuvanasya gopau devā akṛṇvannamṛtasya nābhim |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-40-1) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Soma and Pūṣan, begetters of riches, begetters of heaven, begetters of earth; born as guardians of the whole world, the gods made them the navel of immortality.")

— in this ṛk it is said that the deities Soma and Pūṣan produced Heaven and Earth.

(Ṛ. ### Printed p. 79  (PDF 97)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 2". Special Topics of Ṛk 5, continued.)* — so asking himself, the ṛṣi himself has given the answer there: that god who is one, with eyes everywhere (that is, able to see everything, at all times and in all places), with face, arms and feet in all directions, that is, almighty (the Supreme Self named Viśvakarmā), created these Heaven and Earth.

On the marriage of Heaven and Earth, the Aitareya-Brāhmaṇa says thus —

*(Line 1 as printed here: "समतपत्ते (*samatapatte*)"; on p. 73 the same passage was read "समपतत्ते (*samapatatte*)".)*

> इमौ वै लोकौ सहास्तां तौ व्यैतां नावर्षन्न समतपत्ते पञ्चजना न
> समजानत तौ देवाः समनयंस्तौ संयन्तावेतं देवविवाहं व्यवहेताम् ॥

> *imau vai lokau sahāstāṃ tau vyaitāṃ nāvarṣanna samatapatte pañcajanā na*
> *samajānata tau devāḥ samanayaṃstau saṃyantāvetaṃ devavivāhaṃ vyavahetām ‖*

(Ai. Brā. 19-5) (Gloss as on p. 73.)

That is: formerly these worlds, that is, Heaven and Earth, were together in one place; by other causes they became separate. Then the coming of rain stopped; there was no sunshine either. Then the five peoples, that is, those of the Brāhmaṇa and other varṇas and all living beings, were distressed; they had no happiness. Then the gods, for the welfare of the world, performed the marriage of Heaven and Earth according to divine rule, united them and brought happiness to the world — so it is said. This same thing Sāyaṇa has stated in his bhāṣya.

**युवती (*yuvatī*)** — "youthful, young". It is customary for the ṛṣis generally to describe all the deities as youthful, that is, as always endowed with strength and beauty without being subject to the changes of old age. Especially in regard to the deities Agni, Indra, Uṣas, the Aśvins, Heaven and Earth and the like, this epithet is used much.

> अग्निनाग्निः समिध्यते कविर्गृहपतिर्युवा ।

> *agnināgniḥ samidhyate kavirgṛhapatiryuvā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-12-6) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Agni is kindled by Agni, the sage, the lord of the house, the youthful one.")

— in this ṛk this word refers to Agni;

> पुरां भिन्दुर्युवा कविरमितौजा अजायत ।

> *purāṃ bhinduryuvā kaviramitaujā ajāyata |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-11-4; the reference is printed below the next line of prose) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The breaker of forts, youthful, the sage, of boundless might, was born.")

— here to Indra;

*(As read: "पूर्व्येभिरेन्वैः (*pūrvyebhirenvaiḥ*) [?]" (the ligature looks like n + v) and "यु (*yu*)[?]वाना (*vānā*)" (a mark like *śi* between *yu* and *vā*).)*

> युवं तुग्राय पूर्व्येभिरेन्वैः [?] पुनर्मन्यावभवतं यु[?]वाना ।

> *yuvaṃ tugrāya pūrvyebhirenvaiḥ [?] punarmanyāvabhavataṃ yu[?]vānā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-14) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "You two, for Tugra, with your ancient courses, became again worthy of honour, O youthful ones.")

— here to the Aśvins;

> आ नो जने श्रवयतं युवाना श्रुतं मे मित्रावरुणा हवेमा ।

> *ā no jane śravayataṃ yuvānā śrutaṃ me mitrāvaruṇā havemā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-62-5) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Make us famous among the people, O youthful ones; hear these calls of mine, O Mitra and Varuṇa.")

— in such ṛks to Mitra and Varuṇa;

> एषा दिवो दुहिता प्रत्यदर्शि व्युच्छन्ती युवतिः शुक्रवासाः ।

> *eṣā divo duhitā pratyadarśi vyucchantī yuvatiḥ śukravāsāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-113-7) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "This daughter of heaven has appeared, shining forth, a young woman in bright garments.")

— in such ṛks to the deity Uṣas, *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 80  (PDF 98)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 185". Special Topics of Ṛk 5, continued.)*

> उत स्वसारा युवती भवन्ती आदु ब्रुवाते मिथुनानि नाम ।

> *uta svasārā yuvatī bhavantī ādu bruvāte mithunāni nāma |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-54-7) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "And, being sisters, young women, they then call each other by paired names.")

— in such ṛks this word is used in reference to Heaven and Earth also.

**समन्ते — समानान्तिके समानपर्यन्ते वा । (*samante — samānāntike samānaparyante vā |*)** The two worlds called Heaven and Earth have one and the same end, or have equal pervasion; that is, the other world is as wide as the extent of the one world. The purport is that the extent of both is the same. In the Taittirīya-saṃhitā (in the Yajurveda) —

> अन्तर्हितो हि देवलोको मनुष्यलोकात् ।

> *antarhito hi devaloko manuṣyalokāt |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-1.1, as printed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "For the world of the gods is hidden from (set within) the world of men.")

— that is, it is said that the world of men (the earth) and the world of the gods (Svarga) are interwoven, the one within the other. That is, the purport is that the earth and Svarga (the Antarikṣa) are of equal extent.

**स्वसारा — परस्परं स्वसृभूते । (*svasārā — parasparaṃ svasṛbhūte |*)** Here the use of the word *svasṛ* does not indicate the meaning "elder and younger sisters". But the purport is: "having mutual affection like elder and younger sisters, and having an equal place (rank)". The words **युवती, समन्ते, स्वसारा (*yuvatī, samante, svasārā*)** in the present ṛk are words that indicate the very meaning of the epithets of Heaven and Earth such as **दूरेअन्ते (*dūreante*)** in the 7th ṛk; they are seen also in such ṛks as —

> समान्या वियुते दूरे अन्ते ध्रुवे पदे तस्थतुर्जागरूके ।
> उत स्वसारा युवती भवन्ती आदु ब्रुवाते मिथुनानि नाम ॥

> *samānyā viyute dūre ante dhruve pade tasthaturjāgarūke |*
> *uta svasārā yuvatī bhavantī ādu bruvāte mithunāni nāma ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-54-7) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Sharing one end, yet apart, with far-off ends, the two watchful ones have stood in a firm place; and, being sisters, young women, they then call each other by paired names.")

**जामी (*jāmī*)** — having mutual kinship. Since Prajāpati alone created Heaven and Earth at one and the same time, it is explained that they have kinship with each other. The word *jāmi* is read among the names of water (Ni. 2-24, as printed). But here the bhāṣyakāra has given the meaning "kinship". Yāska in his Nirukta —

*(As printed: "जामयो (*jāmayo*)".)*

> न जामयो भगिन्यै । जामिरन्येऽस्यां जनयन्ति जामपत्यम् । जमतेर्वा
> स्याद्गतिकर्मणो निर्गमनप्राया भवति ॥

> *na jāmayo bhaginyai | jāmiranye 'syāṃ janayanti jāmapatyam | jamatervā*
> *syādgatikarmaṇo nirgamanaprāyā bhavati ‖*

(Ni. 3-7) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Not to the sister (*jāmi*): she is *jāmi* because others beget offspring (*jā*) in her; or it may be from *jam*, a verb of going: she is one who mostly goes out.")

That is, the word *jāmi* has the meaning *bhaginī* (sister, *sahodarī*), because others, that is the husband, produce sons in this woman: hence the name *jāmi*. Or, since the word *jāmi* has the sense of going — that is, this woman after marriage leaves the house of the father where she was born and, of the husband (*gaṇḍa*) *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 81  (PDF 99)

*(As read: "पितृस्थानिययोः (*pitṛsthāniyayoḥ*)", with short i, where the bhāṣya has *pitṛsthānīyayoḥ*.)*

**पित्रोः उपस्थे — पित्रोः सर्वस्य पितृस्थानिययोः पालकयोस्तयोरुपस्थ उत्सङ्गे स्थितम् । (*pitroḥ upasthe — pitroḥ sarvasya pitṛsthāniyayoḥ pālakayostayorupastha utsaṅge sthitam |*)** They have given the meaning "being in the lap of these Heaven and Earth, who are protectors, like father and mother, of all the living beings in the world". On the point that these Heaven and Earth are the father and mother of the world —

> उरुव्यचसा महिनी असश्चता पिता माता च भुवनानि रक्षतः ।

> *uruvyacasā mahinī asaścatā pitā mātā ca bhuvanāni rakṣataḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-160-2) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The wide-extending, mighty, inexhaustible father and mother protect the worlds.")

> तन्नो वातो मयोभु वातु भेषजं तन्माता पृथिवी तत्पिता द्यौः ।

> *tanno vāto mayobhu vātu bheṣajaṃ tanmātā pṛthivī tatpitā dyauḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-89-4) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "May the wind waft to us that healing remedy, may mother Earth, may father Heaven (grant) that.")

> इदं द्यावापृथिवी सत्यमस्तु पितर्मातर्यदिहोपब्रुवे वाम् ।

> *idaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī satyamastu pitarmātaryadihopabruve vām |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-185-11) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "O Heaven and Earth, may this be true, O father, O mother, which I here address to you.")

> आ सुष्टुती नमसा वर्तयध्यै द्यावा वाजाय पृथिवी अमृध्रे ।
> पिता माता मधुवचाः सुहस्ता भरेभरे नो यशसावविष्टाम् ॥

> *ā suṣṭutī namasā vartayadhyai dyāvā vājāya pṛthivī amṛdhre |*
> *pitā mātā madhuvacāḥ suhastā bharebhare no yaśasāvaviṣṭām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-43-2) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "With fair praise and homage I would turn hither, for strength, Heaven and Earth, the unfailing; may the father and mother, sweet-spoken, fair-handed, glorious, help us in every contest.")

— in these and many other ṛks it is explained that the Earth is mother to the whole world and Svarga (the Antarikṣa) is the father. Just as father and mother seat their sons on their lap, so Heaven and Earth, the father and mother of the world, hold on their lap, that is, in the Antarikṣa, for the nourishment of the world, the water of the clouds gathered for the rain, which stands in the place of a son: so the ṛṣi has described.

**अभिजिघ्रन्ती — अभिघ्राणं कुर्वन्त्यौ, स्पृशन्त्यौ । (*abhijighrantī — abhighrāṇaṃ kurvantyau, spṛśantyau |*)** Sāyaṇa's explanation is "those who smell, that is, those who touch". But this meaning does not fit here; and why the ṛṣi has used this word, what his intention is, cannot be clearly known. Since this use of the word is found nowhere else in the Ṛgveda, it is not possible to know the opinion of other ṛṣis on the meaning of this word. Since generally in the world people are seen here and there smelling an object dear to them and keeping it safely with themselves, the ṛṣi's intention may be that these Heaven and Earth hold lovingly within themselves the water in the mass of clouds, for the use of the people.

**भुवनस्य नाभिं (*bhuvanasya nābhiṃ*)** — the word *bhuvana* is read among the names of water (Ni. 2-24, as printed). And, *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 82  (PDF 100)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 185". Special Topics of Ṛk 5, concluded; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā begins.)*

*(As printed: "वयं न (*vayaṃ na*)" in line 2.)*

> नीचीनबारं वरुणः कवन्धं प्र ससर्ज रोदसी अन्तरिक्षं ।
> तेन विश्वस्य भुवनस्य राजा वयं न वृष्टिर्व्युनत्ति भूम ॥

> *nīcīnabāraṃ varuṇaḥ kavandhaṃ pra sasarja rodasī antarikṣaṃ |*
> *tena viśvasya bhuvanasya rājā vayaṃ na vṛṣṭirvyunatti bhūma ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-85-3) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Varuṇa poured out the cask with its opening downward over the two worlds and the mid-space; with it the king of the whole world moistens the ground, as rain the barley.")

— for the word **भुवनस्य (*bhuvanasya*)** in this ṛk Yāska has given the derivation **सर्वस्य भुवसन्य (*sarvasya bhuvasanya*)** [sic] (**भूतजातकस्योदकस्य वा (*bhūtajātakasyodakasya vā*)**) (as printed) (Ni. 10-4): *bhuvana* means the world or the living beings of the world. But here the bhāṣyakāra has taken the meaning "water". For the word *nābhi* Yāska has given the derivation —

> संबन्धनान्नाभिः सन्नहनान्नाभ्या सन्नद्धा गर्भा जायन्त इत्याहुरेतस्मादेव
> ज्ञातीन् सनाभय इत्याचक्षते ।

> *saṃbandhanānnābhiḥ sannahanānnābhyā sannaddhā garbhā jāyanta ityāhuretasmādeva*
> *jñātīn sanābhaya ityācakṣate |*

(Ni. 4-20) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "*Nābhi* (navel) from binding together: they say that embryos are born bound by the navel; for this very reason kinsmen are called *sanābhi*.")

That is, for the word *nābhi* the meaning "the middle region which joins together" may be given. Sāyaṇa, explaining the ṛk

> पृच्छामि त्वा परमन्तं पृथिव्याः पृच्छामि यत्र भुवनस्य नाभिः ।

> *pṛcchāmi tvā paramantaṃ pṛthivyāḥ pṛcchāmi yatra bhuvanasya nābhiḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-34) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "I ask you about the farthest end of the earth; I ask where is the navel of the world.")

— has explained: **भुवनस्य भूतजातस्य नाभिः संनाहो बन्धनम् । यत्र सर्वं संनद्धं भवति तमित्यर्थः (*bhuvanasya bhūtajātasya nābhiḥ saṃnāho bandhanam | yatra sarvaṃ saṃnaddhaṃ bhavati tamityarthaḥ*)** — that is, the place where everything is joined and gathered together has the name *nābhi*. In the present ṛk the purport is: the water of the clouds gathered together in one place for the sake of rain, that is, the water which is joined together.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly; continues on the next page).** *saṃgacchamāne* (root *gamḷ gatau*; with the upasarga *sam*, *ātmanepada* by *samo gamyṛcchibhyām* (Pā. Sū. 1-3-29); *śānac* for *laṭ*; by *tāsyanudāttet…* the *lasārvadhātuka* is unaccented, so the root accent remains; in the compound the original accent of the *kṛt* final member; *ṭāp* in the feminine). *yuvatī* (suffix *ti* to *yuvan* in the feminine by *yūnas tiḥ* (Pā. Sū. 4-1-77); by *an* (Pā. Sū. 6-4-167) *prakṛtibhāva*, so no *ṭi*-loss; loss of *n* by *nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya* (Pā. Sū. 8-[?]-7); final acute by the suffix accent; in the dual *pūrvasavarṇa* lengthening by *supāṃ suluk*). *samante* (समानम् अन्तिकं ययोस्ते समन्ते (*samānam antikaṃ yayoste samante*); loss of the *k* of *antika*; *sa* for *samāna* by *samānasya chandasy…* (as printed; Pā. Sū. 6-3-84); first-member accent by *bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā…* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1)).
