## Sūkta 185, Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

*(As printed: "पथिवी (*pathivī*)" in line 2, without *ṛ*; the Pada has पृथिवी.)*

> उर्वी सद्मनी बृहती ऋतेन हुवे देवानामवसा जनित्री ।
> दधाते ये अमृतं सुप्रतीके द्यावा रक्षतं पथिवी नो अभ्वात् ॥ ६ ॥

> *urvī sadmanī bṛhatī ṛtena huve devānāmavasā janitrī |*
> *dadhāte ye amṛtaṃ supratīke dyāvā rakṣataṃ pathivī no abhvāt ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उर्वी इति । सद्मनी इति । बृहती इति । ऋतेन । हुवे । देवानां । अवसा । जनित्री इति ।
> दधाते इति । ये इति । अमृतं । सुप्रतीके इति सुऽप्रतीके । द्यावा । रक्षतं । पृथिवी इति । नः । अभ्वात् ॥ ६ ॥

> *urvī iti | sadmanī iti | bṛhatī iti | ṛtena | huve | devānāṃ | avasā | janitrī iti |*
> *dadhāte iti | ye iti | amṛtaṃ | supratīke iti su 'pratīke | dyāvā | rakṣataṃ | pṛthivī iti | naḥ | abhvāt ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed)*

*Gist:* By the sacrifice and for the gods' satisfaction I invoke the wide, great Heaven and Earth, the abode of all, the begetters of rain and crops, who hold the water (*amṛta*).

> उर्वी विस्तीर्णे सद्मनी सदनाधारभूते बृहती महत्यौ महानुभावे देवानां । उपलक्षणमेतत् । देवमनुष्यादीनामवसा प्रीत्या निमित्तेन जनित्री वृष्टिसस्ययोर्जनित्र्यौ । वृष्ट्यादेर्देवानामवसा तर्पणेन निमित्तेन ऋतेन यज्ञेन च निमित्तभूतेन हुवे । आह्वयामि । देवानां हविरर्थमस्मद्यज्ञायेत्यर्थः । ये सुप्रतीके शोभनरूपे अमृतमुदकं दधाते धारयतः ते युवामाह्वयामि । शिष्टं स्पष्टम् ॥

> *urvī vistīrṇe sadmanī sadanādhārabhūte bṛhatī mahatyau mahānubhāve devānāṃ | upalakṣaṇametat | devamanuṣyādīnāmavasā prītyā nimittena janitrī vṛṣṭisasyayorjanitryau | vṛṣṭyāderdevānāmavasā tarpaṇena nimittena ṛtena yajñena ca nimittabhūtena huve | āhvayāmi | devānāṃ havirarthamasmadyajñāyetyarthaḥ | ye supratīke śobhanarūpe amṛtamudakaṃ dadhāte dhārayataḥ te yuvāmāhvayāmi | śiṣṭaṃ spaṣṭam ‖*

---

### Printed p. 84  (PDF 102)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 185". Ṛk 6, continued.)*

**Pratipadārtha.** *urvī* — exceedingly wide; *sadmanī* — the support of all; *bṛhatī* — of great dignity; *janitrī* — mothers (of rain and crops and the like); (and) *ye* — who; *supratīke* — being of beautiful form; *amṛtam* — the rain-water, like nectar; *dadhāte* — hold — such Heaven and Earth; *devānām* — of the gods (and men); *avasā* — which causes satisfaction; *ṛtena* — for the sake of the sacrifice; *huve* — I call with praise; *dyāvāpṛthivī* — O Heaven and Earth; *abhvāt* — from great fear; *naḥ* — us; *rakṣatam* — protect.

**Bhāvārtha.** Heaven and Earth, who are exceedingly wide, the support of all, of great dignity, mothers of rain and crops and the like, of beautiful form, and who hold the rain-water that is like nectar — them I call with prayer for the sake of the sacrifice which is the cause of the satisfaction of gods and men. O Heaven and Earth, save us from great calamity and protect us.

**English Translation (as printed):** I Invoke [sic] to the sacrifice, for the preservation of gods (and men), the two vast, all supporting, and mighty parents (of the rain and corn) ; who, beautiful in form, sustain ambrosial (showers); defend us, Heaven and Earth, from great danger.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

As in the previous ṛk, in this ṛk too there is a description of the qualities of Heaven and Earth. It may be said that the pleasing word-arrangements found in the Vedas began with Heaven and Earth themselves. In nature there are no other things so firmly connected as Heaven and Earth. Therefore this gradually gave room to the idea that the two are a married couple. In the Ṛgveda there are only six sūktas addressed to Heaven and Earth (*dyāvāpṛthivī*). There is no sūkta praising the deity Dyu alone. Only one small sūkta of three ṛks (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-84-3) praises the Earth; in that too there is a mention of the deity Dyu.

**उर्वी (*urvī*)** — the word *urvī* is formed from the word *uru*. The word *uru* is stated among the names of "many" (*bahu*) (Ni. 2-13, as read). The meaning is "exceedingly wide".

**सद्मनी (*sadmanī*)** — Yāska has read the word *sadma* among the names of a house (Ni. 3-13). Here *sadmanī* means the earth which has houses fit for dwelling.

---

### Printed p. 85  (PDF 103)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 3". Special Topics of Ṛk 6, continued.)*

**बृहती (*bṛhatī*)** — "large", or "having greater greatness".

**देवनामवसा जनित्री (*devanāmavasā janitrī*)** (as printed, *devanām-* for *devānām-*) — Sāyaṇa's explanation is: "who, for the protection of the gods (and men), pour down rain and through it bring about the growth of crops". Since the word **जनित्री (*janitrī*)** means "producing", it may mean "who produce creatures, living beings, crops and the like".

**ऋतेन (*ṛtena*)** — we have explained the extended meaning of the word *ṛta* many times before. Though the word *ṛta* has the meanings truth, water, sacrifice and the like, here Sāyaṇa has given the meaning "sacrifice" for this word.

**दधाते ये अमृतम् (*dadhāte ye amṛtam*)** — the word *amṛta* is read among the names of water (Ni. 2-14, as read) and among the names of gold (Ni. 2-10). Besides this, Yāska —

*(As read: the first word "रुश[?]वत्सा (*ruśa[?]vatsā*)" — the conjunct looks like *pv*/*dv*; "आरैगु (*āraigu*)" as printed.)*

> रुश[?]वत्सा रुशती श्वेत्यागादारैगु कृष्णा सदनान्यस्याः ।
> समानबन्धू अमृते अनूची द्यावा वर्णं चरत आमिनाने ॥

> *ruśa[?]vatsā ruśatī śvetyāgādāraigu kṛṣṇā sadanānyasyāḥ |*
> *samānabandhū amṛte anūcī dyāvā varṇaṃ carata āmināne ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-113-2) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The bright one with a bright calf, the white one, has come; the dark one has vacated her seats for her. Of common kin, immortal, following each other, the two, changing their colour, move across the sky.")

— citing this ṛk, he has explained for the word **अमृते (*amṛte*)** **अमरधर्माणौ (*amaradharmāṇau*)** — "those who never die" (Ni. 2-20); and

*(As printed: "भुपनस्य (*bhupanasya*)" in line 2.)*

> यत्रा सुपर्णा अमृतस्य भागमनिमेषं विदथाभिस्वरन्ति ।
> इनो विश्वस्य भुपनस्य गोपाः स मा धीरः पाकमत्रा विवेश ॥

> *yatrā suparṇā amṛtasya bhāgamanimeṣaṃ vidathābhisvaranti |*
> *ino viśvasya bhupanasya gopāḥ sa mā dhīraḥ pākamatrā viveśa ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-21) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Where the fair-winged ones unceasingly sing forth at the assemblies of their share of immortality, there the lord, the guardian of the whole world, the wise one, has entered me, the simple one.")

— citing this ṛk, he has also explained the meaning **अमृतस्य उदकस्य (*amṛtasya udakasya*)** (Ni. 3-11). In the present ṛk *amṛta* means water itself. The purport is: "who hold (in the Antarikṣa, in the form of clouds) the rain-water that is the support of all living beings".

**सुप्रतीके — प्रतीकं मुखं प्रकाशाख्यं दर्शनं वा । (*supratīke — pratīkaṃ mukhaṃ prakāśākhyaṃ darśanaṃ vā |*)** The word *pratīka* means either "face" or "radiant manifestation". The Nirukta's author —

*(As printed: "सुवर्ण्यो३ (*suvarṇyo3*)" with the pluta numeral 3, *v* where *suparṇyo* would be expected.)*

> यावन्मात्रमुषसो न प्रतीकं सुवर्ण्यो३ वसते मातरिश्वः ।
> तावद्दधात्युप यज्ञमायन् ब्राह्मणो होतुरवरो निषीदन् ॥

> *yāvanmātramuṣaso na pratīkaṃ suvarṇyo3 vasate mātariśvaḥ |*
> *tāvaddadhātyupa yajñamāyan brāhmaṇo hoturavaro niṣīdan ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-19) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "As long as the fair-winged ones (?) clothe themselves like the face of the dawn, O Mātariśvan, so long the Brāhmaṇa, coming to the sacrifice, sitting below the Hotṛ, sets (it) down.")

— citing this ṛk, has given the meaning "radiant manifestation". Here the meaning is: "having a beautiful form, filled with water, crops and the like, delightful to the eye and the mind".

## Sūkta 185, Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उर्वी पृथ्वी बहुले दूरेअन्ते उप ब्रुवे नमसा यज्ञे अस्मिन् ।
> दधाते ये सुभगे सुप्रतूर्ती द्यावा रक्षतं पृथिवी नो अभ्वात् ॥ ७ ॥

> *urvī pṛthvī bahule dūreante upa bruve namasā yajñe asmin |*
> *dadhāte ye subhage supratūrtī dyāvā rakṣataṃ pṛthivī no abhvāt ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उर्वी इति । पृथ्वी इति । बहुले इति । दूरेअन्ते इति दूरेऽअन्ते । उप । ब्रुवे । नमसा । यज्ञे । अस्मिन् ।
> दधाते इति । ये इति । सुभगे इति सुऽभगे । सुप्रतूर्ती इति सुऽप्रतूर्ती । द्यावा । रक्षतं । पृथिवी इति । नः । अभ्वात् ॥ ७ ॥

> *urvī iti | pṛthvī iti | bahule iti | dūreante iti dūre 'ante | upa | bruve | namasā | yajñe | asmin |*
> *dadhāte iti | ye iti | subhage iti su 'bhage | supratūrtī iti su 'pratūrtī | dyāvā | rakṣataṃ | pṛthivī iti | naḥ | abhvāt ‖ 7 ‖*

### Printed p. 87  (PDF 105)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 3". Ṛk 7, continued.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed)*

*Gist:* I praise with homage at this sacrifice the vast, wide, multiform, far-ending (boundless) Heaven and Earth, of good fortune and good bounty, who hold the whole world.

> उर्वी उर्व्यौ महत्यौ पृथ्वी पृथिव्यौ बहुले अनेकप्रकारेण प्रथमाने बह्वाकारे दूरेअन्ते विप्रकृष्टान्तदेशे । अपारे इत्यर्थः । ईदृश्यौ युवामस्मिन्यज्ञे नमसा नमस्साधनेन स्तोत्रेणोप ब्रुवे । उपेत्य ब्रवीमि । स्तौमीत्यर्थः । पुनः कीदृश्यौ । ये सुभगे शोभनभाग्ये सुप्रतूर्ती सुप्रतरणे शोभनदाने दधाते विश्वं जगत् ते युवामुप ब्रुवे स्तौमि ॥

> *urvī urvyau mahatyau pṛthvī pṛthivyau bahule anekaprakāreṇa prathamāne bahvākāre dūreante viprakṛṣṭāntadeśe | apāre ityarthaḥ | īdṛśyau yuvāmasminyajñe namasā namassādhanena stotreṇopa bruve | upetya bravīmi | staumītyarthaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśyau | ye subhage śobhanabhāgye supratūrtī suprataraṇe śobhanadāne dadhāte viśvaṃ jagat te yuvāmupa bruve staumi ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** *urvī* — having a great form; *pṛthvī* — exceedingly extensive; *bahule* — having forms of many kinds; *dūreante* — endless; (and) *ye* — who; *subhage* — being of auspicious nature; *supratūrtī* — being givers of good things; *dadhāte* — (the whole world) holding — such Heaven and Earth; *asmin yajñe* — in this sacrifice; *namasā* — with praise accompanied by obeisance; *upabruve* — approaching, I pray; *dyāvāpṛthivī* — O Heaven and Earth; *naḥ* — us; *abhvāt* — from great fear; *rakṣatam* — protect.

**Bhāvārtha.** Heaven and Earth, who have a great form, are exceedingly extensive, have forms of many kinds, are endless, of auspicious nature, givers of good things, and who hold the whole world — them I approach and pray to in this sacrifice with praise accompanied by obeisance. O Heaven and Earth, save us from fearful sin and protect us.

**English Translation (as printed; heading printed "English Trnslation" [sic]):** I glorify with reverence, at this sacrifice, (the two), who are vast, expansive, multiform, infinite, auspicious; who support (all beings) by their bounty : defend us, Heaven and Earth, from great danger.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**बहुले (*bahule*)** — the meaning is: having many kinds of form through the many kinds of visible things, mountains, rivers, forests, trees, houses and the like.

**दूरे अन्ते (*dūre ante*)** — *anta* means the end. Its end is very far away, that is, it extends to a very great distance and is boundless: this is the intention. This use of the word (is found) in the Ṛgveda: in this ṛk also — *(continues on the next page)*

---

### Printed p. 88  (PDF 106)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 185". Special Topics of Ṛk 7, concluded; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā; Ṛk 8 begins.)*

> समान्या वियुते दूरे अन्ते ध्रुवे पदे तस्थतुर्जागरूके ।
> उत स्वसारा युवती भवन्ती आदु ब्रुवाते मिथुनानि नाम ॥

> *samānyā viyute dūre ante dhruve pade tasthaturjāgarūke |*
> *uta svasārā yuvatī bhavantī ādu bruvāte mithunāni nāma ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-54-7) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Common to both, parted, with far-off ends, the two wakeful ones have stood in a firm place; and being young sisters, they speak twin names.")

— it occurs only in this ṛk; it is found nowhere else. There too it praises the qualities of Heaven and Earth.

**दधाते (*dadhāte*)** — though this word has only the meaning "holding", here the intention is "who hold the whole world through nourishment and the like".

**सुप्रतूर्ती (*supratūrtī*)** — "having good bounty", that is, the intention is "who provide rain (*maḷe*), crops and the like, food, and all the means and wealth most necessary to the living beings of the world".

**नमसा (*namasā*)** — the word *namas* has many meanings: obeisance, food, praise. Here the bhāṣyakāra has adopted the meaning "praise".

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** *urvī* (the word *uru* is a quality-word, printed "*adanta*"; *ṅīp* (as printed) in the feminine by *voto guṇavacanāt* (Pā. Sū. 4-1-44); *yaṇ* substitution; by *udāttayaṇo halpūrvāt* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-174) the *ī* becomes acute; before the dual *pūrvasavarṇa* lengthening by *supāṃ suluk* — here in all the *ī*-final words this lengthening has come). *bruve* (root *brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci*; *laṭ*, first person singular; *nighāta* of a verb after a non-verb). *subhage* (by *ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-119) the initial acute of the final member). *supratūrtī* (शोभना प्रतूर्तिः दानं ययोस्ते (*śobhanā pratūrtiḥ dānaṃ yayoste*); by *parādiś chandasi bahulam* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-199) the initial acute of the final member; *pūrvasavarṇa* lengthening in the dual as before). ‖ 7 ‖

*(Ornament: end of Ṛk 7.)*

## Sūkta 185, Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

*(As printed: "सदमिजास्पतिं (*sadamijāspatiṃ*)" with single *j*; continues on the next page.)*

> देवान्वा यच्चकृमा कच्चिदागः सखायं वा सदमिजास्पतिं वा ।

> *devānvā yaccakṛmā kaccidāgaḥ sakhāyaṃ vā sadamijāspatiṃ vā |*

---

### Printed p. 89  (PDF 107)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 3". Ṛk 8, continued: second line of the Saṃhitā.)*

> इयं धीर्भूया अवयानमेषां द्यावा रक्षतं पृथिवी नो अभ्वात् ॥ ८ ॥

> *iyaṃ dhīrbhūyā avayānameṣāṃ dyāvā rakṣataṃ pṛthivī no abhvāt ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

*(As printed: "सदं (*sadaṃ*)" and "जाःपतिं (*jāḥpatiṃ*)" without a compound mark.)*

> देवान् । वा । यत् । चकृम । कत् । चित् । आगः । सखायं । वा । सदं । इत् । जाःपतिं । वा ।
> इयं । धीः । भूयाः । अवऽयानं । एषां । द्यावा । रक्षतं । पृथिवी इति । नः । अभ्वात् ॥ ८ ॥

> *devān | vā | yat | cakṛma | kat | cit | āgaḥ | sakhāyaṃ | vā | sadaṃ | it | jāḥpatiṃ | vā |*
> *iyaṃ | dhīḥ | bhūyāḥ | ava 'yānaṃ | eṣāṃ | dyāvā | rakṣataṃ | pṛthivī iti | naḥ | abhvāt ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed)*

*Gist:* Whatever offence we have ever done to gods, to a friend, or to a son-in-law (by quarrels and the like), may this praise-rite be its expiation; Heaven and Earth are asked to stay favourable in their own place.

*(As printed: "पापानामुपगमं (*pāpānāmupagamaṃ*)", where the sense needs *apagamaṃ*.)*

> हे द्यावापृथिव्यौ वयं देवान् देवान्प्रति यत्कच्चिदागोऽपराधं तत्तद्यागकाले तेषां तेषामयागलक्षणं सदमित्सर्वदैव चकृम कृतवन्तो वयं । सखायं वा प्रियं मित्रं वा प्रति यच्चकृम । जास्पतिं । जाः पुत्र्यः । तासां पतिं जामातरं वा जायापतिं प्रति दोषारोपणकलहोत्पादनादिरूपं यत्सर्वदैव चकृम । एषामुक्तरूपाणां पापानामुपगमं कर्तुमियं धीर्युष्मत्स्तुतिरूपमिदं कर्म भूयाः । भूयात् । भवतु । द्यावेत्यादि गतं । अत्र सर्वत्र प्रकारान्तरेण मन्त्रमन्तरेण रक्षतं रक्षतमिति प्रार्थनं तयोरश्विन्यादिबहुमननासंभवादुचितमेव । तस्मात्स्वस्थान एव स्थिते अनुकूले भवतमित्येवं प्रार्थ्यते ॥

> *he dyāvāpṛthivyau vayaṃ devān devānprati yatkaccidāgo 'parādhaṃ tattadyāgakāle teṣāṃ teṣāmayāgalakṣaṇaṃ sadamitsarvadaiva cakṛma kṛtavanto vayaṃ | sakhāyaṃ vā priyaṃ mitraṃ vā prati yaccakṛma | jāspatiṃ | jāḥ putryaḥ | tāsāṃ patiṃ jāmātaraṃ vā jāyāpatiṃ prati doṣāropaṇakalahotpādanādirūpaṃ yatsarvadaiva cakṛma | eṣāmuktarūpāṇāṃ pāpānāmupagamaṃ kartumiyaṃ dhīryuṣmatstutirūpamidaṃ karma bhūyāḥ | bhūyāt | bhavatu | dyāvetyādi gataṃ | atra sarvatra prakārāntareṇa mantramantareṇa rakṣataṃ rakṣatamiti prārthanaṃ tayoraśvinyādibahumananāsaṃbhavāducitameva | tasmātsvasthāna eva sthite anukūle bhavatamityevaṃ prārthyate ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** (O Heaven and Earth,) *vayam* — we; *devān vā* — whether in regard to the gods; *yat kaccid āgaḥ* — whatever offence, in the form of omission or fault; *sadam it* — at any time; *cakṛma* — may have done (likewise); *sakhāyaṃ vā* — or in regard to friends; *jāspatiṃ vā* — or in regard to a son-in-law (whatever offence we may have done); *eṣām* — for such offences; *avayānam* — as the means of expiation; *iyaṃ dhīḥ* — this rite accompanied by praise; *bhūyāḥ* — may it be; *dyāvāpṛthivī* — O Heaven and Earth; *naḥ* — us; *abhvāt* — from great fear; *rakṣatam* — protect.

---

### Printed p. 90  (PDF 108)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 185". Ṛk 8, continued.)*

**Bhāvārtha.** O Heaven and Earth, whatever offences we have committed in regard to the gods at all the times of the sacrifices we perform, and likewise whatever offences we have committed in regard to friends and sons-in-law — for all such offences may this rite, consisting of praise, be the expiation. O Heaven and Earth, save us from fearful sin and protect us.

**English Translation (as printed):** May this sacrifice be the means of expiating those offences which we may have committed against the gods, against a friend at any time, against a sun-in-law [sic] : defend us, Heaven and Earth, from great danger.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

In this ṛk the ṛṣi humbly prays to the deities that they should pardon the many omissions and faults and the offences that may occur in the rite, in the form of a sacrifice, which he performs or is now performing.

**आगः (*āgaḥ*)** — the meaning is sin, offence. Yāska, stating the derivation of this word —

> यस्मै त्वं सुद्रविणो ददाशोऽनागास्त्वमदिते सर्वताता ।
> यं भद्रेण शवसा चोदयासि प्रजावता राधसा ते स्याम ॥

> *yasmai tvaṃ sudraviṇo dadāśo 'nāgāstvamadite sarvatātā |*
> *yaṃ bhadreṇa śavasā codayāsi prajāvatā rādhasā te syāma ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-94-15) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "To whom you, O possessor of good wealth, grant sinlessness, O Aditi, in all things; whom you urge on with auspicious strength and with bounty rich in offspring — may we be such.")

— citing this ṛk, has stated the derivation:

*(As printed: "आग" for *āgaḥ* at the start; the conjunct after *avaśyame-* is unclear, [?].)*

> आग आङ्पूर्वाद्गमेः (अवश्यमे[?]तदागच्छति कर्तारमित्यागः) एन एतेः । किल्बिषं सुकृतकर्मणो भयं कीर्तिमस्य भिनत्तीति वा ।

> *āga āṅpūrvādgameḥ (avaśyame[?]tadāgacchati kartāramityāgaḥ) ena eteḥ | kilbiṣaṃ sukṛtakarmaṇo bhayaṃ kīrtimasya bhinattīti vā |*

(Gloss, mine and tentative: "*Āgas* from *gam* preceded by *ā* (it is *āgas* because it surely comes to the doer); *enas* from *i*; *kilbiṣa* is the fear of one who has done good deeds, or it breaks his fame.")

That is: the sin that can arise from the omissions and faults the sacrificer may commit in the sacrifice and other rites comes following the sacrificer himself; hence such a sin or offence has the name *āgaḥ* — so he has explained, and in passing he has also stated that the word *kilbiṣa* has the same meaning.

It is stated that the offence the ṛṣi has mentioned need not be thought of as relating to the deities alone; it also expresses repentance in regard to the people taking part in the sacrificial rites, such as the ṛtviks, and to friends, the son-in-law and other relatives. As for offences in regard to people — since mutual imputation of faults, quarrels and the like can occur, the ṛṣi has prayed that these should be pardoned.

**जास्पतिम् (*jāspatim*)** — the word *jāḥ* is read among the names of offspring (*apatya*) (Ni. 3. 2.); the meaning is "daughter". The daughter's husband is well known by the name *jāspati* or *jāmātā*. The derivation of the word *jāmātā* *(continues on the next page)*

---

### Printed p. 91  (PDF 109)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 3". Ṛk 8, concluded; Ṛk 9 begins.)*

— Yāska has stated: **जामाता जा अपत्यं तन्निर्माता (*jāmātā jā apatyaṃ tannirmātā*)** ("*jāmātā*: *jā* is offspring; its maker"). On this Durgācārya, in his commentary, has said:

*(As printed: "हि न्मैथुनेन" and "निर्मिणोति".)*

> जा अपत्यं स्त्रीत्वं हि न्मैथुनेन व्यवहारेणासौ निर्मिणोति तेनासौ दुहितुः पतिर्जामाता भवति ।

> *jā apatyaṃ strītvaṃ hi nmaithunena vyavahāreṇāsau nirmiṇoti tenāsau duhituḥ patirjāmātā bhavati |*

(Ni. 6-9) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "*Jā* is offspring; for he produces it in the woman by the conduct of union; therefore he, the daughter's husband, is *jāmātā*.")

Since he produces offspring in the daughter, the son-in-law has the name *jāmātā*.

**धीः (*dhīḥ*)** — **इयं धीर्युष्मत्स्तुतिरूपं कर्म (*iyaṃ dhīryuṣmatstutirūpaṃ karma*)**. The word *dhī* is read among the names of rite (*karma*) (Ni. 3-2, as printed). The ṛṣi has said: "the rite, in the form of praise, that I am performing in regard to you, Heaven and Earth".

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** *cakṛma* (because of the connection with *yad*, no *nighāta* of the verb; final acute by the suffix accent). *jāspatim* (जायन्ते इति जाः (*jāyante iti jāḥ*); by the force of the mention of *dṛśi*, suffix *ḍa* even without an *upapada*; *ṭi*-loss because of the *ḍ*-marker; plural by the nature of the word; जानां पतिः तम् (*jānāṃ patiḥ tam*); the original accent of the first member). *āgaḥ* (root *iṇ gatau*; suffix *asun* by *iṇa āgo 'parādhe ca* (Uṇ. Sū. 4-631, as printed); *āga* substituted for the root; initial acute because the suffix has the *n*-marker). *bhūyāḥ* (root *bhū sattāyām*; by *vyatyayo bahulam* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-85) in the *liṅ* the second-person singular ending in place of the third-person singular; *nighāta* because it follows a non-verb). *(No ‖ 8 ‖ printed at the end of the grammar.)*

*(Rule: end of Ṛk 8.)*

## Sūkta 185, Ṛk 9

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उभा शंसा नर्या मामविष्टामुभे मामूती अवसा सचेतां ।
> भूरि चिदर्यः सुदास्तरायेषा मदन्त इषयेम देवाः ॥ ९ ॥

> *ubhā śaṃsā naryā māmaviṣṭāmubhe māmūtī avasā sacetāṃ |*
> *bhūri cidaryaḥ sudāstarāyeṣā madanta iṣayema devāḥ ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥** *(continues on the next page)*

> उभा । शंसा । नर्या । मां । अविष्टां । उभे इति । मां । ऊती इति । अवसा । सचेतां ।

> *ubhā | śaṃsā | naryā | māṃ | aviṣṭāṃ | ubhe iti | māṃ | ūtī iti | avasā | sacetāṃ |*

---

### Printed p. 92  (PDF 110)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 185". Ṛk 9, continued: second half of the Pada.)*

> भूरि । चित् । अर्यः । सुदाःऽतराय । इषा । मदंतः । इषयेम । देवाः ॥ ९ ॥

> *bhūri | cit | aryaḥ | sudāḥ 'tarāya | iṣā | madaṃtaḥ | iṣayema | devāḥ ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed)*

*Gist:* The two praise-worthy ones (Heaven and Earth, or the two praises of this world and the next) are asked to protect the poet; the gods within Heaven and Earth, gladdened with Soma-food, are asked for wealth so that the praisers may give liberally.

*(As printed: "हितावीदृश्यावुभयाश्रये"; the glyph(s) after "षष्ठ्य" at the line end are unclear, [?].)*

> उभा शंसा द्यावापृथिव्योरुभयोर्विषयावुभावपि शंसौ नर्यौ नरेभ्यो हितावीदृश्यावुभयाश्रये स्तुती मामविष्टां । रक्षतां । यद्वा । द्यावापृथिव्यभिमानिदेवयोरेव शंसशब्देनाभिधानात्पुल्लिंगता । तथोभे ऊती रक्षिके द्यावापृथिव्यौ मामवसा रक्षणेन सचेतां । यद्वा । प्राणिभ्यो हितकरावुभावैहिकामुष्मिकविषयौ शंसौ मामविष्टां । प्राप्नुतां । तथोभे अप्यूती तयोः संबंधिन्योरभिमानिदेवतयोरवसास्मत्तर्पणेन निमित्तेन सचेतां । हे देवा द्यावापृथिव्योरंतर्भूताः सर्वेऽपि देवाः अर्यः स्तोतारो वयं सुदास्तरायातिशयेन शोभनदातृत्वायेषान्नेन सोमलक्षणेन मदंतो मादयंतः संतो भूरि चित् । चित् पूजायां । अभिपूजितं धनमिषयेम । इच्छेम । यद्वा । अर्य इति षष्ठ्य[?] रूपं । ईश्वराद्राजादेरपि सुदास्तरायेत्यर्थः । शिष्टं समानं ॥

> *ubhā śaṃsā dyāvāpṛthivyorubhayorviṣayāvubhāvapi śaṃsau naryau narebhyo hitāvīdṛśyāvubhayāśraye stutī māmaviṣṭāṃ | rakṣatāṃ | yadvā | dyāvāpṛthivyabhimānidevayoreva śaṃsaśabdenābhidhānātpulliṃgatā | tathobhe ūtī rakṣike dyāvāpṛthivyau māmavasā rakṣaṇena sacetāṃ | yadvā | prāṇibhyo hitakarāvubhāvaihikāmuṣmikaviṣayau śaṃsau māmaviṣṭāṃ | prāpnutāṃ | tathobhe apyūtī tayoḥ saṃbaṃdhinyorabhimānidevatayoravasāsmattarpaṇena nimittena sacetāṃ | he devā dyāvāpṛthivyoraṃtarbhūtāḥ sarve 'pi devāḥ aryaḥ stotāro vayaṃ sudāstarāyātiśayena śobhanadātṛtvāyeṣānnena somalakṣaṇena madaṃto mādayaṃtaḥ saṃto bhūri cit | cit pūjāyāṃ | abhipūjitaṃ dhanamiṣayema | icchema | yadvā | arya iti ṣaṣṭhya[?] rūpaṃ | īśvarādrājāderapi sudāstarāyetyarthaḥ | śiṣṭaṃ samānaṃ ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** *naryā* — who bring about good to men; *ubhā śaṃsā* — (Heaven and Earth,) who are the objects of praises of both kinds, or: these praises sung addressing both Heaven and Earth; *mām* — me; *aviṣṭām* — may they protect; *ubhe ūtī* — these two, who are protectors; *mām* — me; *avasā* — with the act of protection; *sacetām* — may they join; *devāḥ* — O all the deities (included between Heaven and Earth); *aryaḥ* — we, the praisers; *iṣā* — with food in the form of oblation; *madantaḥ* — gladdening you; *sudāstarāya* — for the sake of making excellent gifts; *bhūri cit* — very abundant wealth; *iṣayema* — we desire.

**Bhāvārtha.** May Heaven and Earth, who bring about good to men and who are worthy of praises of both kinds, protect me. May these two protectors join me with the act of protection. O all the deities included between Heaven and Earth, we, the praisers, gladdening you with food in the form of oblation, desire very abundant wealth, with the aim of becoming excellent givers.

**English Translation (as printed):** May both these, accepting praise, and friendly to man, be favourable to me : may they both be associated as guardians for my protection : deities, *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 93  (PDF 111)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 3 [as printed: the Adhyāya numeral has the same glyph as the Varga numeral], Varga 3". Ṛk 9, continued.)*

we your adorers, propitiating you with (sacrificial) food, desire ample (wealth), for the sake of making liberal donations.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**चित् (*cit*)** — as Yāska has said, **चिदित्येषोऽनेककर्मा (*cidityeṣo 'nekakarmā*)**, this word is used in many senses. In **आचार्यश्चिदिदं ब्रूयादिति पूजायां (*ācāryaścididaṃ brūyāditi pūjāyāṃ*)** ("the teacher himself has said this"), the word indicates venerableness. In **दधिचिदित्युपमार्थे (*dadhicidityupamārthe*)** (Ni. 1-4) ("like curds") this word indicates comparison. In the present ṛk he has stated the sense of veneration.

**अर्यः (*aryaḥ*)** — **ईरयिता स्तुतेरीश्वरो वा (*īrayitā stuterīśvaro vā*)**: it has been explained in the sense "the prompter of praise, or the lord (master) of the making of praise". In the present ṛk the sense is "we who are making praise". The Niruktakāra has read this word among the names of *īśvara* (Ni. 3-11), and, citing the ṛk that uses this word in the sense of *īśvara* —

*(As printed: "क्षयेतमस्य" (*kṣayantam asya* by sense).)*

> प्र तत्ते अद्य शिपिविष्ट नामार्यः शंसामि वयुनानि विद्वान् ।
> तं त्वा गृणामि तवसमतव्यान् क्षयेतमस्य रजसः पराके ॥

> *pra tatte adya śipiviṣṭa nāmāryaḥ śaṃsāmi vayunāni vidvān |*
> *taṃ tvā gṛṇāmi tavasamatavyān kṣayetamasya rajasaḥ parāke ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-100-5) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Today, O Śipiviṣṭa, I, the *arya*, knowing the ways, proclaim that name of yours; you, the strong, I, the less strong, praise, who dwell far beyond this region.")

— has explained: **अर्योऽहमस्मीश्वरः स्तोमानामर्यस्त्वमसीति वा (*aryo 'hamasmīśvaraḥ stomānāmaryastvamasīti vā*)** (Ni. 5-9) ("I am the *arya*, the master of praises; or: you are the *arya*"). Here the Vṛttikāra (Durga) has explained:

> यस्मादर्योऽहमस्मि ईश्वरः स्तुतीनामुदीरणे युष्मद्गुणाभिज्ञः अथवा अर्यस्त्वमसि अर्य ईश्वरः मदनुग्रहाय समर्थः ।

> *yasmādaryo 'hamasmi īśvaraḥ stutīnāmudīraṇe yuṣmadguṇābhijñaḥ athavā aryastvamasi arya īśvaraḥ madanugrahāya samarthaḥ |*

(Gloss: "Because I am the *arya*, the one able in uttering praises, knowing your qualities; or you are the *arya*, the lord, able to show favour to me.") — that is, "I am able to know your qualities so as to praise you", or it may also be "you are able to show favour". Uses of this word in the sense "venerable" are also found in many places. For example —

*(Pluta 3 printed after "अर्या".)*

> पृथू रथो दक्षिणाया अयोज्यैनं देवासो अमृतासो अस्थुः ।
> कृष्णादुदस्थादर्या३ विहायाश्चिकित्संती मानुषाय क्षयाय ।

> *pṛthū ratho dakṣiṇāyā ayojyainaṃ devāso amṛtāso asthuḥ |*
> *kṛṣṇādudasthādaryā3 vihāyāścikitsaṃtī mānuṣāya kṣayāya |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-123-2) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The broad chariot of Dakṣiṇā has been yoked; the immortal gods have mounted it; the noble one, vast, has risen from the darkness, taking thought for the human dwelling.")

In this ṛk, describing the qualities of the Uṣas deity understood from the context, there is the epithet *aryā*. Sāyaṇa has taken this word to mean "venerable" (*pūjyā*). Its use, however, is more frequent in the sense of "the Lord of all".

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** *ubhā* (by *supāṃ suluk* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) the substitute *ā* for the dual ending; likewise *ā* in the following words). *(continues on the next page)*

## Sūkta 185, Ṛk 10

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> ऋतं दिवे तदवोचं पृथिव्या अभिश्रावाय प्रथमं सुमेधाः ।
> पातामवद्याद्दुरितादभीके पिता माता च रक्षतामवोभिः ॥ १० ॥

> *ṛtaṃ dive tadavocaṃ pṛthivyā abhiśrāvāya prathamaṃ sumedhāḥ |*
> *pātāmavadyādduritādabhīke pitā mātā ca rakṣatāmavobhiḥ ‖ 10 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥** *(continues on the next page)*

*(As printed: "पथिव्यै (*pathivyai*)" without the ṛ-sign.)*

> ऋतं । दिवे । तत् । अवोचं । पथिव्यै । अभिऽश्रावाय । प्रथमं । सुऽमेधाः ।

> *ṛtaṃ | dive | tat | avocaṃ | pathivyai | abhi 'śrāvāya | prathamaṃ | su 'medhāḥ |*

> पातां । अवद्यात् । दुःऽइतात् । अभीके । पिता । माता । च । रक्षतां । अवःऽभिः ॥ १० ॥

> *pātāṃ | avadyāt | duḥ 'itāt | abhīke | pitā | mātā | ca | rakṣatāṃ | avaḥ 'bhiḥ ‖ 10 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed)*

*Gist:* Ṛks 10–11 are the anuvākyās for the puroḍāśa-oblation in the animal sacrifice to Heaven and Earth (Āś. 3-8). The wise poet has spoken this foremost praise to Heaven and Earth, to be heard all round; may father Heaven and mother Earth guard him from blameworthy sin, staying near with their protections.

*(As printed: "द्यावापृथिवीये"; in "तत्तृप्ति[?]रीतिकरं" the consonant before the *r*-subscript is not printed (*prīti* by sense); "प्रतमं" as printed.)*

> ऋतं दिव इति द्वे द्यावापृथिवीये पशौ पुरोडाशहविषोरनुवाक्ये । अग्नीषोमाविति खंडे सूत्रितं । ऋतं दिवे तदवोचं पृथिव्या इति द्वे । आ. ३-८ । इति ॥
> सुमेधाः शोभनप्रज्ञोऽहं दिवे द्युदेवतायै पृथिव्यै पृथिवीदेवतायै तत्तृप्ति[?]रीतिकरमृतं स्तोत्रं प्रथमं । मुख्यनामैतत् । प्रतमं प्रकृष्टतममवोचं । ब्रवीमि । किमर्थं । अभिश्रावायाभितः सर्वतः श्रवणाय । किंच पिता पालको द्युलोको माता सस्यादेर्निर्मात्री पृथिवी चोभे अवद्यान्निंदिताद्दुःखप्रापकादंहसः सकाशात्पातां । रक्षतां । तथाभीके । अंतिकनामैतत् । समीप एवावोभिरभिमततर्पणैः रक्षतां । पालयतां ॥

> *ṛtaṃ diva iti dve dyāvāpṛthivīye paśau puroḍāśahaviṣoranuvākye | agnīṣomāviti khaṃḍe sūtritaṃ | ṛtaṃ dive tadavocaṃ pṛthivyā iti dve | ā. 3-8 | iti ‖*
> *sumedhāḥ śobhanaprajño 'haṃ dive dyudevatāyai pṛthivyai pṛthivīdevatāyai tattṛpti[?]rītikaramṛtaṃ stotraṃ prathamaṃ | mukhyanāmaitat | pratamaṃ prakṛṣṭatamamavocaṃ | bravīmi | kimarthaṃ | abhiśrāvāyābhitaḥ sarvataḥ śravaṇāya | kiṃca pitā pālako dyuloko mātā sasyādernirmātrī pṛthivī cobhe avadyānniṃditādduḥkhaprāpakādaṃhasaḥ sakāśātpātāṃ | rakṣatāṃ | tathābhīke | aṃtikanāmaitat | samīpa evāvobhirabhimatatarpaṇaiḥ rakṣatāṃ | pālayatāṃ ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** *sumedhāḥ* — I, who possess excellent understanding; *dive* — the Dyu deity; *pṛthivyai* — and Earth; (addressing them) *tat* — pleasing; *prathamam* — most principal; *ṛtam* — the praise; *abhiśrāvāya* — so that it may be heard everywhere; *avocam* — I am reciting; *pitā* — the Dyu deity, who is the protector; *mātā ca* — and Earth, who is the maker of the world; *avadyāt* — blameworthy; *duritāt* — from sin; *pātām* — may they protect (us); (likewise) *abhīke* — staying near us; *avobhiḥ* — with acts of protection; *rakṣatām* — may they protect.

**Bhāvārtha.** I, who possess excellent understanding, recite, addressing the Dyu deity and Earth, a praise that is pleasing and most principal, so that it may be heard everywhere. May the Dyu deity, the protector, and Earth, the maker of the world, protect us from blameworthy sin. Likewise, staying near us, may they protect us with acts of protection —

**English Translation (as printed):** Endowed with understanding, I repeat to Heaven and Earth this initial praise, to be heard around : may paternal (heaven) and maternal (earth) preserve us from reprehensible iniquity; and ever nigh defend us with their protection.

### Printed p. 96  (PDF 114)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 185". Ṛk 10, concluded.)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

This ṛk, **ऋतं दिव (*ṛtaṃ diva*)**, and the next ṛk, **इदं द्यावापृथिवी (*idaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī*)**, are to be recited in the animal sacrifice, when the puroḍāśa oblations are offered into the fire, as the *puro'nuvākyā* mantras having Heaven and Earth as their deity: this is set out by the sūtra **ऋतं दिवे तदवोचं पृथिव्या इति द्वे (*ṛtaṃ dive tadavocaṃ pṛthivyā iti dve*)** (Āś. 3-8) in the khaṇḍa **अग्नीषोमौ (*agnīṣomau*)** of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra.

**ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)** — although the word *ṛta* has many meanings such as truth, sacrifice and dharma, here the bhāṣyakāra has taken it to mean praise (*stotra*).

**प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*)** — for this word Yāska has given the derivation **प्रथम इति मुख्यनाम प्रतमो भवति (*prathama iti mukhyanāma pratamo bhavati*)** (Ni. 2-22), that is, the word *prathama* means "principal".

In this ṛk the ṛṣi, addressing Heaven and Earth as mother and father, has prayed that they protect him too from the sin that brings sorrow. Among Heaven and Earth it is the established custom to call the Dyu deity the father and Earth the mother —

> तन्नो वातो मयोभु वातु भेषजं तन्माता पृथिवी तत्पिता द्यौः ।

> *tanno vāto mayobhu vātu bheṣajaṃ tanmātā pṛthivī tatpitā dyauḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-89-4) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "May the wind blow to us that healing remedy which is a joy; that may mother Earth, that may father Heaven (grant).")

> उरुव्यचसा महिनी असश्चता पिता माता च भुवनानि रक्षतः ।

> *uruvyacasā mahinī asaścatā pitā mātā ca bhuvanāni rakṣataḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-160-2) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Wide-extending, great, never failing, the father and the mother protect the worlds.")

> इदं द्यावापृथिवी सत्यमस्तु पितर्मातर्यदिहोपब्रुवे वां ।

> *idaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī satyamastu pitarmātaryadihopabruve vāṃ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-185-11) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "O Heaven and Earth, O father, O mother, may this be true which I here address to you.")

> आ सुष्टुती नमसा वर्तयध्यै द्यावा वाजाय पृथिवी अमृध्रे ।
> पितामाता मधुवचाः सुहस्ता भरेभरे नो यशसावविष्टां ॥

> *ā suṣṭutī namasā vartayadhyai dyāvā vājāya pṛthivī amṛdhre |*
> *pitāmātā madhuvacāḥ suhastā bharebhare no yaśasāvaviṣṭāṃ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-43-2) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "To turn hither, with fair praise and homage, Heaven and Earth, the unfailing, for strength — may father and mother, sweet-spoken, skilful-handed, glorious, help us in every contest.")

— in these ṛks, and in Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-43-15; 6-51-5; 6-70-6; 6-72-2; 8-92-2; 10-54-3; 10-88-15; Atha. Ve. 2-28-4; 3-[?]3-6; 6-4-3; 6-120-2; 8-7-2, 12-1-10 and other ṛks, Heaven and Earth are praised as father and mother.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** *dive* (by *ūḍidaṃpadādi…* (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) the case ending (dative) is acute). *avocam* (root *brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci*; by *chandasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ* the *luṅ* in the sense of the *laṭ*; first-person singular; *tiṅanta-nighāta*). *(continues on the next page)*

Sū. 5-4-38); when *a* is dropped by *yasyeti ca*, *vṛddhi* of the penultimate *a* by *ata upadhāyāḥ* (Pā. Sū. 7-2-116); final acute by the suffix accent; dative singular). *sumedhāḥ* (शोभनं मेधः यस्य (*śobhanaṃ medhaḥ yasya*), as printed; final acute of the latter member by *nañsubhyām* (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172)). *pātām* (root *pā rakṣaṇe*; called a *loṭ* "madhyama-puruṣa" dual, as printed; no *nighāta* because it stands at the beginning of a pāda; final acute by the suffix accent). *avadyāt* (root *vada vyaktāyāṃ vāci*; with *nañ* as *upapada*, formed irregularly (*nipātita*) with the suffix *yat* in the sense of "blameworthy" by *avadyapaṇyavaryā garhya…* (Pā. Sū. 3-1-101)).

*(Rule ":O:" — end of Ṛk 10.)*

## Sūkta 185, Ṛk 11

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> इदं द्यावापृथिवी सत्यमस्तु पितर्मातर्यदिहोपब्रुवे वां ।
> भूतं देवानामवमे अवोभिर्विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥ ११ ॥

> *idaṃ dyāvāpṛthivī satyamastu pitarmātaryadihopabruve vāṃ |*
> *bhūtaṃ devānāmavame avobhirvidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānuṃ ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> इदं । द्यावापृथिवी इति । सत्यं । अस्तु । पितः । मातः । यत् । इह । उपऽब्रुवे । वां ।
> भूतं । देवानां । अवमे इति । अवःऽभिः । विद्याम । इषं । वृजनं । जीरऽदानुं ॥ ११ ॥

> *idaṃ | dyāvāpṛthivī iti | satyaṃ | astu | pitaḥ | mātaḥ | yat | iha | upa 'bruve | vāṃ |*
> *bhūtaṃ | devānāṃ | avame iti | avaḥ 'bhiḥ | vidyāma | iṣaṃ | vṛjanaṃ | jīra 'dānuṃ ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; continues on the next page)*

> हे द्यावापृथिवी द्यावापृथिव्यौ इदमस्माभिः क्रियमाणं स्तोत्रं सत्यमस्तु । अवितथं भवतु । फलवद्भवत्वित्यर्थः । इदमित्युक्तं किं तदित्याह । हे पितर्द्यौः हे

> *he dyāvāpṛthivī dyāvāpṛthivyau idamasmābhiḥ kriyamāṇaṃ stotraṃ satyamastu | avitathaṃ bhavatu | phalavadbhavatvityarthaḥ | idamityuktaṃ kiṃ tadityāha | he pitardyauḥ he*

*(Footer: "[7]" and "Vol. 14".)*

### Printed p. 98  (PDF 116)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 185". Ṛk 11, continued.)*

*(Bhāṣya of Ṛk 11, concluded: the block continues the sentence "… he pitardyauḥ he" of p. 97.)*

*Gist:* O father Heaven, O mother Earth, may the praise I here approach you with be true; you who are ever near to us praisers, be joined with your gratifying protections. The rest has been explained.

> मातः पृथिवि वां युवां प्रतीहास्मिन्यज्ञे यत्स्तोत्रमुपब्रुवे उपेत्य ब्रवीमि तत्सत्यमस्तु । देवानां स्तोतॄणामस्माकमवमे । अंतिकनामैतत् । नित्यसंनिहिते युवामवोभिस्तर्पणैर्युक्ते भूतं । भवतं । अवशिष्टं गतं ॥

> *mātaḥ pṛthivi vāṃ yuvāṃ pratīhāsminyajñe yatstotramupabruve upetya bravīmi tatsatyamastu | devānāṃ stotṝṇāmasmākamavame | aṃtikanāmaitat | nityasaṃnihite yuvāmavobhistarpaṇairyukte bhūtaṃ | bhavataṃ | avaśiṣṭaṃ gataṃ ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** *pitaḥ* — who is of the form of the father; *mātaḥ* — and who is of the form of the mother; *dyāvāpṛthivī* — O Heaven and Earth; *vām* — addressing you both; *iha* — in this sacrifice; *yat* — which praise; *upabruve* — I recite (approaching you); *idam* — this praise of that kind; *satyam* — so as to give true fruit; *astu* — may it be; *devānām* — to us, who are praisers; *avame* — (you both) who are near; *avobhiḥ* — joined with acts of protection; *bhūtam* — be; *iṣam* — food; *vṛjanam* — strength; *jīradānum* — long life; *vidyāma* — may (we) obtain.

**Bhāvārtha.** O Heaven and Earth, who are mother and father to the whole world, may the praise recited in this sacrifice addressing you both be such as gives us true fruit. You both, being near us praisers, be joined with the work of protection. By your grace may we obtain food, strength and long life —

**English Translation (as printed):** May this (hymn), Heaven and Earth, be successful ; (the hymn) which, Father and Mother, I repeat to you both on this occasion ; be ever with your protection in the proximity of those who praise you, that we may obtain food, strength, and long life.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

In this ṛk the ṛṣi concludes the sūkta praying to the deities: may all the works of protection and the rest described in this praise he has recited come true; may there be the presence of the deities; may there be food, strength and long life.

**पितः मातः (*pitaḥ mātaḥ*)** — as was said in the previous ṛk, in this ṛk too he has prayed with devotion to Heaven and Earth, using the words *pitaḥ mātaḥ* (father and mother), which express respect and are natural.

**यत् इह उपब्रुवे वां इदं सत्यमस्तु (*yat iha upabruve vāṃ idaṃ satyamastu*)** — "O deities, may this praise which I speak (recite) about you, approaching you, bring about a true fruit": so he has clearly made known the devotion and the desire in his mind.

**देवानां (*devānāṃ*)** — for this word Sāyaṇa has given the meaning स्तोतॄणामस्माकं (*stotṝṇāmasmākaṃ*): "of us, the sacrificers and others, who are reciting praise".

**अवमे (*avame*)** — since the word *avame* is read among the eleven names for "near" (*antika*) beginning with तळित् (*taḷit*), असात् (*asāt*) (as printed), this word means "in proximity" (Ni. 3-9, as printed).

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** *dyāvāpṛthivī* (द्यौश्च पृथिवी च द्यावापृथिवी (*dyauśca pṛthivī ca dyāvāpṛthivī*); *dyāvā*-substitute by *divo dyāvā*; before the vocative dual ending, *pūrvasavarṇa* lengthening by *supāṃ suluk* (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39); *nighāta* accent by *āmantritasya ca* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-19)). *satyam* (सत्सु साधु सत्यम् (*satsu sādhu satyam*); formed irregularly with final acute by *satyād aśapathe* (Pā. Sū. 5-4-66)). *upabruve* (root *brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci*; *loṭ*, first person singular; *nighāta* barred by *yadvṛttān nityam* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66), so final acute by the suffix accent; the *gati* (*upa*) wholly unaccented by *tiṅi codāttavati* (Pā. Sū. 8-1-71)). *bhūtam* (root *bhū sattāyām*; *loṭ*, second person dual, *tam* substitute; *luk* of the *vikaraṇa* by *bahulaṃ chandasi*; *guṇa* barred by *bhūsuvos tiṅi* (Pā. Sū. 7-3-88); no *nighāta* at the beginning of a pāda; final acute by the suffix accent).

*(Rule ":O:" — end of Ṛk 11 and of Sūkta 185.)*

## Sūkta 186 — *ā na iḷābhiḥ* (Anuvāka 24, seventh Sūkta; 11 ṛks)

*(Kannada half-title: "ನೂರ ಎಂಭತ್ತಾರನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು", "the hundred-and-eighty-sixth sūkta".)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; Anukramaṇikā wording and viniyoga)*

> आ न इळाभिरिति सप्तमं सूक्तमेकादशर्चमागस्त्यं त्रैष्टुभं वैश्वदेवं । आ नो वैश्वदेवमित्यनुक्रांतं ॥ विनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

> *ā na iḷābhiriti saptamaṃ sūktamekādaśarcamāgastyaṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ | ā no vaiśvadevamityanukrāṃtaṃ ‖ viniyogo laiṃgikaḥ ‖*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta, *ā na iḷābhiḥ*, is the seventh sūkta in the twenty-fourth anuvāka. There are eleven ṛks in it. Agastya is the ṛṣi of this sūkta; the Viśvedevas are the devatā; the metre is *triṣṭubh*. In the Anukramaṇikā it is stated "*ā no vaiśvadevam*". The application (*viniyoga*) of this sūkta is by its indicative marks (*laiṅgika*).

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अपि यथा युवानो मत्सथा नो विश्वं जगदभिपित्वे मनीषा ॥ १ ॥

> *api yathā yuvāno matsathā no viśvaṃ jagadabhipitve manīṣā ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> आ । नः । इळाभिः । विदथे । सुऽशस्ति । विश्वानरः । सविता । देवः । एतु ।
> अपि । यथा । युवानः । मत्सथ । नः । विश्वं । जगत् । अभिऽपित्वे । मनीषा ॥ १ ॥

> *ā | naḥ | iḷābhiḥ | vidathe | su 'śasti | viśvānaraḥ | savitā | devaḥ | etu |*
> *api | yathā | yuvānaḥ | matsatha | naḥ | viśvaṃ | jagat | abhi 'pitve | manīṣā ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; the block opens with "नो" as printed)*

*Gist:* May Agni Vaiśvānara, beneficial to all beings, and Savitṛ the impeller come to our sacrifice with praises and gifts (or with the earth-deities); O ever-young gods, gladden us, as you gladden the whole world, by your own will.

> नो विदथेऽस्मदीये यज्ञे सुशस्ति । सुपो लुक् । सुशस्तिभिः शोभनशंसनैः स्तुतिभिः प्रदेयै रत्नैः सह । यद्वा । इळाभिः । तदाश्रितेषु ताच्छब्द्यं । भूमिस्थानाभिर्देवताभिः सह । विश्वानरः सर्वप्राणिहितकार्यग्निः सविता प्रेरक आदित्यश्च देव एतु । आगच्छतु । हे युवानो नित्यतरुणा यज्ञस्य मिश्रयितारो वा यूयं नोऽस्मानभिपित्वेऽभिपतनीयेऽस्मद्यज्ञे मनीषा मनीषया मनस ईशितृत्वेन । स्वेच्छयेत्यर्थः । अपिः संभावनायां । अप्यस्मान्मत्सथ । मादयथ । यथा विश्वं जगत् । एतत्स्थावरस्याप्युपलक्षणं । यद्वा । कृत्स्नं प्रपंचं मत्सथ तथास्मानपि । यद्वा । जगच्छब्दो यजमानरूपमनुष्यवाची । सर्वानपि यजमानान्यथा मत्सथ तथेत्यर्थः ॥

> *no vidathe 'smadīye yajñe suśasti | supo luk | suśastibhiḥ śobhanaśaṃsanaiḥ stutibhiḥ pradeyai ratnaiḥ saha | yadvā | iḷābhiḥ | tadāśriteṣu tācchabdyaṃ | bhūmisthānābhirdevatābhiḥ saha | viśvānaraḥ sarvaprāṇihitakāryagniḥ savitā preraka ādityaśca deva etu | āgacchatu | he yuvāno nityataruṇā yajñasya miśrayitāro vā yūyaṃ no 'smānabhipitve 'bhipatanīye 'smadyajñe manīṣā manīṣayā manasa īśitṛtvena | svecchayetyarthaḥ | apiḥ saṃbhāvanāyāṃ | apyasmānmatsatha | mādayatha | yathā viśvaṃ jagat | etatsthāvarasyāpyupalakṣaṇaṃ | yadvā | kṛtsnaṃ prapaṃcaṃ matsatha tathāsmānapi | yadvā | jagacchabdo yajamānarūpamanuṣyavācī | sarvānapi yajamānānyathā matsatha tathetyarthaḥ ‖*

*(The Pratipadārtha follows on the next page.)*

### Printed p. 101  (PDF 119)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 4". Ṛk 1, continued.)*

**Pratipadārtha.** *viśvānaraḥ* — Agni, who is beneficial to all the world; *savitā devaḥ* — and Savitṛ, who is of divine nature; *iḷābhiḥ* — together with the deities presiding over the earth-region; *naḥ vidathe* — to this sacrifice of ours; *suśasti* — with praiseworthy jewels; *etu* — may come; *yuvānaḥ* — O Viśvedeva deities, ever young; *abhipitve* — in the sacrifice now being accomplished; *manīṣā* — by your own contentment; *yathā viśvaṃ jagat* — just as (you gladden) the whole universe, or all the performers of sacrifice; *naḥ api* — us also; *matsatha* — gladden.

**Bhāvārtha.** May Agni, who is beneficial to all the world, and Savitṛ, who is of divine nature, come to this sacrifice of ours together with the deities presiding over the earth-region, with praiseworthy jewels. O Viśvedeva deities, ever young, in the sacrifice now being accomplished, by your own contentment, just as you gladden all the performers of sacrifice, gladden us also.

**English Translation (as printed):** May the divine Savitri, the benefactor of all men, come benignantly to our solemniy [sic], togther [sic] with the divinities of earth, and do you, who are (always) young, willingly present at uur [sic] sacrifice, lexhilarate [sic] us, as (you exhilarate) the whole world.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).** *(As printed, the topics on this page treat the words* sajoṣāḥ *and* śavaḥ*, which do not occur in Ṛk 1.)*

**सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*)** — for this word, derived from the root जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः (*juṣī prītisevanayoḥ*), Yāska in his Nirukta, citing the ṛk

*("देवनामसि" as printed, without the long ā.)*

> आजुह्वान ईड्यो वन्द्यश्चा याह्यग्ने वसुभिः सजोषाः ।
> त्वं देवनामसि यह्व होता स एनान् यक्षीषितो यजीयान् ॥

> *ājuhvāna īḍyo vandyaścā yāhyagne vasubhiḥ sajoṣāḥ |*
> *tvaṃ devanāmasi yahva hotā sa enān yakṣīṣito yajīyān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-110-3) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Invoked, to be praised and revered, come, O Agni, in accord with the Vasus; you are the mighty Hotṛ of the gods; impelled, best at sacrificing, offer sacrifice to them.")

— has explained सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*) as सह जोषणः (समानप्रीतिर्भूत्वा) (*saha joṣaṇaḥ (samānaprītirbhūtvā)*), that is, "being endowed with equal affection".

**शवः (*śavaḥ*)** — since the word *śavaḥ* is mentioned among the names for water (Ni. 2-24, as printed) and among the names for strength (Ni. 3-9, as printed), *śavaḥ* means strength. Here the commentator has given the meaning "food that produces strength (nourishing food)".

### Printed p. 102  (PDF 120)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued.)*

**Viśvedevas (विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*))** — the name of these deities is read among the thirty-one names indicating particular deities that begin with अश्विनौ (*aśvinau*). The commentator says that they are distinct, particular deities; some say they are all the gods. But from the matter in other sūktas it can be said clearly that the ṛṣis worshipped distinct deities as the Viśvedevas. In this connection Yāska has written an explanation of the ṛk ओमासः (*omāsaḥ*):

> अवितारो वावनीया वा मनुष्यधृतः सर्वे देवा इहागच्छत दत्तवन्तो दत्तवतः सुतमिति, तदेतदेकमेव वैश्वदेवं गायत्रं तृचं दशतयीषु विद्यते यत्तु किंचिद्बहुदैवतं तद्वैश्वदेवानां स्थाने युज्यते यदेव विश्वलिंगमिति शाकपूणिः ॥

> *avitāro vāvanīyā vā manuṣyadhṛtaḥ sarve devā ihāgacchata dattavanto dattavataḥ sutamiti, tadetadekameva vaiśvadevaṃ gāyatraṃ tṛcaṃ daśatayīṣu vidyate yattu kiṃcidbahudaivataṃ tadvaiśvadevānāṃ sthāne yujyate yadeva viśvaliṃgamiti śākapūṇiḥ ‖*

(Ni. 12-40) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "'O protectors, or ones to be gratified, supporters of men, all gods, come hither, givers, to the soma of the giver' — this alone is the one Vaiśvadeva triplet in Gāyatrī found in the ten maṇḍalas; but whatever is addressed to many deities is used in the place of Vaiśvadeva ones, whatever has the mark 'viśva' — so Śākapūṇi.")

There is no difference between the meaning we have given in discussing the meaning of this ṛk and Yāska's meaning. But Yāska himself has stated that in his own view *viśvedevāḥ* means "all the gods", and that it is the view of one Śākapūṇi that the Viśvedevas are particular deities called by that name. Hence it can be said firmly that even in his time there was a difference of opinion on this question. If one speaks as is customary now in the domestic (*gṛhya*) and other rites, it becomes known that these Viśvedevas do not belong to the group of general deities and that they are a special group of thirteen persons of their own. Be that as it may; it seems proper to say that the Viśvedevas described in the Ṛgveda belong to the group of distinct deities.

In the Ṛgveda there are 63 sūktas that praise the Viśvedevas alone. Besides these, in Ṛ. Saṃ. sūkta 1-164 the first 41 ṛks relate to the Viśvedevas. In all of these — leaving aside the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-155 (as printed) — in all the remaining sūktas many deities are set forth: that is, besides the praise of deities such as Agni and Indra, as in other sūktas, trees, rivers, mountains, cows, horses and the like are also treated. Besides these, in sūktas having other deities, in many places, 17 ṛks in all have the Viśvedevas as deity; in all these places the Viśvedevas are stated to be the deities of these ṛks. And in the mantra Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-125-1 the Vasus, Rudras and Ādityas are included together with the Viśvedevas.

In mantra 2-22 of the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā (Śukla Yajurveda) Indra, the Ādityas, the Vasus and the Maruts are prayed to join with the Viśvedevas. In mantras 33-45 to 47 of the same Saṃhitā Indra, Vāyu and other deities are praised together with the Viśvedevas.

In mantra 20-62-6 of the Atharvaveda the Viśvedevas are indicated in the singular, and there are many sūktas relating to the Viśvedevas in the Atharvaveda.

### Printed p. 103  (PDF 121)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 4". Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued.)*

In the Brāhmaṇas too the name of the Viśvedevas is indicated here and there. In the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa 4-14 and the Gopatha Brāhmaṇa 1-20 all the gods are addressed by the very name Viśvedevas. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 3-9-2-6 the Viśvedevas are called the rays of the sun; in Śa. Brā. 14-2-2-37 the vital airs beginning with *prāṇa*; in Śa. Brā. 7-1-1-42 the sacrificial rites; and in Śa. Brā. 2-4-4-13 Indra and Agni. In the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka (Tai. Ā. 5-1-6) Indra and Agni are praised together with the Viśvedevas.

In the Purāṇas, in some places, these Viśvedevas are said to be the lords of the quarters. In the Nirukta (Ni. 12-39) it is said that the Viśvedevas are all the gods. Durgācārya, the commentator on the Nirukta, has taken the Viśvedevas to mean the rays of the sun. Yāska, the author of the Nirukta, besides stating his own opinion that the Viśvedevas are all the gods, has indicated the opinion of one Śākapūṇi. Śaunaka, in his work named Bṛhaddevatā (Bṛ. De. 2-148 to 134 ślokas, as printed), speaking about the Viśvedevas, has said that Yāska and Śāṇḍilya hold that *viśvedevāḥ* means all the gods. Śaunaka's view too is the same.

Sāyaṇācārya, in explaining this ṛk, has expressed his opinion that the thirty-one deities beginning with the Aśvin deities are together called the Viśvedevas.

Among the Western scholars, Langlois, Kaegi and Hopkins have taken the Viśvedevas to mean all the gods, and Wilson, Griffith and Macdonell have approved both kinds of meaning: all the gods, or a group of distinct deities called the Viśvedevas.

The main point is this: it may be said that in former times, that is in very ancient times, the meaning "all the gods" alone was current for the Viśvedevas, and that in course of time the conception of the Viśvedevas as a group of distinct deities of that name came into use. In many Brāhmaṇas and Purāṇas the Viśvedevas are indicated as a distinct group of deities. But it becomes known from Yāska's Nirukta itself that even in Yāska's time there was a difference of opinion on this subject.

In the Ṛgveda, besides ṛks relating to the Viśvedevas occurring here and there, there are 58 separate sūktas having the Viśvedevas as deity (as printed; p. 102 gives 63): in the first maṇḍala of the Ṛ. Saṃ., 14, 89, 90, 105, 106, 107, 121, *(the list continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 104  (PDF 122)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued.)*

… 122nd sūktas; in the second maṇḍala, the 29th and 31st sūktas; in the third maṇḍala, the 54th sūkta; in the fourth maṇḍala, the 55th sūkta; in the fifth maṇḍala, 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 48, 49, 50, 51; in the sixth maṇḍala, 49, 50, 51, 52; in the seventh maṇḍala, 35, 36, 37, 39, 40, 42, 43; in the eighth maṇḍala, 27, 28, 29, 30, 58, 83; in the tenth maṇḍala, 31, 32, 35, 36, 64, 65, 66, 92, 93, 100, 101, 109, 114, 126, 128, 137, 141, 157, 181 — these sūktas have the Viśvedevas as deity.

**विदथे (*vidathe*)** — यज्ञे (*yajñe*): "in the sacrifice", that is, "in the place of sacrifice". By वेदयित्सु[?] स्तोत्रेषु निमित्तभूतेषु (*vedayitsu[?] stotreṣu nimittabhūteṣu*) the derivation (*nirvacana*) of the word *vidatha* has been shown; here only one of the derivations of the author of the Nirukta has been followed. It is read among the names of sacrifice, यज्ञः, वेनः (*yajñaḥ, venaḥ*) and the rest (Ni. 3-19); and, to show that the word *vidatha* means knowledge, with विदथानि वेदनानि (*vidathāni vedanāni*) (Ni. 6-7), citing the ṛk

> होता देवो अमर्त्यः पुरस्तादेति मायया । विदथानि प्रचोदयन् ॥

> *hotā devo amartyaḥ purastādeti māyayā | vidathāni pracodayan ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-27-7) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The Hotṛ, the immortal god, goes in front by his wondrous power, impelling the *vidathas*.")

— he has made known that there it is derived from the root *vid* in the sense of knowing. Here Sāyaṇa has given the meaning विदथानि वेदितव्यानि कर्माणि (*vidathāni veditavyāni karmāṇi*): "rites that are to be known". Some scholars have tried to state a definite meaning for this word, and all have made known their individual opinions. Since each one has shown a different derivation of this word and given a different meaning, it becomes known that all those meanings fit according to context. The scholar Max Muller [as printed], in explaining the ṛk

> अमादेषां भियसा भूमिरेजति नौर्न पूर्णा क्षरति व्यथिर्यती ।
> दूरेदृशो ये चितयंत एमभिरंतर्महे विदथे येतिरे नरः ॥

> *amādeṣāṃ bhiyasā bhūmirejati naurna pūrṇā kṣarati vyathiryatī |*
> *dūredṛśo ye citayaṃta emabhiraṃtarmahe vidathe yetire naraḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-59-2) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "From their onset the earth trembles with fear; like a full ship she goes reeling; the far-seen heroes who shine with their courses have striven within the great *vidatha*.")

— has given for the word *vidathe* the meaning "(sacrificial) assembly (the great sacrificial assembly)". And, while giving its explanation, he set out the meaning that other German scholars have given to this word and their opinions about its root, and finally:

> Vidatha may have been the name of a sacred act. as Veda is of sacred knowledge. But the fact remains that it is best translated by assembly, particularly an assembly for sacrificial purposes.
>
> (Sacred Books of the East. Vol. 32 p. 349-50)

Some have said that, just as "sacred knowledge" is the meaning of the word *veda*, "sacred act" is the meaning of the word *vidatha*. But he has concluded that there is no doubt that "sacrificial assembly" is the principal meaning of this word.

### Printed p. 105  (PDF 123)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 4". Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued.)*

The scholar Hermann Oldenberg, in the work named Vedic Hymns, while explaining the meaning of the word *vidathe* in the ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-6, has made known his opinion in this way. His sentences are quoted, and afterwards his opinions are made known.

*(Quoted in English as printed; the Sanskrit words in it are printed in Kannada script and are given here in Devanagari.)*

On the derivation and meaning of विदथ (*vidatha*) Various opinions have been pronounced in the last years which have been collected by prof. Max Muller in hi• [sic] note on R. V V-59-2 (S. B. E• Vol. 32 p. 349 sq.) without trying to discuss here all different theories, I proceed to state my own opinion-

I propose to derive विदथ (*vidatha*) from वि+धा (*vi+dhā*); The Verb वि+धा (*vi+dhā*) means 'to distribute, to arrange, to ordain;' thus the original meaning of विदथ (*vidatha*) must be like the meaning of विधान (*vidhāna*), 'distribution, disposition, ordinance; In V. 3-6, we read विदथेषु अह्नां (*vidatheṣu ahnāṃ*): this phrase receives its explanation by VII. 66-11 we may call attention also to VI. 51-2 within the sphere of the Vedic poets' thoughts, the most prominent example of something most artificially विहित (*vihita*) was the secrifice [sic]. यज्ञ (*yajña*) and विदथ (*vidatha*), Sacrifice and ordinance became nearly synonymous. (III 3-3) …. …. …. …. …. finally विदथ (*vidatha*) seems to mean 'the act of disposing of any business' or the like; this meaning appears, I believe, in some passages like the well-known phrase, बृहद्वदेम विदथे (*bṛhadvadema vidathe*) [?]वीराः (*vīrāḥ*):—may we with Valiant men mightily raise our voice in the determining of ordinances. Thus the word वि (*vi*)[?]थ (*tha*) and सभा (*sabhā*) approach each other in their meaning; a person influential in council is called both विदथ्य (*vidathya*) and सभेय (*sabheya*)'.

(Sacred Books of the East• Vol. 46• p. 27)

*(In the phrase from the well-known verse the first syllable before "vīrāḥ" and, later, the middle letter of "vi-?-tha" are blurred in the print.)*

The main gist of this writing is: the word *vidatha* is formed by joining the upasarga *vi* to the root *dhā*. *vidhā* means "to divide, to regulate"; it may also mean "the keeping of rules". That the meanings of the two words *vidatha* and *vidhā* are the same is known, by similarity of meaning, from the words विदथेष्वह्नां (*vidatheṣvahnāṃ*) in the ṛk

> वयमग्ने वनुयाम त्वोता वसूयवो हविषा बुध्यमानाः ।
> वयं समर्ये विदथेष्वह्नां वयं राया सहसस्पुत्र मर्तान् ॥

> *vayamagne vanuyāma tvotā vasūyavo haviṣā budhyamānāḥ |*
> *vayaṃ samarye vidatheṣvahnāṃ vayaṃ rāyā sahasasputra martān ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-3-6, "Saṃ." printed with a broken letter) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "May we, O Agni, helped by you, seeking wealth, awake with the oblation, overcome mortals — we in battle, in the ordinances of the days, we by riches, O son of strength.")

and from the words वि — दधुः (*vi — dadhuḥ*) in the ṛk

> वि ये दधुः शरदं मासमादहर्यज्ञमक्तुं चादृचं ।
> अनाप्यं वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा क्षत्रं राजान आशत ॥

> *vi ye dadhuḥ śaradaṃ māsamādaharyajñamaktuṃ cādṛcaṃ |*
> *anāpyaṃ varuṇo mitro aryamā kṣatraṃ rājāna āśata ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-66-11) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Who ordained the autumn, the month, the day, the sacrifice, the night and the ṛk — Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, the kings, have attained an unattainable dominion.")

And, the meanings of the words *vihita* and *vidatha* being one, the sacrifice enjoined by the śāstras is itself (called) by the name *vidatha* *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 106  (PDF 124)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued.)*

… was called. This scholar has explained that the meaning "sacrifice" or "sacrificial assembly" remained in the end.

The scholar Bloomfield has shown the faults in the meaning stated by both Max Muller [as printed] and Oldenberg, saying that *vidatha* does not mean "assembly" at all, and that the meaning "a private house (*gṛha*)" alone is correct. His opinion is as follows:—

*(Quoted in English as printed; the Sanskrit words in it are printed in Kannada script and are given here in Devanagari.)*

The word विदथ (*vidatha*) contains the root विद् (*vid*) in its ordinary sense of 'get, acquire'. Instead of this, the radical idea underlying the word was generally felt to be 'come to-gether,' 'assemble'. Again, the false start from the notion of 'assemblage' resulted in an approximation of the word to other words for assemblage, especially to सभा (*sabhā*) with which विदथ (*vidatha*) was almost identified. We shall see that there are decided points of contact between the words विदथ (*vidatha*) and सभा (*sabhā*) but the contact is that of extreme opposites in a way. विदथ (*vidatha*) refers to home matters; सभा (*sabhā*) generally to public matters.

In the interpretation of a term that figures prominently in the mystic—hieratic sphere of the Veda it is peculiarly necessary to search for its uses outside of that sphere, if there be such uses. In X—85-26, the bride after the wedding ceremoney [sic] proper, as the newly married couple are about to travel to their new home is addressed with the words "May Pushan taking thee by the hand lead thee home, may the Aswins lead thee forth on their car. Go to your house in order that thou mayst be mistress of the house".

Now विदथ (*vidatha*) here, can but have one meaning, 'household' or something very like it. It certainly cannot refer to anything in the nature of a public gathering similar to the सभा (*sabhā*). In the phrase बृहद्वदेम विदथे सुवीराः (*bṛhadvadema vidathe suvīrāḥ*) (R. V. 2-1-16), the word सुवीराः (*suvīrāḥ*) refers to family relations not to public life.

Thus far, it may not be doubted, the word appears in the language of ordinary life. But it is found to a very much greater extent in the sacerdotal sphere: indeed, as all interpreters from Yaska on, have agreed, it often has a meaning very close to Yagna 'Sacrifice' itself. This is as it should be. In as much as the sacrifice is a private, home affair, it is very natural विदथ (*vidatha*) the house, the premises, the establishment, should figure prominently in connection with the sacrifice.

*(No source reference is printed after this quotation.)*

The gist of this writing is: that some have given the meaning *sabhā* (assembly) to the word *vidatha* is not right. This word means a private house. The use of this word in this very sense may be observed in many places. For example —

*(Only the first half of the ṛk is printed on this page; the second half is on the next page.)*

> पूषा त्वेतो नयतु हस्तगृह्याश्विना त्वा प्र वहतां रथेन ।

> *pūṣā tveto nayatu hastagṛhyāśvinā tvā pra vahatāṃ rathena |*

### Printed p. 107  (PDF 125)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 4". Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued.)*

> गृहान् गच्छ गृहपत्नी यथासो वशिनी त्वं विदथमा वदासि ॥

> *gṛhān gaccha gṛhapatnī yathāso vaśinī tvaṃ vidathamā vadāsi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-26) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "May Pūṣan, taking you by the hand, lead you hence; may the Aśvins carry you forth on their chariot. Go to the house, that you may be mistress of the house; as mistress you shall speak to the *vidatha*.")

— in this ṛk it is clear that the meaning is: "May Pūṣan and the Aśvin deities lead you safely to your husband's house". Besides,

> ये स्तोतृभ्यो गोअग्रामश्वपेशसमग्ने रातिमुपसृजंति सूरयः ।
> अस्माञ्च तांश्च प्र हि नेषि वस्य आ बृहद्वदेम विदथे सुवीराः ॥

> *ye stotṛbhyo goagrāmaśvapeśasamagne rātimupasṛjaṃti sūrayaḥ |*
> *asmāñca tāṃśca pra hi neṣi vasya ā bṛhadvadema vidathe suvīrāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-16) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The patrons who, O Agni, bestow on the praisers a gift headed by cows and adorned with horses — lead both us and them forward to what is better; may we, rich in heroes, speak loudly in the *vidatha*.")

— in this ṛk too, since *suvīrāḥ* has been explained as शोभनपुत्रादिसहिताः (*śobhanaputrādisahitāḥ*), "accompanied by good sons and others", the meaning is "house". But since the work of sacrifice is carried on in the house, in the present context it comes to mean "house of sacrifice". In Yāska and others' saying that it is a synonym of *yajña* this same meaning is present. In this way many Western scholars have given their individual opinions.

Thus, since the different meanings "house", "sacrifice" and "assembly" all fit, none of them can be said to be wrong. In Sāyaṇa's bhāṣya itself all these meanings are found. For example, in ṛks such as 10-85-26 and 27, 7-84-3 he has given the meaning "house"; in many ṛks such as 10-100-6, 10-110-7 the meaning "sacrifice". It also comes to mean "house of sacrifice" and "sacrificial assembly".

**इळाभिः (*iḷābhiḥ*)** — since the word *iḷā* is read among the names of the earth (Ni. 2-5, as printed), among the names of speech (Ni. 2-23, as printed), among the names of food (Ni. 3-9, as printed) and among the names of the cow (Ni. 3-9, as printed), the word *iḷā* has the different meanings earth, speech, food and cow. Here the commentator has accepted the meaning "earth" and explained इळाभिः भूमिस्थानाभिर्देवताभिः (*iḷābhiḥ bhūmisthānābhirdevatābhiḥ*): "by (with) the deities that have the earth as their abode".

**विश्वानरः (*viśvānaraḥ*)** — सर्वप्राणिहितकार्यग्निः (*sarvaprāṇihitakāryagniḥ*): the commentator's explanation is "Agni, who brings about the good of all living beings". Yāska in his Nirukta —

> वैश्वानरः । वैश्वानरः कस्माद्विश्वान्नरान्नयति । विश्व एनं नरा नयंतीति वा ।
> अपि वा विश्वानर एव स्यात् प्रत्यृतः सर्वाणि भूतानि तस्य वैश्वानरः ।

> *vaiśvānaraḥ | vaiśvānaraḥ kasmādviśvānnarānnayati | viśva enaṃ narā nayaṃtīti vā |*
> *api vā viśvānara eva syāt pratyṛtaḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni tasya vaiśvānaraḥ |*

(Ni. 7-21)

— having raised the question "What is Vaiśvānara? Why did this deity get this name?", in answer: because this deity (Agni) leads all, that is, because he is the guide of all; or because in sacrificial and other rites the sacrificer and the ṛtviks lead this Agni from the eastern altar to the place of the Āhavanīya fire — hence the name Vaiśvānara. And this Agni … all living beings *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 108  (PDF 126)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued.)*

… because he enters (all living beings), that is, because he has entered within all living beings in the form of the digestive fire (*jāṭharāgni*), this Agni has the name Vaiśvānara. They have stated the derivation that Viśvānara itself is Vaiśvānara.

For the word *vaiśvānara* they have given derivations in three ways: विश्वे सर्वे नरा एनमग्निं यज्ञादौ प्रणयंतीति विश्वेनराः तत्संबंधाद्वैश्वानरः (*viśve sarve narā enamagniṃ yajñādau praṇayaṃtīti viśvenarāḥ tatsaṃbaṃdhādvaiśvānaraḥ*) — "all men lead this Agni forward at the beginning of the sacrifice and so on, hence *viśvenarāḥ*; from connection with them, *vaiśvānara*"; विश्वेषां नराणां लोकांतरं प्रति नेतृतया संबंधी वैश्वानरः (*viśveṣāṃ narāṇāṃ lokāṃtaraṃ prati netṛtayā saṃbaṃdhī vaiśvānaraḥ*) — "connected with all men as their leader to the other world"; and विश्वान् सर्वान् प्राणिनः प्रत्यृतो गच्छत इति वैश्वानरौ, मध्यमोत्तमौ, ताभ्यामुत्पन्नः वैश्वानरः (*viśvān sarvān prāṇinaḥ pratyṛto gacchata iti vaiśvānarau, madhyamottamau, tābhyāmutpannaḥ vaiśvānaraḥ*) — "the two that go to all living beings, the middle and the highest (fires), are the *vaiśvānaras*; he who is born of them is *vaiśvānara*". The sense (of the ṛk) describing the greatness of Vaiśvānara — who slew Vṛtra, the obstructer of the clouds, who is the giver of rain and the destroyer of the Rākṣasas — has been stated. The Nirukta that indicates this same purport is as follows:

*(Nirukta passage; reference printed after it: Niru. 7-20.)*

*(Gist of the Nirukta passage: "I proclaim the greatness of the bull, the raingiver of the waters, whom men, the slayer of Vṛtra (the cloud), serve when desiring rain; Agni Vaiśvānara, slaying the Dasyu, shook down the waters and split Śambara, the cloud.")*

> प्रब्रवीमि तन्महित्वं महाभाग्यं वृषभस्य वर्षितुरपां यं पूरवः पूरयितव्या मनुष्या वृत्रहणं मेघहनं सचंते सेवंते वर्षकामा दस्युर्दस्यतेः क्षयार्थादुपदस्यंत्यस्मिन् रसा उपदासयति कर्माणि तमग्निर्वैश्वानरो घ्नन्नवाधूनोदपः काष्ठा अभिनच्छंबरं मेघं

> *prabravīmi tanmahitvaṃ mahābhāgyaṃ vṛṣabhasya varṣiturapāṃ yaṃ pūravaḥ pūrayitavyā manuṣyā vṛtrahaṇaṃ meghahanaṃ sacaṃte sevaṃte varṣakāmā dasyurdasyateḥ kṣayārthādupadasyaṃtyasmin rasā upadāsayati karmāṇi tamagnirvaiśvānaro ghnannavādhūnodapaḥ kāṣṭhā abhinacchaṃbaraṃ meghaṃ*


Upon this they have inquired who the Vaiśvānara spoken of here is. Then some have said that Vāyu or Indra, who are in the middle region, should be called Vaiśvānara, because those two have authority in the work of raining; in the matter of obtaining rain it is generally they who are to be praised; and since the earth alone is stated to be the place of Agni, that (rain-giving) is not possible for him — so they have argued. Again some say that the word *vaiśvānara* spoken of here indicates the sun. For, having set out the morning pressing (*prātassavana*), the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina savana*) and the evening pressing (*sāyaṃsavana*) as, in order, the worlds Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ and Svarga, they have decided that by the performance of each pressing the corresponding world is obtained. Then by the performance of the third pressing heaven is attained, and complete fall from the earth results. To ward off such a fall, they recite the *śastra* mantra so as to come back again to the earth by the final *śastra*, which has the nature of the Agni-Marut (*agnimāruta*). That *śastra* mantra begins with the Vaiśvānara sūkta. Afterwards they descend, by reciting the sūktas having those deities, to the deity Rudra and the Marut deities, who belong to the middle region; since Agni has the earth as his place, if the word *vaiśvānara* here did not denote the sun, how could the descent to the earth be connected with it? — so arguing they have given the meaning "sun" to the word *vaiśvānara*. But Sāyaṇācārya's opinion is that the word *vaiśvānara* means the Agni connected with the lightning that is in the middle region.

**॥ The greatness of Agni Vaiśvānara ॥** *(Kannada heading)*

> इंद्रं मित्रं वरुणमग्निमाहुरथो दिव्यः स सुपर्णो गरुत्मान् ।
> एकं सद्विप्रा बहुधा वदंत्यग्निं यमं मातरिश्वानमाहुः ॥

> *iṃdraṃ mitraṃ varuṇamagnimāhuratho divyaḥ sa suparṇo garutmān |*
> *ekaṃ sadviprā bahudhā vadaṃtyagniṃ yamaṃ mātariśvānamāhuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-46) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "They call him Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa, Agni, and he is the heavenly, well-winged Garutmān; what is One the sages speak of in many ways: they call it Agni, Yama, Mātariśvan.")

### Printed p. 109  (PDF 127)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 4". Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued.)*

*(Nirukta passage, continuing the citation of Ṛ. 1-164-46; reference printed after it: Ni. 7-18.)*

*(Gist: "This very Agni, the great Self, the one Self, the wise call by many names"; and a Brāhmaṇa also says "Agni is all the deities".)*

> इममेवाग्निं महांतमात्मानमेकमात्मानं बहुधा मेधाविनो वदंति ॥ अग्निः सर्वा देवताः इति ब्राह्मणमपि भवति ।

> *imamevāgniṃ mahāṃtamātmānamekamātmānaṃ bahudhā medhāvino vadaṃti ‖ agniḥ sarvā devatāḥ iti brāhmaṇamapi bhavati |*


All worship this very Agni, who is the great Self and the Self of all, designating him by different names such as Indra. And there are also Śruti sayings that this Vaiśvānara Agni alone is the root of all the portions of Agni that appear in different forms in different settings, and that all the remaining forms are branches of this Vaiśvānara Agni.

> वया इदग्ने अग्नयस्ते अन्ये त्वे विश्वे अमृता मादयंते ।
> वैश्वानर नाभिरसि क्षितीनां स्थूणेव जनाँ उपमिद्ययंथ ॥

> *vayā idagne agnayaste anye tve viśve amṛtā mādayaṃte |*
> *vaiśvānara nābhirasi kṣitīnāṃ sthūṇeva janā~ upamidyayaṃtha ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-59-1) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The other fires are but your branches, O Agni; in you all the immortals rejoice. O Vaiśvānara, you are the navel of the peoples; like a pillar you have upheld men.")

The Vaiśvānara Agni alone, being the cause of all the states of the whole world of gods and men, is the leader of all the affairs of the universe. Therefore all beings who desire their own good and the good of the world should know the nature of this Vaiśvānara Agni, the Self of all, and worship him: so both the Śrutis that teach the performance of rites and the Śrutis that teach spiritual knowledge make known alike the necessity of the worship of the Vaiśvānara Agni. The Saṃhitās such as the Ṛk say वैश्वानरस्य सुमतौ स्याम (*vaiśvānarasya sumatau syāma*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-98-1) ("may we be in the favour of Vaiśvānara"); the Brāhmaṇas such as the Śatapatha say स यो हैतमेवमग्निं वैश्वानरं पुरुषविधं पुरुषेऽंतः प्रतिष्ठितं वेदाप पुनर्मृत्युं जयति सर्वमायुरेति (*sa yo haitamevamagniṃ vaiśvānaraṃ puruṣavidhaṃ puruṣe 'ṃtaḥ pratiṣṭhitaṃ vedāpa punarmṛtyuṃ jayati sarvamāyureti*) — all who know the nature of this Vaiśvānara Agni, who is hidden within man and has the form of man, conquer death and obtain the full span of life (Śa. Brā. 10-6-1-11); and the Upaniṣads such as the Chāndogya, saying अथ य एतदेवं विद्वानग्निहोत्रं जुहोति तस्य सर्वेषु लोकेषु सर्वेषु भूतेषु सर्वेष्वात्मसु हुतं भवति (*atha ya etadevaṃ vidvānagnihotraṃ juhoti tasya sarveṣu lokeṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu sarveṣvātmasu hutaṃ bhavati*) — the man who, knowing the nature of the Vaiśvānara Agni thus, performs the Agnihotra, it is as though he has offered oblation in all beings, in all worlds and in all selves (Chā. U. 5-24-2) — have stated the greatness of the worship of the Vaiśvānara Agni. Therefore it is most necessary to know in this context what the nature of this deity is, and what connection this deity has with the performance of rites and with the attainment of spiritual knowledge. In the above ṛk, with राजा हि कं भुवनानामभिश्रीः (*rājā hi kaṃ bhuvanānāmabhiśrīḥ*), Vaiśvānara is described as the lord worthy of worship by all beings. But the question who that Vaiśvānara is arose along with it, and the author of the Nirukta, while explaining this very ṛk, taking many examples, has concluded that Vaiśvānara is the earthly Agni. His explanation is as follows. *(The Nirukta passage continues on the next page.)*

> वैश्वानरः कस्माद्विश्वान्नरान्नयति । विश्व एनं नरा नयंतीति वा ।

> *vaiśvānaraḥ kasmādviśvānnarānnayati | viśva enaṃ narā nayaṃtīti vā |*

### Printed p. 110  (PDF 128)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued: the Nirukta passage, concluded.)*

> अपि वा विश्वानर एव स्यात् प्रत्यृतः सर्वाणि भूतानि तस्य वैश्वानरः ॥

> *api vā viśvānara eva syāt pratyṛtaḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni tasya vaiśvānaraḥ ‖*

(Ni. 7-21-)

— because he is the leader of all, being their guide; or because all bring him forward in the sacrifice as the chief deity; or because he pervades everywhere and has entered into all beings — so they (Yāska) have made known the nature of this deity, explaining the ṛk under discussion, वैश्वानरस्य सुमतौ स्याम (*vaiśvānarasya sumatau syāma*):

> इतो जातः सर्वमिदमभिपश्यति वैश्वानरः संयतते सूर्येण राजा यः । सर्वेषां भूतानामभिश्रयणीयस्तस्य वयं वैश्वानरस्य कल्याण्यां मतौ स्यामेति ।

> *ito jātaḥ sarvamidamabhipaśyati vaiśvānaraḥ saṃyatate sūryeṇa rājā yaḥ | sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāmabhiśrayaṇīyastasya vayaṃ vaiśvānarasya kalyāṇyāṃ matau syāmeti |*

"Since he is lord over all and the refuge of all, may we all be worthy of the gracious regard of this Vaiśvānara. Born from here in the form of the earthly fire, he beholds the whole world and becomes one with the sun" — so explaining the meaning of the ṛk,

with तत्को वैश्वानरः । (*tatko vaiśvānaraḥ |*) "Who is this Vaiśvānara?" (Ni. 6[?]-22) they raise the question, discuss the disagreement among the traditions (*āgama*), and at the end make known their definite view. In their discussion they first point out the defect in the views that designate Vaiśvānara as a deity of the middle region (*antarikṣa*).

> मध्यम इत्याचार्याः । वर्षकर्मणा ह्येनं स्तौति । प्र नू महित्वं वृषभस्य वोचं ।

> *madhyama ityācāryāḥ | varṣakarmaṇā hyenaṃ stauti | pra nū mahitvaṃ vṛṣabhasya vocaṃ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-59-6) — "the ācāryas hold that he is the deity of the middle region, since, as described in this ṛk, he is praised as the cause of the work of raining". Moreover,

> एषां लोकानां रोहेण सवनानां रोह आम्नातो रोहात् प्रत्यवरोहश्चिकीर्षितस्तामनुकृतिं होताग्निमारुते शस्त्रे वैश्वानरीयेण सूक्तेन प्रतिपद्यते ।

> *eṣāṃ lokānāṃ roheṇa savanānāṃ roha āmnāto rohāt pratyavarohaścikīrṣitastāmanukṛtiṃ hotāgnimārute śastre vaiśvānarīyeṇa sūktena pratipadyate |*

> सूर्यप्रसूतावग्नी तु दृष्ट्वा पार्थिवमध्यमौ ।
> एतेषामेव लोकानां त्रयाणामध्वरेऽध्वरे ॥
> रोहात्प्रत्यवरोहेण चिकीर्षन्नग्निमारुतं ।
> शस्त्रं वैश्वानरीयेण सूक्तेन प्रतिपद्यते ॥

> *sūryaprasūtāvagnī tu dṛṣṭvā pārthivamadhyamau |*
> *eteṣāmeva lokānāṃ trayāṇāmadhvare 'dhvare ‖*
> *rohātpratyavaroheṇa cikīrṣannagnimārutaṃ |*
> *śastraṃ vaiśvānarīyeṇa sūktena pratipadyate ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 1-101 : 1-102) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Seeing the two fires, the earthly and the middle, as produced from the sun, in every sacrifice, wishing to make the descent after the ascent of these three worlds, (the Hotṛ) begins the Agnimāruta *śastra* with the Vaiśvānara sūkta.")

There is an injunction that the increase of the oblations should follow the ascending order of earth, mid-region and heaven. After the ascending order the descending order must be carried out. Following this method, the sacrificer, in this Vaiśvānarīya sūkta recited addressed to Agni and the Maruts, praises Vaiśvānara first, in the descending order. With this very intention the (Vaiśvānara) designated here *(continues on the next page)*
