### Printed p. 111  (PDF 129)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 4". Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued.)*

… having explained the prior view (*pūrvapakṣa*) — अथासावादित्य इति पूर्वे याज्ञिकाः । (*athāsāvāditya iti pūrve yājñikāḥ |*) — that the ancient sacrificers (*yājñika*) hold the Vaiśvānara designated here to be the Āditya (sun), then:

> सोऽपि न स्तोत्रियमाद्रियेताग्नेयो हि भवति । तत आगच्छति मध्यस्थाना देवता रुद्रं च मरुतश्च ततोऽग्निमिहस्थानमत्र वै स्तोत्रियं शंसति ।

> *so 'pi na stotriyamādriyetāgneyo hi bhavati | tata āgacchati madhyasthānā devatā rudraṃ ca marutaśca tato 'gnimihasthānamatra vai stotriyaṃ śaṃsati |*

Since this sūkta is addressed chiefly to Agni, and since, after designating Rudra and the Maruts, the sacrificer again praises, addressing it once more, the Agni that belongs to that earthly world, in whatever earthly sacrificial hall he recites this sūkta — therefore they (Yāska) have refuted the above view, holding that the Vaiśvānara Agni designated here is a deity of the earthly region and not one of the mid-region. And, supporting their thesis that this Vaiśvānara Agni is an earthly deity, they have cited suitable Śruti sentences:

*("अथास्याद" as printed.)*

> अथास्याद – इतो जातो विश्वमिदं वि चष्टे वैश्वानरो यतते सूर्येण ॥

> *athāsyāda – ito jāto viśvamidaṃ vi caṣṭe vaiśvānaro yatate sūryeṇa ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-98-1) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Born from here, he surveys this whole world; Vaiśvānara vies with the sun.")

> न च पुनरात्मनात्मा संयततेऽन्येनैवान्यः संयतत इत इममादधात्यमुतोऽमुष्य रश्मयः प्रादुर्भवंतीतोऽस्यार्चिषस्तयोर्भासोः संसंगं दृष्ट्वैवमवक्ष्यत् ॥

> *na ca punarātmanātmā saṃyatate 'nyenaivānyaḥ saṃyatata ita imamādadhātyamuto 'muṣya raśmayaḥ prādurbhavaṃtīto 'syārciṣastayorbhāsoḥ saṃsaṃgaṃ dṛṣṭvaivamavakṣyat ‖*

The Saṃhitā sentence, that Vaiśvānara himself spreads widely and joins with the sun, also helps this support. If Vaiśvānara were himself the sun, it would be impossible that he should spread out and join with himself; it is natural to say that one thing, spreading out, joins with another. After the sacrificer has made Agni blaze on the earth, its rays spread to the world above and appear there too. Seeing them join with the rays of the Āditya that pervade the mid-region, and the two becoming one, it is described as यतते सूर्येण (*yatate sūryeṇa*). Moreover,

> अथ यान्येतान्यौत्तमिकानि सूक्तानि भागानि वा सावित्राणि वा सौर्याणि वा पौष्णानि वा वैष्णवानि वा वैश्वदेव्यानि वा तेषु वैश्वानरीयाः प्रवादा अभविष्यन्नादित्यकर्मणा चैनमस्तोष्यन्नित्युदेषीत्यस्तमेषीति विपर्येषीति ।

> *atha yānyetānyauttamikāni sūktāni bhāgāni vā sāvitrāṇi vā sauryāṇi vā pauṣṇāni vā vaiṣṇavāni vā vaiśvadevyāni vā teṣu vaiśvānarīyāḥ pravādā abhaviṣyannādityakarmaṇā cainamastoṣyannityudeṣītyastameṣīti viparyeṣīti |*

If Vaiśvānara were the sun, then the nature and the actions of the mid-region deities such as Savitṛ, Pūṣan, Viṣṇu and the Viśvedevas would have had to be described as attributed (*adhyāhṛta*) to him, and there would also have had to be descriptions such as "he rises, he sets, he goes round". But *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 112  (PDF 130)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued.)*

… since here there are only descriptions that have Agni as their deity, it is firmly known that (*vaiśvānara*) is a synonym of the earthly Agni. From these and other grounds,

*("निरूप्यते (*nirūpyate*)" as printed.)*

> यस्तु सूक्तं भजते यस्मै हविर्निरूप्यतेऽयमेव सोऽग्निर्वैश्वानरः ।

> *yastu sūktaṃ bhajate yasmai havirnirūpyate 'yameva so 'gnirvaiśvānaraḥ |*

— it can be said with certainty that the praise recited in the sūkta and the offering of the oblation are both offered addressed to the Agni in the form of Vaiśvānara alone (Ni. 7-22 to 7-31). The manifestation of this Vaiśvānara Agni is, even apart from the earth, he alone: राजा हि कं भुवनानामभिश्रीः । (*rājā hi kaṃ bhuvanānāmabhiśrīḥ |*) — he is the lord and the refuge of all classes of beings. Therefore it has been stated clearly in many places that all, gods and men alike, can attain the highest good (*śreyas*) only through his worship. If worship that knows his earthly form through the performance of rites is one way, worship to be done through spiritual (*ādhyātmika*) knowledge, which knows his greatness — that he pervades the universe and is present within all the sentient and the insentient of the whole world — is the other way. Making known the connection between the performance of rites and the worship by knowledge, the greatness of the Vaiśvānara Agni, the Self of all, has been described in the Brāhmaṇas such as the Śatapatha and in the Upaniṣads such as the Chāndogya. The story of the ṛṣis who went seeking a worthy teacher in order to know his true nature is described in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (10-6-1-1 to 11).

> अपि वा विश्वानर एव स्यात् प्रत्यृतः सर्वाणि भूतानि तस्य वैश्वानरः ।

> *api vā viśvānara eva syāt pratyṛtaḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni tasya vaiśvānaraḥ |*

(Ni. 7-21) — just as in the Niruktakāra's derivation, "he who pervades everywhere and is present within all beings", this story makes known the nature of Viśvānara, the inner controller (*antaryāmin*) of all:

*("अरुणे औपवेशौ (*aruṇe aupaveśau*)" as printed.)*

> अथ हैतेऽरुणे औपवेशौ समाजग्मुः सत्ययज्ञः पौलुषिर्महाशालो जाबालो बुडिल आश्वतराश्विरिंद्रद्युम्नो भाल्लवेयो जनः शार्कराक्ष्यस्ते ह समासत तेषां ह वैश्वानरे न समियाय ॥ १ ॥

> *atha haite 'ruṇe aupaveśau samājagmuḥ satyayajñaḥ pauluṣirmahāśālo jābālo buḍila āśvatarāśviriṃdradyumno bhāllaveyo janaḥ śārkarākṣyaste ha samāsata teṣāṃ ha vaiśvānare na samiyāya ‖ 1 ‖*

Satyayajña Pauluṣi, Mahāśāla Jābāla, Buḍila Aśvatara Āśvi, Indradyumna Bhāllaveya and Jana Śārkarākṣya gathered together in the house of Aruṇa Aupaveśi; though they all met and discussed in order to know the nature of the Vaiśvānara Agni, no definite understanding arose for them; there arose a difference in their opinions; there arose disagreement. ‖ 1 ‖

> ते होचुः । अश्वपतिर्वायं कैकेयः संप्रति वैश्वानरं वेद तं गच्छामेति ते हाश्वपतिं कैकेयमाजग्मुस्तेभ्यो ह पृथगावसथान्पृथगपचितीः पृथक्साहस्रान्सोमान्प्रोवाच ते ह प्रातरसंविदाना एव समित्पाणयः प्रतिचक्रमिर उप त्वायामेति ॥ २ ॥

> *te hocuḥ | aśvapatirvāyaṃ kaikeyaḥ saṃprati vaiśvānaraṃ veda taṃ gacchāmeti te hāśvapatiṃ kaikeyamājagmustebhyo ha pṛthagāvasathānpṛthagapacitīḥ pṛthaksāhasrānsomānprovāca te ha prātarasaṃvidānā eva samitpāṇayaḥ praticakramira upa tvāyāmeti ‖ 2 ‖*

### Printed p. 113  (PDF 131)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 4". Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued: the Śatapatha story.)*

Then all of them together went to Aśvapati Kaikeya, who knew the nature of the Vaiśvānara Agni completely. He offered all these guests who had come there separate lodgings, individual honours and thousands of drinks, and entertained them. Next morning all of them, keeping their differences of opinion, holding samidh-sticks in their hands, made the request: "We wish to become your disciples." ‖ 2 ‖

*("खलु न्वा (*khalu nvā*)" as printed.)*

> स होवाच । यन्नु भगवंतोऽनूचाना अनूचानपुत्राः किमिदमिति ते होचुर्वैश्वानरं ह भगवान्त्संप्रति वेद तं नो ब्रूहीति स होवाच संप्रति खलु न्वा अहं वैश्वानरं वेदाभ्याधत्त समिध उपेता स्थेति ॥ ३ ॥

> *sa hovāca | yannu bhagavaṃto 'nūcānā anūcānaputrāḥ kimidamiti te hocurvaiśvānaraṃ ha bhagavāntsaṃprati veda taṃ no brūhīti sa hovāca saṃprati khalu nvā ahaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vedābhyādhatta samidha upetā stheti ‖ 3 ‖*

Then he asked them in wonder: "You are sons of men versed in all the śāstras and have yourselves studied; why have you come to me for discipleship?" Then they requested: "You know well the nature of the Vaiśvānara Agni; teach its secret to us also." He said: "I know that secret; I will teach it to you also. Offer samidh-sticks to the fire; from today you are my disciples." ‖ 3 ‖

*("एतं रयिं वैश्वानर एतं (*etaṃ rayiṃ vaiśvānara etaṃ*)", "प्रतिष्ठा वैश्वानरं (*pratiṣṭhā vaiśvānaraṃ*)", "प्रज्ञया (*prajñayā*)" and "पादौ त्वा एतौ (*pādau tvā etau*)" as printed.)*

> स होवाचारुणमौपवेशिं । गौतम कं त्वं वैश्वानरं वेत्थेति पृथिवीमेव राजन्निति होवाचोमिति होवाचैष वै प्रतिष्ठा एतं रयिं वैश्वानर एतं हि वै त्वं प्रतिष्ठा वैश्वानरं वेत्थ तस्मात्त्वं प्रतिष्ठितः प्रज्ञया पशुभिरसि यो वा एतं प्रतिष्ठां वैश्वानरं वेदाप पुनर्मृत्युं जयति सर्वमायुरेति पादौ त्वा एतौ वैश्वानरस्य पादौ तेऽम्लास्यतां यदि ह नागमिष्य इति पादौ तेऽविदितावभविष्यतां यदि ह नागमिष्य इति वा ॥ ४ ॥

> *sa hovācāruṇamaupaveśiṃ | gautama kaṃ tvaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vettheti pṛthivīmeva rājanniti hovācomiti hovācaiṣa vai pratiṣṭhā etaṃ rayiṃ vaiśvānara etaṃ hi vai tvaṃ pratiṣṭhā vaiśvānaraṃ vettha tasmāttvaṃ pratiṣṭhitaḥ prajñayā paśubhirasi yo vā etaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vedāpa punarmṛtyuṃ jayati sarvamāyureti pādau tvā etau vaiśvānarasya pādau te 'mlāsyatāṃ yadi ha nāgamiṣya iti pādau te 'viditāvabhaviṣyatāṃ yadi ha nāgamiṣya iti vā ‖ 4 ‖*

Then, addressing Aruṇa Aupaveśi, he asked: "Gautama, as you know it, who is Vaiśvānara?" He said: "The earth is Vaiśvānara." Then the king said: "Yes; that is Vaiśvānara, the support of all. Because you know this secret you are firmly established with cattle, sons and the rest! He who knows this conquers death and obtains the full span of life. But in truth these are only the feet of Vaiśvānara. Had you not come here (to know the full nature of Vaiśvānara), your feet would have grown slack and withered, or they would not have come within your perception." ‖ 4 ‖

*("हनागमिष्य (*hanāgamiṣya*)" printed joined. The small stroke under त्वा (*tvā*) before हास्यद्यदि (*hāsyadyadi*) is the subscript va of त्वा (*tvā*); read with p. 115.)*

> अथ होवाच सत्ययज्ञं पौलुषिं । प्राचीनयोग्य, कं त्वं वैश्वानरं वेत्थेत्यप एव राजन्निति होवाचोमिति होवाचैष वै रयिर्वैश्वानर एतं हि वै त्वं रयिं वैश्वानरं वेत्थ तस्मात्त्वं रयिमान्पुष्टिमानसि यो वा एतं रयिं वैश्वानरं वेदाप पुनर्मृत्युं जयति सर्वमायुरेति वस्तिस्त्वा एष वैश्वानरस्य वस्तिस्त्वाहास्यद्यदि ह नागमिष्य इति वस्तिस्तेऽविदितोऽभविष्यद्यदि हनागमिष्य इति वा ॥ ५ ॥

> *atha hovāca satyayajñaṃ pauluṣiṃ | prācīnayogya, kaṃ tvaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vetthetyapa eva rājanniti hovācomiti hovācaiṣa vai rayirvaiśvānara etaṃ hi vai tvaṃ rayiṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vettha tasmāttvaṃ rayimānpuṣṭimānasi yo vā etaṃ rayiṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vedāpa punarmṛtyuṃ jayati sarvamāyureti vastistvā eṣa vaiśvānarasya vastistvāhāsyadyadi ha nāgamiṣya iti vastiste 'vidito 'bhaviṣyadyadi hanāgamiṣya iti vā ‖ 5 ‖*

*(The Kannada explanation of ¶ 5 follows on the next page.)*

### Printed p. 114  (PDF 132)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued: the Śatapatha story.)*

Then, addressing Satyayajña Pauluṣi, he asked: "O Prācīnayogya, whom do you know as Vaiśvānara?" He said: "The waters (*udaka*) are Vaiśvānara." Approving that too, the king said: "That is the wealth belonging to Vaiśvānara. Because you know the nature of that wealth you are wealthy and of high standing. He who knows it conquers death and surely obtains the full span of life. But this is only the inner treasury (*antaḥkośa*) of Vaiśvānara. Had you not come here, your treasury would have become useless, or it would not have come within your perception at all." ‖ 5 ‖

*(वैशानर (*vaiśānara*) as printed for वैश्वानर (*vaiśvānara*) in the second clause; त्वाहास्यद्यदि (*tvāhāsyadyadi*) printed as on p. 113.)*

> अथ होवाच महाशालं जाबालं । औपमन्यव कं त्वं वैश्वानरं वेत्थेत्याकाशमेव राजन्निति होवाचोमिति होवाचैष वै बहुलो वैशानर एतं हि वै त्वं बहुलं वैश्वानरं वेत्थ तस्मात्त्वं बहु प्रजया पशुभिरसि यो वा एतं बहुलं वैश्वानरं वेदाप पुनर्मृत्युं जयति सर्वमायुरेत्यात्मा त्वा एष वैश्वानरस्यात्मा त्वाहास्यद्यदि ह नागमिष्य इत्यात्मा तेऽविदितोऽभविष्यद्यदि ह नागमिष्य इति वा ॥ ६ ॥

> *atha hovāca mahāśālaṃ jābālaṃ | aupamanyava kaṃ tvaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vetthetyākāśameva rājanniti hovācomiti hovācaiṣa vai bahulo vaiśānara etaṃ hi vai tvaṃ bahulaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vettha tasmāttvaṃ bahu prajayā paśubhirasi yo vā etaṃ bahulaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vedāpa punarmṛtyuṃ jayati sarvamāyuretyātmā tvā eṣa vaiśvānarasyātmā tvāhāsyadyadi ha nāgamiṣya ityātmā te 'vidito 'bhaviṣyadyadi ha nāgamiṣya iti vā ‖ 6 ‖*

Then, addressing Mahāśāla Jābāla, he said: "O Aupamanyava, whom do you know as Vaiśvānara?" When he gave the answer "the sky (*ākāśa*)", (the king) accepted that too and said: "That is Vaiśvānara the abundant (*bahula*, i.e. prosperous); because you know this, you have an abundance of cattle, sons and the like. He who knows this conquers death and obtains the full span of life. But this is only the main trunk of Vaiśvānara. Had you not come here, the chief essence of your body would have become useless, or you would not have known it at all." ‖ 6 ‖

*(होच (*hoca*)[?] as printed at the opening, not होवाच (*hovāca*).)*

> अथ होच[?] बुडिलमाश्वतराश्विं । वैयाघ्रपद्य कं त्वं वैश्वानरं वेत्थेति वायुमेव राजन्निति होवाचोमिति होवाचैष वै पृथग्वर्त्मा । वैश्वानर एतं हि वै त्वं पृथग्वर्त्मानं वैश्वानरं वेत्थ तस्मात्त्वां पृथग्रथश्रेणयोऽनुयांति यो वा एतं पृथग्वर्त्मानं वैश्वानरं वेदाप पुनर्मृत्युं जयति सर्वमायुरेति प्राणस्त्वा एष वैश्वानरस्य प्राणस्त्वाहास्यद्यदि ह नागमिष्य इति प्राणस्तेऽविदितोऽभविष्यद्यदि ह नागमिष्य इति वा ॥ ७ ॥

> *atha hoca[?] buḍilamāśvatarāśviṃ | vaiyāghrapadya kaṃ tvaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vettheti vāyumeva rājanniti hovācomiti hovācaiṣa vai pṛthagvartmā | vaiśvānara etaṃ hi vai tvaṃ pṛthagvartmānaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vettha tasmāttvāṃ pṛthagrathaśreṇayo 'nuyāṃti yo vā etaṃ pṛthagvartmānaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vedāpa punarmṛtyuṃ jayati sarvamāyureti prāṇastvā eṣa vaiśvānarasya prāṇastvāhāsyadyadi ha nāgamiṣya iti prāṇaste 'vidito 'bhaviṣyadyadi ha nāgamiṣya iti vā ‖ 7 ‖*

Again, addressing Buḍila Āśvatarāśvi, he said: "O Vaiyāghrapadya, whom do you know as Vaiśvānara?" He said: "Vāyu is Vaiśvānara." Accepting that too, the royal sage said: "Vāyu is the manifold path of Vaiśvānara. Because you know this, chariots that move on many paths follow you. He who knows this surely conquers death and the full span of life *(continues on the next page)*

… obtains. But this is only the breath (*usiru*) of Vaiśvānara. Had you not come to me, your breath too would have become useless, or you would not have had any knowledge of it." ‖ 7 ‖

*(वैयाघ्रपद्य (*vaiyāghrapadya*) and त्वां (*tvāṃ*) as printed.)*

> अथ होवाचेंद्रद्युम्नं भाल्लवेयं । वैयाघ्रपद्य कं त्वं वैश्वानरं वेत्थेत्यादित्यमेव राजन्निति होवाचोमिति होवाचैष वै सुततेजा वैश्वानर एतं हि वै त्वां सुततेजसं वैश्वानरं वेत्थ तस्मात्त्वैष सुतोऽद्यमानः पच्यमानोऽक्षीयमाणो गृहेषु तिष्ठति यो वा एतं सुततेजसं वैश्वानरं वेदाप पुनर्मृत्युं जयति सर्वमायुरेति चक्षुस्त्वा एतद्वैश्वानरस्य चक्षुस्त्वाहास्यद्यदि ह नागमिष्य इति चक्षुस्तेऽविदितमभविष्यद्यदि ह नागमिष्य इति वा ॥ ८ ॥

> *atha hovāceṃdradyumnaṃ bhāllaveyaṃ | vaiyāghrapadya kaṃ tvaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vetthetyādityameva rājanniti hovācomiti hovācaiṣa vai sutatejā vaiśvānara etaṃ hi vai tvāṃ sutatejasaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vettha tasmāttvaiṣa suto 'dyamānaḥ pacyamāno 'kṣīyamāṇo gṛheṣu tiṣṭhati yo vā etaṃ sutatejasaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vedāpa punarmṛtyuṃ jayati sarvamāyureti cakṣustvā etadvaiśvānarasya cakṣustvāhāsyadyadi ha nāgamiṣya iti cakṣuste 'viditamabhaviṣyadyadi ha nāgamiṣya iti vā ‖ 8 ‖*

Then, addressing Indradyumna Bhāllaveya, when he asked him whom he knew as Vaiśvānara, he said: "Āditya is Vaiśvānara." Approving that too, (the king said): "Truly, Vaiśvānara is the splendour of Soma. Because you know this, Soma juice and its cooking are never absent from your house. He who knows this conquers death and obtains the full span of life. But this is only the eye of Vaiśvānara. Had you not come to me, your eye too would have become useless, or you would not have had any knowledge of it." ‖ 8 ‖

*(वाऽअतिष्ठा (*vā 'atiṣṭhā*) and हि वे (*hi ve*) as printed; मूर्धा त्वाहास्यद्यदि (*mūrdhā tvāhāsyadyadi*) as in ¶ 6.)*

> अथ होवाच जनं शार्कराक्ष्यं । सायवस कं त्वं वैश्वानरं वेत्थेति दिवमेव राजन्निति होवाच ओमिति होवाचैष वाऽअतिष्ठा वैश्वानर एतं हि वे त्वमतिष्ठा वैश्वानरं वेत्थ तस्मात्त्वं समानानतितिष्ठसि यो वा एतमतिष्ठां वैश्वानरं वेदाप पुनर्मृत्युं जयति सर्वमायुरेति मूर्धा त्वा एष वैश्वानरस्य मूर्धा त्वाहास्यद्यदि ह नागमिष्य इति मूर्धा तेऽविदितोऽभविष्यद्यदि ह नागमिष्य इति वा ॥ ९ ॥

> *atha hovāca janaṃ śārkarākṣyaṃ | sāyavasa kaṃ tvaṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vettheti divameva rājanniti hovāca omiti hovācaiṣa vā 'atiṣṭhā vaiśvānara etaṃ hi ve tvamatiṣṭhā vaiśvānaraṃ vettha tasmāttvaṃ samānānatitiṣṭhasi yo vā etamatiṣṭhāṃ vaiśvānaraṃ vedāpa punarmṛtyuṃ jayati sarvamāyureti mūrdhā tvā eṣa vaiśvānarasya mūrdhā tvāhāsyadyadi ha nāgamiṣya iti mūrdhā te 'vidito 'bhaviṣyadyadi ha nāgamiṣya iti vā ‖ 9 ‖*

Then, addressing Jana Śārkarākṣya, he asked: "O Sāyavasa, whom do you know as Vaiśvānara?" He said: "The mid-region (*antarikṣa*)." (So the Kannada, as printed; the Sanskrit has दिवमेव (*divameva*), "heaven".) Approving that too, (the king said): "The mid-region is the most excellent part of Vaiśvānara. Because you know it, you have become pre-eminent above all your equals. He who knows this conquers death and obtains the full span of life. But this is only the head of Vaiśvānara. Had you not come to me, your head too would have become useless, or you would not have had any understanding of it." ‖ 9 ‖

*(पृथगन्नमघस्तं (*pṛthagannamaghastaṃ*) as printed.)*

> तान् होवाच एते वै यूयं पृथग्वैश्वानरान्विद्वांसः पृथगन्नमघस्तं प्रादेशमात्रमिव ह वै देवाः सुविदिता अभिसंपन्नास्तथा तु व एनान्वक्ष्यामि यथा प्रादेशमात्रमेवाभिसंपादयिष्यामीति ॥ १० ॥

> *tān hovāca ete vai yūyaṃ pṛthagvaiśvānarānvidvāṃsaḥ pṛthagannamaghastaṃ prādeśamātramiva ha vai devāḥ suviditā abhisaṃpannāstathā tu va enānvakṣyāmi yathā prādeśamātramevābhisaṃpādayiṣyāmīti ‖ 10 ‖*

*(The Kannada explanation of ¶ 10 follows on the next page.)*

### Printed p. 116  (PDF 134)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued: the Śatapatha story.)*

Finally, addressing all of them together, (the king) said: "Each one of you has grasped only separate parts of Vaiśvānara. That is why you eat separate food. Since these well-known deities exist only as span-measured (*prādeśa-vartin*) (Measure of a span), I shall explain them to you so that those deities are (seen as) only span-measured." ‖ 10 ‖

*("वैशानर (*vaiśānara*)" in the first clause, "नासिकेऽउपदिशन्नुवाचैष (*nāsike 'upadiśannuvācaiṣa*)", "छुबकम् (*chubakam*)" and the closing numeral ‖ १० ‖ (10, where 11 is expected; the Kannada explanation below closes ‖ 11 ‖) as printed.)*

> स होवाच । मूर्धानमुपदिशन्नेष वा अतिष्ठा वैशानर इति, चक्षुषी उपदिशन्नुवाचैष वै सुततेजा वैश्वानर इति, नासिकेऽउपदिशन्नुवाचैष वै पृथग्वर्त्मा वैश्वानर इति, मुख्यमाकाशमुपदिशन्नुवाचैष वै बहुलो वैश्वानर इति मुख्या अप उपदिशन्नुवाचैष वै रयिर्वैश्वानर इति छुबकमुपदिशन्नुवाचैष वै प्रतिष्ठा वैश्वानर इति, स एषोऽग्निर्वैश्वानरो यत्पुरुषः स यो हैतमेवमग्निं वैश्वानरं पुरुषविधं पुरुषेऽन्तः प्रतिष्ठितं वेदाप पुनर्मृत्युं जयति सर्वमायुरेति न हास्य ब्रुवाणं च न वैश्वानरो हिनस्ति ॥ १० ॥

> *sa hovāca | mūrdhānamupadiśanneṣa vā atiṣṭhā vaiśānara iti, cakṣuṣī upadiśannuvācaiṣa vai sutatejā vaiśvānara iti, nāsike 'upadiśannuvācaiṣa vai pṛthagvartmā vaiśvānara iti, mukhyamākāśamupadiśannuvācaiṣa vai bahulo vaiśvānara iti mukhyā apa upadiśannuvācaiṣa vai rayirvaiśvānara iti chubakamupadiśannuvācaiṣa vai pratiṣṭhā vaiśvānara iti, sa eṣo 'gnirvaiśvānaro yatpuruṣaḥ sa yo haitamevamagniṃ vaiśvānaraṃ puruṣavidhaṃ puruṣe 'ntaḥ pratiṣṭhitaṃ vedāpa punarmṛtyuṃ jayati sarvamāyureti na hāsya bruvāṇaṃ ca na vaiśvānaro hinasti ‖ 10 ‖*

Finally, pointing to the head, (he explained) that this is the most excellent part of Vaiśvānara; pointing to the eyes, that this is the splendour of Soma, a part of Vaiśvānara; pointing towards the nose, that this is the manifoldness of the paths of Vaiśvānara; pointing to the space (*ākāśa*) (of the mouth), that this is the prosperous Vaiśvānara; pointing towards the water of the mouth, that this is the wealth of Vaiśvānara; pointing to the chin, that this is the support of Vaiśvānara. He explained that this Vaiśvānara Agni is none other than the best of persons (*puruṣa-śreṣṭha*); that he who knows this Vaiśvānara Agni, who has the form of a person and is established within the person, conquers death and obtains the full span of life; and that no harm can come to him who constantly praises him. ‖ 11 ‖

(Śa. Brā. 10, 6-1-1 to 11)

अभिपित्वे (*abhipitve*) — for this word Sāyaṇa has given the explanation अभिपतने (*abhipatane*), "now going on, or now attained". Yāska in the Nirukta (Ni. 3-15) also says अभिपित्वम् अभिप्राप्तिम् (*abhipitvam abhiprāptim*), giving the same sense, "now going on, or now being done".

*(Ni. 3-15 read on a zoom.)*

विश्वं जगत् (*viśvaṃ jagat*) — for these words Sāyaṇa has given two kinds of meaning:

> एतत्स्थावरस्याप्युपलक्षणम् । कृत्स्नं प्रपंचम् ।

> *etatsthāvarasyāpyupalakṣaṇam | kṛtsnaṃ prapaṃcam |*

that is, one meaning, "the whole world, including the immobile"; and

> यद्वा जगच्छब्दो यजमानरूपमनुष्यवाची । सर्वानपि यजमानान्

> *yadvā jagacchabdo yajamānarūpamanuṣyavācī | sarvānapi yajamānān*

or else, the word जगत् (*jagat*) denotes men in the form of sacrificers. Therefore he has given the second meaning, that here विश्वं जगत् (*viśvaṃ jagat*) means "all the sacrificers".

### Printed p. 117  (PDF 135)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 4". Special Topics of Ṛk 1, concluded; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā; Ṛk 2 begins.)*

मनीषा (*manīṣā*) —

> मनीषया । मनस ईशितृत्वेन । स्वेच्छयेत्यर्थः ।

> *manīṣayā | manasa īśitṛtvena | svecchayetyarthaḥ |*

that is, "as one's own mind says, or as it approves" — the intention is "out of self-contentment".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly). इळाभिः (*iḷābhiḥ*) from ईड स्तुतौ (*īḍa stutau*) (short vowel, छान्दस (*chāndasa*); क्विप् (*kvip*) by क्विप् च (*kvip ca*); टाप् (*ṭāp*) by आपं चापि हलन्तानां यथा वाचा दिशा निशा (*āpaṃ cāpi halantānāṃ yathā vācā diśā niśā*), Kau. 2-4-82 as printed, zoomed); सुशस्ति (*suśasti*) from शंसु स्तुतौ (*śaṃsu stutau*) (स्त्रियां क्तिन् (*striyāṃ ktin*); अनुदात्तोपदेशवनति… (*anudāttopadeśavanati…*) Pā. Sū. 6-4-37; नञ्सुभ्याम् (*nañsubhyām*) Pā. Sū. 6-2-172; सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) Pā. Sū. 7-1-39); वैश्वानरः (*vaiśvānaraḥ*) by नरे संज्ञायाम् (*nare saṃjñāyām*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-129, zoomed); एतु (*etu*) (इण् गतौ (*iṇ gatau*), लोट् (*loṭ*)); मत्सथ (*matsatha*) (मदी हर्षग्लेपनयोः (*madī harṣaglepanayoḥ*); सिब्बहुलं लेटि (*sibbahulaṃ leṭi*) Pā. Sū. 3-1-34; खरि च (*khari ca*); तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*) Pā. Sū. 6-1-186); मनीषा (*manīṣā*) (सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*), लुक् (*luk*) of the instrumental singular).

## Sūkta 186, Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

*(अ (*a*) printed at the opening, not आ (*ā*); see the Pada.)*

> अ नो विश्व आस्क्रा गमन्तु देवा मित्रो अर्यमा वरुणः सजोषाः ।
> भुवन्यथा नो विश्वे वृधासः करन्त्सुषाहा विथुरं न शवः ॥ २ ॥

> *a no viśva āskrā gamantu devā mitro aryamā varuṇaḥ sajoṣāḥ |*
> *bhuvanyathā no viśve vṛdhāsaḥ karantsuṣāhā vithuraṃ na śavaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

---

### Printed p. 118  (PDF 136)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Ṛk 2, continued. The Pada has आ (*ā*), so the Saṃhitā's अ (*a*) on p. 117 is a misprint; Pada सुऽसहा (*su 'sahā*) as printed.)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> आ । नः । विश्वे । आस्क्राः । गमन्तु । देवाः । मित्रः । अर्यमा । वरुणः । सऽजोषाः ।
> भुवन् । यथा । नः । विश्वे । वृधासः । करन् । सुऽसहा । विथुरम् । न । शवः ॥ २ ॥

> *ā | naḥ | viśve | āskrāḥ | gamantu | devāḥ | mitraḥ | aryamā | varuṇaḥ | sa 'joṣāḥ |*
> *bhuvan | yathā | naḥ | viśve | vṛdhāsaḥ | karan | su 'sahā | vithuram | na | śavaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed)*

*Gist:* Use: the puronuvākyā of the oblation at the Vaiśvadeva animal-offering (Āś. 3-7, as read). May all the gods, assailants of foes, and Mitra, Aryaman, Varuṇa, of one accord, come, so that they increase us and, overcoming foes, do not make our food scant.

> वैश्वदेवे पशावा नो विश्व इत्येषा हविषः पुरोऽनुवाक्या । आ नो देवानामुपवेतु शंस आ नो विश्व आस्क्रा गमन्तु देवाः । आ. ३-७ । इति ॥
> नोऽस्माकं यज्ञं विश्वे सर्वे देवा आस्क्राः शत्रूणामास्कंदयितार आक्रमितारो वा आ गमन्तु । आगच्छन्तु । के ते । मित्रोऽर्यमा वरुणश्च त्रयोऽपि सजोषाः समानप्रीतयः सन्त आगच्छन्तु । किन्तु विश्वे देवा नोऽस्माकं वृधासो वर्धयितारो यथा भुवन् भवेयुः तथा सुषाहा सुष्ठु शत्रूणामभिभवेन नोऽस्मदीयं शवोऽन्नं विथुरं हीनं यथा न करन् न कुर्युः तथागच्छन्तु ॥

> *vaiśvadeve paśāvā no viśva ityeṣā haviṣaḥ puro 'nuvākyā | ā no devānāmupavetu śaṃsa ā no viśva āskrā gamantu devāḥ | ā. 3-7 | iti ‖*
> *no 'smākaṃ yajñaṃ viśve sarve devā āskrāḥ śatrūṇāmāskaṃdayitāra ākramitāro vā ā gamantu | āgacchantu | ke te | mitro 'ryamā varuṇaśca trayo 'pi sajoṣāḥ samānaprītayaḥ santa āgacchantu | kintu viśve devā no 'smākaṃ vṛdhāso vardhayitāro yathā bhuvan bhaveyuḥ tathā suṣāhā suṣṭhu śatrūṇāmabhibhavena no 'smadīyaṃ śavo 'nnaṃ vithuraṃ hīnaṃ yathā na karan na kuryuḥ tathāgacchantu ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** विश्वे (देवाः) (*viśve (devāḥ)*) — the Viśvedevas; नः (*naḥ*) — for us; वृधासः (*vṛdhāsaḥ*) — as causers of increase; यथा भुवन् (*yathā bhuvan*) — as they may become (and); सुषाहा (*suṣāhā*) — by defeating and destroying the enemies; नः (*naḥ*) — our; शवः (*śavaḥ*) — food; विथुरम् (*vithuram*) — as diminished; (यथा (*yathā*)) न करन् (*na karan*) — as they do not make (it), (so); मित्रः (*mitraḥ*) — Mitra; अर्यमा (*aryamā*) — Aryaman; वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*) — Varuṇa; विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*) — all these deities; सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*) — joined together with equal love; आस्क्राः (*āskrāḥ*) — confronting (our enemies); नः (*naḥ*) — towards our sacrifice; आ गमन्तु (*ā gamantu*) — may they come.

**Bhāvārtha.** So that the Viśvedevas may be causers of increase for us and, by defeating and destroying our enemies, may be such as increase our food without letting it fail, may Mitra, Aryaman, Varuṇa and all these deities, joined together with equal love and confronting our enemies, come towards our sacrifice.

**English Translation (as printed; heading printed "English Trnslation" [sic]):**

May all the triumphant gods, Mitra, Aryaman, Varuna equally well pleased, come (to our rite) : may they all be propitious to us : may they not leave us in want of food, after overcoming (our foes).

### Printed p. 119  (PDF 137)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 4". Ṛk 2, continued.)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

It is laid down by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra आ नो देवानामुपवेतु शंस आ नो विश्व आस्क्रा गमन्तु देवाः (*ā no devānāmupavetu śaṃsa ā no viśva āskrā gamantu devāḥ*) (Āś. 3-7, as read) that, when the oblation having the Viśvedevas as deity is offered in the animal sacrifice, this ṛk आ नो विश्वे (*ā no viśve*) is to be used as the puronuvākyā mantra.

आस्क्राः (*āskrāḥ*) — those who defeat, or who assail, the enemies. It is prayed that the deities, defeating our enemies, come to our place of sacrifice and grant us food and other sustenance.

विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*) — it is prayed here that all the deities come together with the deities Mitra, Aryaman and Varuṇa. If it is asked whether, when "all the deities" is said, the deities Mitra, Aryaman and Varuṇa are not already included among them — even though they are included, the names of these three deities are indicated separately in order to stress that these three deities in particular must surely come.

मित्रः अर्यमा, वरुणः (*mitraḥ aryamā, varuṇaḥ*) — although these three deities are conceived as separate deities,

it appears that here they are described as partial deities (*aṃśa-devatā*) of these names among the many forms of the Sun, that is, among the twelve Ādityas. Besides this, in some places these three deities are said to be other forms of Agni.

> त्वमग्ने वरुणो जायसे यत्त्वं मित्रो भवसि यत्समिद्धः ।

> *tvamagne varuṇo jāyase yattvaṃ mitro bhavasi yatsamiddhaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-3-1)

> त्वमर्यमा भवसि यत्कनीनां नाम स्वधावन् गुह्यं बिभर्षि ।

> *tvamaryamā bhavasi yatkanīnāṃ nāma svadhāvan guhyaṃ bibharṣi |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-3-2) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "You, Agni, are born as Varuṇa; you become Mitra when you are kindled. … You become Aryaman when, O self-powered one, you bear the secret name of maidens.")

In these ṛks it is said that Agni has these three names: when Agni is born he is Varuṇa; when, well kindled, he is blazing brightly, that Agni is Mitra; and in the homas and other rites connected with maidens Agni is Aryaman. Besides this, in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa —

> मित्रोऽसि वरुणोऽसीत्याह । मैत्रं वा अहः । वारुणी रात्रिः । अहोरात्राभ्यामेवैनमुपावहरति ॥

> *mitro 'si varuṇo 'sītyāha | maitraṃ vā ahaḥ | vāruṇī rātriḥ | ahorātrābhyāmevainamupāvaharati ‖*

(Tai. Brā. 1-7-10-1)

— it is said that Mitra is the lord of the day and Varuṇa the lord of the night. Therefore it should be noted that these three deities are in some places said to be partial deities of the Sun, and in some places different names of Agni.

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-3-1, 5-3-2 and Tai. Brā. 1-7-10-1 read on a zoom; the first reference is printed with a doubled opening parenthesis.)*

### Printed p. 120  (PDF 138)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Special Topics of Ṛk 2, continued.)*

In the Purāṇas and similar works Mitra is one of the twelve Ādityas. In the Ṛgveda, although Mitra is another name of the Sun, Mitra has a clear distinctiveness, that is, an individual prominence. In the Ṛgveda Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman are said to be the sons of Aditi; therefore they are called Ādityas in many places. That these Ādityas, that is, the sons of Aditi, are six in number —

> इमा गिर आदित्येभ्यो घृतस्नूः सनाद्राजभ्यो जुह्वा जुहोमि ।
> शृणोतु मित्रो अर्यमा भगो नस्तुविजातो वरुणो दक्षो अंशः ॥

> *imā gira ādityebhyo ghṛtasnūḥ sanādrājabhyo juhvā juhomi |*
> *śṛṇotu mitro aryamā bhago nastuvijāto varuṇo dakṣo aṃśaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-27-1) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "These songs dripping with ghee I offer with the ladle to the Ādityas, kings from of old; may Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga hear us, the mighty-born Varuṇa, Dakṣa, Aṃśa.")

— that is, the names of only six are given: Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Dakṣa, Aṃśa.

> देवा आदित्या ये सप्त तेभिः सोमाभि रक्ष न इन्द्रायेन्दो परि स्रव ।

> *devā ādityā ye sapta tebhiḥ somābhi rakṣa na indrāyendo pari srava |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-114-3) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The gods, the Ādityas, who are seven — with them, O Soma, guard us; flow round for Indra, O drop.")

— in this ṛk the sons of Aditi are said to be seven.

*(तन्व१स्परि (*tanva1spari*) with the numeral and देवाँ (*devā~*) as printed.)*

> अष्टौ पुत्रासो अदितेर्ये जातास्तन्व१स्परि ।
> देवाँ उपप्रैत्सप्तभिः परा मार्तंडमास्यत् ।
> सप्तभिः पुत्रैरदितिरुप प्रैत्पूर्व्यं युगं ।
> प्रजायै मृत्यवे त्वत्पुनर्मार्तंडमाभरत् ॥

> *aṣṭau putrāso aditerye jātāstanva1spari |*
> *devā~ upapraitsaptabhiḥ parā mārtaṃḍamāsyat |*
> *saptabhiḥ putrairaditirupa praitpūrvyaṃ yugaṃ |*
> *prajāyai mṛtyave tvatpunarmārtaṃḍamābharat ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-72-8, 9) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Eight are the sons of Aditi who were born of her body; with seven she went to the gods, Mārtāṇḍa she cast away. With seven sons Aditi went to the former age; Mārtāṇḍa she brought back again for birth and death.")

— in these ṛks it is said that Aditi had at first seven, and afterwards Mārtāṇḍa, eight sons in all. Besides this, in the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka —

*(अग्ंशश्च (*agṃśaśca*) as printed; विवस्वाग्श्चेत्येते (*vivasvāgścetyete*) as printed, broken across the line after ग् (*g*).)*

> अष्टौ पुत्रासो अदितेः । ये जातास्तन्वः परि । देवाँ उपप्रैत्सप्तभिः । परामार्तंडमास्यत् । सप्तभिः पुत्रैरदितिः । उपप्रैत्पूर्व्यं युगं । प्रजायै मृत्यवे तत् । परामार्तंडमाभरदिति । ताननुक्रमिष्यामः । मित्रश्च वरुणश्च । धाता चार्यमा च । अग्ंशश्च भगश्च । इन्द्रश्च विवस्वाग्श्चेत्येते ।

> *aṣṭau putrāso aditeḥ | ye jātāstanvaḥ pari | devā~ upapraitsaptabhiḥ | parāmārtaṃḍamāsyat | saptabhiḥ putrairaditiḥ | upapraitpūrvyaṃ yugaṃ | prajāyai mṛtyave tat | parāmārtaṃḍamābharaditi | tānanukramiṣyāmaḥ | mitraśca varuṇaśca | dhātā cāryamā ca | agṃśaśca bhagaśca | indraśca vivasvāgścetyete |*

(Tai. Ā. 1-[?]3-3)

— the names of the eight sons Aditi had are also given: Mitra, Varuṇa, Dhātā, Aryaman, Aṃśa, Bhaga, Indra and Vivasvān are said to be those eight. This same matter, in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa —

> अदितिः पुत्रकामा । साध्येभ्यो देवेभ्यो ब्रह्मौदनमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्प्राश्नात् । सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्यै धाता चार्यमा चाजा-

> *aditiḥ putrakāmā | sādhyebhyo devebhyo brahmaudanamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatprāśnāt | sā reto 'dhatta | tasyai dhātā cāryamā cājā-*

*(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 121  (PDF 139)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 4". Special Topics of Ṛk 2, continued: the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa passage, continued from p. 120.)*

*(रेतोधत्त (*retodhatta*) (without avagraha) in the first clause and विवस्वाग्ंश्चाजायेतां (*vivasvāgṃścājāyetāṃ*) as printed.)*

> -येतां । सा द्वितीयमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्प्राश्नात् । सा रेतोधत्त । तस्यै मित्रश्च वरुणश्चाजायेतां । सा तृतीयमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्प्राश्नात् । सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्या अग्ंशश्च भगश्चाजायेतां । सा चतुर्थमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्प्राश्नात् । सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्या इंद्रश्च विवस्वाग्ंश्चाजायेतां

> *-yetāṃ | sā dvitīyamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatprāśnāt | sā retodhatta | tasyai mitraśca varuṇaścājāyetāṃ | sā tṛtīyamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatprāśnāt | sā reto 'dhatta | tasyā agṃśaśca bhagaścājāyetāṃ | sā caturthamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatprāśnāt | sā reto 'dhatta | tasyā iṃdraśca vivasvāgṃścājāyetāṃ*

(Tai. Brā. 1-1-9-1, 2, 3)

— it is stated. The matter of Aditi obtaining eight sons is clearly explained here. Of these eight, only the three, Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman, are especially famous in the Ṛgveda. In the 27th sūkta of Ṛ. Saṃ. 2 (2-27) there is an extensive description of the world-benefiting heroic deeds of Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman.

मित्रः (*mitraḥ*) — Yāska has given the derivation (निर्वचन (*nirvacana*)) of the word मित्र (*mitra*) in his Nirukta thus:

> मित्रः प्रमीतेस्त्रायते । संमिन्वानो द्रवतीति वा । मेदयतेर्वा ।

> *mitraḥ pramītestrāyate | saṃminvāno dravatīti vā | medayatervā |*

(Ni. 10-21)

What is the meaning of the word मित्र (*mitra*)? —

> मित्रः कस्मात् । स हि प्रमीतेः त्रायते । प्रमीतिः मरणम् । ततः सर्वलोकं त्रायते वर्षद्वारेण ।

> *mitraḥ kasmāt | sa hi pramīteḥ trāyate | pramītiḥ maraṇam | tataḥ sarvalokaṃ trāyate varṣadvāreṇa |*

प्रमीति (*pramīti*) means death. Because, causing rain for the people in the world and thereby supplying food and other sustenance, he protects them by averting the fear of death that may arise from hunger, this deity has the name Mitra.

> समन्ततो मिन्वानः उदकेन द्रवति अन्तरिक्षलोके ।

> *samantato minvānaḥ udakena dravati antarikṣaloke |*

Because this deity, being lord of the waters and staying in the mid-region (the Kannada word for "in the mid-region" is printed without the syllable ರಿ [sic]), makes the whole region all round drenched, that is, wet with water, by means of the clouds, this deity has the name Mitra.

> अथवा — स्नेहनार्थस्य सर्वं ह्यसावुदकेन स्नेहयति ।

> *athavā — snehanārthasya sarvaṃ hyasāvudakena snehayati |*

Because this deity with water makes everything cohere, that is, join together into one, this deity has the name Mitra — thus he states a threefold derivation, and to support it —

> मित्रो जनान् यातयति ब्रुवाणो मित्रो दाधार पृथिवीमुत द्याम् ।
> मित्रः कृष्टीरनिमिषाभि चष्टे मित्राय हव्यं घृतवज्जुहोत ॥

> *mitro janān yātayati bruvāṇo mitro dādhāra pṛthivīmuta dyām |*
> *mitraḥ kṛṣṭīranimiṣābhi caṣṭe mitrāya havyaṃ ghṛtavajjuhota ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59-1) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Mitra, speaking, stirs people to action; Mitra upholds the earth and the heaven; Mitra watches the peoples with unwinking eye; to Mitra offer the oblation rich in ghee.")

— he has given this ṛk as an example. In this ṛk (it is said that) Mitra, as a helper in agriculture and other works, pouring down rain and the like and supplying food and other sustenance to the people, upholds, that is, nourishes, both the people of the earth and the dwellers in heaven. "O men, *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 122  (PDF 140)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Special Topics of Ṛk 2, continued from p. 121.)*

offer oblations mixed with ghee to such a deity Mitra" — thus it describes very well Mitra's extraordinary qualities and his benefit to the world. In the Ṛgveda the sūkta devoted to Mitra is only this sūkta of 9 ṛks (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59); elsewhere Mitra is praised together with Varuṇa and the other deities.

Because the association of Mitra and Varuṇa is very great, the sūkta having Mitra alone as its deity is, as said before, only one in the Ṛgveda (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59); there too the part praising that deity is not clear. But only in the first ṛk is Mitra's distinctiveness well stated. In the fifth ṛk of the same sūkta —

> महाँ आदित्यो नमसोपसद्यो यातयज्जनो गृणते सुशेवः ।

> *mahā~ ādityo namasopasadyo yātayajjano gṛṇate suśevaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59-5, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The great Āditya, to be approached with homage, who sets people in order, most kind to the praiser.")

— this Mitra is called the great Āditya who brings all men together. The word यातयज्जन (*yātayajjana*), which gives this meaning, is used —

> व्रतेन स्थो ध्रुवक्षेमा धर्मणा यातयज्जना ।

> *vratena stho dhruvakṣemā dharmaṇā yātayajjanā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-72-2, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "By your vow you two are of firm abode, by ordinance setting people in order.")

— in this ṛk with reference to both Mitra and Varuṇa, and

> मित्रस्तयोर्वरुणो यातयज्जनोऽर्यमा यातयज्जनः ।

> *mitrastayorvaruṇo yātayajjano 'ryamā yātayajjanaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-136-3, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman — each of them sets people in order.")

— in this ṛk with reference to all three, Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman. According to the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59 mentioned above, Mitra is the support of heaven and earth; the five classes of men (पञ्चजनाः (*pañcajanāḥ*)) are subject to him; he is the support of life for all the other deities — such is the description of Mitra's qualities. That Savitṛ and Mitra are one, in Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-81-4; that Viṣṇu took his three steps following the ordinances of Mitra, in the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā (Vā. Saṃ. 4-3, as printed); that Agni, established before dawn, himself produces Mitra for himself, in Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-8-4; that the kindled Agni is Mitra, in Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-5-4; that Agni when born is Varuṇa and when kindled is Mitra, in Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-3-1 (these references zoomed);

> मित्रो अग्निर्भवति यत्समिद्धो मित्रो होता वरुणो जातवेदाः ।
> मित्रो अध्वर्युरिषिरो दमूना मित्रः सिन्धूनामुत पर्वतानाम् ॥

> *mitro agnirbhavati yatsamiddho mitro hotā varuṇo jātavedāḥ |*
> *mitro adhvaryuriṣiro damūnā mitraḥ sindhūnāmuta parvatānām ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-5-4; the closing double daṇḍa is printed broken) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Agni becomes Mitra when he is kindled; Mitra is the Hotṛ, Varuṇa is Jātavedas; Mitra is the vigorous Adhvaryu, the house-friend; Mitra of the rivers and of the mountains.")

— here there is the description of Mitra's qualities: that the well-blazing Agni is Mitra; that this Mitra himself is, in the sacrifice, the Hotṛ, the Adhvaryu, Varuṇa, and the Agni called Jātavedas; and that he is Mitra (friend, benefactor) to the rivers and to the mountains.

### Printed p. 123  (PDF 141)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 4". Special Topics of Ṛk 2, continued.)*

वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*) — वरुणो वृणोतीति सतः (*varuṇo vṛṇotīti sataḥ*) (Ni. 10-2, as printed, zoomed): Yāska's derivation is that this deity has the name Varuṇa because it is covered by the mass of clouds.

Varuṇa is a most excellent deity, equal to Indra in power and the like. The number of mantras having Varuṇa as deity is very small. The sūktas having Varuṇa as deity are twelve in the Ṛgveda. But the sūktas praising Mitra and Varuṇa together are twenty-four.

Varuṇa has a human body and human activities. But more than his physical body and activities, it is the description of his moral activities and deeds that is chiefly indicated. He has a face, eyes, arms, hands and feet; he drives a chariot, sits, eats, drinks — such is the account of his bodily activities. That the Sun is the eye of Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa is clearly stated in the ṛks

> चित्रं देवानामुदगादनीकं चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्याग्नेः ।

> *citraṃ devānāmudagādanīkaṃ cakṣurmitrasya varuṇasyāgneḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-115-1) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The bright face of the gods has risen, the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, Agni.")

> उदु त्यच्चक्षुर्महि मित्रयोराँ एति प्रियं वरुणयोरदब्धम् ।

> *udu tyaccakṣurmahi mitrayorā~ eti priyaṃ varuṇayoradabdham |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-51-1, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Up comes that great eye of Mitra and Varuṇa, dear, undeceivable.")

> उद्वां चक्षुर्वरुण सुप्रतीकं देवयोरेति सूर्यस्ततन्वान् ।

> *udvāṃ cakṣurvaruṇa supratīkaṃ devayoreti sūryastatanvān |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-61-1, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Up rises, O Varuṇa, the fair-faced eye of you two gods, the Sun, spreading out.")

> चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्य देवश्चर्मेव यः समविव्यक् तमांसि ।

> *cakṣurmitrasya varuṇasya devaścarmeva yaḥ samavivyak tamāṃsi |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-63-1, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The god, eye of Mitra and Varuṇa, who has rolled up the darkness like a hide.")

> नमो मित्रस्य वरुणस्य चक्षसे महो देवाय तदृतं सपर्यत ।

> *namo mitrasya varuṇasya cakṣase maho devāya tadṛtaṃ saparyata |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-37-1) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Homage to the eye of Mitra and Varuṇa; to the great god offer this truth in worship.")

Since this matter, that the Sun is like an eye to him, stands in the very first ṛk of the sūktas having Mitra and Varuṇa as deities, it appears that this is the aspect which first comes to mind whenever Mitra and Varuṇa are mentioned. Further, in the ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-66-10 Aryaman, Mitra and Varuṇa are said to be sun-eyed. That Varuṇa is far-sighted (उरुचक्षसम् (*urucakṣasam*)) is said in ṛks such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-25-5; 1-25-16 (zoomed).

*(बर्ही (*barhī*) as printed.)*

> आ नो बर्ही रिशादसो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा । सीदन्तु मनुषो यथा ॥

> *ā no barhī riśādaso varuṇo mitro aryamā | sīdantu manuṣo yathā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-26-4, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "On our sacred grass may Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, destroyers of foes, sit, as at Manu's.")

> व्रतेन स्थो ध्रुवक्षेमा धर्मणा यातयज्जना । नि बर्हिषि सदतं सोमपीतये ॥

> *vratena stho dhruvakṣemā dharmaṇā yātayajjanā | ni barhiṣi sadataṃ somapītaye ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-72-2, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "By your vow you are of firm abode, by ordinance setting people in order; sit down on the sacred grass to drink the Soma.")

### Printed p. 124  (PDF 142)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Special Topics of Ṛk 2, continued.)*

— in such ṛks it is prayed that Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman come and sit, for the drinking of Soma, on the darbha grass spread on the sacrificial altar.

*(सोमैः (*somaiḥ*) and मादयैते (*mādayaite*) as printed.)*

> यदी सखाया सख्याय सोमैः सुतेभिः सुप्रयसा मादयैते ।

> *yadī sakhāyā sakhyāya somaiḥ sutebhiḥ suprayasā mādayaite |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-41-3) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "When the two friends gladden themselves, for friendship, with pressed Soma, with good offerings.")

In such ṛks it is said that Varuṇa drinks Soma together with Indra and the other deities.

> बिभ्रद्द्रापिं हिरण्ययं वरुणो वस्त निर्णिजम् । परि स्पशो नि षेदिरे ।

> *bibhraddrāpiṃ hiraṇyayaṃ varuṇo vasta nirṇijam | pari spaśo ni ṣedire |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-25-13, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Wearing a golden mantle Varuṇa has clothed himself in a shining robe; his spies have sat down around.")

— in this ṛk there is the description that Varuṇa wears a golden upper covering or cloak and a shining garment. Varuṇa's chariot is golden and radiant like the Sun, and in it there are whips for urging on the horses. Mitra and Varuṇa mount their chariot in a very high region (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-63-1, zoomed) — such descriptions exist.

The dwelling of Mitra and Varuṇa is golden, and it is in the upper world. And Varuṇa, sitting in his palace —

> नि षसाद धृतव्रतो वरुणः पस्त्यास्वा । साम्राज्याय सुक्रतुः ।
> अतो विश्वान्यद्भुता चिकित्वाँ अभि पश्यति । कृतानि या च कर्त्वा ॥

> *ni ṣasāda dhṛtavrato varuṇaḥ pastyāsvā | sāmrājyāya sukratuḥ |*
> *ato viśvānyadbhutā cikitvā~ abhi paśyati | kṛtāni yā ca kartvā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-25-10, 11) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Varuṇa, upholder of ordinances, has sat down in the dwellings, the wise one, for sovereignty. From there the knowing one looks upon all wonders, the things done and those to be done.")

— sees all that happens in the world. The dwelling-place of Mitra and Varuṇa is very large and very high, made firm resting on a thousand pillars; and their house has a thousand doors (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-88-5, zoomed). The all-seeing Sun, setting out from his dwelling-place, goes to the house of Mitra and Varuṇa to report the deeds of men, and enters their beloved house — such descriptions too exist.

Varuṇa, alone or together with Mitra, is like the other deities called king in many places —

> अबुध्ने राजा वरुणो वनस्योर्ध्वं स्तूपं ददते पूतदक्षः ।

> *abudhne rājā varuṇo vanasyordhvaṃ stūpaṃ dadate pūtadakṣaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-7, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "In the bottomless region King Varuṇa of purified will holds up the crest of the tree.")

> त्वं विश्वेषां वरुणासि राजा ये च देवा असुर ये च मर्ताः ।

> *tvaṃ viśveṣāṃ varuṇāsi rājā ye ca devā asura ye ca martāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-27-10, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "You, Varuṇa, are king of all, O Asura, those who are gods and those who are mortals.")

> तेन विश्वस्य भुवनस्य राजा यवं न वृष्टिर्व्युनत्ति भूम ।

> *tena viśvasya bhuvanasya rājā yavaṃ na vṛṣṭirvyunatti bhūma |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-85-3) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Thereby the king of the whole world moistens the earth as rain the barley.")

### Printed p. 125  (PDF 143)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 4". Special Topics of Ṛk 2, continued.)*

In such ṛks it is said that Varuṇa is king not only of men but also of the deities and of all the worlds. Besides Varuṇa, the deities Indra, Yama, Soma and others also have the name "king", which indicates honour.

The stories connected with Indra are many. But with regard to Varuṇa it is quite the opposite: there are no stories at all. Varuṇa is greatly praised as the controller of the physical and moral laws (वरुणस्य व्रतानि (*varuṇasya vratāni*)). The divine power of Mitra and Varuṇa is described by the word माया (*māyā*). When this applies to deities it means the hidden power they have to do good; in a context where it applies to Rākṣasas, the same word means the hidden power they have to do evil. In the good sense this word is fitting for Mitra and Varuṇa; in the bad sense it applies to the Rākṣasas. Like the meaning of the word *asura*, the word *māyā* too is used in both senses. By this māyā-power hidden in himself Varuṇa, standing in the atmosphere, measures the earth with the Sun as one measures with a measuring rod. He makes the Sun cross the mid-region and makes him hidden by rain-clouds. Then drops mixed with honey (sweet) fall (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-63-4, zoomed). He makes the sky rain. Therefore this word माया (*māyā*)

*(The first reference below is broken in print.)*

is said, in ṛks such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-48-[?]4; 7-28-4; 10-99-10; 10-147-5 (zoomed), chiefly of Varuṇa among the deities.

Varuṇa is the one who ordains the laws of nature. He himself established the earth and heaven. And

*(संराड्विश्वेत्तानि (*saṃrāḍviśvettāni*) as printed.)*

> आसीदद्विश्वा भुवनानि संराड्विश्वेत्तानि वरुणस्य व्रतानि ।

> *āsīdadviśvā bhuvanāni saṃrāḍviśvettāni varuṇasya vratāni |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-42-1, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The sovereign has sat down over all the worlds; all these are Varuṇa's ordinances.")

— in this ṛk (it is said) that Varuṇa dwells in all the worlds and that his laws and the like are observed everywhere; and

> तिस्रो द्यावो निहिता अंतरस्मिन् तिस्रो भूमीरुपराः षड्विधानाः ।

> *tisro dyāvo nihitā aṃtarasmin tisro bhūmīruparāḥ ṣaḍvidhānāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-87-5, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Three heavens are placed within him, three earths below, in sixfold order.")

— here it is said that the three upper worlds and the three earth-worlds (the lower worlds) are under his control. Varuṇa and Mitra rule the whole world (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-63-2, zoomed). They are the protectors of the whole world (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-27-4, zoomed). Varuṇa is the support of heaven, earth and sky (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-69-1, 4, as printed, zoomed). He has placed Agni in the waters, the Sun in the sky, and Soma upon the rock. He has made a broad path for the Sun. Varuṇa, Mitra and *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 126  (PDF 144)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Special Topics of Ṛk 2, continued.)*

Aryaman clear the path for the Sun (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-60-4, zoomed). In many such ṛks there is the description of Varuṇa's authority.

In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-8-3, zoomed) मित्रोऽहरजनयद्वरुणो रात्रिं (*mitro 'harajanayadvaruṇo rātriṃ*) — that is, it is said that Mitra created the day and Varuṇa the night. Therefore मैत्रं वा अहः । वारुणी रात्रिः (*maitraṃ vā ahaḥ | vāruṇī rātriḥ*) — that is, it is said in many places that Mitra is the lord of the day and Varuṇa the lord of the night (Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-7-4). In one place it is said that Varuṇa divided the seasons:

> वेद मासो धृतव्रतो द्वादश प्रजावतः । वेदा य उपजायते ।

> *veda māso dhṛtavrato dvādaśa prajāvataḥ | vedā ya upajāyate |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-25-8) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "He who upholds the ordinances knows the twelve months with their offspring; he knows the one that is born in addition.")

— here (it is said) that Varuṇa knows the twelve months; and

*(चादृचं (*cādṛcaṃ*) as printed.)*

> वि ये दधुः शरदं मासमादहर्यज्ञमक्तुं चादृचं ।
> अनाप्यं वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा क्षत्रं राजान आशत ॥

> *vi ye dadhuḥ śaradaṃ māsamādaharyajñamaktuṃ cādṛcaṃ |*
> *anāpyaṃ varuṇo mitro aryamā kṣatraṃ rājāna āśata ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-66-11, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "They who apportioned the autumn, the month, the day, the sacrifice, the night and the ṛk — Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, the kings, have attained unattainable dominion.")

— in this ṛk it is said that Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman divided the year, the months, the day and the nights.

It is said in many places that he too is the one who regulates the waters. He it is who made the rivers flow; by his command they flow continually (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-28-4, zoomed). Though the rivers swiftly bring water and pour it into the ocean, that it does not fill up is by his hidden power alone (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-85-6, zoomed). Varuṇa and Mitra are the lords of the rivers. Although that Varuṇa is lord of the oceans is an established point, its occurrence in the Ṛgveda is very rare; probably the reason for this may be that it is not prominent. In the Purāṇas and the like Varuṇa is famous as the lord of waters. And that Varuṇa, as one of the eight guardians of the quarters, is the lord of the western quarter is a matter stated in the Purāṇas and the like; in the Ṛgveda there is no support at all for it. In general, all that is connected with Varuṇa is with the water in the atmosphere; among the deities prayed to for rain, Varuṇa and Mitra are the chief. That, when the mountains are all covered by clouds, Varuṇa pours water on heaven, earth and sky from an upturned vat (the cloud) and makes the whole earth wet, is said in the ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-85-3, 4. One whole sūkta (that is, the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-63) indicates their power of making rain fall (zoomed). In the Yajurveda Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 5-5-4-1, zoomed) आपो वरुणस्य पत्नय आसन् (*āpo varuṇasya patnaya āsan*) — that the waters were the wives of Varuṇa — and (Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-3-2, zoomed) मित्रावरुणौ वा अपां नेतारौ (*mitrāvaruṇau vā apāṃ netārau*) — that Mitra and Varuṇa are the leaders of the waters — are also said.

### Printed p. 127  (PDF 145)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 4". Special Topics of Ṛk 2, continued.)*

It is said again and again that Varuṇa's ordinances are firmly established. For this very reason he has the name धृतव्रत (*dhṛtavrata*) (upholder of ordinances). This epithet belongs to both Mitra and Varuṇa.

> परि धामानि मर्मृशद्वरुणस्य पुरो गये विश्वे देवा अनु व्रतं नभंतामन्यके समे ॥

> *pari dhāmāni marmṛśadvaruṇasya puro gaye viśve devā anu vrataṃ nabhaṃtāmanyake same ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-41-2, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Touching all the abodes of Varuṇa before his house, all the gods follow his ordinance; let all the others perish.")

> न वां देवा अमृता आ मिनंति व्रतानि मित्रावरुणा ध्रुवाणि ।

> *na vāṃ devā amṛtā ā minaṃti vratāni mitrāvaruṇā dhruvāṇi |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-69-4, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The immortal gods do not infringe your firm ordinances, O Mitra and Varuṇa.")

In such ṛks it is said that the deities themselves keep the commands of Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman, and that even the beginningless deities cannot transgress their fixed ordinances. Mitra and Varuṇa are the controllers of law (ऋत (*ṛta*)) and of light. It is by the strength of these ordinances that they are able to give support to the laws. This quality is found especially in these two, sometimes in the Ādityas, or in other ordinary deities as well. The epithet that they are the ones who make truth (ऋत (*ṛta*)) and justice prosper (ऋतस्य गोपाः (*ṛtasya gopāḥ*)), that is, who keep the laws (or who cause them to be kept), is seen to be used many times of Mitra and Varuṇa.

Varuṇa's power is unfathomable. Neither the flying birds nor the flowing rivers can reach the limit of the boundary of his kingdom. They cannot exceed his power; they cannot withstand his anger. Neither the sky nor the rivers have reached where the boundary of Mitra and Varuṇa ends. Everything is contained in Varuṇa alone. The dwellings of all beings, the three heavenly worlds and the three earthly worlds, are placed in him. Varuṇa is all-knowing. The flight of birds in the sky, the movement of ships on the ocean, the course of the far-going wind — all these are known to him. He sees all things, those gone by in the past and those to come in the future. He is the witness of the true and false deeds of men. The works, plans and devices that every man makes are all known to Varuṇa. He can grasp all that is in the heavenly and earthly worlds and beyond them. However far one runs away beyond the sky, no one can escape the path of Varuṇa's sight.

Because he is the controller of moral law, Varuṇa becomes very angry at sin. Whether one transgresses his laws or (provokes his) anger, for both of these he ordains very cruel punishment. Varuṇa's noose (*pāśa*), which binds sinners, is mentioned in ṛks such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-15; 1-25-21; 6-74-4; 10-85-24 (zoomed). That noose binds the speaker of untruth; it lets go the speaker of truth.

*(The fifth word of this line is printed with displaced vowel signs and repha; undecided, zoomed.)*

> *yuvo rāṣṭraṃ bṛhadinvati dyā[?]yau[?] setṛbhirarajjubhiḥ sinīthaḥ |*

### Printed p. 128  (PDF 146)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Special Topics of Ṛk 2, continued: the second line of the quoted ṛk and its reference.)*

> परि नो हेळो वरुणस्य वृज्या उरुं न इंद्रः कृणवदु लोकं ॥

> *pari no heḷo varuṇasya vṛjyā uruṃ na iṃdraḥ kṛṇavadu lokaṃ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-84-2, zoomed) (Gloss of the whole ṛk, mine and tentative: "Your kingdom, great, quickens; you bind with fetters that are no ropes. May Varuṇa's anger pass us by; may Indra make wide room for us.")

— in this ṛk it is said that Varuṇa, the companion of Indra, binds with bonds that are not ropes. The word पाश (*pāśa*) (noose) occurs in the whole Ṛgveda in only one place in a mantra whose deity is Agni, and that too in a context of praying "release the noose that binds his devotees". Therefore it may be said that these acts of binding with the noose and of releasing (loosening the noose) belong to Varuṇa alone. Varuṇa, joined with Mitra, drives away untruth, hates it and punishes it. Mitra and Varuṇa punish those who are negligent about their worship; but Varuṇa forgives those who repent. He loosens (sin) as one loosens a rope, and takes away sin; not only from sin committed by oneself — he also frees a man from sin committed by his forefathers. Even those who transgress daily the rules ordained by him and afterwards repent, he spares. And he shows compassion to those who transgressed his commands through forgetfulness. In Varuṇa there are medicines by hundreds and by thousands. He keeps death far away, and takes away sin. He can take away life, and he can also give life. He is most skilled among those who protect permanence (नित्यत्व (*nityatva*)). Thus the description of Varuṇa's qualities is found in many ṛks. Here we have explained it very briefly; in a fitting context we shall explain it at length.

In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā — फल्गुनीनक्षत्रमर्यमा देवता (*phalgunīnakṣatramaryamā devatā*) .... .... .... .... अनूराधा नक्षत्रं मित्रो देवता (*anūrādhā nakṣatraṃ mitro devatā*) .... .... .... .... (Tai. Saṃ. 4-4-9-2, as printed, zoomed) — that is, it is said that Aryaman is the lord of the Pūrva-phalgunī nakṣatra and Mitra of the Anūrādhā nakṣatra.

**Aryamā.** — In the sūktas concerning the Ādityas, generally by "the Ādityas" Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman alone are meant. As we have said before, in the Ṛgveda (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-27-1, zoomed) there are only the names of six persons: Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Dakṣa and Aṃśa. In the 3rd ṛk of Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-114 (zoomed) the number of the Ādityas is seven; and in Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-72-8 (zoomed) it is (said) that Aditi first handed over seven sons to the deities and afterwards obtained the eighth, Mārtaṇḍa. In A. Ve. 8-9-21 and in Tai. Brā. 1-1-9-1 (zoomed) it is said that Aditi has eight sons: Mitra, Aryaman, Varuṇa, Aṃśa, Bhaga, Dhātṛ, Indra and Vivasvān. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (Śa. Brā. 6-1-2-8; 11-6-3-8, zoomed) it is said that the Ādityas are twelve, one for each month. In the Purāṇas and the like, too, the Ādityas are twelve.

Although the name of the deity Aryaman occurs about a hundred times in the Ṛgveda, because he has no complete individuality Yāska in his Nirukta (in the Nighaṇṭu), when explaining the derivation of the forms of the deities' names, has left out the name of this deity Aryaman. Except in two mantras *(continues on the next page)*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-126-1, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "No distress, no misfortune reaches that mortal, O gods, whom Aryaman, Mitra and Varuṇa, of one accord, lead beyond the haters.")

> *śunamasmabhyamūtaye varuṇo mitro aryamā |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-126-7, as printed, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "For our welfare and help may Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman, the Ādityas, grant the wide shelter that we ask, beyond the haters.")

Although in the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-126 (zoomed) the deities are said to be the Viśvedevas, from the ṛks quoted above it is chiefly the Ādityas alone who are praised here. Moreover, what is said in the first ṛk as देवासः अष्ट (*devāsaḥ aṣṭa*) refers to the eight Ādityas (in the Veda the number of the Ādityas is nowhere given as more than eight). Moreover, in the 7th ṛk (zoomed) the word आदित्यासः (*ādityāsaḥ*) also shows this very thing clearly. In every ṛk of this sūkta (except the last ṛk) the names of Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman — वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा (*varuṇo mitro aryamā*) — fall again and again like a refrain (*pallavi*); this indicates that among the Ādityas these three, Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman, have obtained the chief place. Since the subject of Aryaman is not explained much in the Ṛgveda, a special explanation (of him) is not possible.

Sū. 3-1-86, read unzoomed); no guṇa as it is ṅit; उवङ् (*uvaṅ*) by अचि श्नुधातुभ्रुवां (*aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ*) and आगमशास्त्रमनित्यम् (*āgamaśāstramanityam*) (Pari. 93-2, as read, not zoomed) … *(continues on the next page)*

… the यासुट् (*yāsuṭ*) augment does not come; being at the beginning of the pāda it does not take the nighāta accent; by the root accent it is ādyudātta. वृधासः (*vṛdhāsaḥ*) — root वृधु वृद्धौ (*vṛdhu vṛddhau*); suffix क (*ka*) by इगुपधज्ञाप्रीकिरः कः (*igupadhajñāprīkiraḥ kaḥ*); no laghūpadha guṇa as it is kit; antodātta by the suffix accent; before जस् (*jas*), the augment असुक् (*asuk*) by आज्जसेरसुक् (*ājjaserasuk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-50). करन् (*karan*) — root डुकृञ् करणे (*ḍukṛñ karaṇe*); luṅ in the sense of liṅ by छंदसि लुङ्लङ्लिटः (*chaṃdasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ*); अङ् (*aṅ*) for cli by कृमृदृरुहिभ्यः (*kṛmṛdṛruhibhyaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-75); root accent kept (pāda-initial). सुसाहा (*susāhā*) (headword so printed) — root षह मर्षणे (*ṣaha marṣaṇe*), क्विप् (*kvip*); prādi-compound with the accent of the kṛt final member; instrumental singular; lengthening in the Saṃhitā is chāndasa. विथुरम् (*vithuram*) — root व्यथ भयसंचलनयोः (*vyatha bhayasaṃcalanayoḥ*); suffix उरच् (*urac*) by व्यथेः संप्रसारणं किच्च (*vyatheḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ kicca*) (Uṇ. Sū. 1-39); samprasāraṇa i of y (the bar न संप्रसारणे संप्रसारणम् (*na saṃprasāraṇe saṃprasāraṇam*) being noted), pūrvarūpa; antodātta by चितः (*citaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163).

## Sūkta 186, Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> प्रेष्ठं वो अतिथिं गृणीषेऽग्निं शस्तिभिस्तुर्वणिः सजोषाः ।
> असद्यथा नो वरुणः सुकीर्तिरिषश्च पर्षदरिगूर्तः सूरिः ॥ ३ ॥

> *preṣṭhaṃ vo atithiṃ gṛṇīṣe 'gniṃ śastibhisturvaṇiḥ sajoṣāḥ |*
> *asadyathā no varuṇaḥ sukīrtiriṣaśca parṣadarigūrtaḥ sūriḥ ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> प्रेष्ठं । वः । अतिथिं । गृणीषे । अग्निं । शस्तिऽभिः । तुर्वणिः । सऽजोषाः ।
> असत् । यथा । नः । वरुणः । सुऽकीर्तिः । इषः । च । पर्षत् । अरिऽगूर्तः । सूरिः ॥ ३ ॥

> *preṣṭhaṃ | vaḥ | atithiṃ | gṛṇīṣe | agniṃ | śasti 'bhiḥ | turvaṇiḥ | sa 'joṣāḥ |*
> *asat | yathā | naḥ | varuṇaḥ | su 'kīrtiḥ | iṣaḥ | ca | parṣat | ari 'gūrtaḥ | sūriḥ ‖ 3 ‖*

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 4". Ṛk 3, continued.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed)*

*Gist:* O gods, I, eager and of one accord with you, praise with hymns Agni, your dearest guest (or: Agni, eager and pleased with you), so that Varuṇa, of fair fame, slayer of foes, the impeller, may fill us with food; him too we praise.

> हे देवाः वो युष्माकं प्रेष्ठं प्रियतमं । सर्वेषामाह्वातृत्वाद्धविर्वहनाच्चाग्निर्देवानां प्रियतमः । तमतिथिं गृणीषे । गृणे । स्तौमि ॥ व्यत्ययेन मध्यमः ॥ केन साधनेन । शस्तिभिः शंसनैः स्तुतिभिः । कीदृशोऽहं । तुर्वणिस्तूर्णवनिः शीघ्रं संभक्ता सजोषा युष्माभिः सह प्रीयमाणः । यद्वा । एते अग्निविशेषणे । यस्तुर्वणिः शीघ्रं यज्ञस्य संभक्ता सजोषा युष्माभिः सह प्रीयमाणः तमग्निं गृणीषे । यथा येन प्रकारेण नोऽस्माकं वरुण एतन्नामको देवः सुकीर्तिः शोभनकीर्तिमानसत् । सुकीर्तिं भिक्षे वरुणस्य भूरेः । ऋ. २-२८-१ । इत्यादिमंत्रवर्णेषु वरणात्सुकीर्तिरेवैषणीया । अरिगूर्तोऽरिष्वदात्रेषु सदा शब्दितः अरीणां हनना- योद्युक्तो वा सूरिः प्रेरयिताऽयं वरुण इषश्चान्नानि पर्षत् । पूरयेत् । तथा तमपि स्तुम इत्यर्थः ॥

> *he devāḥ vo yuṣmākaṃ preṣṭhaṃ priyatamaṃ | sarveṣāmāhvātṛtvāddhavirvahanāccāgnirdevānāṃ priyatamaḥ | tamatithiṃ gṛṇīṣe | gṛṇe | staumi ‖ vyatyayena madhyamaḥ ‖ kena sādhanena | śastibhiḥ śaṃsanaiḥ stutibhiḥ | kīdṛśo 'haṃ | turvaṇistūrṇavaniḥ śīghraṃ saṃbhaktā sajoṣā yuṣmābhiḥ saha prīyamāṇaḥ | yadvā | ete agniviśeṣaṇe | yasturvaṇiḥ śīghraṃ yajñasya saṃbhaktā sajoṣā yuṣmābhiḥ saha prīyamāṇaḥ tamagniṃ gṛṇīṣe | yathā yena prakāreṇa no 'smākaṃ varuṇa etannāmako devaḥ sukīrtiḥ śobhanakīrtimānasat | sukīrtiṃ bhikṣe varuṇasya bhūreḥ | ṛ. 2-28-1 | ityādimaṃtravarṇeṣu varaṇātsukīrtirevaiṣaṇīyā | arigūrto 'riṣvadātreṣu sadā śabditaḥ arīṇāṃ hananā- yodyukto vā sūriḥ prerayitā 'yaṃ varuṇa iṣaścānnāni parṣat | pūrayet | tathā tamapi stuma ityarthaḥ ‖*

*(The reference ऋ. २-२८-१ (*ṛ. 2-28-1*) in the bhāṣya was zoomed; हनना- योद्युक्तो (*hananā- yodyukto*) is broken across a gap in the print.)*

**Pratipadārtha.** देवाः (*devāḥ*) — O deities; तुर्वणिः (*turvaṇiḥ*) — eager to perform sacrifice and satisfy the deities; सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*) — and an object of equal love for all the deities — I; [or: यः (*yaḥ*) — which Agni; तुर्वणिः (*turvaṇiḥ*) — eager to carry the oblation to the deities; सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*) — an object of equal love among the deities] is, such a one, and; वः (*vaḥ*) — to you; प्रेष्ठं (*preṣṭhaṃ*) — most dear; अतिथिं (*atithiṃ*) — who is like a guest; अग्निं (*agniṃ*) — Agni; शस्तिभिः (*śastibhiḥ*) — with hymns; गृणीषे (*gṛṇīṣe*) — I praise; यथा (*yathā*) — in which way; अरिगूर्तः (*arigūrtaḥ*) — who destroys the enemies, the non-givers; सूरिः (*sūriḥ*) — who impels men to (their) works; वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*) — Varuṇa; सुकीर्तिः (*sukīrtiḥ*) — as the maker of excellent fame; असत् (*asat*) — may become, (and); इषश्च (*iṣaśca*) — food also; पर्षत् (*parṣat*) — may become such as to fill (us) (in that way I praise Varuṇa too).

**Bhāvārtha.** O deities, I, who am eager to perform sacrifice and satisfy the deities and an object of equal love for all the deities, praise with hymns Agni, who is most dear to the deities and like a guest. And I praise also Varuṇa, the destroyer of the non-givers and the impeller of men to (their) works, so that he may become the maker of excellent fame for us and may fill us with food.

**English Translation (as printed):**

I praise with hymns, (O gods), your best beloved guest, Agni, who is prompt (to partake of the oblation), and who is well pleased along (with you); so that (thereby) Varuna, the possessor of renown, the subduer of foes, the animator (of men), may fill us with food.

### Printed p. 132  (PDF 150)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Ṛk 3, continued.)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).**

For this sūkta the Viśvedevas are said to be the deity. Therefore, having praised chiefly the deity Savitṛ in the first ṛk of this sūkta, and in the second ṛk the deities called Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman (the Ādityas), in this present third ṛk, that is, the ṛk प्रेष्ठं वो अतिथिं (*preṣṭhaṃ vo atithiṃ*), the ṛṣi praises Agni and Varuṇa.

प्रेष्ठं — प्रियतमं । सर्वेषामाह्वातृत्वाद्धविर्वहनाच्चाग्निर्देवानां प्रियतमः । (*preṣṭhaṃ — priyatamaṃ | sarveṣāmāhvātṛtvāddhavirvahanāccāgnirdevānāṃ priyatamaḥ |*) — the meaning is: Agni, who is the object of the utmost love. How Agni is dear to the deities: because, in the sacrifices and the like that men perform, Agni takes on the office of Hotṛ, invites the deities whom the sacrificers have in view and brings them to the sacrificial ground; and because he carries the oblations and the like which the sacrificers offer into the fire for the deities and makes them reach the deities — it is natural to say that Agni is dear to the deities.

In the sacrifices too there is a close kinship between Agni and the daily life of men. Agni delivers to the deities what is offered by men (what is offered into the fire). For that very reason he has the name हव्यवाट् (*havyavāṭ*). Without him no joy at all arises for the deities — this is said in the ṛk

> महाँ अस्यध्वरस्य प्रकेतो न ऋते त्वदमृता मादयंते ।

> *mahā~ asyadhvarasya praketo na ṛte tvadamṛtā mādayaṃte |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-11-1, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Great are you, the banner of the sacrifice; without you the immortals do not rejoice.") And in the matter of Agni's bringing the deities and delivering the oblation to them —

> अग्निं दूतं वृणीमहे होतारं विश्ववेदसं ।

> *agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe hotāraṃ viśvavedasaṃ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-12-1, zoomed) — in this ṛk Agni is prayed to as the messenger who brings the deities to the sacrificial ground and invites them. (Gloss, mine and tentative: "We choose Agni as messenger, the Hotṛ, the all-possessing.")

> अग्ने देवाँ इहावह जज्ञानो वृक्तबर्हिषे । असि होता न ईड्यः ।

> *agne devā~ ihāvaha jajñāno vṛktabarhiṣe | asi hotā na īḍyaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-12-2, as printed, zoomed) — in this ṛk Agni is prayed to: "O Agni, since you are the Hotṛ who brings the deities, come bringing the deities to this sacrificial ground." In Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-14-1 (zoomed), देवेभिर्याहि (*devebhiryāhi*) — it is prayed, "Come to this sacrifice of ours together with the deities." Agni goes on both the paths, the one that goes to the earth and the one that goes to the presence of the deities. For that very reason it has become customary to call him a messenger.

---

### Printed p. 133  (PDF 151)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 4". Special Topics of Ṛk 3, continued.)*

Since it is said that in sacrifices Agni bears the most important part in accomplishing the rites, the very place that is given among men to the purohitas has been given to Agni among the deities. Therefore he has epithets such as ऋत्विक् (*ṛtvik*), विप्र (*vipra*), पुरोहित (*purohita*), होता (*hotā*). More than all these, calling Agni होता (*hotā*) (the one who invokes the deities, or the accomplisher of the homa) is special. He is the most beloved and the best among the Hotṛs. The work of carrying the oblations is Agni's chief work. Therefore the ṛṣi has described Agni as the object of the utmost love to the deities.

अतिथिं (*atithiṃ*) — Since it is said that man obtains Agni by the gracious boon of the deities, and that Mātariśvan first saw Agni and brought him to the earth, it was as good as established that Agni belongs to the heavenly world. In this very sense Agni may be called the guest of men. Or, since a guest is at all times worthy of worship and of honour, Agni too, being likewise worthy of worship, may be praised with the epithet "guest".

तुर्वणिः (*turvaṇiḥ*) — तुर्वणिस्तूर्णवनिः (*turvaṇistūrṇavaniḥ*) — so Yāska has given the derivation of this word (Ni. 6-14, zoomed). For this word, formed from the root वन षण संभक्तौ (*vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau*), (it is said) तूर्णं हि यः संभजते स तूर्णवनिरित्युक्तः । (*tūrṇaṃ hi yaḥ saṃbhajate sa tūrṇavanirityuktaḥ |*) — the meaning is "one who comes quickly". In the present ṛk, तुर्वणिः सजोषाः (*turvaṇiḥ sajoṣāḥ*) means: Agni is praised as one who, being loved by the other deities, or in company with the other deities, comes quickly to this sacrificial ground of ours.

सजोषाः (*sajoṣāḥ*) — For this word the commentator has given two kinds of meaning. Having given one kind of meaning — सजोषा युष्माभिः सह प्रीयमाणः (*sajoṣā yuṣmābhiḥ saha prīyamāṇaḥ*), that is, "O deities, I praise (so that) Agni, the object of love, should come with you" — he has also explained the meaning in another way: यस्तुर्वणिः शीघ्रं यज्ञस्य संभक्ता सजोषा युष्माभिः सह प्रीयमाणस्तमग्निं गृणीषे (*yasturvaṇiḥ śīghraṃ yajñasya saṃbhaktā sajoṣā yuṣmābhiḥ saha prīyamāṇastamagniṃ gṛṇīṣe*) — "O deities, I praise that Agni whom you love, who comes quickly to the sacrificial ground."

वरुणः सुकीर्तिः (*varuṇaḥ sukīrtiḥ*) — "In the way in which Varuṇa, being of good fame, was prayed to bring about fame for us — in that way": such is Sāyaṇa's explanation. On this point he has quoted the ṛk

> अति यो मंद्रो यजथाय देवः सुकीर्तिं भिक्षे वरुणस्य भूरेः ।

> *ati yo maṃdro yajathāya devaḥ sukīrtiṃ bhikṣe varuṇasya bhūreḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-28-1, zoomed). In this ṛk it is clear that (the poet) praises Varuṇa, expecting fame from him in abundance. (Gloss, mine and tentative: "I beg the fair fame of the abundant Varuṇa, the god who is pleasing beyond (all) for worship.")

### Printed p. 134  (PDF 152)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Special Topics of Ṛk 3, concluded; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā begins.)*

अरिगूर्तः (*arigūrtaḥ*) — This word occurs in the Ṛgveda only in this ṛk; it is found nowhere else. For it Sāyaṇa has explained अरिगूर्तोऽरिष्वदात्रेषु सदा शब्दितः अरीणां हननायोद्युक्तो वा (*arigūrto 'riṣvadātreṣu sadā śabditaḥ arīṇāṃ hananāyodyukto vā*) — that is, "one who always makes a sound, that is, censures, in the matter of the misers who do not give gifts, who give nothing to anyone"; or else another meaning is also possible, "one who is ready to destroy the enemies".

सूरिः (*sūriḥ*) — The word सूरि (*sūri*) is read among the names of the praiser (स्तोतृ (*stotṛ*)) (Ni. 3-19, zoomed); the meaning is "one who should be praised" [*as printed: ಸ್ತೋತ್ರಮಾಡತಕ್ಕವನು*]. And Yāska, quoting the ṛk

> इहेह जाता समवावशीतामरेपसा तन्वा३ नामभिः स्वैः ।
> जिष्णुर्वामन्यः सुमखस्य सूरिर्दिवो अन्यः सुभगः पुत्र ऊहे ॥

> *iheha jātā samavāvaśītāmarepasā tanvā3 nāmabhiḥ svaiḥ |*
> *jiṣṇurvāmanyaḥ sumakhasya sūrirdivo anyaḥ subhagaḥ putra ūhe ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-181-4, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Born here and there, the two, spotless in body and in their own names, have called to each other; one of you is the victorious impeller of the well-sacrificing, the other is called the fortunate son of heaven.") — has explained the word सूरि (*sūri*) in it as ईरयिता (*īrayitā*), that is प्रेरयिता (*prerayitā*) ("impeller") (Ni. 12-3, zoomed). The commentator too has adopted this very meaning in the present ṛk and explained सूरिः (*sūriḥ*) as प्रेरयिता अयं वरुणः (*prerayitā ayaṃ varuṇaḥ*) — "this Varuṇa, who is the impeller".

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** (grammar page, noted briefly; numerals read unzoomed unless stated). प्रेष्ठम् (*preṣṭham*) — अतिशयेन प्रियः (*atiśayena priyaḥ*) (the next word is printed like श्रेष्ठः (*śreṣṭhaḥ*) [?] for प्रेष्ठः (*preṣṭhaḥ*)); इष्ठन् (*iṣṭhan*) by अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ (*atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau*); प्र (*pra*) for प्रिय (*priya*) by प्रियस्थिरस्फिर (*priyasthirasphira*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-157, zoomed); no ṭi-lopa by प्रकृत्यैकाच् (*prakṛtyaikāc*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-163); guṇa; ādyudātta as the suffix is nit. अतिथिम् (*atithim*) — root अत सातत्यगमने (*ata sātatyagamane*); suffix इथिन् (*ithin*) by ऋतन्यंजि (*ṛtanyaṃji*) (Uṇ. Sū. 4-48[?]2, zoomed, undecided); ādyudātta by ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ñnityādirnityam*). गृणीषे (*gṛṇīṣe*) — root गॄ शब्दे (*gṝ śabde*) (kryādi); madhyama ending for the uttama by व्यत्ययो बहुलम् (*vyatyayo bahulam*); vikaraṇa श्ना (*śnā*) by क्र्यादिभ्यः श्ना (*kryādibhyaḥ śnā*); shortening by प्वादीनां ह्रस्वः (*pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-80); ī for the ā of the vikaraṇa by ई हल्यघोः (*ī halyaghoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-113); ṇatva after ṛ; tiṅanta nighāta. तुर्वणिः (*turvaṇiḥ*) — root तुर्वी हिंसायाम् (*turvī hiṃsāyām*); auṇādika suffix अनि (*ani*); ādyudātta of the suffix. असत् (*asat*) — root अस भुवि (*asa bhuvi*); leṭ, 3rd singular तिप् (*tip*); loss of final i by इतश्च लोपः (*itaśca lopaḥ*); by लेटोऽडाटौ (*leṭo 'ḍāṭau*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-94) the augment अट् (*aṭ*) … *(continues on the next page)*

## Sūkta 186, Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उप व एषे नमसा जिगीषोषासानक्ता सुदुघेव धेनुः ।
> समाने अहन्विमिमानो अर्कं विषुरूपे पयसि सस्मिन्नूधन् ॥ ४ ॥

> *upa va eṣe namasā jigīṣoṣāsānaktā sudugheva dhenuḥ |*
> *samāne ahanvimimāno arkaṃ viṣurūpe payasi sasminnūdhan ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उप । वः । आ । ईषे । नमसा । जिगीषा । उषसानक्ता । सुदुघाऽइव । धेनुः ।
> समाने । अहन् । विऽमिमानः । अर्कं । विषुऽरूपे । पयसि । सस्मिन् । ऊधन् ॥ ४ ॥

> *upa | vaḥ | ā | īṣe | namasā | jigīṣā | uṣasānaktā | sudughā 'iva | dhenuḥ |*
> *samāne | ahan | vi 'mimānaḥ | arkaṃ | viṣu 'rūpe | payasi | sasmin | ūdhan ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; continues on the next page)*

> हे देवाः वो युष्माकं नमसा हविषा नमस्कारेण वोपोपेत्य जिगीषा पापानां जिगीषयेषे इच्छामि ॥ इष गतावित्यस्य वेषतेर्वा गत्याद्यर्थस्य लिट्युत्तमैकवचन इदं रूपं ॥ भजामि । कस्मिन्काले । उषासानक्ताऽहनि रात्रौ च । यद्वा । अहोरात्रदेवते अप्यभिगच्छामि । गतौ दृष्टांतः । सुदुघा धेनुरिव सुदोग्ध्री धेनुर्यथा दोहाय दोग्धुर्गृहमागच्छति तद्वत् । किं कुर्वन् । सस्मिन् समान ऊधन्यूधस्युत्पन्ने विषुरूपे नानारूपे पयसि क्षीरघृतादिकेऽर्कमर्चनीयमन्नं चरुपुरोडाशादिकं विमिमानो विविधं मिमानः । कस्मिन्काले । समानेऽहन् षष्ठेऽहनि । एकस्मिन्नेवाहनि ० वर्ड्यैव ने[?]त्यर्थः । एकस्मिन्नेवाहनि समान ऊधस्युत्पन्ने नानारूपे …

> *he devāḥ vo yuṣmākaṃ namasā haviṣā namaskāreṇa vopopetya jigīṣā pāpānāṃ jigīṣayeṣe icchāmi ‖ iṣa gatāvityasya veṣatervā gatyādyarthasya liṭyuttamaikavacana idaṃ rūpaṃ ‖ bhajāmi | kasminkāle | uṣāsānaktā 'hani rātrau ca | yadvā | ahorātradevate apyabhigacchāmi | gatau dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ | sudughā dhenuriva sudogdhrī dhenuryathā dohāya dogdhurgṛhamāgacchati tadvat | kiṃ kurvan | sasmin samāna ūdhanyūdhasyutpanne viṣurūpe nānārūpe payasi kṣīraghṛtādike 'rkamarcanīyamannaṃ carupuroḍāśādikaṃ vimimāno vividhaṃ mimānaḥ | kasminkāle | samāne 'han ṣaṣṭhe 'hani | ekasminnevāhani 0 varḍyaiva ne[?]tyarthaḥ | ekasminnevāhani samāna ūdhasyutpanne nānārūpe …*

*(In the bhāṣya, लिट्युत्त- (*liṭyutta-*) is broken at the line end and the next syllable, read as म (*ma*), looks like न (*na*) (zoomed); after समानेऽहन् (*samāne'han*) the word षष्ठे (*ṣaṣṭhe*) was doubtful in the zoom but is confirmed by the Kannada Pratipadārtha and Bhāvārtha on p. 136 ("the sixth day"); "वर्ड्यैव ने[?]त्यर्थः" is given letter by letter as printed, undecided; the ० is printed.)*

### Printed p. 136  (PDF 154)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Ṛk 4, continued.)*

> पयसि त्वदर्थं हविर्विमिमान उपगच्छामीत्यर्थः । यद्वा । सस्मिन् सर्वस्मिन्नूधसि फलाख्यक्षीरोत्पादके यज्ञे निमित्तभूते सति विषुरूपे पयसि नानारूपे सोमलक्षणोदकेऽर्कमन्नसाधनं स्तोत्रं विमिमानोऽहं युष्मानभिगच्छामि ॥

> *payasi tvadarthaṃ havirvimimāna upagacchāmītyarthaḥ | yadvā | sasmin sarvasminnūdhasi phalākhyakṣīrotpādake yajñe nimittabhūte sati viṣurūpe payasi nānārūpe somalakṣaṇodake 'rkamannasādhanaṃ stotraṃ vimimāno 'haṃ yuṣmānabhigacchāmi ‖*

*Gist:* O gods, with oblation and salutation, out of the wish to overcome sin, I come to you day and night (or to the Day-and-Night deities), as a good milch-cow comes to be milked, preparing on the one (sixth) day the offering of caru and puroḍāśa in milk of many forms from one udder; or, at the sacrifice that yields fruit, preparing a hymn in the Soma-water. (त्वदर्थं (*tvadarthaṃ*) as printed.)

**Pratipadārtha.** (O all deities,) समाने अहन् (*samāne ahan*) — on one and the same (the sixth) day, or at all times; सस्मिन् (*sasmin*) — the same (one and the same); ऊधन् (*ūdhan*) — arising from the udder, and; विषुरूपे (*viṣurūpe*) — undergoing transformation into various forms; पयसि (*payasi*) — in milk; अर्कं (*arkaṃ*) — the worshipful food, caru and the like; विमिमानः (*vimimānaḥ*) — I, who mix; जिगीषा (*jigīṣā*) — with the desire to conquer sin; सुदुघा (*sudughā*) — yielding milk well; धेनुः इव (*dhenuḥ iva*) — as a cow comes of itself for milking; उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*) — day and night; नमसा (*namasā*) — with oblation and also with salutation; वः (*vaḥ*) — you; उप (*upa*) — approaching; एषे (*eṣe*) — (your presence) I desire.

**Bhāvārtha.** O all deities, I, who mix the caru, puroḍāśa and other food worthy of worship in the milk obtained from one and the same udder on the sixth day of the sacrifice and transformed into various forms, approach you day and night with the desire to conquer sin, just as a cow that yields milk well comes of itself to be milked, with oblation and with salutation together, and desire your presence.

**English Translation (as printed):**

I approach you, (deities), with reverence, night and day, in the hope of overcoming (sin), as (willingly) as a gentle cow (comes to be milked)' [sic] mixing (for you) on the appropriate day the (sacrificial) food, (consisting) of multiform (preparations) of milk (generated) from the same udder.

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).**

Although in this ṛk the deities are prayed to, apart from the deity called उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*) the other deities are praised generally, that is, collectively.

नमसा (*namasā*) — हविषा नमस्कारेण वा (*haviṣā namaskāreṇa vā*) — the intention is: "I approach you, the deities, with oblation or with salutation."

उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*) — अहनि रात्रौ च । यद्वा । अहोरात्रदेवते अप्यभिगच्छामि (*ahani rātrau ca | yadvā | ahorātradevate apyabhigacchāmi*) — the commentator has explained one kind of meaning, "in the day and in the night too", and another kind of meaning, "(I approach) the deities called उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*), the presiding deities of day and night".
