### Printed p. 164 (PDF 182)

*(Header printed "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Ṛk 10: Special Topics continued.)*

— in these two ṛks both deities, Vāyu and Vāta, are praised. Of these two, Vāyu and Vāta, it is Vāyu who is praised together with Indra.

> इंद्रवायू इमे सुता उप प्रयोभिरा गतं । इंदवो वामुशंति हि ॥

> *iṃdravāyū ime sutā upa prayobhirā gataṃ | iṃdavo vāmuśaṃti hi ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-2-4, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Indra and Vāyu, these (soma drinks) are pressed; come hither with delights; for the drops long for you.")

— in these and other ṛks Indra and Vāyu are both praised together. Vāta is generally connected with Parjanya.

> पर्जन्यवाता वृषभा पृथिव्याः पुरीषाणि जिन्वतमप्यानि ।

> *parjanyavātā vṛṣabhā pṛthivyāḥ purīṣāṇi jinvatamapyāni |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-49-6, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Parjanya and Vāta, bulls, quicken the watery fillings of the earth.")

— in these and other ṛks Parjanya and Vāta are praised together. The epithets used for the two are generally different; the epithets of Vāta especially indicate speed and impetuosity.

> पूषणं — पूषा यद्रश्मिपोषं पुष्यति तत्पूषा भवति ।

> *pūṣaṇaṃ — pūṣā yadraśmipoṣaṃ puṣyati tatpūṣā bhavati |*

(Ni. 12-[?]6; the first digit of the second number is broken, a stroke before the 6) — the Nirukta says that this deity is named Pūṣan because he nourishes by the rays. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa too —

> इयं वै पूषा पूषेयं हीदं सर्वं पुष्यति यदिदं किंच ।

> *iyaṃ vai pūṣā pūṣeyaṃ hīdaṃ sarvaṃ puṣyati yadidaṃ kiṃca |*

(Śa. Brā. 14-4-2-25, zoomed) — it is said that this deity (the earth) is called Pūṣan because it nourishes everything. This kind of meaning supports the view that Pūṣan is one of the twelve Ādityas.

> पुष्यन् क्षितिं पोषयति प्रणुदन् रश्मिभिस्तमः ।
> तेनैनमस्तौत्पूषेति भरद्वाजस्तु पंचभिः ॥

> *puṣyan kṣitiṃ poṣayati praṇudan raśmibhistamaḥ |*
> *tenainamastautpūṣeti bharadvājastu paṃcabhiḥ ‖*

(Bṛ. De. 2-63, zoomed) — the Bṛhaddevatā says: because, dispelling the darkness, he nourishes the earth so that it grows, his name is Pūṣan; the ṛṣi Bharadvāja has praised this deity in these five sūktas of the sixth Maṇḍala, 53, 54, 55, 56, 58 (zoomed).

The name of this deity occurs in about 120 places in the Ṛgveda (zoomed). There are eight sūktas praising this deity. Of them, 2 sūktas in the first Maṇḍala, 5 sūktas in the sixth Maṇḍala and 1 sūkta in the tenth Maṇḍala praise Pūṣan. In Ṛ. Saṃ. sūkta 6-57 he is praised together with Indra, and in Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-40 together with Soma (both zoomed).

Since all paths are known to Pūṣan, they call him the protector of the roads. Robbers, thieves and dacoits that may befall on the road (or at the time of a journey) …
### Printed p. 165 (PDF 183)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 5" (zoomed). Ṛk 10: Special Topics continued.)*

… they pray to him to drive them away from the roads (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-42-1 to 3, zoomed). In this very context he has the name विमुचोनपात् (*vimuconapāt*) — "son of deliverance" (the Kannada gives "son of vivecana"). This epithet is also in Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-55-1.

> वि पथो वाजसातये चिनुहि वि मृधो जहि । साधंतामुग्र नो धियः ।

> *vi patho vājasātaye cinuhi vi mṛdho jahi | sādhaṃtāmugra no dhiyaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-53-4, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Clear the paths for the winning of booty, strike away the foes; O mighty one, let our thoughts succeed.")

— in this ṛk and in the ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-42-7, 8 (zoomed) there is the prayer: "strike down the enemies, make the road bright, and let the road reach a place with good pasture." In many places it is prayed that he remove the troubles that may come on the way and make the way auspicious. In the ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-49-8; 6-53-1 (zoomed) it is said that he alone is the protector of every road and shows the way on the road. Therefore it is stated in places such as the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya Sūtra 3-6-8 and the Śāṅkhāyana Śrauta Sūtra 3-4-9 (zoomed) that everyone setting out on a journey should, reciting the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-53, offer worship to Pūṣan, the architect of roads, and that all who have lost their way should seek refuge in Pūṣan alone.

It is said in places such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-23-14, 15 and Tai. Saṃ. 3-3-9-1 (zoomed) that Pūṣan, being prayed to find, as one searches for a creature that has strayed, found the king who was lost and hidden. Therefore whoever has lost anything should offer worship to Pūṣan (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 3-7-9, zoomed). In the same way, following the cattle and protecting them is a special mark of Pūṣan. He guards them from falling into a pit and getting hurt, and drives them home behind them so that no harm comes to them. He brings back those that have strayed (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-54-7 and 10, zoomed). His goad drives the cattle straight. He protects the horses. He creates the cattle (Mai. Saṃ. 4-3-7; Tai. Brā. 1-7-2-4, zoomed) — such descriptions are abundant in the Ṛgveda. The words of praise to Pūṣan to be used when the cattle have gone out to graze and strayed are given in the Śāṅkhāyana Gṛhya Sūtra (Śāṃ. Gṛ. Sū. 3-9, zoomed).

विष्णुः (*viṣṇuḥ*) — Although in the Brāhmaṇas and the Purāṇas Viṣṇu is counted as a most important deity, in the Ṛgveda Viṣṇu has no such prominence. Only five sūktas and some portion of one sūkta have Viṣṇu as their deity. Apart from this, in many places Viṣṇu's name is mentioned here and there together with other deities, chiefly with Indra. Viṣṇu's chief feat is said to be the placing of the three steps. These three steps are in heaven, the atmosphere and the earth. Besides these, Viṣṇu's place called the "highest step" (paramapada) is reckoned the most excellent abode.
### Printed p. 166 (PDF 184)

*(Header printed "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Ṛk 10: Special Topics continued (Viṣṇu).)*

In the Ṛgveda Viṣṇu's connection with Indra is seen to be closer than with other deities. At the time of slaying the demon Vṛtra, Indra seeks Viṣṇu's help. In the Yajurveda the subject of Viṣṇu is described in various ways. There are many mantras describing Viṣṇu as the lord of sacrifice and of the mountains, as the very form of sacrifice, and as the one who goes in front of all the deities (Leader). Yāska has given the derivation of the word viṣṇu in this way —

> विष्णुः — अथ यद्विषितो भवति तद्विष्णुर्भवति विष्णुर्विशतेर्वा व्यश्नोतेर्वा ।

> *viṣṇuḥ — atha yadviṣito bhavati tadviṣṇurbhavati viṣṇurviśatervā vyaśnotervā |*

(Ni. 12-18, read from the strip) — because he pervades everything, or because he enters everything and pervades it, or because by his rays he is the one pervading all, his name is Viṣṇu; therefore Viṣṇu may also be said to be Āditya (the sun) — so the word viṣṇu has been explained.

In the Ṛgveda Viṣṇu's great deed is the trivikrama, or the act of placing three steps. What are these three kinds of step, and where? On this there is a difference of opinion. Western scholars have explained it by the three states of the sun — its rising, its being at the zenith, and its setting.

[This stepping of Vishnu is emblamatic [sic] of the rising, the culminating and setting of the sun·]

[Max Muller· Sacred Books of the East· Vol· XXXII· p· 133]

From the words of the Nirukta it is known that ancient scholars such as Aurṇavābha also supported this meaning.

> समारोहणे विष्णुपदे गयशिरसीत्यौर्णवाभः ।

> *samārohaṇe viṣṇupade gayaśirasītyaurṇavābhaḥ |*

(Ni. 12-19, read from the strip) — thus the Niruktakāra has given the view of Aurṇavābha. On this sentence Durgācārya says:

> समारोहणे — उदयगिरावुद्यन् पदमेकं निधत्ते । विष्णुपदे माध्यंदिनेऽन्तरिक्षे । गयशिरसि — अस्तंगिरौ ।

> *samārohaṇe — udayagirāvudyan padamekaṃ nidhatte | viṣṇupade mādhyaṃdine 'ntarikṣe | gayaśirasi — astaṃgirau |*

— one step placed on the eastern mountain at the time of sunrise, in the form of rising; another step being at the zenith in the atmosphere at midday; and the third step placed on the western mountain at the time of setting — that this is indicated by the words त्रेधा निदधे पदं (*tredhā nidadhe padaṃ*) is the view of Aurṇavābha, the Niruktakāra has stated. Further,

> विष्णुस्त्रिधा निधत्ते पदं त्रेधाभावाय पृथिव्यामन्तरिक्षे दिवीति शाकपूणिः ।

> *viṣṇustridhā nidhatte padaṃ tredhābhāvāya pṛthivyāmantarikṣe divīti śākapūṇiḥ |*

(Ni. 12-19, read from the strip) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Viṣṇu places his step threefold, for threefold being: on the earth, in the atmosphere, in heaven — so Śākapūṇi.")
### Printed p. 167 (PDF 185)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 5" (zoomed). The scan has a blank band above the header. Ṛk 10: Special Topics continued (Viṣṇu).)*

— it is also stated that it is Śākapūṇi's view that this threefold placing of the step indicates the three states of the sun moving in the three worlds, the earth, the atmosphere and the heaven. On this Durgācārya:

> पार्थिवोऽग्निर्भूत्वा पृथिव्यां यत्किंचिदस्ति तद्विक्रमते । अंतरिक्षे विद्युदात्मना दिवि सूर्यात्मना ।

> *pārthivo 'gnirbhūtvā pṛthivyāṃ yatkiṃcidasti tadvikramate | aṃtarikṣe vidyudātmanā divi sūryātmanā |*

— he has explained that in the forms of Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya he strides over the three worlds. Supporting this same meaning:

> विष्णुमुखा वै देवाश्छंदोभिरिमांल्लोकाननपजय्यमभ्यजयन् यद्विष्णुक्रमान्क्रमते विष्णुरेव भूत्वा यजमानश्छंदोभिरिमांल्लोकाननपजय्यमभिजयति विष्णोः क्रमोस्यभिमातिहेत्याह गायत्री वै पृथिवी त्रैष्टुभमंतरिक्षं जागती द्यौरानुष्टुभीर्दिशश्छंदोभिरेवेमांल्लोकान् यथापूर्वमभिजयति ।

> *viṣṇumukhā vai devāśchaṃdobhirimāṃllokānanapajayyamabhyajayan yadviṣṇukramānkramate viṣṇureva bhūtvā yajamānaśchaṃdobhirimāṃllokānanapajayyamabhijayati viṣṇoḥ kramosyabhimātihetyāha gāyatrī vai pṛthivī traiṣṭubhamaṃtarikṣaṃ jāgatī dyaurānuṣṭubhīrdiśaśchaṃdobhirevemāṃllokān yathāpūrvamabhijayati |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 1-7-5-4, zoomed) (Gist, mine and tentative: the gods, led by Viṣṇu, won these worlds by the metres; the sacrificer taking the Viṣṇu-strides, having become Viṣṇu, wins them in due order — earth as gāyatrī, atmosphere as triṣṭubh, sky as jagatī, the quarters as anuṣṭubh.)

*(Next: "mā no pra hārasti vā idaṃ" as printed, zoomed.)*

> अन्या देवतासीत्सोऽब्रवीद्विष्णवे हीदमा हरिष्यावो येनायमिदमिति स विष्णुस्त्रेधात्मानं वि न्यधत्त पृथिव्यां तृतीयमंतरिक्षे तृतीयं दिवि तृतीयमभिपर्यावर्ताद्ध्यबिभेद्यत्पृथिव्यां तृतीयमासीत्तेनेंद्रो वज्रमुदयच्छद्विष्ण्वनुस्थितस्सोऽब्रवीन्मा नो प्र हारस्ति वा इदं ॥

> *anyā devatāsītso 'bravīdviṣṇave hīdamā hariṣyāvo yenāyamidamiti sa viṣṇustredhātmānaṃ vi nyadhatta pṛthivyāṃ tṛtīyamaṃtarikṣe tṛtīyaṃ divi tṛtīyamabhiparyāvartāddhyabibhedyatpṛthivyāṃ tṛtīyamāsītteneṃdro vajramudayacchadviṣṇvanusthitasso 'bravīnmā no pra hārasti vā idaṃ ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 2-4-12-3, zoomed) (Gist, mine and tentative: Viṣṇu set himself down in three parts — a third on earth, a third in the atmosphere, a third in heaven; with the third that was on the earth Indra raised the thunderbolt, Viṣṇu standing by.)

— in these and other Saṃhitā passages, and also

*(Next: "divamuttamenaitānvevaiṣa etasmai viṣṇuryajñaṃ" as printed, zoomed.)*

> यद्वेव विष्णुक्रमान्क्रमते । यज्ञो वै विष्णुः स देवेभ्य इमां विक्रांतिं विचक्रमे यैषामियं विक्रांतिरिदमेव प्रथमेन पदेन पस्पाराथेदमंतरिक्षं द्वितीयेन दिवमुत्तमेनैतान्वेवैष एतस्मै विष्णुर्यज्ञं विक्रांतिं विक्रमते तस्माद्विष्णुक्रमान्क्रमते ।

> *yadveva viṣṇukramānkramate | yajño vai viṣṇuḥ sa devebhya imāṃ vikrāṃtiṃ vicakrame yaiṣāmiyaṃ vikrāṃtiridameva prathamena padena paspārāthedamaṃtarikṣaṃ dvitīyena divamuttamenaitānvevaiṣa etasmai viṣṇuryajñaṃ vikrāṃtiṃ vikramate tasmādviṣṇukramānkramate |*

(Śa. Brā. 1-9-3-9, zoomed) (Gist, mine and tentative: Viṣṇu is the sacrifice; he strode for the gods this striding — this earth with the first step, the atmosphere with the second, the sky with the last; therefore one takes the Viṣṇu-strides.)

> यद्वेव विष्णुक्रमवात्सप्रे भवतः । विष्णुक्रमैर्वै प्रजापतिरिमं लोकमसृजत वात्सप्रेणाग्निं विष्णुक्रमैर्वै प्रजापतिरंतरिक्षमसृजत वात्सप्रेण वायुं विष्णुक्रमैर्वै प्रजापतिर्दिवमसृजत वात्सप्रेणादित्यं ।

> *yadveva viṣṇukramavātsapre bhavataḥ | viṣṇukramairvai prajāpatirimaṃ lokamasṛjata vātsapreṇāgniṃ viṣṇukramairvai prajāpatiraṃtarikṣamasṛjata vātsapreṇa vāyuṃ viṣṇukramairvai prajāpatirdivamasṛjata vātsapreṇādityaṃ |*

(Śa. Brā. 6-7-4-7, zoomed) (Gist, mine and tentative: by the Viṣṇu-strides Prajāpati created this world, the atmosphere and the sky; by the Vātsapra hymn Agni, Vāyu and Āditya.)

— in these and other Brāhmaṇa passages too, in accordance with Śākapūṇi's view, a connection is shown between the three steps of Viṣṇu, the worlds earth, atmosphere and heaven, and the deities Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya. Further,

> आ यो विवाय सचथाय दैव्य इंद्राय विष्णुः सुकृते सुकृत्तरः ।
> वेधा अजिन्वत्त्रिषधस्थ आर्यमृतस्य भागे यजमानमाभजत् ॥

> *ā yo vivāya sacathāya daivya iṃdrāya viṣṇuḥ sukṛte sukṛttaraḥ |*
> *vedhā ajinvattriṣadhastha āryamṛtasya bhāge yajamānamābhajat ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-156-5, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "The divine Viṣṇu, the better doer, who came for companionship to Indra the good doer — the disposer of the three abodes quickened the Ārya and gave the sacrificer a share in the order.")

### Printed p. 168 (PDF 186)

*(Header printed "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Ṛk 10: Special Topics continued (Viṣṇu; Aśvins begun).)*

— in this ṛk it is said that Viṣṇu himself strides over the three worlds, the earth and the rest. The point that, as stated in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa mantra 6-7-4-7 cited above, Viṣṇu's three steps (printed "prādatraya", for pādatraya) are the cause of the creation and maintenance of the worlds, the earth and the rest — in the ṛk (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-154-2, zoomed), अधिक्षियंति भुवनानि विश्वा (*adhikṣiyaṃti bhuvanāni viśvā*) — the greatness of Viṣṇu's strides is praised: all the worlds rest on the support that is in the form of Viṣṇu's three strides.

In the Purāṇas and similar works Viṣṇu has a prominent place. Because he pervades the whole universe they call Viṣṇu the Supreme Lord and the Supreme Brahman. Or, among the Trimūrtis Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśvara who conduct the origin, maintenance and dissolution of the world, Viṣṇu is famed as the one who protects the world. Since for this work of protecting the world Viṣṇu had to undertake many incarnations, the commentator (Sāyaṇa) and other scholars hold that the Vāmana or Trivikrama incarnation, one of those incarnations, is what is described in this ṛk. Western and modern scholars hold that, because the incarnations of Viṣṇu and the like are not indicated in the Ṛgveda, because the deeds of the deities seen here and there in the Veda are described in a special manner in the Purāṇas, and because the Veda itself is the source of the Purāṇic stories, it is not right to interpret Vedic mantras by fitting the incarnations contained in the Purāṇas to them.

As told in the story in the Purāṇas: when the asura called Bali Cakravartin had conquered the gods and was ruling, the defeated gods appealed to Viṣṇu; Viṣṇu, to protect them, took the Vāmana incarnation and, when Bali Cakravartin had undertaken the consecration for a sacrifice, went to him and asked to be given as much land as three steps; Bali agreed and said he would give accordingly. Then Viṣṇu in the form of Vāmana took the Trivikrama incarnation, that is, assumed a huge form so as to pervade the earth and the atmosphere entirely, and with one step covered the whole earth and with another step the atmosphere, and asked Bali where he should place the third step. That king, being true to his word, prayed that, since there was no other place, he should place the third step on his head and show him favour; accordingly Trivikrama placed his third step on Bali's head, made him go to the nether world (Pātāla) and live happily ruling there, and gave him the boon he desired — there is an extensive description of this.

अश्विनौ (*aśvinau*) — We have explained the subject of the Aśvin deities many times before. Here we shall now state briefly only a short introduction to them and an account of the help they gave to those who praised them.

The Aśvin deities are two. Although one of them is named Dasra and the other Nāsatya, both are very often called by the name Dasrā or Nāsatyā.
### Printed p. 169 (PDF 187)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 5". Ṛk 10: Special Topics continued (Aśvins).)*

Their chariot is golden, and all its parts, wheel, axle and the rest, are made of gold (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-44-4, 1-180-1, 8-5-29, 8-22-5 etc., zoomed). It is a wonderful chariot. It has three wheels, three fellies, and some other parts too are three each. It has the speed of thought. The three-wheeled chariot is theirs alone.

> यदयातं शुभस्पती वरेयं सूर्यामुप ।
> क्वैकं चक्रं वामासीत् क्व देष्ट्राय तस्थतुः ॥

> *yadayātaṃ śubhaspatī vareyaṃ sūryāmupa |*
> *kvaikaṃ cakraṃ vāmāsīt kva deṣṭrāya tasthatuḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-15, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "When you came, O lords of beauty, as wooers to Sūryā, where was one wheel of yours? Where did you stand for the giving?")

— here it is said that when they went to the wedding of the goddess Sūryā one wheel of the chariot was lost. Although the word aśvinau means "possessors of horses", it is nowhere said that the name came to them because they were horse-riders. The horses that draw their chariot (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-2), birds (6-63-6), swans (4-45-4), eagle-birds (1-118-4), horses in the form of falcons (8-5-7) are mentioned (all zoomed). But their chief vehicle, as Yāska has said, रासभावश्विनोः (*rāsabhāvaśvinoḥ*) — for the Aśvin deities asses alone are the vehicles (Ni. 2-28, zoomed).

> कदा योगो वाजिनो रासभस्य येन यज्ञं नासत्योपयाथः ।

> *kadā yogo vājino rāsabhasya yena yajñaṃ nāsatyopayāthaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-34-9, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "When is the yoking of the swift ass, by which, O Nāsatyas, you come to the sacrifice?")

> तद्रासभो नासत्या सहस्रमाजा यमस्य प्रधने जिगाय ।

> *tadrāsabho nāsatyā sahasramājā yamasya pradhane jigāya |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-2, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "That ass of yours, O Nāsatyas, won a thousand in the race, in the contest of Yama.")

— in these and other ṛks it is clearly said that the ass (kattē) is the vehicle of the Aśvin deities.

Those who sacrifice always invoke them in the morning hours. They have a connection with the daughter of the Sun; Sūryā herself chose them (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-69-4); both of them are her husbands (4-43-6); Sūryā mounted their chariot (5-73-5; 8-8-10); the daughter of the Sun mounts their chariot (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-34-5; 1-116-17; 1-118-5; 6-63-5); they regard Sūryā as their own (7-68-3); and she goes with them in the chariot (8-29-8) — there are such descriptions (references zoomed; 8-29-8 read from the strip).

There are many legends showing that they help people in distress. These have been explained at length in their respective contexts. But we have explained only some important ones among them here.

> जुजुरुषो नासत्योत वव्रिं प्रामुंचतं द्रापिमिव च्यवानात् ।
> प्रातिरतं जहितस्यायुर्दस्रादित्पतिमकृणुतं कनीनां ॥

> *jujuruṣo nāsatyota vavriṃ prāmuṃcataṃ drāpimiva cyavānāt |*
> *prātirataṃ jahitasyāyurdasrāditpatimakṛṇutaṃ kanīnāṃ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-10, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "From the aged Cyavāna, O Nāsatyas, you stripped off his covering like a mantle; you lengthened the life of the abandoned one, O Dasras, and then made him the husband of maidens.")

### Printed p. 170 (PDF 188)

*(Header printed "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Ṛk 10: Special Topics continued (Aśvins: Cyavāna, Kali, Vimada).)*

— the ṛṣi named Cyavana, when he had become very old, his body loosened and without strength, was abandoned by his people. When this ṛṣi prayed to the Aśvin deities, they came, removed his loosened body, made him a youth, made him dear to his wife, and increased his life-span — so it is said. This same subject —

> युवं च्यवानमश्विना जरंतं पुनर्युवानं चक्रथुः शचीभिः ।

> *yuvaṃ cyavānamaśvinā jaraṃtaṃ punaryuvānaṃ cakrathuḥ śacībhiḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-13, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "You, O Aśvins, by your powers made the aged Cyavāna young again.")

> निष्टौग्र्यं पारयथः समुद्रात् पुनश्च्यवानं चक्रथुर्युवानं ।

> *niṣṭaugryaṃ pārayathaḥ samudrāt punaścyavānaṃ cakrathuryuvānaṃ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-118-6, zoomed; the opening bracket is not printed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "You carry the son of Tugra safely out of the ocean; you made Cyavāna young again.")

> प्र च्यवानाज्जुजुरुषो वव्रिमत्कं न मुंचथः ।
> युवा यदी कृथः पुनरा काममृण्वे वध्वः ॥

> *pra cyavānājjujuruṣo vavrimatkaṃ na muṃcathaḥ |*
> *yuvā yadī kṛthaḥ punarā kāmamṛṇve vadhvaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-74-5, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "From the aged Cyavāna you loosen his covering like a garment; when you make him young again, he wins the desire of the bride.")

> उत त्यद्वां जुरते अश्विना भूच्च्यवानाय प्रतीत्यं हविर्दे ।

> *uta tyadvāṃ jurate aśvinā bhūccyavānāya pratītyaṃ havirde |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-68-6, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "And that favour of yours, O Aśvins, came to the aged Cyavāna, the giver of oblation.")

> युवं च्यवानं जरसोऽमुमुक्तं नि पेदव ऊहथुराशुमश्वं ।

> *yuvaṃ cyavānaṃ jaraso 'mumuktaṃ ni pedava ūhathurāśumaśvaṃ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-71-5, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "You freed Cyavāna from old age; you brought the swift horse to Pedu.")

> युवं च्यवानं सनयं यथा रथं पुनर्युवानं चरथाय तक्षथुः ।

> *yuvaṃ cyavānaṃ sanayaṃ yathā rathaṃ punaryuvānaṃ carathāya takṣathuḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-39-4) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "You fashioned the old Cyavāna, like an old chariot, young again so that he could move.")

— in these ṛks too there is a description of making the aged ṛṣi Cyavana a youth. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa too there is an extensive legend on this subject. Likewise —

> युवं विप्रस्य जरणामुपेयुषः पुनः कलेरकृणुतं युवद्वयः ।

> *yuvaṃ viprasya jaraṇāmupeyuṣaḥ punaḥ kalerakṛṇutaṃ yuvadvayaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-39-8) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "For the sage Kali, who had reached old age, you made youthful vigour again.")

— in this ṛk there is mention of removing the old age of the one called Kali and making him a youth.

> याभिर्वम्रं विपिपानमुपस्तुतं कलिं याभिर्वित्तजानिं दुवस्यथः ।

> *yābhirvamraṃ vipipānamupastutaṃ kaliṃ yābhirvittajāniṃ duvasyathaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-15, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "With which aids you favoured Vamra as he drank, and Upastuta, and Kali who had won a wife.")

— it is said that when the Kali mentioned above took a wife and married, they gave him their help and did him many favours.

For the young women who were Vimada's wives they (granted) a chariot (1-112-19, zoomed, third try), or granted him a wife (1-117-1, zoomed). It appears that she had been the wife of Puramitra (as printed) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-20; 10-39-6, zoomed), and her name was Kamadhyu (as printed) (10-65-12, zoomed) …

### Printed p. 171 (PDF 189)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 5". Ṛk 10: Special Topics continued (Aśvins: Viśvaka, Bhujyu, Viśpalā, Ṛjrāśva, Parāvṛja, Rebha).)*

To Viśvaka, the son of the one called Kṛṣṇa, they brought back and handed over his son who had been lost (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-23; 1-117-7; 10-65-12, zoomed). In the ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-75-1 to 3 (as read, zoomed) the names of Viśvaka and Viṣṇāpū are indicated.

The story of Bhujyu is told again and again. Bhujyu is the son of a king called Tugra. While he was making a sea voyage he began to sink; amid the waves Bhujyu was floating, holding on to a piece of wood. Then he called upon the Aśvin deities. In the great ocean whose depth is unknown, the Aśvin deities took him into a ship with a hundred oars and carried him home. In a boat without leaks that seemed to fly in the sky, or in four winged troughs, or in three flying chariots with a hundred feet and six horses, or in their own chariot swift as the mind, with the help of their horses that fly swiftly, they seated Bhujyu, brought him and delivered him to his home. (1-116-3, 4-5, 1-117-04, 15; 1-182-5, 6, 7; 7-68-7; 1-112-6, 20; 1-118-6; 1-119-4; 1-158-3; 6-62-6; 7-69-6; 8-5-22; 10-39-4; 10-47-7 (as read); 10-65-12; 10-143-5; all zoomed.)

When the woman called Viśpalā had her leg cut off in battle and prayed to the Aśvin deities, they came, fitted her with an iron leg and saved her — so it is said in the ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-10; 1-116-15; 1-117-11; 1-118-8; 10-39-8 (zoomed).

(When the ass, the vehicle of the Aśvin deities, was in the form of a wolf) the one called Ṛjrāśva cut up a hundred sheep from the flock he was tending and gave them as food to that wolf. His father became angry at this, put out Ṛjrāśva's eyes and made him blind. Then the wolf praised the Aśvin deities. Pleased, they gave Ṛjrāśva eyes (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-16; 1-117-17, 18, zoomed). In the ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-100-17 (zoomed) there is the matter of the one called Ṛjrāśva having praised Indra.

The one called Parāvṛja was blind and lame, and he had not been admitted into the caste. The Aśvin deities gave him sight to see and strength to walk, that is, they granted him eyes and legs (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-8, zoomed). The name of Parāvṛja is indicated, where it comes up in connection with Indra, in the ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-13-12; 2-15-7 (zoomed; no full stop printed).

The ṛṣi named Rebha had been bound hand and foot by wicked men and thrown into a well. For nine days and ten nights he lay there and was in a dying state. The Aśvin deities raised him up out of the well as one lifts Soma juice with a ladle, and gave him life (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-5; 1-109-24; 1-117-12; 1-117-4; 1-118-6; 1-119-6; 10-39-9, zoomed).

### Printed p. 172 (PDF 190)

*(Header printed "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Ṛk 10: Special Topics continued (Aśvins: Vandana, Kakṣīvat, Atri, Vadhrimatī, Ghoṣā, Śayu, Pedu).)*

The one called Vandana, too, was in the same way carried off by wicked men and thrown into a dark place (into a pit); then the Aśvin deities rescued him from danger and brought him to light (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-5; 1-116-11; 1-117-5; 1-118-6; 10-39-8' 1-119-6, 7; zoomed; the separator before 1-119 printed as an apostrophe).

To Kakṣīvat (printed "Kakṣīvata"), of the Pajra lineage, they gave boons as he wished, and from the hoof of a horse they poured out hundreds of jars of surā (liquor) or honey, as if pouring it through a sieve (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-7; 1-117-6, zoomed).

When the ṛṣi called Atri, out of hatred and envy, had been thrown into a great chasm covered in darkness and blazing with fire, and was in distress, he prayed to the Aśvin deities; they came, quenched the fire with frost, gave him food and other things, satisfied him, and rescued him from that state (1-112-7; 1-116-8; 1-117-3; 1-118-7; 1-119-6; 5-78-4 to 6; 7-31-5; 8-62-3, 7 to 9; 10-39-9; zoomed). In the ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-80-3 (zoomed) it is indicated that Agni protected Atri.

The woman called Vadhrimatī, since she had no children and was barren, prayed to the Aśvin deities, and they granted her a son called Hiraṇyahasta (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-13; 1-117-24; 6-62-7, zoomed; 10-39-7, read from the strip).

The woman called Ghoṣā stayed in her father's house and remained unmarried; therefore, at her prayer, the Aśvin deities granted her a fitting husband (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-7; 10-39-3, 6; 10-4-5 as printed; zoomed). In the bhāṣya of the ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-117-7 (read from the strip) Sāyaṇa has said that this woman Ghoṣā was wasting away with leprosy and that the Aśvin deities cured that disease. In the tenth maṇḍala (10-39) there is a sūkta seen by this Ghoṣā.

When the cow of the one called Śayu had grown old and was not bearing calves, they produced in it the power to give milk (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-22; 1-117-20; 1-118-8; 1-119-6; 10-39-73, zoomed).

It is said that the Aśvin deities gave the king called Pedu a white horse, very strong like Indra, and that with it he conquered his enemies and obtained abundant goods, vehicles and the like (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-116-6; 1-117-9; 1-118-9; 1-119-10; 7-71-5; 10-39-10, zoomed).

Besides this, as told in sūktas 1 2 (as printed, with a gap after the first 1), 116, 117, 118, 119 of the first maṇḍala (zoomed), it is said that these Aśvin deities, besides having helped many men, did good also to animals and birds. In this connection — when a wolf was carrying off a sparrow, holding it in its mouth, at the sparrow's prayer they released it from the wolf's mouth and saved it — Ṛ. Saṃ. …

1-116-14; 1-117-16; 1-118-8; 10 39-13 (as printed; zoomed) — so it is said in these ṛks. Besides these matters there are many more matters concerning the Aśvin deities. They will be explained in their respective contexts.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** कृणुध्वम् (*kṛṇudhvam*) — root कृवि हिंसाकरणयोश्च (*kṛvi hiṃsākaraṇayośca*); loṭ, second person plural; tiṅanta nighāta accent. स्वतवसः (*svatavasaḥ*) — स्वं स्वीयं तवः बलं येषां ते स्वतवसः (*svaṃ svīyaṃ tavaḥ balaṃ yeṣāṃ te svatavasaḥ*); by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā*) (no number printed) the first member keeps its own accent. संति (*saṃti*) — root अस भुवि (*asa bhuvi*); laṭ, third person plural; by हि च (*hi ca*) (printed "hica"; Pā. Sū. 8-1-34, zoomed) nighāta is barred, so the initial acute of the suffix remains. अद्वेषः (*adveṣaḥ*) — न विद्यते द्वेषः यस्य (*na vidyate dveṣaḥ yasya*); by नञ्सुभ्याम् (*nañsubhyām*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172, zoomed) the second member is end-acute. वातः (*vātaḥ*) — root वा गतिगन्धनयोः (*vā gatigandhanayoḥ*); suffix तन् (*tan*) by हसिमृग्रिण्व (*hasimṛgriṇva*) (as printed; Uṇ. Sū. 3-366, zoomed); initial acute because it has n as marker. अच्छ (*accha*) — lengthening in the Saṃhitā by निपातस्य च (*nipātasya ca*) (printed "U. Sū." 6-3-136, zoomed). ववृतीय (*vavṛtīya*) — root वृतु वर्तने (*vṛtu vartane*); liṅ, first person singular, suffix iṭ; its a by इटोऽत् (*iṭo 't*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-106, zoomed); augment sīyuṭ by लिङः सीयुट् (*liṅaḥ sīyuṭ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-102, zoomed; bracket not closed); ślu-vikaraṇa by the sūtra बहुलं छन्दसि (*bahulaṃ chandasi*); reduplication etc. of the root because of ślu; s dropped by लिङः सलोपोऽनन्त्यस्य (*liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya*) (printed "liṅaḥ salopo—"; Pā. Sū. 7-2-69, zoomed); tiṅanta nighāta accent.

*(Rule ":O:" — end of Ṛk 10.)*

## Sūkta 186, Ṛk 11

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> इयं सा वो अस्मे दीधितिर्यजत्रा अपिप्राणी च सदनी च भूयाः ।
> नि या देवेषु यतते वसूयुर्विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥ ११ ॥

> *iyaṃ sā vo asme dīdhitiryajatrā apiprāṇī ca sadanī ca bhūyāḥ |*
> *ni yā deveṣu yatate vasūyurvidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānuṃ ‖ 11 ‖*

*(The Pada-pāṭha follows on p. 174.)*

### Printed p. 174 (PDF 192)

*(Header printed "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 186". Ṛk 11: Pada, bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English.)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥** *(no ṛk number printed after the closing ॥)*

> इयं । सा । वः । अस्मे इति । दीधितिः । यजत्राः । अपिऽप्राणी । च । सदनी । च । भूयाः ।
> नि । या । देवेषु । यतते । वसुऽयुः । विद्याम । इषं । वृजनं । जीरऽदानुं ॥

> *iyaṃ | sā | vaḥ | asme iti | dīdhitiḥ | yajatrāḥ | api 'prāṇī | ca | sadanī | ca | bhūyāḥ |*
> *ni | yā | deveṣu | yatate | vasu 'yuḥ | vidyāma | iṣaṃ | vṛjanaṃ | jīra 'dānuṃ ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* O gods worthy of worship, may this radiance of yours, which strives among the gods bringing wealth, always quicken us and give us a dwelling.

> हे यजत्रा यष्टव्या देवाः वो युष्मत्संबंधिनी सेयं प्रसिद्धा दीधितिर्दीप्तिरस्मे अस्माकमपिप्राणी सर्वदा चेष्टयित्री सदनी च निवासवती च भूयाः । भूयात् । भवतु । या दीधितिर्वसूयुर्वसुमती देवेषु नि यतते नियमेन प्रयत्नं करोति । तानपि प्रकाशितुं सैव भूयात् । विद्यामेति गतः ॥

> *he yajatrā yaṣṭavyā devāḥ vo yuṣmatsaṃbaṃdhinī seyaṃ prasiddhā dīdhitirdīptirasme asmākamapiprāṇī sarvadā ceṣṭayitrī sadanī ca nivāsavatī ca bhūyāḥ | bhūyāt | bhavatu | yā dīdhitirvasūyurvasumatī deveṣu ni yatate niyamena prayatnaṃ karoti | tānapi prakāśituṃ saiva bhūyāt | vidyāmeti gataḥ ‖*


**Pratipadārtha.** यजत्राः (*yajatrāḥ*) — O deities worthy of sacrifice; या (*yā*) — which radiance; वसूयुः (*vasūyuḥ*) — endowed with wealth; देवेषु (*deveṣu*) — among the deities; नि यतते (*ni yatate*) — regularly attains manifestation (printed "havirbhāva", zoomed; the Bhāvārtha has āvirbhāva); सा (*sā*) — famous in the world; वः (*vaḥ*) — and belonging to you; इयं दीधितिः (*iyaṃ dīdhitiḥ*) — this radiance; अस्मे (*asme*) — to us; अपि प्राणी च (*api prāṇī ca*) — always giving consciousness; सदनी च (*sadanī ca*) — and furnished with a dwelling; भूयाः (*bhūyāḥ*) — may it be; इषं (*iṣaṃ*) — food; वृजनं (*vṛjanaṃ*) — strength; जीरदानुं (*jīradānuṃ*) — long life; विद्याम (*vidyāma*) — may we obtain.

**Bhāvārtha.** O deities worthy of sacrifice, may that radiance of yours, which, being rich in wealth and famous in the world, becomes manifest among you, be for us always the giver of consciousness and the giver of a dwelling. May we obtain food, strength and long life by your grace.

**English Translation (as printed):**

Objects of admiration (the a of "admiration" damaged in print), may that wealth-abounding effulgence which manifests itself amongst the gods, give animation to our existence, and (permanence to) our dwellings; that we may (thence) obtain food, strength, and long life· [sic]

### Printed p. 175 (PDF 193)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 5". Ṛk 11: Special Topics begun (the word asme in the senses of the cases).)*

**Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).**

The word अस्मे (*asme*) is used in the senses of all seven cases. For example —

(1) अस्मे ते बंधुः । वयमित्यर्थः ॥ (*asme te baṃdhuḥ | vayamityarthaḥ ‖*)

> अस्मे इत्येतत्पदं सर्वविभक्त्यंतं । तस्मादनेकार्थं । एकमेव ह्येतच्छब्दरूपं सप्तस्वपि विभक्त्यर्थेषु वर्तते । प्रकरणादिवशात् तस्य नियमो भवति । तद्यथा— प्रथमायास्तावत्— अस्मे ते बंधुः । वयमित्यर्थः ॥

> *asme ityetatpadaṃ sarvavibhaktyaṃtaṃ | tasmādanekārthaṃ | ekameva hyetacchabdarūpaṃ saptasvapi vibhaktyartheṣu vartate | prakaraṇādivaśāt tasya niyamo bhavati | tadyathā— prathamāyāstāvat— asme te baṃdhuḥ | vayamityarthaḥ ‖*

(No source is printed for this Sanskrit passage.) That is, the word asme is used in the senses of all seven cases according to the context; that is, according to the particular context, the sense of any one of the seven cases may be given to this word. For instance, in the sentence अस्मे ते बंधुः (*asme te baṃdhuḥ*) the word asme has the meaning वयम् (*vayam*) — "we". This is the example of the sense of the first case.

(2) अस्मे यातं नासत्या सजोषाः । अस्मानित्यर्थः ॥ (*asme yātaṃ nāsatyā sajoṣāḥ | asmānityarthaḥ ‖*)

द्वितीयायास्तावत् (*dvitīyāyāstāvat*) — for the word asme the meaning of the second case, अस्मान् (*asmān*) — "us". As an example of this sense —

> आ श्येनस्य जवसा नूतनेनास्मे यातं नासत्या सजोषाः ।
> हवे हि वामश्विना रातहव्यः शश्वत्तमाया उषसो व्युष्टौ ॥

> *ā śyenasya javasā nūtanenāsme yātaṃ nāsatyā sajoṣāḥ |*
> *have hi vāmaśvinā rātahavyaḥ śaśvattamāyā uṣaso vyuṣṭau ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-118-11, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Come to us, O Nāsatyas, of one accord, with the fresh speed of the falcon; for I, having offered the oblation, invoke you, O Aśvins, at the dawning of each perpetual morning.")

— this ṛk they have given. The word asme in this ṛk means अस्मान् (*asmān*) — "us".

(3) अस्मे समानेभिर्वृषभ पौंस्येभिः । अस्माभिरित्यर्थः ॥ (*asme samānebhirvṛṣabha pauṃsyebhiḥ | asmābhirityarthaḥ ‖*)

तृतीयायास्तावत् (*tṛtīyāyāstāvat*) — here asme means अस्माभिः (*asmābhiḥ*) — "by us", the sense of the third case. On this matter —

> भूरि चकर्थ युज्येभिरस्मे समानेभिर्वृषभ पौंस्येभिः ।
> भूरीणि हि कृणवामा शविष्ठेंद्र क्रत्वा मरुतो यद्वशाम ॥

> *bhūri cakartha yujyebhirasme samānebhirvṛṣabha pauṃsyebhiḥ |*
> *bhūrīṇi hi kṛṇavāmā śaviṣṭheṃdra kratvā maruto yadvaśāma ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-165-7, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Much have you done, O bull, with us, your allies, with equal manly powers; many things indeed shall we do, O mightiest Indra, by our skill, when we Maruts so will.")

— this ṛk they have given as the example. Here asme means अस्माभिः (*asmābhiḥ*) — "by us".

(4) अस्मे प्रयंधि मघवन्नृजीषिन् । अस्मभ्यमित्यर्थः ॥ (*asme prayaṃdhi maghavannṛjīṣin | asmabhyamityarthaḥ ‖*) *(printed with a stray colon after the syllable mi of the last word)*

चतुर्थ्यास्तावत् (*caturthyāstāvat*) — here asme means अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*) — "for us", the sense of the fourth case. Example —

> अस्मे प्र यंधि मघवन्नृजीषिन्निंद्र रायो विश्ववारस्य भूरेः ।
> अस्मे शतं शरदो जीवसे धा अस्मे वीराञ्छश्वत इंद्र शिप्रिन् ॥

> *asme pra yaṃdhi maghavannṛjīṣinniṃdra rāyo viśvavārasya bhūreḥ |*
> *asme śataṃ śarado jīvase dhā asme vīrāñchaśvata iṃdra śiprin ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-36-10, zoomed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "Grant to us, O bounteous Indra, drinker of the pressed Soma, abundant wealth desired by all; grant us a hundred autumns to live; grant us many heroes, O Indra of the fair jaws.")

— the word asme in this ṛk means अस्मत् (*asmat*) — "from our side", the sense of the fifth case.

षष्ठ्यास्तावत् (*ṣaṣṭhyāstāvat*) — here asme means अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*) — "ours / to us". To explain this sense —

— this ṛk they have cited. The word asme in this ṛk means अस्माकं (*asmākaṃ*) — "our, to us", the sense of the sixth case.

— the word asme in this ṛk means अस्मासु (*asmāsu*) — "in us", the sense of the seventh case.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** अस्मे (*asme*) (by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-34 as printed, zoomed) the substitute शे (*śe*) for the genitive plural ending). यजत्राः (*yajatrāḥ*) (root यज देवपूजासंगतिकरणदानेषु (*yaja devapūjāsaṃgatikaraṇadāneṣu*); suffix अत्रन् (*atran*) by अमिनक्षियजि (*aminakṣiyaji*)— (U. Sū. 3-385, per numeral file); vocative, so the आमंत्रितनिघात (*āmaṃtritanighāta*) accent). सदनी (*sadanī*) (root षद्ऌ विशरणगत्यवसादनेषु (*ṣadḷ viśaraṇagatyavasādaneṣu*); suffix ल्युट् (*lyuṭ*) with अन (*ana*) substitute; acute on the syllable before the suffix by लिति (*liti*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193, zoomed); feminine, टित् (*ṭit*), hence ङीप् (*ṅīp*)) *(grammar continues on the next page)*.

## Sūkta 187 — introductory matter (Pīṭhike)

*(Kannada half-title: "ನೂರ ಎಂಭತ್ತೇಳನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು", "the hundred-and-eighty-seventh sūkta".)*

**Pīṭhike (Introduction).**

The devatā of this sūkta is the praise of food (*anna-stuti*). As Śaunaka has said in his Ṛgvidhāna (Ṛgvi. 1-27, zoomed), it has been the practice among the Āryans from of old to worship food, that is, one's meal, with devotion and meditate on it, then give a small portion to guests and the like, and only after that eat oneself. Some reflection here on the greatness of food is necessary. The word *anna* is derived from the root अद भक्षणे (*ada bhakṣaṇe*) (*ad* — to eat). Regarding the origin of food —

> तस्माद्वा एतस्मादात्मन आकाशः संभूतः । आकाशाद्वायुः । वायोरग्निः ।
> अग्नेरापः । अद्भ्यः पृथिवी । पृथिव्या ओषधयः । ओषधीभ्योऽन्नं ।
> अन्नात्पुरुषः ॥

> *tasmādvā etasmādātmana ākāśaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ | ākāśādvāyuḥ | vāyoragniḥ |*
> *agnerāpaḥ | adbhyaḥ pṛthivī | pṛthivyā oṣadhayaḥ | oṣadhībhyo 'nnaṃ |*
> *annātpuruṣaḥ ‖*

(Tai. U. 2-1, zoomed; the ā-sign of अग्नेरापः (*agnerāpaḥ*) is broken in print)

— so runs the Śruti statement. It says that at the time of the creation of the world, that is, of the five elements, from the Supreme Brahman (the Paramātman) first space (*ākāśa*) arose; from space, air; from air, fire; from fire, water; from water, the earth (*bhūmi*); from the earth, the plants (crops and the like); and from the plants, food. From such food the origin of man (together with the other living beings) *(continues on the next page)*

---


### Printed p. 178 (PDF 196)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 187" (zoomed; the first digit of 24 broken). Pīṭhike of Sūkta 187, continued.)*

— (the origin of man) also came about, it says. And what is the excellence of food? What is the use that comes from food? What is the reason the name अन्न (*anna*) came to food? The answers to such questions too are given there itself —

> अन्नाद्वै प्रजाः प्रजायंते । याः काश्च पृथिवीग्ं श्रिताः । अथो अन्नेनैव
> जीवंति । अथैनदपियंत्यंततः । अन्नग्ंहि भूतानां ज्येष्ठं । तस्मात्सर्वौ-
> षधमुच्यते । सर्वं वै तेऽन्नमाप्नुवंति । येऽन्नं ब्रह्मोपासते ।
> अन्नग्ंहि भूतानां ज्येष्ठं । तस्मात्सर्वौषधमुच्यते । अन्नाद्भूतानि
> जायंते । जातान्यन्नेन वर्धंते । अद्यतेऽत्ति च भूतानि । तस्मादन्नं
> तदुच्यत इति ॥

> *annādvai prajāḥ prajāyaṃte | yāḥ kāśca pṛthivīgṃ śritāḥ | atho annenaiva*
> *jīvaṃti | athainadapiyaṃtyaṃtataḥ | annagṃhi bhūtānāṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ | tasmātsarvau-*
> *ṣadhamucyate | sarvaṃ vai te 'nnamāpnuvaṃti | ye 'nnaṃ brahmopāsate |*
> *annagṃhi bhūtānāṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ | tasmātsarvauṣadhamucyate | annādbhūtāni*
> *jāyaṃte | jātānyannena vardhaṃte | adyate 'tti ca bhūtāni | tasmādannaṃ*
> *taducyata iti ‖*

(Tai. U. 2-2, zoomed)

That is, all creatures that rest on the earth (together with all living beings) are born of food alone, live by food alone, and in the end are dissolved in it. Among the beings (or among the things created out of the five great elements) food alone is the eldest of all; therefore they call it सर्वौषध (*sarvauṣadha*) (the remedy for all). Those who worship the (Supreme) Brahman in the form of food obtain all food: that is, food will be available to them as much as they wish. Food alone is the eldest among all beings.

By "beings" (भूत (*bhūta*)) are meant the five great elements: earth, water, fire (तेजस् (*tejas*)), air and space. These five great elements are themselves, in their original form, food. Thus: earth is solid matter; in the food we eat there are always solid substances such as grain. These are the earth-portion. The second is water. Water we drink. Besides this, in the other things we eat or drink (milk and the like) there is always a water-portion. Living beings need water even more than the earth-portion (the solid) of food; in our body too the water-portion (the blood) is the larger. The third is तेजस् (*tejas*). तेजस् (*tejas*) means heat. Living beings cannot live without heat. We obtain heat both from the food we take and from the warmth present in the sunshine, the air and so on around us. As soon as the heat in the body stops, death occurs. From birth until death there must always be heat in the body; so there is no need to say how great the need for heat, or तेजस् (*tejas*), is. We need तेजस् (*tejas*) even a degree more than water. The fourth is air. When we draw our breath in, we attract the air outside and take it into the body. We cannot remain even a moment without breathing; as soon as breathing stops, life departs — that is, death occurs. From birth until death *(continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 179 (PDF 197)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 6" (zoomed). Pīṭhike of Sūkta 187, continued.)*

— air is utterly necessary for all living beings, and air is needed in greater measure than the earth-portion, solid food, water and तेजस् (*tejas*) spoken of before. The fifth is space (आकाश (*ākāśa*), room): without space it is impossible for us or for other living beings to exist. For our movements and for the needs of the body space is indispensable. Though the three things तेजस् (*tejas*), air and space are not seen by our eyes, they are utterly necessary for the nourishment of our body. Besides, we (and the other living beings too) need water a degree more than the solid food that is the earth-portion; तेजस् (*tejas*) more than water; air more than तेजस् (*tejas*); and space more than air. And another particular point: in the food connected with the earth-portion water, तेजस् (*tejas*), air and space are mixed; in तेजस् (*tejas*) there are air and space; in air, space is contained. In this way the five elements and their mixture (that is,) the plants and trees have been provided as food for living beings. Food of this kind is named अन्न (*anna*); therefore they call it (food) सर्वौषध (*sarvauṣadha*).

From food comes the origin of beings (living creatures). The creatures born grow and attain increase (become big) by food alone. It (food) is eaten, and it also eats the living beings; therefore it is named अन्न (*anna*). Here the last sentence (food is eaten and it eats the living beings) needs explanation. For the living beings that move about in the world, apart from the five elements such as water in their original form, all other food has arisen from living beings themselves. There is no food in the world other than food connected with living beings. Thus, the flesh-eating animals eat the plant-eating animals; the plant-eating animals eat plants. Since plants too have life (if a plant had no life, how could it grow?), the moving creatures that have life must live by eating one another. Because the plant kind does not belong to the moving class, plants take their food directly from the earth, or from the five elements, and grow. Therefore moving creatures cannot live without food connected with living beings or with plants. So "living beings eat food; food eats living beings" means that food arises from living beings themselves — so it has been said above. The chief point is that in the world the moving creatures (men included) must live by eating one another; for them life without food connected with living beings is not possible at all. This very idea is stated in the sentences अद्यतेऽत्ति च भूतानि । तस्मादन्नं तदुच्यते (*adyate 'tti ca bhūtāni | tasmādannaṃ taducyate*) (as printed here, with taducyate).

On worshipping food (one's meal) and regarding it with reverence there are also Śruti statements — *(the ra-subscript of tadvratam displaced in print (zoomed); the passage continues on the next page)*

> अन्नं न निंद्यात् । तद्व्रतं । प्राणो वा अन्नं । शरीरमन्नादं । प्राणे
> शरीरं प्रतिष्ठितं । शरीरे प्राणः प्रतिष्ठितः । तदेतदन्नमन्ने प्रतिष्ठितं ।

> *annaṃ na niṃdyāt | tadvrataṃ | prāṇo vā annaṃ | śarīramannādaṃ | prāṇe*
> *śarīraṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ | śarīre prāṇaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ | tadetadannamanne pratiṣṭhitaṃ |*

Food should not be reviled; one should regard that as a vow. Prāṇa itself is food. The body eats food and grows by it. The body is established in prāṇa; prāṇa is established in the body. Therefore prāṇa and body have a mutual relation. That these two are established in food means that the growth and protection of body and prāṇa come about through food alone. Without food neither body nor prāṇa can exist. He who knows that food is established in food (in the Supreme Brahman in the form of food) is honoured. He becomes rich in food and one who enjoys food. He becomes endowed with offspring (progeny and the like), with wealth of cattle, with brahma-splendour and with fame, and becomes eminent and honoured among men.

Do not despise food; regard doing so as a vow. Water itself is food; light (तेजस् (*tejas*)) eats food. Light is established in water; water is established in light. These two, light and water, are established in food. (In food there are heat and a water-portion.) He who knows that food is established in food (in the Supreme Brahman in the form of food) is honoured. He becomes rich in food and one who enjoys food. He becomes endowed with offspring (progeny and the like), with wealth of cattle, with brahma-splendour and with fame, and becomes eminent and honoured among men.

On the point that one should give food to guests and visitors and only then eat oneself there are also many Śruti authorities.

That is, the food (one's meal) that a miser who gives nothing to anyone acquires is in vain. No benefit comes to him from the food he acquires; it becomes the cause of his death (and harm). "This I say is true." The man who eats alone, not giving oblations and the like to deities such as Aryaman — that is, not offering food to the deities — and not satisfying with food a friend, or the guests and visitors who come to the house like a friend, is a great sinner: so it is said. And,

> न स सखा यो न ददाति सख्ये सचाभुवे सचमानाय पित्वः ।
> अपास्मात्प्रेयान्न तदोको अस्ति पृणंतमन्यमरणं चिदिच्छेत् ॥

> *na sa sakhā yo na dadāti sakhye sacābhuve sacamānāya pitvaḥ |*
> *apāsmātpreyānna tadoko asti pṛṇaṃtamanyamaraṇaṃ cidicchet ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ 10-117-4, zoomed; "Saṃ" without a stop as printed) (Gloss, mine and tentative: "He is no friend who does not give of his food to a friend, a companion who comes to him; let one turn away from him — that is no home — and seek another who gives, even a stranger.")

He who does not give food to a friend, to his companion, to one who is near him, is no friend at all. Therefore one should leave the house of such a man; that is not the only house. The house of generous men who give food surely exists; it is better to go there — so the ṛṣi has described. Therefore good householders should prepare food in the house a little more than suffices for themselves, for the hospitality of guests and visitors. On this matter —

Food should be made plentiful; one should regard doing so as a vow. The earth is food; space eats food. That is, the crops and the like that grow on the earth, and the grains and the like, are consumed in the form of oblations by the deities who dwell in the antarikṣa (svarga). Space is established in the earth; the earth is established in space. These two (earth and space) are established in food. That food is established in food (in Brahman in the form of food). He who knows that food is established in food lives with standing, that is, with honour. He becomes rich in food and one who enjoys food; and, endowed with progeny of sons, grandsons and so on, possessed of cattle, accompanied by brahma-splendour and fame, he obtains esteem among men. A *sāttvika* gift means this: when giving a gift one should not wish that some return favour may come to oneself later from the man who receives it. Without any wish for a return favour, *(continued on p. 183)*
### Printed p. 183 (PDF 201)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 6". Pīṭhike of Sūkta 187, continued.)*

… the gift given in the highest sense, after weighing place and time and worthiness and unworthiness of the recipient, is called a *sāttvika* gift. That is to say: in holy places such as tīrthas and sacred sites, on chief days such as saṅkrānti and the new-moon day, one should give food to a guest (*atithi*) or a visitor (*abhyāgata*) who comes invited or uninvited of his own accord. If that guest is accomplished in the study of the Vedas and śāstras, practises them, and is of good conduct, so much the better. Such a man one should honour with faith, attend on with respect and the like, and give him food. Giving food to any man afflicted by hunger is good; even more, when food is given to guests and visitors having the qualities said above, it not only becomes a *sāttvika* gift, but the giver thereby lives happily in later births endowed with plenty of food. That is what is explained here by the sentences एतद्वै मुखतोऽन्नग्ं राद्धं । मुखतोऽस्मा अन्नग्ं राध्यते । (*etadvai mukhato 'nnagṃ rāddhaṃ | mukhato 'smā annagṃ rādhyate |*). Now the manner of the second kinds, the *rājasa* and *tāmasa* gifts, is as follows —

*(Verse 1, line 2: "paṃkliṣṭaṃ" as printed, zoomed; parikliṣṭam expected. No reference printed for either verse.)* (Gloss, mine and tentative: "But what is given for the sake of a return, or again with a fruit in view, and grudgingly — that is declared rājasa. The gift given at the wrong place and time, to unworthy persons, without respect and with contempt — that is declared tāmasa.")

> यत्तु प्रत्युपकारार्थं फलमुद्दिश्य वा पुनः ।
> दीयते च पंक्लिष्टं तद्राजसमुदाहृतं ॥
> अदेशकाले यद्दानमपात्रेभ्यश्च दीयते ।
> असत्कृतमवज्ञातं तत्तामसमुदाहृतं ॥

> *yattu pratyupakārārthaṃ phalamuddiśya vā punaḥ |*
> *dīyate ca paṃkliṣṭaṃ tadrājasamudāhṛtaṃ ‖*
> *adeśakāle yaddānamapātrebhyaśca dīyate |*
> *asatkṛtamavajñātaṃ tattāmasamudāhṛtaṃ ‖*

The man who gives in expectation of a return — the gift he makes is called a *rājasa* gift. That is to say: the gift made with the thought "if I give food to this man today, tomorrow or some day later he too will honour me in the same way" is named *rājasa*. Such a gift is explained here by the sentences एतद्वै मध्यतोऽन्नग्ं राद्धं । मध्यतोऽस्मा अन्नग्ं राध्यते (*etadvai madhyato 'nnagṃ rāddhaṃ | madhyato 'smā annagṃ rādhyate*).

Besides this, the gift made merely for self-praise, without weighing place, time, and worthiness and unworthiness of the recipient, and without proper hospitality, is called *tāmasa*: that is, at a place where the mind fancies, i.e. in a censured place; at a time that is not the time, i.e. at an untimely hour such as midnight; to an unworthy person, i.e. to one who, not suffering from hunger, has already eaten to the throat and has no need of any food — the hospitality or gift made out of the pride that others should see one's hospitality to guests and admire it is called *adharma* (as printed). This is explained here by the sentences एतद्वा अंततोऽन्नग्ं राद्धं । अंततोऽस्माअन्नग्ं राध्यते । (*etadvā aṃtato 'nnagṃ rāddhaṃ | aṃtato 'smāannagṃ rādhyate |*). Therefore, knowing all these matters well, one should give food to a fit recipient at the proper time.

It is explained that, knowing food to be of the nature of the Supreme Brahman, with whatever attitude a man worships it, according to his attitude he obtains the fruit of it. That is to say —

### Printed p. 184 (PDF 202)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 187". Pīṭhike of Sūkta 187, concluded; Sūkta 187 begins.)*

तत्प्रतिष्ठेत्युपासीत । प्रतिष्ठावान्भवति । (*tatpratiṣṭhetyupāsīta | pratiṣṭhāvānbhavati |*) — If one worships it, regarding it as support (*pratiṣṭhā*), one becomes endowed with the means of comfort such as food and clothing and possessed of standing. He who worships it as splendour (*mahaḥ*) becomes prosperous with wealth and the like and, endowed with qualities of greatness, worthy of honour. He who worships it as *manaḥ* becomes endowed with the power of reflection. He who worships it as *namaḥ* (worthy of salutation) becomes one saluted by all and one who brings all under his control. To him all desires (*kāma*), that is, all his wishes, become subject, that is, are accomplished. He who worships it as *brahma* becomes one who knows the Vedas and the secrets of the truth of the Veda's meaning. For him who worships it as तद्ब्रह्मणः परिमर (*tadbrahmaṇaḥ parimara*), the enemies around him and the mental and bodily ills all perish. All enemies, haters and those who are disagreeable perish completely. He who is in this person and he who is in the sun is the same. He who has knowledge of this kind, departing from this world and passing beyond the states of the self called *annamaya*, *prāṇamaya*, *manomaya*, *vijñānamaya* and *ānandamaya*, becoming a Vidyādhara (that is, a deity having the power to assume whatever forms he wishes), enjoying his desires, wanders hither and thither singing these (following) Sāman-mantras. What a wonder is this! I am food; I am the eater of food; I am the maker of praise; I was born before truth (*ṛta*); before the gods I was born in the navel (the middle) of immortality.

Whoever offers (food) to me becomes like me. I am food. Him who eats food, I eat. I overcome this universe and this world. He who knows this becomes like golden light. In this way there are manifold descriptions of food, or of the deity presiding over food (Brahman). Many more mantras containing matters relating to food are in the Vedas in abundance; for fear of enlarging the book it is not possible to explain all of them here.

*(Rule ":o:" — end of the Pīṭhike.)*

## Sūkta 187 — *pituṃ nu* (Anuvāka 24, eighth Sūkta; 11 ṛks)

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; Anukramaṇikā wording and viniyoga. "Anu. 5-7" and "Ṛgvi. 1-27" zoomed.)*

> पितुं न्वित्येकादशर्चमष्टमं सूक्तमागस्त्यमन्नदेवताकं गायत्रं । आद्यानुष्टुब्गर्भोष्णिक् । आद्यः पंचकस्त्रयोऽष्टका अनुष्टुब्गर्भा । अनु. ५-७ । इत्युक्तत्वात् । तृतीया पंचमी षष्ठी सप्तम्येकादशी चेति पंचानुष्टुभः । तथा चानुक्रमणिका । पितुं न्वन्नस्तुतिर्गायत्रं त्वाद्यानुष्टुब्गर्भा तृतीयांत्ये पंचम्याद्याश्च तिस्रोऽनुष्टुभ इति ॥ विनियोगं शौनक आह । पितुं न्वित्युपतिष्ठेत नित्यमन्नमुपस्थितं । पूजयेदशनं नित्यं भुंजीत ह्यविकुत्सयन् ॥ नास्य स्यादन्नजो व्याधिर्विषमप्यमृतं भवेत् । विषं च पीत्वैतत्सूक्तं जपेद्विषविनाशनं ॥ नावाग्यतस्तु भुंजीत नाशुचिर्न जुगुप्सितं । दद्याच्च पूजयेच्चैव जुहुयाच्च हविस्तदा । क्षुद्भयं नास्य किंचित्स्यान्नान्नजं व्याधिमाप्नुयात् । ऋग्वि. १-२७ ॥ इति ॥

> *pituṃ nvityekādaśarcamaṣṭamaṃ sūktamāgastyamannadevatākaṃ gāyatraṃ | ādyānuṣṭubgarbhoṣṇik | ādyaḥ paṃcakastrayo 'ṣṭakā anuṣṭubgarbhā | anu. 5-7 | ityuktatvāt | tṛtīyā paṃcamī ṣaṣṭhī saptamyekādaśī ceti paṃcānuṣṭubhaḥ | tathā cānukramaṇikā | pituṃ nvannastutirgāyatraṃ tvādyānuṣṭubgarbhā tṛtīyāṃtye paṃcamyādyāśca tisro 'nuṣṭubha iti ‖ viniyogaṃ śaunaka āha | pituṃ nvityupatiṣṭheta nityamannamupasthitaṃ | pūjayedaśanaṃ nityaṃ bhuṃjīta hyavikutsayan ‖ nāsya syādannajo vyādhirviṣamapyamṛtaṃ bhavet | viṣaṃ ca pītvaitatsūktaṃ japedviṣavināśanaṃ ‖ nāvāgyatastu bhuṃjīta nāśucirna jugupsitaṃ | dadyācca pūjayeccaiva juhuyācca havistadā | kṣudbhayaṃ nāsya kiṃcitsyānnānnajaṃ vyādhimāpnuyāt | ṛgvi. 1-27 ‖ iti ‖*
### Printed p. 185 (PDF 203)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 6". Introduction of Sūkta 187, concluded.)*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta, *pituṃ nu*, is the eighth sūkta in the twenty-fourth anuvāka. There are eleven ṛks in it. Of this sūkta Agastya is the ṛṣi, the praise of food (*annastuti*) the devatā, and *gāyatrī* the metre. The first ṛk is of the metre called *anuṣṭubgarbhā uṣṇik*. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said आद्यः पंचकस्त्रयोऽष्टका अनुष्टुप्गर्भा (*ādyaḥ paṃcakastrayo 'ṣṭakā anuṣṭupgarbhā*) (Anu. 5-7). The third, fifth, sixth, seventh and eleventh ṛks of this sūkta are in the *anuṣṭubh* metre. And on this matter the Anukramaṇikā says पितुं न्वन्नस्तुतिर्गायत्रं त्वाद्यानुष्टुब्गर्भा तृतीयांत्ये पंचम्याद्याश्च तिस्रोऽनुष्टुभ इति (*pituṃ nvannastutirgāyatraṃ tvādyānuṣṭubgarbhā tṛtīyāṃtye paṃcamyādyāśca tisro 'nuṣṭubha iti*). On the application (*viniyoga*) of this sūkta Śaunaka has said thus in his work called the Ṛgvidhāna —

*(The verses of p. 184 repeated, in larger type; the reference numerals read from the larger type, unzoomed.)*

> पितुं न्वित्युपतिष्ठेत नित्यमन्नमुपस्थितं ।
> पूजयेदशनं नित्यं भुंजीत ह्यविकुत्सयन् ॥
> नास्य स्यादन्नजो व्याधिर्विषमप्यमृतं भवेत् ।
> विषं च पीत्वैतत्सूक्तं जपेद्विषविनाशनं ॥
> नावाग्यतस्तु भुंजीत नाशुचिर्न जुगुप्सितं ।
> दद्याच्च पूजयेच्चैव जुहुयाच्च हविस्तदा ॥
> क्षुद्भयं नास्य किंचित्स्यान्नान्नजं व्याधिमाप्नुयात् ॥

> *pituṃ nvityupatiṣṭheta nityamannamupasthitaṃ |*
> *pūjayedaśanaṃ nityaṃ bhuṃjīta hyavikutsayan ‖*
> *nāsya syādannajo vyādhirviṣamapyamṛtaṃ bhavet |*
> *viṣaṃ ca pītvaitatsūktaṃ japedviṣavināśanaṃ ‖*
> *nāvāgyatastu bhuṃjīta nāśucirna jugupsitaṃ |*
> *dadyācca pūjayeccaiva juhuyācca havistadā ‖*
> *kṣudbhayaṃ nāsya kiṃcitsyānnānnajaṃ vyādhimāpnuyāt ‖*

(Ṛgvidhāna 1-26)

One should daily, at meal-time, recite this sūkta *pituṃ na* (as printed) with devotion, worship the food, and then take the meal. One should never revile food. If one does so, the troubles such as illness that may arise from faults of diet do not occur. Even poison becomes nectar. For some other reason, that is, even if one has unknowingly eaten poison, if one recites this sūkta the poison is removed. While taking the meal one should eat with the mind not wandering, with restraint, and being pure. One should not eat food with disgust, or food the mind does not want, or food that is blameworthy. At meal-time one should give a small portion of the food to others, worship the food, offer the oblation as *homa* in the fire, and only then take one's own meal. To the man who does so there is no affliction arising from hunger; and no disease arising from eating unfit food befalls him: so they have explained the greatness of this sūkta.

*(Ornament at the foot of the page.)*

> यस्य । त्रितः । वि । ओजसा । वृत्रं । विऽपर्वं । अर्दयत् ॥ १ ॥

> अहमगस्त्यो नु क्षिप्रं पितुं पालकमन्नं स्तोषं । स्तौमि । महो महांतं धर्माणं सर्वस्य धारकं तविषीं बलात्मकं । यद्वा । महतो लोकस्य धारकं । यस्यान्नस्यौजसा बलेन सामर्थ्येन त्रितो विस्तीर्णतमः प्रख्यातकीर्तिस्त्रिषु क्षित्यादिस्थानेषु तायमानोऽपींद्रो वृत्रं विपर्वं विच्छिन्नसंधिकं यथा तथार्दयत् हिंसितवान् ॥

> *ahamagastyo nu kṣipraṃ pituṃ pālakamannaṃ stoṣaṃ | staumi | maho mahāṃtaṃ dharmāṇaṃ sarvasya dhārakaṃ taviṣīṃ balātmakaṃ | yadvā | mahato lokasya dhārakaṃ | yasyānnasyaujasā balena sāmarthyena trito vistīrṇatamaḥ prakhyātakīrtistriṣu kṣityādisthāneṣu tāyamāno 'pīṃdro vṛtraṃ viparvaṃ vicchinnasaṃdhikaṃ yathā tathārdayat hiṃsitavān ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** *yasya* — of which food; *ojasā* — by the power that gives consciousness; *tritaḥ* — Indra, whose fame is renowned in all three worlds; *vṛtram* — the asura Vṛtra; *viparvam* — (making him) one whose joints are cut; *vi ardayat* — completely slew; *tam* — that very … *(continued on p. 187)*
### Printed p. 187 (PDF 205)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 6". Ṛk 1, continued.)*

(and) | *mahaḥ* — which is great; *dharmāṇam* — which upholds all; [or: *mahaḥ* — of the great world; *dharmāṇam* — which is the upholder;] *taviṣīm* — which is of the nature of strength; *pitum* — which is the protector — that food; *nu* — quickly; *stoṣam* — I praise.

**Bhāvārtha.** I quickly praise the food by whose consciousness-giving power Indra, of fame renowned in all three worlds, cut up and destroyed the joints of the asura Vṛtra; which is also the upholder of the great world, of the nature of strength, and the protector.

**English Translation (as printed).**

I glorify Pitu, the great, the upholder, the strong, by whose invigorating power Trita slew the mutilated Vritra· [sic]

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**पितुं—पालकमन्नं (*pituṃ—pālakamannaṃ*)** — the meaning is: the food that protects us from the affliction of hunger. The word *pituḥ* is read among the twenty-eight names of food beginning with *andhaḥ*, *vājaḥ* (Ni. 2-9, as printed; zoomed). Besides this, Yāska —

*(Ni. 9-24 and Ni. 9-25 zoomed.)*

> पितुरित्यन्ननाम पातेर्वा, पिबतेर्वा, प्यायतेर्वा ।

> *piturityannanāma pātervā, pibatervā, pyāyatervā |*

(Ni. 9-24)

— has thus stated the etymology of the word *pitu*. That is: पातेर्वा (*pātervā*) — because it protects us from hunger, *pituḥ* means food. Or, because it is used for drinking, it has the name *pitu*. This applies also to food in liquid form (milk and the like). Therefore he has said that it is used for drinking and may be derived from the root *pā* (*pib*) — to drink, to take a drink; or प्यायतेर्वा (*pyāyatervā*) — that it may be derived also from the root *pyāyati*, which gives the sense "to satisfy". Taking as example this very ṛk in which the word is used, its etymology —

> पितुं नु स्तोषं महो धर्माणं तविषीं ।
> यस्य त्रितो व्योजसा वृत्रं विपर्वमर्दयत् ॥
> तं पितुं स्तौमि महतो धारयितारं बलस्य । तविषीति बलनाम तवतेर्वा वृद्धिकर्मणः । यस्य त्रित ओजसा बलेन त्रितस्त्रिस्थान इंद्रो वृत्रं विपर्वाणं व्यर्दयति ॥

> *pituṃ nu stoṣaṃ maho dharmāṇaṃ taviṣīṃ |*
> *yasya trito vyojasā vṛtraṃ viparvamardayat ‖*
> *taṃ pituṃ staumi mahato dhārayitāraṃ balasya | taviṣīti balanāma tavatervā vṛddhikarmaṇaḥ | yasya trita ojasā balena tritastristhāna iṃdro vṛtraṃ viparvāṇaṃ vyardayati ‖*

(Ni. 9-25) *(Ṛk 1 Special Topics continue on p. 188.)*

---

### Printed p. 188 (PDF 206)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 187". Ṛk 1, Special Topics continued.)*

— so he has stated, that is: I praise the food that gives great strength. The sense is that Indra, pervading the three worlds, having obtained the nourishment of this food and with its help become powerful, crushed all the joints and fastenings of the asura Vṛtra and destroyed him. The use of the word *pitu* (in the sense of food) is found in the ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-61-6, 1-132-6, 1-187-1, 6-20-4 and others, and also in places such as Atha. Ve. 4-6-3; Tai. Saṃ. 5-7-2-4, Vā. Saṃ. 2-20, 12-65, Ai. Brā. 1-13. *(Reference lines zoomed.)*

**महो धर्माणं—महांतं धर्माणं सर्वस्य धारकं । महतो लोकस्य धारकं (*maho dharmāṇaṃ—mahāṃtaṃ dharmāṇaṃ sarvasya dhārakaṃ | mahato lokasya dhārakaṃ*)** — Sāyaṇa's explanation is: that which upholds everything, that is, the great world and the beings of the world. Yāska has said महतो धारयितारं बलस्य (*mahato dhārayitāraṃ balasya*) — that which produces great strength. Since this is an attribute of the word *pitum*, and since food has the power of giving nourishment and strength to him who partakes of it, both kinds of meaning fit.

**तविषीं—तविषीति बलनाम (*taviṣīṃ—taviṣīti balanāma*)** — because the word *taviṣī* is read among the twenty-eight names of strength beginning with *ojaḥ*, *pājaḥ* (Ni. 3-9, as printed; zoomed). *Taviṣīm* means strength, power. That men and other beings alike obtain strength and vigour by partaking of food (nourishment) is a matter known to all. Or else the Niruktakāra, giving for the word *taviṣī* the derivation तवतेर्वा वृद्धिकर्मणः (*tavatervā vṛddhikarmaṇaḥ*), has explained that this word *taviṣīm* is formed from the root *tavati*, which has the sense "to cause growth", and that by partaking of nourishment (food) the body grows and increases.

**त्रितः (*tritaḥ*)** — for the word *tritaḥ* the Bhāṣyakāra has said विस्तीर्णतमः (*vistīrṇatamaḥ*), and the Niruktakāra त्रितस्तीर्णतमः (*tritastīrṇatamaḥ*) (Ni. 4-6, zoomed); that is, the sense is: pervading all the wide quarters. Besides this, the Niruktakāra in the etymology of this ṛk has explained त्रितस्त्रिस्थान इंद्रः (*tritastristhāna iṃdraḥ*). *Tristhāna* means Indra, who has unobstructed power in the three worlds, earth, mid-air and heaven. *Tritaḥ* also gives the meaning Trita Āptya. The relation between Trita Āptya and Indra, the meaning of the word *trita* and other matters connected with it we have explained at length in Ṛ. Saṃ. Bhāga 5, pages 230–231, in pages iii–viii of the Pīṭhike section of Ṛ. Saṃ. Bhāga 8, and in Ṛ. Saṃ. Bhāga 8, pages 443–447 *(zoomed)*. In the present ṛk *tritaḥ* means Indra, who has greatness in the three places, earth, mid-air and heaven.

**वृत्रं विपर्वमर्दयत् (*vṛtraṃ viparvamardayat*)** — among Indra's heroic deeds the slaying of Vṛtra is the most important. This matter —

> इंद्रस्य नु वीर्याणि प्र वोचं यानि चकार प्रथमानि वज्री ।

> *iṃdrasya nu vīryāṇi pra vocaṃ yāni cakāra prathamāni vajrī |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-32-1, zoomed)

### Printed p. 189 (PDF 207)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 6". Ṛk 1: Special Topics concluded; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā; end of Ṛk 1.)*

— is described in various ways in the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-32, which begins thus, and in many other places as well. For this very reason the name *vṛtrahā* — the slayer of Vṛtra — is renowned for Indra. That Indra slew Vṛtra by his own power is said in ṛks such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-165-8; 7-21-6, 10-138-6. And there are descriptions such as: for the fight with Vṛtra the gods increased his valour (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-113-8), or gathered strength and power for him (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-80-5, 6-20-2, 10-48-3, 10-120-3), or placed the weapon *vajra* in his hand (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-20-8). Very often the Marut-deities themselves are those who urge him on and who support him (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-32-4, 10-73-1 and others); when the other gods all ran away in fear of Vṛtra (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-85-7 (as printed), 4-18-11, Ai. Brā. 1-20), the Marut-deities alone helped Indra. But it is also said that the Maruts themselves once abandoned him (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-7-31). Descriptions such as that Agni, Soma and Viṣṇu were helpers of Indra when he fought with Vṛtra are found here and there. In the Purāṇas such as the Bhāgavata there is an extensive legend about the slaying of the asura Vṛtra. *(All references on this page zoomed.)*

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** पितुम् (*pitum*) — root पा पाने (*pā pāne*); suffix *tu* by the sūtra printed पः किच्च (*paḥ kicca*) (U. Sū. 1-[?]0; middle digit 2 or 7, undecided); because it is *kit*, *i* for the root's *ā*; end-acute by the suffix accent. स्तोषम् (*stoṣam*) — root ष्टुञ् स्तुतौ (*ṣṭuñ stutau*); luṅ by Vedic usage, first person singular; no augment *aṭ* (Vedic); tiṅanta nighāta accent. धर्माणम् (*dharmāṇam*) — root धृञ् धारणे (*dhṛñ dhāraṇe*); suffix मनिन् (*manin*) by अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्ते (*anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-75, zoomed); initial acute of the suffix by *vyatyaya*. विपर्वम् (*viparvam*) — विगतः पर्वः यस्मात् सः (*vigataḥ parvaḥ yasmāt saḥ*), accusative; by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā*) (no number printed) the first member keeps its own accent. अर्दयत् (*ardayat*) — root अर्द हिंसायाम् (*arda hiṃsāyām*), curādi; luṅ (as printed), third person singular *tip*, loss of *i*; *ṇic* in its own sense by सत्यापपाश (*satyāpapāśa*)— (Pā. Sū. 3-1-25, zoomed); guṇa of the root before *ṇic* because of the *śap* vikaraṇa, *ay* substitute; no augment *aṭ* (Vedic); because of the connection with the word *yat* there is no nighāta, the *ṇic* accent remains.

*(A short rule: end of Ṛk 1.)*

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 187".)*

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स्वादो पितो मधो पितो वयं त्वा ववृमहे ।
> अस्माकमविता भव ॥ २ ॥

> *svādo pito madho pito vayaṃ tvā vavṛmahe |*
> *asmākamavitā bhava ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> स्वादो इति । पितो इति । मधो इति । पितो इति । वयं । त्वा । ववृमहे ।
> अस्माकं । अविता । भव ॥ २ ॥

> *svādo iti | pito iti | madho iti | pito iti | vayaṃ | tvā | vavṛmahe |*
> *asmākaṃ | avitā | bhava ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; two places zoomed.)*

> हे स्वादो आस्वादनीय पितो पालक मधो माधुर्योपेत पितो हे पानसाधनान्न वयं त्वा त्वां ववृमहे । सेवामहे ॥ अत्र सर्वत्रन[?]नुदात्तानां पूर्वस्या सामान्यवचनत्वेनानिघातत्वं । अनुदात्तानां तु विशेषवचनत्वान्निघातत्वं ॥ असकृत्पितुशब्दश्रवणं तस्य प्राशस्त्यज्ञापनार्थं । हे पितो अस्माकमविता तर्पयिता भव ॥

> *he svādo āsvādanīya pito pālaka madho mādhuryopeta pito he pānasādhanānna vayaṃ tvā tvāṃ vavṛmahe | sevāmahe ‖ atra sarvatrana[?]nudāttānāṃ pūrvasyā sāmānyavacanatvenānighātatvaṃ | anudāttānāṃ tu viśeṣavacanatvānnighātatvaṃ ‖ asakṛtpituśabdaśravaṇaṃ tasya prāśastyajñāpanārthaṃ | he pito asmākamavitā tarpayitā bhava ‖*

*Gist:* The repeated vocative *pito* shows the excellence of food; the accent remark explains which of the vocatives are unaccented (nighāta).

**Pratipadārtha.** *svādo* — which is tasty; *pito* — which is the protector; *madho* — which is endowed with sweetness; *pito* — O food, which is also the means of drinking; *vayam* — we; *tvā* — you; *vavṛmahe* — partake of (serve); *asmākam* — to us; *avitā* — as protector (as giver of satisfaction); *bhava* — be.

**Bhāvārtha.** O food, worthy to be relished, protecting, endowed with sweetness, and the means of drinking, we partake of you. Be the giver of satisfaction to us.

**English Translation (as printed).**

Savoury Pitu ; sweet Pitu ; we worship you : become our protector· [sic]

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**स्वादो पितो मधो पितो (*svādo pito madho pito*)** — *svādu* means that which is tasty, which is wholesome for eating. That here *pito* is addressed twice indicates the great regard of the praiser for food and its excellence.

**अविता—तर्पयिता (*avitā—tarpayitā*)** — the Bhāṣyakāra's explanation is: that which produces satisfaction. *Avitā* may also mean रक्षकः (*rakṣakaḥ*) — he who protects by removing the affliction of hunger.

### Printed p. 191 (PDF 209)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 6". Ṛk 2: Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā; end of Ṛk 2. Ṛk 3: Saṃhitā, Pada, bhāṣya begun.)*

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** स्वादो (*svādo*) — being at the beginning of the pāda it does not take the āmantrita-nighāta accent; initial acute by आमन्त्रितस्य च (*āmantritasya ca*) (printed "āmantritasya—"; Pā. Sū. 6-1-198, zoomed). ववृमहे (*vavṛmahe*) — root वृञ् वरणे (*vṛñ varaṇe*); laṭ, first person plural, suffix *mahiṅ*; *e* for the *ṭi* by टित आत्मनेपदानां टेरे (*ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭere*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-79, zoomed); *ślu* vikaraṇa by बहुलं छन्दसि (*bahulaṃ chandasi*) (no number printed), hence reduplication etc.; nighāta accent because it follows a non-tiṅanta word. अविता (*avitā*) — root अव रक्षणे (*ava rakṣaṇe*); suffix तृच् (*tṛc*) in the agent sense; end-acute by चितः (*citaḥ*) (no number printed). पितो (*pito*) — a vocative form. Since a vocative precedes it here, it would become as if non-existent by आमन्त्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवत् (*āmantritaṃ pūrvamavidyamānavat*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-72, zoomed) (and having no word before it, would not take the nighāta accent); but by नामन्त्रिते समानाधिकरणे सामान्यवचनम् (*nāmantrite samānādhikaraṇe sāmānyavacanam*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-69 as printed; zoomed) it is not treated as non-existent: this (*pito*) being the qualified word and *svādo* the general term (the qualifier), in such instances the preceding general term is not treated as absent; hence the āmantrita-nighāta accent comes on the qualified word. So also is it to be understood in the following attributes.

*(A short rule: end of Ṛk 2.)*

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> उप नः पितवा चर शिवः शिवाभिरूतिभिः ।
> मयोभुरद्विषेण्यः सखा सुशेवो अद्वयाः ॥ ३ ॥

> *upa naḥ pitavā cara śivaḥ śivābhirūtibhiḥ |*
> *mayobhuradviṣeṇyaḥ sakhā suśevo advayāḥ ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उप । नः । पितो इति । आ । चर । शिवः । शिवाभिः । ऊतिऽभिः ।
> मयःऽभुः । अद्विषेण्यः । सखा । सुऽशेवः । अद्वयाः ॥ ३ ॥

> *upa | naḥ | pito iti | ā | cara | śivaḥ | śivābhiḥ | ūti 'bhiḥ |*
> *mayaḥ 'bhuḥ | adviṣeṇyaḥ | sakhā | su 'śevaḥ | advayāḥ ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; headed "Vyākaraṇaprakriyā" in the print by a misprint; continues on p. 192.)*

> हे पितो यतस्त्वं शिवो मंगलः अतः शिवाभिर्मंगलयुक्ताभिरूतिभी रक्षणैर्नोऽस्माना चर । आगच्छ । आगत्य च मयोभुः सुखस्य भावयिताद्विषेण्योऽद्वेष्य-

> *he pito yatastvaṃ śivo maṃgalaḥ ataḥ śivābhirmaṃgalayuktābhirūtibhī rakṣaṇairno 'smānā cara | āgaccha | āgatya ca mayobhuḥ sukhasya bhāvayitādviṣeṇyo 'dveṣya-*

### Printed p. 192 (PDF 210)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 187". Ṛk 3, continued.)*

> रसः । प्रियरस इत्यर्थः । सखा सखिवत्प्रियकारी सुशेवोऽत एव सुष्ठु सुखकरोऽद्वया द्वयरहित उक्तगुण एव न तु तद्विपरीतो भवेत्यर्थः । अथवा दृष्टांतवादोऽयं । सुशेवोऽद्वया मनःकर्मविसंवादरहितः सखा यथा मयोभुरद्वेष्यश्च भवति तद्वत्त्वमपि भवेत्यर्थः ॥

> *rasaḥ | priyarasa ityarthaḥ | sakhā sakhivatpriyakārī suśevo 'ta eva suṣṭhu sukhakaro 'dvayā dvayarahita uktaguṇa eva na tu tadviparīto bhavetyarthaḥ | athavā dṛṣṭāṃtavādo 'yaṃ | suśevo 'dvayā manaḥkarmavisaṃvādarahitaḥ sakhā yathā mayobhuradveṣyaśca bhavati tadvattvamapi bhavetyarthaḥ ‖*

*Gist:* Come with auspicious protections, delightful, of pleasing taste, friendly, without duality (only of the stated qualities); or, be like a friend free of discord between mind and act.

**Pratipadārtha.** *pito* — O protecting food; *śivaḥ* — you, who are auspicious; *śivābhiḥ* — auspicious; *ūtibhiḥ* — with protections; *naḥ upa* — to our presence; *ā cara* — come; *suśevaḥ* — worthy to be honoured excellently; *advayāḥ* — having brought about unity of mind and deed; *sakhā* — a friend; *mayobhuḥ* — producing happiness; *adviṣeṇyaḥ* — and free of hatred, be. [Or: *mayobhuḥ* — causing delight; *adviṣeṇyaḥ* — being free of unpleasant taste (having pleasing taste); *sakhā* — producing what is dear, like a friend; *suśevaḥ* — (for that very reason) worthy to be partaken of; *advayāḥ* — having no quality other than the venerable and acceptable ones (be).]

**Bhāvārtha.** O auspicious food, come to our presence with your auspicious protections. Be the giver of delight to the sacrificers, free of unpleasant taste and of pleasing taste, producing what is dear like a friend, and for that very reason venerable and worthy to be partaken of.

**English Translation (as printed).**

Come to us, Pitu, auspicious with auspicious aids ; a source of delight not unpalatable, a friend well respected, and having none (bnt [sic] agreeable properties)·

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**शिवः, शिवाभिः, सुशेवः (*śivaḥ, śivābhiḥ, suśevaḥ*)** — since the word *śivaḥ* is mentioned among the twenty names of happiness (*sukha*) (Ni. 3-13, as printed; zoomed), *śivaḥ* means happiness. The Bhāṣyakāra has explained the meaning as auspicious. Yāska —

> अमीवहा वास्तोष्पते विश्वा रूपाण्याविशन् । सखा सुशेव एधि नः ।

> *amīvahā vāstoṣpate viśvā rūpāṇyāviśan | sakhā suśeva edhi naḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-55-1, zoomed)

— in the etymology of this ṛk, explaining the meaning of the word *śeva*, says ('śiṣyaternakāro' as printed, zoomed; the passage continues on p. 193.):

> शेव इति सुखनाम । शिष्यतेर्नकारो नामकरणोऽन्तस्थांतरोपलिंगी । विभाषितगुण शिवमित्यस्य भवति ।

> *śeva iti sukhanāma | śiṣyaternakāro nāmakaraṇo 'ntasthāṃtaropaliṃgī | vibhāṣitaguṇa śivamityasya bhavati |*

### Printed p. 193 (PDF 211)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 6". Ṛk 3: Special Topics concluded; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā begun.)*

(Ni. 10-17, zoomed) — giving for the word *śeva* the meaning "happiness", he has shown that the word *śiva* too has the same meaning. In the lexicons and the like the word *śiva* has the meaning "auspicious". There is nothing against saying that all that produces happiness is auspicious. Therefore in the present ṛk both meanings, "producing happiness" and "auspicious", are fitting.

**मयोभुः (*mayobhuḥ*)** — since the word *mayaḥ* too is mentioned among the twenty names of happiness beginning with *śiṃbātā*, *śatarā* (no reference printed), *mayaḥ* means happiness. That which produces happiness is named *mayobhuḥ*. The use of the word *mayobhuḥ* in the sense "producing happiness" is frequent in the Ṛgveda and in the other Vedas.

**अद्विषेण्यः—अद्वेष्यरसः (*adviṣeṇyaḥ—adveṣyarasaḥ*)** — the meaning is: having a taste (relish) that does not produce aversion, or that is wholesome. The sense is: that which is both dear and tasty.

**सखा—सखिवत्प्रियकारी (*sakhā—sakhivatpriyakārī*)** — that which does what is dear, like a friend. The sense is: since a friend always seeks only one's good and does what is dear, food too, being desired by all, produces good. Here the ṛṣi, out of great love for food, has addressed it with the affectionate word *sakhā*, friend.

**अद्वयाः—द्वयरहितः उक्तगुण एव न तु तद्विपरीतो भवेत्यर्थः (*advayāḥ—dvayarahitaḥ uktaguṇa eva na tu tadviparīto bhavetyarthaḥ*)** — the Bhāṣyakāra has explained it in one way as: having no quality other than the venerable and acceptable ones; and in another way as अद्वयाः मनःकर्मविसंवादरहितः (*advayāḥ manaḥkarmavisaṃvādarahitaḥ*) — without being one way in the mind and another way in deed and so on, producing good wholeheartedly. In worldly dealings it is not impossible to see those who pose as friends speaking only words of good with the mouth, while in their conduct doing harm contrary to them. Therefore the food is praised as one whose nature is not to act in that way, but to be the same in both mind and deed and to produce good.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar page, noted briefly).** चर (*cara*) — root चर गतिभक्षणयोः (*cara gatibhakṣaṇayoḥ*); loṭ, second person singular; tiṅanta nighāta accent. शिवः (*śivaḥ*) — शेते अस्मिन् सर्वमिति शिवः (*śete asmin sarvamiti śivaḥ*), root शीङ् स्वप्ने (*śīṅ svapne*); formed irregularly (*nipātita*) with the suffix *va* by सर्वनिघृष्वरिष्वलष्वशिव (*sarvanighṛṣvariṣvalaṣvaśiva*)— (U. Sū. 1-151, zoomed). अद्विषेण्यः (*adviṣeṇyaḥ*) — root द्विष अप्रीतौ (*dviṣa aprītau*); Uṇādi suffix *eṇya*; *nañ* as first member; in the bahuvrīhi the second member is end-acute by नञ्सुभ्याम् (*nañsubhyām*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172, zoomed).

*(Footer: signature "[13]", "Vol. 14". The grammar of Ṛk 3 may continue on p. 194.)*
