### Printed p. 288 (PDF 307)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 1…" — the scan of this page cuts off the right edge of the text block: the Sūkta numeral of the header and one to three characters at the end of most lines are lost; lost text is marked […] and not supplied. Ṛk 5: Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics.)*

**Bhāvārtha.** O mighty Agni, do not abandon us and make us subject to the enemy[…] who is injurious, gluttonous and causes sorrow. Likewise do not let us be caught by those that, having teeth and the like, bite[…] (and) by creatures that, without teeth, injure with horns and the like. Do not make us objects of defeat[…] and disgrace.

**English Translation (as printed).**

Abandon us not, Agni, to a wicked, voracious, malevolent fo[…] (abandon us) not to one who has fangs, and who bites ; nor to one witho[…] teeth ; nor to the malignant ; nor give us up, powerful Agni, to disgrace· [sic]

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**अघाय (*aghāya*)** — हिंसकाय (*hiṃsakāya*) | The word *agha*, formed when the upasarga आङ् (*āṅ*) [is joined …] to the root हन हिंसागत्योः (*hana hiṃsāgatyoḥ*), has the meaning "one who injures, a wicked person". The word रिषते (*riṣate*) too has the same meaning. […] By the words अघाय, अविष्यवे रिपवे (*aghāya, aviṣyave ripave*) and so on, standing in the dative singular, [it is said] "do not [make us] subject (*vaśa*[…]) to the injurer", that is, it is prayed that he should save us from falling into the hands of the injurer.

**अविष्यवे (*aviṣyave*)** — अविष्यतिरत्तिकर्मा । अत्तेच्छवे (*aviṣyatirattikarmā | attecchave*) | to the one who eats excessively, that is, to r[…]sas and the like *(the middle of the word is cut off; rākṣasas presumably)*.

**दुच्छुनायै (*ducchunāyai*)** — since the word *śuna* is read among the twenty names of happiness (Ni. 3-13, as printed; zoomed), ś[…] means happiness. दुष्टसुखकारिणे दुःखकारिण इत्यर्थः (*duṣṭasukhakāriṇe duḥkhakāriṇa ityarthaḥ*) | The intention is: one who drives away[…] such happiness and brings about sorrow.

**दत्वते (*datvate*)** — दंतवते (*daṃtavate*) — wicked creatures that have teeth. These bite men with their sharp[…] teeth.

**दशते (*daśate*)** — serpents and the like that bite with poisonous teeth. Even if the teeth of poisonous creatures are not frightful[…], when they bite the poison enters the body and brings about death; therefore serpents and the like are dangerous.

**अदते (*adate*)** — wicked creatures without teeth; that is, though for some creatures the teeth are not frightful[…], they do harm to men with their horns, hooves and the like: the wild buffalo, the bull and the like with their horns, and the donkey, the horse and the like with their le[…] (legs), cause harm to people. It is prayed that [he] should pro[…] us from such various wicked creatures *(no closing stop printed)*.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, noted briefly).** सृजः (*sṛjaḥ*) — root printed स्रज विसर्गे (*sraja visarge*) (as it looks; zoomed), tudādi; with *māṅ* as upapada, *luṅ* second person singular; because of the connection with *māṅ*, no augment *aṭ*; standing after a non-verb, nighāta. अविष्यवे (*aviṣyave*) — by सनाशंसभिक्ष उः (*sanāśaṃsabhikṣa uḥ*) suffix *u* after the desiderative *aviṣya*; elision of the preceding *a* by अतो लोपः (*ato lopaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-48, zoomed); end-acute by the suffix accent; dative singular. दुच्छुनायै (*ducchunāyai*) — दुष्टं शुनं यस्य सः (*duṣṭaṃ śunaṃ yasya saḥ*); change of gender by *vyatyaya*; by परादिश्छंदसि बहुलम् (*parādiśchaṃdasi bahulam*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-199, zoomed) the latter member is initial-acute. दत्वते (*datvate*) — दंताः अस्य संति इति तद्वान् (*daṃtāḥ asya saṃti iti tadvān*); *dat* for *danta*; by the dictum स्वरविधौ व्यंजनमविद्यमानवत् (*svaravidhau vyaṃjanamavidyamānavat*) the intervening *t* counts as absent, so by ह्रस्वनुड्भ्यां मतुप् (*hrasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-176, zoomed) the *matup* is udātta; dative singular. दशते (*daśate*) — root दंश दशने (*daṃśa daśane*); *śatṛ* for *laṭ*, vikaraṇa *śap*; elision of the penultimate nasal by दंशसंजस्वंजां शपि (*daṃśasaṃjasvaṃjāṃ śapi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-25, zoomed); by तास्यनुदात्तेत्— (*tāsyanudāttet—*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186, zoomed) the *lasārvadhātuka* is anudātta, so the root accent remains. रिषते (*riṣate*) — root रिष हिंसायां (*riṣa hiṃsāyāṃ*); *śatṛ* for *laṭ*; by the dictum संज्ञापूर्वको विधिरनित्यः (*saṃjñāpūrvako vidhiranityaḥ*) no laghūpadha guṇa; root accent as before. दाः (*dāḥ*) — root डुदाञ् दाने (*ḍudāñ dāne*); with *māṅ*, *luṅ* second person singular; no augment *aṭ* because of *māṅ*; nighāta of the verb.

*(A short rule closes Ṛk 5.)*

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(In the first line a printed word before "varūthaṃ" is struck through and illegible [?]; a handwritten correction above it reads "tanve", which is transcribed here. The Pada (next page) is not yet viewed.)*

> वि घ त्वावाँ ऋतजात यंसद्गृणानो अग्ने तन्वे वरूथं ।
> विश्वाद्रिरिक्षोरुत वा निनित्सोरभिह्रुतामसि हि देव विष्पट् ॥ ६ ॥

> *vi gha tvāvā~ ṛtajāta yaṃsadgṛṇāno agne tanve varūthaṃ |*
> *viśvādririkṣoruta vā ninitsorabhihrutāmasi hi deva viṣpaṭ ‖ 6 ‖*

### Printed p. 290 (PDF 309)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 189". Ṛk 6: Pada, bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English.)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥** *(The Pada prints "tanve" in type, with no correction: it agrees with the handwritten correction in the Saṃhitā on p. 289.)*

> वि । घ । त्वाऽवान् । ऋतऽजात । यंसत् । गृणानः । अग्ने । तन्वे । वरूथं ।
> विश्वात् । रिरिक्षोः । उत । वा । निनित्सोः । अभिऽह्रुतां । असि । हि । देव । विष्पट् ॥ ६ ॥

> *vi | gha | tvā 'vān | ṛta 'jāta | yaṃsat | gṛṇānaḥ | agne | tanve | varūthaṃ |*
> *viśvāt | ririkṣoḥ | uta | vā | ninitsoḥ | abhi 'hrutāṃ | asi | hi | deva | viṣpaṭ ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed.)*

> हे ऋतजात यज्ञार्थमुत्पन्नाग्ने वरूथं वरणीयं त्वां तन्वे शरीरपोषाय गृणानः स्तुवंस्त्वावांस्त्वया देवतया तद्वाञ्जनो वि घ यंसत् । विमुंचति खल्वात्मानं । कस्मात्सकाशात् । रिरिक्षोर्हिंसितुमिच्छोश्चोरादेः सकाशात् । उत वाथवा निनित्सोर्निंदितुमिच्छतः । हे देव अभिह्रुतामाभिमुख्येन कुटिलं कुर्वतां द्विषां विष्पड्विशेषेण बाधकोऽसि हि । अतस्त्वदनुग्रहादयं जनो वि यंसत् ॥

> *he ṛtajāta yajñārthamutpannāgne varūthaṃ varaṇīyaṃ tvāṃ tanve śarīrapoṣāya gṛṇānaḥ stuvaṃstvāvāṃstvayā devatayā tadvāñjano vi gha yaṃsat | vimuṃcati khalvātmānaṃ | kasmātsakāśāt | ririkṣorhiṃsitumicchoścorādeḥ sakāśāt | uta vāthavā ninitsorniṃditumicchataḥ | he deva abhihrutāmābhimukhyena kuṭilaṃ kurvatāṃ dviṣāṃ viṣpaḍviśeṣeṇa bādhako 'si hi | atastvadanugrahādayaṃ jano vi yaṃsat ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** ऋतजात (*ṛtajāta*) — born for the sake of the sacrifice; अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; वरूथं (*varūthaṃ*) — you, who are greatly desired; तन्वे (*tanve*) — for the nourishment of his own body; गृणानः (*gṛṇānaḥ*) — the sacrificer, praising (you) and having a body grown great just like you who are of divine nature *(so the gloss, which takes in the sense of त्वावान् (*tvāvān*))*; रिरिक्षोः (*ririkṣoḥ*) — from thieves and the like who injure; उत वा (*uta vā*) — or else (otherwise); निनित्सोः (*ninitsoḥ*) — from the enemy who reviles; वि घ यंसत् (*vi gha yaṃsat*) — frees himself (is not caught in their violence); देव (*deva*) — O shining Agni, (you); अभिह्रुतां (*abhihrutāṃ*) — to deceitful enemies; विष्पट् (*viṣpaṭ*) — as one who causes injury; असि हि (*asi hi*) — are you not?

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni born for the sake of the sacrifice, the sacrificer who praises you, greatly desired, for the nourishment of his own body, and who has a body grown great just like you who are of divine nature, frees himself from thieves and the like who injure and from the enemy who reviles; and he is not caught in his violence. O shining Agni, to deceitful enemies you are the cause of injury.

**English Translation (as printed).**

Agni, born for sacrifice, (a man) praising you, who are excellent, for (the sake of cherishing) his body, becomes such as you are exempts himself from all who are inclined to harm or revile him ; for you, Agni, are the especial adversary of those who do wrong.

### Printed p. 291 (PDF 310)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 11". Ṛk 6: Special Topics; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā begins.)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**ऋतजात (*ṛtajāta*)** — The word *ṛta* has many meanings. Here the commentator has taken it to mean "sacrifice" and explained that Agni is addressed as one born for the sake of that sacrifice.

**वरूथं (*varūthaṃ*)** — Since the word *varūtha* is read among the names of house (Ni. 3-13, as printed; zoomed), the word means "house". But this word, formed from the root वृञ्-वरणे (*svādi*, *ubhayapadī*) *(so printed)*, gives the meaning वरणीयं (*varaṇīyaṃ*), "desired by all". In this sense it is used here as an epithet of Agni (त्वां (*tvāṃ*)).

**रिरिक्षोः (*ririkṣoḥ*)** — हिंसितुमिच्छोश्चोरादेः सकाशात् (*hiṃsitumicchoścorādeḥ sakāśāt*) | The intention is: from wicked people such as thieves who wish to do injury.

**निनित्सोः (*ninitsoḥ*)** — from hostile people who have the wish to revile.

**अभिह्रुतां (*abhihrutāṃ*)** — the intention is: wicked people who strive to deceive, chiefly by other means.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, noted briefly; continues on p. 292).** त्वावान् (*tvāvān*) — the word *yuṣmad*; with the suffix *matup*, *ā* for the *d* by आ सर्वनाम्नः (*ā sarvanāmnaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-91, zoomed); *tva*-substitution up to the *ma* by प्रत्ययोत्तरपदयोश्च (*pratyayottarapadayośca*) (Pā. Sū. 8-3-3, as printed; zoomed); lengthening; *matup* being *pit* is anudātta, so the stem accent remains; *ru* for the *n* by दीर्घादटि समानपादे (*dīrghādaṭi samānapāde*), and nasalization of the preceding *ā* by आतोऽटि नित्यम् (*āto 'ṭi nityam*). यंसत् (*yaṃsat*) — root यमु उपरमे (*yamu uparame*); *leṭ* third person singular *tip*; final *i* elided by इतश्च लोपः (*itaśca lopaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-97, zoomed); augment *aṭ* by लेटोऽडाटौ (*leṭo 'ḍāṭau*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-94, zoomed); *sip* by सिब्बहुलं लेटि (*sibbahulaṃ leṭi*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-34, zoomed); anusvāra for the root's *m* before *s*; nighāta of the verb. वरूथम् (*varūtham*) — root वृञ् वरणे (*vṛñ varaṇe*); suffix *ūthan* by जॄवृञ्भ्यामूथन् (*jṝvṛñbhyāmūthan*) (U. Sū. 2-163, as printed; zoomed); guṇa of the *ṛ* with *r* by सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः (*sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ*); the suffix being *nit*, initial-acute by ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ñnityādirnityam*). रिरिक्षोः (*ririkṣoḥ*) — रिरिक्षतीति रिरिक्षुः (*ririkṣatīti ririkṣuḥ*); root रिष हिंसायाम् (*riṣa hiṃsāyām*); *san* in the desiderative sense by धातोः कर्मणः समान— (*dhātoḥ karmaṇaḥ samāna—*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-7, zoomed); reduplication and the rest because of *san*; सनाशंसभिक्ष उः (*sanāśaṃsabhikṣa uḥ*) … *(continues on p. 292)*

Sū. 6-1-71, zoomed); the kṛt-final latter member keeps its own accent; genitive plural.

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(The Ṛk numeral stands at the head of the next strip of the page.)*

> त्वं ताँ अग्न उभयान्वि विद्वान्वेषि प्रपित्वे मनुषो यजत्र ।
> अभिपित्वे मनवे शास्यो भूर्मर्मृजेन्य उशिग्भिर्नाक्रः ॥ ७ ॥

> *tvaṃ tā~ agna ubhayānvi vidvānveṣi prapitve manuṣo yajatra |*
> *abhipitve manave śāsyo bhūrmarmṛjenya uśigbhirnākraḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वं । तान् । अग्ने । उभयान् । वि । विद्वान् । वेषि । प्रऽपित्वे । मनुषः । यजत्र ।
> अभिऽपित्वे । मनवे । शास्यः । भूः । मर्मृजेन्यः । उशिक्ऽभिः । न । अक्रः ॥ ७ ॥

> *tvaṃ | tān | agne | ubhayān | vi | vidvān | veṣi | pra 'pitve | manuṣaḥ | yajatra |*
> *abhi 'pitve | manave | śāsyaḥ | bhūḥ | marmṛjenyaḥ | uśik 'bhiḥ | na | akraḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; "sannihita eva" zoomed: the top stroke of the *ta* could be an *e*-sign, "sannihite".)*

*Gist:* Agni, distinguishing sacrificers from non-sacrificers, desires the sacrificers at the time at hand; *manave* is genitive in sense; be instructible by the sacrificer at his sacrifice, purifying (him), as by the willing priests.

> हे यजत्र यष्टव्याग्ने त्वं तान्यष्टॄनयष्टॄंश्चोभयान्मनुषो मनुष्यान्विविच्य विद्वाञ्जानन् प्रपित्वे सन्निहित एव काले वेषि । कामयसे यष्टॄन् । तथा कुर्वन्नक्र आक्रमिता त्वं मनवे । षष्ठ्यर्थे चतुर्थी । मनुष्यस्य यजमानस्याभिपित्वेऽभिप्राप्तकालेऽभिगमनवति यज्ञे वा शास्यो भूः । शिक्षणीयो भव । इदं कुर्विदं कुर्विति विधेयो भव । मर्मृजेन्यः शोधयिता यजमान उशिग्भिः कामयमानैर्ऋत्विग्भिरिव ॥

> *he yajatra yaṣṭavyāgne tvaṃ tānyaṣṭṝnayaṣṭṝṃścobhayānmanuṣo manuṣyānvivicya vidvāñjānan prapitve sannihita eva kāle veṣi | kāmayase yaṣṭṝn | tathā kurvannakra ākramitā tvaṃ manave | ṣaṣṭhyarthe caturthī | manuṣyasya yajamānasyābhipitve 'bhiprāptakāle 'bhigamanavati yajñe vā śāsyo bhūḥ | śikṣaṇīyo bhava | idaṃ kurvidaṃ kurviti vidheyo bhava | marmṛjenyaḥ śodhayitā yajamāna uśigbhiḥ kāmayamānairṛtvigbhiriva ‖*

**Pratipadārtha** *(continues on p. 293)*. यजत्र (*yajatra*) — worthy of sacrifice; अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; तान् उभयान् (*tān ubhayān*) — of both kinds, those who perform sacrifice and those who do not; मनुषः (*manuṣaḥ*) — men; विद्वान् (*vidvān*) — knowing (them); प्रपित्वे (*prapitve*) — at the time of sacrifice that is at hand; वेषि (*veṣi*) — (you) desire only the performers of sacrifice …

### Printed p. 293 (PDF 312)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 11". Ṛk 7: Pratipadārtha concluded, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics.)*

… (you) desire; (then) अक्रः (*akraḥ*) — you, who pervade; मनवे (*manave*) — for the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice; अभिपित्वे (*abhipitve*) — in the sacrifice that is being accomplished at once *(an ink blot stands between two words of this line)*; मर्मृजेन्यः (*marmṛjenyaḥ*) — the purifying sacrificer; उशिग्भिः न (*uśigbhiḥ na*) — like (one who) knows the enjoined acts according to the wishes of the priests; शास्यः भूः (*śāsyaḥ bhūḥ*) — become one who makes known "do this, leave this".

**Bhāvārtha.** O Agni worthy of sacrifice, distinguishing and knowing men of two kinds, those who perform sacrifice and those who do not, you desire only the performers of sacrifice at the time of sacrifice that is at hand. Then, you who pervade the whole sacrificial ground, be a teacher who makes known the injunctions "do this, leave this", so that the sacrificer performing the sacrifice is instructed by the priests, you too along with them.

**English Translation (as printed).**

Adorable Agni, you are sagacious, and in a short time discriminate between both those men (who do and do not ·worship you) ; approach the worshipper at the proper time, and be compliant (with his wishes), like an institutor of the rite, (who is directed) by the desires (of the priests)· [sic: stray mark before "worship" and raised point at the end]

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**उभयान् मनुषः (*ubhayān manuṣaḥ*)** — people of two kinds, that is, those who worship Agni and satisfy him by sacrifices and the like, and the others who do not do so: thus Sāyaṇa has explained the sense.

**प्रपित्वे, अभिपित्वे (*prapitve, abhipitve*)** — सन्निहिते (*sannihite*) | The meaning is: in the sacrifice that has now arrived, that is going on. Yāska has read this word among the twenty "dviśa" names *(so printed: "ippattu dviśanāmagaḷalli"; zoomed, the term is unclear)*. And —

> प्रपित्वेऽभीक इत्यासन्नस्य । प्रपित्वे प्राप्ते । अभीकेऽभ्यक्ते ।

> *prapitve 'bhīka ityāsannasya | prapitve prāpte | abhīke 'bhyakte |*

(Ni. 3-20, zoomed)

— he has given this derivation. Therefore the intention is that *prapitve* means "in the (sacrifice) now being accomplished". The word *abhipitve* too has the same meaning. अभिपित्वे — अभिगमनवति यज्ञे (*abhipitve — abhigamanavati yajñe*) | The meaning is: in this sacrifice going on before us.

**उशिग्भिः (*uśigbhiḥ*)** — The word *uśik* is read among the words denoting *kānti* (desire) (Ni. 3-9, as printed; zoomed) and among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19, as printed; zoomed). Here the intention is: priests who are wise (intelligent).

**अक्रः (*akraḥ*)** — आक्रमिता त्वं (*ākramitā tvaṃ*) | It is an epithet of Agni: he who overruns and burns everything. Yāska, giving the derivation अक्र आक्रमणात् (*akra ākramaṇāt*) (Ni. 6-12, zoomed), …

### Printed p. 294 (PDF 313)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 189". Ṛk 7: Special Topics concluded; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā; end of Ṛk 7; Ṛk 8: Saṃhitā.)*

… has given as example the ṛk —

> अक्रो न बभ्रिः समिथे महीनां दिदृक्षेयः सूनवे भाऋजीकः ।
> उदुस्रिया जनिता यो जजानापां गर्भो नृतमो यह्वो अग्निः ॥

> *akro na babhriḥ samithe mahīnāṃ didṛkṣeyaḥ sūnave bhāṛjīkaḥ |*
> *udusriyā janitā yo jajānāpāṃ garbho nṛtamo yahvo agniḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-1-12, zoomed) *(an ink blot touches "nṛtamo")*

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, noted briefly).** तान् + अग्ने (*tān + agne*) — *ru* for the *n* by दीर्घादटि समानपादे (*dīrghādaṭi samānapāde*) (Pā. Sū. 8-3-9, zoomed); nasalization of the preceding *ā* by आतोऽटि नित्यम् (*āto 'ṭi nityam*) (Pā. Sū. 8-3-3, zoomed). वेषि (*veṣi*) — root वी कान्त्यादिषु (*vī kāntyādiṣu*), *kānti* here meaning desire; *laṭ* second person singular *sip*; *luk* of *śap* by अदिप्रभृतिभ्यः (*adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ*); guṇa of the *ī*; at the head of the pāda, so no nighāta; *sip* being anudātta, the root accent remains. शास्यः (*śāsyaḥ*) — root शासु अनुशिष्टौ (*śāsu anuśiṣṭau*); suffix *kyap* by एतिस्तुशास्— (*etistuśās—*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-109, zoomed); the *ya* remains; being *pit* it is anudātta, so the root accent remains. भूः (*bhūḥ*) — root भू सत्तायाम् (*bhū sattāyām*); *luṅ* in the sense of *loṭ* by छंदसि लुङ्लङ्लिटः (*chaṃdasi luṅlaṅliṭaḥ*); second person singular; in Vedic no augment *aṭ*; nighāta of the verb. मर्मृजेन्यः (*marmṛjenyaḥ*) — root मृजू शुद्धौ (*mṛjū śuddhau*); suffix *ṣeṇyaṇ* *(as printed)* after the *yaṅ*-stem; reduplication and the rest because of *yaṅ*; initial-acute of the suffix. उशिग्भिः (*uśigbhiḥ*) — root वश कांतौ (*vaśa kāṃtau*); suffix *iji* by वशेः कित् (*vaśeḥ kit*) (U. Saṃ. 2-229, abbreviation as printed; per numeral file); being made *kit*, *u* for the root's *v* (samprasāraṇa) by ग्रहिज्यावयि— (*grahijyāvayi—*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-16, zoomed), *pūrvarūpa* for the following *a*: the word *uśij*; instrumental plural; the *i* is udātta by the initial-acute of the suffix. अक्रः (*akraḥ*) — root क्रमु पादविक्षेपे (*kramu pādavikṣepe*); in Vedic suffix *ḍa*; by force of its being *ḍit*, elision of the *ṭi* (*am*); end-acute by the suffix accent.

*(A short rule closes Ṛk 7.)*

#### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अवोचाम निवचनान्यस्मिन्मानस्य सूनुः सहसाने अग्नौ ।
> वयं सहस्रमृषिभिः सनेम विद्यामेषं वृजनं जीरदानुं ॥ ८ ॥

> *avocāma nivacanānyasminmānasya sūnuḥ sahasāne agnau |*
> *vayaṃ sahasramṛṣibhiḥ sanema vidyāmeṣaṃ vṛjanaṃ jīradānuṃ ‖ 8 ‖*

### Printed p. 295 (PDF 314)

*(Header: "A. [2] A. 5 Va. 11" — the Aṣṭaka numeral prints like "ಅ.ವ", as on p. 285. Ṛk 8: Pada, bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics begin.)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥** *(A stray point follows "agnau".)*

> अवोचाम । निऽवचनानि । अस्मिन् । मानस्य । सूनुः । सहसाने । अग्नौ ।
> वयं । सहस्रं । ऋषिऽभिः । सनेम । विद्याम । इषं । वृजनं । जीरऽदानुं ॥ ८ ॥

> *avocāma | ni 'vacanāni | asmin | mānasya | sūnuḥ | sahasāne | agnau |*
> *vayaṃ | sahasraṃ | ṛṣi 'bhiḥ | sanema | vidyāma | iṣaṃ | vṛjanaṃ | jīra 'dānuṃ ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed.)*

> वयमस्मिन्नग्नौ निवचनानि नियमपूर्वकाणि वचांसि स्तोत्ररूपाण्यवोचाम । ब्रूमः । अग्निर्विशेष्यते । मानस्य सूनुः । मीयत इति मानो मंत्रः । तस्य सूनुरग्निः मंत्रेणोत्पद्यमानत्वात् । सप्तम्यर्थे प्रथमा । मानस्य सूनौ सहसाने शत्रूणामभिभवितर्यग्नाववोचाम । वयमेभिर्ऋषिभिरतींद्रियार्थप्रकाशकैर्मंत्रैः साधनैः सहस्रमपरिमितं धनं सनेम । संभजेमहि । विद्यामेति गतं ॥

> *vayamasminnagnau nivacanāni niyamapūrvakāṇi vacāṃsi stotrarūpāṇyavocāma | brūmaḥ | agnirviśeṣyate | mānasya sūnuḥ | mīyata iti māno maṃtraḥ | tasya sūnuragniḥ maṃtreṇotpadyamānatvāt | saptamyarthe prathamā | mānasya sūnau sahasāne śatrūṇāmabhibhavitaryagnāvavocāma | vayamebhirṛṣibhiratīṃdriyārthaprakāśakairmaṃtraiḥ sādhanaiḥ sahasramaparimitaṃ dhanaṃ sanema | saṃbhajemahi | vidyāmeti gataṃ ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** मानस्य सूनुः (*mānasya sūnuḥ*) — the son born of the mantra; सहसाने (*sahasāne*) — and having the power to defeat enemies; अस्मिन् अग्नौ (*asmin agnau*) — in this Agni (with reference to Agni); निवचनानि (*nivacanāni*) — words in the form of praises; अवोचाम (*avocāma*) — we recite; वयं (*vayaṃ*) — we; ऋषिभिः (*ṛṣibhiḥ*) — by mantras that reveal supersensible matters; सहस्रं (*sahasraṃ*) — unlimited wealth; सनेम (*sanema*) — may we obtain; (and) इषं (*iṣaṃ*) — food; वृजनं (*vṛjanaṃ*) — strength; जीरदानुं (*jīradānuṃ*) — long life; विद्याम (*vidyāma*) — may we obtain.

**Bhāvārtha.** With reference to this Agni, the son born of the mantra, who has the power to defeat enemies, we recite praises. By mantras that reveal supersensible matters may we obtain unlimited wealth, food, strength and long life.

**English Translation (as printed).**

We address our pious prayers to you, Agni, the son of prayer, the subduer of foes; may we procure, by these sacred supplications, infinite wealth that we may thence obtain food, strength, and long life· [sic]

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**मानस्य सूनुः (*mānasya sūnuḥ*)** — मीयत इति मानो मंत्रः । तस्य सूनुरग्निः । मंत्रेणोत्पद्यमानत्वात् । सप्तम्यर्थे प्रथमा (*mīyata iti māno maṃtraḥ | tasya sūnuragniḥ | maṃtreṇotpadyamānatvāt | saptamyarthe prathamā*) | Here they have taken *māna* to mean mantra. *(The page ends here; whether this topic continues is to be seen on p. 296.)*

### Printed p. 296 (PDF 315)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 189". Ṛk 8, Special Topics continued.)*

From the root माङ् माने (*māṅ māne*), "to measure", comes the word *māna*: the meaning is a mantra having a fixed (*klṛpta*) number of syllables (a ṛk or a metre). Since Agni is produced in the araṇi preceded by mantras, Agni is described by the epithet मानस्य सूनुः (*mānasya sūnuḥ*), "born from the mantra (the son of the mantra)". Here the nominative case is used in the sense of the locative. The commentator has explained that मानस्य सूनुः (*mānasya sūnuḥ*) is to be taken in the sense "in Agni".

**सहस्रं (*sahasraṃ*)** — unlimited, of great number.

**ऋषिभिः (*ṛṣibhiḥ*)** — ऋषी गतौ (*ṛṣī gatau*) | Since roots meaning motion are also used in the sense of knowing, the word *ṛṣi* also has the senses knowledge, understanding and the like. Since the mantra brings about knowledge, here ऋषिभिः (*ṛṣibhiḥ*) means "by mantras whose nature is knowledge": that is the intention.

**जीरदानुं (*jīradānuṃ*)** — In 1-165-15 (zoomed) Sāyaṇa has explained this word as जयशीलदानं (*jayaśīladānaṃ*). For this there is also the variant reading जयशीलं दानं जीवनं वा (*jayaśīlaṃ dānaṃ jīvanaṃ vā*). How the word *jīra* comes to mean "victory" or "causing victory" is a matter for enquiry. *Jīra* and *dānu*, these two words joined, have become *jīradānu*. These two words are used separately in many places and give different meanings. Besides, there are usages such as *jīrāśva*, *jīrādhvara*, where words like *aśva*, *adhvara* are joined with the word *jīra*.

> मनुष्वद्देव धीमहि प्रचेतसं जीरं दूतममर्त्यं ।

> *manuṣvaddeva dhīmahi pracetasaṃ jīraṃ dūtamamartyaṃ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-44-11, zoomed)

In this ṛk, explaining the derivation of the word *jīra*, Sāyaṇa has stated that the word is derived from the root जु (*ju*) (जोरी च (*jorī ca*), U. Sū. 2-181, zoomed) and has given the meaning (शत्रूणां (*śatrūṇāṃ*)) वयोहानिकरं (*vayohānikaraṃ*), "causing the loss of life (of enemies)". Here जीरं (*jīraṃ*) is an epithet of Agni. From this meaning it appears that the derivation is possible also from the root ज्या वयोहानौ (*jyā vayohānau*). The Niruktakāra has read the word *jīra* among the names of "swift" (*kṣipra*) (Ni. 3-9, as printed; zoomed).

> दिविस्पृशं यज्ञमस्माकमश्विना जीराध्वरं कृणुतं सुम्नमिष्टये ।
> प्राचीनरश्मिमाहुतं घृतेन तद्देवानामवो अद्या वृणीमहे ॥

> *divispṛśaṃ yajñamasmākamaśvinā jīrādhvaraṃ kṛṇutaṃ sumnamiṣṭaye |*
> *prācīnaraśmimāhutaṃ ghṛtena taddevānāmavo adyā vṛṇīmahe ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-36-6, zoomed)

In this ṛk the Aśvin deities are prayed: "make our rite *jīrādhvara*". Here *jīrādhvara* means a sacrifice accomplished without hindrance from obstacles, free of violence, and quickly.

### Printed p. 297 (PDF 316)

*(Header: "A. 2. A. 5 Va. 11". Ṛk 8, Special Topics continued.)*

> पृक्षे ता विश्वा भुवना ववक्षिरे मित्राय वा सदमा जीरदानवः ।
> पृषदश्वासो अनवभ्रराधस ऋजिप्यासो न वयुनेषु धूर्षदः ॥

> *pṛkṣe tā viśvā bhuvanā vavakṣire mitrāya vā sadamā jīradānavaḥ |*
> *pṛṣadaśvāso anavabhrarādhasa ṛjipyāso na vayuneṣu dhūrṣadaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-34-4, zoomed)

In such places जीरदानवः (*jīradānavaḥ*) is an epithet of the Maruts; the meaning is "those who fulfil the sacrificer's desired objects very quickly". In the same way the compound words जीराश्वः (*jīrāśvaḥ*), जीराश्वं (*jīrāśvaṃ*) too are epithets of Agni and other deities; or they are also epithets of their chariot.

> आ वां रथं पुरुमायं मनोजुवं जीराश्वं यज्ञियं जीवसे हुवे ।
> सहस्रकेतुं वनिनं शतद्वसुं श्रुष्टीवानं वरिवोधामभि प्रयः ॥

> *ā vāṃ rathaṃ purumāyaṃ manojuvaṃ jīrāśvaṃ yajñiyaṃ jīvase huve |*
> *sahasraketuṃ vaninaṃ śatadvasuṃ śruṣṭīvānaṃ varivodhāmabhi prayaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-119-1, zoomed)

In such ṛks the chariot of the Aśvin deities is described as having horses that run swiftly. In the same way the word *dānu* too, used both separately and in compounds such as सुदानवः (*sudānavaḥ*), जीरदानवः (*jīradānavaḥ*), gives a meaning suited to the context. That the word *dānu* gives the meaning either "giver" (*dātṛ*) or "asura" is known from the context the Niruktakāra cites:

*(So printed: "ā parṣate" (zoomed; the first letter of the verb looks like pa); a point stands after "stuṣeyyaṃ".)*

> स्तुषेय्यं पुरुवर्पसमृभ्वमिनतममाप्त्यमाप्त्यानां ।
> आ पर्षते शवसा सप्त दानून् प्र साक्षते प्रतिमानानि भूरि ॥

> *stuṣeyyaṃ puruvarpasamṛbhvaminatamamāptyamāptyānāṃ |*
> *ā parṣate śavasā sapta dānūn pra sākṣate pratimānāni bhūri ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-120-6)

In giving the meaning of this ṛk, the Niruktakāra has stated that the word सप्त दानून् (*sapta dānūn*) means सप्त दातॄन् इति वा सप्त दानवान् इति वा (*sapta dātṝn iti vā sapta dānavān iti vā*) (zoomed), "seven givers" or "seven Dānavas". But, indicating his difficulty as to how the meaning "asura" is possible for the word *dānu* in such contexts, the scholar Max Muller has said this —

It must be confessed that even the meaning of Danu is by no means quite clear· It is clear enough where it means Demon, II. 11, 18 : II. 12. 11 ; IV. 30.7 : X. 120·6 ; The seven Demons, in I· 32.9; III. 30·8 ; Danu› Demon is applied to the mother of Vritra‘ the dark cloud ; From this Danu we have the derivative Danava, meaning again Demon, why the demons conquered by Indra, were called Danu is not clear, unless they were conceived originally as dark clouds, like Danu, the mother of Indra. Danu might mean wise or even powerful, for this meaning also is ascribed to Danu by the author of Unadi Sutras. [sic: "clear·", "I· 32.9", "Danu›", "Vritra‘" as printed]

[ S. B. E. XXXII· P. 114-115 ]

### Printed p. 298 (PDF 317)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 188" — so printed (zoomed; the sūkta is 189). Ṛk 8: Special Topics concluded; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā.)*

*Dānu* is the name of an asura woman, that is, of Vṛtra's mother. This scholar asks: her sons ought to be *Dānava*; how did they become *Dānu*? And from the Uṇādi sūtra it is known that the meanings "power" and "wise" too are possible for this word. But the meaning "giver" (*dātṛ*) is the better known.

If, in this way, the word *jīra* means "swift" (*kṣipra*) and the word *dānu* means "gift" (*dāna*), then in the present ṛk the meaning has to be "a swift gift". But Sāyaṇa has given the meaning "a victorious gift". Since the word *jīra* has been used in many places in the sense of "impelling", here the meaning "a gift that impels victory" may be given. Generally the word जीरदानवः (*jīradānavaḥ*) comes most often as an epithet of the Maruts.

> पृक्षे ता विश्वा भुवना ववक्षिरे मित्राय वा सदमा जीरदानवः ॥

> *pṛkṣe tā viśvā bhuvanā vavakṣire mitrāya vā sadamā jīradānavaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-34-4, zoomed; no closing parenthesis printed)

In such ṛks जीरदानवः मरुतः (*jīradānavaḥ marutaḥ*) is well known. And —

> वृषा न क्रुद्धः पतयद्रजःस्वा यो अर्यपत्नीरकृणोदिमा अपः ।
> स सुन्वते मघवा जीरदानवेऽविंदज्ज्योतिर्मनवे हविष्मते ॥

> *vṛṣā na kruddhaḥ patayadrajaḥsvā yo aryapatnīrakṛṇodimā apaḥ |*
> *sa sunvate maghavā jīradānave 'viṃdajjyotirmanave haviṣmate ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-43-8, zoomed)

In such ṛks this word is an epithet also of the performer of the sacrifice who offers oblations and the like.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, noted briefly).** अवोचाम (*avocāma*) — root ब्रूञ् व्यक्तायां वाचि (*brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci*); in Vedic, *luṅ* in the sense of the present; substitution of *vac* for the root by ब्रुवो वचिः (*bruvo vaciḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 2-4-53, zoomed); *aṅ* for *cli* by अस्यतिवक्तिख्याति— (*asyativaktikhyāti—*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-82, zoomed); when it follows, the augment *um* by वच उम् (*vaca um*) and guṇa; at the head of the pāda, so no nighāta; initial-acute by the accent of the augment *aṭ*. मानस्य (*mānasya*) — root माङ् माने (*māṅ māne*); suffix *ghañ*, being *ñit*, gives the initial-acute; in मानस्य सूनुः (*mānasya sūnuḥ*) the nominative stands in the sense of the locative by the statement सुपां सुपो भवन्ति (*supāṃ supo bhavanti*). सहसाने (*sahasāne*) — root षह मर्षणे (*ṣaha marṣaṇe*); *s* for the initial by धात्वादेः षः सः (*dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-64, zoomed); suffix *asānac* by ऋञ्जिवृधिमंदिसहिभ्यः कित् (*ṛñjivṛdhimaṃdisahibhyaḥ kit*) (U. Sū. 2-2[?]4 — the middle digit undecided after zooming; no opening parenthesis printed); being *cit*, end-acute by चितः (*citaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-163, zoomed); locative singular. सनेम (*sanema*) — root षण संभक्तौ (*ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau*); *s* for the initial as before; *liṅ* first person plural; nighāta by तिङ्ङतिङः (*tiṅṅatiṅaḥ*).

*(After the grammar note on सनेम (*sanema*) at the foot of p. 298 no closing rule, "… vargavu mugidudu" line or colophon is printed; p. 299 opens with the Pīṭhike of the next sūkta. End of Ṛk 8 and of Sūkta 189.)*

### Printed p. 299 (PDF 318)

*(Header: "A. 2. A 5. Va. 11." (zoomed). Pīṭhike (introduction) of the next sūkta (Sūkta 190; its number is not printed on this page).)*

## Pīṭhike to Sūkta 190

**Pīṭhike.** *(Centred title, with a short rule below.)*

The deity of this sūkta is Bṛhaspati. Yāska in his Nirukta, explaining the derivation of the word Bṛhaspati —

> बृहस्पतिः बृहतः पाता वा पालयिता वा ।

> *bṛhaspatiḥ bṛhataḥ pātā vā pālayitā vā |*

(Ni. 10-11, zoomed)

— has said so. On this the commentator Durgācārya says — बृहस्पतिः कस्मात् (*bṛhaspatiḥ kasmāt*)? "बृहतः पाता वा पालयिता वा (*bṛhataḥ pātā vā pālayitā vā*)" बृहतः महतोऽस्य जगतः उदकस्य वा पाता रक्षिता, पालयिता अपि रक्षितैव धात्वन्यत्वमर्थैकत्वं (*bṛhataḥ mahato 'sya jagataḥ udakasya vā pātā rakṣitā, pālayitā api rakṣitaiva dhātvanyatvamarthaikatvaṃ*) ‖ — that is, the protector, the guardian of the great world or of water. He has said that, though to express the meaning of the word *pati* there are the words पाता (*pātā*), पालयिता (*pālayitā*) derived from different roots, the meaning is one only. Sāyaṇa in many contexts, explaining बृहतः पाता (*bṛhataḥ pātā*), has given for the word बृहतः (*bṛhataḥ*) the meaning बृहतः यज्ञाख्यकर्मणः अथवा वृष्ट्याख्यकर्मणः (*bṛhataḥ yajñākhyakarmaṇaḥ athavā vṛṣṭyākhyakarmaṇaḥ*), that is, "of the rite in the form of the sacrifice, or of the rite in the form of granting rain". Since Bṛhaspati, as the purohita of the gods, accomplishes the sacrificial rite, and brings about the rain that men need, both kinds of epithets are natural to him. Describing Bṛhaspati's office of purohita and his granting of rain —

> यद्देवापिः शंतनवे पुरोहितो होत्राय वृतः कृपयन्नदीधेत् ।
> देवश्रुतं वृष्टिवनिं रराणो बृहस्पतिर्वाचमस्मा अयच्छत् ॥

> *yaddevāpiḥ śaṃtanave purohito hotrāya vṛtaḥ kṛpayannadīdhet |*
> *devaśrutaṃ vṛṣṭivaniṃ rarāṇo bṛhaspatirvācamasmā ayacchat ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-98-7, zoomed)

— this ṛk Yāska has given as an example. In the explanation of this ṛk — बृहस्पतिर्ब्रह्मासीत् सोऽस्मै वाचमयच्छत् (*bṛhaspatirbrahmāsīt so 'smai vācamayacchat*) — it is described that Bṛhaspati, in the sacrifice performed by the king named Śantanu, became the purohita called Brahmā and taught the mantra in the form of speech, and that when the sacrificer praised with that mantra, rain came. Besides this, in the Yajurveda and other texts —

> बृहस्पतिर्देवानां पुरोहित आसीच्छंडामर्कावसुराणां ।

> *bṛhaspatirdevānāṃ purohita āsīcchaṃḍāmarkāvasurāṇāṃ |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-10-1, zoomed)

— it is said that Bṛhaspati was the purohita of the gods, and those called Śaṇḍa and Marka were the purohitas of the asuras.

> ब्रह्म वै देवानां बृहस्पतिर्ब्रह्मणैवैनमभिचरति ।

> *brahma vai devānāṃ bṛhaspatirbrahmaṇaivainamabhicarati |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 2-2-9-1, zoomed)

### Printed p. 300 (PDF 319)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24 Sū. 189" (the Pīṭhike of Sūkta 190 stands under the header of Sūkta 189). Pīṭhike continued.)*

— it is also said that Bṛhaspati, in the sacrifice performed by the gods, accomplished the sacrifice as the ṛtvij called Brahmā.

> तस्मै विशः स्वयमेवा नमंते यस्मिन् ब्रह्मा राजनि पूर्व एति ।

> *tasmai viśaḥ svayamevā namaṃte yasmin brahmā rājani pūrva eti |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-50-8, zoomed)

> अवस्यवे यो वरिवः कृणोति ब्रह्मणे राजा तमवंति देवाः ॥

> *avasyave yo varivaḥ kṛṇoti brahmaṇe rājā tamavaṃti devāḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-50-9, zoomed)

> सोमं राजानमवसेऽग्निं गीर्भिर्हवामहे ।
> आदित्यान्विष्णुं सूर्यं ब्रह्माणं च बृहस्पतिं ॥

> *somaṃ rājānamavase 'gniṃ gīrbhirhavāmahe |*
> *ādityānviṣṇuṃ sūryaṃ brahmāṇaṃ ca bṛhaspatiṃ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-141-3, zoomed)

In such ṛks Bṛhaspati is described as the ṛtvij called Brahmā.

In the Ṛgveda Bṛhaspati has a truly prominent place. Besides being praised in eleven sūktas, he is praised in two sūktas (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-49 ; 7-97, zoomed) as a dual deity together with Indra. The word Bṛhaspati occurs in the Ṛgveda about 120 times. In many contexts the deities Bṛhaspati and Brahmaṇaspati are praised interchangeably in one and the same mantra. Even so, Bṛhaspati is one deity and Brahmaṇaspati another.

Some Western scholars, and some among modern learned men as well, have expressed the opinion that, since in the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-23 (zoomed) Bṛhaspati and Brahmaṇaspati are praised interchangeably, the two are one deity. But the ancient commentators on the Veda, Yāska, Śaunaka, Sāyaṇa and others, have said clearly that Bṛhaspati is one and Brahmaṇaspati another. Of the 19 ṛks in the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-23 mentioned above, only the 6 ṛks 1, 5, 9, 11, 17, 19 (zoomed) praise Bṛhaspati; the remaining 13 ṛks concern Brahmaṇaspati. Yāska too has given separate derivations for the word Bṛhaspati and for the word Brahmaṇaspati. Therefore Bṛhaspati is one and Brahmaṇaspati another.

Bṛhaspati has a distinctiveness quite different from the other deities. While the other deities are all particular forms of nature or of the power of nature, Bṛhaspati appears to belong to the sphere of man's moral and religious life. There are many examples in the Ṛgveda showing that this deity, the protector of praise, hymn or prayer, exerts his influence on the mind, resolve or power of the gods. In the 98th sūkta of the 10th maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda (zoomed) there is a historical narrative about the Kuru princes named Devāpi and Śantanu. That Bṛhaspati's part in it is of great importance the Niruktakāra has described thus —

### Printed p. 301 (PDF 320)

*(Header: "A. 2. A. 5. Va. 11." Pīṭhike continued.)*

*(The quotation prints "kauravau" (zoomed).)*

> अत्रेतिहासमाचक्षते । देवापिश्चार्ष्टिषेणः शंतनुश्च कौरवौ भ्रातरौ बभूवतुः । स शंतनुः कनीयानभिषेचयांचक्रे । देवापिस्तपः प्रतिपेदे । ततः शंतनो राज्ये द्वादश वर्षाणि देवो न ववर्ष । तमूचुर्ब्राह्मणा अधर्मस्त्वया चरितो ज्येष्ठं भ्रातरमंतरित्याभिषेचितं तस्मात्ते देवो न वर्षतीति । स शंतनुर्देवापिं शिशिक्ष राज्येन । तमुवाच देवापिः पुरोहितस्तेऽसानि याजयानि च त्वेति ॥

> *atretihāsamācakṣate | devāpiścārṣṭiṣeṇaḥ śaṃtanuśca kauravau bhrātarau babhūvatuḥ | sa śaṃtanuḥ kanīyānabhiṣecayāṃcakre | devāpistapaḥ pratipede | tataḥ śaṃtano rājye dvādaśa varṣāṇi devo na vavarṣa | tamūcurbrāhmaṇā adharmastvayā carito jyeṣṭhaṃ bhrātaramaṃtarityābhiṣecitaṃ tasmātte devo na varṣatīti | sa śaṃtanurdevāpiṃ śiśikṣa rājyena | tamuvāca devāpiḥ purohitaste 'sāni yājayāni ca tveti ‖*

(Ni. 2-11, zoomed)

In former times, in the Kuru line, the king named Ṛṣṭiṣeṇa had two sons, Devāpi and Śantanu. Of them Devāpi was the elder and Śantanu the younger. After their father Ṛṣṭiṣeṇa died, his elder son, Devāpi, wished to become king. But his younger brother Śantanu, giving him no opportunity for it and wishing to obtain the kingdom himself, drove away his elder brother Devāpi and began to rule himself. The elder brother Devāpi, distressed, went to the forest and passed his time in penance. Meanwhile, in his country there was no rain for 12 years (zoomed) and a great famine came. Then King Śantanu, considering what should be done about it, asked the advice of the brāhmaṇas. The brāhmaṇas then told the king: "According to the Dharmaśāstra the king's eldest son alone is entitled to the kingdom; therefore your elder brother Devāpi ought to have borne the burden of the kingdom. But you, giving him no opportunity, drove him away and have seized the kingdom. Since you are thus practising adharma, the god of rain does not pour rain in your kingdom." King Śantanu, repenting of the injustice he had done, called his elder brother Devāpi, who was doing penance in the forest, and handed the kingdom over to him. But Devāpi said that he did not want the kingdom and would keep to the path of withdrawal (*nivṛttimārga*), doing penance in the forest; and he said that Śantanu should perform a sacrifice to remove the drought that had come upon the kingdom, and that he himself would take the office of purohita in it and help to bring rain. The king agreeing, Devāpi took the part of the ṛtvij called Hotṛ in his sacrifice. Bṛhaspati was the ṛtvij called Brahmā. In that sacrifice, performed for rainfall, Devāpi, the Hotṛ, prayed to Bṛhaspati, the Brahmā: "O Bṛhaspati, you have great influence over the minds of the gods; therefore you must teach me mantras that win them over." Bṛhaspati said "So be it" and taught Devāpi, the Hotṛ, mantras containing the prayers to the gods needed for rainfall. When homa was made with those mantras, addressed to the gods, rain came as desired: so it is said. Therefore this sūkta is also named the "Vṛṣṭikāma sūkta" (the sūkta for those who desire rain). This matter, with some differences, is stated also in Purāṇa works such as the Viṣṇu Purāṇa 4-20-7, the Mahābhārata, Ādiparva, and the Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9-22-14 to 17 (zoomed).

### Printed p. 302 (PDF 321)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 189" (zoomed; the Pīṭhike of Sūkta 190 still stands under the header of Sūkta 189). Pīṭhike continued.)*

In the 108th sūkta of the 10th maṇḍala of the Ṛ. Saṃ. (zoomed) there is another episode (*upākhyāna*). The asuras called Paṇis carried off the cows of the gods (the clouds laden with water) and hid them in an impregnable fortress. Indra sent Saramā, the bitch of the gods, to search for them. That Saramā came to the Paṇis, carried on a dispute with them and asked them to give back the stolen cows. Those Paṇis urged her in many ways: "What is Indra's power? We are great heroes and our weapons are very keen (*harita*); therefore the gods cannot conquer us, and the gods cannot even find the place where the cows are kept; therefore, if Saramā leaves the side of the gods and joins our band, we will give her whatever wealth and the like she wants." But Saramā did not agree to it; she turned back from there and told the whole matter to the gods. Then Bṛhaspati by his power found out the place where those cows were hidden. Afterwards the gods subdued them and brought the cows back: such is the episode.

In many such bold deeds Bṛhaspati's part is very important. Moreover, when men need rain, Bṛhaspati's help is most necessary *(printed "atyavaśakavāgide")*. This kind of prayer is found especially in the sūktas whose deity is Bṛhaspati.

Let us examine closely what Bṛhaspati's qualities and achievements are, as described in the Ṛgveda. Bṛhaspati was born of Dyāvāpṛthivī, and he was nourished by [his own?] greatness *(the word before "mahattva" is faint; it looks like "svara" [?])* (Ṛ Saṃ 7-97-8, zoomed). But in one place it is said that Tvaṣṭṛ created him (2-23-17, zoomed). He has the name "father of the gods" (2-26-3, zoomed); it is also said that the gods were born from him as sparks fly from the blow of a smith's hammer (10-72-8, zoomed).

He has the name Brahmā (the ṛtvij called Brahmā) (10-141-3, zoomed). He is connected with the ṛtvijs (7-10-4 ; 10-14-3, zoomed). He has also the name Āṅgirasa (4-40-1 ; 4-73-1 ; 10-47-6, zoomed; "4-73" as printed). He is the composer and the utterer of words of praise; their lord and impeller (2-23-1, 2 ; 1-40-5 ; 10-10-[?]; the last digit undecided); he accomplishes all his aims by mantra alone (2-24-3); mounting the shining chariot called sacrifice he sets out to conquer the enemies of the gods and of the praisers (2-23 3; hyphen missing, as printed); he is the nourisher and protector of the faithful. He is their guide; he rescues them from calamities (2-23-4, zoomed). He bestows wealth and the like on them (2-23-9, zoomed). He is reckoned the father of all the gods; he is endowed with all divine qualities (3-62-4 ; 4-50-6, zoomed); he is of all forms (*viśvarūpa*); all the things that everyone desires are in him (7-10-4, 7-97-4); he holds a golden spear (7-97-7, zoomed); joining with Indra, he too has become a leader of armies (10-103-8).

### Printed p. 303 (PDF 322)

*(Header: "A. 2. A. 5. Va. 11." (zoomed). Pīṭhike continued.)*

— he is the increaser of life (10-100-5, zoomed); the plants were produced by him (10-97-15 and 19, zoomed); it is said that tawny-coloured horses are his vehicle (Ni. 2-28, zoomed).

It is said that, hearing the cry of distress of Trita, who had been thrown into a well by the rākṣasas and was calling on the gods for help, Bṛhaspati freed him from that perilous state (1-105-17), and that, joining with Indra, Bṛhaspati made the waters that had been covered by darkness flow again (2-23-18 ; 1-56-5 ;, zoomed).

Bṛhaspati by his power broke the stone door of the well filled with honey. The gods drank that honey and poured down rain as they wished (2-24-3, 4); when Bṛhaspati with his fiery rays split the fortresses of Vala, the herds of cows became visible; he drove the cows out as one breaks an egg; seeing the honey (water) enclosed by the rock, he split it by his roar alone and made it come out (10-68-4 to 9). Bṛhaspati brought the cows out from the rocks; he seized Vala's cows and made them his own (10-68-5).

Bṛhaspati is endowed with divinity (2-23-2); he is the kinsman of all the gods (3-62-4 ; 4-50-6): and he has more divinity than all the gods: in the form of a deity he takes all the gods and all things into himself (2-24-11 ; 8-61-18, zoomed); being powerful, he keeps the two ends of the earth apart (4-50-1); the rising of the sun and the moon one after the other is a deed of his worthy of imitation (10-68-10). In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (in the Yajurveda) a connection of Bṛhaspati with certain nakṣatras is stated. Bṛhaspati is the deity of the Puṣya nakṣatra (Tai. Saṃ. 4-4 10-1, as printed); in the Purāṇas and other works Bṛhaspati is described as Vācaspati and as the presiding deity of the planet Bṛhaspati (Jupiter).

Some scholars have held that the deities called Bṛhaspati and Brahmaṇaspati are transformed forms of Agni. The scholar M. Langlois, in his work, the translation of the Ṛgveda, Part I p. 249, 254, 578, has supported with many examples the view that these two deities are both forms of Agni. The scholar Wilson too has expressed the same opinion in the introduction to the first part of his translation of the Ṛgveda; the scholar Max Muller also —

Brihaspati and Brahmanaspati are both varieties of Agni, the priest and the purohit of the Gods and men and as such he is invoked together with the Maruts &c.

That is, Bṛhaspati and Brahmaṇaspati both are forms of Agni, and stand in the place of ṛtvij and purohita to gods and men; from this very point of view, together with the Marut deities —

### Printed p. 304 (PDF 323)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 189" (the Pīṭhike of Sūkta 190 still under the header of Sūkta 189). Pīṭhike continued.)*

— he has said that their being invoked [together] is found in many places. In this way we give one or two examples that state the identity (*tādātmya*) of Agni with Bṛhaspati and Brahmaṇaspati.

> त्वमग्न इंद्रो वृषभः सतामसि त्वं विष्णुरुरुगायो नमस्यः ।
> त्वं ब्रह्मा रयिविद्ब्रह्मणस्पते त्वं विधर्तः सचसे पुरंध्या ॥

> *tvamagna iṃdro vṛṣabhaḥ satāmasi tvaṃ viṣṇururugāyo namasyaḥ |*
> *tvaṃ brahmā rayividbrahmaṇaspate tvaṃ vidhartaḥ sacase puraṃdhyā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-3, zoomed)

*(The print breaks "rayividbrahmaṇaspate" between "rayividb" and "rahmaṇaspate".)* "O Agni, you are Indra, the most excellent among the good; you are Viṣṇu, worthy of worship and of very large body; O Brahmaṇaspati, you are the ṛtvij called Brahmā, rich in wealth": thus Agni is described as the very form of various deities.

> तं शुभ्रमग्निमवसे हवामहे वैश्वानरं मातरिश्वानमुक्थ्यं ।
> बृहस्पतिं मनुषो देवतातये विप्रं श्रोतारमतिथिं रघुष्यदं ॥

> *taṃ śubhramagnimavase havāmahe vaiśvānaraṃ mātariśvānamukthyaṃ |*
> *bṛhaspatiṃ manuṣo devatātaye vipraṃ śrotāramatithiṃ raghuṣyadaṃ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-26-2, zoomed)

"We invoke for our protection Agni, who is bright and the friend of all mankind; we invoke, that they may come to the sacrifices and other rites of men, Mātariśvan, who is fit to be the object of the mantras, and Bṛhaspati, who is wise, who praises with reference to the gods, who is like a guest and goes swiftly."

Sāyaṇācārya, when writing his commentary on the ṛk 5-43-12 (read from the strip), says of the word Bṛhaspati —

> अथवा इयमाग्नेयी। बृहतः परिवृढस्य कर्मणः स्वामीति बृहस्पतिरग्निरुच्यते। तथा नीलवर्णधूमपृष्ठत्वसदनसादनहिरण्यवर्णत्वादिलिंगैरप्यग्निरेव बृहस्पतिः ॥

> *athavā iyamāgneyī| bṛhataḥ parivṛḍhasya karmaṇaḥ svāmīti bṛhaspatiragnirucyate| tathā nīlavarṇadhūmapṛṣṭhatvasadanasādanahiraṇyavarṇatvādiliṃgairapyagnireva bṛhaspatiḥ ‖*

That is — "Or, this mantra may be said to set forth Agni as its deity. Because he is the lord of the great work in the form of the present sacrifice, Agni has the name Bṛhaspati. Likewise, from marks such as the black smoke being his back, the sacrificial altar his seat, the golden colour and so on, Bṛhaspati is to be called Agni himself": so he has said.

Now let us examine examples that state the difference of Agni from Bṛhaspati and Brahmaṇaspati.

> सोषामविंदत्स स्वः १ सो अग्निं सो अर्केण वि बबाधे तमांसि ।
> बृहस्पतिर्गो वपुषो वलस्य निर्मज्जानं न पर्वणो जभार ॥

> *soṣāmaviṃdatsa svaḥ 1 so agniṃ so arkeṇa vi babādhe tamāṃsi |*
> *bṛhaspatirgo vapuṣo valasya nirmajjānaṃ na parvaṇo jabhāra ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-68-9, zoomed)

*(Printed "soṣāmaviṃdat" without avagraha; the small "1" after "svaḥ" is the kampa sign; "bṛhaspatirgo vapuṣo" with a space, as printed.)* In this ṛk it is said that Bṛhaspati obtained the dawn, heaven and Agni, and dispelled the darkness by a mantra; so it is said that Bṛhaspati and Agni are different.

> इंद्रं नो अग्ने वसुभिः सजोषा रुद्रं रुद्रेभिरा वहा बृहंतं ।
> आदित्येभिरदितिं विश्वजन्यां बृहस्पतिमृक्वभिर्विश्ववारं ॥

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-10-4, zoomed)

In this ṛk Agni is prayed to bring Indra accompanied by the Vasus, Rudra accompanied by the Marut deities, Aditi, the mother of all, accompanied by the Āditya (deities), and Bṛhaspati accompanied by the Aṅgiras ṛṣis who are singing praises. Besides this, mantras that indicate the sense that Bṛhaspati or Brahmaṇaspati is one and Agni another — the ṛks 3-20-5, 4-40-1. 5-51-12 (zoomed), 7-41-1, 7-44-1, 9-5-11, 10-35-11, 10-65-1, 10-130-4, 10-141-3 (read from the strip) and others — are many in the Ṛgveda. Therefore the conclusion that Agni is one and Bṛhaspati and Brahmaṇaspati another is the one supported in the Ṛgveda.

## Sūkta 190 — *anarvāṇam* (Anuvāka 24, eleventh Sūkta; 8 ṛks)

**The Hundred and Ninetieth Sūkta.** *(Half-title, in Kannada: "Nūra tombhattaneya sūktavu"; a short double rule follows.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; introduction to the sūkta. The bhāṣya prints "so 'ślokyaṃ" where the Anuvāda's quotation below prints "suślokyaṃ".)*

*Gist:* the eight-ṛk eleventh sūkta of Agastya, triṣṭubh, to Bṛhaspati; its śrauta use is by indicative marks; Śaunaka: one who bathes, salutes Bṛhaspati and recites it obtains heroes, wealth and fame.

> अनर्वाणमित्यष्टर्चमेकादशं सूक्तमागस्त्यं बार्हस्पत्यं त्रैष्टुभं । अनर्वाणं बार्हस्पत्यमित्यनुक्रांतं ॥ श्रौतविनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥ अत्र शौनकः । स्नात्वा जपेदनर्वाणं नमस्कृत्य बृहस्पतिं । वीरान्धनं च प्राप्नोति सोऽश्लोक्यं च नियच्छति । ऋग्वि. १-२७ । इति ॥

> *anarvāṇamityaṣṭarcamekādaśaṃ sūktamāgastyaṃ bārhaspatyaṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ | anarvāṇaṃ bārhaspatyamityanukrāṃtaṃ ‖ śrautaviniyogo laiṃgikaḥ ‖ atra śaunakaḥ | snātvā japedanarvāṇaṃ namaskṛtya bṛhaspatiṃ | vīrāndhanaṃ ca prāpnoti so 'ślokyaṃ ca niyacchati | ṛgvi. 1-27 | iti ‖*

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** This sūkta, अनर्वाणं (*anarvāṇaṃ*), is the eleventh sūkta in the twenty-fourth anuvāka. There are eight ṛks in it. Of this sūkta Agastya is the ṛṣi; Bṛhaspati the deity; *triṣṭubh* the metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is stated beginning with अनर्वाणं बार्हस्पत्यं (*anarvāṇaṃ bārhaspatyaṃ*). The śrauta application of this sūkta is by its indicative marks (*laiṅgika*), that is, according to the sense of the mantra. On the application of this sūkta the great sage Śaunaka, in his work called the Ṛgvidhāna —

> स्नात्वा जपेदनर्वाणं नमस्कृत्य बृहस्पतिं ।
> वीरान् धनं च प्राप्नोति सुश्लोक्यं च नियच्छति ॥

> *snātvā japedanarvāṇaṃ namaskṛtya bṛhaspatiṃ |*
> *vīrān dhanaṃ ca prāpnoti suślokyaṃ ca niyacchati ‖*

(Ṛgvidhāna 1-27, zoomed)

— has said that to the man who bathes, becomes pure, salutes the deity called Bṛhaspati and recites this sūkta of eight ṛks beginning अनर्वाणं (*anarvāṇaṃ*), Bṛhaspati gives heroic sons, wealth and fame.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Accents not reproduced.)*

> अनर्वाणं वृषभं मंद्रजिह्वं बृहस्पतिं वर्धया नव्यमर्कैः ।
> गाथान्यः सुरुचो यस्य देवा आशृण्वंति नवमानस्य मर्ताः ॥ १ ॥

> *anarvāṇaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ maṃdrajihvaṃ bṛhaspatiṃ vardhayā navyamarkaiḥ |*
> *gāthānyaḥ suruco yasya devā āśṛṇvaṃti navamānasya martāḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥** *(The Pada prints "gāthānyaḥ" without the compound mark, as printed.)*

> अनर्वाणं । वृषभं । मंद्रऽजिह्वं । बृहस्पतिं । वर्धय । नव्यं । अर्कैः ।
> गाथान्यः । सुऽरुचः । यस्य । देवाः । आऽशृण्वंति । नवमानस्य । मर्ताः ॥ १ ॥

> *anarvāṇaṃ | vṛṣabhaṃ | maṃdra 'jihvaṃ | bṛhaspatiṃ | vardhaya | navyaṃ | arkaiḥ |*
> *gāthānyaḥ | su 'rucaḥ | yasya | devāḥ | ā 'śṛṇvaṃti | navamānasya | martāḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed. "draṣṭavyaṃ": the first akṣara is partly broken (zoomed); "Ni. 6-23" zoomed.)*

> हे होतः नव्यं नवतरं स्तुत्यं वा तमनर्वाणमगंतारं । स्तोतुरधीनमित्यर्थः । वृषभमपां फलानां वर्षितारं मंद्रजिह्वं मादकवाचकं बृहस्पतिं मंत्रस्य पालयितारमेतन्नामकं देवमर्कैरर्चनसाधनैर्मंत्रैर्वर्धय । प्रवृद्धं कुरु । सुरुचः शोभनदीप्तेर्नवमानस्य स्तूयमानस्य । कर्मणि कर्तृप्रत्ययः ॥ यस्य बृहस्पतेः ॥ कर्मणि षष्ठ्यौ ॥ रोचमानं स्तूयमानं गाथान्यः । गाथेति वाङ्नाम । स्तुतिवचसो नेतारो देवा व्यवहर्तारो मर्ता मनुष्या होत्रादयः । यद्वा । नवमानस्य स्तुवानस्य यजमानस्य संबंधिनस्ते । आशृण्वंति आश्रावयंति पुरा तं बृहस्पतिं वर्धय । अत्रानर्वाणमप्रत्यृतमन्यस्मिन्नित्यादि निरुक्तं द्रष्टव्यं । नि. ६-२३ ॥

> *he hotaḥ navyaṃ navataraṃ stutyaṃ vā tamanarvāṇamagaṃtāraṃ | stoturadhīnamityarthaḥ | vṛṣabhamapāṃ phalānāṃ varṣitāraṃ maṃdrajihvaṃ mādakavācakaṃ bṛhaspatiṃ maṃtrasya pālayitārametannāmakaṃ devamarkairarcanasādhanairmaṃtrairvardhaya | pravṛddhaṃ kuru | surucaḥ śobhanadīpternavamānasya stūyamānasya | karmaṇi kartṛpratyayaḥ ‖ yasya bṛhaspateḥ ‖ karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhyau ‖ rocamānaṃ stūyamānaṃ gāthānyaḥ | gātheti vāṅnāma | stutivacaso netāro devā vyavahartāro martā manuṣyā hotrādayaḥ | yadvā | navamānasya stuvānasya yajamānasya saṃbaṃdhinaste | āśṛṇvaṃti āśrāvayaṃti purā taṃ bṛhaspatiṃ vardhaya | atrānarvāṇamapratyṛtamanyasminnityādi niruktaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ | ni. 6-23 ‖*

### Printed p. 307 (PDF 326)

*(Header: "A. 2. A. 5. Va. 12" (zoomed). Ṛk 1: Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics begun.)*

**Pratipadārtha.** (O Hotṛ) सुरुचः (*surucaḥ*) — who has beautiful lustre; नवमानस्य (*navamānasya*) — and who is being praised; यस्य (*yasya*) — of which Bṛhaspati (the praise); गाथान्यः (*gāthānyaḥ*) — who are the makers and leaders of words of praise; देवाः (*devāḥ*) — the gods; मर्ताः (*martāḥ*) — and men; आशृण्वंति (*āśṛṇvaṃti*) — proclaim and make heard; such a one; नव्यं (*navyaṃ*) — who is praiseworthy; अनर्वाणं (*anarvāṇaṃ*) — who does not go to another place (leaving the praiser); वृषभं (*vṛṣabhaṃ*) — who showers desired objects; मंद्रजिह्वं (*maṃdrajihvaṃ*) — who has gladdening speech; बृहस्पतिं (*bṛhaspatiṃ*) — Bṛhaspati, the protector of the mantra; अर्कैः (*arkaiḥ*) — by mantras, the means of worship; वर्धय (*vardhaya*) — make him grow (praise him).

**Bhāvārtha.** By mantras that are the means of worship make Bṛhaspati grow — him of beautiful lustre, worthy of praise, whose praise the gods and men, leaders of words of praise, proclaim and make heard; who is praiseworthy, who stays bound to the praiser, who showers desired objects, whose speech gladdens, and who is the protector of the mantra.

**English Translation (as printed).**

Priests, augment by your hymns Brihaspati, who deserts not (his worshipper) ; the showerer (of benefits), the pleasant-tongued, the adorable ; of whom resplendent, gods and men, (the ministers) of the institutor of the sacrifice, emulous in sacred songs, proclaim (the praise)

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

**अनर्वाणं (*anarvāṇaṃ*)** — अगंतारं स्तोतुरधीनमित्यर्थः (*agaṃtāraṃ stoturadhīnamityarthaḥ*) । Sāyaṇa has explained it as "not going away from the vicinity of the sacrificer who praises, that is, being subject to the sacrificer who praises". According to the Niruktakāra this word means —

> अप्रत्यृतः अप्रतिगतोऽन्यस्मिन् अन्यमनाश्रितः स्वतंत्र इत्यर्थः

> *apratyṛtaḥ apratigato 'nyasmin anyamanāśritaḥ svataṃtra ityarthaḥ*

(Ni-4-27, as printed; zoomed)

— that is, one who does not look for the help of another, independent. There is room here for both kinds of meaning.

**वृषभं (*vṛṣabhaṃ*)** — अपां फलानां वर्षितारं (*apāṃ phalānāṃ varṣitāraṃ*) । We have explained the derivation of the word *vṛṣabha* at length in the Ṛ. Saṃ., Part 5, page 682, Part 8, page 168, and other places. In the present ṛk it means "who showers fruits in the form of water" *(a stray mark is printed after "surisuvavanu" [sic])*. On Bṛhaspati being a helper in granting rain, see what is said in the Pīṭhike of this sūkta (page 301).

### Printed p. 308 (PDF 327)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 190". Ṛk 1: Special Topics continued.)*

**मंद्रजिह्वं (*maṃdrajihvaṃ*)** — मादकवाचं (*mādakavācaṃ*) *(so printed here; the bhāṣya on p. 306 has "mādakavācakaṃ")* । One who has a tongue (*nālage*) that speaks words producing joy in the mind; that is, one who speaks delightful words so that those who praise him are pleased.

**अर्कैः (*arkaiḥ*)** — अर्चनसाधनैर्मंत्रैः (*arcanasādhanairmaṃtraiḥ*) । By mantras that are the means of praising. Because they are used for praising, mantras are named *arkas*. For the word *arka* Yāska —

> अर्को देवो भवति यदेनमर्चंति । अर्को मंत्रो भवति यदनेनार्चंति
> अर्कमन्नं भवत्यर्चति भूतानि । अर्को वृक्षो भवति संवृत्तः कटुकिम्ना ॥

> *arko devo bhavati yadenamarcaṃti | arko maṃtro bhavati yadanenārcaṃti*
> *arkamannaṃ bhavatyarcati bhūtāni | arko vṛkṣo bhavati saṃvṛttaḥ kaṭukimnā ‖*

(Ni. 5-4, zoomed)

— has stated a meaning of four kinds —

(1)

> अर्को देवो भवति यदेनमर्चंति । तावत्सर्व एवार्क इत्युच्यते यद्यस्मादेनं देवं अर्चंति स्तोतारः ॥

> *arko devo bhavati yadenamarcaṃti | tāvatsarva evārka ityucyate yadyasmādenaṃ devaṃ arcaṃti stotāraḥ ‖*

The word *arka* means the deity: because the person or god whom devotees use (it) to worship, that is, the object (the deity) which devotees worship, is named *arka*.

(2)

> अर्को मंत्रो भवति । यद्यस्मात् अनेन मंत्रेण अर्चंति स्तोतारः तस्मादर्कः ॥

> *arko maṃtro bhavati | yadyasmāt anena maṃtreṇa arcaṃti stotāraḥ tasmādarkaḥ ‖*

The word *arka* also means mantra: because those who praise worship the deity with it (with the *arka*, that is, with the mantra). Therefore the word *arka* also names the mantra.

(3)

> अर्कमन्नं भवति । तद्धि अर्चति भूतानि यो हि पूज्यः तस्यान्नमपि संस्कारविशेषेण संस्कृतं पूजायां क्रियते पूज्यं च सर्वस्यैवान्नं ।

> *arkamannaṃ bhavati | taddhi arcati bhūtāni yo hi pūjyaḥ tasyānnamapi saṃskāraviśeṣeṇa saṃskṛtaṃ pūjāyāṃ kriyate pūjyaṃ ca sarvasyaivānnaṃ |*

The word *arka* also means food. Because food (nourishment) is necessary to all living beings, everyone seeks it, honouring it with regard; that is, because everyone desires it, honouring it with love and regard, the word *arka* also means food.

(4)

> अर्को वृक्षो भवति य एष प्रसिद्धः । संवृत्तः हि संगतः संव्याप्तः कटुकिम्ना कटुकभावेन भवति ॥

> *arko vṛkṣo bhavati ya eṣa prasiddhaḥ | saṃvṛttaḥ hi saṃgataḥ saṃvyāptaḥ kaṭukimnā kaṭukabhāvena bhavati ‖*

Further, the name "tree" for the word *arka* is well known. The *arka* tree is called *ekkada giḍa* in the Kannada language. Because its sacrificial sticks are used in homas, and because it is customary to use it in medicines and the like, the *arka* tree is a thing known to all. Because it is bitter they call it कटुकिम्ना (*kaṭukimnā*). As an example for the explanation of the word *arka*, Yāska (cites) गायंति त्वा (*gāyaṃti tvā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-10-1, zoomed) …

### Printed p. 309 (PDF 328)

*(Header: "A. 2. A 5. Va. 12." (zoomed). Ṛk 1: Special Topics concluded; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā begun.)*

— taking the ṛk (beginning गायंति त्वा, *gāyaṃti tvā*) he has given its derivation. That explanation is not relevant here. In the present ṛk the bhāṣyakāra has accepted the meaning "mantra" for the word *arka*.

**गाथान्यः (*gāthānyaḥ*)** — Because the word *gāthā* is read among the fifty-seven names of speech, *śloka*, *dhārā* and the rest (Ni. [?]-[?]3 — the first two digits undecided after zooming), *gāthā* means words in the form of praise. गाथा नयंतीति गाथान्यः (*gāthā nayaṃtīti gāthānyaḥ*) । The sense is: the gods who are the leaders of such mantras in the form of praise, and the Hotṛ and other priests who recite the mantras.

**अथवा नवमानस्य (संबंधिनस्ते) गाथान्यः आशृण्वंति आश्रावयंति (*athavā navamānasya (saṃbaṃdhinaste) gāthānyaḥ āśṛṇvaṃti āśrāvayaṃti*)** । For this sentence the bhāṣyakāra has also given another kind of meaning: the Hotṛ and the others, who are connected with the sacrificer who is praising, recite the mantras to Bṛhaspati and satisfy him.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, noted briefly).** अनर्वाणम् (*anarvāṇam*) — end-acute of the final member by नञ्सुभ्याम् (*nañsubhyām*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-172, read from the strip); accusative singular *(a stray mark is printed before "dvitīyā" [sic])*; because अर्वणस्त्रसावनञः (*arvaṇastrasāvanañaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-172, as printed; zoomed and compared with the header digits) excludes it by "anañaḥ", *tṛ* does not come as the final substitute. मंद्रजिह्वम् (*maṃdrajihvam*) — मंद्रा जिह्वा यस्य सः । तम् (*maṃdrā jihvā yasya saḥ | tam*); the first member keeps its own accent by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1, zoomed). वर्धय (*vardhaya*) — root वृधु वर्धने (*vṛdhu vardhane*); causative activity, so *ṇic* by हेतुमति च (*hetumati ca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-26, zoomed); *loṭ* on the *ṇic*-stem, second person singular; nighāta, as it follows a word that is not a finite verb. गाथान्यः (*gāthānyaḥ*) — root णीञ् प्रापणे (*ṇīñ prāpaṇe*); *n* for the initial by णो नः (*ṇo naḥ*); गाथाः नयंति इति गाथान्यः (*gāthāḥ nayaṃti iti gāthānyaḥ*); suffix *kvip*; the *ī* udātta by the accent of a *kṛt*-final member; before *jas*, *yaṇ* substitution; the *yaṇ* standing in the udātta's place and an anudātta case-ending following, svarita by उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः (*udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-2-4, zoomed). आशृण्वंति (*āśṛṇvaṃti*) — root श्रु श्रवणे (*śru śravaṇe*); *laṭ*, third person plural *jha*; *anta* for it by झोऽन्तः (*jho 'ntaḥ*); *śṛ* for the root by श्रुवः शृ च (*śruvaḥ śṛ ca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-74, read from the strip); vikaraṇa *śnu*; *yaṇ*; at the head of the pāda, so no nighāta; initial-acute of the suffix; the *gati* (*āṅ*) anudātta by तिङि चोदात्तवति (*tiṅi codāttavati*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-71, read from the strip). नवमानस्य (*navamānasya*) — root णु स्तुतौ (*ṇu stutau*); *n* for the initial by णो नः (*ṇo naḥ*); *śānac* for *laṭ*; by *vyatyaya* the active suffix in the passive sense; vikaraṇa *śap*; सार्वधातुकार्ध— (*sārvadhātukārdha—*) … *(continues on p. 310)*

(continuing सार्वधातुकार्ध— (*sārvadhātukārdha—*) …) by which guṇa of the root's *u*; *av* substitution; the augment *muk* by आने मुक् (*āne muk*) (Pā. #### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Accents not reproduced.)*

> तमृत्विया उप वाचः सचंते सर्गो न यो देवयतामसर्जि ।
> बृहस्पतिः स ह्यंजो वरांसि विभ्वाभवत्समृते मातरिश्वा ॥ २ ॥

> *tamṛtviyā upa vācaḥ sacaṃte sargo na yo devayatāmasarji |*
> *bṛhaspatiḥ sa hyaṃjo varāṃsi vibhvābhavatsamṛte mātariśvā ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> तं । ऋत्वियाः । उप । वाचः । सचंते । सर्गः । न । यः । देवऽयतां । असर्जि ।
> बृहस्पतिः । सः । हि । अंजः । वरांसि । विऽभ्वा । अभवत् । सं । ऋते । मातरिश्वा ॥ २ ॥

> *taṃ | ṛtviyāḥ | upa | vācaḥ | sacaṃte | sargaḥ | na | yaḥ | deva 'yatāṃ | asarji |*
> *bṛhaspatiḥ | saḥ | hi | aṃjaḥ | varāṃsi | vi 'bhvā | abhavat | saṃ | ṛte | mātariśvā ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; "Ā. 3-7" zoomed; "upa saṃcate" so printed in the gloss (the Saṃhitā has "sacaṃte"); "sṛṣṭavānvṛṣṭyudakaṃ" zoomed.)*

*Gist:* The verse is the vapā-yājyā for Bṛhaspati's animal; the season's (rain-season) voices of the middle region attend on Bṛhaspati, who released water (or fruit) for the god-seekers; he, the manifester, became pervading, producing desirable fruits when water is at hand — or, alternatively, in the sacrifice, desiring oblations.

> बार्हस्पत्ये पशौ तमृत्वियेत्येषा वपायाज्या । सूत्रितं च । बृहस्पते अति यदर्यो अर्हात्तमृत्विया उप वाचः सचंते । आ. ३-७ । इति ॥
> तं बृहस्पतिमृत्विया वर्षर्तुसंबंधिन्यो वाचो माध्यमिका उप संचते । समीपे सेवंते । यः सर्गो नोदकस्य स्रष्टापि । नशब्दोऽप्यर्थे । देवयतां देवानिच्छतां यजमानानामसर्जि फलं । यद्वा । देवं तमिच्छतां मनुष्याणामसर्जि सृष्टवान्वृष्ट्युदकं । यद्वा । ऋत्वियाः प्राप्तकालीना वाचो होत्रादिप्रेरिता वाच उप सचंते तं यः सर्गो नोदकसृष्टिरिव सः स एव बृहस्पतिरंजो हि व्यंजकः खलु । तस्मिन्वर्षति सर्वे भवंति । अत एव विभ्वा विभुर्व्याप्तो मातरिश्वा वृष्टिनिर्मातर्यंतरिक्षे चेष्टमानो वायुसदृशो वा वरांसि वरणीयानि वृष्ट्यादिफलानि संपादयन्नृत उदके निमित्तभूते सति समभवत् । संभूतः । अथवा । अंजो यज्ञियानां व्यंजको मातरिश्वा फलस्य निर्मातरि यज्ञे श्वसिता वर्तमानः स बृहस्पतिर्ऋते यज्ञे निमित्तभूते सति वरांसि वरणीयानि हवींषीच्छन् विभ्वा विभुः समभवत् ॥

> *bārhaspatye paśau tamṛtviyetyeṣā vapāyājyā | sūtritaṃ ca | bṛhaspate ati yadaryo arhāttamṛtviyā upa vācaḥ sacaṃte | ā. 3-7 | iti ‖*
> *taṃ bṛhaspatimṛtviyā varṣartusaṃbaṃdhinyo vāco mādhyamikā upa saṃcate | samīpe sevaṃte | yaḥ sargo nodakasya sraṣṭāpi | naśabdo 'pyarthe | devayatāṃ devānicchatāṃ yajamānānāmasarji phalaṃ | yadvā | devaṃ tamicchatāṃ manuṣyāṇāmasarji sṛṣṭavānvṛṣṭyudakaṃ | yadvā | ṛtviyāḥ prāptakālīnā vāco hotrādipreritā vāca upa sacaṃte taṃ yaḥ sargo nodakasṛṣṭiriva saḥ sa eva bṛhaspatiraṃjo hi vyaṃjakaḥ khalu | tasminvarṣati sarve bhavaṃti | ata eva vibhvā vibhurvyāpto mātariśvā vṛṣṭinirmātaryaṃtarikṣe ceṣṭamāno vāyusadṛśo vā varāṃsi varaṇīyāni vṛṣṭyādiphalāni saṃpādayannṛta udake nimittabhūte sati samabhavat | saṃbhūtaḥ | athavā | aṃjo yajñiyānāṃ vyaṃjako mātariśvā phalasya nirmātari yajñe śvasitā vartamānaḥ sa bṛhaspatirṛte yajñe nimittabhūte sati varāṃsi varaṇīyāni havīṃṣīcchan vibhvā vibhuḥ samabhavat ‖*

### Printed p. 311 (PDF 330)

*(Header: "A. 2. A. 5. Va. 12". Ṛk 2: Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics begun.)*

**Pratipadārtha.** यः (*yaḥ*) — which Bṛhaspati; सर्गो न (*sargo na*) — was also the creator (of water) (and); देवयतां (*devayatāṃ*) — for the sacrificers who seek the gods for help; असर्जि (*asarji*) — creates and hands over the fruit; तं (*taṃ*) — that Bṛhaspati; ऋत्वियाः (*ṛtviyāḥ*) — belonging to the rainy season; वाचः (*vācaḥ*) — the words of the middle region; उप सचंते (*upa sacaṃte*) — approach and serve; सः बृहस्पतिः (*saḥ bṛhaspatiḥ*) — that same Bṛhaspati; अंजः हि (*aṃjaḥ hi*) — is he not the one who makes everything manifest?; विभ्वा (*vibhvā*) — who pervades; मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*) — he who moves in the mid-region, or who is like the wind; वरांसि (*varāṃsi*) — procuring the desired fruits such as rain; ऋते (*ṛte*) — for the sake of water; समभवत् (*samabhavat*) — was born.

**Bhāvārtha.** The words of the middle region belonging to the rainy season approach and serve Bṛhaspati, who creates water and who creates and hands over the fruit in the form of rain to the sacrificer seeking the gods for help. That same Bṛhaspati makes everything manifest. And by his impulse alone the wind, which pervades everywhere and moves in the mid-region, was born for the sake of water, procuring the desired rain and the rest.

**English Translation (as printed; heading printed "English Translatin" [sic]).**

The hymns of the (rainy) season are addressed to him, who is verily the creator (of the rain), and has granted it (to the prayers) of the devout ; for that Brihaspati is the manifester (of all), the expansive wind that (dispensing) blessing has been produced for (the diffusion of water).

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

In the animal sacrifice, when the vapā-homa is performed addressed to Bṛhaspati, this ṛk तमृत्विया (*tamṛtviyā*) is to be used as the yājyā mantra — this is set out by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra, बृहस्पते अति यदर्यो अर्हात्तमृत्विया उप वाचः सचंते (*bṛhaspate ati yadaryo arhāttamṛtviyā upa vācaḥ sacaṃte*) (Ā. 3-7, as on p. 310).

**ऋत्विया (*ṛtviyā*)** — वर्षर्तुसंबंधिन्यो वाचः (*varṣartusaṃbaṃdhinyo vācaḥ*) । Since Bṛhaspati is connected with rain, they are called here words connected with the rainy season.

**न (*na*)** — The word *na* is used here in the sense of conjunction (in the sense of अपि, *api*). Besides —

> नेति प्रतिषेधार्थीयो भाषायां । उभयमन्वध्यायं ।

> *neti pratiṣedhārthīyo bhāṣāyāṃ | ubhayamanvadhyāyaṃ |*

— that is, in ordinary usage … *(continues on p. 312)*

### Printed p. 312 (PDF 331)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 190". Ṛk 2: Special Topics concluded; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā.)*

— in the spoken language the word *na* has the sense of negation (it indicates the sense "is not"); in the Veda it indicates two kinds, that is, the sense of negation and the sense of comparison: this is Yāska's explanation (Ni. 1-4, zoomed).

**मातरिश्वा (*mātariśvā*)** — सर्वस्य जगतः निर्मातरि अंतरिक्षे श्वसन् वर्तमानः (*sarvasya jagataḥ nirmātari aṃtarikṣe śvasan vartamānaḥ*) । "Being in the mid-region, which is the maker of the whole world": this is the sense of the derivation of the word *mātariśvā*. The word may mean the deities Agni, Vāyu and so on. Here Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning as "like the wind", that is, pervading in the mid-region.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, noted briefly).** ऋत्वियाः (*ṛtviyāḥ*) — suffix *ghas* to the word *ṛtu* by छंदसि घस् (*chaṃdasi ghas*) (Pā. Sū. 5-1-106, zoomed); *iya* for it by आयनेयीनीयियः— (*āyaneyīnīyiyaḥ—*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-2, zoomed); the suffix being *nit* *(so printed)*, by सिति च (*siti ca*) (Pā. Sū. 1-4-16, zoomed) the *pada* designation comes as an exception to the *bha* designation, so no guṇa of the *u* by ओर्गुणः (*orguṇaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-146, zoomed); *yaṇ*; initial-acute of the suffix. सचंते (*sacaṃte*) — root षच समवाये (*ṣaca samavāye*); *s* for the initial; *laṭ* third person plural; nighāta, as it follows a word that is not a finite verb. देवयताम् (*devayatām*) — देवान् आत्मनः इच्छंतः देवयंतः तेषाम् (*devān ātmanaḥ icchaṃtaḥ devayaṃtaḥ teṣām*); *kyac* by सुप आत्मनः क्यच् (*supa ātmanaḥ kyac*); on it *laṭ*, *śatṛ* for it; genitive plural; a vowel-initial case-ending following the *śatṛ* without *num*, udātta for it by शतुरनुमो नद्यजादी (*śaturanumo nadyajādī*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-173, zoomed). असर्जि (*asarji*) — root सृज विसर्गे (*sṛja visarge*); *luṅ* in the passive; third person singular *ta*; *ciṇ* for *cli* by चिण् भावकर्मणोः (*ciṇ bhāvakarmaṇoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-66, zoomed); guṇa of the light penultimate; *luk* of the suffix after *ciṇ* by चिणो लुक् (*ciṇo luk*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-104, zoomed); augment *aṭ*; connection with *yat*, so nighāta is barred by यद्वृत्तान्नित्यम् (*yadvṛttānnityam*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66, zoomed); initial-acute by the accent of *aṭ*. अञ्जः (*añjaḥ*) — root अंजू व्यक्तिम्रक्षणकांतिगतिषु (*aṃjū vyaktimrakṣaṇakāṃtigatiṣu*); suffix *ac*, applicable to all roots; being *nit* *(so printed)*, initial-acute. वरांसि (*varāṃsi*) — root वृञ् वरणे (*vṛñ varaṇe*); suffix *asun* as before; with it as cause, guṇa of the root's *ṛ* by सार्वधातुका— (*sārvadhātukā—*); accusative plural.

विभ्वा (*vibhvā*) — root भू सत्तायाम् (*bhū sattāyām*); with *vi* as upapada, suffix *ḍu* by विप्रसंभ्यो ड्वसंज्ञायाम् (*viprasaṃbhyo ḍvasaṃjñāyām*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-180, zoomed); being *ḍit*, elision of the *ṭi*: the form *vibhu*; before *su*, *ā* for it by सुपां सुलुक्— (*supāṃ suluk—*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39, zoomed); the *yaṇ* due by ओः सुपि (*oḥ supi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-83, zoomed) is barred by न भूसुधियोः (*na bhūsudhiyoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-85, zoomed); *yaṇ* again by छंदस्युभयथा (*chaṃdasyubhayathā*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-86, zoomed); initial-acute by *vyatyaya*. Or: Uṇādi suffix *ḍun* to *bhū* preceded by *vi*; being *nit*, initial-acute by ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ñnityādirnityam*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197, zoomed).

#### Ṛk 3

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Accents not reproduced; "ahanyo3 yo" with the pluti numeral, zoomed.)*

> उपस्तुतिं नमस उद्यतिं च श्लोकं यंसत्सवितेव प्र बाहू ।
> अस्य क्रत्वाहन्यो३ यो अस्ति मृगो न भीमो अरक्षसस्तुविष्मान् ॥ ३ ॥

> *upastutiṃ namasa udyatiṃ ca ślokaṃ yaṃsatsaviteva pra bāhū |*
> *asya kratvāhanyo3 yo asti mṛgo na bhīmo arakṣasastuviṣmān ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥** *(Heading printed "padapāṭha" without visarga.)*

> उपऽस्तुतिं । नमसः । उत्ऽयतिं । च । श्लोकं । यंसत् । सविताऽइव । प्र । बाहू इति ।
> अस्य । क्रत्वा । अहन्यः । यः । अस्ति । मृगः । न । भीमः । अरक्षसः । तुविष्मान् ॥ ३ ॥

> *upa 'stutiṃ | namasaḥ | ut 'yatiṃ | ca | ślokaṃ | yaṃsat | savitā 'iva | pra | bāhū iti |*
> *asya | kratvā | ahanyaḥ | yaḥ | asti | mṛgaḥ | na | bhīmaḥ | arakṣasaḥ | tuviṣmān ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(Sanskrit, transcribed; "prayacchatyasmai" is followed by a printed "!" for the daṇḍa [sic]. Continues on p. 314.)*

> अयं बृहस्पतिरुपस्तुतिं यजमानेनोपेत्य क्रियमाणां स्तुतिं नमसो हविर्लक्षणस्यान्नस्योद्यतिमुद्धारं च श्लोकमन्यो यो मंत्रविशेषोऽस्ति तं च प्र यंसत् । प्रकर्षेण यतते स्वीकर्तुं । यजमानो वा तत्सर्वं प्रयच्छत्यस्मै । तत्र दृष्टांतः । सवितेव सूर्य इव स यथा स्तोत्रादिकं स्वीकरोति तद्वत् । यजमानप्रदानपक्षे सविता सर्वस्य प्रसविता सूर्य इव । स यथा बाहुभ्यः प्रकाशादि प्रयच्छति तद्वद्बाहू बाहुभ्यां यजमानोऽपीत्यर्थः । तस्य महत्त्वमाह । अरक्षसः …

> *ayaṃ bṛhaspatirupastutiṃ yajamānenopetya kriyamāṇāṃ stutiṃ namaso havirlakṣaṇasyānnasyodyatimuddhāraṃ ca ślokamanyo yo maṃtraviśeṣo 'sti taṃ ca pra yaṃsat | prakarṣeṇa yatate svīkartuṃ | yajamāno vā tatsarvaṃ prayacchatyasmai | tatra dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ | saviteva sūrya iva sa yathā stotrādikaṃ svīkaroti tadvat | yajamānapradānapakṣe savitā sarvasya prasavitā sūrya iva | sa yathā bāhubhyaḥ prakāśādi prayacchati tadvadbāhū bāhubhyāṃ yajamāno 'pītyarthaḥ | tasya mahattvamāha | arakṣasaḥ …*

### Printed p. 314 (PDF 333)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 190". Ṛk 3: end of the bhāṣya; Pratipadārtha; Bhāvārtha; printed English; Special Topics begun.)*

*Gist (rest of the bhāṣya):* The Sun, free of Rākṣasas hostile to him, shines by his power, terrible and strong like a beast; by Bṛhaspati's might the sacrificer's offering is accepted.

> स्वविरोधिरक्षोरहितस्यास्य बृहस्पतेः क्रत्वा कर्मणा सामर्थ्येनाहन्योऽह्नि साधुर्यः सूर्योऽस्ति स भीमो न मृग इव भयजनकः सिंहादिरिव भीमो भयहेतुस्तुविष्मान् बलवान् परिभ्रमतीति शेषः । यस्य माहात्म्येन मंत्राभिमानिनो बृहस्पतेः सामर्थ्यान्मंदेहाद्यसुराञ्जित्वातितेजस्वी भवति तादृशो महानुभावो यजमानदत्तं हविरादिकं स्वीकरोतीत्यर्थः ॥

> *svavirodhirakṣorahitasyāsya bṛhaspateḥ kratvā karmaṇā sāmarthyenāhanyo 'hni sādhuryaḥ sūryo 'sti sa bhīmo na mṛga iva bhayajanakaḥ siṃhādiriva bhīmo bhayahetustuviṣmān balavān paribhramatīti śeṣaḥ | yasya māhātmyena maṃtrābhimānino bṛhaspateḥ sāmarthyānmaṃdehādyasurāñjitvātitejasvī bhavati tādṛśo mahānubhāvo yajamānadattaṃ havirādikaṃ svīkarotītyarthaḥ ‖*

**Pratipadārtha.** सविता (*savitā*) — the sun; प्र बाहू इव (*pra bāhū iva*) — as he spreads out his hands (rays); अयं (*ayaṃ*) — this Bṛhaspati; उपस्तुतिं (*upastutiṃ*) — the praise recited (by the sacrificer); नमसः (*namasaḥ*) — of the food in the form of oblation; उद्यतिं (*udyatiṃ*) — the offering; श्लोकं (*ślokaṃ*) — the other kinds of mantras; प्र यंसत् (*pra yaṃsat*) — strives, out of his own wish, to accept. Or: as the sun spreads out his rays and gives light, so the sacrificer too spreads out his arms and offers praises and the like; अरक्षसः (*arakṣasaḥ*) — made so that there are no Rākṣasas hostile to him; अस्य (*asya*) — of this Bṛhaspati; क्रत्वा (*kratvā*) — by power; अहन्यः (*ahanyaḥ*) — he who shines, making the day; यः अस्ति (*yaḥ asti*) — whichever sun there is (सः (*saḥ*) — he); मृगो न (*mṛgo na*) — like a cruel beast; भीमः (*bhīmaḥ*) — terrible; तुविष्मान् (*tuviṣmān*) — strong.

**Bhāvārtha.** As the sun spreads out his rays, so this Bṛhaspati strives, out of his own wish, to accept the praise recited by the sacrificer, the food offered by him and the other special mantras. This Bṛhaspati, who has made it so that there are no Rākṣasas hostile to him, makes by his power the sun shine, making the day; and that sun is terrible like a cruel beast and strong.

**English Translation (as printed; heading printed "Englih Tranlation" [sic]).**

He is ready (to accept) the offered praise, the presentation of the homage· the hymn, as the sun (is ready to put forth) his rays ; by the acts of him whom the Rakshasas (oppose not), the daily (revolving sun) exists, and he is strong as a fearful beast of prey· *(stray points after "homage" and "prey" [sic])*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu).**

On the first half of this ṛk Sāyaṇa has given two kinds of meaning. This Bṛhaspati, hearing the stotra which the sacrificer makes sitting near, stretches out his hands and accepts the food in the form of an oblation, the mantra in the form of praise, and as the sun accepts hymns and the like *(continues on p. 315)*

---

### Printed p. 315 (PDF 334)

*(Header: "A. 2. A. 5. Va. 12" (the varga numeral read from the strip, not zoomed). Ṛk 3: Special Topics continued, grammar. Note: the scan repeats this page as PDF 335; see the progress note.)*

— (accepts) so — this is one kind of meaning. Or: while this sacrificer praises Bṛhaspati, as the sun, the cause of the whole world, gives by his rays in the form of arms light and the like (brightness, warmth) to the people of the world, so this sacrificer too stretches out his hands to Bṛhaspati and offers the oblation-food and the other mantras in the form of praise — this is the other kind of meaning. For both these meanings there is room here.

In the latter half Bṛhaspati's power and valour are described. **अरक्षसः (*arakṣasaḥ*)** — one who has no Rākṣasas hostile to him; that is, none among the Rākṣasas has the strength and power to withstand this Bṛhaspati. **तुविष्मान् (*tuviṣmān*)** — very strong. **मृगो न भीमः (*mṛgo na bhīmaḥ*)** — terrible in majesty like a lion or other beast. The simile मृगो न भीमः (*mṛgo na bhīmaḥ*) for one of great valour is given in many places in the Ṛgveda —

> प्र तद्विष्णुस्तवते वीर्येण मृगो न भीमः कुचरो गिरिष्ठाः ।

> *pra tadviṣṇustavate vīryeṇa mṛgo na bhīmaḥ kucaro giriṣṭhāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-154-2) *(mine and tentative: "Viṣṇu is praised for that heroism, terrible like a beast, roaming, dwelling on the mountains")*

> मृगो न हस्ती तविषीमुषाणः सिंहो न भीमः आयुधानि बिभ्रत् ॥

> *mṛgo na hastī taviṣīmuṣāṇaḥ siṃho na bhīmaḥ āyudhāni bibhrat ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-16-14, middle digit [?]) *(mine and tentative: "like a beast, an elephant, ... strength; terrible like a lion, bearing weapons")*

> अश्वो न क्रदो वृषभिर्युजानः सिंहो न भीमो मनसो जवीयान् ।

> *aśvo na krado vṛṣabhiryujānaḥ siṃho na bhīmo manaso javīyān |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-97-28) *(mine and tentative: "like a horse ... yoked ...; terrible like a lion, swifter than the mind")*

> आशुः शिशानो वृषभो न भीमो घनाघनः क्षोभणश्चर्षणीनां ॥

> *āśuḥ śiśāno vṛṣabho na bhīmo ghanāghanaḥ kṣobhaṇaścarṣaṇīnāṃ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-103-1) *(mine and tentative: "swift, sharpening himself, terrible like a bull, the smiter of smiters, the agitator of the peoples")*

— in these ṛks the word भीम (*bhīma*) is used in the sense of terrible valour, with the comparison of strong beasts such as the lion and the bull.

**॥ व्याकरणप्रक्रिया ॥ — Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammar, noted briefly).** **नमसः (*namasaḥ*)** — root णमु प्रह्वत्वे शब्दे च (*ṇamu prahvatve śabde ca*); *n* for the initial by णो नः (*ṇo naḥ*) (sūtra number not printed); Uṇādi suffix *asun*; being *nit*, initial-acute; genitive singular in another form. **यंसत् (*yaṃsat*)** — root यम उपरमे (*yama uparame*); *leṭ*, third person singular; *sip* by सिब्बहुलं लेटि (*sibbahulaṃ leṭi*) (Vā. Sū. 3-1-34); nighāta accent by तिङ्ङतिङः (*tiṅṅatiṅaḥ*) (as it looks). **बाहू (*bāhū*)** — by *vyatyaya* the first dual has come in place of the third dual; end-acute by the accent of the suffix. **अहन्यः (*ahanyaḥ*)** — अह्नि भवः (*ahni bhavaḥ*) "one who is in the day"; suffix *yat* in the sense of "being"; being *tit*, the *svarita* accent by तित्स्वरितम् (*titsvaritam*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-185).

### Printed p. 316 (PDF 336; PDF 335 is a second copy of printed p. 315)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 190" with a stray mark before "A." [sic]. Ṛk 3: grammar concluded; Ṛk 4: Saṃhitā, Pada, bhāṣya.)*

**अस्ति (*asti*)** — since यः (*yaḥ*) stands before it, the nighāta accent is barred by यद्वृत्तान्नित्यम् (*yadvṛttānnityam*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66); the root's accent remains, the suffix being *pit*. **भीमः (*bhīmaḥ*)** — root ञिभी भये (*ñibhī bhaye*) (as it looks); suffix *mak* by भियः षुग्वा (*bhiyaḥ ṣugvā*) (U. Sū. 1-145, as printed); end-acute by the accent of the suffix. Yāska explains "भीमः भिभ्यत्यस्मात् (*bhīmaḥ bibhyatyasmāt*)" (Ni. 1-20).
