### Printed p. 345 (PDF 365)

*(Header: "A. 2. A. 5 Va. 14", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Ṛk 5: Special Topics, Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā.)*

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)** *(Special Topics)*

त्ये (*tye*) — ते (*te*). In the Ṛgveda the word त्यद् (*tyad*) is commonly used in many places in place of तद् (*tad*) (printed "tacchabda"); it is a usage of the language of the hymns.

> एता उ त्या उषसः केतुमक्रत पूर्वे अर्धे रजसो भानुमंजते ।

> *etā u tyā uṣasaḥ ketumakrata pūrve ardhe rajaso bhānumaṃjate |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-1.) In ṛks of this kind त्याः (*tyāḥ*) means ताः (*tāḥ*).

प्रत्यदृश्रन् प्रदोषं (*pratyadṛśran pradoṣaṃ*) — "they are seen at night": in the night-time that is full of darkness the snakes are generally recognised by the sounds of their breathing; this is the sense.

तस्करा इव (*taskarā iva*) — the thief is given as the example of moving about in darkness. It is well known in the world that thieves commit their thieving at night, when the darkness is thick, so that no one may see them while everyone sleeps. In the same way these wicked snakes move about in the night full of darkness and bring harm to people.

अदृष्टाः विश्वदृष्टाः (*adṛṣṭāḥ viśvadṛṣṭāḥ*) — People cannot look at snakes that move about in the darkness or that creep about. (continued on p. 346)

Therefore they are as if unseen to the eye. Yet they alone can see everyone. Because of this ability it is possible that greater harm comes to people from them. Therefore the ṛṣi says —

प्रतिबुद्धा अभूतन (*pratibuddhā abhūtana*) — "O people, you must be very watchful about these snakes": thus he informs the people.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*

त्ये (*tye*): the word त्यद् (*tyad*); in the nominative plural jas is replaced by ति (*ti*) (printed so); by the sūtra त्यदादीनामः (*tyadādīnāmaḥ*) (no number printed) the final is replaced by a (atva), with the following form as the single replacement (pararūpa); guṇa.

अदृश्रन् (*adṛśran*): root दृशिर् प्रेक्षणे (*dṛśir prekṣaṇe*); luṅ in the sense of the present by Vedic usage; by इरितो वा (*irito vā*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-57) cli gets aṅ; by बहुलं छन्दसि (*bahulaṃ chandasi*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-8) jhi gets ruṭ; tiṅanta-nighāta accent.

तस्कराः (*taskarāḥ*): तद्बृहतोः करपत्योः (*tadbṛhatoḥ karapatyoḥ*) [?] (Vā. [?]): when the word tat is followed by the word kara/pati in the sense "thief", the augment suṭ comes in the middle and the d of tad is dropped.

विश्वदृष्टाः (*viśvadṛṣṭāḥ*): विश्वं दृष्टं यैस्ते विश्वदृष्टाः (*viśvaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yaiste viśvadṛṣṭāḥ*), a bahuvrīhi; since it has the character of a name (saṃjñā), by बहुव्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञायाम् (*bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām*) (as it looks; no number) the word viśva does not take the final-udātta accent; by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*) the first member keeps its natural accent, so the initial syllable is udātta.

### Printed p. 346 (PDF 366)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 191"; page number printed "346". Grammar of Ṛk 5 concluded; Ṛk 6: Saṃhitā, Pada, bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha begun.)*

अभूतन (*abhūtana*): root भू सत्तायाम् (*bhū sattāyām*); luṅ in the sense of the imperative (vidhi) by Vedic usage; second person plural, the affix thas; by the sūtra तस्थस्थमिपां तांतंतामः (*tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ*) (no number) it is replaced by ta; by तप्तनप्तनथनाश्च (*taptanaptanathanāśca*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-44, as printed and as in the file) again by tana; by भूसुवोस्तिङि (*bhūsuvostiṅi*) (no number) guṇa is prohibited; the aṅga gets the augment aṭ; tiṅanta-nighāta accent.

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Accents not reproduced.)*

> द्यौर्वः पिता पृथिवी माता सोमो भ्राताऽदितिः स्वसा ।
> अदृष्टा विश्वदृष्टास्तिष्ठतेळयता सु कं ॥ ६ ॥

> *dyaurvaḥ pitā pṛthivī mātā somo bhrātā 'ditiḥ svasā |*
> *adṛṣṭā viśvadṛṣṭāstiṣṭhateḷayatā su kaṃ ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> द्यौः । वः । पिता । पृथिवी । माता । सोमः । भ्राता । अदितिः । स्वसा ।
> अदृष्टाः । विश्वऽदृष्टाः । तिष्ठत । इळयत । सु । कं ॥ ६ ॥

> *dyauḥ | vaḥ | pitā | pṛthivī | mātā | somaḥ | bhrātā | aditiḥ | svasā |*
> *adṛṣṭāḥ | viśva 'dṛṣṭāḥ | tiṣṭhata | iḷayata | su | kaṃ ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* After the snake-poison remedies: O serpents, heaven is your father, earth your mother, Soma your brother, Aditi your sister; stay in your own places and do not come to me.

> अतः परं विषविचिकित्सा । तत्र तावत् हे सर्पाः वो युष्माकं द्यौः पिता । पृथिवी माता । सोमो भ्राता । अदितिर्देवमाता स्वसा । एवंमहानुभावा महोरगाः अदृष्टा अन्यैरदृश्यमानरूपाः स्वयं तु विश्वदृष्टाः सर्वस्य द्रष्टारो यूयं तिष्ठत स्वस्वस्थाने । मां प्रति मा गच्छत । सु सुतरां कं सुखं यथा तथेळयत । ईरयत । गच्छत । सोमशब्देन सोमाधारो द्युलोक उच्यते । पृथिव्यंतरिक्षद्युस्थानस्थाः सर्पाः स्वस्वस्थानं प्राप्नुतास्मद्बाधं मा कुरतेत्यर्थः ॥

> *ataḥ paraṃ viṣavicikitsā | tatra tāvat he sarpāḥ vo yuṣmākaṃ dyauḥ pitā | pṛthivī mātā | somo bhrātā | aditirdevamātā svasā | evaṃmahānubhāvā mahoragāḥ adṛṣṭā anyairadṛśyamānarūpāḥ svayaṃ tu viśvadṛṣṭāḥ sarvasya draṣṭāro yūyaṃ tiṣṭhata svasvasthāne | māṃ prati mā gacchata | su sutarāṃ kaṃ sukhaṃ yathā tatheḷayata | īrayata | gacchata | somaśabdena somādhāro dyuloka ucyate | pṛthivyaṃtarikṣadyusthānasthāḥ sarpāḥ svasvasthānaṃ prāpnutāsmadbādhaṃ mā kuratetyarthaḥ ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

(O serpents) **वः (*vaḥ*)** — to you. **द्यौः (*dyauḥ*)** — the heaven-world. **पिता (*pitā*)** — father. **पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*)** — the earth. **माता (*mātā*)** — mother. **सोमः (*somaḥ*)** — the atmosphere (antarikṣa), the support of Soma *(so printed; the bhāṣya says dyuloka)*. **भ्राता (*bhrātā*)** — one born together (brother). **अदितिः (*aditiḥ*)** — Aditi, mother of the gods. **स्वसा (*svasā*)** — sister. **अदृष्टाः (*adṛṣṭāḥ*)** — though you are not seen by others. **विश्वदृष्टाः (*viśvadṛṣṭāḥ*)** — you can see everything. **तिष्ठत (*tiṣṭhata*)** — be safe, each in your own place. **सु (*su*)** — exceedingly. **कं (*kaṃ*)** — so as to obtain happiness. **इलयत (*ilayata*)** [?] — conduct yourselves.

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

O serpents, the heaven-world is your father, the earth is your mother. Soma (the atmosphere that supports Soma) is your brother. Aditi, the mother of the gods, is your sister. Though others cannot see you, you can see all the rest. Come not to us and give us no trouble; remain in your own places and enjoy happiness.

### Printed p. 347 (PDF 367)

*(Header: "A. 2. A. 5 Va. 15", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". The Bhāvārtha of Ṛk 6 ends; printed English; Special Topics begin.)*

*(Bhāvārtha concluded:)* … (Though you cannot be seen by others) you can see all the rest. Do not come to us and give us trouble; remain in your own places and enjoy happiness.

**Printed English** *(heading "English Translation")*

Heaven, (serpents), is your father, Earth your mother, Soma your brother, Aditi your sister, unseen, all seeing, abide (in your own holes), enjoy (your own) good pleasure.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)** *(Special Topics)*

Up to now the ṛṣi Agastya, having spoken in blame of the harm that snakes and the like do to people, said that people must be very watchful about them; now, both in this ṛk and in the next, he indicates the wish that they should give trouble to no one and that they themselves should be happy in their own places, and so prays.

सोमः (*somaḥ*) — here the commentator's view is that the word सोम (*soma*) means the heaven-world where Soma is; that is, the idea is that there are various snakes in the earth, the atmosphere and heaven. This matter is stated plainly in the mantra of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā —

> नमो अस्तु सर्पेभ्यो ये के च पृथिवीमनु ।
> ये अंतरिक्षे ये दिवि तेभ्यः सर्पेभ्यो नमः ॥

> *namo astu sarpebhyo ye ke ca pṛthivīmanu |*
> *ye aṃtarikṣe ye divi tebhyaḥ sarpebhyo namaḥ ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 4-2-8-3.) Snakes that are also in other places than the three main places, earth, atmosphere and heaven, are likewise mentioned there —

> ये ऽदो रोचने दिवो ये वा सूर्यस्य रश्मिषु ।
> येषामप्सुसदः कृतं तेभ्यः सर्पेभ्यो नमः ॥
> या इषवो यातुधानानां ये वा वनस्पतीग्ं रनु ।
> ये वावटेषु शेरते तेभ्यः सर्पेभ्यो नमः ॥

> *ye 'do rocane divo ye vā sūryasya raśmiṣu |*
> *yeṣāmapsusadaḥ kṛtaṃ tebhyaḥ sarpebhyo namaḥ ‖*
> *yā iṣavo yātudhānānāṃ ye vā vanaspatīgṃ ranu |*
> *ye vāvaṭeṣu śerate tebhyaḥ sarpebhyo namaḥ ‖*

(Tai. Saṃ. 4-2-8-3.) *(In the first line a small numeral mark is printed after ये; kept out of the text as an accent sign. The reading वनस्पतीग्ं रनु (*vanaspatīgṃ ranu*) is as printed.)* In these mantras the names of many kinds of snakes are given: snakes in the shining heaven; snakes that wish to be in the sun's rays (in the heat); snakes in the water (Annaconda [sic]); snakes used as arrows of the rākṣasas; snakes that live on trees (green snakes); snakes that live in pits.

*(Ṛk 6 is left open: the rest of the Special Topics and the grammar page follow on p. 348.)*

**व्याकरणप्रक्रिया (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*

तिष्ठत (*tiṣṭhata*): root ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तौ (*ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*); loṭ, second person plural, replaced by त (*ta*); by the sūtra पाघ्राध्मा… (*pāghrādhmā…*) (abbreviated as printed; no number) the root is replaced by तिष्ठ (*tiṣṭha*); at the beginning of a pāda there is no nighāta accent; by the root accent the first syllable is udātta.

इळयत (*iḷayata*): root इल प्रेरणे (*ila preraṇe*), curādi; by सत्यापपाश… (*satyāpapāśa…*) (as it looks; no number) the affix ṇic; by Vedic usage no guṇa of the penultimate short vowel; an alternative form of the loṭ second person plural; by अन्येषामपि दृश्यते (*anyeṣāmapi dṛśyate*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-136, as in the file; not zoomed) lengthening in the saṃhitā; being after a tiṅanta no nighāta accent; by the ṇic accent the a after the l is udātta.

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Accents not reproduced.)*

> ये अंस्या ये अंग्याः सूचीका ये प्रकंकताः ।
> अदृष्टाः किं चनेह वः सर्वे साकं नि जस्यत ॥ ७ ॥

> *ye aṃsyā ye aṃgyāḥ sūcīkā ye prakaṃkatāḥ |*
> *adṛṣṭāḥ kiṃ caneha vaḥ sarve sākaṃ ni jasyata ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

*(A small compound sign is printed between प्र and कं in the Pada, as it looks.)*

> ये । अंस्याः । ये । अंग्याः । सूचीकाः । ये । प्रकंकताः ।
> अदृष्टाः । किं । चन । इह । वः । सर्वे । साकं । नि । जस्यत ॥ ७ ॥

> *ye | aṃsyāḥ | ye | aṃgyāḥ | sūcīkāḥ | ye | prakaṃkatāḥ |*
> *adṛṣṭāḥ | kiṃ | cana | iha | vaḥ | sarve | sākaṃ | ni | jasyata ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Whatever snakes and venomous creatures there are, moving by shoulder, body, needle-tailed or very venomous, unseen: all together leave us and go.

> येऽंस्या अंसाहर्ा अंसगा अंसे भवा अंसाभ्यां खादंतो वा । तथा येऽंग्या अंगगा अंगेन शरीरेण हंतारो वा लूतिकादयः । सूचीकाः सूचीसदृशपुच्छरोमाणो वृश्चिकाद्याः । ये च प्रकंकताः प्रकृष्टविषाः प्रकृष्टगामिनो वा महोरगा अदृष्टा अदृश्यमानाः किं चन यत्किंचित्सर्पजातमस्ति । इहास्मिन् समीपे वो युष्माकं किमस्ति । अतो यूयं सर्वे साकं सह नितरां जस्यत । मुंचतास्मान् ॥ जसु मोक्षणे दैवादिकः ॥

> *ye 'ṃsyā aṃsāharā aṃsagā aṃse bhavā aṃsābhyāṃ khādaṃto vā | tathā ye 'ṃgyā aṃgagā aṃgena śarīreṇa haṃtāro vā lūtikādayaḥ | sūcīkāḥ sūcīsadṛśapuccharomāṇo vṛścikādyāḥ | ye ca prakaṃkatāḥ prakṛṣṭaviṣāḥ prakṛṣṭagāmino vā mahoragā adṛṣṭā adṛśyamānāḥ kiṃ cana yatkiṃcitsarpajātamasti | ihāsmin samīpe vo yuṣmākaṃ kimasti | ato yūyaṃ sarve sākaṃ saha nitarāṃ jasyata | muṃcatāsmān ‖ jasu mokṣaṇe daivādikaḥ ‖*

*(The word printed अंसाहर्ा after अंस्याः is garbled in the print, [?].)*

**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

**ये (*ye*)** — which snakes. **अंस्याः (*aṃsyāḥ*)** — that move by the arm (bhuja). **ये (*ye*)** — which. **अंग्याः (*aṃgyāḥ*)** — that move by the body *(the Kannada adds "(pūrṇavāda)", "complete")*. **सूचीकाः (*sūcīkāḥ*)** — those that have tail and hair like a needle, scorpions and the like. **ये (*ye*)** — which. **प्रकंकताः (*prakaṃkatāḥ*)** — those of strong venom. **अदृष्टाः (*adṛṣṭāḥ*)** — [continues on p. 349]

### Printed p. 349 (PDF 369)

*(Header: "A. 2. A. 5 Va. 15", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". The Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 7 continues; Bhāvārtha; printed English; Special Topics begin.)*

*(Pratipadārtha continued:)* … those not visible to the eye. **किंचन (*kiṃcana*)** — all other subtle venomous creatures, serpents and the rest. **इह (*iha*)** — here. **वः (*vaḥ*)** — whatever cruel creatures belong to your company. **सर्वे साकं (*sarve sākaṃ*)** — all of them gathering together. **जस्यत (*jasyata*)** — leave us and go.

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

There are many venomous snakes that move by the arm, those that move by the body, scorpions and the like with tails and hair like a needle, creatures of strong venom, and other subtle poisonous creatures that cannot be seen by the eye. Let all those of them that have come near to us and may do us harm leave us and go far away.

**Printed English** *(heading "English Translation")*

Those (who move with their) shoulders, those (who move with their) bodies, those who sting with sharp fangs, those who are virulently venomous ; what do you here, you unseen, depart together far from us. *(A stray dot is printed before "their" in the first line.)*

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)** *(Special Topics)*

अंस्याः (*aṃsyāḥ*) — "अंसाहर्ा, अंसगा, अंसे भवा, अंसाभ्यां खादंतो वा (*aṃsāharā, aṃsagā, aṃse bhavā, aṃsābhyāṃ khādaṃto vā*)" [?] (the commentary). That is: snakes that have the arm (bhuja) as their chief part; snakes that make their movement, turning and so on, chiefly by the arms. For this reason snakes have the names bhujaṅga and bhujaga; the nature of four kinds of snake has been described: those born from the arm, those that bite with the arm, and so on. Here "biting with the arm" means that the poison spreads by mere touch; it is to be understood that snakes of such a kind are meant. That snakes move by the arms is a poetic fancy (utprekṣā). That snakes have no legs is known to all. Yet, since the structure of their backbone is made suitable for moving, they can move very fast. Therefore to say that snakes move by the arm is established usage (rūḍhi).

अंग्याः (*aṃgyāḥ*) — "अंगगाः अंगेन शरीरेण हंतारो वा (*aṃgagāḥ aṃgena śarīreṇa haṃtāro vā*)". Two senses are given: moving by the aṅga, or killing by the aṅga. Moving by the aṅga means moving with a curved movement, as said before; killing by the aṅga means that, like snakes of the *koḷakumaṇḍala* class (as printed), they make the poison spread by mere touch and kill. The meaning is: snakes of such a class.

सूचिकाः (*sūcikāḥ*) (as printed here) — "सूचीसदृशपुच्छरोमाणो वृश्चिकाद्याः (*sūcīsadṛśapuccharomāṇo vṛścikādyāḥ*)". That is: venomous creatures such as scorpions that have at the tail stings sharp like the point of a needle.

### Printed p. 350 (PDF 370)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 191". The Special Topics of Ṛk 7 conclude; grammar; Ṛk 8 begins.)*

प्रकंकताः (*prakaṃkatāḥ*) — "प्रकृष्टविषाः प्रकृष्टगामिनो वा (*prakṛṣṭaviṣāḥ prakṛṣṭagāmino vā*)". That is: snakes of very sharp venom, or snakes that move very fast.

Such great snakes of great venom, and other venomous creatures, lie hidden in the grass and in the bushes so that none can see them. Addressing them, the ṛṣi has prayed: "O snakes of various kinds, what do you do here? What business have you? Come, all of you together, and leave our neighbourhood."

**व्याकरणप्रक्रिया (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*

अंस्याः (*aṃsyāḥ*): अंसे भवाः (*aṃse bhavāḥ*); by भवे छन्दसि (*bhave chandasi*) (Pā. Sū. 4-4-110) the affix yat; by the sūtra यस्येति च (*yasyeti ca*) the preceding a is dropped; by यतोऽनावः (*yato 'nāvaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-213) the first syllable is udātta. In अंग्याः (*aṃgyāḥ*) likewise the affix and the accents come.

जस्यत (*jasyata*): root जसु मोक्षणे (*jasu mokṣaṇe*), divādi; loṭ, second person plural, replaced by त (*ta*) (tādeśa); by दिवादिभ्यः श्यन् (*divādibhyaḥ śyan*) the vikaraṇa śyan; because it stands after a tiṅanta (printed "atiṅanta", [sic]?) the tiṅanta-nighāta accent comes.

#### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Accents not reproduced.)*

> उत्पुरस्तात्सूर्य एति विश्वदृष्टो अदृष्टहा ।
> अदृष्टान्त्सर्वाञ्जंभयन्त्सर्वाश्च यातुधान्यः ॥ ८ ॥

> *utpurastātsūrya eti viśvadṛṣṭo adṛṣṭahā |*
> *adṛṣṭāntsarvāñjaṃbhayantsarvāśca yātudhānyaḥ ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उत् । पुरस्तात् । सूर्यः । एति । विश्वऽदृष्टः । अदृष्टऽहा ।
> अदृष्टान् । सर्वान् । जंभयन् । सर्वाः । च । यातुऽधान्यः ॥ ८ ॥

> *ut | purastāt | sūryaḥ | eti | viśva 'dṛṣṭaḥ | adṛṣṭa 'hā |*
> *adṛṣṭān | sarvān | jaṃbhayan | sarvāḥ | ca | yātu 'dhānyaḥ ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* The sun rises in the east, seen by all, destroyer of the unseen; crushing all unseen things and all yātudhānīs.

> असौ सूर्यः पुरस्तात्पूर्वस्यां दिश्युदेति । कीदृशः सः । विश्वदृष्टः । विश्वे द्रष्टव्या यस्य स तादृशः । अदृष्टहा । अदृष्टा विषविशेषा विषधरविशेषा वा । तेषां हंता । यद्वा । अदृष्टमुदर्शनमज्ञानमंधकारः । तस्य हंता । सूर्ये उदिते सति सर्वे विषधरा विषाणि वा पलायंते । किं कुर्वन्नुदेतीति चेत् उच्यते । सर्वानदृष्टानद्रष्टव्यान्विषराक्षसादीञ्जंभयन् हिंसयन् । तथा सर्वा यातुधान्यः ।

> *asau sūryaḥ purastātpūrvasyāṃ diśyudeti | kīdṛśaḥ saḥ | viśvadṛṣṭaḥ | viśve draṣṭavyā yasya sa tādṛśaḥ | adṛṣṭahā | adṛṣṭā viṣaviśeṣā viṣadharaviśeṣā vā | teṣāṃ haṃtā | yadvā | adṛṣṭamudarśanamajñānamaṃdhakāraḥ | tasya haṃtā | sūrye udite sati sarve viṣadharā viṣāṇi vā palāyaṃte | kiṃ kurvannudetīti cet ucyate | sarvānadṛṣṭānadraṣṭavyānviṣarākṣasādīñjaṃbhayan hiṃsayan | tathā sarvā yātudhānyaḥ |*

*(The words after सर्वान् are garbled in the print, read as it looks, [?]. The bhāṣya continues beyond p. 350; Ṛk 8 is left open.)*

> यातवो यातनास्तीव्रवेदनाः । तासां धात्रीरुत्पादयित्रीर्महोरगीराक्षसीर्वा जंभयन् पुरस्तादुदेति । अतोऽस्मत्[?] नि जस्यतेति संबंधः ॥

*(The word after अतः is not clear in the print — it looks like "ऽस्मत्त्रो" — [?]. The sense: "therefore the connection is: leave us".)*

**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

**विश्वदृष्टः (*viśvadṛṣṭaḥ*)** — one who is fit to be looked at by the whole world. **अदृष्टहा (*adṛṣṭahā*)** — the destroyer of venomous creatures and the like that cannot be seen by the eye, or the destroyer of darkness. **सूर्यः (*sūryaḥ*)** — the sun. **सर्वान् अदृष्टान् (*sarvān adṛṣṭān*)** — all venomous creatures that cannot be seen by the eye; and **सर्वाश्च यातुधान्यः (*sarvāśca yātudhānyaḥ*)** — all female creatures that are the cause of their birth (or the Asura women). **जंभयन् (*jaṃbhayan*)** — destroying by injuring. **पुरस्तात् (*purastāt*)** — in the eastern quarter. **उदेति (*udeti*)** — rises.

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

The sun, who is fit to be looked at by the whole world and who destroys venomous creatures and the like that cannot be seen by the eye, rises in the eastern quarter, destroying by injury all venomous creatures that cannot be seen by the eye and all the female creatures that are the cause of their birth.

**Printed English** *(heading "English Translation")*

The all-seeing sun rises in the east, the destroyer of the unseen, driving away all the unseen (venomous creatures), and all evil spirits.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)** *(Special Topics)*

In this Ṛk the ṛṣi, knowing that the sun rises at the end of the night as a remedy against the dark, and that the fear that may arise from venomous creatures is thereby removed, has expressed his joy.

विश्वदृष्टः (*viśvadṛṣṭaḥ*) — the sun, who is looked at by all. When the sun has risen, all look at him. The sun is dear to everyone; he is the one who brings joy to all. Because in the night-time the harm done by wild beasts and venomous creatures is especially great, all creatures and people welcome with great joy the rising of the sun when the night has passed and the day has dawned. Therefore the word विश्वदृष्टः (*viśvadṛṣṭaḥ*) means the sun whom all look at with delight.

अदृष्टहा (*adṛṣṭahā*) — Sāyaṇa: "अदृष्टा विषविशेषा विषधरविशेषा वा । तेषां हंता । यद्वा (*adṛṣṭā viṣaviśeṣā viṣadharaviśeṣā vā | teṣāṃ haṃtā | yadvā*) …" (the unseen are special kinds of poison or of poison-bearers; he is their destroyer; or else …). Here अदृष्ट (*adṛṣṭa*) means venomous serpents that cannot be seen, or that lie hidden so as not to be seen. Because he kills them, the sun is praised by the epithet अदृष्टहा (*adṛṣṭahā*). Or else अदृष्ट (*adṛṣṭa*) means: the unseen, ignorance, darkness, and the like.
### Printed p. 352 (PDF 372)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 191". The Special Topics of Ṛk 8 continue; grammar page.)*

*(Special Topics continued:)* Because he destroys them, the sun is also named अदृष्टहा (*adṛṣṭahā*). For when the sun has risen, venomous serpents and the like run away at once. In the daytime, which has the light of the sun, they have no special movement. Moreover modern scientists accept that sun-rays (sunlight) have the power to remove poison. Therefore:

अदृष्टान् सर्वान् जंभयन् (*adṛṣṭān sarvān jaṃbhayan*) — it is described that the sun rises, with his light destroying (driving away) all evil creatures that lie hidden so as not to be seen.

यातुधान्यः (*yātudhānyaḥ*) — Sāyaṇa: "यातवो यातनास्तीव्रवेदनाः तासां धात्रीरुत्पादयित्रीर्महोरगी राक्षसीर्वा (*yātavo yātanāstīvravedanāḥ tāsāṃ dhātrīrutpādayitrīrmahoragī rākṣasīrvā*)." यातु (*yātu*) means very sharp pain, suffering. Sāyaṇa's explanation is: great snakes full of poison, or female rākṣasas, that cause such pain.

The Yātudhānas are a special tribe within the class of rākṣasas. Because they cause people harm of many kinds, there are many mantras in the Ṛgveda praying to Agni (Rakṣohāgni, or Agni) to avert their harm. In Maṇḍala 1, in Sūkta 87[?] and in Sūkta 118[?] (numerals as they look in the small print), Agni has likewise been prayed to protect from their harm.

These Yātudhānas eat the flesh of men and horses, and drink cow's milk (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-87-16, 17). To satisfy their longing for blood and flesh these rākṣasas attack men. This attack is generally by means of entering them; Agni has been prayed to hold them back so that they do not enter the sacrificers (8-48-20). These bhūta-pretas generally enter through our mouth when we eat or drink (Atharva-veda 5-29-6 to 8); they enter also by other doors (Atharva-veda 8-6-3). Once inside, they eat the flesh of the man, cutting it up, and produce disease (Atharva-veda 5-29-5, 10), produce madness and destroy the power of speech (Atharva-veda 6-111-3; Hiraṇyakeśi Gṛhya-sūtra 1-15-5). They attack the dwellings of men (Kauśika-sūtra 135-9). Their time of moving about is night or evening (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-104-8). In the eastern quarter their mischief does not go on at all; the sun that rises there drives them away (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 2-6-6-3). Many such descriptions of the Yātudhānas occur in the Ṛgveda and also elsewhere in the other Vedas.

**व्याकरणप्रक्रिया (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*

पुरस्तात् (*purastāt*): from the word पूर्व (*pūrva*) (east); by दिक्छब्देभ्यः (*dikchabdebhyaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 5-3-27) the affix, a form of the "plural" kind [as printed]; the tiṅanta-nighāta accent comes.

अदृष्टहा (*adṛṣṭahā*): root हन (*hana*) (*hana*, "hiṃsāgatyoḥ"); by बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-88) when अदृष्ट (*adṛṣṭa*) is the upapada, the affix kvip; all of it is elided; the form is अदृष्टन् (*adṛṣṭan*) [sic?].
### Printed p. 353 (PDF 373)

*(Header: "A. 2. A. 5 Va. 15", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Grammar of Ṛk 8 concludes; a short rule; Ṛk 9: Saṃhitā, Pada, bhāṣya and the beginning of the Pratipadārtha.)*

*(Grammar continued:)* The nominative singular su comes after; the penultimate vowel is lengthened and the n is dropped. By the rule on a kṛt after a gati or kāraka upapada (no number printed), the accent of the kṛt-final word comes in its natural (prakṛti) form.

जंभयन् (*jaṃbhayan*): root जभि नाशने (*jabhi nāśane*) (*jabhi nāśane*), curādi. By the sūtra beginning सत्यापपाश… (*satyāpapāśa…*) (printed abbreviated, no number) the affix ṇic in its own sense; laṭ after the ṇijanta; because it has the marker i, the augment num; laṭ is replaced by śatṛ; because śap is marked p and the sārvadhātuka that follows it becomes anudātta by the sūtra तास्यनुदात्तेत्… (*tāsyanudāttet…*) (no number printed), and by the ṇic accent, the a after the bha becomes udātta.

यातुधान्यः (*yātudhānyaḥ*): the word यातुधानी (*yātudhānī*); before jas the replacement yaṇ comes by Vedic usage. Because yaṇ stands in the place of an udātta, by उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः (*udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-2-4) the svarita accent comes after the yaṇ.

#### Ṛk 9

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Accents not reproduced.)*

> उदपप्तदसौ सूर्यः पुरु विश्वानि जूर्वन् ।
> आदित्यः पर्वतेभ्यो विश्वदृष्टो अदृष्टहा ॥ ९ ॥

> *udapaptadasau sūryaḥ puru viśvāni jūrvan |*
> *ādityaḥ parvatebhyo viśvadṛṣṭo adṛṣṭahā ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> उत् । अपप्तत् । असौ । सूर्यः । पुरु । विश्वानि । जूर्वन् ।
> आदित्यः । पर्वतेभ्यः । विश्वऽदृष्टः । अदृष्टऽहा ॥ ९ ॥

> *ut | apaptat | asau | sūryaḥ | puru | viśvāni | jūrvan |*
> *ādityaḥ | parvatebhyaḥ | viśva 'dṛṣṭaḥ | adṛṣṭa 'hā ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* The sun, visible in the east, rises, destroying many poisons; he benefits living beings, sees all and destroys the unseen; so there is no need to fear poison.

> असौ पुरस्ताद्दृश्यमानः सूर्यः सर्वस्य प्रेरक आदित्य उदपप्तत् । ऊर्ध्वं गच्छति ॥ पततेर्लुङि पुमागमो रूपं ॥ किं कुर्वन् । विश्वानि बहूनि विषाणि पुरु प्रभूतं जूर्वन् हिंसन् । कीदृशोऽसौ । पर्वतेभ्यः पर्ववद्भ्यः प्राणिभ्यस्तेषामुपकारायादित्यो विषोदकादीनामदनशीलः । विश्वदृष्टो विश्वं दृष्टं येन तादृशः अदृष्टहादृष्टानां विषविशेषाणां हंता । एवंमहानुभावः सूर्यः ऊर्ध्वमारोहति । अतो विषशंका न कार्या ॥

> *asau purastāddṛśyamānaḥ sūryaḥ sarvasya preraka āditya udapaptat | ūrdhvaṃ gacchati ‖ pataterluṅi pumāgamo rūpaṃ ‖ kiṃ kurvan | viśvāni bahūni viṣāṇi puru prabhūtaṃ jūrvan hiṃsan | kīdṛśo 'sau | parvatebhyaḥ parvavadbhyaḥ prāṇibhyasteṣāmupakārāyādityo viṣodakādīnāmadanaśīlaḥ | viśvadṛṣṭo viśvaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yena tādṛśaḥ adṛṣṭahādṛṣṭānāṃ viṣaviśeṣāṇāṃ haṃtā | evaṃmahānubhāvaḥ sūryaḥ ūrdhvamārohati | ato viṣaśaṃkā na kāryā ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

**पर्वतेभ्यः (*parvatebhyaḥ*)** — for the benefit of living beings. **आदित्यः (*ādityaḥ*)** — the sun in the Āditya form, who consumes poisonous water and the like. **विश्वदृष्टः (*viśvadṛṣṭaḥ*)** — the one who is to be looked at by all. **अदृष्टहा (*adṛṣṭahā*)** — the destroyer of the subtle poison-moving creatures …

*(Ṛk 9 is left open: the Pratipadārtha is cut off at the foot of this page and continues on p. 354. The page ends with the footer "[23]" and "Vol. 14.", which is the printer's signature mark.)*

### Printed p. 354 (PDF 374)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 191". Ṛk 9: Pratipadārtha concludes, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics begun.)*

*(Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 9 continued, without repeating:)* … the destroyer of the subtle poison-moving creatures; **असौ सूर्यः (*asau sūryaḥ*)** — this sun; **विश्वानि (*viśvāni*)** — all poisons; **पुरु (*puru*)** — fully; **जूर्वन् (*jūrvan*)** — destroying; **उदपप्तत् (*udapaptat*)** — rises and comes upward.

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

This sun, who in the Āditya form drinks up poisonous water and the like for the benefit of living beings, who is fit to look at all, and who destroys the subtle poison-moving creatures, rises and comes upward, fully destroying all poisons.

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

The Sun has risen on high, destroying all the many (poisons) ; Aditya, the all-seeing, the destroyer of the unseen, (rises) for (the good of) living benigs [sic].

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

In the previous Ṛk the sunrise and the flight of the evil creatures were introduced; in this Ṛk the gradual rising of the sun and the destruction of poisons and the like by the sharpness of the rays so produced are described.

**सूर्यः—सर्वस्य प्रेरक आदित्यः (*sūryaḥ—sarvasya preraka ādityaḥ*)** — "The sun is the impeller of all, the Āditya." The sun impels all the world, that is, all the living beings in the world. If we do not receive the warmth that comes through the rays from the sun, we cannot live. As is said in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-115-1 in the words **सूर्य आत्मा जगतः (*sūrya ātmā jagataḥ*)** ("the sun is the soul of the world"; the printed Kannada has the visarga), the sun is the very self of the whole world. Without the sun's brilliance not even a blade of grass on the earth could stir. For the whole animal kingdom and for men the sun's brilliance (heat; the printed word is *śākhavu*) is absolutely necessary. Since the heat (fire) is one of the five elements, the sun's brilliance is as necessary as air, water and food. The brilliance produced by fire and the like differs from the sun's brilliance. The sun's brilliance has the power to remove poison and to produce health. It is for that reason that the sharp rays of the midday sun destroy poison; this is said here by the sentence **पुरु विश्वानि विषाणि जूर्वन्—हिंसन् (*puru viśvāni viṣāṇi jūrvan—hiṃsan*)** ("fully all poisons, destroying—harming"). Earlier the sage Praskaṇva (as printed) prayed:

**हृद्रोगं मम सूर्य हरिमाणं च नाशय (*hṛdrogaṃ mama sūrya harimāṇaṃ ca nāśaya*)**

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-50-11)

"O sun, destroy the disease that has spread in my heart and the yellow colour (*toṇṇu*, 'Leprosy' printed in English) produced by the leprosy spread over my skin": this prayer is an illustration of the sun's power to cure disease.

### Printed p. 355 (PDF 375)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 15 ]" (Varga numeral 15 read unzoomed), "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Special Topics concludes; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Ṛk 9; Ṛk 10 begun.)*

**पर्वतेभ्यः—पर्ववद्भ्यः प्राणिभ्यस्तेषामुपकारायादित्यो विषोदकादीनामदनशीलः उदपप्तत् (*parvatebhyaḥ—parvavadbhyaḥ prāṇibhyasteṣāmupakārāyādityo viṣodakādīnāmadanaśīlaḥ udapaptat*)** — Sāyaṇa explains the word *parvata* as "living beings that have joints", that is, bodies like lumps; the body is made of different parts such as the foot, the knee, the thigh, the belly, the neck and the head, joined together as one great object. In the same way a mountain (hill) has many rocks one over another, and the name *parvata* is for all of them together; that example is here applied to the bodies of living beings. And the words "for doing good to such beings" he has supplied (*adhyāhāra*) to complete the sense of the sentence.

**विश्वदृष्टो अदृष्टहा (*viśvadṛṣṭo adṛṣṭahā*)** — the explanation and meaning of these words have been given in the previous Ṛk itself.

**व्याकरणप्रक्रिया (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*

अपप्तत् (*apaptat*): root पत्ऌ गतौ (*patḷ gatau*), bhvādi; luṅ, third person singular, affix tip; by इतश्च (*itaśca*) the i is elided; because the root is ḷ-marked, cli receives the replacement printed as "ajādeśa" [as printed; aṅ intended?] by the rule beginning पुषादिद्युताद् (*puṣādidyutād*) (printed so, no number); by पतेः पुम् (*pateḥ pum*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-19) the root takes the augment pum, which, being m-marked, comes after the last vowel (file said 6-4-19, crop shows the flat-footed 7); the augment aṭ to the aṅga; because it stands after an "atiṅanta" [as printed] the nighāta accent comes.

जूर्वन् (*jūrvan*): root जुर्वी हिंसायाम् (*jurvī hiṃsāyām*); laṭ is replaced by śatṛ; by उपधायां च (*upadhāyāṃ ca*) (printed so, no number) the u is lengthened; because the lasārvadhātuka is anudātta the root accent remains; nominative singular form.

### Printed p. 356 (PDF 376)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 191". Ṛk 10: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Agastya says he fixes the poison, as a skin bag in a wine-maker's house, in the sun's disc; it does not harm the sun, and by the sun's grace neither he nor the poison's victims die; the sun's horses carry the poison far off; the honey-lore turns it into nectar.

> आदित्यमंडले चतुर्थेनांगुलिना विषमादाय मधुकृत्य योजयित्वा निर्विषो भवेदिति यदेतद्विषविद्यायामुक्तं तदिदमत्रोच्यते । अहं विषावृतोऽगस्त्यः सूर्ये सर्वस्य प्रेरयितरि मधुविद्यारूपे सूर्यमंडले विषमावृत्य वर्तमानं सूर्य आ सजामि । आसक्तं करोमि । तत्र दृष्टांतः । सुरावतो गृहे सुरानिर्मातृसदने दृतिमिव चर्ममयं सुरापात्रमिव । यथा तत्कर्तुर्न दोषाय भवति तद्वद्विषमादित्यस्य न बाधकमित्यर्थः । सो चित् स । चित् पूजायं [?] । उः प्रसिद्धा । पूज्यः स सूर्यः खलु स मराति । न म्रियते । नो वयं मराम । तदनुग्रहात्त्रैव [?] विषस्य योजितत्वाद्वयमपि न म्रियामहै । उभयोरमरणे कारणमाह । हरिष्ठाः । हरयोऽश्वाः । तेषु स्थित आदित्य आरे दूरेऽस्य विषस्य योजनं प्रापणं चकार । तदेवोच्यते । हे विष त्वा त्वां मध्वमृतं चकार । विषस्य विषभावं दूरेऽपनोद्यामृतीचकारेति । एष्यैव [?] मधुला मधुदात्री निर्विषीकर्त्री मधुविद्या । यदेतदादित्यस्य विषयोजनं तेन चामृतीकरणं यदस्ति एषा मधुविद्या ॥

> *ādityamaṃḍale caturthenāṃgulinā viṣamādāya madhukṛtya yojayitvā nirviṣo bhavediti yadetadviṣavidyāyāmuktaṃ tadidamatrocyate | ahaṃ viṣāvṛto 'gastyaḥ sūrye sarvasya prerayitari madhuvidyārūpe sūryamaṃḍale viṣamāvṛtya vartamānaṃ sūrya ā sajāmi | āsaktaṃ karomi | tatra dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ | surāvato gṛhe surānirmātṛsadane dṛtimiva carmamayaṃ surāpātramiva | yathā tatkarturna doṣāya bhavati tadvadviṣamādityasya na bādhakamityarthaḥ | so cit sa | cit pūjāyaṃ [?] | uḥ prasiddhā | pūjyaḥ sa sūryaḥ khalu sa marāti | na mriyate | no vayaṃ marāma | tadanugrahāttraiva [?] viṣasya yojitatvādvayamapi na mriyāmahai | ubhayoramaraṇe kāraṇamāha | hariṣṭhāḥ | harayo 'śvāḥ | teṣu sthita āditya āre dūre 'sya viṣasya yojanaṃ prāpaṇaṃ cakāra | tadevocyate | he viṣa tvā tvāṃ madhvamṛtaṃ cakāra | viṣasya viṣabhāvaṃ dūre 'panodyāmṛtīcakāreti | eṣyaiva [?] madhulā madhudātrī nirviṣīkartrī madhuvidyā | yadetadādityasya viṣayojanaṃ tena cāmṛtīkaraṇaṃ yadasti eṣā madhuvidyā ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

**सुरावतः (*surāvataḥ*)** — in the house of the maker of liquor (wine); **दृतिं इव (*dṛtiṃ iva*)** — like placing a skin that is to be filled with liquor; **विषं (*viṣaṃ*)** — the poison spread all around us; **सूर्ये (*sūrye*)** — in the sun's disc (in the sunshine); **आ सजामि (*ā sajāmi*)** — I join (place); **सो चित् (*so cit*)** — as for that revered sun; **नु (*nu*)** — in the least; **न मराति (*na marāti*)** — he does not meet death; **नो वयं मराम (*no vayaṃ marāma*)** — by his grace we too do not meet death; **आरे (*āre*)** — even though far off; **हरिष्ठाः (*hariṣṭhāḥ*)** — the sun mounted on the horses; **अस्य (*asya*)** — of this poison; **योजनं (*yojanaṃ*)** — contact he has brought about (made it so that the power of this poison does not spread to me) (O poison!); **मधुला (*madhulā*)** — the honey-lore; **त्वा (*tvā*)** — you; **मधु चकार (*madhu cakāra*)** — has turned into nectar.

**भावार्थः (Bhāvārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

As a skin that is to be filled with liquor is placed in the house of the liquor-maker, so I join the poison spread all around us to the sun's disc. That revered sun does not in the least meet death; by his grace there is no death for us either, even though we are far off. The sun, mounted on his horses, has brought this poison into contact so that its power does not spread to us. O poison, the honey-lore has turned you into nectar.

*(Ṛk 10 is left open: printed English, Special Topics and grammar follow on p. 357.)*

### Printed p. 357 (PDF 377)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 15 ]" (Varga numeral read unzoomed), "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Ṛk 10 continued: printed English and Special Topics begun.)*

**English Translatin [sic]** *(printed heading)*

I deposit the poison in the solar orb, like a leather bottle in the house of a vender [sic] of spirits ; verily, that adorable (Sun) never dies, nor, (through his favour), shall we die (of the venom) ; for, through afar off, yet drawn by his coursers, he will overtake (the poison) ; the science of antidotes converted you, (Poison), to ambrosia.

**विशेषविषयगळು (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In the previous Ṛks the rising of the sun and the ascent of the sun were told; in this Ṛk the method by which the sun removes poison is described.

The method of removing poison is what is told in the Viṣavidyā or Madhuvidyā; the commentator says: **आदित्यमंडले चतुर्थेनांगुलिना विषमादाय मधुकृत्य योजयित्वा निर्विषो भवेदिति यदेतद्विषविद्यायामुक्तं तदिदमत्रोच्यते (*ādityamaṃḍale caturthenāṃgulinā viṣamādāya madhukṛtya yojayitvā nirviṣo bhavediti yadetadviṣavidyāyāmuktaṃ tadidamatrocyate*)** — that is, taking the poison that is in the body with the fourth finger of the right hand, that is, the finger called *anāmikā*, and joining it to the sun's disc (in a picture drawn to resemble the sun's disc, in the sunshine), by performing the practices of the Madhuvidyā the poison is removed; this, which is stated in the book called Viṣavidyā, is said here — thus the commentator explains the chief matter of this Ṛk.

**सूर्ये विषं आ सजामि (*sūrye viṣaṃ ā sajāmi*)** — **विषावृतोऽगस्त्योऽहं सूर्ये सर्वस्य प्रेरयितरि मधुविद्यारूपे सूर्यमंडले विषमावृत्य वर्तमानं सूर्य आ सजामि (*viṣāvṛto 'gastyo 'haṃ sūrye sarvasya prerayitari madhuvidyārūpe sūryamaṃḍale viṣamāvṛtya vartamānaṃ sūrya ā sajāmi*)** — "I, Agastya, whose body is pervaded by poison, gather all the poison [that is in my body] and place it in the sun's disc, which is of the form of the Madhuvidyā and impels the whole world" — so the sage has said. Here "the sun's disc" may mean a figure like the sun's disc, in the sunshine, in the practices carried out for removing poison (or, according to the Mantra-tantra-śāstra, a diagram of the sun's disc made of seed-syllables); chiefly it can be said to mean a place with sun's rays, or the sunshine.

**दृतिं सुरावतो गृहे (*dṛtiṃ surāvato gṛhe*)** — the sage tells an example about gathering the poison and placing it in the sunshine:

**सुरावतो गृहे सुरानिर्मातृसदने दृतिमिव चर्ममयं सुरापात्रमिव । यथा तत्कर्तुर्न दोषाय भवति तद्वद्विषमादित्यस्य न बाधकमित्यर्थः (*surāvato gṛhe surānirmātṛsadane dṛtimiva carmamayaṃ surāpātramiva | yathā tatkarturna doṣāya bhavati tadvadviṣamādityasya na bādhakamityarthaḥ*)** — as a man who makes liquor stores it in his house, gathering it in a cloth (bag) of leather, so I too gather all the poison

---


### Printed p. 358 (PDF 378)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 1. A. 24. Sū. 191". Ṛk 10 Special Topics continued.)*

and place it in one place in the sunshine — so the sage states a simile. And just as, by gathering liquor and placing it in one place (without drinking it), no harm of any kind comes to the maker of liquor, so by the poison-gathering placed in the sunshine no harm of any kind comes to the sun — so it is explained.

**चित् (*cit*)** — **चिदिति पूजायां । अत्यंतमविनश्वरा (*ciditi pūjāyāṃ | atyaṃtamavinaśvarā*)** [as printed]. Yāska says that the particle *cit* is of many kinds of use (*aneka-karma*) — that it is employed in many different senses — and, **आचार्यश्चिदिदं ब्रूयादिति पूजायां । दधिचिदित्युपमार्थे । कुल्माषांश्चिद्वाहरेत्यवकुत्सिते (*ācāryaścididaṃ brūyāditi pūjāyāṃ | dadhicidityupamārthe | kulmāṣāṃścidvāharetyavakutsite*)** (as printed; the last word-division as it looks); he explains the meaning by giving examples: in the sentence "ācāryaś cit" the particle *cit* is used in the sense of honour; in the sentence "dadhicit" in the sense of comparison; and in "kulmāṣāṃś cit" in the sense of reproach. Here Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning as used in the sense of honour.

**सो चिन्नु न मराति नो वयं (*so cin nu na marāti no vayaṃ*)** — for this sentence Sāyaṇa says: **पूज्यः सः सूर्यः खलु न मराति । न म्रियते । नो वयं मराम । तदनुग्रहात्त्रैव [?] विषस्य योजितत्वाद्वयमपि न म्रियामहै (*pūjyaḥ saḥ sūryaḥ khalu na marāti | na mriyate | no vayaṃ marāma | tadanugrahāttraiva [?] viṣasya yojitatvādvayamapi na mriyāmahai*)** (the word *tadanugrahāttraiva* as it looks [?]). By placing the poison in the sunshine there is no harm to the sun. Therefore the sun does not die; we too do not die. The chief intention is: since the sun has the power of removing poison, no harm at all comes to the sun from the poison we place in the sunshine. By that sun's favour our poison is removed and no harm comes to us either, that is, we too do not die. The reason for this he tells in the next sentence.

**अस्य योजनं हरिष्ठा चकार (*asya yojanaṃ hariṣṭhā cakāra*)** — the sun, even though he is very far off, with the help of his rays overcomes the poison and makes it powerless (*nirvīrya*). And the poison goes away and becomes nectar; this the sage has said here, addressing the poison itself.

**मधु त्वा मधुला चकार (*madhu tvā madhulā cakāra*)** — **विषस्य विषभावं दूरेऽपनोद्यामृतीचकारेति । विष्यैव [?] मधुना मधुदात्री निर्विषीकत्री मधुविद्या । यदेतदादित्यस्य विषयोजनं तेन चामृतीकरणं यदस्ति एषा मधुविद्या (*viṣasya viṣabhāvaṃ dūre 'panodyāmṛtīcakāreti | viṣyaiva [?] madhunā madhudātrī nirviṣīkatrī madhuvidyā | yadetadādityasya viṣayojanaṃ tena cāmṛtīkaraṇaṃ yadasti eṣā madhuvidyā*)** (*viṣyaiva* as it looks [?]). The placing of poison in the sun's disc, and the sun's turning that poison into nectar, is called Madhuvidyā; therefore the sage, addressing the poison, says: "O poison, the sun not only makes your poison [the power of killing] powerless, but by the Madhuvidyā also changes the poison into nectar." On this matter the scholar Wilson —

The notion that pervades this stanza and forms the burden of the three following, is derived, according to Sayana, from the Visha-Vidya, the science of poisonns [sic] or of antidotes,

whence it is also termed Madhu-vidya, science of ambrosia ; one formula of which, as cited by him is — " having taken the poison in the solar arb [sic] with the fourth finger ; having made it ambrosia and caused them to blend together, may it become poisonless" By the Surya Mandala or orb of the Sun is probably to be understood a mystical diagram or figure wholely [sic] or partly typical of the solar orb ; the Sun being considered as especially instrumental in counteracting the operation of poison ; the science of antidotes is also named in the text Madhula, as synonymous with Madhuvidya. **व्याकरणप्रक्रिया (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*

सजामि (*sajāmi*): root षञ्ज सङ्गे (*ṣañja saṅge*); because of the interchange of vikaraṇa in the Chandas, śa instead of śap in laṭ; since there is the *jhaldvad* [?] state, the nasal is elided; by the rule printed as अतो दीर्घो यञि (*ato dīrgho yañi*) [as it looks] the aṅga is lengthened; the nighāta accent after an *atiṅanta*.

दृतिम् (*dṛtim*): root दृ विदारणे (*dṛ vidāraṇe*); the affix ti by the Uṇādi rule beginning दृणातेर्ह्रस्वश्च (*dṛṇāterhrasvaśca*) (Uṇ. Sū. number unclear [?]); shortening of the root; since the affix is *nit* by the rule printed as पदिप्रथिभ्यां नित् (*padiprathibhyāṃ nit*) [as it looks], the accent on the first syllable by ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ñnityādirnityam*) (as it looks; no number).

मराति (*marāti*): root मृङ् प्राणत्यागे (*mṛṅ prāṇatyāge*); parasmaipada affix by vyatyaya; by लेटोऽडाटौ (*leṭo 'ḍāṭau*) the aḍāgama to ti of leṭ; guṇa of the ṛ of the root; nighāta accent because of the *atiṅanta* that follows.

मराम (*marāma*): the first person plural form of leṭ of the same root; the accent rules as before.

हरिष्ठाः (*hariṣṭhāḥ*): "he who stands on the horses"; root ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तौ (*ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*); by सुपिस्थः (*supisthaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-4, file value; the numeral was not zoomed, it looks ३-२-४) the affix ka; by आतो लोप इटि च (*āto lopa iṭi ca*) [as it looks; no number] the ā of the root is elided. *(The note continues on the next page.)*

*(continuing hariṣṭhāḥ:)* by vyatyaya the plural affix has come; by the rule beginning गतिकारकोप (*gatikārakopa*) (as printed, truncated; no number) the word after it (*kṛduttarapada*) keeps its natural (*prakṛti*) accent.

**मधुला (*madhulā*)**: root ला आदाने (*lā ādāne*). In सुपिस्थः (*supisthaḥ*) the word सुपि (*supi*) is taken as a separate rule (*yogavibhāga*); therefore, when a subanta stands as upapada, the affix ka comes also after other roots ending in ā; so here too the affix ka; as before the second member keeps its natural accent. *(No sūtra numbers printed.)* *(Ṛk 10 grammar ends; चकार not treated.)*

#### Ṛk 11

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Accents not reproduced.)*

> इयत्तिका शकुंतिका सका जघास ते विषं ।
> सो चिन्नु न मराति नो वयं मरामारे अस्य योजनं
> हरिष्ठा मधु त्वा मधुला चकार ॥ ११ ॥

> *iyattikā śakuṃtikā sakā jaghāsa te viṣaṃ |*
> *so cinnu na marāti no vayaṃ marāmāre asya yojanaṃ*
> *hariṣṭhā madhu tvā madhulā cakāra ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> इयत्तिका । शकुंतिका । सका । जघास । ते । विषं ।
> सो इति । चित् । नु । न । मराति । नो इति । वयं । मराम । आरे । अस्य । योजनं ।
> हरिऽस्थाः । मधु । त्वा । मधुला । चकार ॥ ११ ॥

> *iyattikā | śakuṃtikā | sakā | jaghāsa | te | viṣaṃ |*
> *so iti | cit | nu | na | marāti | no iti | vayaṃ | marāma | āre | asya | yojanaṃ |*
> *hari 'sthāḥ | madhu | tvā | madhulā | cakāra ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* The little bird has eaten your poison; being poison's natural enemy she does not die; the rest as before.

> इयत्तिका । इयत्तां कुर्वाणेयत्तावती वा । बालेत्यर्थः । शकुंतिका । शकुंतेः शकुनः । तस्य स्त्री । तां कपिंजलीमाहुः । सका सा ते तव विषं जघास । भक्षितवती । सा विषहंत्रीति प्रसिद्धा । सो चित् ॥ सा उ इति निपातसमुदायः एकं पदं ॥ सापि शकुंतिका न म्रियते नित्यप्रतिपक्षत्वाद्विषस्य । शिष्टं व्याख्यातचरं । अनेन विद्यायां युद्धेहावृतं [?] विषं तस्य शकुनेभ्य आदित्याय च प्रदानमस्तीत्युक्तं भवति ॥

> *iyattikā | iyattāṃ kurvāṇeyattāvatī vā | bāletyarthaḥ | śakuṃtikā | śakuṃteḥ śakunaḥ | tasya strī | tāṃ kapiṃjalīmāhuḥ | sakā sā te tava viṣaṃ jaghāsa | bhakṣitavatī | sā viṣahaṃtrīti prasiddhā | so cit ‖ sā u iti nipātasamudāyaḥ ekaṃ padaṃ ‖ sāpi śakuṃtikā na mriyate nityapratipakṣatvādviṣasya | śiṣṭaṃ vyākhyātacaraṃ | anena vidyāyāṃ yuddhehāvṛtaṃ [?] viṣaṃ tasya śakunebhya ādityāya ca pradānamastītyuktaṃ bhavati ‖*


**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

**इयत्तिका (*iyattikā*)** — of this small form. **सका शकुंतिका (*sakā śakuṃtikā*)** — that same bird. **ते (*te*)** — your. **विषं (*viṣaṃ*)** — poison. **जघास (*jaghāsa*)** — has eaten (even so). **सो चित् (*so cit*)** — that, being powerful. **नु (*nu*)** — certainly. **न मराति (*na marāti*)** — does not meet death. **नो वयं मराम (*no vayaṃ marāma*)** — we too shall not die.

*(Pratipadārtha continues on p. 361.)*

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 16 ]" (Varga numeral zoomed: ೧ then the hooked ೬, so 16; the previous pages read 15 unzoomed), "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Ṛk 11: Pratipadārtha ends, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics begun.)*

*(Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 11 continued from p. 360:)*

**आरे (*āre*)** — though far away. **हरिष्ठाः (*hariṣṭhāḥ*)** — the sun, mounted on horses. **अस्य (*asya*)** — of this poison. **योजनं (*yojanaṃ*)** — attains contact; (he makes the power of this poison not spread to us). *(O poison!)* **मधुला (*madhulā*)** — the Madhuvidyā. **त्वा (*tvā*)** — you. **मधु चकार (*madhu cakāra*)** — has changed into nectar.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

This small-formed bird has eaten your poison. Yet, because it is powerful, it does not die. Even from afar, the sun, mounted on horses, makes contact with this poison and so acts that the power of the poison does not spread to us. O poison, the Madhuvidyā has changed you into nectar.

**English Translation** *(printed heading)*

That little insignificant bird has swallowed your venom ; she does not die, nor shall we die; for, although afar off, yet drawn by his coursers, (the Sun) will overtake (the poison) ; the science of antidotes has converted you (Poison), to ambrosia.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In the preceding Ṛk it was told that the sun, being in the solar disc, removes poison; now it is described that a bird called the *kapiñjala* eats the poison and removes it.

**इयत्तिका शकुंतिका (*iyattikā śakuṃtikā*)** — **इयत्तां कुर्वाणेयत्तावती वा । बालेत्यर्थः (*iyattāṃ kurvāṇeyattāvatī vā | bāletyarthaḥ*)**. It is the nature of children to imitate what they see someone do. So इयत्तिका (*iyattikā*) means one who has the nature of imitating, a girl (बालिका (*bālikā*)). शकुंतेः (*śakuṃteḥ*) means of the शकुन (*śakuna*) bird, or the *kapiñjala* is also its name (Francoline partridge). शकुंतिका (*śakuṃtikā*) means the female bird. Therefore इयत्तिका-शकुंतिका (*iyattikā-śakuṃtikā*) means a small शकुन (*śakuna*) or the female young of the *kapiñjala* bird. The name of the शकुंत (*śakuṃta*) bird is mentioned in Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-42-3 and 2-43-1 (the file agrees; unzoomed).

**सका जघास ते विषं (*sakā jaghāsa te viṣaṃ*)** — सका (*sakā*) means सा (*sā*). The female *kapiñjala* bird described before ate your (the poison's) poison. A small bird eats poison without taking notice of it. Since that is its natural food, it does not die. We too do not die. All such details are as before.

### Printed p. 362 (PDF 382)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 191". Ṛk 11 Special Topics end; Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā of Ṛk 11; Ṛk 12 Saṃhitā and Pada.)*

**सो चिन्नु (*so cinnu*)** — here the commentator has not divided the words as सः चित् नु (*saḥ cit nu*), as he did in the preceding Ṛk. Instead the division is सा (*sā*) + उ (*u*) = सो (*so*). Since the particle उ (*u*) is used as a filler, if one divides सा (*sā*), it becomes a qualifying word of शकुंतिका (*śakuṃtikā*); so he explains.

**व्याकरणप्रक्रिया (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*

**सका (*sakā*)**: the word तद् (*tad*). By अव्ययसर्वनाम्नामकच् प्राक् टेः (*avyayasarvanāmnāmakac prāk ṭeḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 5-3-71, file agrees, not zoomed) akac comes in the middle; by a rule printed as तेदोः सावन् (*tedoḥ sāvan*) (as it looks: the Kannada prints a garbled word after तेदोः सा) [?] the initial ta becomes sa; since akac is *cit*, the final-udātta accent comes by चितः (*citaḥ*); since it ends in a (by *tyadādyatva*), ṭāp in the feminine; by the ekādeśa accent it too becomes udātta.

**जघास (*jaghāsa*)**: root अद भक्षणे (*ada bhakṣaṇe*); when liṭ is intended, by लिट्यन्यतरस्याम् (*liṭyanyatarasyām*) (Pā. Sū. 2-4-40, file agrees, not zoomed) the substitute ghasḷ for the root; reduplication etc.; by अत उपधायाः (*ata upadhāyāḥ*) the penultimate vowel is lengthened; nighāta accent because of the atiṅanta that follows.

**सो इति (*so iti*)**: here there are two words, सा (*sā*) and उ (*u*). By निपाताः (*nipātāḥ*) (as printed, no number): since these are read [in the list], both receive the name nipāta and make one pada.

### Printed p. 363 (PDF 383)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 16 ]" (Varga numeral unzoomed, read 16), "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Ṛk 12: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics begun.)*

**सायणभाष्यम् (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)**

*Gist:* Three times seven, i.e. twenty-one, kinds of sparks (or small birds), antagonists of poison; may they devour the strength of the poison that envelops us.

> त्रिः सप्त त्रिगुणिताः सप्तसंख्याका विष्पुलिंगका विविधाः विष्पुलिंगकाः । सप्तसु जिह्वासु लोहितशुक्लकृष्णभेदेन्यैकविंशतिर्यासां ताः । यद्वा । त्रिः सप्तैकविंशतिभेदा विष्पुलिंगकाः सूक्ष्मचटकिका विषप्रतिपक्षभूताः । विषस्यास्मदावरकस्य पुष्यं पोषमक्षन् । अदंतु नाशयंतु । ताश्च न मरंति न वयमपि । शिष्टमवशिष्टं ॥

> *triḥ sapta triguṇitāḥ saptasaṃkhyākā viṣpuliṃgakā vividhāḥ viṣpuliṃgakāḥ | saptasu jihvāsu lohitaśuklakṛṣṇabhedenyaikaviṃśatiryāsāṃ tāḥ | yadvā | triḥ saptaikaviṃśatibhedā viṣpuliṃgakāḥ sūkṣmacaṭakikā viṣapratipakṣabhūtāḥ | viṣasyāsmadāvarakasya puṣyaṃ poṣamakṣan | adaṃtu nāśayaṃtu | tāśca na maraṃti na vayamapi | śiṣṭamavaśiṣṭaṃ ‖*


**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

**त्रिः सप्त (*triḥ sapta*)** — of the threefold seven, i.e. twenty-one (२१) in number. **विष्पुलिंगकाः (*viṣpuliṃgakāḥ*)** — various fire-sparks. **विषस्य (*viṣasya*)** — of the poison that has enveloped us. **पुष्यं (*puṣyaṃ*)** — the strong power. **अक्षन् (*akṣan*)** — let them swallow up (destroy). **ताश्चिन्नु (*tāścinnu*)** — as for them. **न मराति (*na marāti*)** — though broken up they do not meet death. **नो वयं मराम (*no vayaṃ marāma*)** — we too do not meet death. **आरे (*āre*)** — though far away. **हरिष्ठाः (*hariṣṭhāḥ*)** — the sun, mounted on horses. **अस्य (*asya*)** — of this poison. **योजनं (*yojanaṃ*)** — attains contact (he makes the power of this poison not spread to us). **मधुला (*madhulā*)** — the Madhuvidyā. **त्वा (*tvā*)** — you. **मधु चकार (*madhu cakāra*)** — has changed into nectar.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

The twenty-one kinds of fire-sparks, or birds, swallow up and destroy the strong power of the poison that has enveloped us. They themselves do not die; by their influence we too do not die. Even from afar, the sun, mounted on horses, makes contact with this poison and so acts that its power does not spread to us. O poison, the Madhuvidyā has changed you into nectar.

**English Translation** *(printed heading)*

May the thrice-seven sparks (of Agni) consume the influence of the venom ; they verily do not perish ; nor shall we die ; for although afar off, the Sun, drawn by his coursers, will overtake the poison ; the science of antidotes has converted you, (Poison), to ambrosia.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this Ṛk it is prayed that the twenty-one kinds of sparks of Agni, or birds, remove our poison.

**त्रिः सप्त (*triḥ sapta*)** — **त्रिगुणिताः सप्तसंख्याकाः (*triguṇitāḥ saptasaṃkhyākāḥ*)**. The meaning is: three times seven, or twenty-one.

### Printed p. 364 (PDF 384)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 191". Ṛk 12 Special Topics end, Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā; Ṛk 13 Saṃhitā and Pada, Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya begun.)*

**विष्पुलिंगकाः (*viṣpuliṃgakāḥ*)** — **विविधाः विष्पुलिंगकाः । सप्तसु जिह्वासु लोहितशुक्लकृष्णभेदेन्यैकविंशतिर्यासां ताः । यद्वा । त्रिः सप्तैकविंशतिभेदा विष्पुलिंगकाः सूक्ष्मचटकिका विषप्रतिपक्षभूताः (*vividhāḥ viṣpuliṃgakāḥ | saptasu jihvāsu lohitaśuklakṛṣṇabhedenyaikaviṃśatiryāsāṃ tāḥ | yadvā | triḥ saptaikaviṃśatibhedā viṣpuliṃgakāḥ sūkṣmacaṭakikā viṣapratipakṣabhūtāḥ*)**. The sparks of Agni are said to be of twenty-one kinds. It is well known that Agni has seven tongues (flames); in each flame there are twenty-one sparks, differing as red, white and black. Or *viṣpuliṅga* means sparrows, or small birds such as the *garuḍa* bird (*garuḍapakṣi*); among these there are twenty-one varieties or species. These have the nature of eating poison without taking notice of it. The other matters are as in the preceding Ṛk.

**व्याकरणप्रक्रिया (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*

**पुष्यम् (*puṣyam*)**: root पुष पुष्टौ (*puṣa puṣṭau*); the chāndasa affix śa; since it is śit it takes precedence and the vikaraṇa śyan comes; since it is nit, the first-syllable udātta accent comes.

**अक्षन् (*akṣan*)**: root अद भक्षणे (*ada bhakṣaṇe*); chāndasa luṅ in the sense of loṭ; by लुङ्सनोर्घस्ऌ (*luṅsanorghasḷ*) (Pā. Sū. 2-4-37, file agrees, not zoomed) the substitute ghasḷ for the root; by मंत्रेघस- (*maṃtreghasa-*) (as printed, truncated) cli gets luk; by गमहन- (*gamahana-*) (as printed, truncated) the penultimate is dropped; cartva; satva; the augment aḍ (as it looks); the tiṅanta nighāta accent.

#### Ṛk 13

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Accents not reproduced.)*

> नवानां नवतीनां विषस्य रोपुषीणां ।
> सर्वासामग्रभं नामारे अस्य योजनं हरिष्ठा मधु त्वा
> मधुला चकार ॥ १३ ॥

> *navānāṃ navatīnāṃ viṣasya ropuṣīṇāṃ |*

> नवानां । नवतीनां । विषस्य । रोपुषीणां ।
> सर्वासां । अग्रभं । नाम । आरे । अस्य । योजनं । हरिऽस्थाः । मधु । त्वा । मधुला ।

> *cakāra ‖ 13 ‖*

**सायणभाष्यम् (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)** *(continues on p. 365)*

*Gist:* Of ninety-nine rivers, destroyers of all poison that pervades us — their names I recite; the rest as before.

> नवानां नवतीनां नवाधिकानां नवतिसंख्याकानां नदीनां । पुनः कीदृशीनां । विषस्यास्मद्व्यापकस्य सर्वस्य विषस्य रोपुषीणां लोपयित्रीणां छेत्रीणां । सर्वा-

> *navānāṃ navatīnāṃ navādhikānāṃ navatisaṃkhyākānāṃ nadīnāṃ | punaḥ kīdṛśīnāṃ | viṣasyāsmadvyāpakasya sarvasya viṣasya ropuṣīṇāṃ lopayitrīṇāṃ chetrīṇāṃ | sarvā-*

*(Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya of Ṛk 13 continued from p. 364:)*

> सर्वासामुक्तानां गंगादिनदीनां नामाग्रभं । गृह्णामि । संकीर्तयामि ॥ गृहेश्छांदसे लुङि छांदसश्छ्लेर्लुक् । हृग्रहोर्भः ॥ अस्य योजनमित्यादि गतं ॥

> *sarvāsāmuktānāṃ gaṃgādinadīnāṃ nāmāgrabhaṃ | gṛhṇāmi | saṃkīrtayāmi ‖ gṛheśchāṃdase luṅi chāṃdasaśchlerluk | hṛgrahorbhaḥ ‖ asya yojanamityādi gataṃ ‖*


**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

**नवानां नवतीनां (*navānāṃ navatīnāṃ*)** — of those that are ninety-nine in number. **विषस्य (*viṣasya*)** — of poison. **रोपुषीणां (*ropuṣīṇāṃ*)** — and that are destroyers. **सर्वासां (*sarvāsāṃ*)** — of all the rivers beginning with Gaṅgā. **नाम (*nāma*)** — the sacred name. **अग्रभं (*agrabhaṃ*)** — I praise. **आरे (*āre*)** — though far away. **हरिष्ठाः (*hariṣṭhāḥ*)** — the sun, mounted on horses. **अस्य (*asya*)** — of this poison. **योजनं (*yojanaṃ*)** — attains contact (O poison!). **मधुला (*madhulā*)** — the Madhuvidyā. **त्वा (*tvā*)** — you. **मधु चकार (*madhu cakāra*)** — has changed into nectar.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

I praise the sacred names of all the rivers beginning with Gaṅgā, ninety-nine in number, which are destroyers of poison. Even from afar, the sun, mounted on horses, makes contact with this poison. O poison, the Madhuvidyā has changed you into nectar.

**English Translation** *(printed heading)*

I recite the names of ninety and nine (rivers), the destroyers of poison ; although afar off, (the Sun), drawn by his coursers· will overtake the poison : the science of antidote has converted you, (Poison), to ambrosia.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

Having told so far the means of removing poison, the sage now describes that he will make remembrance of the holy rivers such as the Gaṅgā, for the removal of the fault of poison.

**नवानां नवतीनां (*navānāṃ navatīnāṃ*)** — here नवानां नवतीनां (*navānāṃ navatīnāṃ*) is said to mean नवाधिकानां नवतिसंख्याकानां नदीनां (*navādhikānāṃ navatisaṃkhyākānāṃ nadīnāṃ*), that is, of ninety-nine rivers. When one speaks of the sense of "many" or "numerous", words such as *navanavati*, *śata* and *sahasra* are used in many places in the Ṛgveda. In such places the number need not be taken as exactly so many. The sage says that he will remember the many (numerous) holy rivers such as the Gaṅgā.

**व्याकरणप्रक्रिया (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*

**नवानाम् (*navānām*)**: by षट्त्रिचतुर्भ्योहलादिः (*ṣaṭtricaturbhyohalādiḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-179, file agrees, not zoomed) — since this word, ending in n, has the designation ṣaṭ, the following नाम् (*nām*) case-ending receives the udātta accent. *(Grammar of Ṛk 13 continues on p. 366; Ṛk 13 is left open.)*

**व्याकरणप्रक्रिया (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)** *(Ṛk 13 continued; grammar page, noted briefly)*

**नवतीनाम् (*navatīnām*)**: by पंक्ति विशंति- (*paṃkti viśaṃti-*) (Pā. #### Ṛk 14

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Accents not reproduced.)*

> त्रिः सप्त मयूर्यः सप्त स्वसारो अग्रुवः ।
> तास्ते विषं वि जभ्रिर उदकं कुंभिनीरिव ॥ १४ ॥

> *triḥ sapta mayūryaḥ sapta svasāro agruvaḥ |*
> *tāste viṣaṃ vi jabhrira udakaṃ kuṃbhinīriva ‖ 14 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्रिः । सप्त । मयूर्यः । सप्त । स्वसारः । अग्रुवः ।
> ताः । ते । विषं । वि । जभ्रिरे । उदकं । कुंभिनीःऽइव ॥ १४ ॥

> *triḥ | sapta | mayūryaḥ | sapta | svasāraḥ | agruvaḥ |*
> *tāḥ | te | viṣaṃ | vi | jabhrire | udakaṃ | kuṃbhinīḥ 'iva ‖ 14 ‖*

**सायणभाष्यम् (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)**

*Gist:* Twenty-one peahens, and the seven flowing sisters (rivers), are asked to carry off the body's poison as women with pitchers carry water.

> त्रिः सप्तैकविंशतिसंख्याका मयूर्यो मयूरस्त्रियः ॥ ता विषकारिसर्पद्वेषिण्य इति प्रसिद्धा नागद्वेषिगरुडपक्षादुत्पन्नत्वात् । तथा सप्तैतत्संख्याकाः सर्पणस्वभावाः स्वसारः स्वयमेव सरणा अग्रुवः । नदीनामैतत् [?] । सुरगंगाद्याः प्रसिद्धाः सप्त नद्यः संति । तास्ते हे देह तव विषं वि जभ्रिरे । विशेषेण हरंतु । तत्र दृष्टांतः । उदकं कुंभिनीः कुंभिन्यः कुंभवत्यः कुंभेन जलहारिण्य इव । ता यथा तद्धरंति तद्वन्नद्यो मयूर्यश्चातिप्रभूतं हरंतु ॥

> *triḥ saptaikaviṃśatisaṃkhyākā mayūryo mayūrastriyaḥ ‖ tā viṣakārisarpadveṣiṇya iti prasiddhā nāgadveṣigaruḍapakṣādutpannatvāt | tathā saptaitatsaṃkhyākāḥ sarpaṇasvabhāvāḥ svasāraḥ svayameva saraṇā agruvaḥ | nadīnāmaitat [?] | suragaṃgādyāḥ prasiddhāḥ sapta nadyaḥ saṃti | tāste he deha tava viṣaṃ vi jabhrire | viśeṣeṇa haraṃtu | tatra dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ | udakaṃ kuṃbhinīḥ kuṃbhinyaḥ kuṃbhavatyaḥ kuṃbhena jalahāriṇya iva | tā yathā taddharaṃti tadvannadyo mayūryaścātiprabhūtaṃ haraṃtu ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

(O body — Elaide dehave) **त्रिः सप्त (*triḥ sapta*)** — the twenty-one in number; **मयूर्यः (*mayūryaḥ*)** — the peahens; **सप्त (*sapta*)** — the seven in number; **स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*)** — flowing; **ताः अग्रुवः (*tāḥ agruvaḥ*)** — the rivers beginning with Gaṅgā likewise; **कुंभिनीः (*kuṃbhinīḥ*)** — women who carry water in pitchers; **उदकं इव (*udakaṃ iva*)** — as they go away filling water; **ते (*te*)** — your; **विषं (*viṣaṃ*)** — poison; **वि जभ्रिरे (*vi jabhrire*)** — may they carry off completely (may it be destroyed).

### Printed p. 367 (PDF 387)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 16" (Varga numeral unzoomed, read 16), "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Ṛk 14: Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics, grammar.)*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

O body, may the twenty-one peahens, and the seven flowing rivers beginning with Gaṅgā, carry off your poison completely, as women who bear water in pitchers go away having filled them with water.

**English Translation** *(printed heading)*

May the thrice-seven peahens, the seven-sister rivers, carry off, (O Body), your poison as maidens, with pitchers, carry away water·

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

**त्रिः सप्त मयूर्यः (*triḥ sapta mayūryaḥ*)** — *mayūra* means a peacock; *mayūrī* means a peahen. They are peahens of twenty-one kinds (made up of twenty-one differences of species); it is said that these peacocks are born from the garuḍa birds that hate snakes. Therefore it is well known in the world that these peacocks fearlessly kill and eat snakes.

**सप्त स्वसारो अग्रुवः (*sapta svasāro agruvaḥ*)** — *svasāraḥ* means of a flowing nature, flowing. The word *agruvaḥ* is read both among the names of the finger (Ni. 3-9, file agrees, not zoomed) and among the names of rivers (Ni. 2-24, file agrees, not zoomed). Here rivers are meant; they say that flowing rivers have the power of removing poison. Therefore the bhāṣyakāra says here "the seven rivers beginning with Gaṅgā". Or it may be Gaṅgā and its tributaries. Although there are many holy rivers, since the word *sapta* (seven) is used here, the sage's intention rests on seven principal rivers.

**ते विषं (*te viṣaṃ*)** — the bhāṣyakāra's explanation is that this word "your" addresses the body. It is a prayer that the peahens and the seven flowing rivers may remove the poison of your (body).

**उदकं कुंभिनीरिव (*udakaṃ kuṃbhinīriva*)** — कुंभिनीः कुंभिन्यः कुंभवत्यः कुंभेन जलहारिण्य इव । ता यथा तद्धरंति तद्वन्नद्यो मयूर्यश्चातिप्रभूतं हरंतु । (*kuṃbhinīḥ kuṃbhinyaḥ kuṃbhavatyaḥ kuṃbhena jalahāriṇya iva | tā yathā taddharaṃti tadvannadyo mayūryaścātiprabhūtaṃ haraṃtu |*) *Kumbhinī* means women who bear a *kumbha* (earthen pot or brass pot) for bringing water. As such women take away water in pots from a river or other reservoir, may the rivers take away the poison spread in the body: thus the example is given.

**व्याकरणप्रक्रिया (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*

**मयूर्यः (*mayūryaḥ*)**: the word *mayūra*; since it denotes a species in the feminine, the affix ṅīṣ; in jas, the yaṇ substitution; since yaṇ comes in the place of an udātta, the following syllable gets the svarita accent. *(No sūtra numbers printed.)*

### Printed p. 368 (PDF 388)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 191", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā". Ṛk 14 grammar ends; Ṛk 15 begins; Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 15 begun and runs on to p. 369. The numeral file has no rows for this page; Ṛk numerals read from the strips, unzoomed.)*

**जभ्रिरे (*jabhrire*)**: root हृञ् हरणे (*hṛñ haraṇe*); chāndasa liṭ in the sense of loṭ; for the prathama (third-person) plural the substitute इरेच् (*irec*); because it has the kit-like extension (kittvātideśa) there is no guṇa; yaṇ substitution; since it stands after an atiṅanta [as printed], the nighāta accent comes.

**कुंभिनीः (*kuṃbhinīḥ*)**: कुंभः आसामस्ति (*kuṃbhaḥ āsāmasti*) [as printed] — *kumbhinī*; the affix ini in the sense of "possessing"; since in the feminine it ends in n, ṅīp; by the initial-udātta accent of the affix ini the word becomes madhyodātta; chāndasa: when jas follows, the preceding-similar long vowel (pūrvasavarṇadīrgha).

#### Ṛk 15

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Accents not reproduced.)*

> इयत्तकः कुषुंभकस्तकं भिनद्म्यश्मना ।
> ततो विषं प्र वावृते पराचीरनु संवतः ॥ १५ ॥

> *iyattakaḥ kuṣuṃbhakastakaṃ bhinadmyaśmanā |*
> *tato viṣaṃ pra vāvṛte parācīranu saṃvataḥ ‖ 15 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> इयत्तकः । कुषुंभकः । तकं । भिनद्मि । अश्मना ।
> ततः । विषं । प्र । ववृते । पराचीः । अनु । संऽवतः ॥ १५ ॥

> *iyattakaḥ | kuṣuṃbhakaḥ | takaṃ | bhinadmi | aśmanā |*
> *tataḥ | viṣaṃ | pra | vavṛte | parācīḥ | anu | saṃ 'vataḥ ‖ 15 ‖*

**सायणभाष्यम् (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)**

*Gist:* The little mongoose (kuṣumbhaka) removes the poison; if not, I split it with a stone; then the poison turns away, going far in the directions, not to me.

> इयत्तकः कुत्सितेयत्तः । अल्पप्रमाण इत्यर्थः । कुषुंभकः कुं पृथ्वीं सुंभति विलिखतीति सर्पाणां कुत्सितं सुंभयिता निग्रहीता कुषुंभको नकुलः । स ते विषं हरत्विति शेषः । यदि न तथा स करोति तकं कुत्सितं तं नकुलमश्मना भिनद्मि । विदारयामि । विषनिर्हरणप्रयोगे यावद्विषापगमं तं पाषाणानुघातमनुतिष्ठंति तद्विदः । तदिदमत्रोक्तं । ततः एवं प्रयोगे सति विषं प्र वावृते । विषावृताद्देहाद्विषं प्रवर्तते । निर्गच्छतु । काः प्रति । उच्यते । पराचीः पराग्चनवतीरतिदूरगाः संवतः संविभागवतो दिशोऽनु लक्षीकृत्य । दिगंतं प्रति गच्छतु न मां प्रति गच्छतीत्यर्थः ॥

> *iyattakaḥ kutsiteyattaḥ | alpapramāṇa ityarthaḥ | kuṣuṃbhakaḥ kuṃ pṛthvīṃ suṃbhati vilikhatīti sarpāṇāṃ kutsitaṃ suṃbhayitā nigrahītā kuṣuṃbhako nakulaḥ | sa te viṣaṃ haratviti śeṣaḥ | yadi na tathā sa karoti takaṃ kutsitaṃ taṃ nakulamaśmanā bhinadmi | vidārayāmi | viṣanirharaṇaprayoge yāvadviṣāpagamaṃ taṃ pāṣāṇānughātamanutiṣṭhaṃti tadvidaḥ | tadidamatroktaṃ | tataḥ evaṃ prayoge sati viṣaṃ pra vāvṛte | viṣāvṛtāddehādviṣaṃ pravartate | nirgacchatu | kāḥ prati | ucyate | parācīḥ parāgcanavatīratidūragāḥ saṃvataḥ saṃvibhāgavato diśo 'nu lakṣīkṛtya | digaṃtaṃ prati gacchatu na māṃ prati gacchatītyarthaḥ ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered; continues on p. 369)*

**इयत्तकः (*iyattakaḥ*)** — of small measure; **कुषुंभकः (*kuṣuṃbhakaḥ*)** — the mongoose (if this (mongoose) does not remove this snake-bite poison of mine); **तकं (*takaṃ*)** — that wretched mongoose; **अश्मना (*aśmanā*)** — with a stone; **भिनद्मि (*bhinadmi*)** — […continues on p. 369]

*(Ṛk 15 is left open: the Pratipadārtha runs on to p. 369.)*

### Printed p. 369 (PDF 389)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5 [?], Varga 16" in small Kannada numerals, read unzoomed; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". No numeral rows in the file for this page.)*

**Pratipadārtha (continued from p. 368).** — **भिनद्मि (*bhinadmi*)** — (I) will crush (literally "throw down by crushing"); **ततः (*tataḥ*)** — afterwards; **विषं (*viṣaṃ*)** — the poison; **प्र वावृते (*pra vāvṛte*)** — let it come out; **पराचीः (*parācīḥ*)** — very far-off; **संवतः (*saṃvataḥ*)** — the directions; **अनु (*anu*)** — aiming at (them), let it go away.

**Bhāvārtha.** *(Kannada, rendered)* May the mongoose of small size remove this poison of my snake-bite. If it does not, I will crush it with a stone. Afterwards may the poison come out and go away to a very distant region.

**Printed English** (heading printed "English Translation"):

May the insignificant mungoose (carry off) your venom, (Poison), if not, I will crush the vile (creature) with a stone; so may the poison depart (from my body), and go to distant regions.

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this Ṛk the sage has expressed the wish that the mongoose destroy the poison.

**इयत्तकः (*iyattakaḥ*) — कुत्सितेयत्तः अल्पप्रमाण इत्यर्थः (*kutsiteyattaḥ alpapramāṇa ityarthaḥ*)** — "very small, of a tiny bodily form; slight or small" is the meaning.

**कुषुंभकः (*kuṣuṃbhakaḥ*) — कुं पृथिवीं सुंभति विलिखतीति सर्पाणां कुत्सितं सुंभयिता निग्रहीता कुषुंभको नकुलः (*kuṃ pṛthivīṃ suṃbhati vilikhatīti sarpāṇāṃ kutsitaṃ suṃbhayitā nigrahītā kuṣuṃbhako nakulaḥ*)** — *ku* means the earth (the ground); because the mongoose is aware of the movement of snakes, which, when crawling on that ground, scratch the earth crookedly like a furrow, *kutsitaṃ* means "the snakes"; because it seizes and kills such snakes it is called *kuṣuṃbhaka*; the name is *nakula* or *muṅgasi* (the neul or or [sic] viverra Mungoose, as printed). It is world-famous that these mongooses kill the snakes that are their natural enemies. Such a mongoose is prayed to remove the poison of the body. Here the verb *haratu* ("let it remove") must be supplied.

**तकं भिनद्मि अश्मना (*takaṃ bhinadmi aśmanā*)** — *takam* means "that small or low creature". "If perchance the mongoose does not remove the poison, I will crush that low creature with a stone": so he said. In practices of poison-removal, a stone is struck one against another even for the one who has become well [i.e. even after the poison has wholly gone]; the same is done here too: this is Sāyaṇa's explanation.

**ततो विषं प्र वावृते पराचीरनु संवृताः (*tato viṣaṃ pra vāvṛte parācīranu saṃvṛtāḥ*)** *(as printed; the Saṃhitā has संवतः)* — by this sentence in the latter half: may the poison leave the body and not come back near me, but go far away into the various directions: so he prayed.

### Printed p. 370 (PDF 390)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 Sū. 191", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā". Grammar notes of Ṛk 15, then Ṛk 16. Numeral file: Pā. Sū. 6-1-7 and Ā. Gṛ. 3-5-5 agree, not zoomed.)*

**व्याकरणप्रक्रिया (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*

**भिनद्मि (*bhinadmi*)**: root भिदिर् विदारणे (*bhidir vidāraṇe*), rudhādi class; laṭ, first person singular, mip; the vikaraṇa śnam; since it is mit it comes after the na-kāra [as printed]; since it stands after an atiṅanta [as printed], the nighāta accent comes.

**ववृते (*vavṛte*)**: root वृतु वर्तने (*vṛtu vartane*); by छंदसि लुङ् (*chaṃdasi luṅ*) (printed so, truncated) liṭ in the sense of loṭ; the ending form of the third person singular; since it belongs to the tudādi class, by तुजादीनां दीर्घोऽभ्यासस्य (*tujādīnāṃ dīrgho 'bhyāsasya*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-7) the reduplicative syllable is lengthened in the Saṃhitā; the tiṅanta-nighāta accent comes.

#### Ṛk 16

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Accents not reproduced.)*

> कुषुंभकस्तदब्रवीद्गिरेः प्रवर्तमानकः ।
> वृश्चिकस्यारसं विषमरसं वृश्चिक ते विषं ॥ १६ ॥

> *kuṣuṃbhakastadabravīdgireḥ pravartamānakaḥ |*
> *vṛścikasyārasaṃ viṣamarasaṃ vṛścika te viṣaṃ ‖ 16 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> कुषुंभकः । तत् । अब्रवीत् । गिरेः । प्रऽवर्तमानकः ।
> वृश्चिकस्य । अरसं । विषं । अरसं । वृश्चिक । ते । विषं ॥ १६ ॥

> *kuṣuṃbhakaḥ | tat | abravīt | gireḥ | pra 'vartamānakaḥ |*
> *vṛścikasya | arasaṃ | viṣaṃ | arasaṃ | vṛścika | te | viṣaṃ ‖ 16 ‖*

**सायणभाष्यम् (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)**

*Gist:* This Ṛk is used in the Adhyāya-upākaraṇa and utsarjana; the mongoose, coming from the mountain at Agastya's word, tells the scorpion its poison is powerless; so the poison (of the one bitten) ceased.

> अध्यायोपाकरणोत्सर्गयोः कुषुंभकस्तदित्यंत्या विनियुक्ता । दधिसक्तूञ्जुहोतीत्युपक्रम्य कुषुंभकस्तदब्रवीत् । आ. गृ. ३-५-५ । इति सूत्रितत्वात् ॥

> *adhyāyopākaraṇotsargayoḥ kuṣuṃbhakastadityaṃtyā viniyuktā | dadhisaktūñjuhotītyupakramya kuṣuṃbhakastadabravīt | ā. gṛ. 3-5-5 | iti sūtritatvāt ‖*
>
> एवं महानुभावेनागस्त्यमहर्षिणोच्यमाने सति गिरेः सकाशात्प्रवर्तमानकः प्रवर्तमानोऽतिशीघ्रमभिगच्छन् कुषुंभको नकुलस्तदब्रवीत् । तद्वाक्यमाचख्यौ । किं तदिति उच्यते । वृश्चिकस्यैतद्विषमरसमसारं । बाधकं न भवतीत्यर्थः । तथा लोकेऽपि सर्पदष्टमपि क्रिम्यादिदंशनमेव अतो न बाध इति हि वदंति । एवमभिवचनेन सोऽपि निर्विषोऽभवत् । अथ तं वृश्चिकं प्रति नकुल आह । हे वृश्चिक ते विषमरसं । अतस्त्वृषिं किं करिष्यति । तस्मात्परिहरेति । यद्वैव वादीत् तदाप्रभृति वृश्चिकविषमसारमभवत् । एषा विषनिर्हरण्युपनिषत् ॥

> *evaṃ mahānubhāvenāgastyamaharṣiṇocyamāne sati gireḥ sakāśātpravartamānakaḥ pravartamāno 'tiśīghramabhigacchan kuṣuṃbhako nakulastadabravīt | tadvākyamācakhyau | kiṃ taditi ucyate | vṛścikasyaitadviṣamarasamasāraṃ | bādhakaṃ na bhavatītyarthaḥ | tathā loke 'pi sarpadaṣṭamapi krimyādidaṃśanameva ato na bādha iti hi vadaṃti | evamabhivacanena so 'pi nirviṣo 'bhavat | atha taṃ vṛścikaṃ prati nakula āha | he vṛścika te viṣamarasaṃ | atastvṛṣiṃ kiṃ kariṣyati | tasmātparihareti | yadvaiva vādīt tadāprabhṛti vṛścikaviṣamasāramabhavat | eṣā viṣanirharaṇyupaniṣat ‖*

*(Doubtful readings [?]: आचख्यौ (*ācakhyau*) [?], क्रिम्यादि (*krimyādi*) as printed [?], महर्षिणोच्यमाने (*maharṣiṇocyamāne*) as printed, यद्वैव वादीत् (*yadvaiva vādīt*) [?] — the line is worn with a stray mark.)*

### Printed p. 371 (PDF 391)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5 [?], Varga 16", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Numerals checked against the file: Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 3-5-5, Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-1, 1-191-16, 2-43-3 agree; Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-1 zoomed — file said 2-0-0, crop shows 2-1-1.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थः (Pratipadārtha)** *(Kannada, rendered)*

**गिरेः (*gireḥ*)** — (after Agastya the sage had prayed in this way) from the mountain; **प्रवर्तमानकः (*pravartamānakaḥ*)** — approaching the sage quickly; **कुषुंभकः (*kuṣuṃbhakaḥ*)** — the mongoose; **तदब्रवीत् (*tadabravīt*)** — spoke thus; **वृश्चिकस्य (*vṛścikasya*)** — of the poisonous scorpion; **विषं (*viṣaṃ*)** — the poison; **अरसं (*arasaṃ*)** — powerless (therefore not harmful); **वृश्चिक (*vṛścika*)** — O scorpion; **ते विषं (*te viṣaṃ*)** — your poison; **अरसं (*arasaṃ*)** — powerless.

**Bhāvārtha.** After the sage Agastya had thus prayed, the mongoose, which had come out suddenly from the mountain, approached the sage and said: "The poison of the poisonous scorpion is powerless. O scorpion, your poison has no power. It cannot do harm to anyone."

**Printed English** (heading printed "Englih Tranlation" [sic]):

Hastening forth at the command (of Agastya), thus spoke the mungoose·—The venom of the scorpion is innocuous, scorpion, your venom is innocuous· *(dots as printed; "mun-goose" is hyphenated at the line end)*

**Special Topics (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

**कुषुंभकस्तत् (*kuṣuṃbhakastat*)** — this last Ṛk (of the sūkta, or of the maṇḍala) is used in the dadhisaktu-homa in the rite called Adhyāyopākarma or Utsarjana, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Gṛhyasūtra: **दधिसक्तूञ्जुहोतीत्युपक्रम्य कुषुंभकस्तदब्रवीत् (*dadhisaktūñjuhotītyupakramya kuṣuṃbhakastadabravīt*)** (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 3-5-5).

In the Adhyāyopākarma and Utsarjana rites mentioned above, when the dadhisaktu-homa is performed, the students of the Ṛk-recension recite and offer the first Ṛk of each maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda — for the first maṇḍala **अग्निमीळे पुरोहितं (*agnimīḷe purohitaṃ*)** (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-1) — and the last Ṛk of the maṇḍala, **कुषुंभकस्तदब्रवीत् (*kuṣuṃbhakastadabravīt*)** (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-191-16). Afterwards, in the same way, for the second maṇḍala the first Ṛk **त्वमग्ने द्युभिस्त्वमाशुशुक्षणिः (*tvamagne dyubhistvamāśuśukṣaṇiḥ*)** (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-1) and the last Ṛk of the same maṇḍala **आवदंस्त्वं शकुने भद्रमा वद (*āvadaṃstvaṃ śakune bhadramā vada*)** (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-43-3) are recited and offered. So up to the later maṇḍalas, that is to the tenth maṇḍala, the first and the last Ṛks of every maṇḍala, that is twenty Ṛks in all, are recited and offered.

**गिरेः प्रवर्तमानकः (*gireḥ pravartamānakaḥ*)** — means "coming out at once from the burrows etc. in the slope of the hill". In the preceding Ṛk the sage Agastya addressed the mongoose: "destroy the poison in the body; otherwise I will crush you with a stone." As soon as he had said this, the mongoose […continues on p. 372]

### Printed p. 372 (PDF 392)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 1 A. 24 [?] Sū. 191", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā".)*

**Special Topics (continued from p. 371)** — … became afraid, came out at once from the burrow-region of the mountain, his dwelling, and, in order to console the sage Agastya, spoke thus (that is, the following sentence): this is the meaning.

On this sūkta the scholar Wilson writes thus:

"M. Langlois has preferred a totally different interpretation of this sukta [sic], understan-ding it to allude to the state of the sky before the commencement of a sacrifice; he, therefore, interprets (Kannada-script word *viṣa*) by darkness· Which is dispersed by the morning light, or by the rays of the sun; On what authority this view of the intention of the hymn is founded has not been stated; nothing of the kind is intimated by Sayana [sic] whose interpretation is confirmed by the legendary application of the hymn as related by (Kannada-script word *Śaunaka*) by the corresponding text of the (Kannada-script word *Atharvaṇa*); there are no doubt, many expressions of doubtful import, and some which are used in other places, as in the (Kannada-script word *Yajurveda*), in a different acceptation; but the interpretation given by Sayana appears to be most consistent with the general purport of the text·" *(Wilson's English as printed; punctuation dots as printed.)*

**वृश्चिकस्यारसं विषमरसं वृश्चिक ते विषं (*vṛścikasyārasaṃ viṣamarasaṃ vṛścika te viṣaṃ*)** — this sentence was spoken by the mongoose to remove the poison. In the world, when people are bitten by poisonous creatures such as a scorpion, or by a snake that has poison, they become helpless with fear that they will die. That fear, more than the poison, becomes the effective cause of death. Therefore the wise, speaking to people bitten by a snake, say: "Do not be afraid, it was not a poisonous snake, so it can do no harm, you will be well at once"; it is the custom to remove fear by saying what is untrue (even if a poisonous snake has bitten). If fear is removed, the poison pervading the body is not so dangerous, and there is a chance of surviving. Following exactly this principle the mongoose came out at once from the hole in the mountain and said to Agastya, who was distressed with fear of poison: "O scorpion, your poison is not sharp; it is powerless." The repetition (dvirukti) in the sentence "vṛścikasya arasaṃ viṣaṃ" is to be understood as made to emphasize the sense of the sentence. As to why the mongoose, addressing the scorpion, spoke so: "O sage Agastya, you have no snake-bite; some scorpion with little poison may have bitten. A scorpion's bite causes no great trouble. Why do you suffer for it?" — from this consoling point of view the scorpion's poison is powerless and not sharp like a snake's. The main meaning is that there is no need to fear, said according to worldly custom.

**Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā** *(grammar page, noted briefly)*: **अब्रवीत् (*abravīt*)** — root ब्रूञ् व्यक्तायां वाचि (*brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci*), luṅ [as printed: uttama-puruṣa, ekavacana] ending tip; इतश्च (*itaśca*) drops the i; ब्रुव ईट् (*bruva īṭ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-93) gives the augment īṭ; guṇa/avādeśa of the root's u; aṭ-augment on the aṅga; tiṅanta-nighāta accent results.
