**Explanation (continued from p. 373):** "… O snake, run off and take refuge in the hole in the earth. Otherwise I will strike you with my staff, which is swift like the sun's chariot, strong like Vishnu's arms, and which falls from above like Garuḍa. When Garuḍa merely comes, the three worlds move; the whole earth with mountains and forests trembles in fear. At the rush of Garuḍa's coming the sun and moon become lightless, the stars do not shine, the gods shiver with fear, the wind does not blow. Therefore, O snake full of great poison, go far away; may it be well with you. In this matter make Janamejaya's sacrificial conclusion, the word of the sage Āstīka, known to you. Whatever snake, not heeding the words Āstīka spoke as a warning, does not go away, its head splits into a hundred pieces like the fruit of the śiṃśapā tree. O river Narmadā, to you salutation in the morning and in the night; protect me from the poison-snake. I remember the sage Jaratkāru, of great glory, born of (the maiden) Jaratkāru; for those who remember that great sage's name there is no fear of poison-snakes. Therefore, O poison-filled snake, go far; may you prosper. For the man who remembers Asiti, Arthasiddhi and Sunīti there is no snake-fear, by night or by day. And the man who remembers the five great sages Agasti, Mādhava, Muchukunda, Kapila and Āstīka sleeps happily at night, free of snake-fear."

### Printed p. 375 (PDF 395)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2 [?], Adhyāya 5 [?], Varga 1? [?]" — numerals not verified, no numeral file row; page number 375.)*

> ॥ श्रीः ॥

> *‖ śrīḥ ‖*

> ॥ श्री गणेशाय नमः ॥

> *‖ śrī gaṇeśāya namaḥ ‖*

> अथ द्वितीयं मंडलं

*(Title: "Atha dvitīyaṃ maṇḍalam" — "Now the second maṇḍala." Then a short rule.)*

**Pīṭhike (Introduction).** The Ṛgveda Saṃhitā has ten divisions; these divisions are called maṇḍalas. In the main, the whole body of mantras composed or "seen" by each individual ṛṣi and his family (or group) has been put together and fixed as one maṇḍala. But in the 1st, 9th and 10th maṇḍalas there are many ṛṣis of different groups. Although the 9th maṇḍala has different ṛṣis, all its mantras have one and the same deity, called Pavamāna Soma; that is, unlike the other maṇḍalas, the mantras were not arranged according to the ṛṣis, but all the Soma-deity mantras seen by all the ṛṣis were put together and made into one maṇḍala. Therefore all the mantras in that maṇḍala have the one deity Pavamānaḥ Somaḥ, only the ṛṣis being different [continues p. 375, second strip].

The first maṇḍala has put together the mantras of ṛṣis who saw a hundred, or a little more or less, Ṛks. Each ṛṣi's name has some 100 [as printed ೧೦೦] Ṛks; therefore the ṛṣis of this maṇḍala are called Śatarcinaḥ ("composers of a hundred Ṛks"), and this maṇḍala is called the Śatarcina-maṇḍala.

Following this same order, the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th and 8th maṇḍalas (numerals printed in Latin type) are said to have been "seen" respectively by the ṛṣis Gṛtsamada, Viśvāmitra, Vāmadeva, Atri, Bharadvāja, Vasiṣṭha and Kaṇva. The tenth maṇḍala includes many very long sūktas that cannot be divided in any way, and very small sūktas; they have been put together in this maṇḍala, which is called the maṇḍala of small sūktas and great sūktas (Kṣudrasūkta–Mahāsūkta). As in the first maṇḍala, in this tenth maṇḍala also there are in all 191 [as printed ೧೯೧] sūktas. The maṇḍala in hand, the second, being "seen" by the ṛṣi called Gṛtsamada, is customarily called the Gārtsamada-maṇḍala. In every maṇḍala, according to ṛṣi or subject-division, there are divisions called anuvākas, comprising several sūktas. In the first maṇḍala there are 24 [as printed ೨೪] such anuvākas and 191 sūktas. In this second maṇḍala there are 4 [as printed ೪] anuvākas and 43 [as printed ೪೩] sūktas. This maṇḍala is the smallest of all in size.

### Printed p. 376 (PDF 396)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 1" — the numeral file reads the header as "2.2 . 1 . Sū. 1"; the second item printed looks like the abbreviation for Anuvāka, taken as such; flag.)*

Let us examine closely the matter of the ṛṣi Gṛtsamada, who "saw" this maṇḍala. Explaining the word *gṛtsamada*, the great sage Yāska in his Nirukta says:

> गृत्समदो गृत्समदनः । गृत्स इति मेधाविनाम । गृणातेः स्तुतिकर्मणः ।

*(Nirukta 9-5, numeral as given in the numeral file and the printed page.)*

That is: Gṛtsamada means "Gṛtsamadana"; the word *gṛtsa* is derived from the root गृणाति (*gṛṇāti*), which gives the sense of praise. *Gṛtsa* is a name for the clever (intelligent) person. *Madana* means one who is joyful or has joy. The analysis is:

> गृत्सश्चासौ मदनश्च गृत्समदनः

> *gṛtsaścāsau madanaśca gṛtsamadanaḥ*

Therefore the word Gṛtsamada means a man who is both intelligent and cheerful (with smiling face).

This ṛṣi Gṛtsamada was at first the son of the ṛṣi Śunahotra, born in the Āṅgirasa-ṛṣi lineage. Once, while he was performing a sacrifice, asuras came and carried him off. At Gṛtsamada's prayer Indra freed him and brought him back. It was from Indra's command that the name Gṛtsamada became established for him. Afterwards he became known as the son of Śunaka, of the Bhṛgu family, or of a Śaunaka. Also in the Ṛgvedānukramaṇikā, composed by the great sage Kātyāyana, the pupil of the ṛṣi Śaunaka, in stating the names of the ṛṣis of the various sūktas it says:

> त्वमग्न इति गृत्समदः शौनको भृगुतां गतः ।
> शौनहोत्रः प्रकृत्या तु य आंगिरस उच्यते इति ॥

> *tvamagna iti gṛtsamadaḥ śaunako bhṛgutāṃ gataḥ |*
> *śaunahotraḥ prakṛtyā tu ya āṃgirasa ucyate iti ‖*

That is: the ṛṣi of the sūkta त्वमग्ने द्युभिः (*tvamagne dyubhiḥ*) (as printed; "tvamagne dyubhiḥ"), Gṛtsamada, though born the son of Śunahotra of the Āṅgirasa lineage, afterwards (for some other reason) became known as the son of Śunaka, born in the Bhṛgu-ṛṣi family.

In the Mahābhārata this ṛṣi has a different story. According to the story in the Anuśāsana-parva of the Mahābhārata, Vītahavya, king of the Haihaya country, had a son [this ṛṣi]. Because of harassment by his enemy, Pratardana, the king of Kāśī, Vītahavya abandoned his kingdom and wandered, exiled, and found shelter in the hermitage of the sage Bhṛgu. The angered Pratardana, king of Kāśī, then demanded forcibly that the kṣatriyas who were in Bhṛgu's hermitage be made subject to him. The sage Bhṛgu, unwilling to give up the king who had come for refuge, said that there was no kṣatriya at all in his hermitage. Because he said so, in order that the sage Bhṛgu's word not be untrue, Vītahavya became a brāhmaṇa. His son Gṛtsamada became the famous ṛṣi and the seer of the second maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda [continues p. 377].

### Printed p. 377 (PDF 397)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 1? [?]" [numeral not verified]; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; page number 377.)*

In another place in the Mahābhārata it is said that when the gods were being defeated in the war of the gods and asuras, Indra was hidden in a secret place; the asuras searched to kill him, and Gṛtsamada took Indra's form, deceived the asuras and thus helped Indra escape. Besides, in the sacrificial ground called Naimiśāraṇya, the ṛṣis were performing a twelve-year sacrificial session (*sattra*), passing the time in listening to the Purāṇas and other tales told by the Sūta, the Paurāṇika Lomaharṣaṇa; in that assembly of ṛṣis the name Gṛtsamada is also mentioned. But it is not clear whether this is the same Gṛtsamada who saw this maṇḍala or a different ṛṣi of that name. It is also known that Gṛtsamada was one of the Śākhākāras (founders of recensions) among the branches of the Atharvaveda; Sāyaṇa, the bhāṣyakāra, has indicated this matter there.

The first sūkta of this maṇḍala, seen by the ṛṣi Gṛtsamada, has 16 [as read; ೧೬] Ṛks. Leaving aside the last Ṛk, which is a conclusion praying for desired ends, the remaining 15 [as read; ೧೫] Ṛks all begin with words of the 2nd-person pronoun, त्वं (*tvaṃ*) त्वां (*tvāṃ*) etc. (words denoting "you"). Moreover, in many Ṛks the whole exposition begins with the word *yuṣmad* (you) [the printed sentence continues on the next strip]. Sūktas of this kind with such alliteration (*prāsa*) are many in the Ṛgveda. In the first maṇḍala's [number 9?] sūkta [as printed; numeral unclear [?]] also, as in the sūkta in hand, many Ṛks begin with the word त्वं (*tvaṃ*). In some sūktas all Ṛks begin with the word एतत् (*etat*): in the ninth maṇḍala's sūktas [numbers printed as ೩, ೧೫, ೨೨, ೨೭, ೨೮, … — read unverified [?]] and so on, every Ṛk begins with the word *etat*. In some sūktas — for instance the ninth maṇḍala's sūkta [number unclear [?]] — every Ṛk begins with the word तत् (*tat*), and in it with the word सः (*saḥ*). In this same maṇḍala, in sūkta 14 [as read; ೧೪ [?]] seen by Gṛtsamada, every Ṛk (except the last Ṛk) begins with the word अध्वर्यवः (*adhvaryavaḥ*). And in sūkta 25 [as read; numeral unclear [?]] of this same maṇḍala the last pāda of each Ṛk closes like a refrain: यंयं युजं कृणुते ब्रह्मणस्पतिः (*yaṃyaṃ yujaṃ kṛṇute brahmaṇaspatiḥ*). In this way, mantras and sūktas of various kinds of *prāsa* (alliteration) were composed with the aim of singing, and they show the ṛṣis' skill in composition and mastery of speech. In the maṇḍala in hand, the ṛṣi Gṛtsamada praises various deities by Ṛks and sūktas of many kinds, full of alliteration and rich in meaning. There is no need to say that all such mantras belong to the class of highly mature poetry.

*(Closing ornament "— : o : —"; end of the Pīṭhike. Printed p. 375 had its own half-title; the Pīṭhike here ends at p. 377.)*

### Printed p. 378 (PDF 398)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 2. A. 1. Sū. 1" as read; no numeral row for the header in the file.)*

**The first sūkta in the second maṇḍala** *(half-title printed in Kannada)*

*Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (Sanskrit, in Kannada script):*

> शतर्चिनां प्रथमं मंडलं व्याख्यातं । अथ गार्त्समदं द्वितीयं मंडलं व्याख्यायते । त्वमग्ने द्युभिरित्यादिकं द्वितीयं मंडलं । चत्वारोऽनुवाकाः । तेषु प्रथमोऽनुवाक एकादश सूक्तानि । तत्र त्वमग्ने द्युभिरिति षोडशर्चं प्रथमं सूक्तं । मंडलद्रष्टा गृत्समद ऋषिः । स च पूर्वमांगिरसकुले शुनहोत्रस्य पुत्रः सन् यज्ञकालेऽसुरैर्गृहीत इन्द्रेण मोचितः । पश्चात्तद्वचनेनैव भृगुकुले शुनकपुत्रो गृत्समदनामाभूत् । तथा चानुक्रमणिका । यः आंगिरसः शौनहोत्रो भूत्वा भार्गवः शौनकोऽभवत्स गृत्समदो द्वितीयं मंडलमपश्यदिति । तथा तस्यैव शौनकस्य वचनमृष्यनुक्रमणे । त्वमग्न इति गृत्समदः शौनको भृगुतां गतः । शौनहोत्रः प्रकृत्या तु य आंगिरस उच्यत इति । तस्मान्मंडलद्रष्टा शौनको गृत्समद ऋषिः । जगती छंदः । मंडलादिपरिभाषयाग्नेयं । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । त्वमग्ने जागतं त्विति ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोर्जागते छंदसीदमादिसूक्तद्वयस्य विनियोगः । त्वमग्ने द्युभिरिति सूक्ते । आ. ४-१३ । इति सूत्रितत्वात् ॥ उपाकरणोत्सर्जनयोरप्याद्या विनियुक्ता ॥

*Gist:* The second maṇḍala (four anuvākas; the first has eleven sūktas) is Gārtsamada; Sūkta 1 has sixteen ṛks, ṛṣi Gṛtsamada (born Āṅgirasa, son of Śunahotra, seized by asuras and freed by Indra, later a Bhārgava Śaunaka), deity Agni, metre jagatī; used in the Prātaranuvāka and Āśvinaśastra, and in upākaraṇa/utsarjana (Āśvalāyana 4-13 as printed).

**Anuvāda (Kannada).** The first maṇḍala, seen by the ṛṣis called Śatarcins, has been explained; now the second maṇḍala, seen by the ṛṣi Gṛtsamada, is explained. The second maṇḍala begins with the sūkta त्वमग्ने द्युभिः (*tvamagne dyubhiḥ*). In this maṇḍala there are four anuvākas. Of them, in the first anuvāka there are eleven sūktas; of these त्वमग्ने द्युभिः is the first sūkta, with sixteen ṛks. Gṛtsamada, the seer of the maṇḍala, is the ṛṣi of this sūkta; this ṛṣi Gṛtsamada was at first the son of one called Śunahotra in the Āṅgirasa family; once, while performing a sacrifice, he was carried off by asuras and afterwards freed by Indra. Then, as Indra said, he became the son of the ṛṣi Śunaka in the Bhṛgu family and famous under the name Gṛtsamada. In the Anukramaṇikā:

> यः आंगिरसः शौनहोत्रो भूत्वा भार्गवः शौनकोऽभवत्स गृत्समदो द्वितीयं मंडलमपश्यदिति ।

> *yaḥ āṃgirasaḥ śaunahotro bhūtvā bhārgavaḥ śaunako 'bhavatsa gṛtsamado dvitīyaṃ maṃḍalamapaśyaditi |*

That is: the son of Śunahotra of the Āṅgirasa gotra became the son of the ṛṣi Śunaka, born in the Bhṛgu line, with the name Gṛtsamada. It is said that this Gṛtsamada is the seer of the second maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda. And in the Anukramaṇikā too, the words of its author Śaunaka are as follows —

> त्वमग्न इति गृत्समदः शौनको भृगुतां गतः ।
> शौनहोत्रः प्रकृत्या तु य आंगीरस उच्यत इति ॥

> *tvamagna iti gṛtsamadaḥ śaunako bhṛgutāṃ gataḥ |*
> *śaunahotraḥ prakṛtyā tu ya āṃgīrasa ucyata iti ‖*

### Printed p. 379 (PDF 399)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 17 [?]" as read, no numeral row in the file; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

**Anuvāda (Kannada), continued.** The ṛṣi called Gṛtsamada, who was first the son of one called Śunahotra of the Āṅgirasa gotra and afterwards the son of Śunaka of the Bhṛgu family, is the seer of this second maṇḍala that begins with त्वमग्ने (*tvamagne*). Therefore the ṛṣi called Gṛtsamada, the son of Śunaka, is the seer of this maṇḍala. The deity of the sūkta beginning त्वमग्ने is Agni alone; the metre is jagatī. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: त्वमग्ने जागतं तु (*tvamagne jāgataṃ tu*). The application of this sūkta and the next, for the jagatī ṛks at the time of the recitation of the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra mantras, is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra aphorism त्वमग्ने द्युभिरिति सूक्ते (*tvamagne dyubhiriti sūkte*) (Āśv. 4-13, numeral agrees with the file). And that the first ṛk of this sūkta is applied in the upākaraṇa and utsarjana rites was told in the Anuvāda of the previous sūkta.

### Printed p. 380 (PDF 400)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 1", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā".)*

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥** *(Accents not reproduced.)*

> त्वम॑ग्ने॒ द्युभि॒स्त्वमा॑शुशु॒क्षणि॒स्त्वम॒द्भ्यस्त्वमश्म॑न॒स्परि॑ ।
> त्वं वने॑भ्य॒स्त्वमोष॑धीभ्य॒स्त्वं नृ॒णां नृ॑पते जायसे॒ शुचिः॑ ॥ १ ॥

> *tvamagne dyubhistvamāśuśukṣaṇistvamadbhyastvamaśmanaspari |*
> *tvaṃ vanebhyastvamoṣadhībhyastvaṃ nṛṇāṃ nṛpate jāyase śuciḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वं । अग्ने । द्युऽभिः । त्वं । आऽशुशुक्षणिः । त्वं । अत्ऽभ्यः । त्वं । अश्मनः । परि ।
> त्वं । वनेभ्यः । त्वं । ओषधीभ्यः । त्वं । नृणां । नृऽपते । जायसे । शुचिः ॥ १ ॥

> *tvaṃ | agne | dyu 'bhiḥ | tvaṃ | ā 'śuśukṣaṇiḥ | tvaṃ | at 'bhyaḥ | tvaṃ | aśmanaḥ | pari |*
> *tvaṃ | vanebhyaḥ | tvaṃ | oṣadhībhyaḥ | tvaṃ | nṛṇāṃ | nṛ 'pate | jāyase | śuciḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

*(The small mark after the first letter of आऽशुशुक्षणिः is read as the compound mark, as it looks.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यं ॥**

> हे अग्ने अग्रणीत्यादिगुणविशिष्ट हे नृणां नृपते । नृणां मनुष्याणां मध्ये ये नरा यष्टारः संति तेषां विशेषेण पालयितः । यद्वोभाभ्यां पदाभ्यां बहुत्वं नित्यस्वानित्वं [?] च प्रतिपाद्यते । सर्वेषामपि नराणां नित्यपालकेत्यर्थः ॥ नृणामित्यस्य निघाताभावश्छांदसः ॥ तादृश हे देव त्वं द्युभिर्यागदिवसैर्निमित्तभूतैर्जायसे । यागार्थं मथनेनोत्पद्यस इत्यर्थः । यद्वा तादृशैर्दिवसैः सहितो जायसे । तत्तद्यागदिवसेषु प्रसिद्धो भवसीत्यर्थः । तथा त्वमाशुशुक्षणिर्जायसे । आ सर्वतो दीप्यमानो भवसि ॥ आज्युपपदे [?] शुच दीप्ताविन्त्येतस्य सनंतसु [?] छांदसमिदं रूपं । यद्वा आशु शीघ्रं शुच् दीप्तः सन् यतः स सेव्यते इति । आश्य शुचं शोकं सनोति ददाति शत्रुभ्यो दाहादिनेत्याशुशुक्षणिः ॥ तादृशो भवसि । एवं सर्वत्र प्रतिविशेषणं जायस इति योज्यं । हे अग्ने त्वमद्भ्यो वृष्ट्युदकेभ्यो जायसे वैद्युतरूपेण वा वाडवरूपेण वा समुद्रोदकेभ्यः । अश्मनो मेघात्पाषाणाद्वा परि जायसे । यो अश्मनोरंतरग्निं जजान । २-१२-३ । इति हि मंत्रांतरं । त्वं वनेभ्यो वृक्षादिसमूहेभ्यो दावरूपेण । त्वमोषधीभ्यो वैश्वानररूपेण । एवं महानुभावस्त्वं मथनेनोत्पन्नः सन् सर्वात्मको भवसीत्यर्थः । शुचिरेव जायसे । यद्वा शुचिरादित्यरूपो जायस इत्यर्थः । अत्र त्वमग्ने द्युभिरहोभिरित्यादि निरुक्तमनुसंधेयं । नि. ६-१ ॥

*Gist:* Agni, lord of men, you are born (by friction) on sacrificial days, shining and burning enemies; you arise from waters, stone/cloud, forests and plants (as forest-fire, Vaiśvānara) and are pure, of the form of the Sun. (Mantrāntara 2-12-3 and Nirukta 6-1 as printed; the grammar of āśuśukṣaṇi is only touched on.)

**॥ प्रतिपदार्थः ॥**

Nṛṇāṃ nṛpate — lord and protector of men; Agne — O Agni; tvam — you; dyubhiḥ — on the sacrificial days, for the sake of the sacrifice; jāyase — you are born; tvam — you; āśuśukṣaṇiḥ — shining on all sides and burning enemies, you are; tvam — you; adbhyaḥ — from waters; aśmanaḥ pari — from stones too you are born; tvam — you; vanebhyaḥ — from trees and the like, in the form of forest-fire; tvam — you; oṣadhībhyaḥ — from plants, in the form of Vaiśvānara you are born; tvam — you; śuciḥ — pure and luminous, of the form of the Sun you are.

**॥ भावार्थः ॥**

O Agni, lord and protector of men, you are born on the sacrificial days for the sake of the sacrifice. You are shining everywhere and burn enemies. You are born from waters and from stones. You are born from trees and the like in the form of forest-fire, and from plants in the form of Vaiśvānara. You are pure and luminous, of the form of the Sun.

### Printed p. 381 (PDF 401)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 17 [?]" as read from the strip, no numeral row in the file; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

**Printed English of Ṛk 1 (Latin type):**

"Sovereign of men, Agni, you are born for the days (of sacrifice), pure and all-irradiating, from the waters, from the stones, from trees, and from plants."

**॥ विशेषविषयाः ॥ (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Special Topics)**

In the first Ṛk of this first sūkta, seen by the ṛṣi Gṛtsamada, the various orders of Agni's origin are described; the commentary says it will explain these origins briefly.

त्वं अग्ने नृणां नृपते (*tvaṃ agne nṛṇāṃ nṛpate*) — the ṛṣi addresses Agni with these words. The derivation and various meanings of the word Agni were explained at length in Ṛk. Saṃ. Part 1, pp. 612-614 (printed as "612-614"); here only the bhāṣyakāra's phrase अग्रणीत्यादिगुणविशिष्ट (*agraṇītyādiguṇaviśiṣṭa*) is explained. Yāska says in his Nirukta —

> अग्निः कस्मादग्रणीर्भवत्यग्रं यज्ञेषु प्रणीयतेऽज्ञं नयतीति ।

> *agniḥ kasmādagraṇīrbhavatyagraṃ yajñeṣu praṇīyate 'jñaṃ nayatīti |*

*(Nirukta 7-14, numeral from the file; the word before नयति is printed with the ज्ञ conjunct, as read.)*

That is: Agni has the first place in sacrifices and the like; the word *agra* means chief, hence Agni has the chief place among the deities. When fire is produced in the sacrifice from the two kindling sticks (araṇi) it is at once placed in the Āhavanīya fire-pit, and from there is carried to the Gārhapatya fire-pit; therefore Agni is called अग्रणीः (*agraṇīḥ*). Or अग्रणीः (*agraṇīḥ*) means one who himself (*tāne*) leads the army of the gods, or one who is in front of it as its leader (*nāyaka*, printed also "or Leader"). This is the first reason for the name. Besides, in another Brāhmaṇa it is said:

> अग्निर्देवानां सेनानीः

> *agnirdevānāṃ senānīḥ*

and following this the Ṛgvedic students read in their Mantra-brāhmaṇa:

> अग्निर्मुखं प्रथमो देवतानां

*(Ai. Brā. 1-4, numeral as in the file.)* In another part of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa:

> अग्निर्वै देवानामवमः [?]

*(Ai. Brā. 1-1-1; the word before the visarga is not certain between ava- and upa- shapes, left as read with [?].)* And in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa also:

> अग्निरग्रे प्रथमो देवतानां

*(Tai. Brā. 2-4-3-3)* and also

> अग्निरवमो देवतानां

> *agniravamo devatānāṃ*

From these examples Agni is the first among the deities, one in the foremost place, the leader. In the Śukla Yajurveda (Vā. Saṃ., no reference printed):

> स वा विषोऽग्रे देवतानामजायत तस्मादग्निर्नामेति

> *sa vā viṣo 'gre devatānāmajāyata tasmādagnirnāmeti*

meaning: this Agni was born first among the deities, therefore he is called Agni.

नृणां नृपते (*nṛṇāṃ nṛpate*) — the bhāṣya passage (already given above under Ṛk 1: मनुष्याणां मध्ये ये नराः यष्टारः सन्ति तेषां विशेषेण पालयितः । यद्वोभाभ्यां पदाभ्यां बहुत्वं नित्यस्वामित्वं च प्रतिपाद्यते । सर्वेषामपि नराणां नित्यपालकेत्यर्थः ॥ (*manuṣyāṇāṃ madhye ye narāḥ yaṣṭāraḥ santi teṣāṃ viśeṣeṇa pālayitaḥ | yadvobhābhyāṃ padābhyāṃ bahutvaṃ nityasvāmitvaṃ ca pratipādyate | sarveṣāmapi narāṇāṃ nityapālaketyarthaḥ ‖*)) is explained: among men, those men who perform sacrifices, the yajamānas — Agni is the protector of those; (continued on p. 382).

### Printed p. 382 (PDF 402)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. [1]" — the sūkta numeral is the ∩-shaped numeral for 1.)*

**Special Topics, continued.** ...that is, Agni protects all who sacrifice; or, since the two words नृणां नृपते (*nṛṇāṃ nṛpate*) indicate lordship over many people, the main sense is that this Agni is the protector of all people at all times.

त्वमग्ने द्युभिः (*tvamagne dyubhiḥ*) — the bhāṣya reads:

> त्वमग्ने द्युभिः — यागदिवसैर्निमित्तभूतैर्जायसे । यागार्थं मथनेनोत्पद्यस इत्यर्थः । यद्वा तादृशैर्दिवसैः सहितो जायसे । तत्तद्यागदिवसेषु प्रसिद्धो भवसीत्यर्थः ।

> *tvamagne dyubhiḥ — yāgadivasairnimittabhūtairjāyase | yāgārthaṃ mathanenotpadyasa ityarthaḥ | yadvā tādṛśairdivasaiḥ sahito jāyase | tattadyāgadivaseṣu prasiddho bhavasītyarthaḥ |*

(Printed in the source with the ending …भवसीत्यर्थः (*…bhavasītyarthaḥ*); the same text as in the bhāṣya above.) Kannada explanation: O Agni, you are born on the sacrificial days; that is, for the sake of the sacrifice (sacrifice is by Agni itself) you are produced by churning the araṇis; or, on those sacrificial days, that is on the days of sacrifice performed by the yajamānas, you are born accompanied by those days, that is, as famous; so also the meaning.

त्वमाशुशुक्षणिः (*tvamāśuśukṣaṇiḥ*) — explaining this word the bhāṣyakāra says:

> त्वमाशुशुक्षणिर्जायसे । आ सर्वतो दीप्यमानो भवसि । आज्युपपदे शुच दीप्ताविन्त्येतस्य छांदसमिदं रूपं । यद्वा आशु शीघ्रं शुच् दीप्तः सन् यतः स सेव्यते इति । आशु शुचं शोकं सनोति ददाति शत्रुभ्यो दाहादिनेत्याशुशुक्षणिः । तादृशो भवति ॥

> *tvamāśuśukṣaṇirjāyase | ā sarvato dīpyamāno bhavasi | ājyupapade śuca dīptāvintyetasya chāṃdasamidaṃ rūpaṃ | yadvā āśu śīghraṃ śuc dīptaḥ san yataḥ sa sevyate iti | āśu śucaṃ śokaṃ sanoti dadāti śatrubhyo dāhādinetyāśuśukṣaṇiḥ | tādṛśo bhavati ‖*

*(This is the version printed here; it differs a little from the bhāṣya as I read it earlier in Ṛk 1, where [?] stand: here the text reads आज्युपपदे and has no सनंतसु; the earlier [?] places are better resolved by this clearer printing — see flags.)* Kannada: O Agni, you shine all around; from the root शुच् (*śuc*) giving the sense "to shine", with the prefix ā, this is the Vedic form आशुशुक्षणिः (*āśuśukṣaṇiḥ*); or आशु (*āśu*) (alertly) शुच् (*śuc*) (shining), and क्षणिः (*kṣaṇiḥ*) — because he is served; or by his power of burning he confers शुचं (*śucaṃ*) (sorrow) quickly (सनोति (*sanoti*)) on enemies; hence आशुशुक्षणिः (*āśuśukṣaṇiḥ*). To explain this word Yāska, taking this very Ṛk as example, gives its derivation in his Nirukta —

> त्वमग्ने द्युभिरहोभिस्त्वमाशुशुक्षणिः । आशु इति च शु इति च क्षिप्रनामनी भवतः । क्षणिरुत्तरः क्षणोतेः आशु शुचा क्षणोतीति वा सनोतीति वा ॥ शुक् शोचतेः । पंचम्यर्थे वा प्रथमा । तथा हि वाक्संयोग आ इत्याकार उपसर्गः पुरस्ताच्चिकीर्षितज [?] उत्तर आशु शोचयिषुरिति । शुचिः शोचतेर्ज्वलतिकर्मणः । आयुमुपीतरः [?] शुचिरेतस्मादेव । निष्षिक्तमस्मात् पापकमिति नैरुक्ताः ॥

*(Nirukta 6-1, numerals "೬-೧" as in the file, 6.1.)*

That is: आशु (*āśu*) and शु (*śu*) are both names meaning *kṣipra* (swift). The word क्षणिः (*kṣaṇiḥ*) is formed from the root क्षणोति (*kṣaṇoti*) giving the sense of injuring; or it may be formed from the root सनोति (*sanoti*) meaning "to obtain"/"to give". The syllable शु (*śu*) in the middle is a synonym of शुचि (*śuci*) giving the sense "to shine". Hence आशुशुक्षणिः (*āśuśukṣaṇiḥ*) means that Agni, by his own radiance, is alert and injures (burns) (enemies), or quickly provides what the sacrificer needs. *(continued on p. 383)*

### Printed p. 383 (PDF 403)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 17 [?]" as read, no numeral row in the file; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

**Special Topics, continued.** (...that is, one who, with his radiance, is alert and burns the enemies, or provides quickly what the yajamāna needs.)

Or the word शुक् (*śuk*) is formed from the root शुच् (*śuc*) "to shine"; the first case is used here in the sense of the fifth case. आ (*ā*) is the prefix. So if in आ + शुशुक्षणिः (*ā + śuśukṣaṇiḥ*) the word शुशुक्षणि (*śuśukṣaṇi*) is taken to express a desiderative sense (*cikīrṣita*), then आशुशुक्षणिः (*āśuśukṣaṇiḥ*) means "one who wishes to shine all around" (Agni).

Or the word शुचिः (*śuciḥ*) may be formed from the root शोचति (*śocati*) meaning "to shine"; the above meanings fit in this context. There is also another meaning of शुचिः (*śuciḥ*): pure, clean, sinless. In this view अ + आशुशुक्षणिः (*a + āśuśukṣaṇiḥ*) = आशुशुक्षणिः (*āśuśukṣaṇiḥ*) means "one who is sinless" (Agni). *(Printed in English inside the Kannada: "(अ denotes negative. As there are two अ s, two negetives [sic] make an offirmative [sic]; Sinless)" — the source's words as read: "negetives", "offirmative" are my reading of the print, "negatives"/"affirmative" may be the true spelling; left as read.)* The Nairuktas accept such an explanation.

द्युभिः अहोभिः (*dyubhiḥ ahobhiḥ*) — on the days fit for sacrifice, Pūrṇimā, Amāvāsyā and the like, you are produced by churning Agni for the sacrifice; on such days you are born — so he addressed Agni and said.

त्वमद्भ्यः (*tvamadbhyaḥ*) — the bhāṣya:

> त्वमद्भ्यः — त्वमद्भ्यो वृष्ट्युदकेभ्यो जायसे वैद्युतरूपेण वाडवरूपेण वा समुद्रोदकेभ्यः ।

> *tvamadbhyaḥ — tvamadbhyo vṛṣṭyudakebhyo jāyase vaidyutarūpeṇa vāḍavarūpeṇa vā samudrodakebhyaḥ |*

Kannada: you are born from water; that is, when rain is falling, in the form of lightning born in the clouds, or in the form of the Vāḍava (submarine) fire seen in the sea-water, you are born, so he praised.

त्वमश्मनस्परि (*tvamaśmanaspari*) — the bhāṣya:

> त्वमश्मनस्परि — अश्मनो मेघात्पाषाणाद्वा ।

> *tvamaśmanaspari — aśmano meghātpāṣāṇādvā |*

The word अश्मा (*aśmā*) is read among the cloud-names (Nirukta 2-21, numerals as in the file); so you are born from the clouds in the form of lightning. Or since अश्मन् (*aśman*) also means stone, rock, you are born from the friction of two stones. (In earlier times, when matchsticks were not in use, fire used to be made from flint stones.) On the point that Agni is born from the clouds in the form of lightning the bhāṣyakāra has given as example the Ṛk —

> यो हत्वाहिमरिणात्सप्त सिन्धून्यो गा उदाजदपधा वलस्य । यो अश्मनोरंतरग्निं जजान संवृक्समत्सु स जनास इंद्रः ॥

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-12-3 — numerals as in the file.)* In explaining the sense of this Ṛk Sāyaṇa says —

> यश्चाश्मनोः अश्नुते व्याप्नोत्यंतरिक्षमिति अश्मा मेघः । अत्यंतमृदुरूपयोः … *(the line runs on to p. 384)*

> *yaścāśmanoḥ aśnute vyāpnotyaṃtarikṣamiti aśmā meghaḥ | atyaṃtamṛdurūpayoḥ … *(the line runs on to p. 384)**

### Printed p. 384 (PDF 404)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 1"; "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā".)*

**Special Topics, continued.** The Sāyaṇa quote on Ṛg 2-12-3 runs on from p. 383:

> [?]योरंतर्मध्ये वैद्युतमग्निं जजान उत्पादयामास ।

> *[?]yoraṃtarmadhye vaidyutamagniṃ jajāna utpādayāmāsa |*

That is: the word अश्मा (*aśmā*) is formed from the root अश् (*aś*) meaning "to pervade"; because it pervades the sky (*antarikṣa*), the cloud is called *aśmā*. In the midst of such soft clouds Indra produced the lightning-fire — so the meaning is explained. *(The first letter of the quoted line is not decidable; left as [?].)*

त्वं वनेभ्यः (*tvaṃ vanebhyaḥ*) — the bhāṣya:

> त्वं वनेभ्यः — वृक्षादिसमूहेभ्यो दावरूपेण ।

> *tvaṃ vanebhyaḥ — vṛkṣādisamūhebhyo dāvarūpeṇa |*

Kannada: in the forests you are born in the form of forest-fire. In the forest the bamboos rub one against another, a blaze arises from it and burns the whole forest; this is well known.

त्वमोषधीभ्यः (*tvamoṣadhībhyaḥ*) — the bhāṣya:

> त्वमोषधीभ्यः — वैश्वानररूपेण । मथनेनोत्पन्नः सन् सर्वात्मको भवसीत्यर्थः ।

> *tvamoṣadhībhyaḥ — vaiśvānararūpeṇa | mathanenotpannaḥ san sarvātmako bhavasītyarthaḥ |*

Kannada: Agni is present in all living beings (as the digestive fire, *jāṭharāgni*) and also in herbs and trees as Vaiśvānara. When Agni is produced in the sacrifice, they take two pieces of the aśvattha tree or of the śamī tree, put one upon the other and churn strongly; thereby Agni is produced. On this point —

> शमीगर्भादग्निं मंथति । एषा वा अग्नेर्यज्ञिया तनूः । तामेवास्मै जनयति ॥

*(Tai. Brā. 1-1-9-1, as in the file.)*

Thus there is the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa passage. The method of producing Agni by churning with mantra and with rites in sacrifices is told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (Ai. Brā. 3-5, as in the file) in this way: since churning of Agni is mentioned in this Ṛk, it is proper to describe that procedure here. In the sacrifice, after the *somavikraya* (the purchase of the soma-creeper from those who brought it from mountains and forests) is completed, the work of churning Agni begins. Then the priest called Adhvaryu says to the priest called Hotṛ —

> अग्नये मथ्यमानायानुब्रूहीत्याहाध्वर्युरभि त्वा देव सवितरिति सावित्रीमन्वाह तदाहुर्यदग्नये मथ्यमानायानुवाचाहाथ कस्मात्सावित्रीमन्वाहेति । सविता वै प्रसवानामीशे सवितृप्रसूत एवैनं तन्मथति तस्मात्सावित्रीमन्वाह ।

> *agnaye mathyamānāyānubrūhītyāhādhvaryurabhi tvā deva savitariti sāvitrīmanvāha tadāhuryadagnaye mathyamānāyānuvācāhātha kasmātsāvitrīmanvāheti | savitā vai prasavānāmīśe savitṛprasūta evainaṃ tanmathati tasmātsāvitrīmanvāha |*

The Adhvaryu says to the Hotṛ the *praiṣa* mantra "agnaye mathyamānāyānubrūhi" (a *praiṣa* mantra is the mantra by which, when various rites are done in the sacrifice, the Adhvaryu and others command persons concerned to do such and such a rite or oblation); hearing it, the Hotṛ —

---

### Printed p. 385 (PDF 405)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 17" as read, i.e. Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 17; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

> अभि त्वा देव सवितरीशानं वार्याणाम् । सदावन् भागमीमहे ॥

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-3, as in the file.)*

— recites this mantra addressed to Savitṛ (the Sāvitrī ṛk). A doubt arises here: though the Adhvaryu directed the Hotṛ to say the mantra needed for churning Agni, why does the Hotṛ, without doing so, recite a ṛk addressed to Savitṛ? Is this not wrong? No: according to the sentence "*savitā vai prasavānāmīśe*" Savitṛ is the lord of whatever is to be produced in all sacrifices and rites; therefore here, for beginning the work of producing Agni by churning, it is natural to ask the permission of the deity Savitṛ. For that reason the Hotṛ first recites the ṛk addressed to Savitṛ.

> मही द्यौः पृथिवी च न इति द्यावापृथिवीयामन्वाह । तदाहुर्यदग्नये मथ्यमानायानुवाचाहाथ कस्माद्द्यावापृथिवीयामन्वाहेति द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां वा एतं जातं देवाः पर्यगृह्णंस्ताभ्यामेवाद्यापि परिगृहीतस्तस्माद्द्यावापृथिवीयामन्वाह ॥

> *mahī dyauḥ pṛthivī ca na iti dyāvāpṛthivīyāmanvāha | tadāhuryadagnaye mathyamānāyānuvācāhātha kasmāddyāvāpṛthivīyāmanvāheti dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ vā etaṃ jātaṃ devāḥ paryagṛhṇaṃstābhyāmevādyāpi parigṛhītastasmāddyāvāpṛthivīyāmanvāha ‖*

Next the Hotṛ proceeds —

> मही द्यौः पृथिवी च न इमं यज्ञं मिमिक्षताम् । पिपृतां नो भरीमभिः ॥

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-22-13, as in the file.)*

— and recites this ṛk addressed to Heaven and Earth. Some raise an objection to this: for the work of churning Agni one was to say a ṛk addressed to Agni; why does this Hotṛ recite a ṛk addressed to Heaven and Earth? The answer: formerly, when Agni was born, the gods held him between Heaven and Earth (earth and the heavens); therefore even now it must be so. Since the fire named Pāvaka is held by the earth and the fire in the form of the sun is held by heaven, it is right that for the holding of Agni a ṛk addressed to Heaven and Earth be recited.

> त्वामग्ने पुष्करादधीति तृचमाग्नेयं गायत्रमन्वाहाग्नौ मथ्यमाने स्वयैवैनं तद्देवतया स्वेन छंदसा समर्थयति । अथर्वा निरमंथतेति रूपसमृद्धमेतद्वै यज्ञस्य समृद्धं यद्रूपसमृद्धं यत्कर्म क्रियमाणमृगभिवदति ॥

> *tvāmagne puṣkarādadhīti tṛcamāgneyaṃ gāyatramanvāhāgnau mathyamāne svayaivainaṃ taddevatayā svena chaṃdasā samarthayati | atharvā niramaṃthateti rūpasamṛddhametadvai yajñasya samṛddhaṃ yadrūpasamṛddhaṃ yatkarma kriyamāṇamṛgabhivadati ‖*

Then the Hotṛ, for the churning of Agni, recites the following ṛks addressed to Agni —

---

### Printed p. 386 (PDF 406)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 1"; "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā".)*

> त्वामग्ने पुष्करादध्यथर्वा निरमंथत । मूर्ध्नो विश्वस्य वाघतः ॥
> तमु त्वा दध्यङ्ङृषिः पुत्र ईधे अथर्वणः । वृत्रहणं पुरंदरं ॥
> तमु त्वा पाथ्यो वृषा समीधे दस्युहंतमम् । धनंजयं रणेरणे ॥

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-16-13, 14, 15, as I read it on a zoom (a faint ∩ before the second 6); the file said 6-6-13: see flags.)*

— recites these three ṛks. These three ṛks praise the deity Agni, and are ṛks in the *gāyatrī* metre, dear to Agni; for Agni and the gāyatrī metre are both produced by Prajāpati, therefore the gāyatrī metre is called Agni's "own metre". Now, the words *atharvā niramanthata* said in the second pāda of the first ṛk only say that the ṛṣi Atharvā produced Agni by churning. This ṛṣi Atharvā was the first to churn Agni and produce him in the *araṇis*; therefore there is the prayer that Agni, born as son to the ṛṣi Atharvaṇa, may grow and prosper in the sacrifice. For this reason it is natural to recite these ṛks, which give the sense: "may Agni, taking form from the araṇis and born (that is, in complete fire-form), grow in the sacrificial rite (blazing up greatly) and shine."

> स यदि न जायेत यदि चिरं जायेत रक्षोघ्न्यो गायत्र्योऽनूच्याः । अग्ने हंसि न्यत्रिणमित्येताः रक्षसामुपहत्यै रक्षांसि वा एनं तर्ह्यालभंते यर्हि न जायते यर्हि चिरं जायते ॥

> *sa yadi na jāyeta yadi ciraṃ jāyeta rakṣoghnyo gāyatryo 'nūcyāḥ | agne haṃsi nyatriṇamityetāḥ rakṣasāmupahatyai rakṣāṃsi vā enaṃ tarhyālabhaṃte yarhi na jāyate yarhi ciraṃ jāyate ‖*

Reciting the five ṛks mentioned before, one must churn Agni in the araṇis. If, even so, Agni is not produced, or until after a long time, and is produced only with smoke and the like, then the following sūkta of the *gāyatrī* metre, called *rākṣoghna* (destroyer of demons), must be recited —

> अग्ने हंसि न्यत्रिणं दीद्यन्मर्तेष्वा । स्वे क्षयो शुचिव्रत ॥
> उत्तिष्ठसि स्वाहुतो घृतानि प्रतिमोदसे । यत्त्वा स्रुचः समस्थिरन् ॥
> स आहुतो वि रोचतेऽग्निरीळेन्यो गिरा । स्रुचा प्रतीकमज्यते ॥
> घृतेनाग्निः समज्यते मधुप्रतीक आहुतः । रोचमानो विभावसुः ॥
> जरमाणः समिध्यसे देवेभ्यो हव्यवाहन । तं त्वा हवंत मर्त्याः ॥
> तं मर्ता अमर्त्यं घृतेनाग्निं सपर्यत । अदाभ्यं गृहपतिं ॥
> अदाभ्येन शोचिषाग्ने रक्षस्त्वं दह । गोपा ऋतस्य दीदिहि ॥
> स त्वमग्ने प्रतीकेन प्रत्योष यातुधान्यः । उरुक्षयेषु दीद्यत् ॥
> तं त्वा गीर्भिरुरुक्षया हव्यवाहं समीधिरे । यजिष्ठं मानुषे जने ॥

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-118-1 to 9, as in the file.)*

### Printed p. 387 (PDF 407)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 17" (Varga numeral as read; header not in the numeral file), "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Ṛk 1 Special Topics continuing.)*

In this sūkta there are nine ṛks. These drive away the rākṣasas and kill them. Therefore, by reciting these ṛks the rākṣasas are destroyed. At the time of churning Agni, Agni may fail to be produced, or may be produced only after delay; the reason is that these rākṣasas bind Agni and, without releasing him, keep him under their own control. Therefore, in order to set Agni free, the killing of the rākṣasas is necessary. For that reason it is said that the *rakṣohanana-sūkta* of these nine ṛks must be recited.

> स यद्येकस्यामेवानूक्तायां जायेत यदि द्वयोरथोत ब्रुवन्तु जन्तव इति जाताय जातवतीमभिरूपामनुब्रूयात् ॥

> *sa yadyekasyāmevānūktāyāṃ jāyeta yadi dvayorathota bruvantu jantava iti jātāya jātavatīmabhirūpāmanubrūyāt ‖*

While reciting the rākṣoghna sūkta, if Agni is produced after one ṛk has been recited in the middle; or, if after two, three and so on, he is produced after the recitation of those ṛks, then at that very moment —

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-3, as printed.)*

> उत ब्रुवन्तु जन्तव उदग्निर्वृत्रहाजनि । धनंजयो रणेरणे ॥

> *uta bruvantu jantava udagnirvṛtrahājani | dhanaṃjayo raṇeraṇe ‖*

— this ṛk must be recited at once. For the matter set forth in this ṛk is favourable to the production of Agni. It is to state this favourableness that the word जातवतीं (*jātavatīṃ*) is used. Then in the second pāda, उदग्निर्वृत्रहाजनि (*udagnirvṛtrahājani*), the word अजनि (*ajani*) ("was born"), which denotes birth, is read. Therefore this ṛk, which is fitting at the moment of Agni's production, is directed to be recited at that very moment.

> यद्यज्ञोऽभिरूपं तत्समृद्धं । आ यं हस्तेन खादिनमिति हस्ताभ्यां ह्येनं मंथंति । शिशुं जातमिति शिशुरिव वा एष प्रथमजातो यदग्निः । न बिभ्रति विशामग्निं स्वध्वरमिति यद्वै देवानां नेति तदेषामो३मिति । प्र देवं देववीतये भरता वसुवित्तममिति प्रह्रियमाणायाभिरूपा । यद्यज्ञोऽभिरूपं तत्समृद्धं । आ स्वे योनौ निषीदत्विति एष ह वा अस्य स्वो योनिर्यदग्निरग्नेः ॥

> *yadyajño 'bhirūpaṃ tatsamṛddhaṃ | ā yaṃ hastena khādinamiti hastābhyāṃ hyenaṃ maṃthaṃti | śiśuṃ jātamiti śiśuriva vā eṣa prathamajāto yadagniḥ | na bibhrati viśāmagniṃ svadhvaramiti yadvai devānāṃ neti tadeṣāmo3miti | pra devaṃ devavītaye bharatā vasuvittamamiti prahriyamāṇāyābhirūpā | yadyajño 'bhirūpaṃ tatsamṛddhaṃ | ā sve yonau niṣīdatviti eṣa ha vā asya svo yoniryadagniragneḥ ‖*

Up to this point the six ṛks used for the churning of Agni have been recited (the text names *abhi tvā*, *mahī dyauḥ*, *tvām agne*, *tam u tvā*, *uta bruvantu*; five openings are named, as printed, though it says "six"); and now —

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-16-40, as in the file.)*

> आ यं हस्ते न खादिनं शिशुं जातं न बिभ्रति । विशामग्निं स्वध्वरम् ॥

> *ā yaṃ haste na khādinaṃ śiśuṃ jātaṃ na bibhrati | viśāmagniṃ svadhvaram ‖*

— the Hotṛ recites this seventh ṛk. The meaning of this ṛk is as follows. Newly

### Printed p. 388 (PDF 408)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 1".)*

— born, just as one lifts a newborn child in the hands, so the ṛtvijs lift in their hands the Agni born in the araṇi. The chief purport of this is that this Agni in child-form bears the principal part in the sacrifice performed by the people, and is the eater of the oblations and the like. The use of the word हस्त (*hasta*) in the first pāda: the ṛtvijs churn this Agni with their own hands; therefore it is said that they lift him in their hands. In the second pāda, for the Agni just born, the simile of the newborn child is given. The word न (*na*) used here denotes the sense of assent (*aṅgīkāra*, "Om"). In everyday language the word न (*na*) denotes only the sense of negation; but in the Vedas this word denotes negation, comparison and assent; here assent is the intended sense. Further, for the word देवानां (*devānāṃ*) the meaning may be either "by the mantras that set forth the deities", or, by a change of letters, वेदानां (*vedānāṃ*), "of the Vedas" (connected with the Vedas). Now the eighth ṛk of the churning of Agni, namely —

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-16-41, as in the file.)*

> प्र देवं देववीतये भरता वसुवित्तमं । आ स्वे योनौ नि षीदतु ॥

> *pra devaṃ devavītaye bharatā vasuvittamaṃ | ā sve yonau ni ṣīdatu ‖*

— this ṛk the Hotṛ recites. "O ṛtvijs, place the Agni now produced in his own place, the *āhavanīya* pit. May Agni, there in his own place, sit." This ṛk, bearing such a sense, is fitting for the act of placing Agni in the *āhavanīya* pit. Here, in accordance with the *praiṣa* mantra that is recited in every act, the Hotṛ recites the mantra that is fitting for that act and has the proper meaning. Thus: as soon as Agni is produced, the Adhvaryu, addressing the Hotṛ, says the praiṣa mantra जाताया नुब्रू३हि (*jātāyā nubrū3hi*); in reply the Hotṛ recites the fitting ṛk उत ब्रुवन्तु जन्तवः (*uta bruvantu jantavaḥ*). In the same way, when the Agni produced is placed in the pit called *āhavanīya*, as soon as the Adhvaryu has said the praiṣa mantra प्रह्रियमाणायानुब्रू३हि (*prahriyamāṇāyānubrū3hi*), the Hotṛ recites the ṛk प्र देवं देववीतये (*pra devaṃ devavītaye*) that suits that occasion. It is to be understood that it goes thus in every act. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda, on this matter —

*(Tai. Saṃ. 6-3-5-2, 3.)*

> अग्नये मथ्यमानायानुब्रूहीत्याह सावित्रीमृचमन्वाह सवितृप्रसूत एवैनं मंथति जाताया नुब्रूहि प्रह्रियमाणायानुब्रूहीत्याह कांडेकांड एवैनं क्रियमाणे[?] समर्थयति गायत्रीः सर्वा अन्वाह ॥

> *agnaye mathyamānāyānubrūhītyāha sāvitrīmṛcamanvāha savitṛprasūta evainaṃ maṃthati jātāyā nubrūhi prahriyamāṇāyānubrūhītyāha kāṃḍekāṃḍa evainaṃ kriyamāṇe[?] samarthayati gāyatrīḥ sarvā anvāha ‖*

etc. It is just this matter that is explained here by the sentence यद्यज्ञोऽभिरूपं तत्समृद्धं (*yadyajño 'bhirūpaṃ tatsamṛddhaṃ*). That is: in the several acts, by saying the mantras that are suitable and appropriate to each act, the sacrifice must be carried out in due order; this is the chief purport. At the end, as soon as आ स्वे योनौ निषीदतु (*ā sve yonau niṣīdatu*) is said,

### Printed p. 389 (PDF 409)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 17", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā" (Varga numeral as read). Ṛk 1 Special Topics continuing.)*

they place Agni in the *āhavanīya* pit; for the place of the *āhavanīya* is said to be the place of the Agni just churned (that is, just produced).

> आजातं जातवेदसीति जाते इतरो जातवेदा इतरः । प्रियं शिशीतातिथिमित्येष ह वा अस्य प्रियोऽतिथिर्यदग्निरग्नेः । स्योन आ गृहपतिमिति शांत्यामेवैनं तद्दधाति । अग्निनाग्निः समिध्यते कविर्गृहपतिर्युवा । हव्यवाड्जुह्वास्य इत्यभिरूपा यद्यज्ञोऽभिरूपं तत्समृद्धं । त्वं ह्यग्ने अग्निना विप्रो विप्रेण सन्त्सतेति[?] विप्र इतरो विप्र इतरः सन्नितरः सन्नितरः सखा सख्या समिध्यस इत्येष ह वा अस्य स्वः सखा यदग्निरग्नेः ॥

> *ājātaṃ jātavedasīti jāte itaro jātavedā itaraḥ | priyaṃ śiśītātithimityeṣa ha vā asya priyo 'tithiryadagniragneḥ | syona ā gṛhapatimiti śāṃtyāmevainaṃ taddadhāti | agnināgniḥ samidhyate kavirgṛhapatiryuvā | havyavāḍjuhvāsya ityabhirūpā yadyajño 'bhirūpaṃ tatsamṛddhaṃ | tvaṃ hyagne agninā vipro vipreṇa santsateti[?] vipra itaro vipra itaraḥ sannitaraḥ sannitaraḥ sakhā sakhyā samidhyasa ityeṣa ha vā asya svaḥ sakhā yadagniragneḥ ‖*

Now the Hotṛ, as the ninth ṛk —

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-16-42, as in the file.)*

> आ जातं जातवेदसि प्रियं शिशीतातिथिं । स्योन आ गृहपतिं ॥

> *ā jātaṃ jātavedasi priyaṃ śiśītātithiṃ | syona ā gṛhapatiṃ ‖*

— recites this mantra. The chief purport of this ṛk is this: in this ṛk two kinds of Agni are indicated. जातं (*jātaṃ*) means the Agni just produced by churning; this is the first, and because it has just been produced it is indicated by the word जातं (*jātaṃ*). The second is the one already established in the *āhavanīya* pit; this they call जातवेदसं (*jātavedasaṃ*). Because it knows the form of the Agni produced by churning, the āhavanīya fire is explained as जातवेदसं (*jātavedasaṃ*). Here, to the Agni named *jātavedas* already established in the place of the āhavanīya fire, the freshly churned Agni is like a dear guest, an object of affection. Therefore this churned Agni, who is both dear and of the nature of a guest, is placed in the āhavanīya fire-pit for the sake of securing a comfortable dwelling; this is the chief purport. Then the Hotṛ —

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-12-6, as in the file.)*

> अग्निनाग्निः समिध्यते कविर्गृहपतिर्युवा । हव्यवाड्जुह्वास्यः ॥

> *agnināgniḥ samidhyate kavirgṛhapatiryuvā | havyavāḍjuhvāsyaḥ ‖*

— recites this tenth ṛk. Its meaning: together with the Agni established earlier in the āhavanīya pit, the freshly churned Agni, joining him, blazes well and shines. This churned Agni is the all-knowing seer, the protector of the house or of the sacrificer, ever young, the bearer of oblations and the like to the deities, who has in his mouth the ladle called *juhū*, the instrument of the offering. (That is, because ājya and the like are offered into the flame of Agni with the ladle called *juhū*, Agni is called जुह्वास्यः (*juhvāsyaḥ*).) Thus a mantra fitting the occasion is recited here. After this, the Hotṛ —

---

### Printed p. 390 (PDF 410)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 1". Ṛk 1 Special Topics continuing.)*

> त्वं ह्यग्ने अग्निना विप्रो विप्रेण सन्त्सता । सखा सख्या समिध्यसे ॥

> *tvaṃ hyagne agninā vipro vipreṇa santsatā | sakhā sakhyā samidhyase ‖*

*(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-43-14, numeral agrees with the file. The word सन्त्सता here is printed clearly; it resolves the [?] at "santsateti" on p. 389.)* — the Hotṛ recites this ṛk (the eleventh). "O newly-born Agni, you, the wise one, joined with the wise Āhavanīya Agni, be happy as a friend joined with a friend is happy" — this is the purport.

> तं मर्जयन्त सुक्रतुं पुरोयावानमाजिषु । स्वेषु क्षयेषु वाजिनमिति । एष ह वा अस्य स्वः क्षयो यदग्निरग्नेः । यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजन्त देवा इत्युत्तमया परिदधाति । यज्ञेन वै तद्देवा यज्ञमयजन्त यदग्निनाग्निमयजन्त ते स्वर्गं लोकमायन् तानि धर्माणि प्रथमान्यासन् । ते ह नाकं महिमानः सचन्ते यत्र पूर्वे साध्याः सन्ति देवा इति छन्दांसि वै साध्या देवास्तेऽग्रेऽग्निनाग्निमयजन्त ते स्वर्गं लोमायन् ॥

> *taṃ marjayanta sukratuṃ puroyāvānamājiṣu | sveṣu kṣayeṣu vājinamiti | eṣa ha vā asya svaḥ kṣayo yadagniragneḥ | yajñena yajñamayajanta devā ityuttamayā paridadhāti | yajñena vai taddevā yajñamayajanta yadagnināgnimayajanta te svargaṃ lokamāyan tāni dharmāṇi prathamānyāsan | te ha nākaṃ mahimānaḥ sacante yatra pūrve sādhyāḥ santi devā iti chandāṃsi vai sādhyā devāste 'gre 'gnināgnimayajanta te svargaṃ lomāyan ‖*

*(The last word is printed लोमायन्, without the क of लोकमायन्, as it looks on the zoom [sic]; the same phrase earlier in the passage and on the next page has लोकमायन्.)*

Then the Hotṛ recites the ṛk तं मर्जयन्त सुक्रतुं (*taṃ marjayanta sukratuṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-85-8, as in the file). Having said this, he establishes Agni in the Āhavanīya fire, his own dwelling-place; then, as the last ṛk of the Agni-churning, that is the 13th (printed "13"), the ṛk यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजन्त देवाः (*yajñena yajñamayajanta devāḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-90-16) the Hotṛ recites and so concludes the churning. Here the placing of the churned Agni (the Agni being carried forward, *prahriyamāṇa*) together with the Āhavanīya Agni is what is meant by अग्निनाग्निमयजन्त (*agnināgnimayajanta*). Or: this very act is stated in the last ṛk यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजन्त देवाः (*yajñena yajñamayajanta devāḥ*). Here the word साध्याः (*sādhyāḥ*) means the presiding deities of the metres such as Gāyatrī. These deities of old worshipped the Āhavanīya Agni with the churned Agni, and therefore obtained the heaven-world.

> आदित्याश्चैवेहासन्नङ्गिरसश्च तेऽग्रेऽग्निनाग्निमयजन्त ते स्वर्गं लोकमायन् सैषा स्वर्ग्याहुतिर्यदग्न्याहुतिर्यदि ह वा अप्यब्राह्मणोक्तो यदि दुरुक्तोक्तो यजतेऽथ हैषाहुतिर्गच्छत्येव देवान्न पाप्मना संसृज्यते गच्छत्यस्याहुतिर्देवान्नास्याहुतिः पाप्मना संसृज्यते य एवं वेद ॥

> *ādityāścaivehāsannaṅgirasaśca te 'gre 'gnināgnimayajanta te svargaṃ lokamāyan saiṣā svargyāhutiryadagnyāhutiryadi ha vā apyabrāhmaṇokto yadi duruktokto yajate 'tha haiṣāhutirgacchatyeva devānna pāpmanā saṃsṛjyate gacchatyasyāhutirdevānnāsyāhutiḥ pāpmanā saṃsṛjyate ya evaṃ veda ‖*

Likewise the Ādityas and the Aṅgirases, as said before, performed the sacrifice and went to heaven. This Agni-oblation is the direct way to heaven. Even if the chief priest, while this sacrificial act is going on, is not a Brāhmaṇa as the śāstra requires, or is a bad man, only the Agni-oblation offered in the sacrifice brings the yajamāna to heaven. The faults of the priest do not touch the yajamāna who performs the sacrifice; that is, he suffers no harm from them. He who knows this order of the Agni-oblation described above reaches the gods in heaven, and no contact with sin attaches to him.

### Printed p. 391 (PDF 411)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 17", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; the Varga numeral was zoomed and read 17, consistent with p. 389. Ṛk 1 Special Topics continuing.)*

Here only "even though he is not a Brāhmaṇa as the śāstra requires" has been said in the sentence above; an explanation of that is necessary. Although some persons have obtained, by birth alone as Brāhmaṇas, the right of conducting sacrifices (the right to have sacrifices performed), they misuse their right and become sharers of guilt. Among these *abrāhmaṇas* the smṛtis speak of six kinds. Thus —

> अब्राह्मणास्तु षट् प्रोक्ता इति शातातपोऽब्रवीत् ।
> आद्यस्तु राजभृत्यः स्याद्द्वितीयः क्रयविक्रयी ।
> तृतीयो बहुयाज्याख्यश्च तुर्थोऽश्रौतयाजकः ।
> पंचमो ग्रामयाजी च षष्ठो ब्रह्मबन्धुः स्मृतः ॥

> *abrāhmaṇāstu ṣaṭ proktā iti śātātapo 'bravīt |*
> *ādyastu rājabhṛtyaḥ syāddvitīyaḥ krayavikrayī |*
> *tṛtīyo bahuyājyākhyaśca turtho 'śrautayājakaḥ |*
> *paṃcamo grāmayājī ca ṣaṣṭho brahmabandhuḥ smṛtaḥ ‖*

*(Printed तुर्थो in the third line [sic] for चतुर्थो.)*

Who the *abrāhmaṇas* are, Śātātapa has said in this way: (1) *Rājabhṛtya*: those who, for a livelihood, take refuge in the king and serve him. (2) Those who live by buying and selling and the like: who set up a shop or the like and live by selling goods. (3) Those who, though they have income enough for a livelihood, from the evil hope of gaining more wealth make it their profession to have sacrifices (or priestly rites) performed for anyone whatever: they are called *bahuyājins*. (4) *Aśrautayājakas*: although they are accomplished in the study of the Veda for performing Śrauta acts, that is, sacrifices and the like, they do not engage in Śrauta rites in that way nor have them performed for others, but engage only in Smārta rites, which are not of the highest kind. (5) *Grāmayājakas*: those who, in villages or towns, for anyone whatever, fit or unfit, have sacrifices performed out of desire for wealth; they are called village-and-town priests. (6) *Brahmabandhu*: those who do not perform the twilight rites and the like at the right time at sunrise and sunset. To the rites conducted by priests of these six kinds the above words *abrāhmaṇokta* ("spoken of by a non-Brāhmaṇa") or *duruktokta* have been applied.

> ता एतास्त्रयोदशान्वाह रूपसमृद्धा एतद्वै यज्ञस्य समृद्धं यद्रूपसमृद्धं यत्कर्म क्रियमाणमृगभिवदति । तासां त्रिःप्रथमामन्वाह त्रिरुत्तमां ताः सप्तदश संपद्यन्ते सप्तदशो वै प्रजापतिर्द्वादश मासाः पंचर्तवस्त्रावान्संवत्सरः[?] संवत्सरः प्रजापतिः प्रजापत्यायतनाभिरेवाभीराध्नोति य एवं वेद त्रिः प्रथमां त्रिरुत्तमामन्वाह यज्ञस्स्यैव तद्ब्रसौ[?] नह्यति स्थेम्ने बलायोविस्रंसाय ॥

> *tā etāstrayodaśānvāha rūpasamṛddhā etadvai yajñasya samṛddhaṃ yadrūpasamṛddhaṃ yatkarma kriyamāṇamṛgabhivadati | tāsāṃ triḥprathamāmanvāha triruttamāṃ tāḥ saptadaśa saṃpadyante saptadaśo vai prajāpatirdvādaśa māsāḥ paṃcartavastrāvānsaṃvatsaraḥ[?] saṃvatsaraḥ prajāpatiḥ prajāpatyāyatanābhirevābhīrādhnoti ya evaṃ veda triḥ prathamāṃ triruttamāmanvāha yajñassyaiva tadbrasau[?] nahyati sthemne balāyovisraṃsāya ‖*

*(Ai. Brā. 3-5, numeral as in the file. Doubtful: the word before संवत्सरः in the fourth line, and तद्ब्रसौ at the end of the line; both zoomed and left as printed.)*

In this way the ṛks used in the Agni-churning are thirteen in all. The ṛks addressed to the Rakṣoghna deity [the first letters of this line are cut off at the left edge of the scan; the number before "ṛks" is lost: [?]] are not included in this. Because these thirteen ṛks are recited at the respective times,

### Printed p. 392 (PDF 412)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 1". Close of the Special Topics of Ṛk 1; Ṛk 2: Saṃhitā, Pada, the beginning of the bhāṣya. No grammar page for Ṛk 1 is printed between.)*

the churning of Agni, the origin of Agni, the carrying of Agni and placing him in the Āhavanīya, and joining him there with the Āhavanīya fire — all these acts are completed with all their parts by the recitation of the ṛks suited to the moment; this is called *rūpasamṛddhi* ("perfection of form"). Of these thirteen ṛks the first ṛk (the ṛk अभि त्वा देव सवितः (*abhi tvā deva savitaḥ*)) and the last ṛk (the ṛk यज्ञेन यज्ञमयजन्त देवाः (*yajñena yajñamayajanta devāḥ*)) must be recited by the Hotṛ three times each. Hence in this Agni-churning seventeen ṛks are recited in all. Prajāpati has the nature of the number seventeen (*saptadaśa*): for twelve months and five seasons together make one year; that year is Prajāpati. Therefore he who knows the meaning of these ṛks, placed in Prajāpati, attains prosperity. By reciting the first and last ṛks thrice each, the bonds (knots) of the sacrifice become firm and tight, and have room to stand fast without slipping — thus it is set forth in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (Ai. Brā. 3-5) on the Agni-churning.

**अग्निनिर्मंथनविधिः समाप्तः** — "The rule of the Agni-churning is concluded" (printed in Kannada, centred), then a short rule and the heading "Saṃhitā-pāṭha".

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

Printed in Kannada; the Sanskrit headwords are given in Devanagari.

अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni! होत्रं (*hotraṃ*) — the office of the Hotṛ, who recites the śastras, yājyās and the like. तव (*tava*) — belonging to you. पोत्रं (*potraṃ*) — the office of the Potṛ also. तव (*tava*) — yours; that is, it is for your sake. ऋत्वियं (*ṛtviyaṃ*) — the office of the Ṛtvijs. नेष्ट्रं (*neṣṭraṃ*) — the office of the Neṣṭṛ also. तव (*tava*) — is yours. त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you. ऋतायतः (*ṛtāyataḥ*) — for the sacrificer who desires the sacrifice. अग्नित् (*agnit*) — you are the Agnīdhra. प्रशास्त्रं (*praśāstraṃ*) — the office of the Praśāstṛ also. तव (*tava*) — yours. त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you. अध्वरीयसि (*adhvarīyasi*) — you are the Adhvaryu, that is, you do the work the Adhvaryu does. ब्रह्मा च असि (*brahmā ca asi*) — you are also the Brahmā. नः (*naḥ*) — our. दमे (*dame*) — in the sacrificial house. गृहपतिश्च (*gṛhapatiśca*) — and the householder (or the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice) you are.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni! The office belonging to the Hotṛ, and the office belonging to the Potṛ and the Neṣṭṛ, are yours. For the sacrificer who desires the sacrifice you are the Agnīdhra. The office of the Praśāstṛ also is yours. You are the Adhvaryu and the Brahmā, and in our sacrificial house the householder.

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

Yours, Agni, is the office of the Hotri, of the Potri, of the Ritwij ; of the Neshtri, you are the Agnidhra of the devout, yours is the function of the Prashastri, you are the Adhwaryu and the Brahman, and the householder in our dwelling.

**विशेषविषयगळು (Special Topics)**

In this Ṛk and in the Ṛks that follow, Agni is variously described as the form of the many deities and of the Ṛtvijs. When praising the great, it is the usage to call them Indra, Candra, Devendra. Likewise here too the ṛṣi Gṛtsamada praises Agni by comparing him with various deities. Such a description —

### Printed p. 394 (PDF 414)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 1", numerals as the numeral file reads them (2.2 / 1 / 1; the file reads the first two groups together).)*

> वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि देवानामस्मि वासवः ।
> इन्द्रियाणां मनश्चास्मि भूतानामस्मि चेतना ॥

> *vedānāṃ sāmavedo 'smi devānāmasmi vāsavaḥ |*
> *indriyāṇāṃ manaścāsmi bhūtānāmasmi cetanā ‖*

*(Bhagavadgītā 10-22, as printed "भ. गी. १०=२२". The third word of the second line looks like इन्द्रियोणां in the print; read इन्द्रियाणां.)*

— and the like, is found in the sentences of the Bhagavadgītā and in many other modern works. In the present Ṛk, Agni is praised as the office or the very nature of the Hotṛ, Potṛ, the Ṛtvijs, the Neṣṭṛ, the Adhvaryu, the Brahmā, the householder and others, who bear the chief parts in the sacrifice.

Among the Ṛtvijs who take part in a sacrifice, the Hotṛ, Adhvaryu, Udgātṛ and Brahmā are the chief. As their assistants there are twelve more Ṛtvijs; in all sixteen persons. Namely —

(1) The Ṛtvijs of the Hotṛ group: Hotṛ, मैत्रावरुण (*maitrāvaruṇa*), अच्छावाक (*acchāvāka*) and ग्रावस्तुत् (*grāvastut*); these four are the Ṛtvijs of the Hotṛ group.
(2) Those of the Adhvaryu group: Adhvaryu, प्रतिप्रस्थातृ (*pratiprasthātṛ*), Neṣṭṛ and उन्नेतृ (*unnetṛ*).
(3) Those of the Udgātṛ group: Udgātṛ, प्रस्तोतृ (*prastotṛ*), प्रतिहर्तृ (*pratihartṛ*) and सुब्रह्मण्य (*subrahmaṇya*).
(4) Those of the Brahmā group: Brahmā, ब्राह्मणाच्छंसि (*brāhmaṇācchaṃsi*), Agnīdhra, Potṛ.

The chief duty of the Hotṛ group in these rites is this: when the Adhvaryu has spoken the Praiṣa mantra and uttered "such-and-such a mantra is to be recited", the Hotṛ recites, according to the occasion, the mantras of the Ṛgveda — the Prātaranuvāka mantras, the śastra mantras, the yājyā and puronuvākyā mantras, the mantras to be said in the Agni-churning and the like — and thus brings the sacrificial acts to completion. The Ṛgveda mantras are the chief ones for them.

In the sacrifice the part of the Adhvaryu and his assistant group is by far the largest. For all the work the Adhvaryu goes first and by the Praiṣa mantras at the proper times indicates to the other Ṛtvijs what work is to be done. Therefore it is said अध्वर्युर्वा ऋत्विजां प्रथमो युज्यते (*adhvaryurvā ṛtvijāṃ prathamo yujyate*) ("the Adhvaryu is the first of the Ṛtvijs to be engaged"), that is, he is the chief of all Ṛtvijs. All his work is based on the Yajurveda.

The Udgātṛ group sing the Sāman appropriate to the occasion, at the time of invoking the deities and at the Soma-pressing. The Sāmaveda mantras are the chief ones for them. अयज्ञो वा एष योऽसामा (*ayajño vā eṣa yo 'sāmā*) — that is, "a sacrifice without Sāman-singing is no sacrifice" — so their part too is very important.

---

### Printed p. 395 (PDF 415)

*(Header: "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Aṣṭaka 2, Varga 17 as read; the adhyāya numeral not checked.)*

The Brahmā and his assisting group see to it that the work done in sacrifices and the like proceeds completely and as the Śāstra prescribes, and, if any defect or omission occurs in the middle, they have the proper expiation and the like performed so that the sacrifice may end in good order: this is their duty. They must also have knowledge of the four Vedas.

All that has been said above is the common duty of the Ṛtvijs of each group. Besides these, each Ṛtvij also has his own special and specified duty. To state all these here would make the book long, and since it is not much needed, they are not given here. Only a brief account of the work of the Ṛtvijs indicated in this Ṛk is given here.

The होतृ (*hotṛ*) in the sacrifice invokes the deities, reciting mantras suited to each time. The पोतृ (*potṛ*) belongs to the Brahmā group; he corrects and purifies the defects and omissions that may occur in the sacrifice. The नेष्टृ (*neṣṭṛ*) does the work of bringing the sacrificer's wife and the like; he belongs to the Adhvaryu group. The अग्नीत् (*agnīt*) (अग्नीध्र (*agnīdhra*)) kindles Agni and tends it; he belongs to the Brahmā group. The प्रस्थातृ (*prasthātṛ*) (Maitrāvaruṇa) is the Hotṛ's assistant and directs the other Ṛtvijs (there is a Taittirīya Saṃhitā sentence: मैत्रावरुणो हि पुरस्तादृत्विग्भ्यो वाचं विभजति (*maitrāvaruṇo hi purastādṛtvigbhyo vācaṃ vibhajati*)). The अध्वर्यु (*adhvaryu*) takes the lead in all the activities of the sacrifice; whatever work is to be done is done through him or by his order. The ब्रह्मा (*brahmā*) sees to it that the sacrifice goes on correctly and that no mantra or rite is omitted. The गृहपति (*gṛhapati*) here may be Agni, the lord of the sacrificial house, or the sacrificer himself, who performs the sacrifice. The ṛṣi describes all of these as the very form of Agni, saying that Agni is of great majesty.

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वं । अग्ने । इन्द्रः । वृषभः । सतां । असि । त्वं । विष्णुः । उरुऽगायः । नमस्यः ॥
> त्वं । ब्रह्मा । रयिऽवित् । ब्रह्मणः । पते । त्वं । विधर्तरिति । विऽधर्तः । सचसे । पुरंऽध्या ॥ ३ ॥

> *tvaṃ | agne | indraḥ | vṛṣabhaḥ | satāṃ | asi | tvaṃ | viṣṇuḥ | uru 'gāyaḥ | namasyaḥ ‖*
> *tvaṃ | brahmā | rayi 'vit | brahmaṇaḥ | pate | tvaṃ | vidhartariti | vi 'dhartaḥ | sacase | puraṃ 'dhyā ‖ 3 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Agni is Indra as the showerer of wishes, Viṣṇu as the much-praised, Brahmā as the knower of wealth, and is joined with manifold insight.

> हे अग्ने त्वं यतः सतां वृषभो वर्षितासि अतो इन्द्रोऽसि । यद्वा सतां साधूनामिन्द्रोऽसि । कामानां वर्षितासि । त्वं विष्णुरसि । यत उरुगायो बहुभिर्गीयमानो नमस्यो नमस्कार्यश्च भवसि । हे ब्रह्मणस्पते परिवृढस्य कर्मणो मन्त्रस्य वा पालयितस्त्वं यतो रयिवित् गवादिधनस्य वेत्ता अतो ब्रह्मासि । हे विधर्तर्विविधकारक वैश्वानररूपाग्ने पुरंध्या बहुप्रकारया बुद्ध्या सचसे सह वर्तसे । सर्वदा बुद्ध्या स्तूयस इत्यर्थः ॥

> *he agne tvaṃ yataḥ satāṃ vṛṣabho varṣitāsi ato indro 'si | yadvā satāṃ sādhūnāmindro 'si | kāmānāṃ varṣitāsi | tvaṃ viṣṇurasi | yata urugāyo bahubhirgīyamāno namasyo namaskāryaśca bhavasi | he brahmaṇaspate parivṛḍhasya karmaṇo mantrasya vā pālayitastvaṃ yato rayivit gavādidhanasya vettā ato brahmāsi | he vidhartarvividhakāraka vaiśvānararūpāgne puraṃdhyā bahuprakārayā buddhyā sacase saha vartase | sarvadā buddhyā stūyasa ityarthaḥ ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; सतां (*satāṃ*) — to good men; वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*) — one who showers (grants) wished-for things; इन्द्रः (*indraḥ*) — as Indra; असि (*asi*) — you are; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; उरुगायः (*urugāyaḥ*) — praised by many; नमस्यः (*namasyaḥ*) — worthy of salutation; विष्णुः (*viṣṇuḥ*) — you are Viṣṇu; ब्रह्मणस्पते (*brahmaṇaspate*) — O Agni, protector of the rites; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; रयिवित् (*rayivit*) — wealthy; ब्रह्मा (*brahmā*) — you are Brahmā; विधर्तः (*vidhartaḥ*) — O Vaiśvānara-Agni, the doer of many works; पुरंध्या (*puraṃdhyā*) — by manifold knowledge; सचसे (*sacase*) — you are united (or: you are praised with manifold wisdom).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni! You are Indra, who grants wished-for things to good men; you are Viṣṇu, who is praised by many and worthy of salutation; and you are the wealthy Brahmā. You are endowed with every kind of knowledge.

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

You, Agni, are Indra, the showerer (of bounties) on the good ; you are the adorable Vishnu, the hymned of many ; you, Brahmasanapati [sic], are Brahma, the possessor of riches ; you, the author of various (conditions), are associated with wisdom.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*) — कामानां वर्षिता (*kāmānāṃ varṣitā*): one who showers wished-for things; one who gives wished-for things.

इन्द्रो वृषभः सतां असि (*indro vṛṣabhaḥ satāṃ asi*) — you are one who gives wished-for things to good men, like Indra. Or इन्द्रो सतां असि (*indro satāṃ asi*) [initial vowel of the last word looks long in print] — the meaning is: you are called the best among all good men.

विष्णुरुरुगायः (*viṣṇururugāyaḥ*) — बहुभिर्गीयमानो विष्णुरसि (*bahubhirgīyamāno viṣṇurasi*): you are Viṣṇu. Like Viṣṇu, you are sung of by many in respect of your qualities.

ब्रह्मणस्पते (*brahmaṇaspate*) — यज्ञकर्मणः पालयिता (*yajñakarmaṇaḥ pālayitā*): protector of the sacrificial rites. Or, like Bṛhaspati (Brahmaṇaspati), lord of the hymns.

पुरंध्या (*puraṃdhyā*) — Yāska has the derivation पुरंधिर्बहुधी (*puraṃdhirbahudhī*) ("Purandhi = much thought") (Nirukta 6-13, as printed "ni. 6-13"). बहुप्रकारया बुद्ध्या सचसे (*bahuprakārayā buddhyā sacase*): you are one who possesses abundant or manifold understanding. Or: people praise you with their manifold understanding; this too is the meaning.

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वम॑ग्ने॒ राजा॒ वरु॑णो धृ॒तव्र॑त॒स्त्वं मि॒त्रो भ॑वसि द॒स्म ईड्यः॑ ।
> त्वम॑र्य॒मा सत्प॑ति॒र्यस्य॑ सं॒भुजं॒ त्वमंशो॑ वि॒दथे॑ देव भाज॒युः ॥ ४ ॥

> *tvamagne rājā varuṇo dhṛtavratastvaṃ mitro bhavasi dasma īḍyaḥ |*
> *tvamaryamā satpatiryasya saṃbhujaṃ tvamaṃśo vidathe deva bhājayuḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वं । अग्ने । राजा । वरुणः । धृतऽव्रतः । त्वं । मित्रः । भवसि । दस्मः । ईड्यः ।
> त्वं । अर्यमा । सत्ऽपतिः । यस्य । संऽभुजं । त्वं । अंशः । विदथे । देव । भाजयुः ॥ ४ ॥

> *tvaṃ | agne | rājā | varuṇaḥ | dhṛta 'vrataḥ | tvaṃ | mitraḥ | bhavasi | dasmaḥ | īḍyaḥ |*
> *tvaṃ | aryamā | sat 'patiḥ | yasya | saṃ 'bhujaṃ | tvaṃ | aṃśaḥ | vidathe | deva | bhājayuḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(continues on p. 398)*

*Gist:* Agni is Varuṇa as upholder of vows, Mitra as the praised destroyer of foes, Aryaman as protector of the good, and Aṃśa, distributing fruits at the sacrifice.

> हे अग्ने त्वं यतो धृतव्रतो धारितकर्मासि अतो वरुणो राजासि । यतो दस्मः शत्रूणामुपक्षपयिता ईड्यः स्तुत्यश्च अतो मित्र एतन्नामको

> *he agne tvaṃ yato dhṛtavrato dhāritakarmāsi ato varuṇo rājāsi | yato dasmaḥ śatrūṇāmupakṣapayitā īḍyaḥ stutyaśca ato mitra etannāmako*

### Printed p. 398 (PDF 418)

> देवोऽसि । यतः सत्पतिः सतामभिमतप्रदानेन पालयिता अतोऽर्यमा भवसि । दातृत्वं चार्यम्णो लिंगं । अर्यमेति तमाहुर्यो ददातीति । यस्यार्यम्णो दानं संभुजं संततभुजं व्यापकं भवति । यद्वा यस्य धनं संभुजं सम्यक् भोगाय साधु ग्रहीत्वाणां [?] । तथा त्वमंशः सूर्यमूर्त्यंतरभूते एतन्नामको देवोऽसि । तादृश हे देव विदथेऽस्मदीये यज्ञे भाजयुः फलानां भाजयिता प्रपेयितासि [?] ॥

> *devo 'si | yataḥ satpatiḥ satāmabhimatapradānena pālayitā ato 'ryamā bhavasi | dātṛtvaṃ cāryamṇo liṃgaṃ | aryameti tamāhuryo dadātīti | yasyāryamṇo dānaṃ saṃbhujaṃ saṃtatabhujaṃ vyāpakaṃ bhavati | yadvā yasya dhanaṃ saṃbhujaṃ samyak bhogāya sādhu grahītvāṇāṃ [?] | tathā tvamaṃśaḥ sūryamūrtyaṃtarabhūte etannāmako devo 'si | tādṛśa he deva vidathe 'smadīye yajñe bhājayuḥ phalānāṃ bhājayitā prapeyitāsi [?] ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; धृतव्रतः (*dhṛtavrataḥ*) — controller of truth and other vows; राजा (*rājā*) — the lord; वरुणः (*varuṇaḥ*) — you are Varuṇa; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; दस्मः (*dasmaḥ*) — destroyer of enemies; ईड्यः (*īḍyaḥ*) — worthy of praise; मित्रः (*mitraḥ*) — you are Mitra; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; यस्य (*yasya*) — whose Aryaman's; gift (दानं (*dānaṃ*)); संभुजं (*saṃbhujaṃ*) — as that which is enjoyed everywhere; सत्पतिः (*satpatiḥ*) — protector of good men; अर्यमा (*aryamā*) — as Aryaman; भवसि (*bhavasi*) — you are; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; अंशः (*aṃśaḥ*) — you are the god Aṃśa; देवः (*devaḥ*) — O god, being such, O Agni; विदथे (*vidathe*) — in our sacrifice; भाजयुः (*bhājayuḥ*) — be the distributor of good fruits.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni! You are Varuṇa, the controller of vows and the lord, and Mitra, the destroyer of enemies and worthy of praise. You are Aryaman, the cause of the gift enjoyed by all and the protector of good men, and you are Aṃśa. O Agni, who are the very self of the deities, be the distributor of good fruits in our sacrifice.

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

You, Agni, are the royal Varuna, observant of holy vows : you are the adorable Mitra, the destroyer (of foes) : you are Aryaman, the protector of the virtuous, whose (liberality) is enjoyed by all : you are a portion (of the sun) : be the distributor (of good things), divine (Agni), at our sacrifice.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

In this Ṛk Agni is described as the very form of the deities named Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman and Aṃśa. That these deities Mitra and the rest are called Ādityas —

Passage cited (RV 2-27-1, printed "ṛ. saṃ. 2-27-1"; the sentence introducing it is unfinished at the end of the page, so Special Topics remain open; no gloss given by the source):

> इमा गिर आदित्येभ्यो घृतस्नूः सनाद्राजभ्यो जुह्वा जुहोमि ।
> शृणोतु मित्रो अर्यमा भगो नस्तुविजातो वरुणो दक्षो अंशः ॥

> *imā gira ādityebhyo ghṛtasnūḥ sanādrājabhyo juhvā juhomi |*
> *śṛṇotu mitro aryamā bhago nastuvijāto varuṇo dakṣo aṃśaḥ ‖*

…and in the Ṛk so beginning, and in the Ṛks that follow in this sūkta, they are praised. These three deities, Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryamā, are praised together as a group in many places. For their subject see what we have written at length on pp. 119–129 of this same volume.

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वम॑ग्ने॒ त्वष्टा॑ विध॒ते सु॒वीर्यं॒ तव॒ ग्नावो॑ मित्रमहः सजा॒त्य॑म् ।
> त्वमा॑शु॒हेमा॑ ररिषे॒ स्वश्व्यं॒ त्वं न॒रां शर्धो॑ असि पुरू॒वसुः॑ ॥ ५

> *tvamagne tvaṣṭā vidhate suvīryaṃ tava gnāvo mitramahaḥ sajātyam |*
> *tvamāśuhemā rariṣe svaśvyaṃ tvaṃ narāṃ śardho asi purūvasuḥ ‖ 5*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वं । अग्ने । त्वष्टा । विधते । सुऽवीर्यं । तव । ग्नावः । मित्रऽमहः । सऽजात्यं ।
> त्वं । आशुऽहेमा । ररिषे । सुऽअश्व्यं । त्वं । नरां । शर्धः । असि । पुरुऽवसुः ॥ ५ ॥

> *tvaṃ | agne | tvaṣṭā | vidhate | su 'vīryaṃ | tava | gnāvaḥ | mitra 'mahaḥ | sa 'jātyaṃ |*
> *tvaṃ | āśu 'hemā | rariṣe | su 'aśvyaṃ | tvaṃ | narāṃ | śardhaḥ | asi | puru 'vasuḥ ‖ 5 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Agni, as Tvaṣṭṛ, gives good wealth to the worshipper; praises are his; he is asked to cherish kinship, give fruit with good horses, and is the strength of men.

> हे अग्ने त्वष्टा फलस्य साधु संपादयिता त्वं विधते परिचरते जनाय सुवीर्यं शोभनवीर्यं । वीर्यं धनं । तद्धेतुर्भवसि । ग्नावो याः स्तुतिवाचः संति तास्तव स्वभूताः । हे मित्रमहः हितकारितेजः सजात्यमस्माकं बांधवं भजस [sic] इत्यर्थः । हे अग्ने आशुहेमा आशु प्रेरयिता त्वं स्वश्व्यं शोभनाश्वसमूहोपेतं फलं ररिषे । ददासि । हे अग्ने पुरूवसुः प्रभूतधनस्त्वं नरां नराणां शर्धो बलस्थानीयोऽसि ॥

> *he agne tvaṣṭā phalasya sādhu saṃpādayitā tvaṃ vidhate paricarate janāya suvīryaṃ śobhanavīryaṃ | vīryaṃ dhanaṃ | taddheturbhavasi | gnāvo yāḥ stutivācaḥ saṃti tāstava svabhūtāḥ | he mitramahaḥ hitakāritejaḥ sajātyamasmākaṃ bāṃdhavaṃ bhajasa [sic] ityarthaḥ | he agne āśuhemā āśu prerayitā tvaṃ svaśvyaṃ śobhanāśvasamūhopetaṃ phalaṃ rariṣe | dadāsi | he agne purūvasuḥ prabhūtadhanastvaṃ narāṃ narāṇāṃ śardho balasthānīyo 'si ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*) — one who provides fruit; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; विधते (*vidhate*) — to the people who serve (you); सुवीर्यं (*suvīryaṃ*) — wealth endowed with excellent valour (you give);

---


### Printed p. 400 (PDF 420)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 1". Ṛk 5 continues: Pratipadārtha from p. 399.)*

ग्नावः (*gnāvaḥ*) — all the words in the form of praise; तव (*tava*) — are yours; मित्रमहः (*mitramahaḥ*) — O Agni of the radiance that does good to the world; सजात्यं (*sajātyaṃ*) — protect kinship with us; आशुहेमा (*āśuhemā*) — you who impel (us) swiftly (in our duties); स्वश्व्यं (*svaśvyaṃ*) — the fruit endowed with excellent horses; ररिषे (*rariṣe*) — you give; पुरूवसुः (*purūvasuḥ*) — possessed of abundant wealth; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; नरां (*narāṃ*) — of men; शर्धः (*śardhaḥ*) — in the form of strength; असि (*asi*) — you are.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, you who are Tvaṣṭṛ, give to the people who serve you wealth endowed with excellent valour. All words of praise are yours. O Agni of the radiance that does good to the world, protect kinship with us. You, who impel us swiftly in our duties, give the fruit endowed with excellent horses. You, possessed of abundant wealth, are the very form of the strength of men.

**English Translation** *(as printed; the heading is printed "English Translatin" [sic])*

You, Agni, are Twashtri, (the giver) of great wealth to (your) worshipper : these praises are yours : do you, of benevolent power, (admit) our affinity : you, who are prompt to encourage (us), give us good (store of) horses : you, who abound with opulence, are the strength of men.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*) — फलस्य साधु संपादयिता (*phalasya sādhu saṃpādayitā*) (the printed heading looks like संपेदयिता (*saṃpedayitā*)). For this word the bhāṣyakāra gives the meaning "one who well provides the fruits of sacrifices and other rites to the sacrificers". Or the word त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*) may also be taken as the divine craftsman named Tvaṣṭṛ. As Tvaṣṭṛ, the craftsman of the gods, makes for the deities the instruments they need, so you (Agni) give to the deities and also to men every kind of wealth and prosperity: this is the sense.

ग्नावः (*gnāvaḥ*) — ग्नावो याः स्तुतिवाचः संति तास्तव स्वभूताः (*gnāvo yāḥ stutivācaḥ saṃti tāstava svabhūtāḥ*) — the word ग्नाः (*gnāḥ*) is read among the names of speech (the reference is printed "नि." with numerals that look like 2-23 [?]). Since all praise-words are directed to you, the sense is that you are yourself the form of praise-words.

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वम॑ग्ने रु॒द्रो असु॑रो म॒हो दि॒वस्त्वं शर्धो॒ मारु॑तं पृ॒क्ष ई॑शिषे ।

> *tvamagne rudro asuro maho divastvaṃ śardho mārutaṃ pṛkṣa īśiṣe |*

### Printed p. 401 (PDF 421)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 18", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā"; Varga 18 begins; the numeral was zoomed. Ṛk 6, continued: Saṃhitā ends, Pada, bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha begun.)*

> त्वं वात्यैररुण्यैर्यासि शंगयस्त्वं पूषा विधतः पासि नु त्मना ॥ ६

> *tvaṃ vātyairaruṇyairyāsi śaṃgayastvaṃ pūṣā vidhataḥ pāsi nu tmanā ‖ 6*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वं । अग्ने । रुद्रः । असुरः । महः । दिवः । त्वं । शर्धः । मारुतं । पृक्षः । ईशिषे ।
> त्वं । वात्यैः । अरुण्यैः । यासि । शंऽगयः । त्वं । पूषा । विधतः । पासि । नु । त्मना ॥ ६ ॥

> *tvaṃ | agne | rudraḥ | asuraḥ | mahaḥ | divaḥ | tvaṃ | śardhaḥ | mārutaṃ | pṛkṣaḥ | īśiṣe |*
> *tvaṃ | vātyaiḥ | aruṇyaiḥ | yāsi | śaṃ 'gayaḥ | tvaṃ | pūṣā | vidhataḥ | pāsi | nu | tmanā ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Agni is Rudra, Asura (Āditya), the Maruts' strength and Vāyu, lord of the oblation-food, comes in the winds' red horses to the sacrifice, and as Pūṣan protects his servants.

> हे अग्ने त्वं महो दिवो महतो द्युलोकात् । उपलक्षणमेतत् । लोकत्रयात् । असुरः शत्रूणां निरसिता रुद्रोऽसि । रुद् दुःखं दुःखहेतुर्वा पापादिः । तस्य द्रावयिता एतन्नामको देवोऽसि । रुद्रो वा एष यदग्निः । त्रै. ५-४-३ । इत्यादिष्वग्ने [?] रुद्रशब्देन व्यवहारात् । यद्वा त्वं रुद्रः । रौति मामनिष्ट्वा नरा दुःखे पतिष्यंतीति रुद्रः । तादृशोऽसि । रुद्रो रौतीति सते इति हि निरुक्तं । तथा महो महतो द्युलोकस्य संबंध्यसुरोऽसि । असुर्बलं । तस्य दाताऽऽदित्यरूपश्च त्वमसि । अग्नेर्द्युलोकसंबंध्यसुरत्वमुत वा दिवो असुराय मन्म । ५-४१-३ । इत्यादिषु । तथा त्वं मारुतं शर्धो मरुत्समूहरूपं बलमसि । वायुरूपश्च त्वमसीत्यर्थः । एवमग्न्यादित्यवायुरूपस्त्वं । पृक्षोऽन्नस्य हविर्लक्षणस्य त्वमीशिषे । ईश्वरो भवसि । यस्मादेवं तस्मात्त्वं वात्यैर्वायुसदृश्यैररुण्यै-ररुणवर्णैरश्वैः शंगयः सुखस्य गृहरूप आवासभूतः सन् यासि । प्राप्नोषि यागगृहं । यद्वा अरुण्यैर्गमनशीलैर्वात्यैर्वायुभिरुत्पन्नः सन् यासि वने । तथा त्वं पूषा सर्वस्य पोषकः सन् नु क्षिप्रं त्मना आत्मनानुग्रहरूपया स्वबुद्ध्यैव विधतः परिचरतो यजमानान् पासि ॥

> *he agne tvaṃ maho divo mahato dyulokāt | upalakṣaṇametat | lokatrayāt | asuraḥ śatrūṇāṃ nirasitā rudro 'si | rud duḥkhaṃ duḥkhaheturvā pāpādiḥ | tasya drāvayitā etannāmako devo 'si | rudro vā eṣa yadagniḥ | trai. 5-4-3 | ityādiṣvagne [?] rudraśabdena vyavahārāt | yadvā tvaṃ rudraḥ | rauti māmaniṣṭvā narā duḥkhe patiṣyaṃtīti rudraḥ | tādṛśo 'si | rudro rautīti sate iti hi niruktaṃ | tathā maho mahato dyulokasya saṃbaṃdhyasuro 'si | asurbalaṃ | tasya dātā ' 'dityarūpaśca tvamasi | agnerdyulokasaṃbaṃdhyasuratvamuta vā divo asurāya manma | 5-41-3 | ityādiṣu | tathā tvaṃ mārutaṃ śardho marutsamūharūpaṃ balamasi | vāyurūpaśca tvamasītyarthaḥ | evamagnyādityavāyurūpastvaṃ | pṛkṣo 'nnasya havirlakṣaṇasya tvamīśiṣe | īśvaro bhavasi | yasmādevaṃ tasmāttvaṃ vātyairvāyusadṛśyairaruṇyai-raruṇavarṇairaśvaiḥ śaṃgayaḥ sukhasya gṛharūpa āvāsabhūtaḥ san yāsi | prāpnoṣi yāgagṛhaṃ | yadvā aruṇyairgamanaśīlairvātyairvāyubhirutpannaḥ san yāsi vane | tathā tvaṃ pūṣā sarvasya poṣakaḥ san nu kṣipraṃ tmanā ātmanānugraharūpayā svabuddhyaiva vidhataḥ paricarato yajamānān pāsi ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; महः (*mahaḥ*) — great; दिवः (*divaḥ*) — from the heaven (from the three worlds); असुरः (*asuraḥ*) — the driver away of enemies; रुद्रः (*rudraḥ*) — you are Rudra; [or रुद्रः त्वं (*rudraḥ tvaṃ*) — you who are of the form of Rudra; महः (*mahaḥ*) — great; दिवः (*divaḥ*) — to heaven; असुरः (*asuraḥ*) — the giver of strength, you are Āditya]; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; मारुतं शर्धः (मारुतं शर्धः (*mārutaṃ śardhaḥ*)) — you are strength in the form of the Maruts' multitude; पृक्षः (*pṛkṣaḥ*) — of food in the form of the oblation; ईशिषे (*īśiṣe*) — you are the lord; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; अरुण्यैः (*aruṇyaiḥ*) — swift; वात्यैः (*vātyaiḥ*) — by winds (impelled), or with horses of the form of wind, together with…

*(Pratipadārtha breaks off at the foot of the page; the signature mark "[26]" and "Vol. 14" are printed there. Ṛk 6 is left open: it continues on p. 402.)*

### Printed p. 402 (PDF 422)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 1". Ṛk 6 continues: the Pratipadārtha, begun on p. 401, resumes with the tail of the previous entry.)*

(…impelled by the wind, and) शंगयः (*śaṃgayaḥ*) — as the dwelling-place of happiness; यासि (*yāsi*) — you come to the sacrificial house; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; पूषा (*pūṣā*) — being the nourisher of all; नु (*nu*) — with vigilance; त्मना (*tmanā*) — by your own will; विधतः (*vidhataḥ*) — the sacrificers who serve you; पासि (*pāsi*) — you protect.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, you who are of the form of Rudra, you are Āditya for the great heaven. You are indeed the strength in the form of the Maruts' multitude. You are the lord of all food in the form of the oblation. Impelled by Vāyu and being the dwelling-place of happiness, you come to the sacrificial house. Being the nourisher of all, you protect, with a mind attentive of its own accord, the sacrificer who serves you.

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

You, Agni, are Rudra, the expeller (of foes) from the expanse of heaven ; you are the strength of the Maruts, you are supreme over (sacrificial) food, you, who are pleasantly domiciled (in the hall of sacrifice), go with ruddy horses, (fleet as) the wind ; as Pushan, you cherish, of your own will, those, who offer worship.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

रुद्रः (*rudraḥ*) — रुद्दुःखं दुःखहेतुर्वा पापादिः । तस्य द्रावयिता । (*rudduḥkhaṃ duḥkhaheturvā pāpādiḥ | tasya drāvayitā |*) *Rud* means sorrow; what is the cause of sorrow is sin. Because he makes that sin run away, this deity is called Rudra. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda it is said:

> रुद्रो वा एष यदग्निः ।

> *rudro vā eṣa yadagniḥ |*

(Tai. Saṃ. 5-4-3.) From this the sense is that Agni himself is of the form of Rudra. Or:

> रौति मामनिष्ट्वा नरा दुःखे पतिष्यंतीति रुद्रः ।

> *rauti māmaniṣṭvā narā duḥkhe patiṣyaṃtīti rudraḥ |*

"He cries (*rauti*): 'Men, not worshipping me, will fall into sorrow'; therefore he is Rudra." Since men who do not worship Agni with sacrifices and the like become sharers in sorrow, such an Agni is called Rudra. In the Nirukta also:

> रुद्रो रौतीति सतः । रोरूयमाणो द्रवतीति वा रोदयतेर्वा । यदरुदत्तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वमिति काठकं । यदरोदीत्तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वमिति हारिद्रविकं ॥

> *rudro rautīti sataḥ | rorūyamāṇo dravatīti vā rodayatervā | yadarudattadrudrasya rudratvamiti kāṭhakaṃ | yadarodīttadrudrasya rudratvamiti hāridravikaṃ ‖*

(Ni. 10-2, as zoomed.) Thus Yāska has given the etymology. Following it Sāyaṇa has explained the word Rudra in six ways. The word Rudra is formed from the root *rud* with the suffix *ṇijanta*. Yāska said above: रुद्रो रौतीति सतः । रोरूयमाणो द्रवतीति वा । रोदयतेर्वा । (*rudro rautīti sataḥ | rorūyamāṇo dravatīti vā | rodayatervā |*) ("Rudra is one who cries, being…; or he runs crying; or from *rodayati*, causes to weep.")
