### Printed p. 403 (PDF 423)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 18"; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Ṛk 6, Special Topics continue.)*

Rudra means रौति — स्तनयित्नुशब्दं करोतीति रुद्रः । (*rauti — stanayitnuśabdaṃ karotīti rudraḥ |*) (he who makes the sound of thunder is Rudra): because he sounds like the rumble of a cloud, he is named Rudra. Or रोरूयमाणो द्रवति (*rorūyamāṇo dravati*): he who runs about in the midst of the cloud, making sound. Or रोदयतेर्वा (*rodayatervā*): he who so acts that enemies weep, and makes them weep: this is the meaning given. Again यदरुदत् तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वं (*yadarudat tadrudrasya rudratvaṃ*) ("because he wept, that is Rudra's Rudra-hood"): following the famous story in the Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā, that when he was pierced by arrows and fell, this one saw his father Prajāpati and wept in distress; or following the idea यदरोदीत् तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वं (*yadarodīt tadrudrasya rudratvaṃ*) belonging to the Maitrāyaṇīya branch, the etymology of the word Rudra is given thus: because he wept (*rodana*), this deity is named Rudra (Ni. 10-2). In explaining the word Rudra Sāyaṇa has spoken somewhat differently: because at the time of dissolution he makes everyone weep; or because he destroys the sorrow called *saṃsāra*; or because he is taught by the Upaniṣads in the form of sound; or because he teaches the knowledge of the Self to those who worship that knowledge; or because he destroys the ignorance that covers knowledge, as a cataract covers light: following these differences of meaning of the word *rud*, he has explained the word Rudra with the name suiting this deity. This etymology of the word Rudra and its various meanings have been explained, according to the contexts, in the Ṛg. Saṃ. Part 5 page 589, Part 6 page 350, Part 9 page 101,

*(p. 403 ends here; the sentence continues on p. 404.)*

### Printed p. 404 (PDF 424)

*(Header: "Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 1". Ṛk 6, Special Topics continue.)*

Part 10 page 379; Part 13 page 541, in these places.

असुरः — शत्रूणां निरसिता । (*asuraḥ — śatrūṇāṃ nirasitā |*) ("Asura: the expeller of enemies".) This is an epithet, both for Agni and for the word Rudra, in the sense "one who rebukes enemies". Or असुर्बलं तस्य दाता आदित्यरूपश्च त्वमसि (*asurbalaṃ tasya dātā ādityarūpaśca tvamasi*): *asu* means strength; "you are of the form of Āditya, the giver of that strength": so Agni is praised. The Asura-hood of Agni relating to the heavenly world is in

> उत वा दिवो असुराय मन्म प्रान्धांसीव यज्यवे भरध्वं ।

> *uta vā divo asurāya manma prāndhāṃsīva yajyave bharadhvaṃ |*

"Or bring a hymn for the Asura of heaven, like food(-offerings), for the one to be worshipped" (mine and tentative; the third word read as printed, zoomed). (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-41-3.) The word Asura is a synonym of Rākṣasa in the Purāṇas and elsewhere. But in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā this word is used in various senses: *asu* means breath, intelligence, throwing, and so on; so the word Asura has been used according to those senses. These must be construed according to the context.

> बृहच्छ्रवा असुरो बर्हणा कृतः पुरो हरिभ्यां वृषभो रथो हि षः ।

> *bṛhacchravā asuro barhaṇā kṛtaḥ puro haribhyāṃ vṛṣabho ratho hi ṣaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-54-3; gloss, mine and tentative: "the far-famed Asura, … made before him with the two bay horses; he is the bull, the chariot".) In this Ṛk the word Asura is an epithet of Indra. Here also, as said in this Ṛk, असुरः — शत्रूणां निरसिता (*asuraḥ — śatrūṇāṃ nirasitā*) is one sense, and यद्वा असुः प्राणो बलं वा तद्वान् । रो मत्वर्थीयः । अथवा असवः प्राणाः तेन च आपो लक्ष्यंते । तान् दाति ददातीति असुरः । (*yadvā asuḥ prāṇo balaṃ vā tadvān | ro matvarthīyaḥ | athavā asavaḥ prāṇāḥ tena ca āpo lakṣyaṃte | tān dāti dadātīti asuraḥ |*) is another: either one possessing breath or strength (*ra* being the possessive suffix), or *asavaḥ* means breaths, and by that waters are indicated; he who gives them is Asura, the rain-giving Indra. Because Indra has many such powers, the word can be an epithet of Indra in all these senses. Likewise:

> क्षयन्नस्मभ्यमसुर प्रचेता राजन्नेनांसि शिश्रथः कृतानि ।

> *kṣayannasmabhyamasura pracetā rājannenāṃsi śiśrathaḥ kṛtāni |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-14.) In this Ṛk Varuṇa is given the epithet Asura, as the destroyer of what is undesirable (अनिष्टक्षेपणशीलः (*aniṣṭakṣepaṇaśīlaḥ*)). In the same sense:

> त्वमग्ने रुद्रो असुरो महो दिवस्त्वं शर्धो मारुतं पृक्ष ईशिषे ।

> *tvamagne rudro asuro maho divastvaṃ śardho mārutaṃ pṛkṣa īśiṣe |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-6.) In this very Ṛk, the word Asura is used as an epithet of Agni or Rudra in the sense of "one who casts out enemies".

> वि सुपर्णो अंतरिक्षाण्यख्यद्गभीरवेपा असुरः सुनीथः ।

> *vi suparṇo aṃtarikṣāṇyakhyadgabhīravepā asuraḥ sunīthaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-35-7.) In this Ṛk, असुरः — असुं प्राणं राति ददातीत्यसुरः आदित्यः । (*asuraḥ — asuṃ prāṇaṃ rāti dadātītyasuraḥ ādityaḥ |*) ("he gives breath: the Āditya") means Sūrya, the giver of life (of consciousness).

> पृषद्योनिः पंचहोता शृणोत्वतूर्तपंथा असुरो मयोभुः ।

> *pṛṣadyoniḥ paṃcahotā śṛṇotvatūrtapaṃthā asuro mayobhuḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-42-1.) In this Ṛk, as explained before, the giver of life, Vāyu, is meant.

> अस्मे वीरो मरुतः शुष्म्यस्तु जनानां यो असुरो विधर्ता ॥

> *asme vīro marutaḥ śuṣmyastu janānāṃ yo asuro vidhartā ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-56-24.) In this Ṛk the word Asura has the meaning "possessed of wisdom".

> शतं कक्ष्रीवाँ[?] असुरस्य गोनां दिवि श्रवोऽजरमा ततान ।

> *śataṃ kakṣrīvā~[?] asurasya gonāṃ divi śravo 'jaramā tatāna |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-126-2; the second word read as printed, zoomed, doubtful.) Here "of the Asura of cows" is explained as "of the generous one who gives cows".

> त्रिरुत्तमा दूणशा रोचनानि त्रयो राजंत्यसुरस्य वीराः ।

> *triruttamā dūṇaśā rocanāni trayo rājaṃtyasurasya vīrāḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-56-8.) Here the gloss अस्यति क्षिपति सर्वमित्यसुरः कालात्मा संवत्सरः (*asyati kṣipati sarvamityasuraḥ kālātmā saṃvatsaraḥ*) ("one who casts everything: the Asura is Time, the year") is used with the sense of time.

*(Ṛk 6 is left open; the text continues on p. 405.)*

### Printed p. 405 (PDF 425)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 18" [as read from the strip, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 18], "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Ṛk 6, Special Topics, continued; the words Asura/Sura/Aditi/Diti.)*

> यथा रुद्रस्य सूनवो दिवो वशंत्यसुरस्य वेधसः ।

> *yathā rudrasya sūnavo divo vaśaṃtyasurasya vedhasaḥ |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-20-17.) In this Ṛk the word *asurasya* is used in the sense of "cloud" (*megha*).

> अनायुधासो असुरा अदेवाश्चक्रेण ता अप वप ऋजीषिन् ।

> *anāyudhāso asurā adevāścakreṇa tā apa vapa ṛjīṣin |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-96-9.) In such Ṛks Asuras means Daityas belonging to the company of Rākṣasas. In the Ṛk in hand it means the Agni, or Rudra, who casts out the enemies, the Rākṣasas. In the Purāṇas and so on, and in modern Sanskrit, the sense that *sura* means a deity and *asura* a Rākṣasa, a non-deity, is current. But the word *asura* was not formed as the negation of the word *sura*. The word *asura* itself was current in the Vedas (and among them in the Ṛgveda), and afterwards, by loss of the *a*, the word *sura*, which suggests the contrary sense, came into use. In the same way the word *aditi* was current, and afterwards, by loss of the *a*, the word *diti* came into use. *Aditi* means the mother of the gods, the mother of the deities; and *diti*, the opposite of that, came into use for the mother of the Rākṣasas.

मारुतं शर्धः—मरुत्समूहरूपं बलमसि । वायुरूपश्च त्वमसीत्यर्थः । (mārutaṃ śardhaḥ (*mārutaṃ śardhaḥ*) — "you are strength in the form of the Maruts' multitude; you are also of the form of Vāyu".) Kannada: "Or you are the combined-strength form of the (forty-nine) Marut deities [the numeral printed as "೪೯"; read from the strip, not zoomed]; the combined strength of the Maruts is wonderful. In describing this strength the expression *mārutaṃ śardhaḥ* is the customary one."

> इंद्रं मित्रं वरुणमग्निमूतये मारुतं शर्धो अदितिं हवामहे ।

> *iṃdraṃ mitraṃ varuṇamagnimūtaye mārutaṃ śardho aditiṃ havāmahe |*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-106-1.) In such Ṛks, in speaking of the Marut deities or of their combined strength, the words *mārutaṃ śardhaḥ* are used.

पृक्ष ईशिषे—अन्नस्य हविर्लक्षणस्य त्वमीश्वरो भवसि । (pṛkṣa īśiṣe (*pṛkṣa īśiṣe*) — "you are the lord of food, whose mark is the oblation".) The word *pṛkṣaḥ* is read among the names of food (Nir. 3-9). Agni is described as the lord of food, whether in the form of the oblation or of nourishment.

त्वं वातैररुणैर्यासि शंगयः—त्वं वातैर्वायुसदृशैररुणैरश्वैः शंगयः सुखस्य गृहरूप आवासभूतः सन् यासि प्राप्नोषि योग्यगृहं । (tvaṃ vātairaruṇairyāsi śaṃgayaḥ (*tvaṃ vātairaruṇairyāsi śaṃgayaḥ*) — "you go, as the dwelling of happiness, with ruddy horses like the winds, to the house".) Kannada: "O Agni, you, with horses ruddy in colour and swift as the wind (that is, seated in a chariot yoked with horses), being one whose dwelling is happiness, come to our sacrificial house" — continued on p. 406. *(The Sanskrit is given as printed; the first words differ slightly from the Saṃhitā of the Ṛk, read as printed.)*

(Kannada, continued:) "…the sense is that you come." यद्वा अरुण्यैर्गमनशीलैर्वायुभिरुत्पन्नः सन् यासि वने । (yadvā aruṇyairgamanaśīlairvāyubhirutpannaḥ san yāsi vane (*yadvā aruṇyairgamanaśīlairvāyubhirutpannaḥ san yāsi vane*) — "or, born of the swift winds, you go in the forest".) Kannada: "Or: being born in the forest from constantly moving or blowing wind, you grow and flourish; this too may be the sense."

पूषा—सर्वस्य पोषकः । (pūṣā (*pūṣā*) — "nourisher of all".) Agni, the nourisher of all, or the well-known deity called Pūṣan: you are of such a divine nature.

नु—क्षिप्रं । (nu (*nu*) — "quickly".) "Swiftly. Yāska has said that the word *nu* has many kinds of meaning (Nir. 1-4), *nu ityeṣo 'nekakarmā*. The word is used also in giving a reason and in the sense of comparison. Here *kṣipraṃ*, quickly, is the sense."

त्मना विधतः पासि—आत्मना, अनुग्रहरूपया स्वबुद्ध्यैव विधतः परिचरतो यजमानान् पासि । (tmanā vidhataḥ pāsi (*tmanā vidhataḥ pāsi*) — "by yourself, by your own gracious mind, you protect the sacrificers who serve you".) Kannada: "The long *ā* of *ātmanā* is dropped for the convenience of the metre, giving *tmanā*. Generally in the Ṛgveda, wherever the word *ātmanā* would be expected, the word *tmanā* is used. With your own gracious mind, protect the sacrificers who serve you: thus Agni is prayed."

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वम॑ग्ने द्रविणो॒दा अ॑रं॒कृते॒ त्वं दे॒वः स॑वि॒ता र॑त्न॒धा अ॑सि ।

> *tvamagne draviṇodā araṃkṛte tvaṃ devaḥ savitā ratnadhā asi |*

> त्वं भगो नृपते वस्व ईशिषे त्वं पायुर्दमो यस्तेऽविधत् ॥ ७ ॥

> *tvaṃ bhago nṛpate vasva īśiṣe tvaṃ pāyurdamo yaste 'vidhat ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वं । अग्ने । द्रविणःऽदाः । अरम्ऽकृते । त्वं । देवः । सविता । रत्नऽधाः । असि ।
> त्वं । भगः । नृऽपते । वस्वः । ईशिषे । त्वं । पायुः । दमः । यः । ते । अविधत् ॥ ७ ॥

> *tvaṃ | agne | draviṇaḥ 'dāḥ | aram 'kṛte | tvaṃ | devaḥ | savitā | ratna 'dhāḥ | asi |*
> *tvaṃ | bhagaḥ | nṛ 'pate | vasvaḥ | īśiṣe | tvaṃ | pāyuḥ | damaḥ | yaḥ | te | avidhat ‖ 7 ‖*

*(The Pada is printed "दमो", as the Saṃhitā; read as printed. The Pada's avagraha strokes are printed as small "ऽ".)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Agni gives wealth to the sacrificer who adorns him, is Savitṛ the impeller, lord of wealth as Bhaga, and protector of whoever serves him in the house.

> हे अग्ने त्वमरंकृते त्वामलंकुर्वते यजमानाय द्रविणोदाः । हिरण्यस्य दाताऽसि । देवो द्योतमानः सविता सर्वस्य सत्कर्मसु प्रेरकस्त्वं रत्नधा रमणीयानां धनानां मणिमुक्तादीनां धारयितासि ।

> *he agne tvamaraṃkṛte tvāmalaṃkurvate yajamānāya draviṇodāḥ | hiraṇyasya dātā 'si | devo dyotamānaḥ savitā sarvasya satkarmasu prerakastvaṃ ratnadhā ramaṇīyānāṃ dhanānāṃ maṇimuktādīnāṃ dhārayitāsi |*

### Printed p. 407 (PDF 427)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 18" [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 18], "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Ṛk 7: bhāṣya concluded, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics begun.)*

> तथा हे नृपते नृणां पालकाग्ने त्वं भगो भजनीयः सन् वस्वो वसुनो धनस्यैशिषे । समर्थो भवसि दातुं । यो यजमानो दमो यज्ञगृहे ते त्वामविधत् परिचरति तस्य पायुः पालकस्त्वमसि ॥

> *tathā he nṛpate nṛṇāṃ pālakāgne tvaṃ bhago bhajanīyaḥ san vasvo vasuno dhanasyaiśiṣe | samartho bhavasi dātuṃ | yo yajamāno damo yajñagṛhe te tvāmavidhat paricarati tasya pāyuḥ pālakastvamasi ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; अरंकृते (*araṃkṛte*) — to the sacrificer who adorns you; द्रविणोदाः (*draviṇodāḥ*) — you are the giver of gold and the like; रत्नधाः त्वं (*ratnadhāḥ tvaṃ*) — you who hold beautiful jewels, pearls and the like; देवः सविता (*devaḥ savitā*) — you are Savitṛ, the impeller of all actions and of divine nature; असि (*asi*) — you are; नृपते (*nṛpate*) — O Agni, protector of all men; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; भगः (*bhagaḥ*) — as the worshipful Bhaga; वस्वः (*vasvaḥ*) — over wealth; ईशिषे (*īśiṣe*) — you are lord; यः (*yaḥ*) — whichever sacrificer; दमो (*damo*) — in the sacrificial house; ते (*te*) — you; अविधत् (*avidhat*) — serves; his; पायुः (*pāyuḥ*) — as protector; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you (are).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, you are the giver of gold and the like to the sacrificer who adorns you. You, who hold beautiful jewels, pearls and the like, are Savitṛ, the impeller of all actions and of divine nature. O Agni, protector of all men, you, as the worshipful Bhaga, are lord over wealth. You are the protector of the sacrificer who serves you in the sacrificial house.

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

You, Agni, are Dravinodas, to him who honours you : you are the divine Savitri, the possessor of precious things : protector of men, you are Bhaga and rule over wealth ; you are the cherisher of him who worships you in his dwelling.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

द्रविणोदाः (draviṇodāḥ (*draviṇodāḥ*)) — Yāska has written an extended explanation of this word:

> द्रविणोदाः । द्रविणोदाः कस्माद्धनं द्रविणमुच्यते । यदेनदभिद्रवंति । बलं वा द्रविणं यदेनेनाभिद्रवंति । तस्य दाता द्रविणोदाः ।

> *draviṇodāḥ | draviṇodāḥ kasmāddhanaṃ draviṇamucyate | yadenadabhidravaṃti | balaṃ vā draviṇaṃ yadenenābhidravaṃti | tasya dātā draviṇodāḥ |*

(Nir. 8-1.) Here the derivation of the word *draviṇodāḥ* is द्रविणं ददातीति द्रविणोदाः (draviṇaṃ dadātīti draviṇodāḥ (*draviṇaṃ dadātīti draviṇodāḥ*)). The word *draviṇa* has two meanings, wealth and strength. Therefore *draviṇodāḥ* means one who gives wealth, or strength… *(Special Topics break off at the foot of the page; Ṛk 7 is left open and continues on p. 408.)*

### Printed p. 408 (PDF 428)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 1". Ṛk 7, Special Topics on draviṇodāḥ continued.)*

(Kannada, continued:) "…one who gives; this is the etymological sense of the word. Besides, Yāska has given an explanation for the ṛk beginning *draviṇodā draviṇasaḥ* (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-15-7) as follows —"

> द्रविणोदा यस्त्वं । द्रविणस इति द्रविणसादिन इति वा द्रविणसानिन इति वा द्रविणसस्तस्मात् पिबत्विति वा । यज्ञेषु देवमीळते । याचंति स्तुवंति वर्धयंति पूजयंतीति वा ॥

> *draviṇodā yastvaṃ | draviṇasa iti draviṇasādina iti vā draviṇasānina iti vā draviṇasastasmāt pibatviti vā | yajñeṣu devamīḷate | yācaṃti stuvaṃti vardhayaṃti pūjayaṃtīti vā ‖*

Kannada: "That is, the ṛtvijs, who desire wealth, oblations and the like, pray that you, called Draviṇodāḥ, may drink Soma in the sacrifices; this is the principal sense. Here *draviṇodāḥ* is nominative singular; how then is it an adjective of *devaṃ*, which is accusative singular? The words must be supplied (*adhyāhāra*) so that the sense is *draviṇodā yaḥ devaḥ taṃ devaṃ*, 'that god who is the giver of wealth'. *Draviṇasaḥ* means those who, wishing wealth or oblations for the worship of deities, pray to the god; therefore the word *draviṇasaḥ* means ṛtvijs. And *īḷate* may be said to have many meanings: they ask, praise, extol, worship."

> तत्को द्रविणोदा इंद्र इति क्रौष्टुकिः । स बलधनयोर्दातृतमस्तस्य च सर्वा बलकृतिः ॥

> *tatko draviṇodā iṃdra iti krauṣṭukiḥ | sa baladhanayordātṛtamastasya ca sarvā balakṛtiḥ ‖*

Kannada: "Now, that has told the etymological sense of the word *draviṇodāḥ*. But who is the deity called *draviṇodāḥ*? Indra himself is called *draviṇodāḥ*; for he is the one who gives most abundantly what the word *draviṇa* denotes, strength and wealth. Therefore Indra alone is to be called *draviṇodāḥ*: such is the view of Krauṣṭuki."

> अथाप्यग्निं द्रविणोदसमाह्यैष पुनरेतस्माज्जायते । यो अश्मनोरंतरग्निं जजान इत्यपि निगमो भवति ॥

> *athāpyagniṃ draviṇodasamāhyaiṣa punaretasmājjāyate | yo aśmanoraṃtaragniṃ jajāna ityapi nigamo bhavati ‖*

Kannada: "And they give another sense for this word. Indra created heaven and earth, and created Agni between them. Therefore Agni too may be called *draviṇodāḥ*; to support this sense the ṛk 'aśmanoraṃtaragniṃ jajāna' is given as an example."

> अथास्यर्तुयाजेषु द्रविणोदसः प्रवादा भवंति । तेषां पुनः पात्रस्येंद्रपानमिति भवति ॥ अथाप्येनं सोमपानेन स्तौति अथाप्याह द्रविणोदाः पिबतु द्रविणोदस इति ॥

*(Kannada continues on p. 409.)*

All this is the view of Krauṣṭuki."

> अयमेवाग्निर्द्रविणोदा इति शाकपूणिः । आग्नेयेष्वेव हि सूक्तेषु द्रविणोदसः प्रवादा भवंति ॥

> *ayamevāgnirdraviṇodā iti śākapūṇiḥ | āgneyeṣveva hi sūkteṣu draviṇodasaḥ pravādā bhavaṃti ‖*

Kannada: "It is the view of Śākapūṇi that Agni himself is *draviṇodāḥ*; for in the hymns addressed to Agni, when the ṛtvijs praise Agni, they use the word *draviṇodāḥ* as an epithet of Agni."

> यथो एतत्स बलधनयोर्दातृतमु इति सर्वासु देवतास्वैश्वर्यं विद्यते । यथो "एतदोजसो जातमुतमन्य एनं" इति चाहेत्ययमप्यग्निरोजसा बलेन मथ्यमानो जायते तस्मादेनमाह सहसस्पुत्रं सहसः सूनुं सहसो यहुम् ॥

> *yatho etatsa baladhanayordātṛtamu iti sarvāsu devatāsvaiśvaryaṃ vidyate | yatho "etadojaso jātamutamanya enaṃ" iti cāhetyayamapyagnirojasā balena mathyamāno jāyate tasmādenamāha sahasasputraṃ sahasaḥ sūnuṃ sahaso yahum ‖*

Kannada: "There is lordship in all deities. Therefore Agni too gives strength and wealth; since he gives strength and wealth, Agni too can be called *draviṇodāḥ*. Besides, the word *draviṇa* has only the meaning 'strength'. When Agni is produced, he is churned with strength, and so there is the saying that Agni is born of strength. For that very reason Agni is praised with the words *sahasaspuṭram* (*sahasaḥ*, of strength; *putram*, the son, that is Agni), *sahasaḥ sūnum*, *sahaso yahum*" — [the ṛks follow]:

> द्युन्नः [?] सर्पिरासुतिः प्रत्नो होता वरेण्यः । सहसस्पुत्रो अद्भुतः ॥

> *dyunnaḥ [?] sarpirāsutiḥ pratno hotā vareṇyaḥ | sahasasputro adbhutaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-7-6, as printed, zoomed; the file said 9-2-2 = FILE DISAGREE.) *(The first word is read as printed, uncertain.)*

> त्वं ह यद्यविष्ठ्य सहसः सूनवाहुत । ऋतावा यज्ञियो भुवः ॥

> *tvaṃ ha yadyaviṣṭhya sahasaḥ sūnavāhuta | ṛtāvā yajñiyo bhuvaḥ ‖*

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-75-3.)

> अग्ने वाजस्य गोमत ईशानः सहसो यहो । अस्मे धेहि जातवेदो महिश्रवः ॥

> *agne vājasya gomata īśānaḥ sahaso yaho | asme dhehi jātavedo mahiśravaḥ ‖*

#### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वाम॑ग्ने॒ दम॒ आ वि॒श्पतिं॒ विश॒स्त्वां राजा॑नं सुवि॒दत्र॑मृंजते ।

> *tvāmagne dama ā viśpatiṃ viśastvāṃ rājānaṃ suvidatramṛṃjate |*

> त्वं विश्वानि स्वनीक पत्यसे त्वं सहस्राणि शता दश प्रति ॥ ८ ॥

> *tvaṃ viśvāni svanīka patyase tvaṃ sahasrāṇi śatā daśa prati ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वां । अग्ने । दमो । आ । विश्पतिं । विशः । त्वां । राजानं । सुऽविदत्रं । ऋंजते ।
> त्वं । विश्वानि । सुऽअनीक । पत्यसे । त्वं । सहस्राणि । शता । दश । प्रति ॥ ८ ॥

> *tvāṃ | agne | damo | ā | viśpatiṃ | viśaḥ | tvāṃ | rājānaṃ | su 'vidatraṃ | ṛṃjate |*
> *tvaṃ | viśvāni | su 'anīka | patyase | tvaṃ | sahasrāṇi | śatā | daśa | prati ‖ 8 ‖*

*(Saṃhitā "दम आ", Pada "दमो", as printed.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* The sacrificers serve and adorn Agni, protector of the people, radiant and wise; he is master of all oblations and, in return, provides what is sought, in thousands, hundreds and tens.

> हे अग्ने विश्पतिं यजमानानां पालकं त्वां विशो यजमाना दमो स्वकीये यज्ञगृह आ । आसादयंति ॥ उपसर्गवशाद्योग्यक्रियाध्याहारः । तथा कृत्वा राजानं दीप्यमानं सुविदत्रं शोभनज्ञानमस्मदनुकूलचेतस्कं सुधनं वा त्वामृंजते । प्रसाधयंति ॥ ऋंजतिः प्रसाधनकर्मेति यास्कः ॥ यत एवं ततो हे स्वनीक शोभन-ज्वालारूपसेन त्वं विश्वानि सर्वाणि । हवींषीति शेषः ॥ षष्ठ्यर्थे द्वितीया । विश्वेषां हविषामाज्यसोमपुरोडाशादीनां पत्यसे । ईश्वरो भवसि ॥ ईश्वरनाम्नैतत् । इरज्यति पत्यत इति तन्नामसु पाठात् ॥ यद्वा पतिभावमाचरसि । त्वं तु सहस्राणि शता शतानि दश एतत्संख्यकानि प्रति । एतत्संख्यकानामभिमतसाधनानां प्रतिनिधिरित्यर्थः । प्रतिः प्रतिनिधिप्रतिदानयोरिति कर्मप्रवचनीयत्वं ॥ त्रैर्यत्फलं भवति तत्त्वया लभ्यत इत्यर्थः ॥

*(Its tail: the accusative in the sense of a genitive, the synonym of "lord" from the Nighaṇṭu, and *prati* as a karmapravacanīya; characterized, not explained.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; विश्पतिं (*viśpatiṃ*) — protector of the sacrificers; त्वां (*tvāṃ*) — you; विशः (*viśaḥ*) — the sacrificers; दमो (*damo*) — in their own sacrificial house; आ (*ā*) — serve; राजानं (*rājānaṃ*) — radiant; सुविदत्रं (*suvidatraṃ*) — one who has excellent knowledge or wealth; त्वां (*tvāṃ*) — you; ऋंजते (*ṛṃjate*) — adorn and worship; स्वनीक (*svanīka*) — O Agni, who have an army of the form of flames; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; विश्वानि (*viśvāni*) — to all oblations; पत्यसे (*patyase*) — you are lord; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; सहस्राणि (*sahasrāṇi*) — thousands in number; शता (*śatā*) — hundreds in number; दश (*daśa*) — tens in number, that is, of desired objects; प्रति (*prati*) — as a substitute, you are the one who accomplishes them for him.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Agni, the sacrificers serve you in their own sacrificial house. They adorn and worship you, who are radiant and possess excellent knowledge or wealth. You, who have flame-like… *(the Bhāvārtha breaks off at the foot of the page; Ṛk 8 is left open and continues on p. 411.)*

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 18", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Ṛk 8 continued: end of Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics.)*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)** *(continued from p. 410)*

(Kannada, continued:) "…army, O Agni, you are lord over all oblations. You, as the substitute for the desired objects numbering tens, hundreds and thousands, accomplish them and give them."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

The people adore you, Agni, the protector of the people in their dwellings ; they propitiate you as a benevolent sovereign ; leader of a radiant host, you are lord over all offerings ; you are the distributor of tens, and hundreds, and thousands (of good things).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

सुविदत्रं (*suvidatraṃ*) — this word is formed from the root विद ज्ञाने (*vida jñāne*) preceded by the prefix सु (*su*); it means "one who has good knowledge".

ऋंजते (*ṛṃjate*) — प्रसाधयंति (*prasādhayaṃti*): "they propitiate, they worship". Yāska has said in the Nirukta:

> ऋंजतिः प्रसाधनकर्मा । आ व ऋंजसे ऊर्जां व्युष्टिषु इत्यपि निगमो भवति ।

> *ṛṃjatiḥ prasādhanakarmā | ā va ṛṃjase ūrjāṃ vyuṣṭiṣu ityapi nigamo bhavati |*

(Nir. 6-21; the file agrees.)

विश्वानि पत्यसे (*viśvāni patyase*) — the bhāṣya says:

*Gist:* "Supply the word 'oblations'; the accusative has the sense of a genitive; so 'you are lord of all oblations'."

> विश्वानि पत्यसे — सर्वाणि हवींषीति शेषः । षष्ठ्यर्थे द्वितीया । विश्वेषां हविषामाज्यसोमपुरोडाशादीनां पत्यसे ईश्वरो भवसि ॥

> *viśvāni patyase — sarvāṇi havīṃṣīti śeṣaḥ | ṣaṣṭhyarthe dvitīyā | viśveṣāṃ haviṣāmājyasomapuroḍāśādīnāṃ patyase īśvaro bhavasi ‖*

Kannada: "Here the word हवींषि (*havīṃṣi*) must be supplied (*adhyāhāra*) along with the word विश्वानि (*viśvāni*), and the genitive must be understood for the accusative, say the bhāṣyakāra. Therefore विश्वानि (*viśvāni*) means oblations, ājya, soma, puroḍāśa and other sacrificial substances; पत्यसे (*patyase*) — 'you are the master'; thus Agni is praised. The word पत्यते (*patyate*) (पत्यसे (*patyase*) being the second person singular) is read among the four names of lordship beginning इरज्यति पत्यते (*irajyati patyate*) (Ni. 3-11; the file agrees); therefore पत्यसे (*patyase*) means 'you are lord'."

सहस्राणि शता दश प्रति (*sahasrāṇi śatā daśa prati*) — "Agni is praised as one who gives desired objects to the extent of tens, hundreds and thousands. Here, although प्रति (*prati*) is only a prefix, the word प्रतिनिधि (*pratinidhi*) ('substitute') suitable to it must be supplied. Or else the sense may be: 'you alone provide the many desired objects that are obtained from a thousand people'."

स्वनीक (*svanīka*) — शोभनज्वालारूपसेन (*śobhanajvālārūpasena*): "Fine flames are themselves Agni's army-form; that is, one who shines with luminous flames." This word is used with reference to Agni in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-6-6, 6-15-16, 7-1-23, 7-3-6 (the file agrees).

### Printed p. 412 (PDF 432)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 1". Ṛk 9: Saṃhitā, Pada, bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha begun.)*

#### Ṛk 9

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वाम॑ग्ने पि॒तर॑मि॒ष्टिभि॒र्नर॒स्त्वां भ्रा॒त्राय॒ शम्या॑ तनू॒रुचं॑ ।
> त्वं पु॒त्रो भ॑वसि॒ यस्तेऽवि॑ध॒त्त्वं सखा॑ सु॒शेवः॑ पास्य॒धृषः॑ ॥ ९ ॥

> *tvāmagne pitaramiṣṭibhirnarastvāṃ bhrātrāya śamyā tanūrucaṃ |*
> *tvaṃ putro bhavasi yaste 'vidhattvaṃ sakhā suśevaḥ pāsyadhṛṣaḥ ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वां । अग्ने । पितरं । इष्टिऽभिः । नरः । त्वां । भ्रात्राय । शम्या । तनूऽरुचं ।
> त्वं । पुत्रः । भवसि । यः । ते । अविधत् । त्वं । सखा । सुऽशेवः । पासि । अऽधृषः ॥ ९ ॥

> *tvāṃ | agne | pitaraṃ | iṣṭi 'bhiḥ | naraḥ | tvāṃ | bhrātrāya | śamyā | tanū 'rucaṃ |*
> *tvaṃ | putraḥ | bhavasi | yaḥ | te | avidhat | tvaṃ | sakhā | su 'śevaḥ | pāsi | a 'dhṛṣaḥ ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Leaders (sacrificers) worship Agni with offerings as father and with rites as brother; he is as a son to his servant, and as an unassailable kindly friend he protects.

> हे अग्ने पितरं पालकं त्वां नरो नेतारो यजमाना इष्टिभिरेषणसाधनैर्यागैर्यजंते इति शेषः । पितृवत्पालनाय यजंते इत्यर्थः । तथा तनूरुचं शरीराणां दीपकं शरीरेषु दीप्यमानं वैश्वानरात्मना त्वां भ्रात्राय भ्रातृत्वाय सौभ्रात्राय शम्या ॥ कर्मनामैतत् ॥ कर्मणा यजंते इति शेषः । यद्वोभयत्र वक्ष्यमाणेनाविधदित्यनेन संबंधः । हे अग्ने यो नरस्ते त्वामविधत् परिचरति तस्य त्वं पुत्रो भवसि । पुत्रवत्पालयिता भवसि । तथा त्वं सखा समानख्यानः सखिवद्धितकारी सुशेवः ॥ शेवमिति सुखनाम ॥ सुष्ठु सुखकारी सन् अधृषः अधर्षकात्मा पासि । रक्षसि । पितृत्वकामाय पितृत्वेन भ्रातृत्वकामाय भ्रातृत्वेन पुत्रत्वकामाय पुत्रस्थानीयो भवसि । त्रिप्रकारेण रक्षसीत्यर्थः ॥

> *he agne pitaraṃ pālakaṃ tvāṃ naro netāro yajamānā iṣṭibhireṣaṇasādhanairyāgairyajaṃte iti śeṣaḥ | pitṛvatpālanāya yajaṃte ityarthaḥ | tathā tanūrucaṃ śarīrāṇāṃ dīpakaṃ śarīreṣu dīpyamānaṃ vaiśvānarātmanā tvāṃ bhrātrāya bhrātṛtvāya saubhrātrāya śamyā ‖ karmanāmaitat ‖ karmaṇā yajaṃte iti śeṣaḥ | yadvobhayatra vakṣyamāṇenāvidhadityanena saṃbaṃdhaḥ | he agne yo naraste tvāmavidhat paricarati tasya tvaṃ putro bhavasi | putravatpālayitā bhavasi | tathā tvaṃ sakhā samānakhyānaḥ sakhivaddhitakārī suśevaḥ ‖ śevamiti sukhanāma ‖ suṣṭhu sukhakārī san adhṛṣaḥ adharṣakātmā pāsi | rakṣasi | pitṛtvakāmāya pitṛtvena bhrātṛtvakāmāya bhrātṛtvena putratvakāmāya putrasthānīyo bhavasi | triprakāreṇa rakṣasītyarthaḥ ‖*

*(Its tail: the explanation of शेव (*śeva*) as a name for happiness, and the threefold protection; characterized, not explained.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; पितरं (*pitaraṃ*) — the protector; त्वां (*tvāṃ*) — you; नरः (*naraḥ*) — the sacrificers; इष्टिभिः (*iṣṭibhiḥ*) — with sacrifices and the like (they worship you as one worships a father); तनूरुचं (*tanūrucaṃ*) — you who give lustre to the body; त्वां (*tvāṃ*) — you; शम्या (*śamyā*) — with rites; भ्रात्राय (*bhrātrāya*) — they attend you as a brother; यः (*yaḥ*) — whichever sacrificer; ते (*te*) — you; अविधत् (*avidhat*) — attends (to him); त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; पुत्रः (*putraḥ*) — as a son; भवसि (*bhavasi*) — you become; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; सखा (*sakhā*) — like a friend; सुशेवः (*suśevaḥ*) — being a giver of happiness; अधृषः (*adhṛṣaḥ*) — and being attached (to us) [as printed]; पासि (*pāsi*) — you protect.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada:) "O Agni, the sacrificers attend you, the protector, with sacrifices and similar rites as a father, and you, who give lustre to the body, as a brother. For the sacrificer who attends you, you are a benefactor in the form of a son. You protect, attached like a friend and being a giver of happiness…" *(continues on p. 413 with: "…you protect, being attached like a friend and being a giver of happiness.")*

### Printed p. 413 (PDF 433)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 18", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Ṛk 9 concluded; Ṛk 10 Saṃhitā begins.)*

(Bhāvārtha concluded, Kannada:) "…to the sacrificer who attends you, you are a benefactor in the form of a son; you protect, being attached like a friend and being a giver of happiness."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

(Devout) men (worship) you, Agni, as a father, with secred [sic] rites; they (cherish) you, who are the illuminator of the body, with acts (of kindness), as a brother ; you are as a son to him who propitiates you, and you protect us, a faithful and firm friend.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

Kannada: "In this Ṛk Agni is praised with the words father, brother, son and friend, which indicate affection and trust —"

पितरं (*pitaraṃ*) — पालकं (*pālakaṃ*): "one who protects people like a father. The use of the word 'father' here indicates the affection and trust that Agni has toward the people who worship him."

तनूरुचं (*tanūrucaṃ*) —

> तनूरुचं — शरीराणां दीपकं, शरीरेषु दीप्यमानं वैश्वानरात्मना ।

> *tanūrucaṃ — śarīrāṇāṃ dīpakaṃ, śarīreṣu dīpyamānaṃ vaiśvānarātmanā |*

Kannada: "One who shines in the bodies of living beings in the form of heat. The heat that is in the body of living beings is itself the form of Agni. The digestion of food and other nourishment in the stomach is also Agni's work. Agni who exists in such a form is named Vaiśvānara Agni."

त्वं पुत्रो भवसि यस्तेऽविधत् (*tvaṃ putro bhavasi yaste 'vidhat*) — "Whichever man attends you with sacrifices and the like, to that man you are dear and protecting like a son; this is the sense."

त्वं सखा सुशेवः पासि अधृषः (*tvaṃ sakhā suśevaḥ pāsi adhṛṣaḥ*) — "Making happiness, that is, wishing welfare, you protect us like a friend. That is, you, Agni, protect us in manifold ways, like a father, like a brother, like a son and like a friend; this is the chief sense."

#### Ṛk 10

*(Saṃhitā only on this page; the glyph in "नमस्य[?]स्त्वं" between "स्य" and "स्त्वं" is not clear in the image, and the word is written here without it.)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वम॑ग्न ऋ॒भुरा॒के न॑म॒स्य१॒॑स्त्वं वाज॑स्य क्षु॒मतो॑ रा॒य ई॑शिषे ।
> त्वं वि भा॒स्यनु॑ दक्षि दा॒वने॒ त्वं वि॒शिक्षु॑रसि य॒ज्ञमा॒तनिः॑ ॥ १० ॥

> *tvamagna ṛbhurāke namasyastvaṃ vājasya kṣumato rāya īśiṣe |*
> *tvaṃ vi bhāsyanu dakṣi dāvane tvaṃ viśikṣurasi yajñamātaniḥ ‖ 10 ‖*

### Printed p. 414 (PDF 434)

*(Header: "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 1". Ṛk 10 continued: Pada, bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha.)*

*(Note on the Saṃhitā written on p. 413: the Pada below prints the last syllable of the word after "नमस्य" as a plain visarga, so the word is नमस्यः and the Saṃhitā reads "नमस्यस्त्वं". The unclear glyph flagged on p. 413 is therefore a visarga. The Pada also prints "धक्षि", not "दक्षि", for the word written "दक्षि" in the Saṃhitā on p. 413; the bhāṣya below also has "धक्षि". The p. 413 text is closed and is not altered here. The Saṃhitā reading should be धक्षि.)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वं । अग्ने । ऋभुः । आके । नमस्यः । त्वं । वाजस्य । क्षुऽमतः । रायः । ईशिषे ।
> त्वं । वि । भासि । अनु । धक्षि । दावने । त्वं । विऽशिक्षुः । असि । यज्ञं । आऽतनिः ॥ १० ॥

> *tvaṃ | agne | ṛbhuḥ | āke | namasyaḥ | tvaṃ | vājasya | kṣu 'mataḥ | rāyaḥ | īśiṣe |*
> *tvaṃ | vi | bhāsi | anu | dhakṣi | dāvane | tvaṃ | vi 'śikṣuḥ | asi | yajñaṃ | ā 'taniḥ ‖ 10 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Agni, near and visible, is to be saluted; he is lord of renowned food and wealth; he shines, burns the fuel, and as accomplisher of the sacrifice gives its fruit widely.

> हे अग्ने त्वमृभुः । उरुभासमानो मेधावी वा । त्वमाकेऽन्तिके सन्निधावेव नमस्यो नमस्कार्यः । स्तुत्य इत्यर्थः । इतरदेवतावन्मंत्रप्रतिपाद्याकारेण स्तुत्यो न भवसि किंतु प्रत्यक्ष इत्यर्थः । तथा त्वं क्षुमतः शब्दवतः सर्वत्र श्रूयमाणस्य वाजस्यान्नस्य रायो धनस्य चेशिषे । स्वामी भवसि । अतस्तद्देहीत्यर्थः । हे अग्ने त्वं विभासि । विशेषेण दीप्यसे । तदर्थमनुक्रमेणैव धक्षि । दहसि काष्ठादीन् ॥ दहेर्लटि सिपि रूपं । संहितायां भष्भावाभावश्छांदसः ॥ किमर्थमेवं । दावने छेदनायांधकारस्य । यद्वा हविषो दानवते यजमानाय वा । किंच त्वं यज्ञं विशिक्षुर्विशेषेण शिक्षयिता साधयितासि ॥ न लोकाव्ययेति षष्ठ्याः निषेधः ॥ तथातनिः फलस्य सर्वतो विस्तारयिता ॥

> *he agne tvamṛbhuḥ | urubhāsamāno medhāvī vā | tvamāke 'ntike sannidhāveva namasyo namaskāryaḥ | stutya ityarthaḥ | itaradevatāvanmaṃtrapratipādyākāreṇa stutyo na bhavasi kiṃtu pratyakṣa ityarthaḥ | tathā tvaṃ kṣumataḥ śabdavataḥ sarvatra śrūyamāṇasya vājasyānnasya rāyo dhanasya ceśiṣe | svāmī bhavasi | atastaddehītyarthaḥ | he agne tvaṃ vibhāsi | viśeṣeṇa dīpyase | tadarthamanukrameṇaiva dhakṣi | dahasi kāṣṭhādīn ‖ daherlaṭi sipi rūpaṃ | saṃhitāyāṃ bhaṣbhāvābhāvaśchāṃdasaḥ ‖ kimarthamevaṃ | dāvane chedanāyāṃdhakārasya | yadvā haviṣo dānavate yajamānāya vā | kiṃca tvaṃ yajñaṃ viśikṣurviśeṣeṇa śikṣayitā sādhayitāsi ‖ na lokāvyayeti ṣaṣṭhyāḥ niṣedhaḥ ‖ tathātaniḥ phalasya sarvato vistārayitā ‖*

*(Its tail: the form of the root दह् (*dah*) in the present tense, second person singular; the Vedic absence of the change of the aspirate in the Saṃhitā; and the prohibition of the genitive by a sūtra beginning "na lokāvyaya…". Characterized, not explained. The sūtra number is not printed.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; ऋभुः (*ṛbhuḥ*) — you are one who shines exceedingly (or: you are intelligent); आके (*āke*) — even while you are near and visible; नमस्यः (*namasyaḥ*) — one worthy of being worshipped; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; क्षुमतः (*kṣumataḥ*) — widely renowned; वाजस्य (*vājasya*) — of food; रायः (*rāyaḥ*) — of wealth; ईशिषे (*īśiṣe*) — you are lord (O lord); त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; वि भासि (*vi bhāsi*) — you blaze exceedingly; दावने (*dāvane*) — for the driving away of darkness, or for the sacrificer who offers oblation; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; अनु धक्षि (*anu dhakṣi*) — you burn fuel and the like; यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*) — the sacrifice; विशिक्षुः (*viśikṣuḥ*) — one who accomplishes it in a special manner; असि (*asi*) — you are (so); आतनिः (*ātaniḥ*) — you are also the giver of its fruit to that sacrifice.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada:) "O Agni, you shine exceedingly. You are worthy of being worshipped even while you are near and visible. You are lord over the renowned food and wealth. You, who blaze exceedingly, burn fuel and the like for the sacrificer who offers oblations. You accomplish the sacrifice in a special manner and are also the giver of its fruit."

### Printed p. 415 (PDF 435)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 18", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". The English translation of Ṛk 10, then Special Topics. The file's header row was garbled ("2.8"); the strip shows the usual A. 2 A. 5 Va. 18.)*

**English Translation** *(as printed; heading printed "Englih Tranlation" [sic])*

You, Agni, are (ever) resplendent, and are to be glorified when present ; you are lord over all renowned food and riches ; you shine brightly, and you consume (the oblation) for him who offers it ; you are the especial accomplisher of the sacrfice [sic, as it appears; the print is blurred], and bestower (of its rewards).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

ऋभुः (*ṛbhuḥ*) — उरुभासमानो मेधावी वा (*urubhāsamāno medhāvī vā*). (Kannada:) "'Shining abundantly, or intelligent (possessing understanding)' is Sāyaṇa's explanation. One may also say, if one wishes, that it is the form of the deity named Ṛbhu, but the meaning Sāyaṇa has given is the apt one here."

आके नमस्यः (*āke namasyaḥ*) — (Kannada:) "The word आके (*āke*) is read among the names of 'near' (Ni. 3-9) and also among the names of 'far' (Ni. 3-20). Here Sāyaṇa says:"

*Gist:* "Worthy of salutation because he is near and present; unlike other deities he is not praised only by what the mantras set forth, but is visible."

> अंतिके सन्निधावेव नमस्यो नमस्कार्यः स्तुत्य इत्यर्थः । इतरदेवतावन्मंत्रप्रतिपाद्याकारेण स्तुत्यो न भवसि किंतु प्रत्यक्ष इत्यर्थः ।

> *aṃtike sannidhāveva namasyo namaskāryaḥ stutya ityarthaḥ | itaradevatāvanmaṃtrapratipādyākāreṇa stutyo na bhavasi kiṃtu pratyakṣa ityarthaḥ |*

(Kannada:) "The other deities are not visible to our eyes; they are far away. Therefore, according to the śruti sentence परोक्षं वा अन्ये ते वा इज्यंते (*parokṣaṃ vā anye te vā ijyaṃte*) (as printed; Tai. Saṃ. 1-2-3-1 [?]) they have to be worshipped indirectly, by hymns and the like. But the case of Agni is not so. Since Agni is visible directly, right near us, we not only praise him with hymns and the like but also make salutation to him who is facing us. Therefore the use here of the words अंतिके (*aṃtike*) and नमस्यः (*namasyaḥ*) is appropriate in relation to Agni."

त्वं वाजस्य क्षुमतः राय ईशिषे (*tvaṃ vājasya kṣumataḥ rāya īśiṣe*) — (Kannada:) "क्षुमतः (*kṣumataḥ*) means 'making sound', that is, 'that which everyone is asking for, wanting it'. O Agni, you are lord over the food that all ask for and over riches and other wealth; this is the meaning."

त्वं वि भासि अनु धक्षि दावने (*tvaṃ vi bhāsi anu dhakṣi dāvane*) — (Kannada:) "I shine for the sacrificer who offers oblations; and burning the fuel and the like that are offered in the fire, and the oblation, ghee and so on [reading of the first word printed "पवि/हवि" doubtful], I blaze well for the sacrificer's attainment of satisfaction; this is the meaning."

त्वं विशिक्षुः असि यज्ञं (*tvaṃ viśikṣuḥ asi yajñaṃ*) — (Kannada:) "One who tells the sacrificer and the priests, so that they understand it well, the rites to be performed one after another in the sacrifice. Since you know well the duties of the hotṛ, adhvaryu and the others, you teach them the sacrificial procedure; this is the meaning."

आतनिः (*ātaniḥ*) — फलस्य सर्वतो विस्तारयिता (*phalasya sarvato vistārayitā*) — (Kannada:) "One who gives abundantly the fruits to be obtained from sacrificial acts; this is the meaning."

#### Ṛk 11

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वम॑ग्ने॒ अदि॑तिर्देव दा॒शुषे॒ त्वं होत्रा॒ भार॑ती वर्धसे गि॒रा ।
> त्वमिळा॑ श॒तहि॑मासि॒ दक्ष॑से॒ त्वं वृ॑त्र॒हा व॑सुपते॒ सर॑स्वती ॥ ११ ॥

> *tvamagne aditirdeva dāśuṣe tvaṃ hotrā bhāratī vardhase girā |*
> *tvamiḷā śatahimāsi dakṣase tvaṃ vṛtrahā vasupate sarasvatī ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वं । अग्ने । अदितिः । देव । दाशुषे । त्वं । होत्रा । भारती । वर्धसे । गिरा ।
> त्वं । इळा । शतऽहिमा । असि । दक्षसे । त्वं । वृत्रऽहा । वसुऽपते । सरस्वती ॥ ११ ॥

> *tvaṃ | agne | aditiḥ | deva | dāśuṣe | tvaṃ | hotrā | bhāratī | vardhase | girā |*
> *tvaṃ | iḷā | śata 'himā | asi | dakṣase | tvaṃ | vṛtra 'hā | vasu 'pate | sarasvatī ‖ 11 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* To the sacrificer Agni is Aditi, the protector; he is Hotrā and Bhāratī, grows by praise; as eternal Iḷā (earth) he is able to give; as Sarasvatī he slays sin; the three goddesses are he.

> हे अग्ने देव त्वं दाशुषे हविर्दत्तवते यजमानायादितिरखंडयिता परिपालयितासि । यद्वा अदीना भूमिरसि । किंच त्वं होत्रा होमनिष्पादका भारती भरतस्यादित्यस्यादित्यसंबंधिनी रश्मिरूपा सती गिरा स्तुत्या वर्धसे । प्रवृद्धो भवसि । किंच त्वं शतहिमा । हिमशब्दः कालोपलक्षकः । अपरिमितकाला नित्येळा भूमिरसि । तादृशी सती दक्षसे दानाय समर्था भवसि ॥ तिज[?] उत्तरत्वादनिघातः ॥ तथा हे वसुपते धनपालक वृत्रहा पापादेर्हंता त्वं सरस्वती । सरणवान्वायुः । तत्संबंधिन्येतन्नियामुका माध्यमिकासि । आदित्याग्निवायूनां संबंधिन्यो भारतीळासरस्वत्याख्यायास्तिस्रो देव्यः संति ता अपि त्वमेवेत्यर्थः ॥

> *he agne deva tvaṃ dāśuṣe havirdattavate yajamānāyāditirakhaṃḍayitā paripālayitāsi | yadvā adīnā bhūmirasi | kiṃca tvaṃ hotrā homaniṣpādakā bhāratī bharatasyādityasyādityasaṃbaṃdhinī raśmirūpā satī girā stutyā vardhase | pravṛddho bhavasi | kiṃca tvaṃ śatahimā | himaśabdaḥ kālopalakṣakaḥ | aparimitakālā nityeḷā bhūmirasi | tādṛśī satī dakṣase dānāya samarthā bhavasi ‖ tija[?] uttaratvādanighātaḥ ‖ tathā he vasupate dhanapālaka vṛtrahā pāpāderhaṃtā tvaṃ sarasvatī | saraṇavānvāyuḥ | tatsaṃbaṃdhinyetanniyāmukā mādhyamikāsi | ādityāgnivāyūnāṃ saṃbaṃdhinyo bhāratīḷāsarasvatyākhyāyāstisro devyaḥ saṃti tā api tvamevetyarthaḥ ‖*

*(Its tail: a remark on the absence of the accent-lowering (*anighāta*) because of a following word, with a garbled opening word "तिज[?]"; characterized, not explained.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

देव (*deva*) — O one of divine nature; अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*) — to the sacrificer who offers oblation; अदितिः (*aditiḥ*) — you are Aditi, the complete protector; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; होत्रा (*hotrā*) — as Hotrā, the accomplisher of the homa; भारती (*bhāratī*) — as Bhāratī, related to the Āditya; गिरा (*girā*) — by praise; वर्धसे (*vardhase*) — you grow great; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; शतहिमा (*śatahimā*) — having a time of a hundred in number, that is, eternal; इळा (*iḷā*) — in the form of Iḷā; असि (*asi*) — you are (and further); दक्षसे (*dakṣase*) — you are capable of giving and the like; वसुपते (*vasupate*) — O Agni, protector of wealth; वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*) — slayer of sin and the like; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*) — (related to Vāyu); असि (*asi*) — you are also Sarasvatī.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada:) "O Agni of divine nature, to the sacrificer who offers oblations you are the completely protecting Aditi. You, as Hotrā, the accomplisher of the homa, and as Bhāratī, related to the Āditya, …" *(the Bhāvārtha breaks off at the foot of the page; Ṛk 11 is left open and continues on p. 417)*

### Printed p. 417 (PDF 437)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 19" read from the strip, "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". The Bhāvārtha of Ṛk 11 continues from p. 416; then the printed English, Special Topics and the closing line. The foot of the page carries the signature mark "[27]" and "Vol. 14.")*

*(Bhāvārtha of Ṛk 11, continued.)* (Kannada:) "…[and as Bhāratī,] you grow great through praise. You are in the form of the eternal Iḷā (the earth). And you are capable of giving and the like. O Agni, protector of wealth, you, the slayer of sin and the like, are also Sarasvatī, who is related to Vāyu."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

You, divine Agni, are Aditi to the donor of the oblation; you are Hotra and Bharati, and thrive by praise ; you are Ila of a hundred winters to him who makes you gifts ; you, lord of wealth, are the destroyer of Vritra, Saraswati.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

अदितिः (*aditiḥ*) —

*Gist:* Aditi is the undivided, uninterrupted protector, or the earth.

> अदितिः — अखंडयिता परिपालयितासि । यद्वा अदीना भूमिरसि ।

> *aditiḥ — akhaṃḍayitā paripālayitāsi | yadvā adīnā bhūmirasi |*

(Kannada:) "You are an uninterrupted protector; that is, you are always protecting us. Or you are a nourisher like the earth. The word अदिति (*aditi*) is read among the names of the earth (Ni. 2-5), among the names of speech (Ni. 3-23), among the names of the cow (Ni. 3-9) and among the names of heaven and earth (here अदिती (*aditī*) as a dual ending) (Ni. 3-22). Here the bhāṣyakāra has accepted the meaning 'earth' and explained accordingly. We have described the detailed explanation and discussion of the word अदिति (*aditi*) in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 8, page 559." *(Numerals as read; they agree with the numeral file. The volume and page, "8" and "559", are printed in Latin numerals.)*

भारती (*bhāratī*) —

> भारती — भरतस्यादित्यस्य संबंधिनी रश्मिरूपा सती ।

> *bhāratī — bharatasyādityasya saṃbaṃdhinī raśmirūpā satī |*

(Kannada:) "Bharata means one of the twelve Ādityas. The lustre of the Āditya is called भा (*bhā*). Therefore भारती (*bhāratī*) means the light of the Sun, or the Agni who exists in the form of light in the solar orb. Here a relation is stated between the rays of Agni and the rays of Āditya. Since it is said that Agni himself exists in the heavenly region in the form of Āditya, there is a relation between the rays of the Āditya and the rays of Agni."

इळा (*iḷā*) —

> इळा — भूमिरसि ।

> *iḷā — bhūmirasi |*

(Kannada:) "Since the word इळा (*iḷā*) is read among the names of the earth (Ni. 2-5), it is called भूमि (*bhūmi*)."

सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*) —

> सरस्वती — सरणवान्वायुः । तत्संबंधिन्येतन्नियामुका माध्यमिकासि ॥

> *sarasvatī — saraṇavānvāyuḥ | tatsaṃbaṃdhinyetanniyāmukā mādhyamikāsi ‖*

(Kannada:) "Here the bhāṣyakāra explains the word सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*) as 'Vāyu, who is of a moving nature', and therefore as the deity of the middle region (the atmosphere)." *(Then, printed in bold:)*

> आदित्याग्निवायूनां संबंधिन्यो भारतीळासरस्वत्याख्या यास्तिस्रो देव्यः संति ता असि त्वमेवेत्यर्थः ।

> *ādityāgnivāyūnāṃ saṃbaṃdhinyo bhāratīḷāsarasvatyākhyā yāstisro devyaḥ saṃti tā asi tvamevetyarthaḥ |*

*(The strip prints ता असि (*tā asi*) here; the bhāṣya on p. 416 was written ता अपि (*tā api*). The two printings differ: see doubts.)*

(Kannada:) "That is, Agni is praised thus: you are the very form of the three deities named Bhāratī, Iḷā and Sarasvatī, who are related to Āditya, Agni and Vāyu."

*(Closing line ":o:" of the sūkta section; signature "[27]" and "Vol. 14." at the foot.)*

#### Ṛk 12

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वम॑ग्ने॒ सुभृ॑त उत्त॒मं वय॒स्तव॑ स्पा॒र्हे वर्ण॒ आ सं॒दृशि॒ श्रियः॑ ।
> त्वं वाजः॑ प्र॒तर॑णो बृ॒हन्न॑सि॒ त्वं र॒यिर्ब॑हु॒लो वि॒श्वत॑स्पृ॒थुः ॥ १२ ॥

> *tvamagne subhṛta uttamaṃ vayastava spārhe varṇa ā saṃdṛśi śriyaḥ |*
> *tvaṃ vājaḥ prataraṇo bṛhannasi tvaṃ rayirbahulo viśvataspṛthuḥ ‖ 12 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वं । अग्ने । सुऽभृतः । उत्ऽतमं । वयः । तव । स्पार्हे । वर्णे । आ । संऽदृशि । श्रियः ।
> त्वं । वाजः । प्रऽतरणः । बृहन् । असि । त्वं । रयिः । बहुलः । विश्वतः । पृथुः ॥ १२ ॥

> *tvaṃ | agne | su 'bhṛtaḥ | ut 'tamaṃ | vayaḥ | tava | spārhe | varṇe | ā | saṃ 'dṛśi | śriyaḥ |*
> *tvaṃ | vājaḥ | pra 'taraṇaḥ | bṛhan | asi | tvaṃ | rayiḥ | bahulaḥ | viśvataḥ | pṛthuḥ ‖ 12 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Well nourished, Agni gives supreme food or life; riches rest in his lovely, beautiful form; he is food, carries across sin, is great, wealth, manifold and widely spread.

> हे अग्ने त्वं सुभृतः सुष्ठु पोषितः सन् उत्तमं निरतिशयं वयोऽन्नमायुष्यं वा त्वमसि । तत्संपादकोऽसित्यर्थः [sic] । तथा तव स्पार्हे स्पृहणीये वर्णे लोहितशुक्लादिलक्षणे संदृशि सम्यग्दर्शनीये श्रिय ऐश्वर्याणि कांतयो वाश्रित्य वर्तंते ॥ उपसर्गश्रुतेर्योग्यक्रियाध्याहारः ॥ किंच त्वं वाजोऽन्नं । तत्साधकत्वात्तच्छब्द्यं । अन्नसाधक इत्यर्थः । प्रतरणः प्रतारयिता पापात् । अत एव बृहन् महानसि । तथा त्वं रयिर्धनरूपोऽसि । बहुलः सर्वविषयबाहुल्योपेतो विश्वतः पृथुर्विस्तीर्णः प्रख्यात इत्यर्थः ॥

> *he agne tvaṃ subhṛtaḥ suṣṭhu poṣitaḥ san uttamaṃ niratiśayaṃ vayo 'nnamāyuṣyaṃ vā tvamasi | tatsaṃpādako 'sityarthaḥ [sic] | tathā tava spārhe spṛhaṇīye varṇe lohitaśuklādilakṣaṇe saṃdṛśi samyagdarśanīye śriya aiśvaryāṇi kāṃtayo vāśritya vartaṃte ‖ upasargaśruteryogyakriyādhyāhāraḥ ‖ kiṃca tvaṃ vājo 'nnaṃ | tatsādhakatvāttacchabdyaṃ | annasādhaka ityarthaḥ | prataraṇaḥ pratārayitā pāpāt | ata eva bṛhan mahānasi | tathā tvaṃ rayirdhanarūpo 'si | bahulaḥ sarvaviṣayabāhulyopeto viśvataḥ pṛthurvistīrṇaḥ prakhyāta ityarthaḥ ‖*

*(Its tail: the remark that a suitable verb has to be supplied because of the preposition आ (*ā*) in the text, "upasargaśruteryogyakriyādhyāhāraḥ"; characterized, not explained.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; सुभृतः (*subhṛtaḥ*) — when well nourished; उत्तमं (*uttamaṃ*) — excellent, unsurpassed; वयः (*vayaḥ*) — you become the provider of food (life); तव (*tava*) — your; स्पार्हे (*spārhe*) — attractive; वर्णे (*varṇe*) — having red and other colours; सुदृशि (*sudṛśi*) *(printed thus in the Pratipadārtha)* — in the form that is worth seeing; श्रियः (*śriyaḥ*) — riches or splendours; आ (*ā*) — are contained; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; वाजः (*vājaḥ*) — food (the provider of food); प्रतरणः (*prataraṇaḥ*) — one who carries (across sin); बृहन् (*bṛhan*) — great in spirit; असि (*asi*) — you are; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; रयिः (*rayiḥ*) — you are wealth in form; बहुलः (*bahulaḥ*) — of many forms; विश्वतः (*viśvataḥ*) — on all sides; पृथुः (*pṛthuḥ*) — you are also widespread.

### Printed p. 419 (PDF 439)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 19", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". The Bhāvārtha, printed English and Special Topics of Ṛk 12; then Ṛk 13.)*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada:) "O Agni, when you are nourished you become the provider of unsurpassed food. In your attractive form, which has red and other colours and is worth seeing, riches are contained. You yourself are the provider of food. You, who carry us across from sin, are great in spirit and wealth in form, and have many kinds of forms, spread out on all sides."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

When, well-cherished Agni, you are (the giver of) excellent food : in your desirable and delightful hues, beauties (abound) : you (are) food : (you are) the transporter (beyond sin) ; you are mighty ; you are wealth ; you are manifold, and everywhere diffused.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

स्पार्हे वर्णे (*spārhe varṇe*) —

> स्पार्हे वर्णे — स्पृहणीयो वर्णे लोहितशुक्लादि लक्षणे ।

> *spārhe varṇe — spṛhaṇīyo varṇe lohitaśuklādi lakṣaṇe |*

(Kannada:) "The flames of Agni are very excellent, and are endowed with the colours red, white and so on."

प्रतरणः (*prataraṇaḥ*) —

> प्रतरणः — प्रतारयिता पापात् ।

> *prataraṇaḥ — pratārayitā pāpāt |*

(Kannada:) "One who carries us across from the plight of sins; that is, one who protects us so that sins do not envelop us."

विश्वतः पृथुः (*viśvataḥ pṛthuḥ*) — (Kannada:) "One who is famed in all directions. Or one who pervades widely, spread out in all directions; that is, one who pervades the three worlds, earth, atmosphere and heaven."

*(Closing line ":o:".)*

#### Ṛk 13

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वाम॑ग्न आदि॒त्यास॑ आ॒स्यं१॒॑ त्वां जि॒ह्वां शुच॑यश्चक्रिरे कवे ।
> त्वां रा॑ति॒षाचो॑ अध्व॒रेषु॑ सश्चिरे॒ त्वे दे॒वा ह॒विर॑दं॒त्याहु॑तं ॥ १३ ॥

> *tvāmagna ādityāsa āsyaṃ tvāṃ jihvāṃ śucayaścakrire kave |*
> *tvāṃ rātiṣāco adhvareṣu saścire tve devā haviradaṃtyāhutaṃ ‖ 13 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वां । अग्ने । आदित्यासः । आस्यं । त्वां । जिह्वां । शुचयः । चक्रिरे । कवे ।
> त्वां । रातिऽसाचः । अध्वरेषु । सश्चिरे । त्वे इति । देवाः । हविः । अदंति । आऽहुतं ॥ १३ ॥

> *tvāṃ | agne | ādityāsaḥ | āsyaṃ | tvāṃ | jihvāṃ | śucayaḥ | cakrire | kave |*
> *tvāṃ | rāti 'sācaḥ | adhvareṣu | saścire | tve iti | devāḥ | haviḥ | adaṃti | ā 'hutaṃ ‖ 13 ‖*

*(Ṛk 13 is left open: the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya and what follows continue on p. 420.)*

*(Header: "420", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 1". Ṛk 13 continues from p. 419: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English, and the start of the Special Topics.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Aditi's sons (the gods) have made Agni their mouth and tongue; wealth-giving gods serve him at sacrifices; all gods eat the offered oblation in him.

> हे अग्ने त्वामादित्यासोऽदितेः पुत्रा इंद्रादय आस्यं स्वकीयं मुखं भक्षणपानादिसाधनं चक्रिर इति वक्ष्यमाणेन संबंधः । तथा हे कवे क्रांतप्रज्ञ त्वामेव शुचयः शुद्धा दीप्ता वा देवा जिह्वां स्वकीयजिह्वास्थानीयमास्वादनसाधनं चक्रिरे । त्वन्मुखेनैव भक्षयंति त्वज्जिह्वयैवास्वादयंतीत्यर्थः । तथा त्वामेव रातिषाचः । रातिर्दानं दत्तं हविरादि धनं वा । तेन समुवेता [?] देवा अध्वरेषु यज्ञेषु सश्चिरे । सेवंते । त्वामेव प्रतीक्षंते विना त्वया स्वेषां हविर्भक्षणायोगात् । एवं कृत्वा त्वे त्वयि देवाः सर्व आहुतं सर्वतो दत्तं हविरदंति । भक्षयंति । एवं सर्वदेवोपकारिणं महानुभावं स्तौमीत्यर्थः ॥

> *he agne tvāmādityāso 'diteḥ putrā iṃdrādaya āsyaṃ svakīyaṃ mukhaṃ bhakṣaṇapānādisādhanaṃ cakrira iti vakṣyamāṇena saṃbaṃdhaḥ | tathā he kave krāṃtaprajña tvāmeva śucayaḥ śuddhā dīptā vā devā jihvāṃ svakīyajihvāsthānīyamāsvādanasādhanaṃ cakrire | tvanmukhenaiva bhakṣayaṃti tvajjihvayaivāsvādayaṃtītyarthaḥ | tathā tvāmeva rātiṣācaḥ | rātirdānaṃ dattaṃ havirādi dhanaṃ vā | tena samuvetā [?] devā adhvareṣu yajñeṣu saścire | sevaṃte | tvāmeva pratīkṣaṃte vinā tvayā sveṣāṃ havirbhakṣaṇāyogāt | evaṃ kṛtvā tve tvayi devāḥ sarva āhutaṃ sarvato dattaṃ haviradaṃti | bhakṣayaṃti | evaṃ sarvadevopakāriṇaṃ mahānubhāvaṃ staumītyarthaḥ ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; त्वां (*tvāṃ*) — you; आदित्यासः (*ādityāsaḥ*) — Indra and the other sons of Aditi; आस्यः (*āsyaḥ*) *(printed with visarga)* — (they made you) the mouth that eats the oblation; कवे (*kave*) — O Agni, of far-reaching wisdom; त्वां (*tvāṃ*) — you; शुचयः (*śucayaḥ*) — the shining gods; जिह्वां (*jihvāṃ*) — the tongue that tastes; चक्रिरे (*cakrire*) — they made; त्वां (*tvāṃ*) — you; रातिषाचः (*rātiṣācaḥ*) — the gods who possess wealth in the form of the oblation; अध्वरेषु (*adhvareṣu*) — in sacrifices; सश्चिरे (*saścire*) — serve; त्वे (*tve*) — in you (through you); देवाः (*devāḥ*) — all the gods; आहुतं (*āhutaṃ*) — offered; हविः (*haviḥ*) — the oblation; अदंति (*adaṃti*) — eat.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada:) "O Agni, the wise one, the gods such as Indra have made you their mouth that eats the oblation and their tongue that tastes it. The gods who possess wealth in the form of oblations serve you alone in the sacrifices. All the gods eat through you alone the oblation offered to them."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

The Adityas have made, you Agni, their mouth; the pure (deities) have made you Kavi, their tongue : the (gods), the givers of wealth, depend upon you at sacrifices ; they eat the offered oblation through you.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

त्वां अग्ने आदित्यासः आस्यं चक्रिरे (*tvāṃ agne ādityāsaḥ āsyaṃ cakrire*) —

(Kannada:) "Aditi means the divine mother. The Ādityas, her sons (Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman), or the gods, have made you their mouth (bāyi). That is, the gods do not come visibly to the place of sacrifice and, in the shape of a body and so on, receive oblations in such a way that everyone can see." *(The passage runs over into p. 421.)*

### Printed p. 421 (PDF 441)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 19" read from the strip, not zoomed; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā".)*

(Kannada, continued from p. 420:) "…They do not receive the oblations in that way. But they receive the oblations offered in Agni with the respective mantras, addressed to the gods. The oblation offered in Agni goes and reaches the gods. Therefore Agni is like a mouth to the gods; through him the gods receive the oblation. This is the meaning."

त्वां जिह्वां शुचयश्चक्रिरे कवे (*tvāṃ jihvāṃ śucayaścakrire kave*) —

(Kannada:) "As said before, the shining gods made you, Agni, their tongue. That is, the gods eat the oblations through your mouth (through offering in you). They taste through your tongue (the flame). This is the meaning."

त्वां रातिषाचः अध्वरेषु सश्चिरे (*tvāṃ rātiṣācaḥ adhvareṣu saścire*) —

(Kannada:) "In the sacrifices all the gods assemble and, to obtain their oblations, look to you alone and trust in you. The gods partake of the oblations that the sacrificers offer in you."

त्वे देवाः हविः अदंति आहुतं (*tve devāḥ haviḥ adaṃti āhutaṃ*) —

(Kannada:) "The gods eat the oblation offered in you (in Agni). The matters stated in the four pādas of this Ṛk, though described in different words, all have one meaning: the gods eat the oblations offered in Agni only through Agni. This is the meaning."

#### Ṛk 14

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वे अ॑ग्ने॒ विश्वे॑ अ॒मृता॑सो अ॒द्रुह॑ आ॒सा दे॒वा ह॒विर॑दं॒त्याहु॑तं ।
> त्वया॒ मर्ता॑सः स्वदंत आसु॒तिं त्वं गर्भो॑ वी॒रुधां॑ जज्ञिषे॒ शुचिः॑ ॥ १४ ॥

> *tve agne viśve amṛtāso adruha āsā devā haviradaṃtyāhutaṃ |*
> *tvayā martāsaḥ svadaṃta āsutiṃ tvaṃ garbho vīrudhāṃ jajñiṣe śuciḥ ‖ 14 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वे इति । अग्ने । विश्वे । अमृतासः । अद्रुहः । आसा । देवाः । हविः । अदंति । आऽहुतं ।
> त्वया । मर्तासः । स्वदंते । आऽसुतिं । त्वं । गर्भः । वीरुधां । जज्ञिषे । शुचिः ॥ १४ ॥

> *tve iti | agne | viśve | amṛtāsaḥ | adruhaḥ | āsā | devāḥ | haviḥ | adaṃti | ā 'hutaṃ |*
> *tvayā | martāsaḥ | svadaṃte | ā 'sutiṃ | tvaṃ | garbhaḥ | vīrudhāṃ | jajñiṣe | śuciḥ ‖ 14 ‖*

### Printed p. 422 (PDF 442)

*(Header: "422", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 1". Ṛk 14: bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English, start of the Special Topics.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* All immortal, benevolent gods eat the oblation through Agni's mouth; mortals taste food through him; as the embryo of plants he produces grain.

> हे अग्ने त्वे त्वयि विश्वे सर्वेऽमृतासोऽमरणधर्माणोऽद्रुहोऽद्रोग्यारो [?] देवा आसा त्वदीयेनास्येनाहुतं हविरदंति । भक्षयंति ॥ आस्यशब्दस्य तृतीयैकवचने पद्न्नोमासित्यादिनासन्नादेशः [?] । ऊडिदंपदादीति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं ॥ तथा मर्तासो मनुष्या अपि त्वया साधनभूतेनासुतिं रसरूपमन्नादिकं स्वदंते । आस्वादयंति । त्वमेव वीरुधां लतादीनां गर्भो गर्भस्थानीयः तेषां मध्यावस्थानात् । वसुः सर्वेषां निवासभूतः सन् जज्ञिषे । उत्पादयसि सस्याद्यन्नं ॥

> *he agne tve tvayi viśve sarve 'mṛtāso 'maraṇadharmāṇo 'druho 'drogyāro [?] devā āsā tvadīyenāsyenāhutaṃ haviradaṃti | bhakṣayaṃti ‖ āsyaśabdasya tṛtīyaikavacane padnnomāsityādināsannādeśaḥ [?] | ūḍidaṃpadādīti vibhakterudāttatvaṃ ‖ tathā martāso manuṣyā api tvayā sādhanabhūtenāsutiṃ rasarūpamannādikaṃ svadaṃte | āsvādayaṃti | tvameva vīrudhāṃ latādīnāṃ garbho garbhasthānīyaḥ teṣāṃ madhyāvasthānāt | vasuḥ sarveṣāṃ nivāsabhūtaḥ san jajñiṣe | utpādayasi sasyādyannaṃ ‖*

*(Its tail: the grammatical remark that the word आस्य (*āsya*) in the instrumental singular takes the substitute आसन् (*āsan*) by the sūtra beginning पद्… (*pad…*) (partly illegible to me, no sūtra number printed), and that by the rule ऊडिदंपदादि (*ūḍidaṃpadādi*) the case-ending takes the udātta; characterized, not explained.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; त्वे (*tve*) — in you; विश्वे (*viśve*) — all; अमृतासः (*amṛtāsaḥ*) — those free from the nature of death; अद्रुहः (*adruhaḥ*) — those who do good to the world; देवाः (*devāḥ*) — the gods; आसा (*āsā*) — through your mouth; आहुतं (*āhutaṃ*) — offered in the sacrifice; हविः (*haviḥ*) — the oblation; अदंति (*adaṃti*) — eat; मर्तासः (*martāsaḥ*) — men; त्वया (*tvayā*) — by your help; आसुतिं (*āsutiṃ*) — food and the like in the form of essence; स्वदंते (*svadaṃte*) — eat; शुचिः (*śuciḥ*) — you who are radiant; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; वीरुधां (*vīrudhāṃ*) — of creepers and the like; गर्भः (*garbhaḥ*) — in the form of the embryo, being in their midst; जज्ञिषे (*jajñiṣe*) — you produce grain and the like.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada:) "O Agni, all the gods, free from death and doing good to the world, eat through your mouth alone the oblation offered in the sacrifice. Men too eat food and the like, in the form of essence, only with your help. You, the radiant one, exist as the embryo of creepers and the like, and produce grain and the like."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

All the benignant immortal gods eat the offered oblation through you, as their mouth ; mortals taste the flavour (of all viands) through you : you are born pure, the embryo of plants.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

(Kannada:) "The matter stated in the previous Ṛk, that the gods eat the oblations only through your mouth, you who are Agni, is stated here also."

अमृतासः (*amṛtāsaḥ*) —

> अमरधर्माणः । *(thus printed in the Special Topics; the bhāṣya above has ⟦अमरणधर्माणः⟧)*

> *amaradharmāṇaḥ | *(thus printed in the Special Topics; the bhāṣya above has amaraṇadharmāṇaḥ (*amaraṇadharmāṇaḥ*))**

(Kannada:) "Those who are free from death; it is believed that the gods have no death. In the Ṛgveda the gods are called by the word अमृत (*amṛta*), and men by the word मर्त (*marta*) or…" *(the sentence runs over into p. 423)*

*(Ṛk 14 is left open in its Special Topics, in the middle of the sentence on मर्त (*marta*); continue on p. 423.)*

### Printed p. 423 (PDF 443)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 19" read from the strip, not zoomed; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Ṛk 14, Special Topics, continued from p. 422.)*

(Kannada, continued mid-sentence from p. 422:) "…or by the word मर्त्य (*martya*) there is a usage of describing them. Therefore the word अमृतासः (*amṛtāsaḥ*) in the first half of this Ṛk is an adjective of the word देवाः (*devāḥ*). In the second half the word मर्तासः (*martāsaḥ*) indicates the meaning 'men'."

अद्रुहः (*adruhaḥ*) — अद्रोग्धारः (*adrogdhāraḥ*) —

*(Here the bhāṣya-word is printed clearly as अद्रोग्धारः (*adrogdhāraḥ*) with ग्ध; this corrects my [?] reading अद्रोग्यारो (*adrogyāro*) in the bhāṣya of Ṛk 14 on p. 422.)*

(Kannada:) "Because the gods do harm to no one, they are praised by the epithet अद्रुहः (*adruhaḥ*)."

आसुतिं (*āsutiṃ*) — रसरूपमन्नादिकं (*rasarūpamannādikaṃ*) —

(Kannada:) "Food, Soma and the like, that is, foods and drinks fit to be eaten or drunk."

त्वं गर्भो वीरुधां जज्ञिषे शुचिः (*tvaṃ garbho vīrudhāṃ jajñiṣe śuciḥ*) —

(Kannada:) "O Agni, you are pure. You are born as the embryo-place (womb) of the plants (ओषधि (*oṣadhi*)). On the word वीरुध (*vīrudha*) Yāska has given the etymology:"

> वीरुध ओषधयो भवंति विरोहणात् । वीरुधः पारयिष्ण्वः इत्यपि निगमो भवति

> *vīrudha oṣadhayo bhavaṃti virohaṇāt | vīrudhaḥ pārayiṣṇvaḥ ityapi nigamo bhavati*

(Kannada:) "(Nirukta 6-3, as printed.) Because these grow in the earth, creepers and the like are called ओषधि (*oṣadhi*) (herbs). Grain and the like can also be called ओषधि (*oṣadhi*). The sense is that Agni, being in the womb of the herbs (or grains), is a help to their growth and to the production of food and the like. Or, if the word वीरुध (*vīrudha*) is taken to mean 'tree', the meaning can be given that Agni is produced in the aranis (fire-sticks) that belong to trees."

#### Ṛk 15

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> त्वं तान्त्सं च॒ प्रति॑ चासि म॒ज्मनाग्ने॑ सुजात॒ प्र च॑ देव रिच्यसे ।
> पृ॒क्षो यदत्र॑ महि॒ना वि ते॒ भुव॒दनु॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी रोद॑सी उ॒भे ॥ १५ ॥

> *tvaṃ tāntsaṃ ca prati cāsi majmanāgne sujāta pra ca deva ricyase |*
> *pṛkṣo yadatra mahinā vi te bhuvadanu dyāvāpṛthivī rodasī ubhe ‖ 15 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> त्वं । तान् । सं । च । प्रति । च । असि । मज्मना । अग्ने । सुऽजात । प्र । च । देव । रिच्यसे ।
> पृक्षः । यत् । अत्र । महिना । वि । ते । भुवत् । अनु । द्यावापृथिवी इति । रोदसी इति । उभे इति ॥ १५ ॥

> *tvaṃ | tān | saṃ | ca | prati | ca | asi | majmanā | agne | su 'jāta | pra | ca | deva | ricyase |*
> *pṛkṣaḥ | yat | atra | mahinā | vi | te | bhuvat | anu | dyāvāpṛthivī iti | rodasī iti | ubhe iti ‖ 15 ‖*

### Printed p. 424 (PDF 444)

*(Header: "424", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 1". Ṛk 15: bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Agni by his strength is both united with the gods and distinct from them, and excels them, since all the food offered here spreads, through his might, over heaven and earth.

> हे अग्ने त्वं मज्मना बलेन तान् प्रसिद्धान्देवान् सं चासि । संगच्छसि । तैः सहितोऽपि भवसि । तथा सामर्थ्येन प्रति चासि । प्रत्येकं तैर्विभिन्नः प्रतिनिधिर्वा भवसि । प्रतिस्वीकारसमये तैः सहितो भवसि वियुक्तश्च भवसीत्यर्थः । हे सुजात शोभनजनन । शोभनमंत्रसहितमथनेनोत्पन्नत्वादग्नेः सुजन्मत्वं । तादृशाग्ने हे देव प्ररिच्यसे च । तैर्बलेन चाधिको भवसि । आधिक्ये कारणमाह । यत् यस्मादत्रास्मिन्यज्ञे पृक्षः सर्वसंप्यन्नं [?] ॥ व्यत्ययेन बहुवचनं ॥ ते तवैव विभुवत् । समर्थं भवति महिना माहात्म्येन । यतो महत्त्वमस्ति अत इत्यर्थः । कुत्रेति तदुच्यते । रोदसी सर्वनिरोदनस्वभावे उभे द्यावापृथिव्यावनु । ते प्रति । तयोर्मध्ये व्याप्तमित्यर्थः । त्वयि हुतमन्नं त्वन्महत्त्वेन लोकत्रये व्याप्तमित्यर्थः ॥

> *he agne tvaṃ majmanā balena tān prasiddhāndevān saṃ cāsi | saṃgacchasi | taiḥ sahito 'pi bhavasi | tathā sāmarthyena prati cāsi | pratyekaṃ tairvibhinnaḥ pratinidhirvā bhavasi | pratisvīkārasamaye taiḥ sahito bhavasi viyuktaśca bhavasītyarthaḥ | he sujāta śobhanajanana | śobhanamaṃtrasahitamathanenotpannatvādagneḥ sujanmatvaṃ | tādṛśāgne he deva praricyase ca | tairbalena cādhiko bhavasi | ādhikye kāraṇamāha | yat yasmādatrāsminyajñe pṛkṣaḥ sarvasaṃpyannaṃ [?] ‖ vyatyayena bahuvacanaṃ ‖ te tavaiva vibhuvat | samarthaṃ bhavati mahinā māhātmyena | yato mahattvamasti ata ityarthaḥ | kutreti taducyate | rodasī sarvanirodanasvabhāve ubhe dyāvāpṛthivyāvanu | te prati | tayormadhye vyāptamityarthaḥ | tvayi hutamannaṃ tvanmahattvena lokatraye vyāptamityarthaḥ ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; त्वं (*tvaṃ*) — you; मज्मना (*majmanā*) — with strength; तान् (*tān*) — with those well-known gods; संचासि (*saṃcāsi*) — you are united; प्रतिचासि (*praticāsi*) — you are also distinct; यत् (*yat*) — by which; (ते (*te*) —) your; महिना (*mahinā*) — greatness; अत्र (*atra*) — in this sacrifice (offered); पृक्षः (*pṛkṣaḥ*) — all the food; ते (*te*) — your; वि भुवत् (*vi bhuvat*) — being in your control (and afterwards); रोदसी उभे (*rodasī ubhe*) — both worlds, heaven and earth; अनु (*anu*) — pervades (therefore); सुजात (*sujāta*) — you of excellent birth; देव (*deva*) — O Agni, divine in nature; प्ररिच्यसे च (*praricyase ca*) — you exceed all the gods in capacity.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada:) "O Agni, of excellent birth and divine in nature, with your strength you are united with the gods, and you are also distinct. By your greatness all the food offered in this sacrifice, being first in your control, afterwards pervades both heaven and earth and is distributed to the remaining gods. Therefore you exceed all the remaining gods in capacity."

**English Translation** *(as printed; the heading is printed "English Translatin" [sic])*

You are associated, Agni, by your vigour, with those (goods) [sic]; divine, well-born Agni, you exceed (them in strength), for the (sacrificial) food that is here prepared is, by your power, subsequently diffused through both regions, heaven and earth.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

त्वं तान् सं च प्रति च असि मज्मना (*tvaṃ tān saṃ ca prati ca asi majmanā*) —

(Kannada:) "The word मज्मना (*majmanā*) is read among the names of strength. O Agni, by strength you are equal to the gods. Or: you are in company with the gods. That is, at the time of receiving the oblation you are with the gods. Because the gods eat the offerings made in you, at the time of offering the oblation you and the gods are together. At other times you are also separate; this is the meaning."

अग्ने सुजात प्र च देव रिच्यसे (*agne sujāta pra ca deva ricyase*) —

(Kannada:) "सुजात (*sujāta*): because Agni is produced at the time of churning, with the recitation of excellent mantras, Agni is called सुजात (*sujāta*), 'excellently born'. The meaning is that you, such an Agni, have surpassed the gods in strength. How is that?—"

पृक्षः यदत्र रोदसी उभे (*pṛkṣaḥ yadatra rodasī ubhe*) —

(Kannada:) "The food in the form of oblation that is offered in you in this sacrifice pervades, by your greatness, the whole middle region between heaven and earth. That is, it goes and reaches all the gods who are in the worlds of earth, atmosphere and heaven."

*(Closing line.)*

### Printed p. 426 (PDF 446)

*(Header: "426", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 1". Ṛk 16: bhāṣya, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English, and the first line of the Special Topics. PDF 447 is a duplicate of this page, with the same header "426" and the same text; it is noted here and not written twice.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* The patrons give cows and horses as gifts to the priests; Agni is asked to lead those patrons and us to the best place (heaven), and we, with good sons, will recite a great mantra at the sacrifice.

> अनया [?] होता स्तुतिनिगमव्याजेनाभिमतमाशास्ते । हे ऽग्ने सूरयो मेधाविनः प्रेरयितारो वा यजमानाः स्तोतृभ्यः स्तुतिकर्तृभ्यो गोअग्रां गावोऽग्रगामिन्यो यस्यां तादृशीं गोप्रमुखामश्वपेशसं ॥ पेश इति रूपनाम ॥ अश्वेन निरूपणीयां । एतद्द्वयं प्राधान्याभिप्रायं । गौश्चाश्वश्चाजश्चेति दक्षिणापरिगणनेषु गवाश्वयोः प्राथम्यात् । तादृशीं रातिमुपसृजंति । ददते । तान्यजमानानस्मांश्च ऋत्विजो वस्यो वसीयः श्रेष्ठं स्वर्गादिस्थानं आ सर्वतः प्र हि नेषि । प्रकर्षेण नयसि खलु । नयेत्यर्थः । हि प्रसिद्धौ । वयं च सुवीराः शोभनपुत्रादिसहिता विदथे यज्ञे बृहन्महन्मंत्रजातं वदेम । उच्चारयामः । स्तुमा इत्यर्थः ॥

> *anayā [?] hotā stutinigamavyājenābhimatamāśāste | he 'gne sūrayo medhāvinaḥ prerayitāro vā yajamānāḥ stotṛbhyaḥ stutikartṛbhyo goagrāṃ gāvo 'gragāminyo yasyāṃ tādṛśīṃ gopramukhāmaśvapeśasaṃ ‖ peśa iti rūpanāma ‖ aśvena nirūpaṇīyāṃ | etaddvayaṃ prādhānyābhiprāyaṃ | gauścāśvaścājaśceti dakṣiṇāparigaṇaneṣu gavāśvayoḥ prāthamyāt | tādṛśīṃ rātimupasṛjaṃti | dadate | tānyajamānānasmāṃśca ṛtvijo vasyo vasīyaḥ śreṣṭhaṃ svargādisthānaṃ ā sarvataḥ pra hi neṣi | prakarṣeṇa nayasi khalu | nayetyarthaḥ | hi prasiddhau | vayaṃ ca suvīrāḥ śobhanaputrādisahitā vidathe yajñe bṛhanmahanmaṃtrajātaṃ vadema | uccārayāmaḥ | stumā ityarthaḥ ‖*

*(The first word is printed as अनयो (*anayo*) in the Kannada-script print; I read it as अनया (*anayā*) [?]. The word before व्याजेन (*vyājena*) is स्तुतिनिगम (*stutinigama*) as printed, doubtful.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; ये (*ye*) — who; सूरयः (*sūrayaḥ*) — those who are impelled by good understanding, such sacrificers (yajamānas); स्तोतृभ्यः (*stotṛbhyaḥ*) — to the praisers; गोअग्रां (*goagrāṃ*) — that in which cows are foremost; अश्वपेशसं (*aśvapeśasaṃ*) — that which is delineated (shaped) by horses; रातिं (*rātiṃ*) — the gift; उपसृजंति (*upasṛjaṃti*) — they give; तांश्च (*tāṃśca*) — those sacrificers also; अस्मांश्च (*asmāṃśca*) — us, the priests, also; वस्यः (*vasyaḥ*) — to the excellent place, heaven and the like; आ प्र हि नेषि (*ā pra hi neṣi*) — lead (us) in an exceeding manner; सुवीराः (*suvīrāḥ*) — we, accompanied by excellent sons and the like; विदथे (*vidathe*) — in the sacrifice; बृहत् (*bṛhat*) — the mantra full of greatness; वदेम (*vadema*) — we shall recite.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada:) "O Agni, the sacrificers who are impelled by good understanding give to the praisers a gift in which cows are foremost and which is marked out by horses. Lead those sacrificers, and us the priests, in an exceeding manner to the excellent place, heaven and the like. May we, accompanied by excellent sons and the like, recite at the sacrifice a mantra full of greatness."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

The pious are they who present, as a gift, to the reciters of your praises, an excellent cow and an excellent horse; do you, Agni, lead both us and them to the best of abodes, (or heaven) ,that we and our worthy descendants may repeat the solemn prayer to you at the sacrifice.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

(Kannada:) "In this Ṛk, the last of this sūkta, the ṛṣi prays to Agni for the fulfilment of his desire and brings the sūkta to its close."

### Printed p. 427 (PDF 448)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 20" read from the strip, not zoomed; "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā". Ṛk 16 Special Topics continued; Sūkta 1 ends; Sūkta 2 begins.)*

स्तोतृभ्यः गो अग्रां अश्वपेशसं रातिं उपसृजंति सूरयः (*stotṛbhyaḥ go agrāṃ aśvapeśasaṃ rātiṃ upasṛjaṃti sūrayaḥ*) —

(Kannada:) "These are the priests who praise Agni. It is the custom that the sacrificer gives them, at the time of the completion of the sacrifice, cows, horses, goats and the like in the form of dakṣiṇā. In the same way here too the wise sacrificers are said to give the hotṛ and other priests a dakṣiṇā beginning with cows. Agni is prayed to lead such sacrificers, and us the priests, to the excellent place (heaven and the like). Here गो अग्रां (*go agrāṃ*) means 'that in which the cows are foremost'; अश्वपेशसं (*aśvapeśasaṃ*) means 'by the forms of horses', that is, 'accompanied by horses'; रातिं (*rātiṃ*) means 'the gift or the dakṣiṇā'. This is the meaning of these words."

बृहत् वदेम विदथे सुवीराः (*bṛhat vadema vidathe suvīrāḥ*) —

(Kannada:) "We, accompanied by heroic sons, friends, servants and the like, will recite at this sacrifice an abundant (or greatly filled) hymn of praise: so the prayer is addressed to Agni. This fourth pāda of the Ṛk, बृहद्वदेम विदथे सुवीराः (*bṛhadvadema vidathe suvīrāḥ*), is repeated again and again in the last pāda of the last Ṛk of many sūktas seen by this ṛṣi Gṛtsamada."

*(Rule line.)*

#### Sūkta 2

*(Heading printed: "The second sūkta" — द्वितीयं सूक्तं (*dvitīyaṃ sūktaṃ*); Kannada "ಎರಡನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು". Thirteen Ṛks; ṛṣi Gṛtsamada; deity Agni; metre Jagatī, as the Anuvāda states below.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Introduction: the second sūkta, thirteen Ṛks, seer of the maṇḍala Gṛtsamada, Agni, Jagatī; its uses in the Prātaranuvāka, the Āśvina śastra and the nivid of Jātavedas.

> यज्ञेन वर्धतेति त्रयोदशर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तं मंडलद्रष्टुर्गृत्समदस्यार्षं । मंडलादिष्टाग्नेयमिति परिभाषयाग्नेयं । तुशब्दानुकर्षादिदमपि जागतं । यज्ञेन सप्ते [?] त्यनुक्रांतं ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोर्जागते छंदस्यस्य विनियोगः । सूत्रं तु पूर्वसूक्त एवोक्तं ॥ तथा चातुर्विंशिके तृतीयसवने जातवेदस्यनिविद्धानीयमिदं [?] । यज्ञेन वर्धतेत्याग्निमारुतं । आ. ७-४ । इति सूत्रितत्वात् ॥ पृष्ठ्याभिप्लवषडहयोर्द्वितीयेऽहन्यपि जातवेदस्यनिविद्धानमिदं [?] । चातुर्विंशिकं तृतीयसवनमिति चतुर्विंशादतिदिष्टत्वात् ॥

> *yajñena vardhateti trayodaśarcaṃ dvitīyaṃ sūktaṃ maṃḍaladraṣṭurgṛtsamadasyārṣaṃ | maṃḍalādiṣṭāgneyamiti paribhāṣayāgneyaṃ | tuśabdānukarṣādidamapi jāgataṃ | yajñena sapte [?] tyanukrāṃtaṃ ‖ prātaranuvākāśvinaśastrayorjāgate chaṃdasyasya viniyogaḥ | sūtraṃ tu pūrvasūkta evoktaṃ ‖ tathā cāturviṃśike tṛtīyasavane jātavedasyanividdhānīyamidaṃ [?] | yajñena vardhatetyāgnimārutaṃ | ā. 7-4 | iti sūtritatvāt ‖ pṛṣṭhyābhiplavaṣaḍahayordvitīye 'hanyapi jātavedasyanividdhānamidaṃ [?] | cāturviṃśikaṃ tṛtīyasavanamiti caturviṃśādatidiṣṭatvāt ‖*

*(Its tail: the sūtra-citation "Āśvalāyana 7-4" — printed "आ. ७-४", agreeing with the numeral file "7.4" — and the extension of the rule from the चतुर्विंश (*caturviṃśa*) day to the second day of the पृष्ठ्य (*pṛṣṭhya*) and अभिप्लव (*abhiplava*) ṣaḍahas; characterized, not explained.)*

(Kannada, Anuvāda:) "The Anuvāda: this sūkta beginning यज्ञेन वर्धते (*yajñena vardhate*) is the second sūkta in the first anuvāka. It has thirteen Ṛks. The same Gṛtsamada, the seer of the maṇḍala, is the ṛṣi of this sūkta too; Agni is the deity; the metre is Jagatī. In the Anukramaṇikā it is stated beginning यज्ञेन सप्ते (*yajñena sapte*) [?] and so on. This sūkta has its application for the Ṛks in Jagatī metre at the time of reciting the Prātaranuvāka mantras and at the time of reciting the Āśvina śastra mantras. The sūtra passage was stated earlier. And in the sacrifice performed over twenty-four days, at the third savana, this sūkta has its application for the nivid mantras recited with the deity Jātavedas as their object, as Āśvalāyana's" *(the sentence runs over into p. 428)*

*(Sūkta 2 is left open in the Anuvāda, at the word "Āśvalāyana's"; the Ṛks begin on p. 428.)*

*(Printed heading, in Kannada:)* Maṇḍala 2 · Anuvāka 1 · Sūkta 2 · Aṣṭaka 2 · Adhyāya 5 · Varga 20, 21 · number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 13 · Ṛṣi: गृत्समदः (*gṛtsamadaḥ*) · Devatā: अग्निः (*agniḥ*) · Chandas: जगती (*jagatī*).

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> य॒ज्ञेन॑ वर्धत जा॒तवे॑दसम॒ग्निं य॑जध्वं ह॒विषा॒ तना॑ गि॒रा ।

> *yajñena vardhata jātavedasamagniṃ yajadhvaṃ haviṣā tanā girā |*
> *samidhānaṃ suprayasaṃ svarṇaraṃ dyukṣaṃ hotāraṃ vṛjaneṣu dhūrṣadaṃ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यज्ञेन । वर्धत । जातऽवेदसं । अग्निं । यजध्वं । हविषा । तना । गिरा ।
> संऽइधानं । सुऽप्रयसं । स्वःऽनरं । द्युक्षं । होतारं । वृजनेषु । धूःऽसदम् ॥ १ ॥

> *yajñena | vardhata | jāta 'vedasaṃ | agniṃ | yajadhvaṃ | haviṣā | tanā | girā |*
> *saṃ 'idhānaṃ | su 'prayasaṃ | svaḥ 'naraṃ | dyukṣaṃ | hotāraṃ | vṛjaneṣu | dhūḥ 'sadam ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Priests or sacrificers are told to exalt Agni, who knows all that is born, by sacrifice, and to worship him with oblation and praise.

> हे यजमाना ऋत्विजो वा यूयं जातवेदसं जातानां वेदितारं जातधनं जातप्रज्ञं वाग्निं यज्ञेन यागेन वर्धत । प्रवर्धत । सामान्येनोक्त्वा विशेषेणाह । हविषा चरुपुरोडाशादिना तना विस्तृतया [?] गिरा स्तुत्या च यजध्वं । पूजयध्वं ।

> *he yajamānā ṛtvijo vā yūyaṃ jātavedasaṃ jātānāṃ veditāraṃ jātadhanaṃ jātaprajñaṃ vāgniṃ yajñena yāgena vardhata | pravardhata | sāmānyenoktvā viśeṣeṇāha | haviṣā carupuroḍāśādinā tanā vistṛtayā [?] girā stutyā ca yajadhvaṃ | pūjayadhvaṃ |*

### Printed p. 429 (PDF 450)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 20", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "429". Ṛk 1: bhāṣya continued, Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English, Special Topics begun. Numeral file: row for this page, "Ni. 3-19", agrees with the strip; the header was read from the strip and not zoomed.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(continued)*

*Gist:* The epithets: kindled; having good food; one who leads sacrificers to heaven; resplendent; priest of the offering; the doer of strength. Strength of body is well known to come from the vigour of fire.

> कीदृशं तं । समिधानं । समिध्यमानं । सुप्रयसं । शोभनान्नं । स्वर्णरं । स्वर्गे नेतव्या यजमाना यस्य तादृशं । यद्वा स्वरिति सर्वपर्यायः । स्तुतीनां नेतारः स्तोतारः । बहुस्तोतारमित्यर्थः । द्युक्षं । दीप्तं द्युनिवासिनं वा । होतारं । होमसंपादकं । वृजनेषु बलेषु धूर्षदं । बलस्य कर्तारमित्यर्थः । अग्निपाटवे सति शरीरबलं भवतीति प्रसिद्धं ॥

> *kīdṛśaṃ taṃ | samidhānaṃ | samidhyamānaṃ | suprayasaṃ | śobhanānnaṃ | svarṇaraṃ | svarge netavyā yajamānā yasya tādṛśaṃ | yadvā svariti sarvaparyāyaḥ | stutīnāṃ netāraḥ stotāraḥ | bahustotāramityarthaḥ | dyukṣaṃ | dīptaṃ dyunivāsinaṃ vā | hotāraṃ | homasaṃpādakaṃ | vṛjaneṣu baleṣu dhūrṣadaṃ | balasya kartāramityarthaḥ | agnipāṭave sati śarīrabalaṃ bhavatīti prasiddhaṃ ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

समिधानं (*samidhānaṃ*) — the one who is blazing; सुप्रयसं (*suprayasaṃ*) — the one who has excellent food; स्वर्णरं (*svarṇaraṃ*) — the one who leads (the sacrificers) to heaven; द्युक्षं (*dyukṣaṃ*) — the shining one, or the dweller in the world of heaven; होतारं (*hotāraṃ*) — the accomplisher of the offering; वृजनेषु धूर्षदं (*vṛjaneṣu dhūrṣadaṃ*) — the one who increases the strength of the body; जातवेदसं (*jātavedasaṃ*) — the one of born wisdom (knowing what is born); अग्निं (*agniṃ*) — Agni; यज्ञेन (*yajñena*) — by sacrifice; वर्धत (*vardhata*) — cause (him) to grow; हविषा (*haviṣā*) — with the oblation; तना (*tanā*) — extended; गिरा (*girā*) — also with praise; यजध्वं (*yajadhvaṃ*) — worship.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada:) "Cause Agni, who is blazing, who has excellent food, who leads the sacrificers to heaven, who is shining, who accomplishes the offering, who increases the strength of the body, and who is of born wisdom, to grow by sacrifice. Worship him both with the oblation and with extended praise."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

Exalt with sacrifice, Agni, who knows all that has been born ; worship him with oblations, and with ample praise ; him who is well kindled, well f[?]d [sic: the letter is blurred in the print], much lauded, resplendent, the conveyer of oblations, the giver gf [sic] strength (to the body).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)**

यज्ञेन—यागेन (*yajñena—yāgena*) —

(Kannada:) "Sāyaṇa explains the meaning thus: yajña is the act of offering the substance in the form of oblation into Agni with the deity in view; and the sacrificers who satisfy Agni by this performance make Agni grow."

(Kannada:) "Yāska reads the word yajña among the fifteen names of yajña beginning यज्ञः वेनः (*yajñaḥ venaḥ*) (Ni. ३-१९ (*3-19*)) and says: यज्ञः कस्मात् प्रख्यातं यजति कर्मेति नैरुक्ताः (*yajñaḥ kasmāt prakhyātaṃ yajati karmeti nairuktāḥ*) | या इच्ञ्ये [?] भवतीति वा (*yā icñye [?] bhavatīti vā*), यजुरुन्नतो भवतीति वा (*yajurunnato bhavatīti vā*), बहुकृष्णाजिन इत्यापमन्यवः (*bahukṛṣṇājina ityāpamanyavaḥ*), यजूंष्येनं नयंतीति वा (*yajūṃṣyenaṃ nayaṃtīti vā*). In the world and in the Veda, he explains the sense as the rite that is well known as worshipping deities beginning with Agni through the" *(sentence runs over to p. 430)*
