### Printed p. 460 (PDF 481)

*(Header: "460", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 3", read from the strip. The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

> रायेधनाय । अस्यां वेदी वेद्यां ॥ सप्तम्यर्थे प्रगृह्यसंज्ञा । संहितायां यथादेशश्छांदसः ॥ घृतेनाज्येनाक्तमिदं स्निग्धं बर्हिः सीदत । के । हे वसव एतन्नामकाः हे विश्वेसर्वे देवाः । हे आदित्याः । यज्ञियासो यज्ञार्हास्ते यूयमिदं बर्हिर्निषीदत । अस्मिन्बर्हिषि निषीदतेत्यर्थः ॥

> *rāyedhanāya | asyāṃ vedī vedyāṃ ‖ saptamyarthe pragṛhyasaṃjñā | saṃhitāyāṃ yathādeśaśchāṃdasaḥ ‖ ghṛtenājyenāktamidaṃ snigdhaṃ barhiḥ sīdata | ke | he vasava etannāmakāḥ he viśvesarve devāḥ | he ādityāḥ | yajñiyāso yajñārhāste yūyamidaṃ barhirniṣīdata | asminbarhiṣi niṣīdatetyarthaḥ ‖*

*(Joined with the end of p. 459, the first word reads रायेधनाय, i.e. राये (*rāye*) "for wealth" and धनाय (*dhanāya*) "for wealth, riches". The tail beginning सप्तम्यर्थे (*saptamyarthe*) is grammatical: the Pada word वेदी (*vedī*) is in the sense of the locative, with the designation pragṛhya, and the Chandas-usage of the Saṃhitā; no sūtra numbers printed.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 4)**

(Kannada, translated:) बर्हिः देव (*barhiḥ deva*) — O Barhis, whose nature is divine; अस्यां वेदी (*asyāṃ vedī*) — on this altar; राये (*rāye*) — for wealth; वर्धमानं (*vardhamānaṃ*) — one who brings growth; सुवीरं (*suvīraṃ*) — one who brings excellent valour; सुभरं (*subharaṃ*) — one who is well-filled; स्तीर्णं (*stīrṇaṃ*) — be strewn (by us); यज्ञियासः (*yajñiyāsaḥ*) — O ye worthy of the sacrifice; वसवः (*vasavaḥ*) — O Vasus; विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*) — O Viśvedevas; आदित्याः (*ādityāḥ*) — O Ādityas; घृतेन (*ghṛtena*) — with ghee; अक्तं (*aktaṃ*) — sprinkled; इदं (*idaṃ*) — on this barhis; सीदत (*sīdata*) — sit down.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada, translated:) "O Barhis, whose nature is divine, be the increaser of our wealth, the bringer of excellent valour, well filled; be strewn on our altar and adorn the altar. O Vasus, Viśvedevas, Ādityas, worthy of the sacrifice, sit down on this barhis sprinkled with ghee."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

Divine grass, let the Vasus, the Vishwedevas, the adorable Adityas, sit upon this flourishing, invigorating, well-grown, sacred grass, strewn for the sake of wealth upon this altar, and sprinkled with butter.

*(No Special Topics are printed for Ṛk 4.)*

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> वि श्र॑यंतामुर्वि॒या हू॒यमा॑ना॒ द्वारो॑ दे॒वीः सु॑प्राय॒णा नमो॑भिः ।
> व्यच॑स्वती॒र्वि प्र॑थंतामजु॒र्या वर्णं॑ पुना॒ना य॒शसं॑ सु॒वीरं॑ ॥ ५ ॥

> *vi śrayaṃtāmurviyā hūyamānā dvāro devīḥ suprāyaṇā namobhiḥ |*
> *vyacasvatīrvi prathaṃtāmajuryā varṇaṃ punānā yaśasaṃ suvīraṃ ‖ 5 ‖*

*(The Pada, bhāṣya and the rest of Ṛk 5 follow on p. 461.)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> वि । श्रयंतां । उर्विया । हूयमानाः । द्वारः । देवीः । सुप्रऽअयनाः । नमःऽभिः ।
> व्यचस्वतीः । वि । प्रथंतां । अजुर्याः । वर्णं । पुनानाः । यशसं । सुवीरं ॥ ५ ॥

> *vi | śrayaṃtāṃ | urviyā | hūyamānāḥ | dvāraḥ | devīḥ | supra 'ayanāḥ | namaḥ 'bhiḥ |*
> *vyacasvatīḥ | vi | prathaṃtāṃ | ajuryāḥ | varṇaṃ | punānāḥ | yaśasaṃ | suvīraṃ ‖ 5 ‖*

*(The compound marks in सुप्रऽअयनाः and नमःऽभिः are printed as the small subscript stroke. The Pada has सुप्रऽअयनाः where the bhāṣya later has सुप्रायणाः.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* The door-goddesses of the sacrifice are asked to open wide, being great, easy to approach and called with salutations; and the pervasive, uninjured goddesses, who purify and bestow glorious, heroic splendour on the sacrificer, are asked to be widely famed.

> द्वारो देवीरग्नेर्द्वाराभिमानिन्यो देव्यो विश्रयंतां । विविच्य श्रयंतां । विवृतापिधाना भवंतु । कीदृश्यस्ताः । उर्विया । उर्व्यो महत्यः । नमोभिर्नमस्कारोपेतैः स्तोत्रैर्हूयमानाः । सुप्रायणाः । सुष्ठु प्रकर्षेण गंतव्याः । ईदृश्यो देव्यो विश्रयंतां । किंच व्यचस्वतीर्व्याप्तिमत्योऽजुर्या अहिंस्या अजनना वा सुवीरं शोभनपुत्राद्युपेतं यशसं यशोयुक्तं वर्णं वर्णनीयं रूपविशेषं पुनाना यजमानाय शोधयित्र्यः संपादयित्र्यो देव्यो विप्रथंतां । विशेषेण प्रख्याता भवंतु ॥

> *dvāro devīragnerdvārābhimāninyo devyo viśrayaṃtāṃ | vivicya śrayaṃtāṃ | vivṛtāpidhānā bhavaṃtu | kīdṛśyastāḥ | urviyā | urvyo mahatyaḥ | namobhirnamaskāropetaiḥ stotrairhūyamānāḥ | suprāyaṇāḥ | suṣṭhu prakarṣeṇa gaṃtavyāḥ | īdṛśyo devyo viśrayaṃtāṃ | kiṃca vyacasvatīrvyāptimatyo 'juryā ahiṃsyā ajananā vā suvīraṃ śobhanaputrādyupetaṃ yaśasaṃ yaśoyuktaṃ varṇaṃ varṇanīyaṃ rūpaviśeṣaṃ punānā yajamānāya śodhayitryaḥ saṃpādayitryo devyo viprathaṃtāṃ | viśeṣeṇa prakhyātā bhavaṃtu ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 5)**

(Kannada, translated:) उर्विया (*urviyā*) — endowed with greatness; नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*) — with salutations; हूयमानाः (*hūyamānāḥ*) — those who are called; सुप्रायणाः (*suprāyaṇāḥ*) — those who are to be approached easily; देवीः द्वारः (*devīḥ dvāraḥ*) — the door-goddesses; विश्रयंतां (*viśrayaṃtāṃ*) — let them open fully; व्यचस्वतीः (*vyacasvatīḥ*) — those of pervasive form; अजुर्याः (*ajuryāḥ*) — non-injurers; सुवीरं (*suvīraṃ*) — that which is endowed with heroic sons and the like; यशसं (*yaśasaṃ*) — that which is endowed with fame; वर्णं (*varṇaṃ*) — that which is praiseworthy, the wealth; पुनानाः (*punānāḥ*) — goddesses who give (it) to the sacrificer; वि प्रथंतां (*vi prathaṃtāṃ*) — let them be praised.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada, translated:) "Let the door-goddesses, endowed with greatness, to be called with salutations, easy to approach, open fully. Let the goddesses of pervasive nature, non-injurers, who give to the sacrificer wealth endowed with heroic sons and the like and with fame, be praised."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

Let the divine doors, spacious and easily accessible, and to be saluted with prostrations, be set open: let them be celebrated as expansive, uninjurable and conferring sanctity upon the illustrious class (of worshippers), possessed of virtuous progeny.

*(No Special Topics are printed for Ṛk 5.)*

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> सा॒ध्वपां॑सि स॒नता॑ न उक्षि॒ते उ॒षासा॒नक्ता॑ व॒य्ये॑व रण्वि॒ते ।
> तंतुं॑ त॒तं सं॒वयं॑ती समी॒ची य॒ज्ञस्य॒ पेशः॑ सु॒दुघे॒ पय॑स्वती ॥ ६ ॥

> *sādhvapāṃsi sanatā na ukṣite uṣāsānaktā vayyeva raṇvite |*
> *taṃtuṃ tataṃ saṃvayaṃtī samīcī yajñasya peśaḥ sudughe payasvatī ‖ 6 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> साधु । अपांसि । सनता । नः । उक्षिते इति । उषसानक्ता । वय्या इव । रण्विते इति ।
> तंतुं । ततं । संवयंती इति सम्ऽवयंती । समीची इति सम्ऽईची । यज्ञस्य ।
> पेशः । सुदुघे इति सुऽदुघे । पयस्वती इति ॥ ६ ॥

> *sādhu | apāṃsi | sanatā | naḥ | ukṣite iti | uṣasānaktā | vayyā iva | raṇvite iti |*
> *taṃtuṃ | tataṃ | saṃvayaṃtī iti sam 'vayaṃtī | samīcī iti sam 'īcī | yajñasya |*
> *peśaḥ | sudughe iti su 'dughe | payasvatī iti ‖ 6 ‖*

*(Read as printed: the Pada has उषसानक्ता where the Saṃhitā has उषासानक्ता; the Pada's वय्या is followed by a small stroke before इव, read here as the word-division वय्या इव.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* The goddesses Day and Night, ever-worshipped, weave for us the stretched thread of the sacrifice like two weaving women, mutually favourable, yielding fruit and water.

> साधु साधूनि नोऽस्मदीयान्यपांसि कर्माण्युद्दिश्य सनता सनातनेनाविच्छिन्नप्रवृत्तिकेन स्तोत्रादिनोक्षिते पूजिते । यद्वा पुराणवाची विभक्त्यंतः सनच्छब्दोऽस्ति । तस्य प्रथमाद्विवचनस्याकारः । सनातने नित्ये इत्यर्थः । अस्मिन्पक्ष उक्षिते फलस्य सेचयित्र्यौ ॥ कर्तरि निष्ठा ॥ उषासानक्ताहोरात्रदेवते वय्या इव वानकुशले इव रण्विते शब्दिते स्तुते परस्परं गच्छंत्यौ वा ततं विस्तृतं तंतुं तंतुस्थानीयं यज्ञावयवं संवयंती सम्यक् चित्रं सह वा वयंत्यावुत्पादयित्र्यौ समीची सम्यक्प्रवृत्तिके परस्परानुकूले । किमर्थं संवयंती । यज्ञस्यानुष्ठीयमानस्य पेशो रूपं निर्मातुमिति शेषः । यज्ञं निर्वर्तयितुं तदवयवानुक्रमेणानुष्ठापयित्र्यावित्यर्थः । अहोरात्राभ्यां हि यज्ञास्तन्यंते । सुदुघे सुष्ठु फलस्य दोग्ध्र्यौ [?] पयस्वती उदकवत्यौ । अहोरात्राभ्यां खलु वृष्टिर्जायते । एवं महासुभावे अहोरात्रदेवते अस्मद्यज्ञं निर्वहतामित्यर्थः ॥

> *sādhu sādhūni no 'smadīyānyapāṃsi karmāṇyuddiśya sanatā sanātanenāvicchinnapravṛttikena stotrādinokṣite pūjite | yadvā purāṇavācī vibhaktyaṃtaḥ sanacchabdo 'sti | tasya prathamādvivacanasyākāraḥ | sanātane nitye ityarthaḥ | asminpakṣa ukṣite phalasya secayitryau ‖ kartari niṣṭhā ‖ uṣāsānaktāhorātradevate vayyā iva vānakuśale iva raṇvite śabdite stute parasparaṃ gacchaṃtyau vā tataṃ vistṛtaṃ taṃtuṃ taṃtusthānīyaṃ yajñāvayavaṃ saṃvayaṃtī samyak citraṃ saha vā vayaṃtyāvutpādayitryau samīcī samyakpravṛttike parasparānukūle | kimarthaṃ saṃvayaṃtī | yajñasyānuṣṭhīyamānasya peśo rūpaṃ nirmātumiti śeṣaḥ | yajñaṃ nirvartayituṃ tadavayavānukrameṇānuṣṭhāpayitryāvityarthaḥ | ahorātrābhyāṃ hi yajñāstanyaṃte | sudughe suṣṭhu phalasya dogdhryau [?] payasvatī udakavatyau | ahorātrābhyāṃ khalu vṛṣṭirjāyate | evaṃ mahāsubhāve ahorātradevate asmadyajñaṃ nirvahatāmityarthaḥ ‖*

*(In the printing of दोग्ध्र्यौ the letters are blurred: [?]. The sentence कर्तरि निष्ठा is a grammatical remark that the participle उक्षिते has the active sense; no sūtra numbers printed.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 6)**

(Kannada, translated:) सनता (*sanatā*) — ancient women; उक्षिते (*ukṣite*) — those who shower fruit; [or सनता (*sanatā*) — with hymns; उक्षिते (*ukṣite*) — those who are worshipped;] सुदुघे (*sudughe*) — those who milk out desired objects; पयस्वती (*payasvatī*) — those who possess water, both; उषासानक्ता (*uṣāsānaktā*) — the deities Day and Night; यज्ञस्य (*yajñasya*) — of the sacrifice;

*(The Pratipadārtha continues on p. 463.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 6, continued)**

(Kannada, translated:) पेशः (*peśaḥ*) — the form (in order to build); साधु (*sādhu*) — excellent; नः (*naḥ*) — our; अपांसि (*apāṃsi*) — deeds, with reference to; ततं (*tataṃ*) — extended; तंतुं (*taṃtuṃ*) — the part of the sacrifice that stands in the place of the thread; रण्विते (*raṇvite*) — working together; वय्या इव (*vayyā iva*) — like weaving women; समीची (*samīcī*) — mutually favourable; संवयंती (*saṃvayaṃtī*) — they carry out the sacrifice.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada, translated:) "The deities Day and Night, ancient, bestowers of fruit, who sprinkle (what is desired) for the worshippers and possess water, in order to build the form of the sacrifice, with reference to our excellent deeds, work together like weaving women on the extended thread-like part of the sacrifice, and carry out the sacrifice, mutually favourable."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

In regard of our good deeds, Day and Night, perpetually reverenced, are interweaving in concert, like two famous female weavers, the extended, thread (to complete) the web of the sacrifice, liberal yielders (of rewards) containers of water.

*(The comma after "extended" is as printed. No Special Topics are printed for Ṛk 6.)*

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> दैव्या॒ होता॑रा प्रथ॒मा वि॒दुष्ट॑र ऋ॒जु य॑क्षतः॒ सम्ऋ॒चा व॒पुष्ट॑रा ।
> दे॒वान्यजं॑तावृतु॒था समं॑जतो॒ नाभा॑ पृथि॒व्या अधि॒ सानु॑षु त्रि॒षु ॥ ७ ॥

> *daivyā hotārā prathamā viduṣṭara ṛju yakṣataḥ samṛcā vapuṣṭarā |*
> *devānyajaṃtāvṛtuthā samaṃjato nābhā pṛthivyā adhi sānuṣu triṣu ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> दैव्या । होतारा । प्रथमा । विदुःऽतरा । ऋजु । यक्षतः । सं । ऋचा । वपुःऽतरा ।
> देवान् । यजंता । ऋतुऽथा । सं । अंजतः । नाभा । पृथिव्याः । अधि । सानुषु ।
> त्रिषु ॥ ७ ॥

> *daivyā | hotārā | prathamā | viduḥ 'tarā | ṛju | yakṣataḥ | saṃ | ṛcā | vapuḥ 'tarā |*
> *devān | yajaṃtā | ṛtu 'thā | saṃ | aṃjataḥ | nābhā | pṛthivyāḥ | adhi | sānuṣu |*
> *triṣu ‖ 7 ‖*

*(Numeral: the Saṃhitā has 7; in the Pada the printed numeral looks like ४ [?], not zoomed, read as 7 by the sequence. The compound marks in विदुःऽतरा, वपुःऽतरा, ऋतुऽथा are the printed small subscript stroke.)*

### Printed p. 464 (PDF 485)

*(Header: "464", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 3", read from the strip. The numeral file has no rows for this page. The page continues Ṛk 7.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* The two divine Hotṛ forms of Agni, born of the heavenly Agni, are foremost, wisest and best-formed. They worship the gods in due season with the mantra, faultlessly, on the three high places of the uttaravedī.

> दैव्या । दिवि भवो दिव्योऽग्निः । तस्माद्दिव्यादग्नेर्जातौ होतारावाह्वातारौ देवानां होमनिष्पादकौ वाग्नी पार्थिवांतरिक्ष्यौ प्रथमा प्रथमं यष्टव्यौ विदुष्टरा विद्यत्तमौ [?] वपुष्टरा प्रकृष्टवपुषौ देवा ऋचा मंत्रेण ऋजु अविकलं यथा तथा सम्यक् यक्षतः । पूजयतः । ऋतुथा तत्तदृतौ तत्र तत्र काले देवान्यष्व्यान् [?] यजंतौ देवौ पृथिव्या नाभा नाभावुत्तरवेद्यामधि उपरि त्रिषु सानुषु समुच्छ्रितेषु प्रदेशेषु गार्हपत्यादिषु समंजतः । समांक्तां [?] ॥ अंजेर्लेट्यडागमः ॥

> *daivyā | divi bhavo divyo 'gniḥ | tasmāddivyādagnerjātau hotārāvāhvātārau devānāṃ homaniṣpādakau vāgnī pārthivāṃtarikṣyau prathamā prathamaṃ yaṣṭavyau viduṣṭarā vidyattamau [?] vapuṣṭarā prakṛṣṭavapuṣau devā ṛcā maṃtreṇa ṛju avikalaṃ yathā tathā samyak yakṣataḥ | pūjayataḥ | ṛtuthā tattadṛtau tatra tatra kāle devānyaṣvyān [?] yajaṃtau devau pṛthivyā nābhā nābhāvuttaravedyāmadhi upari triṣu sānuṣu samucchriteṣu pradeśeṣu gārhapatyādiṣu samaṃjataḥ | samāṃktāṃ [?] ‖ aṃjerleṭyaḍāgamaḥ ‖*

*(The last sentence अंजेर्लेट्यडागमः is a grammatical tail: the augment *aṭ* of the Leṭ of the root *añj*; no sūtra number printed.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 7)**

(Kannada, translated:) प्रथमा (*prathamā*) — (among the deities worthy of sacrifice) the chief; विदुष्टरा (*viduṣṭarā*) — the wisest among the learned; वपुष्टरा (*vapuṣṭarā*) — those with most excellent bodies; ऋचा (*ṛcā*) — with the mantra; ऋजु (*ṛju*) — without deficiency; सं यक्षतः (*saṃ yakṣataḥ*) — those who worship (the deities) fully; ऋतुथा (*ṛtuthā*) — at all the seasons of sacrifice; देवान् (*devān*) — with reference to the deities worthy of sacrifice; यजंतौ (*yajaṃtau*) — those who perform the sacrifice; दैव्या होतारा (*daivyā hotārā*) — the two forms of Agni who call the deities to the sacrifice, (together); पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*) — of the earth; नाभा अधि (*nābhā adhi*) — on the uttaravedī which is of the form of the navel; त्रिषु सानुषु (*triṣu sānuṣu*) — in the three high places, namely the Gārhapatya and the other fire-places; समंजतः (*samaṃjataḥ*) — let them be worshipped together.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada, translated:) "Chief among the deities worthy of sacrifice, the wisest of the learned, those of most excellent body, who worship the deities fully, without deficiency, with the mantra, who perform sacrifice for the deities at all the seasons of sacrifice, who call the deities to the sacrifice — the two forms of Agni called Daivya-hotārā — together on the uttaravedī, which is of the form of the navel of the earth, in the three high places such as the Gārhapatya, let them be worshipped together."

**English Translation** *(as printed)*

Let the two divine invokers of the gods, the first (to be reverenced), most wise, sincerely worshipping with sacred texts, most excellent in form, offering homage to the gods in due season, present oblations in the three high places upon the navel of the earth.

*(No Special Topics are printed for Ṛk 7.)*

#### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> सर॑स्वती सा॒धयं॑ती॒ धियं॑ न॒ ईळा॑ दे॒वी भार॑ती वि॒श्वतू॑र्तिः ।
> ति॒स्रो दे॒वीः स्व॒धया॑ ब॒र्हिरेदमच्छि॑द्रं पांतु शर॒णं नि॒षद्य॑ ॥ ८ ॥

> *sarasvatī sādhayaṃtī dhiyaṃ na īḷā devī bhāratī viśvatūrtiḥ |*
> *tisro devīḥ svadhayā barhiredamacchidraṃ pāṃtu śaraṇaṃ niṣadya ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सरस्वती । साधयंती । धियं । नः । इळा । देवी । भारती । विश्वऽतूर्तिः ।
> तिस्रः । देवीः । स्वधया । बर्हिः । आ । इदं । अच्छिद्रं । पांतु । शरणं । निऽसद्य ॥ ८ ॥

> *sarasvatī | sādhayaṃtī | dhiyaṃ | naḥ | iḷā | devī | bhāratī | viśva 'tūrtiḥ |*
> *tisraḥ | devīḥ | svadhayā | barhiḥ | ā | idaṃ | acchidraṃ | pāṃtu | śaraṇaṃ | ni 'sadya ‖ 8 ‖*

*(The compound marks in विश्वऽतूर्तिः and निऽसद्य are the printed small subscript stroke.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Sarasvatī, Iḷā and Bhāratī, the three goddesses, perfecting our understanding, are asked to come to the sacrificial house and protect this sacrifice from any flaw, because of the offering we have given.

> नोऽस्मदीयां धियं बुद्धिं योगं वा साधयंती निर्वर्तयंती सरस्वती इत्येतन्नामिका देवी भारती च विश्वतूर्तिर्विश्वानि तूर्णानि यस्याः सा तादृशी सर्वविषयगता वाक् । एतदुभयविशेषणं । तिस्रो देवीरेताः तिस्रो देव्यः स्वधयास्मद्दत्तहविषा निमित्तेनेदं बर्हिर्यज्ञमच्छिद्रं यथा तथा पांतु । पालयंतु । किं कृत्वा । शरणं योगगृहमानिषद्य आश्रित्य । यद्वा स्वधयेदं बर्हिरिमं यज्ञमागत्यास्मदीयं शरणं गृहं निषद्याच्छिद्रं यथा तथा पांतु ॥

> *no 'smadīyāṃ dhiyaṃ buddhiṃ yogaṃ vā sādhayaṃtī nirvartayaṃtī sarasvatī ityetannāmikā devī bhāratī ca viśvatūrtirviśvāni tūrṇāni yasyāḥ sā tādṛśī sarvaviṣayagatā vāk | etadubhayaviśeṣaṇaṃ | tisro devīretāḥ tisro devyaḥ svadhayāsmaddattahaviṣā nimittenedaṃ barhiryajñamacchidraṃ yathā tathā pāṃtu | pālayaṃtu | kiṃ kṛtvā | śaraṇaṃ yogagṛhamāniṣadya āśritya | yadvā svadhayedaṃ barhirimaṃ yajñamāgatyāsmadīyaṃ śaraṇaṃ gṛhaṃ niṣadyācchidraṃ yathā tathā pāṃtu ‖*

*(In the bhāṣya the name Iḷā is given as इळैतन्नामिका देवी, "the goddess of this name".)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 8)**

(Kannada, translated:) नः (*naḥ*) — our; धियं (*dhiyaṃ*) — the intellect, or the yoga; साधयंती (*sādhayaṃtī*) — the perfecting; सरस्वती (*sarasvatī*) — Sarasvatī; देवी (*devī*) — the divine-natured; इळा (*iḷā*) — the goddess Iḷā; विश्वतूर्तिः (*viśvatūrtiḥ*) — one who pervades everything, or the most excellent; भारती (*bhāratī*) — the goddess Bhāratī; तिस्रः देवीः (*tisraḥ devīḥ*) — these three deities pointed out above; स्वधया (*svadhayā*) — for the sake of the offering given (by us); शरणं (*śaraṇaṃ*) — the sacrificial house; आ निषद्य (*ā niṣadya*) — having resorted to; इदं बर्हिः (*idaṃ barhiḥ*) — this sacrifice; अच्छिद्रं (*acchidraṃ*) — so as not to be broken; पांतु (*pāṃtu*) — let them protect.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

(Kannada, translated:) "Sarasvatī who perfects our intellect, the divine goddess Iḷā, and Bhāratī, the most excellent — these three deities, for the sake of the offering given by us, resorting to the sacrificial house, let them protect this sacrifice so that it is not broken."

#### Ṛk 9

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> पि॒शंग॑रूपः सु॒भरो॑ वयो॒धाः श्रु॒ष्टी वी॒रो जा॑यते दे॒वका॑मः ।
> प्र॒जां त्वष्टा॒ वि ष्य॑तु॒ नाभि॑म॒स्मे अथा॑ दे॒वाना॒मप्ये॑तु॒ पाथः॑ ॥ ९ ॥

> *piśaṃgarūpaḥ subharo vayodhāḥ śruṣṭī vīro jāyate devakāmaḥ |*
> *prajāṃ tvaṣṭā vi ṣyatu nābhimasme athā devānāmapyetu pāthaḥ ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> पिशंगऽरूपः । सुऽभरः । वयःऽधाः । श्रुष्टी । वीरः । जायते । देवऽकामः ।
> प्रऽजां । त्वष्टा । वि । स्यतु । नाभिं । अस्मे इति । अथ । देवानां । अपि । एतु । पाथः ॥ ९ ॥

> *piśaṃga 'rūpaḥ | su 'bharaḥ | vayaḥ 'dhāḥ | śruṣṭī | vīraḥ | jāyate | deva 'kāmaḥ |*
> *pra 'jāṃ | tvaṣṭā | vi | syatu | nābhiṃ | asme iti | atha | devānāṃ | api | etu | pāthaḥ ‖ 9 ‖*

*(Read as printed: the Pada has स्यतु where the Saṃhitā has ष्यतु. The first word of the Pada, पिशंगऽरूपः, has the subscript stroke after the letter *ṅga*, read here as the compound mark. The numerals ९ in the Saṃhitā and Pada were read from the strip, not zoomed.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* This Ṛk is the ninth, the yājyā for the Tvaṣṭṛ animal-offering's cake. Sāyaṇa explains the child as golden-formed, a good bearer, giver of food, swift and heroic, and Tvaṣṭṛ as releasing the family-binding offspring.

> अथ पिशंगरूप इति नवमी त्वाष्ट्रे पशौ पुरोडाशस्य याज्या । पिशंगरूपः सुभरो वयोधाः प्रथमभाजं यशसं वयोधाम् । आ ३-८ । इति सूत्रितत्वात् । पाठस्तु ॥

> *atha piśaṃgarūpa iti navamī tvāṣṭre paśau puroḍāśasya yājyā | piśaṃgarūpaḥ subharo vayodhāḥ prathamabhājaṃ yaśasaṃ vayodhām | ā 3-8 | iti sūtritatvāt | pāṭhastu ‖*
>
> पिशंगरूपः सुवर्णवर्णो नानारूपो वा सुभरः शोभनयज्ञः शोभनभरणो वा वयोधा वयसोऽन्नस्य धारयिता दाता वा श्रुष्टी क्षिप्रगुणो वीरो विविधनि[?]रयिता देवकामो देवाः काम्यंते येन तादृशः पुत्रो जायते । जायुतामुत्सेद्यतां [?] त्वष्टुरनुग्रहात् । स च त्वष्टैतन्नामको देवोऽस्मे अस्मभ्यं नाभिं कुलस्य बंधिकां प्रजां पुत्रादिरूपां विष्यतु । विमुंचतु । एतरत्त्वित्यर्थः [?] । अथ अपि च देवानां संबंधि पाथोऽन्नमप्यस्मानेतु । गच्छतु । अपिः क्रियया वा संबध्यते । गच्छत्वित्यर्थः ॥

> *piśaṃgarūpaḥ suvarṇavarṇo nānārūpo vā subharaḥ śobhanayajñaḥ śobhanabharaṇo vā vayodhā vayaso 'nnasya dhārayitā dātā vā śruṣṭī kṣipraguṇo vīro vividhani[?]rayitā devakāmo devāḥ kāmyaṃte yena tādṛśaḥ putro jāyate | jāyutāmutsedyatāṃ [?] tvaṣṭuranugrahāt | sa ca tvaṣṭaitannāmako devo 'sme asmabhyaṃ nābhiṃ kulasya baṃdhikāṃ prajāṃ putrādirūpāṃ viṣyatu | vimuṃcatu | etarattvityarthaḥ [?] | atha api ca devānāṃ saṃbaṃdhi pātho 'nnamapyasmānetu | gacchatu | apiḥ kriyayā vā saṃbadhyate | gacchatvityarthaḥ ‖*

*(The reference "आ ३-८" after the quotation of the yājyā is printed so, in Kannada numerals, not zoomed; the abbreviation is left unexplained. Several words in the second paragraph are doubtful, see the [?] marks.)*

(Kannada, translated, begun; it continues on p. 467:) पिशंगरूपः (*piśaṃgarūpaḥ*) — one who has a golden form; सुभरः (*subharaḥ*) — one who carries out the excellent sacrifice; वयोधाः (*vayodhāḥ*) — one who holds food; श्रुष्टी (*śruṣṭī*) — (in actions) one who has brisk qualities, …

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 10)**

(Kannada, translated:) वनस्पतिः (*vanaspatiḥ*) — the deity presiding over the sacrificial post (yūpa); अवसृजन् (*avasṛjan*) — approving our rite; उप (*upa*) — near us; स्थात् (*sthāt*) — let him be; अग्निः (*agniḥ*) — Agni, the support of cooking; हविः (*haviḥ*) — the offering in the form of the animal; धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*) — by acts; सूदयाति (*sūdayāti*) — he prepares it; दैव्यः शमिता (*daivyaḥ śamitā*) — Agni, the Śamitṛ of the gods (who cuts the animal and prepares it); त्रिधा (*tridhā*) — in three ways; समक्तं (*samaktaṃ*) — sprinkled; हव्यं (*havyaṃ*) — the offering; प्रजानन् (*prajānan*) — knowing; देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*) — to the gods; उप नयतु (*upa nayatu*) — let him take and present it.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 10)**

(Kannada, translated:) "May the deity presiding over the sacrificial post, approving our rite, be near us. Agni, the support of cooking, prepares the offering in the form of the animal by acts. May Agni, the Śamitṛ of the gods, who cuts the animal and prepares it for the gods, knowing the offering sprinkled in three ways, take it to the gods and present it."

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 10)*

May Agni, who is Vanaspati, approving (of our rite), approach: and by his especial acts fully dress the victim; may the divine immolator convey the burnt-offering to the gods knowing it to have been thrice consecrated.

*(No Special Topics are printed for Ṛk 10.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 11)**

(Kannada, translated:) अस्य (*asya*) — for this Agni; घृतं (*ghṛtaṃ*) — ghee; योनिः (*yoniḥ*) — the cause of origin (therefore); घृतं (*ghṛtaṃ*) — ghee; मिमिक्षे (*mimikṣe*) — I sprinkle; घृते (*ghṛte*) — in ghee; श्रितः (*śritaḥ*) — (Agni) has taken refuge; अस्य (*asya*) — for this Agni; घृतमु (*ghṛtamu*) [as printed] — ghee itself; धाम (*dhāma*) — the support of radiance; वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*) — O Agni, who showers fruits; अनुष्वधं (*anuṣvadhaṃ*) — for all the offerings made; आ वह (*ā vaha*) — bring the gods; मादयस्व (*mādayasva*) — gladden them; स्वाहाकृतं (*svāhākṛtaṃ*) — offered with the call svāhā; हव्यं (*havyaṃ*) — the offering; वक्षि (*vakṣi*) — carry.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 11)**

(Kannada, translated:) "Ghee is the cause of origin of this Agni. He has taken refuge in ghee alone. Therefore I sprinkle ghee. For this Agni ghee alone is the support of radiance. O Agni, giver of fruits, bring the gods for all the offerings made. Gladden them, and carry the offering made with the call svāhā."

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 11)*

I sprinkle the butter, for butter is his birth-place, he is nourished by butter; butter is his radiance; Agni, showerer (of benefits), bring the gods to the offered oblation; exhilarate them; convey to them the offering that has been reverently sanctified.

*(No Special Topics are printed for Ṛk 11. A short rule closes the page below the English, ending Sūkta 3; no colophon is printed on this page.)*

## Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 1 — Sūkta 4

**Fourth sūkta** (printed heading: "ನಾಲ್ಕನೆಯ ಸೂಕ್ತವು").

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥** *(introduction to the sūkta)*

*Gist:* The sūkta हुवे वः (*huve vaḥ*) has nine Ṛks; the ṛṣi is Somāhuti Bhārgava, the deity Agni, the metre Triṣṭup. It is used in the Prātaranuvāka and the Āśvina-śastra, as Āśvalāyana's sūtra says.

> हुवे व इति नवर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तं । भार्गवः सोमाहुतिनामक ऋषिः । अग्निर्देवता । त्रिष्टुप् छंदः । हुवे नव सोमाहुतिर्भार्गवो हेत्यनुक्रमणिका ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोस्त्रैष्टुभे छंदसीदं । सूत्रितं च । हुवे वः सुद्योत्मानं नि होता होतृषदन इति सूक्ते ॥ आ. ४-१३ । इति ॥

> *huve va iti navarcaṃ caturthaṃ sūktaṃ | bhārgavaḥ somāhutināmaka ṛṣiḥ | agnirdevatā | triṣṭup chaṃdaḥ | huve nava somāhutirbhārgavo hetyanukramaṇikā ‖ prātaranuvākāśvinaśastrayostraiṣṭubhe chaṃdasīdaṃ | sūtritaṃ ca | huve vaḥ sudyotmānaṃ ni hotā hotṛṣadana iti sūkte ‖ ā. 4-13 | iti ‖*

**Anuvāda (Kannada, translated):** The sūkta beginning हुवे वः (*huve vaḥ*) is the fourth sūkta in the first Anuvāka. It has nine Ṛks. Somāhuti, born in the family of Bhṛgu, is the ṛṣi of this sūkta; Agni is the deity; the metre is Triṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: हुवे नव सोमाहुतिर्भार्गवो ह (*huve nava somāhutirbhārgavo ha*). The sūkta is applied (viniyoga) to the mantras in Triṣṭup metre at the time of the Prātaranuvāka and the recitation of the Āśvina-śastra mantras; this is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrautasūtra हुवे वः सुद्योत्मानं नि होता होतृषदन इति सूक्ते (*huve vaḥ sudyotmānaṃ ni hotā hotṛṣadana iti sūkte*) (Ā. 4-13, as printed; the last numeral line of the page reads "೪-◌೩", the middle digit blurred in the print, and the first reference on the page is "೪-೧೩").

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> हु॒वे वः॑ सु॒द्योत्मा॑नं सुवृ॒क्तिं वि॒शाम॒ग्निमति॑थिं सुप्र॒यसं॑ ।
> मि॒त्र इ॑व॒ यो दि॑धि॒षाय्यो॒ भूद्दे॒व आदे॑वे॒ जने॑ जा॒तवे॑दाः ॥ १ ॥

> *huve vaḥ sudyotmānaṃ suvṛktiṃ viśāmagnimatithiṃ suprayasaṃ |*
> *mitra iva yo didhiṣāyyo bhūddeva ādeve jane jātavedāḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> हुवे । वः । सुऽद्योत्मानं । सुऽवृक्तिं । विशां । अग्निं । अतिथिं । सुऽप्रयसं ।
> मित्रःऽइव । यः । दिधिषाय्यः । भूत् । देवः । आऽदेवे । जने । जातऽवेदाः ॥ १ ॥

> *huve | vaḥ | su 'dyotmānaṃ | su 'vṛktiṃ | viśāṃ | agniṃ | atithiṃ | su 'prayasaṃ |*
> *mitraḥ 'iva | yaḥ | didhiṣāyyaḥ | bhūt | devaḥ | ā 'deve | jane | jāta 'vedāḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

*(The compound stroke is printed in सुऽद्योत्मानं, सुऽवृक्तिं, सुऽप्रयसं, मित्रःऽइव, आऽदेवे and जातऽवेदाः. In the printed Pada the stroke after मित्रः appears directly before इव.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* The yajamānas are told that the speaker invokes for them Agni, well-shining and sinless, always worthy of honour like a guest; knowing all that is born, he supports all beings from men to gods like a friend.

> हे यजमाना वो युष्मदर्थमग्निं हुवे । आह्वयामि । कीदृशं तं । सुद्योत्मानं सुष्ठु द्योतमानं । सुवृक्तिं सुवर्जितं पाप्मैः शोभनस्तुतिं वा । विशां यजमानानामतिथिवत्सदा पूज्यं । सुप्रयसं शोभनहविर्लक्षणान्नं । किंच जातवेदा जातानां वेदिता यो देवोऽग्निर्मित्र इव सखेव आदित्य इव वा दीधिषाय्यो धारयिता भूत् । भवति । कुत्रेति उच्यते । आदेवे देवपर्यंते जने । मनुष्यप्रभृतिदेवपर्यंतेषु । तेषां धारकोऽभवदित्यर्थः ॥

> *he yajamānā vo yuṣmadarthamagniṃ huve | āhvayāmi | kīdṛśaṃ taṃ | sudyotmānaṃ suṣṭhu dyotamānaṃ | suvṛktiṃ suvarjitaṃ pāpmaiḥ śobhanastutiṃ vā | viśāṃ yajamānānāmatithivatsadā pūjyaṃ | suprayasaṃ śobhanahavirlakṣaṇānnaṃ | kiṃca jātavedā jātānāṃ veditā yo devo 'gnirmitra iva sakheva āditya iva vā dīdhiṣāyyo dhārayitā bhūt | bhavati | kutreti ucyate | ādeve devaparyaṃte jane | manuṣyaprabhṛtidevaparyaṃteṣu | teṣāṃ dhārako 'bhavadityarthaḥ ‖*

*(The word पाप्मैः (*pāpmaiḥ*) is printed so, here and again in the Special Topics; taken at face value. No sūtra reference or grammatical tail is printed.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 1)**

(Kannada, translated:) (O yajamānas) वः (*vaḥ*) — for you; सुद्योत्मानं (*sudyotmānaṃ*) — one who has excellent radiance; सुवृक्तिं (*suvṛktiṃ*) — one free from sin, or one who has excellent praise; विशां (*viśāṃ*) — for the yajamānas; अतिथिं (*atithiṃ*) — one to be honoured like a guest; सुप्रयसं (*suprayasaṃ*) — one who has food in the form of the offering; — such अग्निं (*agniṃ*) — Agni — हुवे (*huve*) — I call, praying; जातवेदाः (*jātavedāḥ*) — he who has knowledge of all that is born; यः देवः (*yaḥ devaḥ*) — which god, of divine nature, that same Agni; मित्र इव (*mitra iva*) — like a friend, or like the god Mitra; आ देवे जने (*ā deve jane*) — the beings from men up to gods; दिधिषाय्यः (*didhiṣāyyaḥ*) — as the one who holds (them); भूत् (*bhūt*) — he is.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 1)**

(Kannada, translated:) "O yajamānas, on your behalf I invoke in prayer that Agni who has excellent radiance, who is free from sin and has excellent radiance, who is to be honoured by the yajamānas like a guest, and who has food in the form of the offering. That Agni, who knows all that is born and is of divine nature, has been the guardian, like a friend, of the beings from men up to the gods."

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 1)*

I invoke, on your behalf, the resplendent, the sinless Agni, the guest of mortals, the accepter of (sacrificial) food, who, knowing all that has been born, is like a friend, the supporter (of all beings), from men to gods.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 1)**

(Kannada, translated:) Addressing the yajamānas, the ṛṣi, the seer of the mantra, has said that on their behalf he invokes Agni, who is सुवृक्तिं—सुवर्जितं पाप्मैः (*suvṛktiṃ—suvarjitaṃ pāpmaiḥ*): "pāpa" means that he is freed from the actions that produce sorrow; or शोभनस्तुतिं वा (*śobhanastutiṃ vā*): he is praised with auspicious hymns. Agni is also described as being always worthy of worship by the yajamāna, like a guest.

जातवेदाः यः देवः मित्र इव दिधिषाय्यः अग्निः सखेव आदित्य इव वा मनुष्यप्रभृति देवपर्यंतेषु जनेषु धारयिता भवति (*jātavedāḥ yaḥ devaḥ mitra iva didhiṣāyyaḥ agniḥ sakheva āditya iva vā manuṣyaprabhṛti devaparyaṃteṣu janeṣu dhārayitā bhavati*) — Agni, who is all-knowing, is the supporter, like a friend, of all beings from men up to the gods; that is, as a friend does good to all beings he is their well-wisher, or, like the Sun, he protects them. This is explained in two ways.

अतिथिं—अतिथिवत्पूज्यं । दर्शादितिथिमुपेक्ष्य आगंतारं वा । (*atithiṃ—atithivatpūjyaṃ | darśāditithimupekṣya āgaṃtāraṃ vā |*) — Agni is worthy of honour by the yajamāna like a guest who has come to the house. Or, he is explained as one who comes according to the wish of the yajamānas who perform sacrifices (darśa-pūrṇamāsa and the others) following the tithis such as amāvāsyā.

The Niruktakāra, citing the Ṛk (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-4-5, as printed after the verse; the file and the strip agree) —

> जुष्वो दमूना अतिथिर्दुरोण इमं नो यज्ञमुप याहि विद्वान् ।
> विश्वा अग्ने अभियुजो विहत्या शत्रूयतामा भरा योजनानि ॥

> *juṣvo damūnā atithirduroṇa imaṃ no yajñamupa yāhi vidvān |*
> *viśvā agne abhiyujo vihatyā śatrūyatāmā bharā yojanāni ‖*

*(शत्रूयतामा (*śatrūyatāmā*) and योजनानि (*yojanāni*) are copied as printed, not zoomed.)*

— and then having said:

> अतिथिरभ्यतितो गृहान् भवति । अभ्येति तिथिषु परकुलानीति वा परगृहाणीति वा ।
> अयमपीतरोऽतिथेरेतस्मादेव ।

> *atithirabhyatito gṛhān bhavati | abhyeti tithiṣu parakulānīti vā paragṛhāṇīti vā |*
> *ayamapītaro 'titheretasmādeva |*

*(Reference printed: Ni. 4-4; the file and the strip agree. The last words are read so from the strip, not zoomed; the same sentence is printed a little lower as अयमपीतरोऽतिथिरेतस्मादेव (*ayamapītaro 'tithiretasmādeva*).)*

— gives this explanation of the word. Durgācārya, commenting on it, says:

> गृहान् अभि आभिमुख्येन असौ अतितो भवति

> *gṛhān abhi ābhimukhyena asau atito bhavati*

— "seeking houses, he goes about; for that reason he is called atithi". Or, on days such as amāvāsyā he comes to the houses of those who perform sacrifice, and therefore Agni is called atithi. Or:

> अभ्येति तिथिषु परकुलानि पौर्णमास्यादिषु यजमानकुलानि अभ्यागच्छति इति अतिथिः । अयमपीतरोऽतिथिरेतस्मादेव ।

> *abhyeti tithiṣu parakulāni paurṇamāsyādiṣu yajamānakulāni abhyāgacchati iti atithiḥ | ayamapītaro 'tithiretasmādeva |*

That is, he goes on the other tithis (days) to the sacrificial houses of persons of other families, and on sacrifice days such as Paurṇamāsī he comes to the houses of the yajamānas; for these two reasons the name atithi has come to Agni; this is the meaning explained.

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> इ॒मं वि॒धन्तो॑ अ॒पां स॒धस्थे॑ द्वि॒ता द॑धु॒र्भृग॑वो वि॒क्ष्वा॒३॒॑योः ।
> ए॒ष विश्वा॑न्य॒भ्य॑स्तु॒ भूमा॑ दे॒वाना॑म॒ग्निर॑र॒तिर्जी॒राश्वः॑ ॥ २ ॥

> *imaṃ vidhanto apāṃ sadhasthe dvitā dadhurbhṛgavo vikṣvāyoḥ |*
> *eṣa viśvānyabhyastu bhūmā devānāmagniraratirjīrāśvaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> इमं । विधन्तः । अपां । सधऽस्थे । द्विता । अदधुः । भृगवः । विक्षु । आयोः ।
> एष । विश्वानि । अभि । अस्तु [?] । भूम [?] । देवानां । अग्निः । अरतिः । जीरऽअश्वः ॥ २ ॥

> *imaṃ | vidhantaḥ | apāṃ | sadha 'sthe | dvitā | adadhuḥ | bhṛgavaḥ | vikṣu | āyoḥ |*
> *eṣa | viśvāni | abhi | astu [?] | bhūma [?] | devānāṃ | agniḥ | aratiḥ | jīra 'aśvaḥ ‖ 2 ‖*

*(The Pada reads "एष" without visarga, as printed. For अभि । अस्तु the strip seems to show a long ā-sign (आस्तु); अस्तु is written, [?]. भूम is written as printed, a plain ma with no ā, while the Saṃhitā has भूमा; this is repeated in the bhāṣya and Pratipadārtha.)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* The Bhṛgus, our ancient sages, served Agni and made him present twice, in the atmosphere and among the yajamāna's ṛtviks; may he, lord of the gods and swift-mounted, overcome all our adversaries.

> इममग्निं विधन्तः परिचरन्तो भृगवोऽस्मत्पूर्वे महर्षयोऽपां सधस्थे सहस्थानेऽन्तरिक्ष आयोर्मनुष्यस्य यजमानस्य स्वभूतासु विक्षु प्रजास्वृत्विक्षु तेषां मध्ये च द्विता द्वयोः स्थानादधुः । अधारयन् ॥ दधातेर्लजः [?] रूपं ॥ एषोऽग्निर्भूम भूम्नात्यर्थं विश्वानि भूतजातान्यस्मद्विरोधीन्यभ्यस्तु । अभिभवतु । स कीदृशः । देवानामरतिरीश्वरः । तेषां मध्ये शीघ्रमरणशीलो वाऽस्मद्यागं प्रति । तथा जीराश्वः क्षिप्राश्वः ॥

> *imamagniṃ vidhantaḥ paricaranto bhṛgavo 'smatpūrve maharṣayo 'pāṃ sadhasthe sahasthāne 'ntarikṣa āyormanuṣyasya yajamānasya svabhūtāsu vikṣu prajāsvṛtvikṣu teṣāṃ madhye ca dvitā dvayoḥ sthānādadhuḥ | adhārayan ‖ dadhāterlajaḥ [?] rūpaṃ ‖ eṣo 'gnirbhūma bhūmnātyarthaṃ viśvāni bhūtajātānyasmadvirodhīnyabhyastu | abhibhavatu | sa kīdṛśaḥ | devānāmaratirīśvaraḥ | teṣāṃ madhye śīghramaraṇaśīlo vā 'smadyāgaṃ prati | tathā jīrāśvaḥ kṣiprāśvaḥ ‖*

*(The grammatical tail, "of the root दधाति (*dadhāti*): this is the form" (अधारयन् । दधातेर्लजः [?] रूपं), is given as printed; the letters after दधातेर् (*dadhāter*) are doubtful. No sūtra number is printed.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 2)**

(Kannada, translated:) इमं (*imaṃ*) — this Agni; विधन्तः (*vidhantaḥ*) — serving; भृगवः (*bhṛgavaḥ*) — the Bhṛgu ṛṣis; अपां सधस्थे (*apāṃ sadhasthe*) — in the atmosphere; आयोः विक्षु (*āyoḥ vikṣu*) — in the company of the ṛtviks belonging to the yajamāna; द्विता (*dvitā*) — from two places, or twice; अदधुः (*adadhuḥ*) — made (him) manifest; देवानां (*devānāṃ*) — of the gods; अरतिः (*aratiḥ*) — the lord; जीराश्वः (*jīrāśvaḥ*) — he who is mounted on a swift horse; एषः अग्निः (*eṣaḥ agniḥ*) — this Agni; भूम (*bhūma*) — abundantly; विश्वानि (*viśvāni*) — all our enemies; अभ्यस्तु (*abhyastu*) — may he conquer and destroy.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 2)**

(Kannada, translated:) "The Bhṛgu ṛṣis who served this Agni made him manifest twice: once in the atmosphere, and once on earth among the ṛtviks; thus in two places, twice. May this Agni, who is lord of the gods and mounted on a swift horse, completely conquer and destroy all our enemies."

### Printed p. 474 (PDF 495)

*(Header: "474", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 4", read from the strip. The numeral file gives only a garbled line, with the final "4" agreeing. Not zoomed.)*

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 2)*

The Bhrigus, worshipping Agni, have twice made him manifest, (once) in the abode of the waters, and (once) amongst the sons of men; may that Agni, the sovereign of the gods mounted on a rapid courser, ever overcome all (our foes).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 2)**

(Kannada, translated:) Here the word भृगवः (*bhṛgavaḥ*) is explained, in the bhāṣya, as अस्मत्पूर्वे महर्षयः (*asmatpūrve maharṣayaḥ*): great sages more ancient than Gṛtsamada, the seer of the mantra. And since Gṛtsamada belonged to the family of Bhṛgu, it is natural that he should call the earlier ṛṣis of the Bhṛgu family his forebears. *(In the strip the name is printed ಗೃತ್ಸವದ-; Gṛtsamada is read, as the ṛṣi of this Maṇḍala.)*

आयोः विक्षु—मनुष्यस्य यजमानस्य स्वभूतासु प्रजासु ऋत्विक्षु (*āyoḥ vikṣu—manuṣyasya yajamānasya svabhūtāsu prajāsu ṛtvikṣu*) — Explaining the word आयु (*āyu*), which denotes man, as "yajamāna", the commentary says that because the ṛtviks, sons, grandsons and the rest are the yajamāna's own people, the great sages made Agni arise in two places: in the atmosphere, that is, in the form of lightning, and in the houses of the yajamāna's own ṛtviks and subjects. That is, it is explained that Agni exists in two ways: in the atmosphere in the form of lightning, and, for the sacrifice, among the ṛtviks.

एषः भूम विश्वानि अभ्यस्तु—अग्निः (भूम्ना) अत्यर्थं अस्मद्विरोधीनि भूतजातानि अभिभवतु (*eṣaḥ bhūma viśvāni abhyastu—agniḥ (bhūmnā) atyarthaṃ asmadvirodhīni bhūtajātāni abhibhavatu*) — The yajamāna's wish is described: may Agni overcome all the creatures that belong to the class of our enemies, we who are the yajamānas.

देवानां अरतिः—अरतिरीश्वरः । शीघ्रमरणशीलो वा (*devānāṃ aratiḥ—aratirīśvaraḥ | śīghramaraṇaśīlo vā*) — Two meanings are given for the word अरति (*arati*): that Agni is the ruler of the gods, or that among the gods he is the one who comes to the sacrifice most quickly of all.

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अ॒ग्निं दे॒वासो॒ मानु॑षीषु वि॒क्षु प्रि॒यं धुः॑ क्षे॒ष्यन्तो॒ न मि॒त्रं ।

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Before leaving for heaven the gods placed Agni among men as a friend to guard the house, as a man going abroad for wealth leaves a friend; he increases the offerer's wealth and shines through all nights.

> देवासो देवाः क्षेष्यन्तः स्वर्गं प्रति गच्छन्तः सन्तः पूर्वं मानुषीषु मनुष्यसंबन्धिनीषु विक्षु प्रजासु प्रियं देवानां प्रीणयितारमग्निं धुः । अधुः स्थापितवन्तः । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । क्षेष्यन्तो मित्रं न । रायं प्रति गच्छन्तो नरा मित्रं प्रियं सखायं स्वगृहरक्षार्थं स्थापयन्ति । तद्वत् । स एवं देवैः स्थापितो योऽग्निर्दास्वते हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय तदर्थं दमे तदीये यागगृह आ आहितः स्थापितो दक्षाय्यः समर्धयिता दाता वा सोऽग्निरुशतीः कामयमाना ऊर्म्या रात्रीः सर्वासु रात्रिषु आदीदयेत् [?] । दीप्यते सर्वतः । सर्वरात्रीरादीपयेति वा ॥

> *devāso devāḥ kṣeṣyantaḥ svargaṃ prati gacchantaḥ santaḥ pūrvaṃ mānuṣīṣu manuṣyasaṃbandhinīṣu vikṣu prajāsu priyaṃ devānāṃ prīṇayitāramagniṃ dhuḥ | adhuḥ sthāpitavantaḥ | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | kṣeṣyanto mitraṃ na | rāyaṃ prati gacchanto narā mitraṃ priyaṃ sakhāyaṃ svagṛharakṣārthaṃ sthāpayanti | tadvat | sa evaṃ devaiḥ sthāpito yo 'gnirdāsvate havirdattavate yajamānāya tadarthaṃ dame tadīye yāgagṛha ā āhitaḥ sthāpito dakṣāyyaḥ samardhayitā dātā vā so 'gniruśatīḥ kāmayamānā ūrmyā rātrīḥ sarvāsu rātriṣu ādīdayet [?] | dīpyate sarvataḥ | sarvarātrīrādīpayeti vā ‖*

*(No sūtra number or separate grammatical tail is printed. The word at "आदीदयेत्" is doubtful in the strip. The line break falls between आ (*ā*) and आहितः (*āhitaḥ*).)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 3)**

(Kannada, translated:) क्षेष्यन्तः (*kṣeṣyantaḥ*) — men who go out for the sake of wealth; मित्रं न (*mitraṃ na*) — as they place their friends (to guard their house); देवासः (*devāsaḥ*) — the gods; क्षेष्यन्तः (*kṣeṣyantaḥ*) — when going as dwellers in heaven; मानुषीषु (*mānuṣīṣu*) — belonging to men; विक्षु (*vikṣu*) — among the people; प्रियं (*priyaṃ*) — Agni, who gives pleasure to the gods; धुः (*dhuḥ*) — they established; यः (*yaḥ*) — which Agni, established by the gods; दास्वते (*dāsvate*) — for the yajamāna who offers the oblation; दमे (*dame*) — in his house of sacrifice; आ (*ā*) — being established; दक्षाय्यः (*dakṣāyyaḥ*) — who increases (his wealth); सः (*saḥ*) — that Agni; उशतीः (*uśatīḥ*) — desired by him; ऊर्म्याः (*ūrmyāḥ*) — in all the nights; आ दीदयत् (*ā dīdayat*) — shines.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 3)**

(Kannada, translated:) "When the gods went to heaven to dwell, they established among men Agni, who gives pleasure to the gods, as a man who goes out for wealth places his friend to guard his house. The Agni who, established in the house of the yajamāna who offers oblations, increases his wealth, shines in all the nights that he desires."

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 3)*

The gods, intending to dwell (in heaven), left, as a dear friend amongst the human races, that Agni, who, present in the chamber of sacrifice, is bounteous to the donor of offerings; aud [sic] shines on the nights when he is wished for.

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Agni's growth is delightful and resounding; when he spreads through the herbs and shakes his flames, he is like a chariot-horse flicking its tail to drive off biting flies.

> अस्याग्नेः पुष्टिः शरीरवृद्धी रण्वा रमणीया शब्दयुक्ता वा । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । स्वस्य पुष्टिरिव । यथा लोके स्वकीया पुष्टिः स्वस्मै रमणीया भवति तद्वत् । यद्वास्याग्नेः संबन्धिनी पुष्टिर्यथा यजमानविषया रण्वा तद्वत् । किंच हियानस्य समृद्धिं गच्छतो व्याप्नुवतो धक्षोः काष्ठान् दिधक्षोर्दग्धुमिच्छोरस्याग्नेः संदृष्टिः संदर्शनाविर्भावोऽपि रण्वा । योऽग्निरोषधीषु काष्ठेषु जिह्वां ज्वालां । जात्येकवचनं । ज्वाला [?] विभरिभ्रत् । अत्यर्थं विहरति । कंपयतीत्यर्थः ॥ हरतेर्यज्लुगन्तत्वेन दाधर्त्यादिषु । पा. ७-४-६५ । निपातिताल्लेट्यैडागमः । युब्योगादनिघातः [?] ॥ तत्र दृष्टान्तः । रथ्यो रथाहोऽत्यो [?] न वाजी यथा वारान् दंशवारणसाधनान्वालान् दोधवीति । कंपयति तद्वत् । योऽग्निर्ज्वालाः कंपयति अस्याग्नेः पुष्टी रण्वेति ॥

> *asyāgneḥ puṣṭiḥ śarīravṛddhī raṇvā ramaṇīyā śabdayuktā vā | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | svasya puṣṭiriva | yathā loke svakīyā puṣṭiḥ svasmai ramaṇīyā bhavati tadvat | yadvāsyāgneḥ saṃbandhinī puṣṭiryathā yajamānaviṣayā raṇvā tadvat | kiṃca hiyānasya samṛddhiṃ gacchato vyāpnuvato dhakṣoḥ kāṣṭhān didhakṣordagdhumicchorasyāgneḥ saṃdṛṣṭiḥ saṃdarśanāvirbhāvo 'pi raṇvā | yo 'gniroṣadhīṣu kāṣṭheṣu jihvāṃ jvālāṃ | jātyekavacanaṃ | jvālā [?] vibharibhrat | atyarthaṃ viharati | kaṃpayatītyarthaḥ ‖ harateryajlugantatvena dādhartyādiṣu | pā. 7-4-65 | nipātitālleṭyaiḍāgamaḥ | yubyogādanighātaḥ [?] ‖ tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | rathyo rathāho 'tyo [?] na vājī yathā vārān daṃśavāraṇasādhanānvālān dodhavīti | kaṃpayati tadvat | yo 'gnirjvālāḥ kaṃpayati asyāgneḥ puṣṭī raṇveti ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 4)**

(Kannada, translated:) रथ्यः (*rathyaḥ*) — fit to carry a chariot; अत्यः (*atyaḥ*) — the horse; वारान् (*vārān*) — the tuft of his tail which drives away the gnats (soḷḷe); दोधवीति न (*dodhavīti na*) — as it flicks it to and fro; यः (*yaḥ*) — which Agni; ओषधीषु (*oṣadhīṣu*) — in wood and the like; जिह्वां (*jihvāṃ*) — his flame, which has the form of a tongue; वि भरिभ्रत् (*vi bharibhrat*) — spreads out in various directions and goes about; अस्य (*asya*) — of that Agni, the nourished (grown) spread; स्वस्य (*svasya*) — of the beholder (the printed word is drashṭṛvina, "of the seer"); पुष्टिः इव (*puṣṭiḥ iva*) — like the growth of one's own body; रण्वा (*raṇvā*) — is delightful; हियानस्य (*hiyānasya*) — of him who grows and spreads; धक्षोः (*dhakṣoḥ*) — of him who burns wood and the like, that same Agni; संदृष्टिः (*saṃdṛṣṭiḥ*) — the sight, which is delightful, is also attractive.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 4)**

(Kannada, translated:) "Just as a horse fit to carry a chariot flicks the tuft of its tail, which drives away gnats, to and fro, so the Agni who spreads his tongue-like flame in all directions in wood and the like, goes about: the spread of that Agni, which is full of growth, is delightful like the growth of one's own body. And the sight of that same Agni, who burns and spreads through wood and the like, is attractive as well."

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 4)*

The cherishing of Agni is as agreeable as (the cherishing) of one's self; (pleasant) is his appearance, when spreading abroad, and consuming (the fuel); he brandishes his flame amongst the bushes, as a chariot-horse lashes with his tail.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 4)**

(Kannada, translated; lemmata in Sanskrit as printed.)

> अस्य पुष्टिः रण्वा स्वस्य पुष्टिरिव—
> अग्नेः शरीरवृद्धिः रमणीया शब्दयुक्ता वा ।

> *asya puṣṭiḥ raṇvā svasya puṣṭiriva—*
> *agneḥ śarīravṛddhiḥ ramaṇīyā śabdayuktā vā |*

The growth of Agni's body is delightful, or it is accompanied by sound. The illustration for this matter has been given.

> यथा लोके स्वकीया पुष्टिं स्वस्मै रमणीयो—

> *yathā loke svakīyā puṣṭiṃ svasmai ramaṇīyo—*

As in the world the bodily nourishment of living beings is beneficial to each, so this is the illustration for the growth of Agni's body.

> यद्वा अस्याग्नेः संबन्धिनी पुष्टिः यजमानविषया रण्वा स्वस्याग्नेः पुष्टिः यथा रण्वा तद्वत्—

> *yadvā asyāgneḥ saṃbandhinī puṣṭiḥ yajamānaviṣayā raṇvā svasyāgneḥ puṣṭiḥ yathā raṇvā tadvat—*

As the growth of this Agni from the oblations offered by the yajamānas is delightful to the yajamānas, so this Agni's own bodily growth is also a source of happiness: another meaning is given.

*(The strip prints रण्वा (*raṇvā*) in the first line with the virāma sign unclear (ರಣಾ); रण्वा is written, [?].)*

> हियानस्य धक्षोः संदृष्टिः रण्वा—
> समृद्धिं गच्छतो काष्ठान् दग्धुमिच्छोः अस्याग्नेः संदर्शनाविर्भावोऽपि रण्वा ।

> *hiyānasya dhakṣoḥ saṃdṛṣṭiḥ raṇvā—*
> *samṛddhiṃ gacchato kāṣṭhān dagdhumicchoḥ asyāgneḥ saṃdarśanāvirbhāvo 'pi raṇvā |*

The Kannada explains: the forest herbs and the like grow; Agni, wishing to burn them, makes himself manifest, and shining brightly, he is delightful to all.

*(In the next passage the final n-sign of वारान् (*vārān*) and वालान् (*vālān*) is printed as a small mark; both are read as in the bhāṣya on p. 477.)*

> रथ्यः अत्योन वारान् दोधवीति—
> रथार्हः वाजी यथा दंशवारणसाधनान् वालान् कंपयति तद्वत् अग्निः काष्ठेषु ज्वालाः कंपयति—

> *rathyaḥ atyona vārān dodhavīti—*
> *rathārhaḥ vājī yathā daṃśavāraṇasādhanān vālān kaṃpayati tadvat agniḥ kāṣṭheṣu jvālāḥ kaṃpayati—*

As a horse that draws the chariot swings its tail to and fro, to drive off the flies and the like that torment its body, so Agni, when he pervades the wood, spreads his flames on every side and makes them tremble. The word अत्य (*atya*) is read by Yāska among the names of the horse (Ni. 2-27, as printed; the file agrees).

The Kannada then adds: In this Ṛk Agni in the form of a forest fire (the "kāḍukiccu") is described. As each man's bodily nourishment is beneficial and pleasant to him, so Agni, when he has grown great and burns wood and the like with a roar, is delightful and gladdening to the people who watch him. An illustration is given here. When gnats settle on a horse's back and bite it, the horse does nothing but swing its tail around to drive them off. In the same way Agni spreads his flames on every side, surrounds trees and the like, and burns them: this is the meaning described here. And it is also said that, although such a sight is terrifying, in one way it is attractive, or even delightful, to look at.

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

*(The strip prints जुजुर्वाँ (*jujurvāṃ*) with a small sign above the ā-stroke; it is written as a chandrabindu.)*

> आ यन्मे॒ अभ्वं॑ व॒नदः॒ पन॑न्तो॒शिग्भ्यो॒ नामि॑मीत॒ वर्ण॑म् ।
> स चि॒त्रेण॑ चिकिते॒ रंसु॑ भा॒सा जु॑जु॒र्वाँ यो मुहु॒रा युवा॒ भूत् ॥ ५ ॥

(Kannada, translated:) यत् (*yat*) — which Agni; अभ्वं (*abhvaṃ*) — greatness; मे (*me*) — my kinsmen; वनदः (*vanadaḥ*) — causing a loud sound; आ पनन्त (*ā pananta*) — praise on every side; सः (*saḥ*) — that Agni; उशिग्भ्यः (*uśigbhyaḥ*) — to the priests who wish to see his form; वर्णं (*varṇaṃ*) — his own delightful form; नामिमीत (*nāmimīta*) — creates and shows (and); रंसु (*raṃsu*) — when delightful oblations such as ājya are offered; चित्रेण (*citreṇa*) — of manifold form; भासा (*bhāsā*) — by radiance; चिकिते (*cikite*) — he becomes manifest; यः (*yaḥ*) — which Agni; जुजुर्वान् (*jujurvān*) — he who grows old (that very one); मुहुः (*muhuḥ*) — again and again (by the offering of ājya-oblations); आ युवा भूत् (*ā yuvā bhūt*) — becomes young.

### Printed p. 480 (PDF 501)

*(Header: "480", "Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā", "[Maṃ. 2 A. 1 Sū. 4", read from the strip, not zoomed. The numeral file has two rows, both Nighaṇṭu references; they agree with my reading.)*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 5)**

(Kannada, translated:) The Agni whose greatness my kinsmen praise on every side with a loud sound makes and shows his own delightful form to the priests who wish to see his form; and when delightful oblations such as ājya are offered, he shines with a radiance of many forms. In the time of growing old, by the offering of ājya-oblations he attains youth again.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 5)*

Whose greatness my colleagues loudly extol, who has manifested his real form to the priests, who is recognized at oblations by his variegated radiance, and who though frequently growing old, again and again becomes young.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 5)**

(Kannada, translated; lemmata in Sanskrit as printed.)

> अभ्वं वनदः आ पनन्त—
> यस्य महत्त्वं संभक्तारः यद्वा वनदोऽवनदो भृशं शब्दयन्तः स्तोतारः समन्तात् स्तुवन्ति—

> *abhvaṃ vanadaḥ ā panan ta—*
> *yasya mahattvaṃ saṃbhaktāraḥ yadvā vanado 'vanado bhṛśaṃ śabdayantaḥ stotāraḥ samantāt stuvanti—*

The Kannada says that the word अभ्व (*abhva*) is read by Yāska among the names of "great" (Ni. 3-13, as printed; the file agrees). Here it is used in the sense of Agni's greatness. For the word वनद (*vanada*) the meaning has been given as "those who make the greatness manifest" or "those who sound loudly". When the yajamāna's priests praise Agni, they either make his abundant greatness manifest by hymns, or praise him with a loud sound, so that all may hear.

> उशिग्भ्यः वर्णं नामिमीत—

> *uśigbhyaḥ varṇaṃ nāmimīta—*

The meaning is: Agni creates for the priests who wish to see his form a form suited to his greatness. The word उशिक् (*uśik*, with the sense "who desires") is said in the kānti-karmas (Ni. 3-9, as printed; the file agrees), and Yāska has also explained it as उशिग्वष्टेः कान्तिकर्मणः (*uśigvaṣṭeḥ kāntikarmaṇaḥ*) (Ni. 6-[?], as printed; the numeral after the 6 is damaged and not given).

*(The printed word is ವಸ್ಟೇಃ; it is written as वष्टेः (*vaṣṭeḥ*), [?].)*

> रंसु—चित्रेण चिकिते

> *raṃsu—citreṇa cikite*

The Kannada says that it is explained: this Agni shines, through the offering of oblations such as ājya, with the lustre of delightful things such as gold. That is to say, Agni's flames, with many kinds of colour (red, golden, white and the like), are delightful to look at.

> जुजुर्वान् मुहुः आ युवा—
> ज्वालोपशमे जीर्णः सन् [?] स एव पुनः पुनः विश्रयिता [?] तरुणो वा भवति ।

> *jujurvān muhuḥ ā yuvā—*
> *jvālopaśame jīrṇaḥ san [?] sa eva punaḥ punaḥ viśrayitā [?] taruṇo vā bhavati |*

*(The first Sanskrit line is followed on the strip by a passage that runs over the page break; the words after जीर्णः (*jīrṇaḥ*) are printed ಸ್ರ್ಣ ಸ; they are written सन् (*san*) [?].)*

The Kannada passage, which continues on the next page, begins: Agni, by withdrawing his flames, becomes devoid of radiance (kānti)...

### Printed p. 481 (PDF 502)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 25", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "481", read from the strip, not zoomed. The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

The sentence from the previous page continues: ...becomes devoid of radiance, yet again at the time of receiving the oblation he shines with youth. For an old man to become young is unknown in the world, but it is said as a contrast that Agni, though he grows old many times, shines with youth. Here the Kannada describes the following: when Agni is dying down he is in old age, but when sacrificial sticks, wood, ājya, oblations and the like are put into the few embers that remain and offered as homa, the Agni who had grown small becomes great again, shines with his flames, and is described here as having become young again, and so on.

> योऽग्निर्वना वनानि वृक्षसमूहान् ततृषाणो न तृषित इव । त्वरमाण इत्यर्थः । आभाति । आभासयति । दहतीत्यर्थः । यद्वा वना वने आभाति । किंच वार्ण उदकमिव पथा प्रवणेन मार्गेण गच्छति । तद्वत् इतस्ततो गच्छति । रथ्येव रथस्य वोढाश्व इव स्वानीत् । शब्दयति । यद्वा रथशब्दात् सोड्र्यादेशः [?] । यथा रथो युद्धमार्गेण गच्छन् स्वनति तद्वत् । किंच कृष्णाध्वा कृष्णवर्त्मा तपुस्तापको रण्वो रमणीय एवंभूतः सन् चिकेत । ज्ञायते । प्रकाशते इत्यर्थः । क इव । नभोभिर्नक्षत्रैः स्मयमानः प्रकाशमानो द्यौरिव द्युलोक इव । यद्वा नभोभिरन्तरिक्षप्रदेशविशेषैः स्मयमानः शोभमानो द्यौरादित्य इव । नीलवर्णान्तरिक्षछायोरादित्यो [?] यथा ज्ञायते तद्वत् स्वसंचारेण कृष्णीभूते मार्गे ज्ञायते । प्रकाशत इत्यर्थः ॥

*(Ṛk 6 continues from p. 481. This page has its Pratipadārtha, Bhāvārtha, printed English and the beginning of the Special Topics. In the Pratipadārtha the printed lemma is वार्ण with a sign that looks like ि, and it is written without it [?]. The second word of the Ṛk is printed ತತೃಷಾಣೋ and is written ततृषाणो as in the Pada.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 6)**

(Kannada, translated:) यः (*yaḥ*) — which Agni; वना (*vanā*) — the forests; ततृषाणो न (*tatṛṣāṇo na*) — like one who is thirsty; आ भाति (*ā bhāti*) — does he burn? [Or: वना (*vanā*) — in the forest; आ भाति (*ā bhāti*) — does he shine?] (and); वार्ण (*vārṇa*) — water, in what manner; पथा (*pathā*) — as it flows swiftly down a sloping region, so does he spread swiftly; रथ्या इव (*rathyā iva*) — like a war-horse that draws a chariot; स्वानीत् (*svānīt*) — he who makes a sound, as one who sounds (that Agni); कृष्णाध्वा (*kṛṣṇādhvā*) — having a path of black colour; तपुः (*tapuḥ*) — burning; रण्वः (*raṇvaḥ*) — (yet) delightful; नभोभिः (*nabhobhiḥ*) — by the stars; स्मयमानः (*smayamānaḥ*) — as though shining; द्यौरिव (*dyauriva*) — like the sky [or: नभोभिः (*nabhobhiḥ*) — in the regions of the atmosphere; स्मयमानः (*smayamānaḥ*) — as though shining; द्यौरिव (*dyauriva*) — like the sun]; चिकेत (*ciketa*) — is known.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 6)**

(Kannada, translated:) The Agni who, like one oppressed with thirst, burns the forests; who, as water flows swiftly down a sloping region, spreads swiftly in the forest; and who, like a war-horse that draws a chariot in battle, makes a harsh sound: that Agni, though he has a path of black colour and is a burner, is nevertheless delightful, and is known like the sky shining with stars in the atmosphere. [Or:] he is known like the sun shining in the sky.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 6)*

Who shines amidst the forests, as if satisfying himself (with food) : who (rushes along), like water down a declivity, and thunders like a chariot (of war) ; dark-pathed, consuming, yet delightful, he is regarded like the sky smiling with constellations.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 6)**

(Kannada, translated; lemmata in Sanskrit as printed.)

Here Agni is described as being in the form of a forest fire (kāḍugiccu).

> वना ततृषाणो न आभाति—वृक्षसमूहान् तृषित इव त्वरमाणः आभासयति ।

> *vanā tatṛṣāṇo na ābhāti—vṛkṣasamūhān tṛṣita iva tvaramāṇaḥ ābhāsayati |*

The Kannada says: Agni is described as spreading over the groups of trees in the forest as swiftly as a man seized by hunger eats his food in haste; or, in the other explanation (वने आभाति (*vane ābhāti*)), as shining in the forest of his own accord. Because Agni's spreading is very swift, the comparison with a man seized by hunger has been made.

> वार्ण पथा—उदकमिव प्रवणेन मार्गेण इतस्ततो गच्छति—

> *vārṇa pathā—udakamiva pravaṇena mārgeṇa itastato gacchati—*

*(The lemma is printed with वार्णि-like sign, as in the Pratipadārtha [?].)*

The Kannada says: As water runs very swiftly down a low-lying region and spreads, so Agni too spreads swiftly here and there among the trees in the forest. Agni's spreading is compared to the spreading of water.

### Printed p. 483 (PDF 504)

*(Header: "A. 2 A. 5 Va. 25]", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "483", read from the strip, not zoomed. The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

> रथ्येव स्वानीत्—रथो यथा युद्धमार्गेण गच्छन् स्वनति—

> *rathyeva svānīt—ratho yathā yuddhamārgeṇa gacchan svanati—*

The Kannada says: As a horse that draws a chariot neighs in battle when it is pressed forward to attack the enemy, so Agni (himself), spreading in the forest and burning, makes terrible noises such as "chaṭachaṭa". Or: as a sound arises from a chariot moving swiftly when the charioteer (rathika) attacks the enemy, so Agni sounds like that sound; the example of the sound is thus explained.

> कृष्णाध्वा तपुः रण्वः नभोभिः स्मयमानः द्यौरिव चिकेत—

> *kṛṣṇādhvā tapuḥ raṇvaḥ nabhobhiḥ smayamānaḥ dyauriva ciketa—*

The Kannada says: Here the ṛṣi has explained the meaning by giving a very excellent and natural simile. As the forest fire burns the forest and goes ahead, the region burnt by the fire becomes black like a forest. In whatever region fire has burnt well and the embers are dying out, that region looks black; this is well known in the world. This fact is clearly known to those who have seen tracts of land burnt by a forest fire. For that very reason it is natural that the region burnt by Agni is called "the black path" (kappāda mārga). Thus, although the forest has burnt and the earth has turned black, it is also natural that here and there, that is, in some places in between, embers remain and the flame is not yet extinguished. Such a region is compared to the sky with its stars: the black earth is compared to the blue-coloured sky, and the embers and flames here and there to the stars; or Agni's flame is compared to the stars. Or it is compared to the sun, shining with great radiance in the blue sky: in this context the Agni that still burns in the midst of the burnt, black earth is to be understood as compared to the sun. Here the poet has used the words द्यौरिव स्मयमानः नभोभिः (*dyauriva smayamānaḥ nabhobhiḥ*) in a very profound expression full of meaning. When it is said that the sky with its stars shines like a man laughing, then, as the mind is delighted on seeing a laughing man or woman, so the mind is delighted on seeing the blue sky twinkling with stars. In the same way the earth burnt by the fire, black as it is, is described; and the ṛṣi has thus explained it and shown his skill in composition.

*(A short divider is printed at this place. Ṛk 6 is closed.)*

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

*(In the Saṃhitā शोचिष्मा is printed with a chandrabindu-like sign above the ā-stroke and is written शोचिष्माँ. The Ṛk numeral looks like the flat-footed glyph for 7, as in the Pada; not zoomed.)*

> स यो व्यस्था॑द॒भि दक्ष॑दु॒र्वीं प॒शुर्नैति॑ स्व॒युरगो॑पाः ।
> अ॒ग्निः शो॒चिष्मा॑ँ अत॒सान्यु॒ष्णन्कृ॒ष्णव्य॑थिरस्वदय॒न्न भूम॑ ॥ ७ ॥

> *sa yo vyasthādabhi dakṣadurvīṃ paśurnaiti svayuragopāḥ |*
> *agniḥ śociṣmā~ atasānyuṣṇankṛṣṇavyathirasvadayanna bhūma ‖ 7 ‖*

> अग्निः । शोचिष्मान् । अतसानि । उष्णन् । कृष्णऽव्यथिः । अस्वदयत् । न । भूम ॥ ७ ॥

> *saḥ | yaḥ | vi | asthāt | abhi | dakṣat | urvīṃ | paśuḥ | na | eti | sva 'yuḥ | agopāḥ |*
> *agniḥ | śociṣmān | atasāni | uṣṇan | kṛṣṇa 'vyathiḥ | asvadayat | na | bhūma ‖ 7 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Agni spreads over the whole earth, roaming unrestrained like a herdless animal, blazing, blackening thorns, as if tasting the trees' sap while drying shrubs.

*(In the bhāṣya नियोमक is read as printed; the plain ma and the vowel mark are not clear [?]. No sūtra number is printed in the grammatical tail.)*

> योऽग्निर्व्यस्थात् । विविधं तिष्ठति । व्याप्नोति विश्वं । तथा योऽग्निरुर्वीं विस्तृतां पृथिवीं सर्वां । यश्चाभिदक्षत् । अभिमुख्येन प्रवर्धमानो भवति ॥ उभे अपि यच्छब्दयोगान्न निहन्येते ॥ सोऽग्निः पशुर्न पशुरिव । यथा जातः पशुः स्वच्छन्देन चरति तथा स्वयुः स्वयमेव गच्छन् अगोपा गोपरहितः । नियोमक[?]वर्जित इत्यर्थः । एति । गच्छति । किं कुर्वन् । शोचिष्मान् प्रकृष्टदीप्तिः कृष्णव्यथिः कृष्णवर्णं प्राप्ता दग्धा व्यथकराः कंटकादयो येन तादृशः सन् भूमात्यधिकमस्वदयन्न । आस्वादयतीव वृक्षगतान् रसान् । अतसानि सततानि नीरसानि वा तरुगुल्मादीन्युष्णन् दहन्नेति ॥

> *yo 'gnirvyasthāt | vividhaṃ tiṣṭhati | vyāpnoti viśvaṃ | tathā yo 'gnirurvīṃ vistṛtāṃ pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ | yaścābhidakṣat | abhimukhyena pravardhamāno bhavati ‖ ubhe api yacchabdayogānna nihanyete ‖ so 'gniḥ paśurna paśuriva | yathā jātaḥ paśuḥ svacchandena carati tathā svayuḥ svayameva gacchan agopā goparahitaḥ | niyomaka[?]varjita ityarthaḥ | eti | gacchati | kiṃ kurvan | śociṣmān prakṛṣṭadīptiḥ kṛṣṇavyathiḥ kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ prāptā dagdhā vyathakarāḥ kaṃṭakādayo yena tādṛśaḥ san bhūmātyadhikamasvadayanna | āsvādayatīva vṛkṣagatān rasān | atasāni satatāni nīrasāni vā tarugulmādīnyuṣṇan dahanneti ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 7)**

(Kannada, translated; the lemma is printed ಭೂಮು and is written भूम.) यः (*yaḥ*) — which Agni; व्यस्थात् (*vyasthāt*) — has pervaded the various regions (and); उर्वीं (*urvīṃ*) — the extensive earth; अभि दक्षत् (*abhi dakṣat*) — pervading, spreads all around; सः अग्निः (*saḥ agniḥ*) — that Agni; पशुर्न (*paśurna*) — as an animal wanders at its own will; स्वयुः (*svayuḥ*) — by himself, independently; roaming; अगोपाः (*agopāḥ*) — being without restraint; शोचिष्मान् (*śociṣmān*) — emitting radiance; कृष्णव्यथिः (*kṛṣṇavyathiḥ*) — producing in burnt thorns and the like an alteration of black form; भूम (*bhūma*) — excessively; अस्वदयन्न (*asvadayanna*) — as if tasting (the sap of trees); अतसानि (*atasāni*) — making shrubs and the like sapless; उष्णन् (*uṣṇan*) — burning; एति (*eti*) — moves about.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 7)**

(Kannada, translated:) The Agni who has pervaded the various regions and spreads in manifold ways; who, pervading the broad earth and spreading all around, moves about like an animal wandering at its own will, independently and without restraint, emitting radiance; causing to thorns and the like that he has burnt a black alteration and also pain; and who, as if tasting in great measure the sap of the trees, moves about burning, making shrubs and the like sapless.

*(Ṛk 7 is left open: its printed English and Special Topics follow on the next page.)*

### Printed p. 485 (PDF 506)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 25 ]", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "485", read from the strip, not zoomed. The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

*(Ṛk 7 continues from p. 484. This page has its printed English and Special Topics.)*

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 7)*

He who is in many places ; who spreads over the whole earth, like an animal without a herdsman, that goes according to its own will, Agni, the bright-shining, consuming the dry-bushes, by whom the pain of blackness (is inflicted on the trees), entirely drinks up (their moisture).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 7)**

(Kannada, translated; lemmata in Sanskrit as printed.)

When Agni spreads over the forest and burns it, he is described as व्यस्थात् विविधं विश्वं व्याप्नोति (*vyasthāt vividhaṃ viśvaṃ vyāpnoti*) — he spreads in many different ways, so that not even a little of the whole forest is left out. Further:

> उर्वीं अभिदक्षत्—विस्तृतां पृथिवीं सर्वां अभिमुख्येन प्रवर्धमानो भवति ।

> *urvīṃ abhidakṣat—vistṛtāṃ pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ abhimukhyena pravardhamāno bhavati |*

The Kannada says: it is described that he spreads over all the trees and herbs in the forest and also over the extensive land of the forest, so that no one else has room to enter that region. For this Agni's moving about of his own accord, spreading through the forests, the simile of an animal has been given:

> पशुर्न स्वयुः अगोपाः एति—जातः पशुः यथा स्वच्छंदेन चरति तथा स्वयमेव गच्छन् नियामकवर्जितो गच्छति ।

> *paśurna svayuḥ agopāḥ eti—jātaḥ paśuḥ yathā svacchaṃdena carati tathā svayameva gacchan niyāmakavarjito gacchati |*

The Kannada says: just as an animal (an elephant and the like) that is born and grows in the forest goes about according to its own wish, in its wandering and conduct, without coming under the control of another, so Agni, born in the forest, grows by his own free conduct, not subject to those who keep him under rule. Here the simile of the animal fits Agni very well. Tigers, lions, wild boars and other creatures that are born and grow in the forest itself and are subject to no one, roam and sport wherever their mind pleases. In the same way a forest fire born in the forest itself (from the friction of trees) overruns and burns the whole extensive forest. The main intention is that no one can stop this.

*(The word नियामकवर्जितो (*niyāmakavarjito*) is printed clearly here, ma with its own sign; this clearer printing corrects the doubtful नियोमक (*niyomaka*) of the bhāṣya on p. 484, which should be read नियामक (*niyāmaka*) — niyāmaka, "controller".)*

> कृष्णव्यथिः भूम अस्वदयन्न अतसानि उष्णन्—कृष्णवर्णं प्राप्ताः [?] दग्धाः व्यथाकराः कंटकादयो येन—

> *kṛṣṇavyathiḥ bhūma asvadayanna atasāni uṣṇan—kṛṣṇavarṇaṃ prāptāḥ [?] dagdhāḥ vyathākarāḥ kaṃṭakādayo yena—*

> वृक्षगर्ताः [?] रसाः आस्वादयतीव—

> *vṛkṣagartāḥ [?] rasāḥ āsvādayatīva—*

> संतता(नि) नीरसानि वा तरुगुल्मादीनि दहन्नेति—

> *saṃtatā(ni) nīrasāni vā tarugulmādīni dahanneti—*

The Kannada says: having burnt thorns and the like, he makes them black, causing pain to those who see them; he spreads through the forest as one who surpasses (all) and, as if tasting, consumes all the sap that is in the trees, like one who tastes for relish; and, burning trees and shrubs that have grown thick and are sapless (or have become dry), the fire goes ahead through the forest, so it is described. Here, when Agni burns green trees, the sap in the trees dries up through the heat of Agni and the tree also is burnt away; the comparison of this with the tasting of sap is both natural and full of meaning.

#### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

*(The Ṛk numeral looks like the glyph for 8 in both the Saṃhitā and the Pada; not zoomed.)*

> नू ते॒ पूर्व॒स्याव॑सो॒ अधी॑तौ तृ॒तीये॑ वि॒दथे॒ मन्म॑ शंसि ।
> अ॒स्मे अ॑ग्ने सं॒यद्वी॑रं बृ॒हंतं॑ क्षु॒मंतं॒ वाजं॑ स्वप॒त्यं र॒यिं दाः॑ ॥ ८ ॥

> *nū te pūrvasyāvaso adhītau tṛtīye vidathe manma śaṃsi |*
> *asme agne saṃyadvīraṃ bṛhaṃtaṃ kṣumaṃtaṃ vājaṃ svapatyaṃ rayiṃ dāḥ ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

*(In the Pada the small subscript stroke in अधिऽइतौ, संयत्ऽवीरं, क्षुऽमंतं and सुऽअपत्यं is the compound mark; it is written ऽ.)*

> नु । ते । पूर्वस्य । अवसः । अधिऽइतौ । तृतीये । विदथे । मन्म । शंसि ।
> अस्मे इति । अग्ने । संयत्ऽवीरं । बृहंतं । क्षुऽमंतं । वाजं । सुऽअपत्यं ।
> रयिं । दाः ॥ ८ ॥

> *nu | te | pūrvasya | avasaḥ | adhi 'itau | tṛtīye | vidathe | manma | śaṃsi |*
> *asme iti | agne | saṃyat 'vīraṃ | bṛhaṃtaṃ | kṣu 'maṃtaṃ | vājaṃ | su 'apatyaṃ |*
> *rayiṃ | dāḥ ‖ 8 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* Remembering the earlier propitiation of Agni, praise is recited now too at the third pressing; Agni is asked to give food with heroes, great and renowned, good offspring and wealth.

*(The bhāṣya prints मध्येऽन्यतमो (*madhye 'nyatamo*) (the last word ending in an ो-like sign) before तृतीये क्रतौ (*tṛtīye kratau*); read as printed [?]. The word before यागे (*yāge*) is विदथे (*vidathe*); the printed form of यागे (*yāge*) has an ō-like sign (ಯೋಗೇ), written यागे (*yāge*) as the sense requires [?]. In the grammatical tail शंसि | अशंसि | शस्यतेऽस्माभिः (*śaṃsi | aśaṃsi | śasyate 'smābhiḥ*) no sūtra is quoted.)*

> हे अग्ने ते तव संबंधिनः पूर्वस्य पूर्वं योगसमये कृतस्यावसोऽभिमततर्पणस्याधीतौ स्मरणे सति तत्स्मृत्या नु अद्यापि तृतीये विदथे यागे [?] तृतीयसवने । यद्वा प्रातरनुवाकसंबंधिनामाग्नेयोषस्याश्विनानां मध्येऽन्यतमो [?] तृतीये क्रतौ मन्म मननीयं स्तोत्रं शंसि । अशंसि । शस्यतेऽस्माभिः । हे अग्ने त्वं चास्मे अस्मभ्यं संयद्वीरं संयतो वीरा यस्मिन् तादृशं बृहंतं महांतं क्षुमंतं शब्दवंतं कीर्तिमंतं वाजमुक्तलक्षणमन्नं स्वपत्यं रयिं च दाः । देहि ॥

> *he agne te tava saṃbaṃdhinaḥ pūrvasya pūrvaṃ yogasamaye kṛtasyāvaso 'bhimatatarpaṇasyādhītau smaraṇe sati tatsmṛtyā nu adyāpi tṛtīye vidathe yāge [?] tṛtīyasavane | yadvā prātaranuvākasaṃbaṃdhināmāgneyoṣasyāśvinānāṃ madhye 'nyatamo [?] tṛtīye kratau manma mananīyaṃ stotraṃ śaṃsi | aśaṃsi | śasyate 'smābhiḥ | he agne tvaṃ cāsme asmabhyaṃ saṃyadvīraṃ saṃyato vīrā yasmin tādṛśaṃ bṛhaṃtaṃ mahāṃtaṃ kṣumaṃtaṃ śabdavaṃtaṃ kīrtimaṃtaṃ vājamuktalakṣaṇamannaṃ svapatyaṃ rayiṃ ca dāḥ | dehi ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 8)**

(Kannada, translated:) अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; ते (*te*) — belonging to you; पूर्वस्य (*pūrvasya*) — (the praise) recited at the time of the earlier savana, and अवसः (*avasaḥ*) — that which made you satisfied; अधीतौ (*adhītau*) — following that praise; नु (*nu*) — even now; तृतीये विदथे (*tṛtīye vidathe*) — at the time of the third savana; मन्म (*manma*) — the praise that is worthy of reflection; शंसि (*śaṃsi*) — is recited. अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; अस्मे (*asme*) — to us; संयद्वीरं (*saṃyadvīraṃ*) — accompanied by heroes; बृहंतं (*bṛhaṃtaṃ*) — great; क्षुमंतं (*kṣumaṃtaṃ*) — deserving of fame; वाजं (*vājaṃ*) — food; स्वपत्यं (*svapatyaṃ*) — excellent offspring; रयिं (*rayiṃ*) — wealth; दाः (*dāḥ*) — give.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 8)**

(Kannada, translated:) O Agni, the praise that belongs to you, that was recited in the earlier savana with you in view, and that made you satisfied: following that very praise, even now at the time of the third savana, a praise worthy of reflection is recited. O Agni, give us food that is accompanied by heroes, great, and deserving of fame, and excellent offspring, and wealth.

### Printed p. 487 (PDF 508)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 25 ]", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "487", read from the strip, not zoomed. The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

*(The Bhāvārtha of Ṛk 8 ends on this page with "…give us". The Kannada here, completing the sentence of p. 486, repeats the sense given above: …may you give us food accompanied by heroes, great and deserving of fame, excellent offspring and wealth.)*

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 8)*

Verily your praise has been recited (by us) at the third (daily) sacrifice, as it was in the repetition of your first propitiation : give us, Agni, ample and notorious food, posterity, riches, such as may be the support of numerous dependants.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 8)**

(Kannada, translated; lemmata in Sanskrit as printed.)

The Kannada says: here, addressing Agni, the yajamānas and ṛtvijs who have performed the sacrifice from the time it began until now remember the stotras and the like that please Agni, and at the third pressing, तृतीये विदथे (*tṛtīye vidathe*), or, in the other explanation,

> यद्वा प्रातरनुवाकसंबंधिनां आग्नेयोषस्याश्विनानां मध्ये तृतीयक्रतौ

> *yadvā prātaranuvākasaṃbaṃdhināṃ āgneyoṣasyāśvinānāṃ madhye tṛtīyakratau*

— while the sacrifices are being performed, among the three kinds of mantras — the Āgneya-kratu, the Uṣasya-kratu and the Āśvina-kratu — which belong to the Prātaranuvāka mantras recited in the morning, the stotras and the like recited in the third kratu, the one distinct from the others, are recited by us. It is described as the hope that Agni may listen to these stotras. With this, what the yajamānas pray for is described: संयद्वीरं (*saṃyadvīraṃ*) — sons who subdue (restrain) heroes; बृहंतं क्षुमंतं वाजं (*bṛhaṃtaṃ kṣumaṃtaṃ vājaṃ*) — abundant food; fame; and wealth: may Agni grant them.

*(A short rule is printed here. Ṛk 8 is closed.)*

#### Ṛk 9

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

*(In the Saṃhitā the word उपरा (*uparā*) is printed with a chandrabindu-like sign above the ā-stroke and is written उपराँ (*uparā~*); the Pada has उपरान् (*uparān*). The Ṛk numeral looks like ९, as in the Pada; not zoomed.)*

> त्वया॒ यथा॑ गृत्सम॒दासो॑ अग्ने॒ गुहा॑ व॒न्वंत॒ उप॑राँ अ॒भि ष्युः ।
> सु॒वीरा॑सो अभिमाति॒षाहः॒ स्मत्सू॒रिभ्यो॑ गृण॒ते तद्वयो॑ धाः ॥ ९ ॥

> *tvayā yathā gṛtsamadāso agne guhā vanvaṃta uparā~ abhi ṣyuḥ |*
> *suvīrāso abhimātiṣāhaḥ smatsūribhyo gṛṇate tadvayo dhāḥ ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

*(In the Pada the subscript stroke in गृत्सऽमदासः, सुऽवीरासः, अभिमातिऽसहः and सूरिऽभ्यः is the compound mark, written ऽ; the Pada has अभिमातिसहः (*abhimātisahaḥ*) with the ordinary स where the Saṃhitā has ष.)*

> त्वया । यथा । गृत्सऽमदासः । अग्ने । गुहा । वन्वंतः । उपरान् । अभि । स्युरिति स्युः ।
> सुऽवीरासः । अभिमातिऽसहः । स्मत् । सूरिऽभ्यः । गृणते । तत् । वयः । धाः ॥ ९ ॥

> *tvayā | yathā | gṛtsa 'madāsaḥ | agne | guhā | vanvaṃtaḥ | uparān | abhi | syuriti syuḥ |*
> *su 'vīrāsaḥ | abhimāti 'sahaḥ | smat | sūri 'bhyaḥ | gṛṇate | tat | vayaḥ | dhāḥ ‖ 9 ‖*

### Printed p. 488 (PDF 509)

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*Gist:* The Gṛtsamada ṛṣis, helped by Agni, ask to gain choice hidden wealth (or to overcome hidden sins). They ask to be rich in heroic sons and to defeat enemies. They also ask Agni to give the worshippers abundant, renowned food.

*(The bhāṣya is printed as a Sanskrit text with a short grammatical tail. In the tail, व्यत्ययेनैकवचनं (*vyatyayenaikavacanaṃ*) is the only remark of that kind and no sūtra is quoted. The word after आत्मनि (*ātmani*) is printed with an ष्ट्य-like conjunct, ಪರೋಷ್ಟ್ಯೇಣ, and is written परोक्ष्येण as the sense requires [?]. The word before स्तोतृभ्यः (*stotṛbhyaḥ*) is printed ಶಬ್ದಯುಧ್ಭ್ಯಃ and is written शब्दयद्भ्यः [?].)*

> हे अग्ने त्वया रक्षकेण वन्वंतश्छांदसं भजंतो गृत्समदा ऋषयः । आत्मनि परोक्ष्येण [?] वचनं । यथा गुहा गुहायां वर्तमानानुपरान् उपरमणसाधनान् उपरि उत्कृष्टे वर्तमानान्वा धनविशेषानभिस्युः । अभिभवेयुः । स्वाधीनान् कुर्युः । यद्वा गूढानुपरान् उपरेऽधिकत्वेन वर्तमानान्पापानभिस्युः । अभिभवेयुः । तथा कुर्वित्यर्थः । कीदृशाः । सुवीरासः । शोभनपुत्राद्युपेताः । अभिमातिसहः । वैरिणां पापादीनां सोढारः । किंच सूरिभ्यो मेधाविभ्यो यजमानेभ्यो गृणते ॥ व्यत्ययेनैकवचनं । शब्दयद्भ्यः [?] स्तोतृभ्यः । यद्वा सूरिभ्यो यजमानेभ्यो गृणते स्तोत्रे च स्मत् सुमत् अतिप्रभूतं तत् तादृशं प्रसिद्धं वयोऽन्नं धाः । धेहि ॥

> *he agne tvayā rakṣakeṇa vanvaṃtaśchāṃdasaṃ bhajaṃto gṛtsamadā ṛṣayaḥ | ātmani parokṣyeṇa [?] vacanaṃ | yathā guhā guhāyāṃ vartamānānuparān uparamaṇasādhanān upari utkṛṣṭe vartamānānvā dhanaviśeṣānabhisyuḥ | abhibhaveyuḥ | svādhīnān kuryuḥ | yadvā gūḍhānuparān upare 'dhikatvena vartamānānpāpānabhisyuḥ | abhibhaveyuḥ | tathā kurvityarthaḥ | kīdṛśāḥ | suvīrāsaḥ | śobhanaputrādyupetāḥ | abhimātisahaḥ | vairiṇāṃ pāpādīnāṃ soḍhāraḥ | kiṃca sūribhyo medhāvibhyo yajamānebhyo gṛṇate ‖ vyatyayenaikavacanaṃ | śabdayadbhyaḥ [?] stotṛbhyaḥ | yadvā sūribhyo yajamānebhyo gṛṇate stotre ca smat sumat atiprabhūtaṃ tat tādṛśaṃ prasiddhaṃ vayo 'nnaṃ dhāḥ | dhehi ‖*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha — Ṛk 9)**

(Kannada, translated:) अग्ने (*agne*) — O Agni; वन्वंतः (*vanvaṃtaḥ*) — praising you and worshipping; गृत्समदासः (*gṛtsamadāsaḥ*) — the Gṛtsamada ṛṣis; त्वया (*tvayā*) — with the help of you, the protector; यथा (*yathā*) — in what manner; गुहा (*guhā*) — in a cave, hidden; उपरान् (*uparān*) — excellent wealths; अभि स्युः (*abhi syuḥ*) — as they obtain, in that manner also (and); सुवीरासः (*suvīrāsaḥ*) — as those who have excellent heroic sons; अभिमातिसहः (*abhimātisahaḥ*) — as those who have the power to crush enemies; (make them so); सूरिभ्यः (*sūribhyaḥ*) — for the performers of the sacrifice; गृणते (*gṛṇate*) — to the praisers who recite praise; स्मत् (*smat*) — abundant; तत् (*tat*) — renowned; वयः (*vayaḥ*) — food; धाः (*dhāḥ*) — give.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha — Ṛk 9)**

(Kannada, translated:) O Agni, with the help of you, the protector, may the Gṛtsamada ṛṣis, who praise and worship you, obtain excellent wealth that lies hidden in a cave, and likewise may they be those who have excellent heroic sons and the power to crush enemies. Give abundant and renowned food to the praisers, who recite praise for the performers of the sacrifice.

**English Translation** *(as printed, Ṛk 9)*

By you (Agni), may the Gritsamadas, repeating your praise, become masters of the precious secret (treasures); so that they may be possessed of excellent dependants, and be able to resist (their) enemies, and do you give to (your) pious worshippers, and to him who glorifies (you), such (abundant) food.

### Printed p. 489 (PDF 510)

*(Header: "Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 5, Varga 26 ]", "Ṛgvedasaṃhitā", "489", read from the strip, not zoomed. The numeral file has no rows for this page.)*

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu — Ṛk 9)**

(Kannada, translated; lemmata in Sanskrit as printed, in bold.)

> वन्वंतः—छांदसं भजंतो गृत्समदा ऋषयः

> *vanvaṃtaḥ—chāṃdasaṃ bhajaṃto gṛtsamadā ṛṣayaḥ*

Here the sense is given as the ṛṣis who are fit for Agni's favour, descendants or relatives of Gṛtsamada and others, who go on with Vedic study. Here the ṛṣi Gṛtsamada, the seer of the mantra, has spoken referring to himself, to those on his side and to his descendants.

> यथा गुहा उपरान् [?] अभि स्युः—गुहायां वर्तमानान् उपरि वर्तमानान् वा धनविशेषान् स्वाधीनान् कुर्युः । यद्वा गूढान् अधिकत्वेन वर्तमानान् पापान् अभिभवेयुः तथा कुरु ।

> *yathā guhā uparān [?] abhi syuḥ—guhāyāṃ vartamānān upari vartamānān vā dhanaviśeṣān svādhīnān kuryuḥ | yadvā gūḍhān adhikatvena vartamānān pāpān abhibhaveyuḥ tathā kuru |*

*(In this passage the nasal ending of उपरान्, धनविशेषान्, स्वाधीनान्, गूढान् and वर्तमानान् is printed with a sign that looks like a chandrabindu with a stroke. It is written -ान् as the grammar and the bhāṣya on p. 488 require [?].)*

Addressing Agni, the Kannada says: may the wealth that has been caused to lie hidden in caves (in a lonely or secret place), or that lies on the surface of the earth, come under the control of us, the ṛṣis who live by the study of the Veda alone. One kind of wish is thus explained. The second kind: may we have power so that the hidden and abundant sins that we have committed in secret, so that no one knows of them, are destroyed. The favour of Agni is prayed for in this way.

> सूरिभ्यः गृणते—मेधाविभ्यः यजमानेभ्यः यद्वा सूरिभ्यः स्तोतृभ्यः

> *sūribhyaḥ gṛṇate—medhāvibhyaḥ yajamānebhyaḥ yadvā sūribhyaḥ stotṛbhyaḥ*

The Kannada says: the word सूरि (*sūri*) is read by Yāska among the names of stotṛ (praisers) (Ni. 3-19, as printed [?]). Here two different meanings of सूरि (*sūri*) are given: for the ṛtvijs who recite the stotra, or for the intelligent sacrificers. With these meanings explained, Agni is prayed to give abundant sons, wealth, food and the like.
